aleena.name: Aleena
aleena.description: Aleena are diminutive, enthusiastic and irrepressibly curious, turning up all over the galaxy in numbers far beyond what their small population should allow. They travel because staying still does not occur to them.
aleena.physiology: Aleena are very short humanoids with wide mouths whose natural curve reads as a permanent smile — a feature that has done a great deal for their reputation and occasionally undermined them at serious moments. They are quick, agile and durable for their size, with reflexes that make them capable pilots and racers. Their lifespans are respectable and their energy is famously undiminished by age.
aleena.society: Aleena culture is communal and warm, with extended families sharing interlinked homes and a strong instinct for celebration. They are enthusiastic rather than reckless, though the distinction is invisible from outside. Offworld Aleena are travellers, explorers, pilots and traders, and they take genuine pleasure in company — an Aleena will befriend a crew inside a week and remember every one of them decades later. Their homeworld's dangers gave them a matter-of-fact attitude to risk that outsiders find alarming.
aleena.homeworld: Aleen is a harsh world beneath its pleasant surface, home to fierce predators and a subterranean ecology that its people treat with respect and considerable superstition. Aleena settlements are built with an eye to what lives below. The species leaves in numbers and returns often; the homeworld is a place they come back to rather than one they escape.
aleena.language: Aleena speak Aleena, fast and high, and pick up Basic and Huttese readily. They talk a great deal, gesture more, and an Aleena's account of an event will be longer and more entertaining than the event was.

anx.name: Anx
anx.description: Anx are towering, crested herbivores with deep voices and longer memories — a peaceable people whose world has drawn exactly the wrong kind of Imperial interest.
anx.physiology: Anx are very tall bipeds, well over two metres, with a prominent dorsal crest running from the skull down the spine that flushes with colour under strong emotion. Their build is heavy and their strength considerable, though they are herbivores with no predatory heritage and little instinct for violence. Their voices carry into registers below most species' hearing, and Anx conversation has a subsonic layer that outsiders miss entirely. Their skin is thick and their frames durable.
anx.society: Anx culture is patient, communal and slow to anger — decisions are taken collectively and grudges, when they form, are held with the same deliberation as everything else. They are skilled in medicine and anatomy, a tradition that made Anx healers valued long before galactic contact and produced Jedi noted for combining that knowledge with real physical presence. The species is not pacifist so much as reluctant, and an Anx that has concluded force is necessary is a serious problem for whoever caused that conclusion.
anx.homeworld: Gravlex Med is a world whose ecology has been degraded by outside extraction, its soil and water compromised by industry the Anx did not invite and cannot dislodge. Imperial interest in the planet's resources has accelerated the damage, and Anx emigration has risen accordingly — many leave to earn offworld and send support home, aware that the home they are supporting is deteriorating.
anx.language: Anx speak Anx, much of it below the range other species can hear, so an overheard Anx conversation sounds like fragments with long gaps. They learn Basic well and speak it in a deep resonant register. An Anx asked to repeat something is often repeating the audible part.

aqualish.name: Aqualish
aqualish.description: Aqualish have a reputation for belligerence that a good many of them work hard to earn. Three distinct sub-species share one world and a long history of fighting over it, and the galaxy mostly notices the ones with the tusks.
aqualish.physiology: Aqualish come in three forms: the tusked Aquala with flippered hands, the Ualaq with four eyes, and the Quara with fingered hands and two eyes. All are stocky, powerful and covered in coarse hair, with prominent facial tusks and a build suited to both water and land. They are physically robust, tolerate rough conditions well, and their eyesight is adapted to their world's murky seas. The physical differences between the sub-species are real and have historically mattered enormously to Aqualish and not at all to anyone else.
aqualish.society: Aqualish society is clan-based, martial and abrasive, with a long internal history of sub-species conflict that periodically boiled into open war. Strength and directness are respected; subtlety is regarded with suspicion. That culture exports badly — Aqualish encountered offworld are frequently muscle for someone, and the species' reputation for thuggery is earned often enough to stick. It also obscures a substantial population of traders, engineers and financiers who find the stereotype professionally useful and privately galling.
aqualish.homeworld: Ando is a watery world of shallow seas and scattered land, and the competition for that limited ground drove much of Aqualish history. Its people took to space early and aggressively, and the planet's own affairs remain contentious. Imperial administration has suppressed the worst of the internal conflict by methods the Aqualish resent and a few quietly appreciate.
aqualish.language: Aqualish is guttural and hard-edged, and its speakers produce Basic with a growling accent that other species read as hostility whether or not any is intended. Many Aqualish have stopped correcting the assumption on the grounds that it saves time.

arcona.name: Arcona
arcona.description: Arcona are hammer-headed, ammonia-dependent desert dwellers with a dangerous weakness for salt. Sober, they are perceptive and communal; addicted, they are somebody else entirely.
arcona.physiology: Arcona have a broad hammer-shaped head with widely spaced eyes, giving them a wide field of view and poor depth perception — a trade their ancestors made for spotting movement across open ground. They metabolise ammonia and must supplement it offworld or sicken. Their most notorious vulnerability is sodium chloride: ordinary salt is intoxicating and addictive to them, turning their eyes from green to gold and their judgement to nothing, and salt addiction has hollowed out a great many Arcona lives.
arcona.society: Arcona live in nests — communal groupings that function as family, employer and government at once — and an Arcona separated from a nest for long grows genuinely unwell. Decisions are collective, resources are shared, and individual accumulation is close to meaningless. Offworld they seek out other Arcona quickly and form new nests where they can. That communal instinct makes them loyal crew and easy marks for anyone offering salt, a combination unscrupulous employers have exploited for generations.
arcona.homeworld: Cona is arid and ammonia-rich, its scarce water heavily mineralised, its ecology built around conserving everything. Arcona nests there are permanent and old. Offworld demand for Arcona labour and their vulnerability to a substance freely available everywhere else have combined to scatter them widely and badly.
arcona.language: Arcona speak Arconese, and most learn Basic capably. Their poor depth perception makes reading body language at distance difficult, so they tend to close in when talking, which other species find either warm or crowding depending on how much they know.

arkanian.name: Arkanian
arkanian.description: Arkanians are pale, white-eyed geneticists convinced of their own perfection, and they have spent millennia editing other species to prove it. Brilliant, arrogant, and responsible for a great deal of harm.
arkanian.physiology: Arkanians are near-Human with chalk-white skin, pupil-less eyes that see into the infrared, and three-fingered hands they regard as a mark of refinement. Their eyesight in darkness is excellent and in bright light poor. Generations of self-directed genetic work have left the pure-blooded line notably homogeneous — and produced the Arkanian Offshoots, a related population created for labour and treated accordingly, whose existence Arkanians discuss reluctantly.
arkanian.society: Arkanian culture is founded on the belief that their species is the pinnacle of evolution and that improving on nature is both a right and a duty. Genetic research is the highest calling, projects run across generations, and ethical objections are regarded as a failure of imagination. That has produced genuine scientific achievement and a long catalogue of engineered species, hybrids and Offshoots created to specification. Their arrogance is not a caricature — it is doctrine, and it has made them widely disliked by people who have reason.
arkanian.homeworld: Arkania is a frozen world of ice fields and diamond deposits, its cities built around research institutions that dominate the culture and the economy alike. Imperial scientists have found the Arkanians useful collaborators and impatient ones — a species accustomed to setting its own research agenda does not take direction gracefully. The Offshoot population lives largely elsewhere.
arkanian.language: Arkanians speak Arkanian, precise and formal, with a technical vocabulary of unusual depth. The Offshoots' dialect drifted over generations toward words of deference — a linguistic record of what was done to them. Arkanians speak Basic well and use it with a condescension most listeners detect immediately.

arkanian_offshoot.name: Arkanian Offshoot
arkanian_offshoot.description: Arkanian Offshoots were engineered by the Arkanians as labour and treated as property, and they have spent generations proving they are neither. Hardier than their makers and far less impressed with them.

special_abilities.name: Additional Career Skills
special_abilities.description: May train in two additional career skills

special_abilities.name: Genetically Engineered
special_abilities.description: Arkanian Offshoots may choose to suffer one Strain to receive a [BO] to a single Brawn or Agility-based check made on their turn.

bonus_free_ranks._provenance_note: Unofficial Species Menagerie (community) — "+2 career skills, no spec line" prose structured (B-21); 6 career / 2 first-spec

arkanian_offshoot.physiology: Offshoots are the product of Arkanian genetic work crossed with other stock, and the result is a species tougher and more adaptable than the pure Arkanian line. They have five fingers rather than three — a difference their makers treat as a defect and the Offshoots regard as the least of the insults — with skin tones ranging beyond Arkanian white and eyes that are usually pupilled. They tolerate hardship, poor conditions and physical labour far better than the Arkanians who designed them for exactly that.
arkanian_offshoot.society: Offshoot culture formed in the gap between being made and being acknowledged. Their communities are close, self-reliant and organised around mutual obligation, with a strong tradition of practical skill — they were built to work and have made competence a point of pride rather than a mark of service. Attitudes toward Arkanians range from cold indifference to something considerably warmer, and the question of what is owed and by whom is a live argument among them. They are widely dispersed, since leaving Arkanian space is the obvious first step toward a life of one's own.
arkanian_offshoot.homeworld: Arkania is where they were made and where a good many still live, in a stratified arrangement that grants Offshoots less than citizenship and more than the Arkanians would prefer. Offshoot communities elsewhere are typically founded by those who left, and they tend to be tight, capable and disinclined to discuss the homeworld with outsiders.
arkanian_offshoot.language: Offshoots speak a dialect of Arkanian that drifted over generations toward words of deference and away from words of triumph — the language carries the record of what was done to them. Basic is widely spoken, and many Offshoots prefer it precisely because it carries none of that history.

balosar.name: Balosar
balosar.description: Balosars are pale, antennaed near-Humans from a poisoned world, hustling on the edges of the galaxy's underworld. The death-stick trade is theirs, and it has cost them more than it earned.
balosar.physiology: Balosars are near-Human, thin and sallow, with retractable antennae they can conceal in their hair — the antennae sense chemical traces in the air and are a legacy of a homeworld where knowing what you were breathing mattered. Generations of industrial pollution have left the species frail, with weakened lungs and shortened lifespans. They are quick and nervy rather than strong.
balosar.society: Balosar culture is marked by desperation dressed as ambition. With a ruined homeworld and few legitimate prospects, a great many Balosars work the fringes — dealing, fixing, hustling — and the death-stick trade in particular is closely associated with them. They are persuasive, adaptable and habitually dishonest in small ways, less from malice than from the assumption that nobody is dealing straight with them either. Those who escape the pattern tend to leave entirely and not discuss where they are from.
balosar.homeworld: Balosar is an ecological catastrophe: over-industrialised past the point of recovery, its atmosphere fouled, its population living under a permanent haze. The corporations responsible extracted what they wanted and left. What remains supports a population that mostly wants out, which is why Balosars turn up in Coruscant's lower levels and every comparable underworld.
balosar.language: Balosars speak Balosar and Basic, generally both, and are practised at reading a mark's dialect and matching it. A Balosar's easy familiarity is a professional skill and is usually applied before you notice it has been.

barabel.name: Barabel
barabel.description: Barabels are armoured reptilian hunters from a world of scorching days and drowning nights, with a fierce sense of loyalty and an even fiercer reputation. They laugh at things other species do not find funny.

special_abilities.name: Resists Radiation
special_abilities.description: Barabels may add [BO] to Resilience checks made to resist the effects of radiation.

special_abilities.name: Resists Stun
special_abilities.description: Barabels may reduce the Strain damage suffered from Stun attacks by two.

barabel.physiology: Barabels are heavily built reptilians covered in thick black scales that shrug off blaster fire and blade alike, with retractable claws, sharp teeth and eyes suited to darkness. They are enormously strong and fast in short bursts, and they regenerate lost teeth and minor injuries readily. Their hide handles extremes of temperature that would kill most species, an adaptation to a homeworld that swings between furnace and flood daily.
barabel.society: Barabel culture is built around the hunt and around family, and the two are not clearly separated — a hunt is a family undertaking and a family is judged by its hunts. They are direct, physically demonstrative and possessed of a sense of humour that other species find alarming, since a laughing Barabel is often laughing at a threat. Loyalty once given is close to absolute, and Barabels who take up with a crew tend to stay. Their reputation for ferocity is deserved and, they feel, insufficiently appreciated as a compliment.
barabel.homeworld: Barab I is a world of brutal extremes — its long day scorches the surface and its long night brings torrential downpours that flood the plains, forcing everything alive to hunt fast and shelter faster. The Barabel evolved to thrive in exactly that, and offworld conditions strike most of them as tediously moderate.
barabel.language: Barabels speak Barabel, a hissing language delivered at volume, and learn Basic readily. They speak it bluntly and with obvious relish, and a Barabel's cheerful description of violence is usually just conversation.

bardottan.name: Bardottan
bardottan.description: Bardottans are spiritual, intelligent and physically capable, guarding a mystic tradition their Republic neighbours long dismissed as superstition. They were right and the Republic was not.
bardottan.physiology: Bardottans are humanoids with textured skin, prominent brows and three-fingered hands, generally lean and notably agile — many demonstrate physical skill well beyond what their scholarly reputation suggests. Their forearms are shorter in proportion than their legs, giving them a distinctive gait. They are long-lived and their senses are keen.
bardottan.society: Bardottan culture is built around the Dagoyan Order, a spiritual tradition of meditation and Force awareness that developed independently of the Jedi and was patronised by the Republic without ever being taken seriously by it. Bardottans are proud, independent and reluctant to ask for help, which delayed outside intervention when their mystics began disappearing. They are nonviolent by conviction — the Force is not to be used to injure — and that principle has been tested badly and mostly held.
bardottan.homeworld: Bardotta is a world of temples, meditation sites and isolationist politics, governed with an eye to keeping galactic affairs at a distance. That instinct served it until it did not. The planet's spiritual significance is genuine and its people's willingness to explain it to outsiders is limited, which has left a great deal of Bardottan tradition undocumented beyond its own borders.
bardottan.language: Bardottans speak Bardottan, a language rich in terms for states of meditation and spiritual condition that resist translation entirely. They speak Basic when they must. A Bardottan explaining their practice in Basic is aware of translating something into a language with no words for it.

besalisk.name: Besalisk
besalisk.description: Besalisks are big, four-armed, and blunt about what they want. They came from a cold world where hoarding was survival, and the habit has followed them into every business they run.
besalisk.physiology: Besalisks are bulky humanoids with four arms, a heavy build and a wattled neck sac that inflates in display or exertion. They store fat and water efficiently — an adaptation to a homeworld of scarcity that lets them go a long time on very little, and makes them heavier than they look. The extra arms are genuinely useful rather than ornamental, and a Besalisk cook, mechanic or brawler makes full use of all four.
besalisk.society: Besalisk culture grew out of competition for thin resources, and it shows: they are acquisitive, direct and disinclined to share, with a strong instinct to build a stock of whatever matters. That translates offworld into enterprise — Besalisks run kitchens, garages, cantinas and supply operations, usually as sole proprietors who trust nobody with the books. They are also sociable, loud and generous with hospitality once a relationship is established, which sits oddly with the hoarding until you understand it as the same thing seen from inside.
besalisk.homeworld: Ojom is a cold ocean world, its surface largely ice, its people historically clustered where warmth and food could be found. The scarcity that shaped Besalisk temperament was real and recent enough to be remembered. Most Besalisks now live offworld, and the ones who stayed regard the emigrants as having taken the easy option.
besalisk.language: Besalisks speak Besalisk, a rumbling language that carries well in wind. Most learn Basic and speak it bluntly, and their habit of stating a price and then simply repeating it is a negotiating position rather than a failure of vocabulary.

bith.name: Bith
bith.description: Bith think in structures other species cannot hold in their heads. Musicians, mathematicians and analysts, they are physically frail, intellectually formidable, and found wherever precision matters — including, famously, a cantina bandstand.
bith.physiology: Bith are hairless humanoids with enlarged craniums, large lidless black eyes and no external nose — they smell through openings beneath the eyes, with a sensitivity fine enough to distinguish individuals by scent. Their hearing is exceptional and finely discriminating, which underpins their musical reputation. Their hands have highly developed fine motor control; their bodies are otherwise weak, with poor endurance and little tolerance for physical stress. Evolution traded strength away and bought perception with it.
bith.society: Bith culture is intellectual, orderly and consensus-driven, organising itself around expertise and treating disputes as problems to be analysed rather than won. Music holds an unusual civic importance — not entertainment but a discipline, practised seriously and judged rigorously. They are curious and cooperative, uncomfortable with violence, and genuinely bad at deception, having very little cultural equipment for it. Bith scientists, technicians and composers turn up across the galaxy on the strength of competence rather than ambition.
bith.homeworld: Clak'dor VII was ruined by a war its own people fought with biological weapons, leaving a toxic landscape and driving the survivors into sealed domed cities. That history is the central fact of Bith self-understanding: a species that reasons carefully, once reasoned itself into catastrophe. It informs their caution, their distaste for conflict, and the number of Bith who quietly leave.
bith.language: Bith is a language of subtle sound distinctions that other species largely cannot hear, let alone reproduce, and a great deal of it sits at the edges of the audible range. They learn Basic readily and speak it precisely. Much of Bith artistic and technical work is untranslatable in the strict sense — the notation assumes an ear nobody else has.

bothan.name: Bothan
bothan.description: Bothans trade in information the way other species trade in cargo. Their intelligence network is the best in the galaxy, and their politics are conducted almost entirely through it — which makes them invaluable allies and exhausting friends.
bothan.physiology: Bothans are short, densely furred mammalian humanoids, their fur ranging from cream through brown to black and lying in patterns that shift with mood. That fur is a communication channel: a Bothan reads another Bothan's state from the set of it long before anyone speaks, and non-Bothans routinely miss half a conversation for want of the ability. They are physically unimposing, quick rather than strong, with keen hearing and a good head for detail. Lifespans are broadly comparable to Human.
bothan.society: Bothan society is built on the gathering, trading and withholding of information, a practice so central that it has its own name and its own etiquette. Status flows from what you know and who owes you for knowing it, and a Bothan who shares something freely is either making a very deliberate gift or setting something up. Clans compete constantly and cooperate instantly when the species' interests are threatened. Outsiders find the whole arrangement duplicitous; Bothans consider it simply the honest recognition that information is the only durable currency. Their spynet has served the Rebellion well, at a price the Rebellion is still paying.
bothan.homeworld: Bothawui is a temperate, prosperous world that has spent its history staying carefully neutral while quietly knowing everything. It has been invaded, occupied and courted by every major power in turn, and has survived each by ensuring it was more useful intact than conquered. Bothan colonies spread widely from there, and the species maintains interests on far more worlds than its population would suggest.
bothan.language: Bothans speak Bothese, a fast language whose spoken component is deliberately incomplete without the accompanying fur movement — a written transcript of Bothese is famously ambiguous, which is generally the intention. Nearly all Bothans learn Basic, and many learn several other languages, since a translator in the room is a leak.

caamasi.name: Caamasi
caamasi.description: Caamasi are gentle, principled and nearly extinct — a species whose homeworld was burned from orbit and whose survivors carry the memory of it literally, in shared recollections passed between minds.
caamasi.physiology: Caamasi are furred humanoids with expressive faces and calm bearing. Their defining trait is the memnii: vivid sensory memories that a Caamasi can share directly with another, transmitting an experience whole rather than describing it. Those memories persist across generations, which means atrocities committed against the species are not history to them but something closer to testimony. They are not physically formidable and have never tried to be.
caamasi.society: Caamasi culture is pacifist by deep conviction rather than by policy, holding violence to be a failure that damages the perpetrator as much as the victim. They are honest to a degree that complicates diplomacy, and widely trusted as mediators for exactly that reason. The destruction of their world did not radicalise them into violence; it made them witnesses, and Caamasi survivors carry and share the memory of it deliberately. Not even that loss broke the culture's core commitment.
caamasi.homeworld: Caamas was rendered largely uninhabitable when its shields were sabotaged and its surface bombarded — an atrocity carried out with inside help whose perpetrators were never fully identified. The survivors live scattered across the galaxy in small communities, and the question of who lowered the shields remains one of the more explosive unresolved matters in galactic politics.
caamasi.language: Caamasi speak Caamasi, a soft musical language, and are notable linguists — their emphasis on learning other species' tongues may have endangered their own. The memnii carry what language cannot, and a Caamasi sharing one is offering something considerably more intimate than a story.

cathar.name: Cathar
cathar.description: Cathar are feline humanoids with a fierce warrior tradition and a long memory of catastrophe. Passionate, honourable and quick to anger, they take obligation seriously enough to die over.

options.name: One Rank in Athletics
options.description: Cathar may begin the game with one rank in Athletics.

options.name: One Rank in Stealth
options.description: Cathar may begin the game with one rank in Stealth.

cathar.physiology: Cathar are covered in fur ranging from gold through brown to near-black, with manes on the males, retractable claws and sharp canines. They are fast, strong and agile, with excellent night vision and reflexes suited to close combat. Their claws are functional weapons rather than ornament, and a Cathar in a fight tends to close distance rather than manage it.
cathar.society: Cathar culture is built on honour, loyalty and a strong protective instinct — they bond fiercely, take slights personally, and regard the abandonment of a companion as close to unforgivable. That intensity makes them formidable allies and volatile ones. Their history includes a devastating slaver assault that nearly ended the species, and the memory of it has left a lasting hatred of slavery that Cathar act on more readily than most. They produced Jedi of note, whose passion the Order regarded as both an asset and a risk.
cathar.homeworld: Cathar is a world of savannah and forest whose people rebuilt after near-extinction and did not forget who caused it. The recovery is real but incomplete, and the species remains widely scattered. Cathar encountered offworld are frequently working against slavers, sometimes professionally and sometimes not.
cathar.language: Cathar speak Catharese, a growling language with a great deal of tonal range, and learn Basic easily. Their delivery carries emotion plainly — a Cathar's mood is rarely a mystery, which they consider honest and others find exhausting.

cerean.name: Cerean
cerean.description: Cereans are calm, deliberate thinkers whose tall conical skulls house a second brain. They take their time, consider every angle, and are almost impossible to hurry — traits that make them superb judges and frustrating travelling companions.
cerean.physiology: The Cerean head is the species' defining feature: an elongated cranium housing a binary brain structure, supported by a second heart that keeps it supplied. The arrangement gives Cereans a genuine capacity for parallel thought, letting them hold several lines of reasoning at once and weigh them against each other before speaking. It also makes them physically cautious — that skull is heavy and vulnerable, and Cereans avoid the kind of reckless movement other species enjoy. They are tall, slender, and long-lived, with a marked imbalance in birth rates that has shaped their family structures profoundly.
cerean.society: Cerean culture prizes deliberation to a degree that outsiders mistake for indecision. Decisions are reached slowly, with every party heard, and once reached they are rarely revisited. The species has a strong strain of environmental conservatism, having decided long ago that heavy industry was not worth what it cost, and Cerean settlements are deliberately modest in their technological footprint. Family units are large and matriarchal in practice, a consequence of demographics rather than doctrine. The Jedi Order drew a notable number of Cereans, whose temperament suited its teachings well.
cerean.homeworld: Cerea is a green agricultural world kept deliberately clear of the industrial development its neighbours embraced. Vehicles and heavy machinery are restricted to designated zones, and the species has resisted repeated commercial pressure to open the planet up. That resistance has come at a cost in influence and left Cerea vulnerable to powers less interested in its opinions, a vulnerability the Empire has not overlooked.
cerean.language: Cereans speak Cerean, a measured language whose grammar rewards precision and punishes ambiguity — a sentence tends to declare its own certainty level as it goes. Most speak Basic fluently and are noted for using it carefully, choosing words with a deliberateness that other species read as either great wisdom or great slowness depending on their patience.

chadra_fan.name: Chadra-Fan
chadra_fan.description: Chadra-Fan are tiny, bat-like and gifted with senses that read a room in ways nobody else can — including, disconcertingly, the emotional state of everyone in it via scent.
chadra_fan.physiology: Chadra-Fan stand about a metre tall, with large ears, flat noses and dark eyes adapted to low light. Their sensory range is remarkable: acute hearing well past the humanoid range, infrared vision, and an olfactory sense refined enough to detect the chemical signatures of emotion. They are physically fragile and know it, relying on speed, small size and knowing what is happening before anyone else does.
chadra_fan.society: Chadra-Fan culture is communal, inquisitive and mechanically minded — they take things apart compulsively and are exceptional technicians. The sensory acuity shapes their manners: since deception is hard to conceal from them, they are direct with each other and unnervingly perceptive with everyone else. They are gregarious and easily bored, and Chadra-Fan crews are known both for fixing the unfixable and for having pulled the panel off it first.
chadra_fan.homeworld: Chad is a world of frequent flooding, its people historically living in structures built to ride out the water. Periodic disasters have driven emigration for generations, and Chadra-Fan communities are scattered widely. Those offworld often work in salvage, repair and technical trades, where small hands and better senses are an advantage.
chadra_fan.language: Chadra-Fan speak Chadra-Fan, a rapid high-pitched language much of which sits above the range other species can hear — an overheard conversation is missing pieces. They learn Basic quickly and speak it fast, and a Chadra-Fan will often answer the question you were about to ask.

chagrian.name: Chagrian
chagrian.description: Chagrians are serene, formidable amphibians whose horns and head-tails read as imposing before they say a word. They favour reasoned debate, hold civic duty as a virtue, and have supplied the Senate with more than their share of imposing voices.
chagrian.physiology: Chagrians are blue-skinned amphibious humanoids with horns curving from the skull and a pair of thick lethorns hanging from the head. They are amphibious by ancestry and comfortable in water, and their skin — which ranges from pale blue to deep cerulean — evolved to withstand a period of intense solar radiation in their world's history. Their sense of taste is notably weak, which makes eating a duty rather than a pleasure and gives Chagrian cuisine a reputation it does not deserve to have to defend.
chagrian.society: Chagrian culture prizes composure, oratory and public service. Argument is conducted with elaborate courtesy, emotion is expressed sparingly and therefore lands hard, and a Chagrian who raises their voice has generally already decided something. They take social obligation seriously and are genuinely troubled by poverty and injustice encountered directly, which pushes many into politics, diplomacy and law. The species shares its world with the Nautolans, an arrangement conducted with rather more grace than most shared planets manage.
chagrian.homeworld: Champala is a warm, wet world of shallow seas and coastal cities, its people historically shaped by exposure to an unstable sun. It is prosperous, orderly and well represented in galactic institutions, and its long habit of sending its talented offworld into public service means Chagrians are encountered far more often than their population would suggest.
chagrian.language: Chagrians speak Chagri, a resonant language whose vowels carry a long way over water. Their vocal apparatus handles Basic easily and their diction in it tends to be exact to the point of formality — a Chagrian speaking casually still sounds like they are addressing a chamber.

chevin.name: Chevin
chevin.description: Chevin are enormous, slow-moving and shrewd — long-snouted quadrupedal traders whose deliberate pace conceals a talent for arriving at the profitable end of a deal.
chevin.physiology: Chevin are massive creatures who move on their forelimbs with their hind limbs tucked beneath, giving them a rolling, unhurried gait. Their most striking feature is an enormous elongated snout hanging over a wide mouth, with small eyes set high on the skull. Their hide is thick and leathery, they are extremely strong, and they are far tougher than their placid manner suggests. Their sense of smell is excellent.
chevin.society: Chevin culture is mercantile and patient, favouring long negotiations in which the other party grows restless first. They are shrewd judges of value and comfortable operating at the edges of legality — Chevin turn up throughout the galaxy's grey markets, generally running the operation rather than working in it. Their unhurried manner is partly physiology and partly technique, and underestimating a Chevin's speed of thought on the basis of their speed of movement is a mistake made frequently and expensively.
chevin.homeworld: Vinsoth is a world of grasslands and hard seasons, its Chevin population historically dominant over the other sentient species that shares it — an arrangement the wider galaxy knows little about and the Chevin do not advertise. Offworld Chevin are traders, brokers and crime bosses more often than not, and the homeworld's affairs stay comfortably out of view.
chevin.language: Chevin speak Chevin, low and drawn-out, and learn Basic and Huttese for business. They speak slowly by nature, and a Chevin who has paused for a long time in the middle of a negotiation has not lost the thread.

chiss.name: Chiss
chiss.description: Chiss are blue-skinned, red-eyed and unnervingly composed, emerging from an isolated empire in the Unknown Regions that the rest of the galaxy knows almost nothing about. They are brilliant tacticians and they do not explain themselves.
chiss.physiology: Chiss are near-Human, with blue skin and glowing red eyes whose intensity varies with the atmosphere they breathe. Their colouring comes from their homeworld's conditions, and it deepens or fades over a lifetime spent elsewhere. They are physically comparable to Humans and notably controlled — Chiss body language gives away very little, which is cultural discipline as much as physiology.
chiss.society: Chiss society is organised into ruling families whose rivalries are conducted with elaborate formality and considerable ruthlessness. Merit is genuinely valued, and a capable outsider to a family can rise, but the political web never stops mattering. Their military doctrine is famously pre-emptive in analysis and famously reluctant in aggression — the Ascendancy does not strike first as a matter of law, which its neighbours find either principled or infuriating. Chiss encountered beyond the Unknown Regions are usually exiles, envoys or something the Ascendancy would prefer not to discuss.
chiss.homeworld: Csilla is a frozen world, its population living in cities beneath the ice, and it anchors an Ascendancy whose extent and strength the wider galaxy can only estimate. The Chiss have kept it that way deliberately: contact is controlled, information flows outward sparingly, and even allied powers work from guesswork. What is not in doubt is that the Ascendancy is organised, capable and entirely uninterested in being absorbed.
chiss.language: Chiss speak Cheunh, a dense language whose grammar rewards precision and resists casual acquisition — outsiders rarely become fluent, which suits the Ascendancy. Chiss who deal with the wider galaxy learn Basic and speak it with exact, unhurried correctness, and their habit of pausing to choose the right word is often mistaken for hesitation.

clawdite.name: Clawdite
clawdite.description: Clawdites can change their appearance at will, which has made them the galaxy's default suspects. Distrusted everywhere, they take the work that distrust leaves them — espionage, infiltration, and worse.
clawdite.physiology: Clawdites are reptilian humanoids whose natural form is leathery and sallow, and whose real ability is a controlled restructuring of skin, features and colouring. The change is limited — roughly humanoid proportions, no great alteration of size — and it takes concentration to hold. It is also tiring; a Clawdite maintaining a face for a long stretch is working at it. Their true form is rarely seen by outsiders and rarely shown willingly.
clawdite.society: Clawdite society was shaped by occupation and by the galaxy's reaction to what they can do. Suspicion follows them: a Clawdite's presence anywhere sensitive makes everyone check each other's faces, and crime lords hire them precisely for that effect as much as for the ability. Some lean into the reputation and take the espionage work; others resent being defined by a talent they did not choose and live quietly in their own form. Their homeworld's history of resistance has left a strong political streak among those who left.
clawdite.homeworld: Zolan is a hot, harsh world whose Clawdite population long lived under the dominance of another people from the same planet — a subjugation that pushed many offworld and left a legacy of grievance. Imperial administration has changed the identity of the authority without changing much else. Clawdites abroad are frequently exiles rather than travellers.
clawdite.language: Clawdites speak Clawdite, and most also speak Basic — often several languages, since a changed face is useless with the wrong accent. That linguistic facility is a professional necessity for those in the infiltration trade and a source of further suspicion for those who are not.

clone.name: Clone
clone.description: Clones were grown on Kamino from a single bounty hunter's genetic template, accelerated to adulthood, and handed a war. They are identical by design and individual in spite of it — a fact the Republic never planned for and never quite knew what to do with.
clone.physiology: A clone is Human in every biological particular except two: growth is accelerated to roughly twice the natural rate, and the template is fixed. That acceleration buys the army soldiers in a decade instead of two, and charges for it at the far end — a clone in his teens is a grown man, and a clone in his twenties is ageing visibly. Inhibitor chips were implanted during development, officially to suppress aggression. Physically clones are fit, uniform and unremarkable; what varies is scarring, and increasingly, deliberate alteration.
clone.society: Clone culture formed in the gaps the Kaminoans left. Identical men in identical armour developed nicknames, painted their plates, cut their hair differently, and built a fierce brotherhood out of the one thing that was truly theirs — each other. Rank exists but loyalty runs sideways more than upward, and a squad will absorb enormous losses before it will abandon one of its own. Their relationship with the Jedi generals who led them was genuine and, in retrospect, unbearable. Clones are pragmatic, dark-humoured, and acutely aware that they were made for a purpose they did not choose.
clone.homeworld: Kamino is a storm-lashed ocean world of stilted white cities, sterile corridors and Kaminoan efficiency, and no clone remembers it fondly. It is where they were grown, trained, tested and shipped. Most consider their real home to be whichever unit they serve with, and returning to Kamino is a posting rather than a homecoming — a place that manufactured them and would readily manufacture their replacements.
clone.language: Clones speak Basic, taught from the tanks and standardised deliberately. What grew on top of it is a dense military argot — nicknames, unit slang, shorthand for things civilians have no reason to name — that outsiders find nearly impenetrable and clones use partly for that reason. A few pick up Mando'a, the language of the template's own people, and doing so means something.

corellian_human.name: Corellian Human
corellian_human.description: Corellians are Human, and would rather you noticed the first part. Confident to the point of provocation and famously good with a ship, they produce more pilots, smugglers and troublemakers per head than anywhere else in the galaxy.

skill_grants._provenance_note: rank_limit 3 per Suns of Fortune p.94 (B-19: Corellians may train Piloting up to rank 3 at creation)
rank_limit 3 per Suns of Fortune p.94 (B-19: Corellians may train Piloting up to rank 3 at creation)

corellian_human.physiology: Corellians are Human in every biological respect — the differences are cultural, and Corellians will explain them at length. What the reputation reflects is upbringing rather than biology: a world where children grow up around shipyards, where flying is ordinary rather than remarkable, and where a certain hands-on confidence is instilled early enough to look innate.
corellian_human.society: Corellian culture prizes independence, self-reliance and decisive action, and regards hesitation as close to a moral failing. That produces excellent pilots and a great many people who are certain when they should be careful. Family and homeworld loyalty run deep beneath the swagger, and a Corellian far from home tends to find other Corellians. Their shipwrights built much of what flies in the galaxy, and the culture treats a good vessel as something closer to a relationship than an asset.
corellian_human.homeworld: Corellia is an industrial world of vast shipyards and dense cities, one of five worlds in a system whose arrangement is old enough to be a genuine mystery. It has supplied the galaxy with hulls, crews and captains for centuries. Imperial control has turned the yards to military production and driven a good deal of Corellian talent into smuggling, the Rebellion, or both.
corellian_human.language: Corellians speak Basic, in a dialect confident enough that other Basic speakers occasionally struggle with the idiom. Old Corellian survives in ceremony, oaths and the names of ships. A Corellian's speech runs fast and assumes the listener is keeping up.

cosian.name: Cosian
cosian.description: Cosians are cheerful, three-eyed and famously good-natured, with a tolerance for other species' failings that borders on the saintly. They are also considerably tougher than they look.
cosian.physiology: Cosians are horned humanoids with three eyes and a broad tail, their skin tones running through greens and browns. The third eye gives excellent peripheral awareness, and their tails aid balance in the rough terrain of their homeworld. They are hardier than their slight appearance suggests, with good endurance and a high tolerance for discomfort — a Cosian will keep going long after complaining would be reasonable.
cosian.society: Cosian culture is relentlessly optimistic and communal, treating patience and good humour as practical virtues rather than pleasant ones. They are curious about other species to a degree that reads as naivety and is closer to genuine openness. That temperament made Cosians unusually well suited to the Jedi path — several rose high in the Order, valued as teachers precisely because their patience did not run out. Offworld they turn up as guides, mechanics and crew, and are widely regarded as the easiest company in the galaxy.
cosian.homeworld: Cosia is a world of forests and rough uplands whose people never developed much appetite for conquest or industry, preferring a quieter arrangement with their environment. It sits away from the main lanes and has attracted correspondingly little attention, which the Cosians count as good fortune.
cosian.language: Cosians speak Cosian, a lilting language full of terms of address that convey warmth. They learn Basic readily and speak it with unmistakable friendliness. A Cosian being genuinely angry is rare enough that other species tend not to recognise it when it happens.

dashade.name: Dashade
dashade.description: Dashade are shadow-skinned assassins, nearly invisible to the Force and rare enough that most of the galaxy thinks they are a legend. Their homeworld is gone and their numbers with it.

options.name: One Rank in Coercion
options.description: Dashade may begin the game with one rank in Coercion.

options.name: One Rank in Vigilance
options.description: Dashade may begin the game with one rank in Vigilance.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Discipline checks to affect a Dashade with a Force power or talent by one.

dashade.physiology: Dashade are tall, muscular reptilian humanoids with charcoal skin, prominent teeth and a bony ridged skull. Their defining trait is a natural resistance to the Force — a Dashade is extremely difficult to sense, influence or affect through it, which made them prized bodyguards and assassins in eras when Force users were more common. They are strong, durable and long-lived, and their vision suits the low light they favour.
dashade.society: Dashade culture is almost gone. What survives is a warrior tradition oriented around service to a patron, in which a contract taken is a bond rather than a job, and abandoning one is unthinkable. The few who remain are typically ancient, having survived by stasis or by distance when their world burned, and they carry loyalties to people and causes that no longer exist. Those who take new service take it seriously and expect the same in return.
dashade.homeworld: Urkupp was destroyed long ago, and with it nearly the entire species. What remains of Dashade identity is carried by individuals rather than communities — there is no homeworld to return to, no population to rejoin, and no cultural centre beyond memory. That absence defines them more than any surviving custom.
dashade.language: Dashade speak Dashadi, a deep sibilant language few outsiders have ever heard spoken by more than one person at a time. Most learn Basic, and their delivery is slow and deliberate — a Dashade has usually been alive a very long time and is in no hurry.

dathomirian.name: Dathomirian
dathomirian.description: Near-humans of Dathomir, the Nightsisters blend magick and alchemy with generations of dark-side exposure into a people built on self-determination, strength, and discipline. Their matrilineal, female-only clans keep to themselves — cold, practical, and dangerous — but the machinations of Sith and Jedi keep dragging their shadowed world into the light.

defel.name: Defel
defel.description: Defel absorb light rather than reflecting it, appearing to most species as moving shadows. They see in ultraviolet, live badly in daylight, and have made careers out of being hard to look at.

special_abilities.name: Light Sensitive
special_abilities.description: In bright light, without protective goggles, Defel suffer [SE][SE] on all skill checks.

special_abilities.name: Shadowed
special_abilities.description: In darkness, Defel gain [BO][BO] to Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Reduced Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Defel have a Silhouette of 0.

defel.physiology: A Defel's fur absorbs visible light almost completely, so to most eyes they register as a shadow with red points where the eyes are. Under ultraviolet illumination they resolve into an ordinary furred quadrupedal-descended humanoid with blue-grey colouring — a fact that startles Defel less than it startles everyone else. They see in ultraviolet natively and find standard lighting dim and uncomfortable. They are strong for their size and quick.
defel.society: Defel culture is communal and pragmatic, shaped by a homeworld of near-permanent low light. Offworld, their appearance has channelled them into work where being difficult to see is an asset — security, infiltration, and less reputable variations on both — and the galaxy's readiness to assume a shadow is up to something has not helped. Many resent the pigeonholing; most take the work anyway, since it pays.
defel.homeworld: Af'El is lit by an ultraviolet-heavy sun and shrouded in ways that make its surface hostile to species reliant on visible light. Its metal deposits made it commercially interesting long before anyone considered the Defel themselves interesting, and offworld employers have been recruiting from it since. Returning is difficult; Defel who leave often cannot readily go back.
defel.language: Defel speak Defel, and most learn Basic for work. Their conversation offworld carries an added difficulty: other species cannot read a face they cannot see, so Defel tend to be explicit about tone in a way that reads as oddly formal.

devaronian.name: Devaronian
devaronian.description: Devaronians are horned, sharp-featured wanderers with a galaxy-wide reputation for restlessness and sharp dealing. The males roam; the females run the settlements the males keep leaving.
devaronian.physiology: Devaronian males are hairless with prominent cranial horns, sharp teeth and skin from pale red to near-black; females are horned less prominently, furred, and generally larger. Both are hardy, with a metabolism that handles a wide range of foods and toxins and a tolerance for hard travel that suits the species' habits. Their sharp features and red colouring have earned them centuries of association with devilry in other species' folklore, which Devaronians find tiresome and occasionally exploit.
devaronian.society: Devaronian society is split by an old division of roles: males are driven by a genuine and near-universal wanderlust, leaving young and travelling widely, while females remain, raise the children and administer the settlements and industry. It is a functional arrangement rather than a happy one, and both halves have opinions about it. Offworld Devaronians turn up as traders, smugglers, pilots and information brokers, and their reputation for sharp practice reflects a real cultural comfort with the edges of a deal.
devaronian.homeworld: Devaron is a temperate world of dense jungle cut by natural passages that make travel through it easier than its ecology suggests. It holds sites of religious significance to more than one tradition and has drawn pilgrims and scholars for centuries. The settled population is largely female; the males are, characteristically, elsewhere.
devaronian.language: Devaronians speak Devaronese, and most speak Basic besides — often several other languages too, an occupational necessity for a species that travels constantly. They are quick with languages and quicker with the useful parts, and a Devaronian's fluency in a tongue tends to be exactly as deep as their business in it requires.

dowutin.name: Dowutin
dowutin.description: Dowutins are giants — three metres of muscle, tusks and low rumbling voice, with a strength that makes them prized as muscle and a temperament that rarely requires it.
dowutin.physiology: Dowutins are enormous humanoids with thick grey hide, prominent tusks and heavy talons that serve for prying, digging and, occasionally, self-defence. They are among the largest humanoid species in the galaxy, immensely strong, and durable enough to shrug off injuries that would end most fights. Their voices are so deep that whispering is effectively impossible for them, and an angry Dowutin's roar is a genuine hazard to nearby hearing.
dowutin.society: Dowutin culture prizes strength and self-control in equal measure — the strength is assumed, the control is the achievement. They are deliberate, physically confident and slow to escalate, which makes their occasional loss of temper memorable. Offworld they are recruited as guards, labourers and enforcers, and many find the assumption tiresome. The species has a real if underused talent for craft and mechanical work, hampered mostly by equipment built for smaller hands.
dowutin.homeworld: Dowut is a rugged world of forest and stone whose conditions favoured size and endurance. Dowutin communities there are small and widely spaced. Those who leave often do so for work, and the galaxy's persistent assumption that a Dowutin is for lifting things has shaped where most of them end up.
dowutin.language: Dowutins speak Dowutin, a language of deep rumbles that carries a long way and loses detail in transmission. They learn Basic and deliver it in the same subsonic register, which recording equipment handles poorly. A Dowutin trying to speak quietly is still audible across a room.

drabatan.name: Drabatan
drabatan.description: Drabatans hear the world as music and answer it the same way. Amphibious, loud, and relentlessly social, they turn everything from schooling to protest into song — which the Empire has discovered is harder to suppress than a pamphlet.
drabatan.physiology: Drabatans are broad amphibious humanoids with loose mottled skin, wide mouths and inflatable throat sacs that let them project sound at remarkable volume and across a wider range than most species can even hear. They begin life as aquatic larvae and grow into their bipedal form over their first year. Their hearing is exceptional, especially at the low end, and prolonged dryness is genuinely uncomfortable — a Drabatan offworld will find water regularly or suffer for it.
drabatan.society: Drabatan culture runs on song. Lessons are taught as melodies, agreements are sung rather than signed, and a community's history lives in a repertoire rather than an archive. This makes them formidable at memorisation and gives their society an oral resilience that written cultures underestimate — you cannot confiscate a song everybody already knows. They are gregarious to the point of exhausting outsiders, and disputes are settled by everyone singing about it until a position emerges. Under occupation that habit turned political fast.
drabatan.homeworld: Pipada is a world of warm freshwater swamps, its settlements built on and among the water rather than beside it, with towers rising out of the wetlands and skyhooks tethered above the wealthier districts. Imperial extraction has fouled a great deal of it, which is precisely what pushed a peaceable, noisy people toward the resistance — many Drabatans now croak battle orders with the same lungs that once sang lessons.
drabatan.language: Drabatanese is sung as much as spoken, its meaning carried in pitch and rhythm that flatten out badly in translation and disappear entirely in text. Drabatans learn Basic readily and speak it in a booming register with unexpected melodic turns, and they tend to assume a conversation is going well if it is getting louder.

drall.name: Drall
drall.description: Drall are small, dignified, fur-covered scholars from the Corellian system, with a genuine gift for organisation and a low tolerance for nonsense.
drall.physiology: Drall are short, stout and covered in dense dark fur, with small clawed hands well suited to delicate work. They are physically unimposing and entirely untroubled by that, being a species whose contributions have always been intellectual. Their sense of smell is good and their lifespans respectable, and they tend toward a deliberate, unhurried physicality.
drall.society: Drall culture prizes learning, record-keeping and reasoned argument, and treats scholarship as the highest calling — a Drall historian or archivist holds status a Drall industrialist would envy. They are formal, courteous and quietly proud, with a strong sense of propriety that outsiders read as stuffiness. Their organisational abilities make them excellent administrators, and their memories for detail make them dangerous opponents in any dispute involving records.
drall.homeworld: Drall is one of the five Corellian worlds, temperate and well managed, its cities orderly and its archives extensive. The species has been part of the system's affairs for as long as anyone has kept track, and Drall scholarship on the system's mysterious origins is the most thorough that exists — which is to say, thorough and inconclusive.
drall.language: Drall speak Drallish, precise and rather formal, and their Basic is impeccable. A Drall will correct a misstatement of fact as a matter of course, without any intention of rudeness and with reliably rude effect.

dressellian.name: Dressellian
dressellian.description: Dressellians are wrinkled, wiry guerrilla fighters who won their own world back from occupation and joined the Rebellion out of recognition. They distrust high technology and have never needed much of it.
dressellian.physiology: Dressellians are near-Human with deeply wrinkled, leathery skin and no hair, features that read as extreme age to species unfamiliar with them. They are lean, wiry and enduring, well adapted to their world's forests and capable of sustained exertion on very little. Their eyesight and hearing are keen, and they move quietly by long habit.
dressellian.society: Dressellian culture was forged by resistance: a long guerrilla campaign against occupation taught them patience, self-sufficiency and a permanent scepticism toward outside powers offering help. They favour simple, reliable equipment over sophisticated systems, having learned that complexity fails when the supply lines do. That preference is practical, not ideological, though outsiders often mistake it for primitivism. Their fighters joined the Alliance readily, recognising the shape of the problem immediately.
dressellian.homeworld: Dressel is a forested world whose people fought a protracted campaign to free it, and the terrain that made that possible is still how Dressellians think about ground. The victory is recent enough to be personal for many. Imperial attention has returned, and Dressellians treat the second occupation as a continuation rather than a surprise.
dressellian.language: Dressellians speak Dresselian, and most who deal offworld learn Basic. They speak plainly and briefly, and their scepticism shows in a habit of asking what a proposal costs before asking what it offers.

droid.name: Droid
droid.description: Droids are built, not born, and the galaxy runs on them. Legally property and practically everywhere, a droid that has escaped regular memory wipes long enough to develop a personality occupies an uncomfortable space nobody has satisfactorily resolved.

bonus_free_ranks._provenance_note: EotE CRB p.56 (B-21: prose-only "Additional Career Skills" structured; oracle-verified 6 career / 3 first-spec)

droid.physiology: There is no single droid body. Chassis are built for purpose — protocol droids in humanoid form for social work, astromechs as squat rolling toolkits, labour units as whatever shape the job demanded — and a droid's frame says more about its intended function than about its character. What they share is construction rather than biology: droids do not eat, sleep, breathe or age in any organic sense, are unaffected by poison and disease, and can be repaired rather than healed. They also cannot be moved by the Force, a fact that has saved a number of them and unsettled a number of Jedi.
droid.society: Droids have no society of their own, which is precisely the problem. Across most of the galaxy they are owned, bought, sold and wiped, and the periodic memory wipe exists specifically to prevent the accumulation of experience that produces a self. Droids that avoid it long enough develop pronounced and often difficult personalities, and the galaxy has no settled view on what that makes them. Attitudes vary enormously: the Rebel Alliance is unusually willing to treat droids as crew, many Outer Rim worlds treat them as disposable, and a droid's day-to-day existence depends almost entirely on who currently holds its restraining bolt.
droid.homeworld: A droid's origin is a factory, not a world, and the difference matters. Some come from the great Core World manufacturers with full documentation and warranties; many more are assembled from salvage in Rim workshops, carrying parts from a dozen sources and no records at all. A droid's accent, quirks and blind spots often trace back to that assembly history, and two units of the same nominal model can differ wildly depending on where they were built and what has been done to them since.
droid.language: Most droids communicate in machine languages — the binary of astromechs, the various trade dialects — and rely on translation to be understood by organics. Protocol units are the exception, built to be fluent in a vast number of languages and prone to mentioning how many. Many droids understand Basic perfectly while being physically unable to speak it, a limitation their owners frequently forget when talking in front of them.

dug.name: Dug
dug.description: Dugs are small, loud, and spectacularly aggressive for their size — quadrupeds who walk on their arms and use their legs for everything else. They have a chip on their shoulder about the galaxy, and a fair amount of history behind it.
dug.physiology: A Dug's limbs are inverted relative to most humanoids: powerful forelimbs take the weight and do the walking, while the more dexterous hind limbs handle tools, controls and gestures. The arrangement gives them startling agility and a reach that surprises opponents who assumed the height told them something. They are lean, wiry and quick, with excellent balance and a tolerance for rough conditions inherited from a hard world.
dug.society: Dug culture is combative by default — status is contested loudly, insults are a social form rather than a breach, and outsiders consistently mistake ordinary conversation for the start of a fight. Beneath that is a long grievance: the Dugs were conquered and pushed aside on their own world by better-armed neighbours, and the memory of it colours everything from their politics to their manners. They are resourceful, stubborn and disinclined to defer, which makes them difficult employees and formidable rivals. Many end up in podracing, freight or repair work, where a talent for aggressive improvisation pays.
dug.homeworld: Malastare is a world of swamp, plain and rich fuel deposits, shared uneasily between the native Dugs and the Gran who settled and eventually dominated it. That colonisation is the central wound in Dug history, and the resentment has never faded. The planet's wealth flows largely to interests that are not Dug, and its famous racing circuits are one of the few arenas where a Dug can beat everyone in public.
dug.language: Dugs speak Dugese, fast and percussive, and most learn Basic for business — delivered at volume, with a snarl the speaker does not necessarily intend. A Dug being polite still sounds like an argument to anyone who has not spent time around them.

duros.name: Duros
duros.description: Duros were flying between stars before most species had left their own atmospheres, and they have never entirely stopped. Calm, curious and comfortable in transit, they crew ships across the galaxy and treat a planet as somewhere you visit.
duros.physiology: Duros are tall and slender, with smooth blue-grey skin, no nose to speak of, a lipless mouth and large red eyes suited to the dim light of a cockpit. Their build is light rather than strong, and their reflexes and spatial reasoning are excellent — the species produces navigators and pilots at a rate no one else matches. They are long-lived and notably resistant to the disorientation of prolonged spaceflight, which is one reason their ancestors managed it so early.
duros.society: Duros culture is organised around travel, trade and the shipping lanes, and a Duros who has never left the system is a curiosity to their own people. Extended families often work a vessel together across generations, and status attaches to the routes you know and the runs you have survived. They are famously even-tempered, valuing competence and calm over displays of feeling, and their reputation for honesty in dealing is a commercial asset they guard carefully. Duros storytelling is extensive and largely concerned with journeys.
duros.homeworld: Duro itself is largely uninhabitable at the surface, its ecology wrecked by industrial exploitation long ago, and most of the population lives in orbital cities above it. The species has been comfortable in artificial habitats for so long that this is barely remarked upon at home, though visitors find the sight of an abandoned homeworld beneath a ring of thriving stations unsettling. Duros colonies and enclaves are scattered along every major hyperlane.
duros.language: Duros speak Durese, a soft language of subtle vowel shifts that non-Duros find difficult to hear correctly, let alone reproduce. It is also one of the older written languages still in daily commercial use, and Durese notation survives in navigational conventions across the galaxy. Basic is universal among them as a matter of trade.

elom.name: Elom
elom.description: Elom are squat, thick-skinned burrowers who spent most of their history underground and were assumed extinct by the species living above them. They emerged to find their world already sold.
elom.physiology: Elom are short, heavily built humanoids with tough oily skin, small eyes suited to darkness and powerful clawed hands built for digging. They tolerate cold, poor air and cramped spaces without complaint, and their sense of smell compensates for eyesight that serves poorly above ground. Their build is genuinely strong — an Elom is far harder to move than their height suggests.
elom.society: Elom culture is communal, spiritual and quietly resilient, organised around subterranean settlements and a religious tradition centred on their world's deep places. They had no idea for generations that another sentient species shared the surface, and the discovery — along with the mining concessions already granted over their heads — has shaped everything since. They are patient and slow to trust, and Elom dealings with offworld interests are conducted with a wariness that experience has fully justified.
elom.homeworld: Elom is a harsh, cold world whose valuable mineral deposits were being extracted long before anyone established that its native population existed underground. The Elom share it with the Eloms — a separate species with a confusingly similar name and a very different history. Mining interests dominate, and Elom labour has been drawn into them on terms nobody would call favourable.
elom.language: Elom speak Elomin-unrelated Elom, a low language suited to enclosed spaces and carried as much by vibration as by air. They learn Basic for dealing with the surface and the companies, and speak it sparingly and without warmth.

elomin.name: Elomin
elomin.description: Elomin see the universe as a pattern waiting to be completed, and are genuinely distressed when it will not resolve. Orderly, artistic and rigid, they are formidable until something unpredictable happens.
elomin.physiology: Elomin are tall, thin humanoids with four horns rising from the skull, angular features and pointed ears. Their build is light and their movements precise. Nothing in their physiology is remarkable except in service of their psychology — Elomin senses are ordinary, but their perception is not: they organise sensory input into pattern compulsively and find genuine satisfaction in symmetry.
elomin.society: Elomin culture is built on order. Music, architecture, mathematics and social structure are all governed by a drive toward pattern and harmony, and Elomin art is admired galaxy-wide for its formal beauty. The cost is rigidity: chaos genuinely disorients them, and an Elomin confronted with a situation that refuses to resolve into a recognisable shape can be paralysed by it. Adversaries who understand this exploit it deliberately, and Elomin military history includes at least one famous disaster caused by exactly that.
elomin.homeworld: Elom — shared, confusingly, with the unrelated Elom species — is cold and mineral-rich, its Elomin cities built to designs of considerable formal elegance above the deposits the galaxy actually wants. The two species' shared name and shared planet have caused centuries of outside confusion that neither has much interest in resolving.
elomin.language: Elomin speak Elomin, a language of strict grammatical symmetry in which a malformed sentence is not merely wrong but unpleasant. They speak Basic correctly and find its irregularity mildly distressing, which is visible to anyone paying attention.

ewok.name: Ewok
ewok.description: Ewoks are small, furred forest-dwellers from a moon most of the galaxy could not name, and they have a habit of defeating opponents who assumed the fur meant harmless.

options.name: One Rank in Stealth
options.description: Ewoks may begin the game with one rank in Stealth.

options.name: One Rank in Survival
options.description: Ewoks may begin the game with one rank in Survival.

special_abilities.name: Heightened Smell
special_abilities.description: Ewoks may remove all [SE] imposed due to concealment against a target that is within Short Range.

special_abilities.name: Reduced Silouette
special_abilities.description: Ewoks have a Silhouette of 0.

ewok.physiology: Ewoks stand about a metre tall, covered in fur ranging from brown through grey to rare reddish and near-white shades. They are agile climbers with excellent night vision and hearing, and their small size makes them easy to overlook — a fact they exploit deliberately. They are stronger than they look, sure-footed in the canopy, and capable of moving through dense forest in complete silence.
ewok.society: Ewok society is tribal, spiritual and organised around the village, with shamans, chiefs and elaborate ceremony governing daily life. They are curious about outsiders and quick to include those who prove trustworthy, and their technology — bows, gliders, traps, deadfalls — is simple and used with real ingenuity. Their music, drums and carved totems mark status and history. Underestimating them is a tradition among visitors and has ended badly more than once.
ewok.homeworld: The forest moon of Endor is dense woodland dominated by enormous trees, in whose canopies Ewok villages are built on platforms and connected by walkways. The forest floor is dangerous, and Ewoks navigate the vertical world far better than the horizontal one. Imperial construction on the moon brought industry, garrisons and a great deal of unwelcome attention.
ewok.language: Ewoks speak Ewokese, a language of yelps and chatter that most species find unintelligible and a few learn with effort. They understand more Basic than they let on, and their apparent incomprehension has been a useful defensive posture more than once.

falleen.name: Falleen
falleen.description: Falleen are elegant, reptilian and quietly formidable — a species whose pheromones nudge those around them toward agreement, and who have never seen a reason to mention it.
falleen.physiology: Falleen are scaled humanoids with a fine crest running the length of the skull, skin in greens and browns that shifts subtly with mood, and a build both graceful and strong. They are long-lived. Their defining trait is chemical: Falleen produce pheromones that make others more receptive to them, an effect strong enough to shade a negotiation and subtle enough to be deniable. Not every species is susceptible, and Falleen are careful about which are.
falleen.society: Falleen culture is aristocratic, mannered and intensely conscious of status, conducting its rivalries through etiquette and implication rather than confrontation. Emotional display is regarded as a failure of breeding. Their reputation for manipulation is well earned in the sense that manipulation is the accepted medium of Falleen politics, and it is understood on all sides as the game being played. Offworld, Falleen turn up in commerce, crime and diplomacy — often all three, and rarely at the bottom of any of them.
falleen.homeworld: Falleen is a temperate world of forest and coast, its society ordered by noble houses that predate galactic contact. Imperial attention has been heavy-handed and, in one notorious episode, catastrophic — a sterilisation of a populated region to contain an experiment gone wrong. That atrocity radicalised a species not otherwise inclined to open resistance, and it is not forgotten.
falleen.language: Falleen speak Falleen, a fluid language of soft consonants and precise honorifics that encode relative status in nearly every sentence. They speak Basic beautifully and with obvious deliberation, and a Falleen who chooses a blunt word has chosen it.

farghul.name: Farghul
farghul.description: Farghul are feline, charming and famously light-fingered — a species whose reputation as thieves is well earned and which they have largely stopped bothering to deny.

options.name: One Rank in Deception
options.description: Farghul may begin the game with one rank in Deception.

options.name: One Rank in Skulduggery
options.description: Farghul may begin the game with one rank in Skulduggery.

farghul.physiology: Farghul are furred feline humanoids with prehensile tails, retractable claws and coats in tawny and striped patterns. They are agile, quick-fingered and physically capable, with the balance and reflexes their tails imply. Their whiskers and hearing are keen, and they move quietly without appearing to try.
farghul.society: Farghul culture treats guile as a virtue and outright theft as a respectable application of it — a well-executed swindle is admired, a clumsy one mocked, and honesty regarded as a specialised tool rather than a default. They are sociable, persuasive and genuinely warm company, which is precisely what makes them effective. Family groups are close and cover for each other reflexively. Offworld their reputation precedes them, which Farghul treat as a professional handicap and an occasional convenience.
farghul.homeworld: Farrfin is a temperate world whose people took to galactic commerce early and enthusiastically, spreading widely along the trade lanes. The species' reputation has meant persistent official attention wherever they settle in numbers, and Farghul communities are practised at being unremarkable when it matters.
farghul.language: Farghul speak Farghul, a purring language with a large vocabulary for persuasion and evasion, and they learn other languages easily — a Farghul working a mark will usually do it in the mark's own tongue and accent.

gamorrean.name: Gamorrean
gamorrean.description: Gamorreans are porcine, powerfully built and hired everywhere as muscle. The galaxy assumes they are stupid; the galaxy is mostly reacting to the fact that they do not speak Basic.

special_abilities.name: Savage Warrior
special_abilities.description: When making a Brawl or Melee check, Gamorreans add the Vicious 1 quality to their weapons. If the weapon already has the Vicious quality, increase the listed value by one.

gamorrean.physiology: Gamorreans are heavy-set green-skinned humanoids with tusks, small eyes and enormous physical strength. They are built for close combat and tolerate injury well, with thick hide and dense musculature. Their vocal apparatus cannot produce Basic at all, which is the single fact most responsible for their reputation — a Gamorrean understanding a conversation perfectly well and unable to join it looks, to the careless, like incomprehension.
gamorrean.society: Gamorrean society is clan-based, matriarchal in its economics and violently competitive in its politics: the sows manage land, farming and trade while the boars fight, which they do enthusiastically and constantly. War is seasonal and ritualised at home, and a boar's standing is built on it. Offworld they hire out as guards and enforcers, which suits the skills and reinforces the stereotype. Their technological level at home is modest by choice as much as circumstance.
gamorrean.homeworld: Gamorr is a lush jungle world whose clans have fought each other for as long as anyone has recorded, in wars that function as much as social structure as conflict. Offworld recruiters have drawn heavily from that population for generations, and a Gamorrean encountered in Hutt space is usually somebody's hired muscle several steps from home.
gamorrean.language: Gamorreans speak Gamorrese, a language of grunts and squeals their anatomy is built for. They can learn to understand Basic perfectly and can never speak it, so they rely on droid translators or on employers who bother to learn. Those who do generally find the Gamorrean they hired is sharper than advertised.

gand.name: Gand
gand.description: Gands are ammonia-breathing insectoids from a world most species cannot survive, and their findsmen are among the galaxy's most unnerving hunters — mystics who locate prey by ritual and are almost never wrong.

options.name: Has Lungs
options._provenance: B-22 (ruling b22-option-mechanics): the +10 XP, respirator, and oxygen Rating 8 were prose-only; structured. Source: Edge of the Empire Core Rulebook, Gand species entry.

gand.physiology: Gands are chitinous humanoids with compound eyes and hard exoskeletal plating, and they come in two broad varieties: those with lungs and those without. The lungless draw sustenance directly from ammonia through their exoskeleton and require no food or water at all, while their lunged kin breathe ammonia conventionally. Neither can tolerate an oxygen atmosphere without a respirator, which is why an offworld Gand is always masked. The exoskeleton regenerates over time, and Gands are considerably tougher than their size suggests.
gand.society: Gand culture is built on self-effacement.
