A Gand does not use a personal name until it has been earned, referring to itself in the third person as 'Gand' until deeds justify more, and losing that right again through failure or dishonour is a real and dreaded punishment. The findsmen are the species' religious hunters, using rituals involving mists and portents to locate their quarry — a practice outsiders dismiss as superstition right up until it works. Gand society is intensely communal and deeply uninterested in the opinions of other species.
gand.homeworld: Gand is shrouded in dense ammonia fog, its surface visible only in patches and its interior largely unexplored by outsiders. The atmosphere that makes it lethal to most visitors is what the Gands are built for, and they have made very little effort to accommodate anyone else. What industry exists is closely held, and the planet's mystic traditions are treated by its people as a practical technology rather than a faith.
gand.language: Gands speak Gand, a language of clicks and rasps produced by the exoskeleton as much as by any vocal apparatus. Its grammar carries the species' self-effacement structurally: constructions that would put the speaker at the centre of a sentence are avoided outright. Gands who learn Basic often carry that habit across, which is why one may describe its own actions as though narrating someone else's.

gank.name: Gank
gank.description: Ganks are heavily cyberised killers in the Hutts' employ, and almost nobody has seen what one looks like underneath. The mystery is deliberate and the reputation is earned.
gank.physiology: What a Gank is beneath the augmentation is genuinely uncertain to outsiders — the species is so extensively cybernetic that an unmodified Gank is a rarity even among their own. Standard modifications include reinforced skeletons, enhanced reflexes, integrated weaponry and sensory implants, all worn under distinctive armour and helmets that are effectively never removed in company. The result is fast, durable and difficult to disable by conventional means.
gank.society: Gank culture is opaque by design. They work for the Hutts in numbers, as killers and enforcers, and the arrangement is old enough to be structural rather than contractual. Among themselves they are said to have a strong code around augmentation and obligation; outside, they volunteer nothing. That silence is a professional asset — a Gank's reputation does the work that explanation would only weaken. The galaxy's willingness to believe the worst about them is treated as a convenience.
gank.homeworld: Gank origins are disputed even among people who deal with them regularly, and the species has made no effort to clarify. What is known is that their long service in Hutt space has scattered them across it thoroughly, and that Ganks encountered offworld are almost always working. The homeworld question is one they decline to discuss.
gank.language: Ganks speak Gank, filtered through helmet vocoders into a flat mechanical rasp. Most understand Basic and Huttese; whether they enjoy speaking either is unclear, since a Gank rarely says more than the situation strictly requires.

geonosian.name: Geonosian
geonosian.description: Geonosians build. Hive-organised, insectoid and industrious to a fault, they turned their arid world into a foundry for the Separatist war machine — and were exterminated for it once the Empire had what it needed.
geonosian.physiology: Geonosians are chitinous insectoids with elongated skulls, thin limbs and a hard exoskeleton. The caste divide is physical: winged drones are slighter and capable of flight, while wingless warrior castes are heavier and built for labour and combat. Their eyes handle the glare of an open desert well, and their tolerance for heat and dust is high. Sound and pheromone both carry meaning among them, and a hive's ambient noise is itself a kind of ongoing conversation.
geonosian.society: Geonosian society is a rigid hive, organised by caste from birth and directed by an aristocracy that treats the drone population as a resource rather than a citizenry. Individual ambition barely registers as a concept; a Geonosian's worth is what the hive needed of them. Their industrial output is extraordinary — droid foundries, weapon works, whole armies fabricated to order — and their architecture, all spires and catacombs, reflects the same collective patience. The Empire's sterilisation of the planet after the war ended that civilisation almost completely, and the few Geonosians encountered now are survivors, exiles, or the last of a hive.
geonosian.homeworld: Geonosis is a harsh red desert world of rock spires and wind-scoured plains, its cities burrowed into towering hives that look natural until you notice the geometry. Beneath the surface lie the foundries that armed the Confederacy. After the war the Empire scoured it and built in orbit, and what remains below is largely ruin, tomb, and salvage worth dying for.
geonosian.language: Geonosian is a clicking, buzzing language produced partly by the throat and partly by wing and carapace, and almost impossible for other species to speak. Pheromonal signals carry a further layer that non-Geonosians cannot perceive at all. Those who deal with outsiders use translation or a laboured Basic, and a Geonosian speaking Basic sounds like it costs effort, because it does.

gigoran.name: Gigoran
gigoran.description: Gigorans are enormous, white-furred and famously gentle — labourers whose strength gets them hired and whose good nature gets them exploited. Crossing one takes real effort, and is a mistake worth avoiding.
gigoran.physiology: Gigorans are massive shaggy primates, taller and heavier than a Wookiee, covered in pale fur that grows long enough over the eyes to need clearing. Their strength is prodigious and their endurance greater still — a Gigoran works a shift that would break most species and does it again the next day. They are adapted to cold, which makes warm worlds a genuine trial, and their eyes handle snow-glare far better than they handle sun.
gigoran.society: Gigoran culture prizes patience, cooperation and steady effort, and dislikes conflict to a degree other species read as timidity right up until it stops being true. They are curious about everything offworld, delighted by novelty, and easy to like. That combination — enormous, capable, agreeable and far from home — has made them a target for labour contractors and outright slavers, and Gigoran communities offworld are frequently indentured. Those who find good crews stay with them for life and treat the arrangement as family.
gigoran.homeworld: Gigor is a cold, rocky, mountainous world where survival demanded cooperation and the fur that looks so distinctive offworld is simply necessary. Life there is hard and communal. Offworld recruitment has drawn generations away, and the flow rarely reverses; a Gigoran who leaves usually does not go back, which has left the homeworld older and quieter than it was.
gigoran.language: Gigorans speak a language of low rumbles and drawn-out vocalisations that carry a long way in mountain air and sit at the bottom edge of most species' hearing. They understand Basic well but produce it slowly and with difficulty, which gets them mistaken for dim by people who should know better.

givin.name: Givin
givin.description: Givin have skull-like faces, mathematical minds, and bodies sealed well enough to survive vacuum. They calculate constantly, greet each other with equations, and find small talk genuinely baffling.

special_abilities.name: Sealed Exoskeleton
special_abilities.description: Given are immune to the effects of vacuum or suffocation.

givin.physiology: Givin have hardened exoskeletons and gaunt skull-like faces with dark eye sockets — an appearance other species find unsettling and Givin find unremarkable. Their bodies seal against vacuum, letting them survive unprotected exposure for a considerable period, an adaptation to a homeworld whose orbit produces extreme conditions. Their joints are exposed and vulnerable, and their build is light.
givin.society: Givin culture is mathematical to a degree other species struggle to credit: greetings take the form of equations, social standing tracks computational ability, and a Givin's answer to almost any question begins with a calculation. Their homeworld's chaotic orbital mechanics made predicting tides and conditions a survival skill, and the culture grew from that necessity into something close to a religion. They are superb navigators, engineers and shipwrights, and their difficulty with imprecision makes negotiation with them exact and slow.
givin.homeworld: Yag'Dhul sits in a complex gravitational arrangement that produces violent and irregular tidal effects, and Givin survival there has always depended on calculating them correctly. Their cities are sealed and their infrastructure built to withstand conditions that arrive on schedules only they can compute. The species' shipyards are well regarded and its people rarely leave.
givin.language: Givin speak Givin, dense with mathematical construction, and their Basic is grammatically exact and conversationally strange. A Givin asked how they are will frequently supply a figure.

gossam.name: Gossam
gossam.description: Gossams are small, long-necked and sharply commercial — the species behind the Commerce Guild, whose corporate ambitions considerably outran their physical stature.
gossam.physiology: Gossams are short, slender humanoids with long necks, small heads and large dark eyes. They are physically unimposing, quick rather than strong, and inclined to compensate with elaborate clothing that signals status precisely. Their eyesight is good and their fine motor control excellent. Nothing about them suggests a species that once helped run a war, which is a point Gossams have made use of.
gossam.society: Gossam culture is corporate to its foundations, organising status by commercial position and treating business as the natural medium of ambition. The Commerce Guild grew from that instinct and carried Gossam influence into galactic politics — and then into the Separatist alliance, which ended badly for everyone involved and worst for the species that had been most visible. Post-war Gossams are commercially capable, politically cautious, and acutely conscious that their reputation preceded their surrender.
gossam.homeworld: Castell is a densely developed world of corporate towers and layered urban sprawl, home to the Commerce Guild's operations and to a population whose fortunes rise and fall with them. Imperial administration has curtailed Gossam commercial autonomy substantially while keeping the productive parts running, an arrangement the Gossams find humiliating and survivable.
gossam.language: Gossams speak Gossam, a rapid language with an extensive vocabulary for obligation, credit and standing. They speak Basic fluently as a matter of trade and use it with careful courtesy — a Gossam's politeness scales precisely with their assessment of your usefulness.

gotal.name: Gotal
gotal.description: Gotals read emotion directly through the cone-shaped horns on their heads, which makes them exceptional judges of character and constant sufferers in crowds. Most keep to quiet places for good reason.
gotal.physiology: Gotals are furred humanoids with two prominent head-cones that sense electromagnetic and emotional fields — they perceive the feelings of those around them as a directly sensed phenomenon rather than an inference. That sense is powerful and unfiltered: a crowded spaceport is genuinely painful, droids and heavy machinery produce interference that reads as static, and a Gotal in a busy environment is enduring it. Their eyesight is poor in bright light, and their fur suits a cold world.
gotal.society: Gotal culture is built around a sense nobody else has, which makes it difficult to explain and easy to misread. Deception within the species is nearly impossible, so social life is direct to the point of bluntness and privacy is a matter of physical distance. They are valued offworld as mediators, interrogators and judges of intent, and are frequently hired by people who want a lie detector and do not much care what it costs the detector. Many prefer solitary work for the simple relief of it.
gotal.homeworld: Antar 4 is a cold moon of forest and tundra, its scattered settlements reflecting a species that finds crowding physically unpleasant. Its history includes a bitter association with a rebellion against the Empire and a subsequent reprisal that Gotals have not forgotten. Offworld communities tend to cluster at the quieter edges of busy places.
gotal.language: Gotals speak Gotal, and a great deal of what passes between them is not spoken at all — the emotional sense carries what other species would need words for. Their Basic is functional and unadorned, and a Gotal will often answer what you meant rather than what you said, which unsettles people who did not realise the difference showed.

gran.name: Gran
gran.description: Gran see the world through three eyes and, they will tell you, more clearly than anyone. A pacifist and communal people by tradition, they have been scattered widely enough that the tradition does not always survive the journey.
gran.physiology: The Gran's three eyes are the obvious feature, mounted on short stalks and giving exceptional depth perception and a very wide field of view — they see into the infrared and can judge distance with a precision that makes them fine marksmen, an irony their pacifists find uncomfortable. They are stocky, goat-descended herbivores with prominent snouts and a strong sense of smell, and their hearing is comparatively poor. Gran perceive colour in a far broader range than most species, and their art is largely incomprehensible to anyone else.
gran.society: Traditional Gran society is communal, consensus-driven and genuinely pacifist, organising life around the group and treating individual ambition with suspicion. That is the ideal; the reality across the wider galaxy is more varied. Gran emigrants, particularly those who ended up in Hutt space, have produced a substantial criminal population that their homeworld regards with embarrassment and their neighbours regard as typical. Both versions of the species are real, and a Gran encountered offworld could be either.
gran.homeworld: Kinyen is a temperate, prosperous agricultural world that has kept itself deliberately clear of galactic conflict for centuries, trading food and staying quiet. Its people take considerable pride in that record. Gran colonies elsewhere — Malastare most notably — have had far rougher histories and have shaped the species' offworld reputation more than Kinyen ever did.
gran.language: Gran speak Gran, a language rich in terms for colour and shade that Basic simply cannot render, which is why Gran translations of their own poetry are considered failures by the Gran. Most learn Basic readily for trade, and speak it in a distinctive bleating register that other species find either charming or grating with little middle ground.

gungan.name: Gungan
gungan.description: Gungans built a civilisation of luminous bubble-cities under Naboo's lakes and spent centuries pretending their surface neighbours did not exist. Amphibious, proud and easily underestimated, they field an army that has surprised better-equipped opponents.
gungan.physiology: Gungans are tall amphibious humanoids with long ears, elongated skulls and eyes set on short stalks that can move independently. They are equally capable in water and on land, with powerful legs, excellent swimming ability and the capacity to remain submerged for extended periods. Their skin needs moisture, and a Gungan far from water gets uncomfortable in ways they will mention. Their reflexes are quick and their tolerance for pressure suits them to considerable depths.
gungan.society: Gungan society is hierarchical and ceremonious, governed by councils and a Boss whose authority is real but bounded by loud collective argument. Honour, obligation and public loyalty matter enormously, and banishment is the traditional grave punishment. Their long estrangement from Naboo's human settlers — each side convinced of the other's arrogance — ended only under invasion, and the alliance that followed remains a point of pride on both sides and awkwardness on neither. Gungan military tradition is genuine, organised, and built around shield technology other species find surprisingly sophisticated.
gungan.homeworld: Naboo's lakes and swamps hold the Gungan cities: hydrostatic bubbles glowing in the deep water, connected by tunnel and current, invisible from the surface world that shares the planet. The arrangement let two civilisations occupy one world for generations while barely acknowledging each other. Imperial attention has fallen mainly on the surface, which has left the Gungans comparatively undisturbed and quietly useful to people who need somewhere to disappear.
gungan.language: Gungans speak Gungan Basic, a distinctive dialect with its own grammar and vocabulary that other Basic speakers understand roughly and mock frequently. That mockery has consequences: a Gungan being talked down to on account of their speech is being underestimated by someone who has not thought it through.

harch.name: Harch
harch.description: Six-armed arachnid near-humans of Secundus Ando: exacting, aggressive, and long-lived. Traditionally solitary fortune-seekers, the Harch were united toward war and empire by their ruling nests, and their belligerence found a natural home among the Separatists after the Republic thwarted their ambitions.

herglic.name: Herglic
herglic.description: Herglics are enormous cetacean humanoids with a talent for trade and a catastrophic weakness for gambling. They were flying between stars before most species, and they have been losing money at it ever since.
herglic.physiology: Herglics are massive, broad, hairless humanoids descended from aquatic stock, with smooth blue-black skin and a blowhole on the crown. They are enormously strong and heavy, comfortable in water, and clumsy in confined spaces built for smaller species. Their bulk makes standard seating, doorways and vehicles a constant low-grade problem, which they endure with practised patience.
herglic.society: Herglic culture is mercantile and social, built around trade consortia and an enthusiasm for games of chance that runs from a harmless national pastime to a genuine species-wide vulnerability. Gambling debts have cost Herglic families fortunes and occasionally their independence, and the Hutts in particular have made a business of it. They are gregarious, generous and hard to offend, and their commercial networks are extensive and old.
herglic.homeworld: Giju is an ocean world whose Herglic population industrialised early and heavily, to the significant cost of the seas they came from. They were among the first species in their region to achieve hyperspace travel, which gave them a commercial head start they have spent centuries slowly gambling away.
herglic.language: Herglics speak Herglic, a booming language that carries underwater and overwhelms small rooms. They learn Basic readily and speak it loudly, and a Herglic attempting discretion is a memorable sight.

human.name: Human
human.description: Humans are everywhere. They are the galaxy's most numerous and most widely spread species, found in every role from moisture farmer to Emperor, and the standard against which most other species are casually measured — usually by Humans.
human.physiology: Humans are mammalian bipeds of unremarkable build, which is rather the point: they run neither especially fast nor especially long, see a narrow band of light, and hear a narrow band of sound. What they lack in specialisation they make up for in tolerance. A Human can eat almost anything organic, endure a wide span of temperature and pressure, and adapt to gravity well outside their ancestral norm. Lifespans run around a standard century, and the species reaches maturity slowly enough that culture, rather than instinct, does most of the teaching.
human.society: There is no single Human society, and any attempt to describe one collapses immediately. Humans have built theocracies, corporate holdings, hereditary monarchies, brutal autocracies and functioning democracies, often on neighbouring worlds and occasionally on the same one. What travels with them is a restless appetite for organisation: Humans arrive, form institutions, and argue about them. The Empire is the current and ugliest expression of that habit, and its human-centric doctrine has made the species' name a grievance across the Outer Rim — resented in places no Human has ever visited.
human.homeworld: Humans no longer agree on where they began. Coruscant claims the honour and has the records to argue it, but Human populations are so old and so widely seeded that dozens of worlds hold plausible traditions of their own. In practice the question is academic: Humans have been a spacefaring species for so long that their homeworld is wherever a given family has been for the last few generations, whether that is a Core ecumenopolis, a Rim mining colony, or a freighter that has not made planetfall in a year.
human.language: Humans speak Basic, and Basic is the galaxy's common tongue largely because Humans went everywhere and insisted on it. Regional dialects run deep enough that a Corellian and a Coruscanti can misunderstand each other in a bar, and many Human worlds keep a local language alongside Basic for use at home. Most Humans read and write it, and a great many never learn a second language at all — an assumption other species find revealing.

hutt.name: Hutt
hutt.description: Hutts are enormous, long-lived, and utterly convinced of their own centrality. They run the galaxy's criminal economy from behind layers of intermediaries, and they have outlasted every government that promised to deal with them.
hutt.physiology: Hutts are massive gastropods, moving by muscular contraction of the broad tail, with thick hides, small arms and enormous mouths. They are far tougher than their sluggishness suggests: the hide resists blaster fire, the body tolerates poisons that would kill most species, and they regenerate from injury slowly but reliably. They live for centuries — a Hutt in its second century is barely established — and they are hermaphroditic, carrying young in a brood pouch. Size increases throughout life, and a genuinely old Hutt is immense.
hutt.society: Hutt society is organised into kajidics — clan-cartels that hold territory, run enterprises and feud with each other in ways that occasionally spill into open war. Status is measured in wealth and influence, cruelty is a legitimate business instrument, and every relationship is understood as a transaction with terms. Hutts almost never do their own work; the whole apparatus of enforcers, bounty hunters, smugglers and slavers exists to keep a Hutt physically distant from consequence. Their contempt for other species is genuine, ancient and rarely disguised.
hutt.homeworld: Nal Hutta — 'Glorious Jewel' — was a fertile world before the Hutts stripped and fouled it into swamp and industrial ruin, and they regard that transformation as evidence of enterprise. Its moon Nar Shaddaa is the real capital of Hutt influence: a vertical smugglers' city where anything is available and no authority reaches far. Hutt space extends well beyond both, held by commerce and threat rather than by fleets.
hutt.language: Huttese is the trade tongue of the Outer Rim's underworld, spoken far beyond the species that named it — a spacer who works the Rim without any Huttese is a spacer who gets cheated. Hutts themselves understand Basic perfectly well and frequently pretend otherwise, requiring visitors to speak Huttese or bring a droid, which establishes who is accommodating whom.

iakaru.name: Iakaru
iakaru.description: Iakaru are flightless avians with a talent for languages and an instinct for company. Their homeworld was made a showpiece for Imperial tourism, and they have been performing for outsiders — and quietly resenting it — ever since.
iakaru.physiology: Iakaru are slender bipedal avians with vestigial wings, long necks and vivid plumage that varies enormously between individuals and shifts with mood and season. They cannot fly, but they are fast on the ground and well balanced, with excellent colour vision and a vocal apparatus of unusual range — an Iakaru can reproduce sounds and accents with uncanny fidelity, which is the foundation of their reputation as linguists.
iakaru.society: Iakaru culture is intensely social and built around hospitality: guests are honoured, conversation is an art, and an Iakaru left alone for long grows genuinely unwell. That openness made them ideal hosts when the Empire decided their world would be a leisure destination, and the tourism economy has reshaped their society around serving visitors. The younger generation increasingly resents the arrangement — the plumage, the performances, the charm all commodified — and Iakaru turn up in the Rebellion more often than their placid reputation suggests.
iakaru.homeworld: Iakar was remade for visitors. Its natural landscapes are beautiful and now heavily managed, its cities rebuilt around resorts and viewing routes, and much of the population employed in hospitality one way or another. The Empire values it as a destination and polices it as an asset, which means the resentment stays quiet and organised rather than loud.
iakaru.language: Iakaru speak Iakaru, a musical language of trills and tonal shifts that pairs naturally with their vocal range. What they are known for, though, is everyone else's languages: an Iakaru who has heard a dialect can generally reproduce it, accent and all, which makes them superb interpreters and unnervingly good mimics.

iktotchi.name: Iktotchi
iktotchi.description: Iktotchi see what is coming. Their precognition is a species trait rather than a Force gift, and it makes them formidable pilots and slightly unnerving company.
iktotchi.physiology: Iktotchi are red-skinned humanoids with a pair of thick horns curving down from the skull past the jaw — horns that regrow if lost. Their skin is tough enough to shrug off the abrasive winds of their homeworld. The species is naturally precognitive to a limited degree, receiving impressions of imminent events, and that sense is sharpest close to home and degrades with distance. It is not the Force, though Force-sensitive Iktotchi are far from rare.
iktotchi.society: Iktotchi culture is disciplined, understated and comfortable with silence. When a substantial share of your neighbours can sense what you are about to do, social life adjusts: directness is normal, small deception is pointless, and privacy is granted deliberately rather than assumed. They are famously stoic — an Iktotchi reacting visibly to something has been genuinely surprised, which is rare. The species produced a notable line of Jedi, whose natural foresight paired well with the Order's training.
iktotchi.homeworld: Iktotch is a moon of harsh terrain and ferocious, constant winds, orbiting the gas giant Iktotchon. The conditions shaped both the species' hide and its temperament — endurance is unremarkable there. Iktotchi who leave often speak of the way the precognitive sense thins as they travel, which some find a relief and most find like losing a limb.
iktotchi.language: Iktotchi speak Iktotchese, spare and low, with a grammar that leaves a great deal unsaid on the assumption the listener has already caught it. They speak Basic competently and briefly. An Iktotchi answering a question before it is fully asked is not being rude; they simply heard the end of it early.

ishi_tib.name: Ishi Tib
ishi_tib.description: Ishi Tib are amphibious, beaked and relentlessly organised — administrators and planners whose talent for systems has made them valued far beyond the reefs they came from.
ishi_tib.physiology: Ishi Tib are green-skinned amphibians with stalked eyes and a hard beak capable of cracking shellfish and, if pressed, doing real damage in a fight. They evolved from reef-dwelling fish and must return to salt water regularly — an Ishi Tib away from it for too long becomes genuinely unwell, and offworld communities cluster around whatever water can be arranged. Their vision is excellent and independently directed, giving them a wide field of view.
ishi_tib.society: Ishi Tib culture is organised to a degree other species find exhausting: planning is a civic virtue, disorder is distressing, and an Ishi Tib presented with an inefficient system will fix it whether or not anyone asked. That temperament makes them superb administrators, logisticians and bureaucrats, and it also makes them intolerant of improvisation. They are ecologically minded, having learned the hard way what overharvesting does to a reef, and their planning horizons run in generations rather than years.
ishi_tib.homeworld: Tibrin is an ocean world of shallow reefs and coastal platform cities, its population historically living on and above the water it depends on. Its ecology has been managed carefully for a long time, which the Ishi Tib regard as the obvious way to treat a finite thing. Offworld demand for their organisational skills has drawn many away, and the ones who leave usually intend to return.
ishi_tib.language: Ishi Tib speak Tibranese, clicking and precise, produced partly by the beak. They learn Basic readily and use it with exact grammar and a faint air of correcting the room. An Ishi Tib's habit of restating a plan back to you is not doubt; it is how they confirm.

ithorian.name: Ithorian
ithorian.description: Ithorians are gentle, deliberate and deeply committed to the living world — a species of herders and gardeners who left their planet's surface largely alone and took to the sky instead. Their word carries weight wherever ecology is taken seriously.
ithorian.physiology: An Ithorian's head curves forward on a long neck in the shape that earned the species its unkind nickname, with eyes set to either side and two mouths, one on each side of the neck. Those paired mouths produce a stereo speech that non-Ithorians cannot reproduce and find striking to hear. They are tall, slow-moving and physically strong, with a lifespan well beyond a Human's, and their sense of smell is acute enough to matter in their agricultural work.
ithorian.society: Ithorian culture is built around the Mother Jungle, a belief system that treats the living world as sacred and its exploitation as violence. Communities live aboard enormous floating herd ships that hover above the surface, descending rarely and taking little, and the great trading arrangements Ithorians run are conducted with an eye to what a world can spare. Decisions are made by long collective discussion, and Ithorian herbalists and agriculturalists are sought across the galaxy. Those who leave to work offworld generally do so as a form of service rather than adventure.
ithorian.homeworld: Ithor is a lush world whose surface the species has deliberately declined to settle, leaving it to grow while they live above it. The herd cities drift over the jungle canopy, and formal descent to the surface is a ceremonial matter rather than a daily one. The Empire's interest in the planet's biological wealth has put that arrangement under a pressure it was never designed to withstand.
ithorian.language: Ithorese is spoken through both mouths at once, producing overlapping harmonic phrases that carry meaning in the interval between them as much as in the words. No other species can speak it properly, and most Ithorians use Basic offworld — delivered in the same doubled voice, which unsettles listeners who were not expecting it.

jawa.name: Jawa
jawa.description: Jawas are small, robed scavengers who see everything on Tatooine and sell most of it. Nobody has had a straight look at one, and they intend to keep it that way.

special_abilities.name: Desert Dweller
special_abilities.description: Jawas may remove one [SE] imposed due to arid or hot environmental conditions.

special_abilities.name: Reduced Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Jawas have a Silhouette of 0.

jawa.physiology: Jawas are diminutive humanoids, entirely concealed beneath heavy robes with only glowing eyes visible — the covering is protection against the desert sun and against dehydration, and removing it in company is not done. Beneath it they are small, thin and rodent-like, with dry-adapted physiology that conserves water ruthlessly. Their eyes see well in the dim interiors of their crawlers and in the dark.
jawa.society: Jawa culture is built on scavenging and trade, organised into clans that roam the desert in enormous sandcrawlers, collecting, repairing and selling technology of every provenance. Their commercial reputation is poor and largely deserved — a Jawa repair is often a Jawa deferral — but their technical scavenging skill is genuine. Clan gatherings for trade and marriage arrangements are the fixed points of the year. They are wary of outsiders, communicate rapidly among themselves, and are almost never encountered alone.
jawa.homeworld: Tatooine's deserts are lethal to most species and merely difficult for Jawas, who navigate them in crawlers that double as home, workshop and shop floor. They share the world uneasily with moisture farmers, Tusken Raiders and whatever the Hutts are running. The scarcity that defines the planet defines them.
jawa.language: Jawas speak Jawaese, delivered at high speed and accompanied by a scent-based component that other species cannot detect — a Jawa trade conversation carries information nobody else is receiving. They pick up enough Basic and Huttese to deal, and their haggling is conducted in whatever gets the price up.

kalleran.name: Kalleran
kalleran.description: Kallerans are semi-amphibious, antennaed and blunt to a fault, from an isolated world that too many outside interests have taken an interest in. They value self-reliance and say so.
kalleran.physiology: Kallerans descend from semi-amphibious stock, with loose greenish skin, prominent facial features and a pair of antennae that move expressively during conversation — a Kalleran's antennae give away their mood well before their words do. They are comfortable in and around water, physically sturdy, and adapted to a climate that swings hard between seasons.
kalleran.society: Kalleran culture prizes self-sufficiency and treats dependence as a genuine failing, which produces capable, resourceful people and a certain bluntness about anyone perceived as dead weight. That directness costs them friends offworld. Their traditional architecture and craft are distinctive and durable, built with stone and now duracrete against a demanding climate. Their world's fragmented politics — never unified under a single authority — reflects a species disinclined to be governed by anyone, including each other.
kalleran.homeworld: Kaller is an isolated Outer Rim world of forests and hard weather, valuable enough in resources to attract outside interest and divided enough politically to make resisting it difficult. No single alliance has ever governed it, which has left it perpetually negotiated over. Imperial presence is heavy and locally resented.
kalleran.language: Kallerans speak Kalleran, accompanied by antenna movement that carries a substantial part of the meaning. They learn Basic capably and use it directly — a Kalleran will tell you your plan is poor before telling you why, which is intended as efficiency.

kaminoan.name: Kaminoan
kaminoan.description: Kaminoans are the galaxy's foremost cloners, and they regard that work the way an artist regards a commission. Tall, pale and unfailingly courteous, they discuss the manufacture of soldiers in the tone of a tailor discussing cloth.
kaminoan.physiology: Kaminoans are extremely tall and slender, with long necks, small heads and large dark eyes suited to their homeworld's perpetual overcast. Their skin is pale and smooth, their movements slow and precise. Their eyes perceive a spectrum outside most species' range, which is why Kaminoan interiors look stark and colourless to visitors and are nothing of the kind to their occupants. They are physically frail by most standards and have never needed to be otherwise.
kaminoan.society: Kaminoan culture is built on genetic perfectionism, applied first to themselves and then, profitably, to everyone else. Deviation is edited out, flaws are not tolerated, and a long history of self-directed selection has produced a species with very little variation and very firm opinions about what variation means. They are scrupulously polite, entirely amoral in commercial terms, and capable of describing an army's production schedule without once acknowledging that its units are people. Contracts are sacred; the purposes they serve are the client's business.
kaminoan.homeworld: Kamino is an ocean world under permanent storm, its cities raised on stilts above the waves — white, curved, immaculate, and lit against a sky that never clears. The rising seas drowned the Kaminoans' original landmass long ago, and the response was characteristic: they rebuilt above it and edited themselves to suit. Since the Empire dispensed with their services the cities have grown quieter and considerably less well funded.
kaminoan.language: Kaminoan is soft, high and precise, with a grammar full of qualifications and exactness that mirrors how its speakers think. They learn Basic readily and speak it with elaborate courtesy, and their habit of naming unpleasant things in perfectly measured language is one of the more unsettling things about dealing with them.

karkarodon.name: Karkarodon
karkarodon.description: Aquatic predators who once pursued their own interests with little thought for homeworld or identity. Many were drawn to the Separatist cause by the promise of a Karkarodon empire — even as their world is remade into an aquatic factory of war, and much of the species resents the loss of sovereignty.

kel_dor.name: Kel Dor
kel_dor.description: Kel Dor cannot breathe the air most of the galaxy takes for granted, and go masked wherever they travel. Behind the goggles is a people of strong moral conviction, quick judgement, and a marked tendency toward the Force.
kel_dor.physiology: Kel Dor breathe a helium-based mix and require an antiox breath mask and protective goggles in standard atmosphere — without them, a Kel Dor is blinded within moments and asphyxiating shortly after. Conversely they survive vacuum considerably longer than most species. Their skin ranges from peach to deep red, their extremities are tapered, and their eyes are entirely black. They can survive on their homeworld's atmosphere unaided and nowhere much else, a constraint that shapes every offworld journey they make.
kel_dor.society: Kel Dor culture holds justice as a near-absolute value, with a strong tradition of acting decisively against wrongdoing rather than deliberating over it. That conviction produces principled defenders and, occasionally, people who are very certain about matters they have not fully understood. The species produced Force-sensitives at a notable rate and contributed a number of them to the Jedi Order, whose teachings on detachment sat somewhat awkwardly with the Kel Dor instinct to intervene. Family ties are strong and obligations to community explicit.
kel_dor.homeworld: Dorin's atmosphere and lighter gravity are what the species is built for, and a Kel Dor at home goes unmasked and comfortable for the only time in their life. The world sits far from the main lanes, which has kept it relatively unmolested, and the species' offworld population is drawn heavily from those who chose to leave rather than those forced out. Returning home is a genuine relief rather than a sentiment.
kel_dor.language: Kel Dor speak Kel Dor, a language whose sounds are shaped by the mask as much as by the speaker — offworld, every Kel Dor voice arrives filtered, and the species has adapted its speech patterns accordingly. Most learn Basic, delivered in the same processed rasp, and Kel Dor are often assumed to be more emotionless than they are simply because the mask flattens everything.

klatooinian.name: Klatooinian
klatooinian.description: Klatooinians are heavy-set, canine-descended, and bound by the same ancient compact that ties the Niktos to the Hutts. They are patient, disciplined and dangerous, and most have made peace with serving.
klatooinian.physiology: Klatooinians are stocky humanoids descended from canine stock, with heavy brows, blunt snouts and thick jowls. They are strong and durable, with keen smell and hearing, and they age slowly enough that a Klatooinian's apparent middle age can run for decades. Their build suits hard labour and hard fighting equally, and their tolerance for discomfort is high.
klatooinian.society: Klatooinian culture treats the ancient obligation to the Hutts as a religious duty rather than a servitude, and reveres it accordingly — a stance that baffles outsiders and irritates the minority of Klatooinians who see it plainly. Young Klatooinians are placed with Hutt masters and trained toward whatever role they show aptitude for, sometimes gaining real responsibility. Loyalty and discipline are prized; ambition outside the compact is regarded as faintly indecent. Those who break with it tend to leave Hutt space entirely, because there is nowhere within it to stand.
klatooinian.homeworld: Klatooine is arid and rocky, marked by sites of religious significance that the compact's terms protect — including a sacred wellspring that Hutt authority has historically been obliged to leave alone. That protection is one of the few things Klatooinians can point to as having been gained rather than surrendered.
klatooinian.language: Klatooinians speak Klatooinian, low and growling, and Huttese is universal among them for obvious reasons. Basic is learned as needed, usually well, and Klatooinian scholars and negotiators pick up further languages as their master's business requires.

kubaz.name: Kubaz
kubaz.description: Kubaz are long-snouted, insect-eating, and famously good at watching people. A great many of them sell what they see, which is why the sight of one in a spaceport makes certain professions nervous.
kubaz.physiology: Kubaz have a distinctive long proboscis suited to extracting insects, small dark eyes highly sensitive to bright light, and dark skin. They wear protective goggles in most lighting conditions — the sensitivity is genuine, not affectation. Their sense of smell is acute, their hearing good, and their unobtrusive build serves the surveillance work many of them end up in.
kubaz.society: Kubaz culture is patient, observant and comfortable with information as a commodity — a society where noticing things carefully is a respectable skill and selling what you noticed is a respectable trade. Their cuisine, built almost entirely on insects, is a serious cultural matter and a reliable source of friction with other species. The reputation for informing is deserved often enough to stick, and Kubaz who work honestly resent both the assumption and the colleagues who earned it.
kubaz.homeworld: Kubindi is hot and arid, its ecology dominated by insect life that the Kubaz have farmed and cultivated into a sophisticated agricultural tradition. Offworld demand for that expertise is limited, which pushes many Kubaz into other work. Imperial interest in the planet has been modest, and Kubaz informants abroad have proven more useful to the regime than anything on the surface.
kubaz.language: Kubaz speak Kubazian, largely produced through the proboscis and nearly impossible for other species to reproduce. Most learn Basic and speak it with a distinctive whistling articulation. A Kubaz who claims not to understand a conversation nearby is very often lying.

kyuzo.name: Kyuzo
kyuzo.description: Kyuzo are small, dense and astonishingly strong for their size, with a martial tradition and a distinctive wide-brimmed helmet that doubles as a weapon. They speak little and mean all of it.
kyuzo.physiology: Kyuzo are compact humanoids from a high-gravity world, which has left them with dense musculature and bone — a Kyuzo is far heavier and stronger than their height implies, and can leap distances that startle opponents. Their skin is greenish and their features flat, with large eyes. In standard gravity they move with a spring that reads as showmanship and is simply what their bodies do.
kyuzo.society: Kyuzo culture is martial, disciplined and reticent, with a strong tradition of honour codes governing combat and obligation. Words are spent sparingly; a Kyuzo who talks a great deal is regarded as unserious. They produce bounty hunters and mercenaries in numbers, and their reputation for reliability is as valuable to them as their reputation for violence. Family and clan obligations are binding, and a debt incurred by one is understood to be owed by all.
kyuzo.homeworld: Phatrong is a high-gravity world of hard terrain, and everything about Kyuzo physiology traces back to it. Its people adapted to conditions that would flatten most species and then, characteristically, made a discipline of it. Offworld Kyuzo often find standard gravity faintly unserious.
kyuzo.language: Kyuzo speak Kyuzo, terse and consonant-heavy, and their Basic is equally economical. A Kyuzo will answer a question and stop, which other species repeatedly mistake for hostility rather than completion.

lannik.name: Lannik
lannik.description: Lanniks are small, large-eared and deceptively formidable — a species of fierce fighters and long memories whose world has been fought over for generations.
lannik.physiology: Lanniks are diminutive humanoids with oversized pointed ears, wrinkled features and wiry strength well beyond their stature. They are quick, tough and hard to intimidate, and their small size has repeatedly been underestimated by opponents who did not survive the correction. Their hearing is exceptional, and their lifespans are long.
lannik.society: Lannik culture is proud, martial and deeply marked by a long history of religious and political conflict on their homeworld — a war that outlasted generations and shaped a people who take principle seriously and grudges more seriously still. They are direct, courageous and stubborn, with a strong tradition of personal honour. The species produced Jedi of note, whose combination of small stature and complete fearlessness made a lasting impression on those who trained beside them.
lannik.homeworld: Lannik has been contested for so long that conflict is part of its self-description — a world of hard terrain and harder politics, whose factional and religious wars drew galactic attention and Jedi intervention more than once. Peace, where it exists, is recent and unconvincing. Many Lanniks leave; those who stay tend to be committed to something.
lannik.language: Lanniks speak Lannik, fast and high-pitched, and most learn Basic well. Their delivery is blunt and their tolerance for circumlocution is low — a Lannik will interrupt a long preamble to ask what you actually want.

lepi.name: Lepi
lepi.description: Lepi are tall lagomorph humanoids with boundless energy, enormous families, and an unshakable conviction that they are the galaxy's best pilots. Some of them are right.

options.name: Athletics
options.description: Lepi may begin the game with one free rank in Athletics.

options.name: Perception
options.description: Lepi may begin the game with one free rank in Perception.

lepi.physiology: Lepi are tall and lean with long ears, powerful legs and fur in browns and greys. Their reflexes are outstanding and their hearing acute, and they are capable of considerable speed and jumping ability. They are also relentlessly energetic — Lepi metabolism runs fast, sleep runs short, and a Lepi at rest is a Lepi waiting for something to happen. They breed prolifically, which shapes their culture more than any other single fact.
lepi.society: Lepi society is organised around enormous extended families and a chronic population surplus that pushes the young offworld in numbers. They are boastful, cheerful and competitive, with a national obsession with piloting and racing that produces genuine talent alongside a great deal of unearned confidence. Family loyalty is strong and family obligations are extensive, and a Lepi far from home is usually sending money back to a great many relatives.
lepi.homeworld: Coachelle Prime is crowded — the species' fertility long ago outran the planet's comfortable capacity, and emigration is a structural feature of Lepi life rather than an individual choice. The world is busy, noisy and affectionate, and Lepi who leave describe it with a mixture of relief and homesickness.
lepi.language: Lepi speak Lepese, fast and high, and learn Basic quickly. They talk constantly, interrupt cheerfully, and a Lepi's account of their own piloting should be discounted by a factor they would dispute.

mandalorian_human.name: Mandalorian Human
mandalorian_human.description: Mandalorian is a creed, not a bloodline, but most who carry it are Human. Raised to armour, clan and a hard code, they have been the galaxy's most feared warriors for so long that the reputation now does much of the work.

options.name: Combat Skill
options._provenance: B-22 (ruling b22-option-mechanics): Mandalorian Humans' entire skill grant was prose-only (missing at creation); structured. Source: Friends Like These, Mandalorian Human entry.

options.name: Knowledge Skills
options._provenance: B-22 (ruling b22-option-mechanics): Mandalorian Humans' entire skill grant was prose-only (missing at creation); structured. Source: Friends Like These, Mandalorian Human entry.

mandalorian_human.physiology: Mandalorian Humans are physiologically Human. What distinguishes them is upbringing: training begins in childhood, endurance and discipline are cultivated deliberately, and beskar armour is worn as identity rather than equipment. A Mandalorian out of armour is still a Mandalorian, but is generally uncomfortable about it, and the helmet in particular carries meaning that varies sharply between the traditions that survive.
mandalorian_human.society: Mandalorian culture is built on clan, creed and combat, held together by a code that different factions interpret with genuine and sometimes murderous disagreement. Foundlings are adopted and raised as full members — the culture propagates by adoption as much as by birth, which is why Mandalorians are not a species. Their history is a cycle of conquest, civil war and reinvention, and the Empire's devastation of their homeworld is only the most recent collapse. Loyalty runs to clan first and to the creed above that; a Mandalorian's word, once given, is a serious matter.
mandalorian_human.homeworld: Mandalore has been fought over, glassed, rebuilt and fought over again. Long stretches of its surface are desert waste from old wars, its cities enclosed against a poisoned landscape, and its population scattered across a diaspora that now outnumbers those at home. Beskar, the iron that makes their armour, comes from its mines and is the reason so many powers have wanted the planet.
mandalorian_human.language: Mandalorians speak Mando'a, a blunt, consonant-heavy language with a vocabulary that runs deep on combat, family and obligation and thin on abstraction. It is taught to foundlings as part of adoption, and speaking it marks belonging more reliably than any bloodline. Basic is universal alongside it.

melitto.name: Melitto
melitto.description: Melittos have no eyes and no ears, sensing the world through hollow tubes across their bodies. They perceive things nobody else does, and they have never needed to explain how.
melitto.physiology: Melittos are insectoid humanoids with hard chitinous shells and no visual or auditory organs at all. Instead, hollow sensory tubes across the body read vibration, air movement and chemical trace with enough resolution to build a full picture of their surroundings — a Melitto in a dark, silent room is not disadvantaged in the slightest. Their carapace is tough, their strength good, and their tolerance for harsh conditions high.
melitto.society: Melitto culture is difficult for other species to characterise, largely because the Melitto sensory world is not translatable — a description of a room to another Melitto conveys things Basic has no words for. They are patient, communal and unbothered by conditions others find intolerable. Offworld they work where their senses give an edge: darkness, smoke, wreckage, anywhere sight fails. Their apparent impassivity is simply the absence of a face built to signal.
melitto.homeworld: Kalee is hot, harsh and dangerous, shared with a fiercer neighbouring species whose long war of extermination against the Melitto shaped both peoples. Survival there required exactly the senses the Melitto have. The planet's brutal recent history is well known to the galaxy chiefly through the other side of it.
melitto.language: Melittos communicate by vibration and chemical signal, a mode other species cannot perceive without instruments. They use translators or written Basic with outsiders, and a Melitto conversation with a non-Melitto is always mediated — a limitation they treat as the other party's problem, reasonably enough.

mikkian.name: Mikkian
mikkian.description: Mikkians wear their identity in colour — bright skin and elaborate head-tendrils that vary enormously between individuals. Honest to a fault and culturally deep, they have lost more to the Empire than most notice.
mikkian.physiology: Mikkians are humanoids with skin in vivid reds, pinks, yellows and blues, and crests of head-tendrils that range from a handful to several dozen depending on the individual. They lack external ears, hearing through the tendrils instead, which also carry a degree of expressive movement. They are lithe and agile, and their colouring is individual rather than familial — two siblings may look nothing alike.
mikkian.society: Mikkian culture values honesty to a degree that makes negotiation with them straightforward and living among them demanding — a Mikkian will tell you the truth and expect the same, and treats social evasion as a small betrayal. Their artistic and musical traditions run deep and long, and their cultural memory is extensive. The species produced Jedi of note. Under the Empire, Mikkia's standing has collapsed from a respected participant in galactic affairs to a marginal world, and two decades of propaganda have not erased what its people remember.
mikkian.homeworld: Mikkia is a temperate world of forest and open country whose people were once well represented in the Republic's cultural and diplomatic life. Imperial policy has reduced it to insignificance, deliberately. The Mikkians regard this as a phase in a much longer history and behave accordingly, which the local administration finds infuriating.
mikkian.language: Mikkians speak Mikkian, a tonal language whose meaning is completed by tendril movement — a transcription is incomplete by definition. They speak Basic plainly and directly, and a Mikkian's disinclination to soften bad news is a cultural feature rather than rudeness.

mirialan.name: Mirialan
mirialan.description: Mirialans wear their history on their skin. The geometric tattoos that mark a Mirialan face record accomplishments and rites of passage, and reading them is the fastest way to learn who you are dealing with — if you know how.
mirialan.physiology: Mirialans are near-Human with yellow-green to olive skin and a cultural practice of tattooing that begins early and continues through life. The markings are not decorative: each is earned, and their placement and pattern encode what the wearer has done and endured. Physically the species is lithe and notably flexible, with a tradition of physical discipline that produces acrobats, martial artists and duellists in unusual numbers.
mirialan.society: Mirialan culture is spiritual and fatalistic in a practical way — a belief that each person's actions feed a larger destiny, and that one's obligation is to act well rather than to control outcomes. The tattoo tradition makes reputation literally visible, which produces a society where deception about one's past is difficult and dishonour is worn permanently. The species has a strong Force tradition and supplied the Jedi Order steadily; Mirialan Jedi were noted for combining that fatalism with real discipline, which made them formidable and occasionally reckless.
mirialan.homeworld: Mirial is an arid, cold world of hard terrain and thin resources, and the culture's emphasis on endurance and shared obligation grew directly out of surviving it. Settlements are close-knit and largely self-sufficient. The planet has stayed peripheral to galactic politics, which the Mirialans generally regard as a blessing, though Imperial attention to their Force-sensitive population has made that peripherality less protective than it once was.
mirialan.language: Mirialans speak Mirialan, though the tattoos do a substantial part of the communicative work — a greeting between strangers involves reading each other before anyone talks. Basic is widely spoken, and offworld Mirialans often find themselves explaining their own faces to people who have asked a question they did not realise was personal.

mon_calamari.name: Mon Calamari
mon_calamari.description: Mon Calamari are the Rebellion's shipwrights and admirals — a thoughtful, idealistic species of aquatic humanoids whose enslavement by the Empire turned a pacifist people into the backbone of a war fleet.
mon_calamari.physiology: Mon Calamari are amphibious, with high-domed heads, large independently swivelling eyes and webbed hands. They are comfortable at depths that would kill most species and can remain submerged for long stretches, though they breathe air readily. Their eyesight is exceptional in low light and murky water, and their skin needs regular moisture — an offworld Mon Cal in a dry environment is quietly uncomfortable in a way they rarely mention. Lifespans are long.
mon_calamari.society: Mon Calamari culture is collaborative, artistic and deeply invested in the idea that things should be built well and made beautiful. Their shipyards produce vessels that are functional works of design, and their approach to problems is patient and consensus-seeking. That pacifist tradition was broken by the Empire's occupation and enslavement of their world, which radicalised a generation and delivered their industrial capacity, and eventually their cruisers and their commanders, to the Alliance. They share their homeworld with the Quarren, an arrangement that has never been comfortable and has periodically been violent.
mon_calamari.homeworld: Dac is an ocean world of floating cities and submerged settlements, with the Mon Calamari occupying the surface and near-surface and the Quarren the depths. Imperial occupation stripped it hard, and the resistance that grew out of that occupation is the reason so much of the Alliance fleet is Mon Calamari-built. The great shipyards are the planet's pride and its principal target.
mon_calamari.language: Mon Calamari speak Mon Calamarian, a fluid language incorporating gestures and eye movements that carry as much as the words; a Mon Cal speaking in earnest is using their whole face. Most learn Basic and speak it well, and the species' diplomats are highly regarded precisely because they translate not just the words but the intent.

mustafarian.name: Mustafarian
mustafarian.description: Mustafarians live on a lava world and are built for it — two distinct forms adapted to heat that would kill anything else, mining ore beside rivers of molten rock.
mustafarian.physiology: Mustafarians come in two forms: the short, broad Northern variety adapted to the mines, and the taller, thinner Southern variety with wing-like structures. Both have hardened skin and internal adaptations that let them work near extreme heat, and both are physically tough well beyond appearances. They cope poorly with cold, and Mustafarians offworld are frequently the ones complaining about the climate control.
mustafarian.society: Mustafarian culture is industrious and clan-based, organised around mining operations that have run for generations. They are pragmatic, undramatic and inclined to judge a person by their work. Outside interest in their world's mineral wealth has brought the Mining Guild and worse, and Mustafarians have long experience of being negotiated with from a position of weakness. Those who take offworld employment often do so in heavy industry, where a tolerance for conditions others cannot survive is genuinely marketable.
mustafarian.homeworld: Mustafar is a volcanic world of lava flows, ash plains and mining settlements built on the stable ground between. It is a place of real industrial value and real danger, and its reputation across the galaxy is grim for reasons that go beyond geology. The Mining Guild's presence is heavy and the profits mostly leave.
mustafarian.language: Mustafarians speak Mustafarian, a language of clicks and hard sounds that carries over industrial noise. They learn trade Basic as commerce requires, and their delivery is flat and functional — a Mustafarian is not being curt, that is simply the register.

muun.name: Muun
muun.description: Muun run the money. Tall, gaunt and relentlessly rational, they built the InterGalactic Banking Clan and have financed every side of every war since — usually all of them at once.
muun.physiology: Muun are exceptionally tall and thin, with elongated skulls, narrow features and long fingers. Their build is fragile by most standards and they have never needed it to be otherwise. What the species has instead is an aptitude for mathematics and abstraction that shows up early and is cultivated hard — Muun children are numerate before they are socially fluent, and the culture treats that order of priorities as correct.
muun.society: Muun society is a meritocracy in its own account and a hereditary financial aristocracy in practice, where advancement is earned through demonstrated competence within families that have held position for generations. Emotional restraint is prized to the point of coldness, contracts are close to sacred, and the species' comfort with financing all parties to a conflict is a matter of principle rather than cynicism: capital is neutral, and taking sides is a category error. That stance survived the Clone Wars, in which the Banking Clan armed both belligerents, and has adjusted only slightly under Imperial supervision.
muun.homeworld: Muunilinst is a wealthy, orderly world of banking houses and vaults, its cities built for permanence and its politics indistinguishable from its finance. Scipio holds the Clan's most sensitive operations, its secrecy laws deliberately impenetrable — which is precisely why every major power has taken an interest in who controls it.
muun.language: Muun speak Muun, a precise language with an unusually developed vocabulary for obligation, interest and contingency — a great deal of Muun grammar exists to specify exactly what has been promised. They learn Basic readily and use it with the same exactness, and a Muun's casual remark is rarely as casual as it sounds.

nagai.name: Nagai
nagai.description: Nagai are pale, elegant near-Humans from beyond the galaxy's edge, arriving with old grievances and a coldness that outsiders read as cruelty. Some of it is.

options.name: Charm
options.description: Nagai may begin the game with one free rank in Charm.

options.name: Coordination
options.description: Nagai may begin the game with one free rank in Coordination

nagai.physiology: Nagai are tall, slender near-Humans with chalk-white skin, dark eyes and sharp features, generally described as striking and rarely as warm. They are quick and physically capable without being powerful, favouring speed and precision — Nagai blade work is a genuine tradition rather than an affectation. Their appearance has earned them the nickname of shadow-people among species that met them under bad circumstances.
nagai.society: Nagai culture is martial, aristocratic and honour-bound, with a long history of conflict against a rival species that pushed them from their own space and shaped everything after. They are disciplined, reserved and slow to trust, and their willingness to pursue a grievance across decades has given them a reputation for coldness that is partly accurate and partly the natural result of a people who arrived as refugees and were treated as invaders. Personal honour is binding.
nagai.homeworld: Nagi lies outside the galaxy proper, in a region few maps trouble with, and the Nagai's arrival in the wider galaxy came as displacement rather than exploration. What they left behind and what drove them out are matters they discuss reluctantly with outsiders. Nagai communities in known space are small, insular and organised.
nagai.language: Nagai speak Nagai, a language of soft consonants and precise formality. Their Basic is exact and cool in tone, and a Nagai's courtesy should not be mistaken for warmth — it is the correct treatment of a stranger, no more and no less.

nautolan.name: Nautolan
nautolan.description: Nautolans read the emotional state of everyone in the room whether they want to or not — their head-tresses sense feeling directly through the water and, less clearly, through air. It makes them superb negotiators and terrible people to lie to.
nautolan.physiology: Nautolans are amphibious humanoids with smooth skin in greens and blues, large black eyes suited to deep water, and fourteen head-tentacles that function as sensory organs. Those tresses detect pheromonal and chemical signals, which in water amounts to reading another creature's emotional state plainly; in air the sense is blunted but not absent. Nautolans swim superbly, tolerate pressure well, and see in near-darkness. Their large eyes are vulnerable to bright light and dry conditions.
nautolan.society: Nautolan culture is open and communal, with an easy attitude toward emotional expression that follows naturally from being unable to conceal it. Deception within the species is difficult and consequently rare, and Nautolans offworld are often startled by how much other species lie casually and expect it to work. They are unhurried, sociable and inclined to resolve disputes by talking them into the ground. The species contributed notable figures to the Jedi Order, where the capacity to sense feeling directly was an obvious asset.
nautolan.homeworld: Glee Anselm is a world of oceans, swamps and river deltas, and Nautolan settlements are built across the boundary between water and air rather than committing to either. The species shares the planet with the Anselmi, with whom relations have historically been poor. Nautolans travel widely and adapt well, though the ones who leave tend to speak of the water more than they realise.
nautolan.language: Nautolans speak Nautila, which is fully expressive only underwater — a great deal of its meaning is carried in chemical signals that simply do not travel in air. Spoken above water it is a reduced version of itself, a fact Nautolans accept with good humour. Basic is widely spoken and Nautolans handle it easily.

neimoidian.name: Neimoidian
neimoidian.description: Neimoidians ran the Trade Federation, bankrolled a war, and have spent the years since insisting it was all a misunderstanding. Cautious to the point of cowardice and grasping to the point of caricature, they are better at commerce than at war and know it.
neimoidian.physiology: Neimoidians are tall, gaunt grey-green humanoids with large red eyes, sloping skulls and a horizontal ridge across the face. They begin life as grubs, competing for food in communal hives where the weak simply do not survive — an upbringing that leaves the adults with a permanent, well-founded anxiety about scarcity. Their eyesight is excellent in low light and their tolerance for physical hardship is poor; a Neimoidian in genuine danger is a Neimoidian looking for the exit.
neimoidian.society: Neimoidian culture is mercantile to its foundations, organising itself into trade guilds and corporate hierarchies where rank is bought as much as earned. Ostentatious display is normal, personal risk is not, and delegation is close to a moral principle. The grub-stage scarcity shapes everything: hoarding is instinctive and generosity is suspicious. Their leadership of the Trade Federation, its blockades and its droid armies, ended in a war they largely watched from orbit and a peace in which they were the convenient villains — a role they resent and have not escaped.
neimoidian.homeworld: Neimoidia and its purse-worlds are heavily cultivated, tightly administered and organised around the fungal agriculture that underpins Neimoidian wealth. The hives where the young compete are kept out of view of visitors. Imperial oversight has curtailed the old commercial autonomy considerably, and the species now trades under supervision it finds humiliating and profitable.
neimoidian.language: Neimoidians speak Pak Pak, a language of clicks and glottal sounds, and most learn Basic for business — delivered in the nasal, mannered accent the rest of the galaxy has made a byword for insincerity. Neimoidians are aware of the caricature and have concluded, correctly, that there is no version of their accent that would not be mocked.

nikto.name: Nikto
nikto.description: Niktos have served the Hutts for so long that the arrangement is written into their culture as duty rather than defeat. Five distinct sub-species share the name, and the galaxy rarely bothers to tell them apart.
nikto.physiology: Niktos come in five varieties shaped by their homeworld's harsh regions — horned, hornless, green, red, mountain and southern forms differing in skin, spines and facial structure. All share leathery hide, protective eye membranes and a build suited to heat and dust. Their facial musculature is limited, so they show little expression, and a Nikto's mood must be read from posture and voice. They are tough, durable and physically capable well beyond their unremarkable size.
nikto.society: The defining fact of Nikto life is the ancient compact that bound their species to the Hutts — a bargain made after a catastrophe their own records call a punishment, and one most Niktos now regard as simply how things are. Service is honourable; the Hutts are patrons rather than owners in the telling, whatever the practice. Sub-species divisions still matter internally and matter not at all to their employers. Niktos work as guards, enforcers, pilots and soldiers across Hutt space, generally competently and generally without complaint.
nikto.homeworld: Kintan is hot, dry and unforgiving, its regional extremes having driven the sub-species apart long before anyone left the planet. Radiation from a nearby stellar event shaped its ecology and, by tradition, its history. The Hutts have administered it in all but name for centuries, and Nikto born offworld into Hutt service may never see it.
nikto.language: Niktos speak Nikto, a guttural language of clipped consonants, and Huttese is effectively a second native tongue given how thoroughly their affairs run through Hutt commerce. Basic is common enough for work, and a Nikto's limited facial expression means outsiders routinely misjudge what they have just been told.

noghri.name: Noghri
noghri.description: Noghri are small, grey and among the deadliest assassins alive — a species whose sense of obligation is absolute and whose homeworld was poisoned to manufacture that loyalty.

special_abilities.name: Concealment
special_abilities.description: Noghri may remove all [SE] imposed due to concealment against a target that is within Short Range.

noghri.physiology: Noghri are compact grey-skinned humanoids, slight in build and extraordinarily fast, with claws, sharp teeth and an olfactory sense acute enough to identify individuals and track them by scent alone. They are far stronger than their size suggests and move with a silence that unnerves people who thought they were alone. Their reflexes are among the best of any humanoid species.
noghri.society: Noghri culture is organised into clans bound by an absolute code of obligation: a debt owed is a debt the entire clan carries, and a life saved commands service without limit. That is the mechanism by which the species was captured — their world was devastated, an outside power arrived offering aid, and the debt created bound generations of Noghri to serve their supposed benefactors as assassins. They are honourable, literal and entirely serious, and the discovery of a deception in such a bond would be catastrophic for whoever practised it.
noghri.homeworld: Honoghr was poisoned — its ecology devastated in a way that left the population dependent on outside assistance to survive at all. That dependence is the whole of modern Noghri history. The clans live in the habitable remnants, working under supervision, and the question of who actually caused the devastation is the most dangerous one anyone could raise.
noghri.language: Noghri speak Honoghran, a language of clicks and low sounds. They learn Basic and speak it sparely, in the third person as often as not when addressing those they serve. A Noghri's brevity is deference, not sullenness.

ortolan.name: Ortolan
ortolan.description: Ortolans are blue, blubbery and permanently hungry, with a musical talent that has carried a great many of them off their frozen world and into cantina bands across the galaxy.

special_abilities.name: Keen Senses
special_abilities.description: Ortolans receive a [BO] on Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Reduced Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Ortolans have a Silhouette of 0.

ortolan.physiology: Ortolans are short, rotund humanoids with blue skin, long trunk-like snouts and broad flat ears. The layer of fat that makes them look comical is insulation against a genuinely cold world, and their snouts and ears give them an exceptional sense of smell and hearing — an Ortolan can detect food at remarkable distance, which is the origin of both their reputation and a fair amount of their behaviour. Their fingers are stubby and surprisingly dextrous.
ortolan.society: Ortolan culture is organised around food and music, in roughly that order. Scarcity on their homeworld made obtaining food the central preoccupation, and abundance offworld has not adjusted the instinct — Ortolans eat compulsively and unapologetically. Their musical tradition is genuine and sophisticated, and Ortolan musicians are found galaxy-wide. Children are expected to support themselves young, which pushes many toward whatever talent they can trade on.
ortolan.homeworld: Orto is a cold world where food is hard-won and the population has always lived close to the margin. That scarcity shaped a species preoccupied with securing the next meal and quick to leave for somewhere better provisioned. Offworld Ortolans rarely go back.
ortolan.language: Ortolans speak Ortolan, a language of hoots and trills produced through the snout, and their musical ear makes them quick with other languages. Basic is common among those who travel, delivered in a distinctive piping register.

pantoran.name: Pantoran
pantoran.description: Pantorans are blue-skinned near-Humans from a frozen moon, marked by facial tattoos that signal family and standing. Politically engaged and proud of it, they punch well above their size in galactic affairs.
pantoran.physiology: Pantorans are near-Human with blue skin in a range of shades and golden or amber eyes, adapted to the cold and thin light of their moon. Facial markings — inherited, earned or adopted — indicate clan and status and are worn permanently. They tolerate cold far better than heat, and a Pantoran on a warm world is usually the one complaining.
pantoran.society: Pantoran culture is intensely political, organised around an elected assembly and a chairman, with clan identity running underneath the formal structures. Public service is a respected calling and debate is a national pastime. Their long relationship with the neighbouring Talz has been a live moral question in Pantoran politics — periods of exploitation followed by genuine reform, argued out publicly. They are proud, sometimes prickly, and take slights to their world's dignity seriously.
pantoran.homeworld: Pantora is a frozen moon of the gas giant Orto Plutonia, its cities built against deep cold and its economy dependent on trade and its Senate seat. The moon it shares a system with — home to the Talz — has been the source of the species' most contentious politics. Imperial rule has curtailed the assembly's power and produced a quiet, well-organised resentment.
pantoran.language: Pantorans speak Pantoran and Basic with equal fluency, and their oratorical tradition shows in both — public speech is a cultivated skill and Pantoran diplomats are known for it. In private the register drops considerably, which surprises people who have only heard them at a podium.

pau_an.name: Pau'an
pau_an.description: Pau'ans live in the sinkholes of Utapau, tall and grey and unsettling to species that meet them in poor light. They govern by inherited office, prize order, and have spent their history letting a smaller neighbour do the heavy work.
pau_an.physiology: Pau'ans are gaunt near-Humans, tall and long-limbed, with pale grey skin deeply lined by a life spent out of direct sunlight. Their sharp teeth and hollowed faces alarm outsiders on first meeting, which they are aware of and mostly untroubled by. They see well in the dim conditions of the sinkholes and find surface daylight harsh. Lifespans are long, and the lining that reads as great age arrives comparatively early.
pau_an.society: Pau'an society is hierarchical and formal, with hereditary Masters of Port Administration governing each city and a strong preference for procedure over improvisation. They share Utapau with the shorter Utai, who perform most of the physical labour — an arrangement Pau'ans describe as complementary and outsiders find harder to characterise so generously. They are hospitable to visitors, deeply invested in propriety, and pragmatic about accommodating whoever currently holds power, a habit that served them during Separatist occupation and again under the Empire.
pau_an.homeworld: Utapau's surface is a wind-scoured expanse of rock and dust, and effectively nobody lives on it. The cities are built into the walls of enormous sinkholes, tiered downward toward the water far below, sheltered from the wind and lit indirectly. It is a striking place and a defensible one, which is why it has been fought over more than its remoteness would suggest.
pau_an.language: Pau'ans speak Utapese, low and measured, and most also speak Basic with the same unhurried delivery. Their formality carries across languages: a Pau'an will use a visitor's title carefully and expect the courtesy returned, and reads its absence as a deliberate statement.

phydolon.name: Phydolon
phydolon.description: Phydolons are quiet, thoughtful and closer to each other than other species realise — at short range they share emotional meaning directly, a fact few outsiders have ever been told.
phydolon.physiology: Phydolons are humanoids of moderate build with distinctive cranial structures and skin in muted tones.
