Their notable trait is barely documented: in close proximity, Phydolons convey emotional content to one another with a directness that language cannot match, a capacity known chiefly to xenoanthropologists and to Phydolons, who do not advertise it. Otherwise they are unremarkable physically, which suits them.
phydolon.society: Phydolon culture is contemplative and consensus-driven, shaped by a form of communication that makes misunderstanding within the species rare and deception nearly pointless. That produces a people comfortable with silence, uninterested in rhetoric, and mildly baffled by how much effort other species spend on saying things. Their spiritual tradition treats the Force as the binding of the universe rather than a tool — Force-sensitive Phydolons tend toward stewardship rather than power, and regard those who reach for it as having misunderstood something basic.
phydolon.homeworld: Phydolon settlements are modest and deliberately unobtrusive, on a world that has attracted little galactic attention and worked to keep it that way. The species' reticence about its own abilities is a survival strategy as much as a preference: a people who can read each other perfectly would be of considerable interest to the wrong parties.
phydolon.language: Phydolons speak Phydolon, spare and unhurried, supplemented among themselves by the proximity sense that carries what words would labour at. They speak Basic competently and briefly. A Phydolon's long pause is not hesitation — it is the shape of a conversation that usually has another channel.

polis_massan.name: Polis Massan
polis_massan.description: Polis Massans are archaeologists and surgeons in equal measure, digging for the remains of a species that vanished from their asteroid field. Silent, gentle and endlessly patient, they speak to outsiders through droids.
polis_massan.physiology: Polis Massans are small, pale humanoids with large black eyes and no visible mouth or nose — they communicate telepathically among themselves and cannot produce vocal speech at all. Their build is slight and their fine motor control exceptional, which underpins their reputation in surgery and delicate excavation. They are adapted to low gravity and enclosed habitats, having lived in them for generations.
polis_massan.society: Polis Massan culture is organised around a single obsession: recovering the history of the Eellayin, the species that once inhabited their asteroid field and disappeared. Everything else — their medical expertise, their technology, their remarkable patience — grew in service of that work. They are pacifist by disposition rather than doctrine, cooperative, and largely uninterested in galactic politics except where it interrupts a dig. Their medical facilities are among the finest available and are offered without much interest in who the patient is.
polis_massan.homeworld: Polis Massa is not a planet but an asteroid field, the shattered remains of a world destroyed long ago. The Polis Massans live in sealed research bases across the fragments, excavating, cataloguing and running medical facilities of considerable sophistication. The isolation is total and entirely deliberate; visitors are rare and, when they come, generally in need of discretion.
polis_massan.language: Polis Massans communicate telepathically among themselves and use droid translators or written text with everyone else — a Polis Massan conversation with an outsider is mediated by definition. They understand Basic perfectly well. The silence is not reticence, and mistaking it for slowness is a common and instantly regretted error.

quarren.name: Quarren
quarren.description: Quarren share a world with the Mon Calamari and have resented the arrangement for generations. Practical, insular and drawn to the deep water, they are excellent engineers and hard people to win over.
quarren.physiology: Quarren are amphibious humanoids with four facial tentacles, leathery skin and turquoise eyes suited to the lightless depths. They are built for pressure and cold, comfortable far below where their surface-dwelling neighbours work, and they can remain submerged indefinitely. The face-tentacles are expressive and used in speech, and their sense of touch is acute enough to work by feel in total darkness.
quarren.society: Quarren culture is conservative, clannish and suspicious of outsiders — a stance formed less by nature than by a long history of being the junior partner on their own planet. Where Mon Calamari idealism produced explorers and artists, Quarren pragmatism produced engineers, labourers and traders, and the perception that the Mon Cal speak for Dac abroad while the Quarren do the work below is a live grievance. That resentment made some Quarren receptive to Imperial overtures during the occupation, a division that still cuts through families.
quarren.homeworld: Dac's depths are Quarren territory: submerged cities anchored to the ocean floor, industrial and functional where the surface settlements are ornamental. The species has never really shared the planet so much as occupied a different layer of it. The Empire exploited the split deliberately during the occupation, and the reconstruction has not healed it.
quarren.language: Quarrenese is spoken with the facial tentacles as much as the voice, and carries clearly through water where sound behaves differently — a conversation that seems muted in air is perfectly distinct below. Most Quarren learn Basic for trade and speak it with a wet, muffled quality that surface species find difficult and rarely admit to.

quermian.name: Quermian
quermian.description: Quermians are tall, long-necked and two-brained, the product of ancient genetic tampering by another species. Cerebral and slightly detached, they read motives well enough to unsettle the people they are reading.
quermian.physiology: A Quermian's most striking feature is the long neck supporting a small head, with a second brain housed in the torso — the arrangement that gives the species its unusual mental capacity and, occasionally, two distinct personalities in one body. They have four arms, though the lower pair is usually kept concealed beneath robes and used sparingly. They lack a conventional sense of smell, sensing chemically through the hands instead, which makes a Quermian greeting a more informative gesture than the other party realises.
quermian.society: Quermian culture is contemplative and communal, oriented toward philosophy, art and the long view. Physical confrontation is regarded as an intellectual failure. Their capacity to read intention makes them excellent mediators and mildly uncomfortable companions — many Quermians deliberately avoid commenting on what they have noticed. The species produced Jedi of note, and under the Empire that same perceptiveness has become dangerous to display: a talent for seeing through people is not a safe reputation to have.
quermian.homeworld: Quermia is a temperate world whose civilisation the Quermians built after the Arkanian scientists who engineered them from Xexto stock moved on. That origin — a species made rather than evolved — sits at the centre of Quermian self-understanding, and their unusually reflective culture is often traced to it. The world is peaceable, cultured and of little strategic interest, which has served it well.
quermian.language: Quermians speak Quermian, an elaborate language rich in terms for states of mind and degrees of certainty. Most speak Basic fluently and find it blunt — a Quermian rendering a Quermian thought into Basic is usually aware of what has been lost in the transfer.

rodian.name: Rodian
rodian.description: Rodians are green-skinned, large-eyed hunters from Rodia, and the galaxy knows them mainly as bounty hunters — a reputation the species has earned, encouraged, and occasionally suffered for.
rodian.physiology: Rodians have smooth green or blue-green skin, a tapered snout, and antennae that read airborne chemical traces with real precision. Their large multifaceted eyes are built for motion and low light, making them excellent trackers and poor readers of the subtle facial expressions other species rely on — a mismatch that gets Rodians labelled cold when they are merely built differently. Ridges run along the skull and back, and the overall frame is lean rather than powerful; a Rodian hunts by patience, tracking and ambush rather than by overwhelming a target.
rodian.society: Rodian culture treats the hunt as the organising principle of a life, and success at it as the measure of a person. Clans compete, feud, and celebrate their best hunters in art, theatre and song — Rodians are enthusiastic dramatists, and a great deal of their finest work is about killing. Offworld, that cultural pressure translates naturally into bounty hunting, which is why so many Rodians end up in the trade and why so many are mediocre at it: the profession attracts them by heritage rather than by aptitude. Hutt influence sits heavily over Rodian affairs and has for generations.
rodian.homeworld: Rodia is a humid jungle world of swamps and dense growth, where the native predators were dangerous enough to make hunting skill a survival trait rather than a sport. Much of the surface is now given over to walled cities and industrial concerns, a good deal of it under Hutt commercial control, and the great hunts of Rodian tradition happen increasingly in preserves and stories rather than in open country. The contrast between the culture's self-image and the planet's actual condition is a live tension among younger Rodians.
rodian.language: Rodians speak Rodese, a rapid clicking speech that pairs with antenna movement to carry meaning most non-Rodians miss entirely. Many learn Basic for business, and speak it with a distinctive buzzing accent that is much imitated and rarely well. A Rodian conversing with another Rodian may appear to be saying very little while in fact communicating a great deal.

ryn.name: Ryn
ryn.description: Ryn are wandering musicians, fortune-tellers and information brokers with no homeworld and a reputation that follows them everywhere. Much of it is prejudice; some of it they have earned.

options.name: Deception
options.description:
Ryn may begin the game with one
free rank in Deception.

options.name: Streetwise
options.description:
Ryn may begin the game with one
free rank in Streetwise.

special_abilities.name: Prehensile Tail
special_abilities.description: Ryn can use their tails to hold and manipulate small items, but cannot use that item to make an attack.

ryn.physiology: Ryn are furred humanoids with prominent beak-like noses, long tails and fur in muted greys and browns. Their hands are dextrous and their hearing acute, both of which serve their musical tradition. They are wiry rather than strong, built for travel and quick movement. Their prehensile tails aid balance and are expressive in conversation.
ryn.society: Ryn culture is nomadic by necessity and now by identity: without a homeworld, the caravan and the clan are the only permanent things. They are musicians, entertainers and — quietly — one of the better-informed information networks in the galaxy, since a people who travel everywhere and are ignored by everyone hear a great deal. Their avoidance of written records is deliberate. The prejudice they face is old and pervasive, and Ryn communities are correspondingly guarded with outsiders and tightly bound within.
ryn.homeworld: The Ryn have none, and the loss is old enough that the details are disputed among them. What remains is the caravan: extended family groups moving between worlds, carrying their culture in music, story and memory rather than in any place. Settlements that tolerate them are noted and returned to; those that do not are also noted.
ryn.language: Ryn speak Ryn, a musical language whose whistled register carries between caravans across distance. They learn whatever local languages travel requires, generally several, and are practised at understanding more than they let on.

sakiyan.name: Sakiyan
sakiyan.description: Sakiyans are dark-skinned, hairless and built for the hunt, with senses that make them exceptional trackers and a cultural confidence that reads as arrogance to almost everyone.
sakiyan.physiology: Sakiyans are near-Human in build, hairless, with dark skin and enlarged eyes adapted to low light. Their senses of smell and hearing are considerably sharper than Human, and their night vision is excellent — a Sakiyan tracking in darkness is working with advantages other species need equipment for. They are lean, quick and physically capable without being imposing.
sakiyan.society: Sakiyan culture is competitive and status-conscious, with a strong hunting tradition that persists in professional form: bounty hunting, tracking and security work draw them in numbers. They regard their sensory advantages as evidence of superiority and are not shy about it, which makes them effective and unpopular in roughly equal measure. Loyalty is transactional rather than sentimental, and a Sakiyan's professional reputation matters more to them than any individual relationship.
sakiyan.homeworld: Saki is a world of dense forest and long nights, conditions that shaped both the species' senses and its hunting culture. It sits away from major routes and has stayed largely outside galactic politics, which suits a people whose interests are mostly conducted elsewhere. Sakiyans abroad rarely discuss home in detail.
sakiyan.language: Sakiyans speak Sakiyan and learn Basic readily, generally along with whatever else the work requires. Their delivery is clipped and confident, and a Sakiyan explaining why they are the right hire will not undersell it.

sathari.name: Sathari
sathari.description: Sathari are slight, feathered and quietly contemplative — an avian species whose ancestors could fly and whose descendants have made peace with the ground, mostly.
sathari.physiology: Sathari are slender humanoids of avian descent, covered in fine feathers with vestigial wings that no longer support flight. They have four eyes, giving them exceptional peripheral vision and depth judgement, and their hollow-boned build makes them light, quick and fragile. Feather colour varies widely and shifts with age. They are agile climbers and glide short distances, which is as close to the ancestral ability as remains.
sathari.society: Sathari culture is patient and analytical, favouring long observation before action — a Sathari asked to solve a problem will study it considerably longer than other species find comfortable and then produce something that works the first time. They are peaceable, meditative and drawn to disciplines requiring precision. The species has a notable Force tradition, and Sathari who leave often do so in pursuit of something specific rather than out of restlessness.
sathari.homeworld: Arbooine is a world of forests and high cliffs where most large fauna evolved four eyes, an ecological curiosity the Sathari treat as unremarkable. Their settlements are built into heights their ancestors could reach on the wing and their descendants reach by ladder. It is remote enough to have escaped the worst galactic attention.
sathari.language: Sathari speak Sathari, a light melodic language of trills, and learn Basic without difficulty. They speak slowly and choose words carefully, and their long pauses are consideration rather than hesitation — interrupting one is a reliable way to be quietly judged.

selkath.name: Selkath
selkath.description: Selkath are amphibious, deliberate and fiercely protective of a homeworld that produces something the galaxy badly wants. Their neutrality is a policy, not a temperament.

options.name: Medicine
options.description:
Selkaths may begin the game with
one free rank in Medicine.

options.name: Negotiation
options.description:
Selkaths begin the game with
one free rank in Negotiation.

selkath.physiology: Selkath are aquatic humanoids with smooth skin, wide-set eyes and cranial tendrils — the females distinguished by a greater number at the back of the head. They breathe water and air both, swim powerfully, and are comfortable at depths that require equipment for anyone else. Their build is lean and their movements unhurried on land, where they are visibly less at home.
selkath.society: Selkath culture is legalistic and deliberate, governed by councils that debate at length and value procedure highly. Their world produces a substance of enormous medical value, and the entire society is organised around controlling it — who may harvest it, who may buy it, and on what terms. That has made them a target for every power that wants leverage, and their careful neutrality is the strategy of a species that knows exactly how outnumbered it is. Manipulation of Selkath politics by outside interests is an old and painful theme.
selkath.homeworld: Manaan is an ocean world with almost no land, its cities floating and its economy resting entirely on the substance harvested from its depths. The species guards both jealously and permits outside presence on tightly controlled terms. Imperial interest has strained an arrangement that survived earlier powers by playing them against each other.
selkath.language: Selkath speak Selkath, fluid and formal, with a legal vocabulary of unusual precision. They speak Basic with the same care, and a Selkath's answer to a direct question will often be a correct description of the applicable rule.

selonian.name: Selonian
selonian.description: Selonians are sleek, otter-like tunnel-dwellers from the Corellian system, organised into female-led dens where males are scarce and the group always outranks the individual.
selonian.physiology: Selonians are long, lithe furred humanoids with sleek bodies, retractable claws and thick tails, built for tunnels and for water. They swim excellently and dig better, and can move on four limbs comfortably when speed matters. Their most consequential trait is demographic: the overwhelming majority of Selonians are sterile females, with fertile males and females rare, which shapes their entire social structure.
selonian.society: Selonian society is organised into dens ruled by a queen, with sterile females forming the working population and the rare fertile members treated as communal assets rather than individuals. Loyalty runs to the den absolutely; the concept of acting against one's den barely parses. That makes Selonians honest, direct and collectively formidable, and it makes their dealings with individualistic species genuinely difficult — they routinely assume an outsider speaks for their group and are baffled when they do not.
selonian.homeworld: Selonia is one of the five worlds of the Corellian system, honeycombed beneath the surface with den-tunnels that make the visible settlements a fraction of the actual population. Selonian dens also exist on other worlds of the system. Their relations with the Corellians and Drall they share the system with are cordial, occasionally strained, and very old.
selonian.language: Selonians speak Selonian, a language of chirps and trills that carries well down a tunnel. They learn Basic readily. Their directness is a constant source of misunderstanding — a Selonian says what the den has concluded, and social softening strikes them as a form of lying.

shistavanen.name: Shistavanen
shistavanen.description: Shistavanens are wolf-like and solitary, superb trackers who prefer their own company and take work that lets them keep it. The galaxy meets them alone, which is how they arrange it.
shistavanen.physiology: Shistavanens are lupine humanoids with muzzles, sharp teeth, claws and coats of coarse fur. Their senses of smell and hearing are outstanding, their night vision is excellent, and they can move on all fours at considerable speed when the situation calls for it. They are strong, fast and built for pursuit — a Shistavanen tracking something across country is very hard to shake.
shistavanen.society: Shistavanen culture is insular and territorial, historically isolationist to the point of discouraging visitors from the homeworld entirely. They are solitary by disposition rather than by rule, and Shistavanens abroad tend to work alone as scouts, trackers, bounty hunters or military reconnaissance. Their reputation for aloofness is accurate; their reputation for savagery is not, and mostly reflects other species' reaction to the teeth.
shistavanen.homeworld: Uvena Prime is a world its people kept closed for a long time, admitting outsiders reluctantly and expanding cautiously to a handful of colonies. That isolation has eroded under Imperial attention, and Shistavanen scouts have found their skills in demand from parties on every side of the current conflict.
shistavanen.language: Shistavanens speak Shistavanen, a growling language of considerable subtlety in registers other species hear as uniform. They speak Basic well and sparingly. A Shistavanen who is not talking is not necessarily unfriendly; they simply see no reason to fill the space.

skakoan.name: Skakoan
skakoan.description: Skakoans live inside pressure suits because our atmosphere would kill them, and they regard everyone outside those suits with a mixture of pity and contempt. Brilliant engineers, catastrophic diplomats.
skakoan.physiology: Skakoans evolved under a methane-rich, high-pressure atmosphere and cannot survive standard conditions unprotected — exposure causes a violent and often fatal reaction. Offworld they wear sealed pressure suits at all times, and a suit breach is a genuine emergency rather than an inconvenience. Beneath the armour they are pale and soft-featured, a fact few outsiders ever confirm. Their eyesight and fine motor control are excellent, which suits the work they are known for.
skakoan.society: Skakoan culture is technocratic and deeply xenophobic, treating outsiders as contaminants in a fairly literal sense and their own engineering tradition as the measure of civilisation. Advancement runs through technical guilds; the Techno Union grew from that structure and carried Skakoan influence into galactic politics. Their leadership of Separatist industry made them enemies of the Republic and then irrelevant to the Empire, which took what it wanted and left them the humiliation. Visitors to Skako must wear their own protective gear — a symmetry the Skakoans find satisfying.
skakoan.homeworld: Skako is a high-pressure world of dense atmosphere and vertical cities, long dismissed by neighbours as uninhabitable and left alone for millennia. That isolation produced both the engineering culture and the xenophobia. Its industrial output was central to the Confederacy's war machine, and it has been under close and unfriendly supervision ever since.
skakoan.language: Skakoans speak Skakoan, filtered through suit vocoders into a flat mechanical register that strips out most of the tonal information the language carries. They learn Basic for business and deliver it in the same processed monotone, which does nothing to soften an already difficult impression.

sluissi.name: Sluissi
sluissi.description: Sluissi are serpentine engineers of legendary patience, coiling beside a repair for as long as it takes and generally getting it right the first time.

options.name: Gearhead
options.description: Begin play with one rank in the Gearhead talent.
options._provenance: B-22 (ruling b22-option-mechanics): structured now; the mechanical landing is deferred to B-23 (no species-talent consumer exists yet). Source: Sluissi species entry.

options.name: Solid Repairs
options.description: Begin play with one rank in the Solid Repairs talent.
options._provenance: B-22 (ruling b22-option-mechanics): structured now; the mechanical landing is deferred to B-23 (no species-talent consumer exists yet). Source: Sluissi species entry.

special_abilities.name: Practiced Mechanic
special_abilities.description: A Sluissi can choose to spend a maneuver just prior to making a Mechanics roll, upgrading the dice pool by one.

sluissi.physiology: Sluissi have humanoid upper bodies with capable hands and long serpentine tails in place of legs, moving by undulation and coiling to rest — a posture they adopt while working, which lets them stay at a task for extraordinary stretches. They are dextrous, patient and physically durable, with good tolerance for the awkward positions engineering demands. Their scaled hide is tough.
sluissi.society: Sluissi culture prizes patience, craft and doing a job properly, and regards haste as the source of most problems worth having. Their shipwrights and engineers are widely respected, and Sluissi repair work has a reputation for lasting. They are calm, agreeable and difficult to hurry — pressing a Sluissi for speed produces the same work on the same timeline, delivered with unfailing politeness. Their communities are cooperative and their disputes rare and slow.
sluissi.homeworld: Sluis Van is best known for its shipyards, a major repair and construction hub whose facilities serve a substantial share of regional traffic. The Sluissi built their prosperity on being the people who fix things properly, and the yards have made the system strategically valuable in ways its inhabitants would rather they were not.
sluissi.language: Sluissi speak Sluissese, a sibilant language delivered slowly. Their Basic carries the same hiss and the same unhurried pace, and a Sluissi will finish their sentence regardless of what is happening around them.

snivvian.name: Snivvian
snivvian.description: Snivvians are stocky, wrinkled artists and satirists with a talent for observation and no instinct for keeping quiet about what they have seen. Several have been exiled for a portrait.

options.name: Charm
options.description: Snivvian may begin the game with one free rank in Charm.

options.name: Perception
options.description: Snivvian may begin the game with one free rank in Perception.

special_abilities.name: Cold Resistance
special_abilities.description: When making skill checks, Snivvians may remove [SE][SE] imposed due to cold environmental conditions.

special_abilities.name: Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Snivvians have a Silhouette of 0.

snivvian.physiology: Snivvians are short and broad, with wrinkled faces, prominent tusks and thick hide suited to a cold homeworld. Their sense of smell is exceptional — good enough to track by, and good enough that a Snivvian usually knows who has been in a room. They are hardy and stubborn physically, tolerating conditions that send other species indoors.
snivvian.society: Snivvian culture prizes artistic expression, and the species has produced generations of painters, sculptors, novelists and — most notoriously — satirists whose work has cost them patronage, freedom and occasionally more. They are keen observers with long memories and little diplomatic instinct, which makes their art sharp and their careers precarious. Beneath the artistic reputation is a practical, resilient people: Snivvians work as scouts, trackers and bounty hunters at least as often as they work in galleries.
snivvian.homeworld: Cadomai Prime is cold, its long winters driving the population into close quarters for months at a stretch — conditions that reliably produce either art or violence, and in the Snivvian case mostly art. The species has emigrated widely, and Snivvian communities offworld tend to cluster around whatever cultural scene will have them.
snivvian.language: Snivvians speak Snivvian, gravelly and consonant-heavy, and learn Basic readily. They are frank to the point of tactlessness in both, and a Snivvian's honest opinion of your work will be offered whether or not it was solicited.

squib.name: Squib
squib.description: Squibs are small, furred and relentless hagglers who see value in what everyone else discarded. They will trade you anything, including things you did not know were for sale.

special_abilities.name: Mechanics
special_abilities.description: Squibs always treat Mechanics as being a career skill, regardless of their starting career.

special_abilities.name: Reduced Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Squibs have a Silhouette of 0.

squib.physiology: Squibs are diminutive furred humanoids with large ears, bright eyes and dextrous hands. They are quick, agile and considerably tougher than their size suggests, with excellent hearing and a keen eye for detail — a Squib assessing a pile of scrap is genuinely appraising it, not rummaging. Their fur ranges through greys and browns and is a matter of considerable personal vanity.
squib.society: Squib culture runs on acquisition and negotiation. Haggling is a competitive art form conducted at volume and length, and a deal closed too quickly is regarded as a deal poorly done. They are salvagers by tradition and preference, running operations that recover, refurbish and resell whatever the galaxy has thrown away — an industry they defend as ecological virtue and pursue as pure profit. They are boastful, litigious and genuinely skilled, and their long commercial rivalry with the Ugnaughts is conducted with real heat.
squib.homeworld: Skor II is a world the Squibs have organised almost entirely around salvage — vast yards of recovered material, sorted and traded. Their reach extends well beyond it through fleets that scour derelicts and battlefields. The Empire's leavings have been extremely good for business, which Squibs mention less loudly than their other opinions.
squib.language: Squibs speak Squibbian, rapid and emphatic, and learn Basic and trade tongues quickly. A Squib negotiating switches languages mid-sentence if it helps, and a conversation with one is rarely as short as intended.

sullustan.name: Sullustan
sullustan.description: Sullustans are born underground and spend their lives trying to get to space. Natural navigators with a flawless sense of direction, they crew ships across the galaxy and remember every route they have ever flown.
sullustan.physiology: Sullustans are short humanoids with large dark eyes adapted to darkness, prominent jowls and large round ears that give them exceptional hearing — good enough to judge distance and direction by echo alone. That combination produces an almost infallible sense of place: a Sullustan who has travelled a route once can retrace it, and the species' navigators are prized accordingly. Bright light is uncomfortable to them, and many wear eye protection on surface worlds.
sullustan.society: Sullustan culture is clan-based and densely social, shaped by generations of living in enclosed underground cities where privacy was scarce and cooperation compulsory. They are gregarious, curious and enthusiastic travellers, and the species' presence on the hyperlanes far exceeds its numbers. Sullustan life has been dominated in recent generations by SoroSuub, the corporation that employs most of the population and for a time simply governed the planet — an arrangement that split the species badly when the corporation sided with the Empire and much of the population did not.
sullustan.homeworld: Sullust is volcanically active and largely hostile at the surface, its people living in vast cavern cities beneath. The industry that built those cities also built SoroSuub, and the planet's politics and its principal employer have been the same thing for longer than is healthy. Its position made it strategically significant to the Alliance, and Sullustans have been prominent in the Rebellion out of proportion to their numbers.
sullustan.language: Sullustans speak Sullustese, a rapid language that other species find hard to follow at conversational speed and that Sullustans rarely slow down. Most speak Basic fluently for trade, and Sullustese has spread along the shipping lanes far enough that a good many spacers of other species have picked up the essentials.

talz.name: Talz
talz.description: Talz are large, four-eyed and covered in white fur, gentle by disposition and formidable when that fails. They were enslaved before most of the galaxy knew they existed.

special_abilities.name: Insulated fur
special_abilities.description: When making skill checks, Talz remove [SE] imposed due to actic or cold environmental conditions.

talz.physiology: Talz are tall and heavily built, insulated by thick white fur against a frozen homeworld, with four eyes — a large pair for the long dark and a smaller pair for the glare of snow and daylight. They are enormously strong and remarkably durable, with a trunk-like proboscis for feeding. Warm climates are genuinely punishing to them, and an offworld Talz is often quietly suffering.
talz.society: Talz culture is peaceable, communal and slow to violence, organised around small groups and a strong protective instinct toward their own. That gentleness made them easy prey: Talz have been enslaved and exploited for generations, taken from a world few outsiders had catalogued. Those who have been freed, or freed themselves, carry the experience without much bitterness and with a very clear sense of what they will not tolerate again. A Talz who has decided to act is not easily stopped.
talz.homeworld: Alzoc III is a frozen world of ice and permanent cold, its Talz population living in conditions that made them physically formidable and left them isolated enough to be exploitable. Mining interests arrived, and the enslavement followed. The world remains bleak and its people scattered.
talz.language: Talz speak Talzzi, a language of hoots and rumbles produced through the proboscis that other species cannot reproduce. Most understand Basic well and cannot speak it, relying on translation or on companions who have learned to read them — a limitation that has repeatedly been used to pretend they do not understand what is being said about them.

thakwaash.name: Thakwaash
thakwaash.description: Thakwaash think in separate mind-sets, switching wholly between them as a task demands — a capability that makes them brilliant specialists and, to outsiders, disconcertingly like several different people.

special_abilities.name: Multiple Personalities
special_abilities.description: At the start of their turn, Thakwaash can choose to suffer 2 strain to upgrade the dice pool once for a specific skill until the start of their next turn.

thakwaash.physiology: Thakwaash are tall, robust humanoids with equine features, manes and considerable physical strength. Their distinguishing trait is neurological: the Thakwaash mind operates in discrete configurations — one for combat, one for analysis, one for social matters — and a Thakwaash shifts fully between them rather than blending. In a given mind-set they are exceptional; outside it, unremarkable at that task. They are hardy and long-lived.
thakwaash.society: Thakwaash culture is built around this mental architecture, with a herd structure in which individuals are valued for the mind-sets they command and the discipline with which they use them. Switching is trained, not automatic, and a Thakwaash who cannot control the transitions is regarded as unwell rather than merely erratic. They are direct, physically confident and comfortable with specialisation — the idea that one person should be moderately good at everything strikes them as a failure of method.
thakwaash.homeworld: Thakwaa is a world of open plains and high country suited to a herd species, its communities organised around cooperation and clear role assignment. The species has not spread widely, and Thakwaash offworld are uncommon enough that most people who meet one assume the mind-shifting is an eccentricity rather than a species trait.
thakwaash.language: Thakwaash speak Thakwaash, and notably speak it differently depending on the mind-set they are in — vocabulary, register and even cadence shift. They learn Basic well, and outsiders who know them learn to read which mode they are addressing before choosing how to ask.

thisspiasian.name: Thisspiasian
thisspiasian.description: Thisspiasians are serpentine below and burly above, with four arms and a beard that signifies standing. Contemplative, long-lived and physically formidable, they made unusually patient Jedi.
thisspiasian.physiology: A Thisspiasian has a long serpentine lower body and a broad muscular torso with four arms, the whole covered in coarse hair and topped with an elaborate beard whose grooming carries real social meaning. They move by muscular undulation, faster than expected, and their strength is considerable. They are very long-lived, which shapes their patience and their politics alike.
thisspiasian.society: Thisspiasian culture is hierarchical and ceremonious, ordered by nobility and by an elaborate etiquette in which grooming, posture and precedence all signal position. Beneath the formality is a genuinely contemplative tradition — Thisspiasians think in long horizons and distrust haste. The species has supplied the Republic with senators and the Jedi Order with masters, and their combination of physical power and unhurried judgement made them formidable in both roles.
thisspiasian.homeworld: Thisspias is a world of dense forest and burrow-cities, its nobility governing from ancestral holdings and its people historically reluctant to involve themselves in galactic affairs. That reluctance has eroded — first through the Republic, then under the Empire — and Thisspiasians abroad are more common than they once were, though still uncommon enough to be remarked upon.
thisspiasian.language: Thisspiasians speak Thisspiasian, sibilant and formal, with honorifics that encode rank precisely. They speak Basic with the same ceremony, and a Thisspiasian who drops the formality has either accepted you completely or given up on you entirely.

tholothian.name: Tholothian
tholothian.description: Tholothians are near-Human, marked by the tendrils that crown their heads, from an old Core world that the Empire has worked hard to erase. Their culture survives mostly in the people who left.
tholothian.physiology: Tholothians are near-Human with a distinctive crown of thick head-tendrils and skin in warm tones. The tendrils are sensory to a degree and expressive besides, moving with mood in ways that other species read imperfectly. They are otherwise Human in build and lifespan, and the species has a notable incidence of Force sensitivity.
tholothian.society: Tholothian culture is old, formal and heavily invested in education and continuity — a species that kept detailed records, taught its history carefully, and considered cultural transmission a civic duty. That made the Imperial suppression of Tholothian language and custom especially damaging: what the Empire attacked was precisely what the culture valued. Tholothians abroad often carry a curatorial streak, preserving practices their homeworld can no longer perform openly, and the Jedi Order drew from them steadily.
tholothian.homeworld: Tholoth is one of the older politically significant worlds in the Republic, long integrated into Core affairs and comfortable there. Under the Empire it has been thoroughly assimilated: the native language group suppressed, local institutions replaced, and the old sites either repurposed or left to decay. Some are quietly used as shelter by people the Empire is looking for.
tholothian.language: Tholothians speak Tholothian, a language of layered vowels that an educator movement tried to preserve formally in the Republic's last years. Imperial policy ended that programme. Basic is universal now, and a Tholothian who still speaks the old language learned it from family rather than from a school.

tognaths.name: Tognaths
tognaths.description: Tognaths cannot survive unaided in an oxygen atmosphere and live inside sealed exosuits, permanently paired with a symbiotic organism that keeps them breathing. The arrangement is not a disability to them — it is what they are.
tognaths.physiology: A Tognath is an insectoid humanoid whose respiratory system cannot process oxygen at all. Survival depends on a symbiote housed within the exosuit, which processes atmosphere on the Tognath's behalf; the pairing forms in childhood and lasts a lifetime, and separation kills them both. Their compound eyes see well into ranges other species do not, and the suits are built to protect that sight as much as to keep them alive. Beneath the gear they are lean, hard-shelled and considerably faster than the bulk of the equipment suggests.
tognaths.society: Tognath culture is shaped by the symbiosis: a life spent depending absolutely on another organism produces a species that treats interdependence as normal and self-sufficiency as a slightly childish idea. They are pragmatic, unsentimental and highly disciplined, and they make excellent soldiers — a reputation earned in mercenary work long before the Rebellion recruited them. Reproduction and childhood pairing are private matters that Tognaths do not discuss with outsiders, which has generated a great deal of inaccurate speculation.
tognaths.homeworld: Yar Togna's atmosphere suits Tognath biology and almost nothing else's. Imperial occupation drove a substantial share of the population offworld, where they must remain suited permanently and where the symbiote's maintenance becomes an ongoing logistical concern. The diaspora is large, tight-knit, and disproportionately represented in mercenary companies and resistance cells.
tognaths.language: Tognaths speak Togna, filtered through the suit's apparatus into a rasping buzz. Most learn Basic and deliver it in the same processed tone, and because the suits hide their faces entirely, other species consistently misjudge their mood — a Tognath's amusement and a Tognath's contempt sound identical from outside.

togorian.name: Togorian
togorian.description: Togorians are enormous feline hunters whose males and females live largely apart — the males roaming the plains, the females in the cities. Both find the arrangement perfectly reasonable.
togorian.physiology: Togorians are tall, powerfully built felines covered in fur, with claws, fangs and reflexes suited to running down prey. Males are larger and more heavily muscled; females are somewhat smaller and, by tradition, the technologists. Both have excellent night vision, acute hearing and the speed their build implies. They are long-lived and physically formidable well into age.
togorian.society: Togorian society is split by sex to a degree other species find startling: males live nomadically on the plains, hunting and travelling in small groups, while females live in cities, run industry and build ships. The two meet by arrangement, and both regard the separation as natural rather than tragic. Honour and personal reputation matter enormously to both, and a Togorian's given word is not casually offered. Offworld they turn up as mercenaries, pilots and hunters, and their size alone ends most arguments.
togorian.homeworld: Togoria is a world of vast plains and scattered cities, the division of the species written into its geography. The mosgoths the males ride are as much a part of that culture as the ships the females build. Outside contact has been limited and mostly commercial, which suits everyone there.
togorian.language: Togorians speak Togorian, a growling language with a considerable tonal range. They learn Basic when travel requires it and speak it economically. A Togorian's silence in a negotiation is not an absence of opinion.

togruta.name: Togruta
togruta.description: Togruta hunt and live as a pack, and their montrals sense the space around them well enough to move as one without a word spoken. Alone they can seem oddly quiet; among their own they are something else entirely.
togruta.physiology: Togruta have red to orange skin with white facial markings, hollow horn-like montrals rising from the skull, and head-tails that grow longer with age. The montrals sense ultrasonic echo and the movement of objects nearby — a spatial awareness that lets a group of Togruta move in coordination without visible signalling. The markings are individual and function as identification. They are lithe and quick, and their colouration works as camouflage in their homeworld's grasslands rather than as decoration.
togruta.society: Togruta culture is communal to a degree that other species struggle with: the group's welfare comes first, ostentatious individualism is regarded as a defect, and a Togruta's competence is measured by their contribution to the whole. Traditional life was organised around collective hunting, and that pack instinct persists in everything from military units to family structures. The species produced many Jedi, and Togruta Padawans were noted for adapting to the Order's collective discipline more easily than most. Isolation is genuinely difficult for them.
togruta.homeworld: Shili is a world of tall grassland and dense forest where the species evolved as pack hunters and prey animals both. The colouring that reads as striking offworld is protective there. Togruta settlements are traditionally villages built for mutual defence, and the cultural memory of being hunted has left a species that is watchful without being fearful.
togruta.language: Togruta speak Togruti, a language accompanied by montral-sensed spatial cues that fill in a layer of meaning no recording captures — two Togruta in a room communicate more than a transcript shows. Basic is common offworld, and Togruta speak it clearly, though they often find single-channel conversation oddly thin.

toydarians.name: Toydarians
toydarians.description: Toydarians hover on rapidly beating wings and haggle for a living. Stubborn, shrewd and entirely immune to Force persuasion, they make merchants nobody can talk into anything.
toydarians.physiology: Toydarians are small, potbellied and winged, kept aloft by wings that beat far faster than their bulk suggests should work — their bodies are largely gas-filled, which is what makes the flight possible and makes them poor swimmers. A short trunk and small tusks complete a shape most species find comic and most Toydarians find perfectly dignified. Their most consequential trait is mental: Toydarian minds simply do not respond to Force influence, a resistance that has saved several of them from very persuasive customers.
toydarians.society: Toydarian culture is mercantile to its bones. Bargaining is entertainment as much as commerce, a deal not haggled over is faintly insulting, and reputation among traders is the real currency. They are proud, quick-tempered and hard to intimidate, which combined with their Force immunity makes them awkward for anyone accustomed to shortcuts. Most Toydarians offworld work within Hutt commercial networks, managing operations for owners who value someone that cannot be leaned on mentally.
toydarians.homeworld: Toydaria is a swampy world of muck and floating vegetation, its cities built above the mire on platforms and stilts. It sat close enough to Hutt space to be shaped by it, and Toydarian commerce has been entangled with Hutt interests for generations — an arrangement of mutual usefulness rather than affection.
toydarians.language: Toydarians speak Toydarian, a nasal buzzing language delivered at speed. Most are fluent in Basic and Huttese besides, since a trader who cannot follow both is a trader losing money, though many are literate only in their own tongue.

trandoshan.name: Trandoshan
trandoshan.description: Trandoshans are heavy reptilian humanoids who measure a life in hunts, and who regard almost everyone else as either a rival hunter or potential prey. They make formidable allies and worse enemies, and they never forget a Wookiee.
trandoshan.physiology: Trandoshans are tall, thickly built reptilians with scaled hide tough enough to serve as armour and claws suited to gripping and tearing. Their eyes see into the infrared, which makes hiding from one in darkness a poor plan. The species' most remarkable trait is regeneration: a Trandoshan can regrow a lost limb over time, though the process is slow and increasingly imperfect with age. Their sense of smell is acute, their reflexes are fast for their bulk, and they shed and regrow their skin periodically throughout life.
trandoshan.society: Trandoshan life is organised around the Scorekeeper, a deity who is understood to tally the worth of every hunt a person completes. Points are earned by taking worthy prey and lost by failure or dishonour, and the total is believed to determine a Trandoshan's standing after death. This makes the species intensely competitive and gives even casual violence a devotional quality. The long enmity with Wookiees is a live part of this: Kashyyyk is close, Wookiees are considered exceptional prey, and Trandoshan slaver crews have hunted them for the Empire with enthusiasm. Family units are close, and a hunter's reputation is a family asset.
trandoshan.homeworld: Trandosha — Dosha to its people — is a hot, harsh world of scrub and rock in the same system as Kashyyyk, an accident of astronomy that has shaped both species' histories badly. The native fauna is aggressive enough that Trandoshan children learn to hunt very young. Offworld industry has arrived heavily, much of it slaving and much of it directed at their green-furred neighbours, and Dosha's cities have grown around that trade rather than in spite of it.
trandoshan.language: Trandoshans speak Dosh, a sibilant language full of hisses and hard consonants that carries poorly over comms and unnervingly well in person. Most learn Basic, which they speak with a pronounced sibilance, and a Trandoshan who addresses you in your own language is generally doing you a courtesy they expect to be noticed.

twi_lek.name: Twi'lek
twi_lek.description: Twi'leks are known across the galaxy for their head-tails and their beauty, and both facts have been used against them for centuries. They are survivors of a hard world and a harder trade, and most have learned to negotiate their way out of trouble rather than fight it.
twi_lek.physiology: Twi'leks are slender humanoids with skin in a wide range of colours — blue, green, red, pale grey, and rarer patterned variations that carry heavy social weight among their own people. The defining feature is the pair of lekku, or head-tails, that grow from the skull and contain a substantial share of the species' neural tissue. Damage to them is serious and can be crippling. Lekku also move expressively, and Twi'leks can hold an entire second conversation with them while speaking aloud about something else.
twi_lek.society: Twi'lek society is clan-based and consensus-driven at home, with leadership held collectively and disputes settled by discussion that can last a very long time. Exile is the traditional severe punishment, and it is effectively a death sentence on Ryll. What dominates the species' galactic experience, though, is slavery: Twi'leks have been trafficked for generations, prized as dancers, servants and status objects, and the trade has scattered them across the Outer Rim and deep into Hutt space. Those born offworld into that system often build lives around getting out of it, which is why so many Twi'leks turn up as smugglers, dancers, fixers and revolutionaries.
twi_lek.homeworld: Ryloth is tidally locked, with one face burned by its sun and the other frozen in permanent night. Twi'leks live in the narrow habitable band between, in cities carved into the rock and connected by tunnel networks that shelter them from the heat and from the vicious storms that sweep the terminator. The world produces ryll, a valuable and heavily criminalised spice, which has drawn Hutt attention for as long as anyone can remember and explains a good deal about Ryloth's politics.
twi_lek.language: Twi'leks speak Ryl, which is spoken and gestural at once — words carry part of the meaning and lekku movement carries the rest, and a transcription of Ryl loses a great deal. There is also a purely gestural form used silently in the presence of slavers and other unwelcome listeners, which most non-Twi'leks have no idea exists. Basic is widely spoken as a matter of practical necessity.

ubese.name: Ubese
ubese.description: Ubese wear sealed helmets and breath masks in company and are known throughout the galaxy as bounty hunters and mercenaries. Almost nobody has seen a Ubese face, which is the intended effect.

options.name: Perception
options.description: Ubese may begin the game with one free rank in Perception.

options.name: Survival
options.description: Ubese may begin the game with one free rank in Survival

ubese.physiology: Ubese are near-Human beneath the gear, with narrow features and eyes disproportionately large — a fact very few outsiders can confirm firsthand. Their homeworld's atmosphere was devastated, and the enclosed helmets and breath masks they wear are medical necessity as much as cultural practice. Generations of exposure have left the species frail in ways the armour conceals, and Ubese lifespans are shorter than they once were.
ubese.society: Ubese culture is guarded, proud and organised around clan, shaped by a catastrophe that poisoned their world and scattered its survivors. They are secretive with outsiders to a degree that reads as menace, and many have leaned into that reputation professionally — mercenary and bounty work suits a people who are already unreadable and already armed. Internal divisions between those who stayed and those who left run deep, with each side questioning the other's honour.
ubese.homeworld: Uba IV was rendered largely uninhabitable, and the Ubese who remained live in conditions that continue to shorten lives. Those who left settled elsewhere in the system and beyond, and the two populations regard each other with a wariness that has hardened into insult over generations.
ubese.language: Ubese speak Ubeninal, filtered through mask vocoders into a flat rasp, and rarely choose to speak Basic even when they can. Silence is a Ubese negotiating position, and the helmet makes it a very effective one.

ugnaught.name: Ugnaught
ugnaught.description: Ugnaughts are short, tusked and industrious, running the machinery of places like Cloud City with a competence their employers routinely fail to notice.

options.name: Mechanics
options.description: Ugnaughts may begin the game with one free rank in Mechanics.

options.name: Negotiation
options.description: Ugnaughts may begin the game with one free rank in Negotiation.

special_abilities.name: Exceptionally Hardy
special_abilities.description: Ugnaughts add [AD] to Resilience checks.

special_abilities.name: Silhouette
special_abilities.description: Ugnaughts have a Silhouette of 0.

ugnaught.physiology: Ugnaughts are diminutive porcine humanoids with tusks, bristly hair and strong, capable hands. They are short but genuinely strong, with stamina suited to long shifts of physical work and a tolerance for industrial conditions that would exhaust larger species. Their eyesight and hearing are ordinary; their manual skill is not.
ugnaught.society: Ugnaught culture is organised into clans defined by trade and craft, with work at the centre of identity and idleness regarded as a personal failing. They are proud, contractual and blunt — an Ugnaught crew agrees terms carefully and then honours them exactly, and expects the same in return. Their history includes enslavement and a hard-won emancipation, which is why the terms of a contract matter to them as more than commerce. Their rivalry with the Squibs over salvage rights is longstanding and enthusiastically maintained.
ugnaught.homeworld: The Ugnaughts came from Gentes, and generations were relocated to labour on Bespin's cloud installations — a history of displacement that ended in a settlement granting them the freedom and the work they now hold. Cloud City runs on Ugnaught labour, and its administration would collapse without them, which they know and mention.
ugnaught.language: Ugnaughts speak Ugnaught, a language of grunts and snorts. Most learn functional Basic for dealing with employers, delivered bluntly, and their negotiations are conducted with a precision that surprises people who mistook the accent for simplicity.

umbaran.name: Umbaran
umbaran.description: Umbarans come from a world of permanent twilight and see a spectrum nobody else does. Subtle, political and widely distrusted, they have a reputation for manipulation that they have never worked very hard to dispel.
umbaran.physiology: Umbarans are pale near-Humans with colourless eyes adapted to near-darkness — their homeworld's shrouded sky means direct sunlight is genuinely painful, and offworld Umbarans favour shades and shadowed rooms. They see well into the ultraviolet and can perceive detail in conditions other species call pitch black. Their build is slight, their movements economical, and their faces notably difficult to read, which does nothing to help the reputation.
umbaran.society: Umbaran society is a dense web of shifting alliances, obligations and quiet leverage, conducted with a subtlety that outsiders experience as scheming. Status is real but rarely stated; power moves through influence rather than office. The species' talent for reading a room and steering it has produced formidable senators and formidable criminals, and the galaxy's belief that Umbarans can cloud minds is superstition attached to something genuinely uncanny about their social instincts. They sided heavily with the Separatists, and paid for it.
umbaran.homeworld: Umbara sits under a permanent shroud that blocks nearly all direct light, its landscape lit by bioluminescence and its ecology built for gloom. Everything there is adapted to the dark, including things that hunt. The Republic's invasion during the Clone Wars was brutal and is remembered as such; Imperial administration since has been heavy, resented, and conducted largely through Umbaran intermediaries who tell their occupiers what they wish to hear.
umbaran.language: Umbaran is quiet and tonally precise, with a great deal of meaning carried in registers that other species hear as monotone. Umbarans learn Basic well and use it carefully, and their habit of saying slightly less than a situation requires is deliberate — the gap is where the negotiation happens.

verpine.name: Verpine
verpine.description: Verpine are insectoid engineers who communicate by radio built into their own bodies, and who understand machinery in a way that borders on intuition. They fix things nobody else can and rarely explain how.
verpine.physiology: Verpine are tall, thin insectoids with green chitin, large multifaceted eyes and antennae capable of transmitting and receiving radio directly — a Verpine can talk to another Verpine across a hull without any equipment at all. Their fine motor control is extraordinary, sufficient for microscale work by hand, and their eyesight resolves detail other species need instruments for. They tolerate vacuum exposure better than most, an adaptation to asteroid life.
verpine.society: Verpine society is consensus-driven to an unusual degree, because their radio sense makes group deliberation nearly continuous — a colony reaches decisions through a background conversation nobody has to convene. Individual credit matters little; the work matters enormously. They are famous shipwrights and weaponsmiths, and their designs are prized across the galaxy. Verpine are curious, cooperative and mildly bewildered by species that have to schedule a meeting.
verpine.homeworld: The Roche asteroid field is the Verpine home, its colonies built into and across the rocks, its industry devoted to shipbuilding and precision manufacture. Living in an asteroid belt shaped both the physiology and the culture — cooperation is not a virtue there, it is a condition of survival. Imperial interest in their output has been heavy-handed and unwelcome.
verpine.language: Verpine speak a language of clicks and radio pulses, the radio component invisible to everyone else — an overheard Verpine conversation is missing most of itself. They learn Basic for trade and speak it competently, and a Verpine pausing mid-sentence is often mid-conversation with somebody a kilometre away.

vurk.name: Vurk
vurk.description: Vurks are reptilian nomads and philosophers, judging themselves and each other by deeds rather than words. Deeply ethical and famously frank, they make uncomfortable friends and excellent diplomats.
vurk.physiology: Vurks are tall reptilian humanoids with a prominent crest running back from the skull, weathered green-grey hide and three-fingered hands. They are physically hardy, comfortable in heat and rough terrain, and long-lived. Their features are difficult for other species to read, which combines with their bluntness to make first meetings memorable.
vurk.society: Vurk culture is nomadic in tradition and ethical in preoccupation — they travel in shifting groups, judge each other by accomplishments rather than lineage, and discuss those judgements openly to a degree other species find brutal. Questions of right conduct are a constant subject of examination rather than a settled matter, which produces genuinely thoughtful people and a certain relentlessness in conversation. Failure is treated as experience rather than disgrace, and a Vurk who has failed publicly is expected to say what they learned.
vurk.homeworld: Sembla is a world of shallow seas and scattered land where Vurk communities historically moved rather than settled, extending that nomadic tradition into the galaxy at large. Imperial extraction has degraded working conditions badly and prompted pockets of resistance across the planet — a species that discusses ethics constantly reaches the obvious conclusion faster than most.
vurk.language: Vurks speak Vurk, direct in construction with a vocabulary well developed for moral distinction. Their Basic is equally direct, and a Vurk's honest assessment of your conduct will be offered whether or not it was requested.

weequay.name: Weequay
weequay.description: Weequay are leathery, taciturn and steady under pressure, which has made them the Outer Rim's default hired muscle. They speak little to outsiders and rather more than anyone realises to each other.
weequay.physiology: Weequay have thick, deeply creased leathery skin that resists sun, wind and abrasion — an adaptation to a harsh homeworld that also happens to shrug off a great deal of casual violence. Their hair is worn in a small number of long braids, and their facial expressions are difficult for other species to read at all. They are physically strong, durable, and notably tolerant of heat and dehydration.
weequay.society: Weequay organise by clan, and clan loyalty outranks employer, contract and law without much apparent internal debate. They are religious in a practical way, venerating an ancestral deity whose favour is read in circumstance. Their reputation for stoic silence around outsiders is accurate and slightly misleading: Weequay of the same clan communicate constantly through pheromonal signals that other species cannot detect, so a room of apparently mute Weequay may be holding a detailed conversation. Offworld they work as guards, enforcers and pirates, generally competently.
weequay.homeworld: Sriluur is hot, arid and unforgiving, its people sharing it uneasily with Houk neighbours and a chaotic mix of criminal interests. Imperial presence is substantial and has curbed none of the disorder. Weequay who leave rarely leave alone — clan networks reach across the Rim and a Weequay in trouble has relations to call on.
weequay.language: Weequay speak Sriluurian, and among clan-mates they supplement it with pheromonal signalling that carries meaning no non-Weequay can perceive. Most learn functional Basic for work and use it sparingly, which outsiders read as sullenness and is closer to economy.

whiphid.name: Whiphid
whiphid.description: Whiphids are enormous tusked hunters from a frozen world, covered in shaggy fur and considerably more thoughtful than their appearance suggests. Most of the galaxy meets them as muscle and never learns otherwise.
whiphid.physiology: Whiphids are massive, heavily furred humanoids with prominent tusks and long arms suited to grappling. Their fur thins in warmer climates and grows dense in cold, and they tolerate freezing conditions that would kill most species. They are immensely strong and surprisingly quick over short distances — a hunting build rather than a labouring one. Their sense of smell is acute enough to track by.
whiphid.society: Whiphid culture is built on the hunt and on the long dark seasons that follow it, when communities live on what they took and pass the time with carving, storytelling and argument. That produces a species that is patient, physically formidable and unexpectedly artistic — Whiphid bone and ice carving is genuinely fine work. Offworld they are hired for their size and reputation, which most find a reductive but profitable misunderstanding. Their honour codes around hunting are taken seriously and travel with them.
whiphid.homeworld: Toola is a frozen world of tundra and glacier, its short warm season followed by a long brutal winter that shaped every Whiphid tradition. The species has been hunted in turn — for its fur, in eras less regulated — and remembers it. Offworld Whiphids often send money home; the ones who stay regard the emigrants with a mixture of pride and suspicion.
whiphid.language: Whiphids speak Whiphid, a deep language of growls and long vowels that carries across open snow. They learn Basic slowly but well, and speak it deliberately. A Whiphid taking a long pause before answering is usually thinking, not struggling.

wookiee.name: Wookiee
wookiee.description: Wookiees are towering, immensely strong, and far more sophisticated than most of the galaxy assumes. Their strength is real and so is their temper, but the reputation for savagery is mostly a slander that suits the people currently enslaving them.
wookiee.physiology: A Wookiee stands well over two metres and is covered in thick hair that ranges from black through russet to near-white with age. The build is heavy through the shoulders and arms, with retractable climbing claws that are tools rather than weapons — using them in a fight is a serious dishonour. Wookiees are strong enough to tear apart machinery with their hands and durable enough to shrug off injuries that would put most species down. They live for centuries, which shapes their patience with everyone else, and their eyesight and hearing are keen enough to work comfortably in the shadowed depths of a forest canopy.
wookiee.society: Wookiee culture runs on obligation and memory. A debt is not a transaction but a bond, and a Wookiee who owes a life debt will follow the person they owe it to across the galaxy and into obvious disaster without much discussion. Family and community structures are dense and deeply felt, and grievances are held for a very long time. Wookiees are skilled engineers and craftspeople, working wood and metal with equal care, and their technological sophistication routinely surprises those who mistook height and hair for simplicity. The Empire's enslavement of the species is the central fact of Wookiee life in this era.
wookiee.homeworld: Kashyyyk is a world of colossal wroshyr trees, whose canopies form the layered cities where Wookiees live. The forest floor lies far below in permanent gloom, home to predators that make descent a genuine expedition rather than a walk, and a Wookiee's status has traditionally been tied to how deep they can safely go. Imperial occupation has turned the planet into a labour resource, its people shipped offworld in numbers and its forests cut for materiel — which is why so many Wookiees are encountered far from home and disinclined to explain why.
wookiee.language: Wookiees speak Shyriiwook, a language of growls, moans and roars that most other species cannot physically reproduce. The reverse is not true: Wookiees generally understand Basic perfectly well and simply cannot pronounce it, which leads to a great many conversations conducted in two languages at once. Those who travel widely often pair up with someone who can translate, and a Wookiee's apparent silence in a negotiation is rarely incomprehension.

xexto.name: Xexto
xexto.description: Xexto are small, quick and equipped with four arms and a nervous system that runs faster than most species can follow. They make superb pilots and hopeless liars.
xexto.physiology: Xexto are wiry six-limbed humanoids — four arms and two legs — with small heads on long necks and reflexes at the top of the humanoid range. Their multiple limbs and speed suit them to controls, tools and anything requiring several things at once. They are physically slight and easily overpowered, which their reflexes usually prevent from mattering. Their species is the ancestral stock from which the Quermians were engineered.
xexto.society: Xexto culture is energetic, gregarious and inclined to spectacle — daring is admired and understatement is not. Their pilots and performers are well known, and the species has a real streak of physical courage that outsiders mistake for recklessness because it usually is. They are poor at concealment: Xexto body language runs at the same speed as everything else about them and gives away a great deal. Many have joined the Rebellion, and their casualty rate reflects the temperament.
xexto.homeworld: Troiken is a world of open ranges and mountains, historically troubled by outside interference — most notably by conflicts that used the planet as a stage. Xexto communities there are close-knit and durable. Offworld, Xexto turn up wherever fast hands are wanted, from podracing circuits to starfighter squadrons.
xexto.language: Xexto speak Xextese, delivered at a speed other species struggle to segment, in a reedy nasal register produced by their long throats. Most learn a serviceable Basic or Huttese; both come out fast, and a Xexto asked to slow down will do so for about a sentence.

zabrak.name: Zabrak
zabrak.description: Zabrak are marked from birth by vestigial horns and facial tattoos, and by a self-confidence that other species find either admirable or insufferable. They believe in their own capability, and they are usually right.
zabrak.physiology: Zabrak are near-Human with a crown of vestigial horns that emerges in adolescence, patterns varying by individual and lineage. They have a second heart and a notably high tolerance for physical pain, which the culture treats as a virtue to be demonstrated rather than a mere trait. Skin tones range widely from pale to deep red-brown depending on regional origin. Facial tattoos are applied in adulthood and carry personal and cultural meaning.
zabrak.society: Zabrak culture prizes self-reliance, resilience and demonstrated competence, and Zabrak are raised to believe there is very little they cannot learn to do. That produces determined, capable people and a species-wide reputation for arrogance that Zabrak generally do not dispute. They colonised aggressively and early, spreading across many worlds and adapting to each, which has made regional Zabrak populations quite distinct from one another. Pain endurance rituals and physical trials feature in coming-of-age traditions across most Zabrak cultures.
zabrak.homeworld: Iridonia is harsh — rocky, storm-scoured and short on easy living — and the species' emphasis on endurance grew from surviving it. Zabrak settled far beyond it long ago, and a Zabrak encountered offworld is as likely to be third-generation Corellian as Iridonian. Those raised on the homeworld tend to regard the colonists as softened, an opinion the colonists return with interest.
zabrak.language: Zabrak speak Zabraki, though the widespread colonisation means regional dialects have drifted far enough to cause genuine confusion between populations. Basic is near-universal among them as a practical consequence of living everywhere, and many Zabrak speak it as a first language with Zabraki reserved for family.

zeltron.name: Zeltron
zeltron.description: Zeltrons are red-skinned, pheromone-producing hedonists who feel the emotions of everyone around them and respond enthusiastically. Charming, exhausting, and harder to lie to than most people realise.

special_abilities.name: Empathy
special_abilities.description: Add [SE] to all incoming Charm or Deception rolls that target the Zeltron.

special_abilities.name: Pheromones
special_abilities.description: Zeltrons add [AD] to all Charm, Deception, and Negotiation skill checks.

zeltron.physiology: Zeltrons are near-Human with red or pink skin and hair in vivid shades. Two traits define them: they are empathic, sensing the emotional state of those nearby, and they produce pheromones that make others find them attractive and agreeable. They also carry a second liver, which lets them consume quantities of intoxicants that would incapacitate anyone else — a fact their culture has made full use of.
zeltron.society: Zeltron culture is hedonistic, affectionate and organised around pleasure, art and company. Their empathy makes them genuinely attentive to others' feelings and their pheromones make them welcome nearly everywhere, a combination that produces superb hosts, negotiators and entertainers — and a persistent galactic assumption that they are frivolous. That assumption is useful to them. Their empathy also means deception nearby is uncomfortable to be around, and a Zeltron generally knows when a room has turned before anyone says anything.
zeltron.homeworld: Zeltros is a world given over almost entirely to pleasure, celebration and the tourist economy that follows, its politics conducted with an informality that appals more serious neighbours. It has survived invasions largely by being more enjoyable to visit than to occupy — an approach that has worked more often than it should.
zeltron.language: Zeltrons speak Zeltron and Basic with equal ease, and the empathic layer means a great deal passes between them that neither language carries. They are effusive in both, and a Zeltron's warmth toward a stranger is genuine rather than performed.

zygerrian.name: Zygerrian
zygerrian.description: Zygerrians built an empire on slavery and have never accepted that the trade is over. Proud, cunning and unrepentant, they regard the galaxy's disapproval as a failure of nerve.
zygerrian.physiology: Zygerrians are feline humanoids with pointed ears, sharp teeth and fur-covered skin, generally tall and physically capable. They are strong, quick and built for confrontation, with keen senses and reflexes suited to it. Their appearance is imposing by default, which their culture has always regarded as an asset rather than a coincidence.
zygerrian.society: Zygerrian culture was organised around slaving for millennia — an empire built on captured labour, with status measured in holdings and a genuine belief that the strong are entitled to the weak. The Republic and the Jedi broke that empire, and Zygerrians have never made peace with it: the trade continues where it can, in the shadows and increasingly with Imperial tolerance, and the culture's grievance about its lost supremacy is nursed rather than forgotten. They are cunning negotiators who assume any deal has a hidden advantage, because theirs usually do.
zygerrian.homeworld: Zygerria prospered for thousands of years on the slave trade and faded when the Jedi cracked down on it, its capital's grandeur outlasting the economy that built it. The Empire's arrival has been read locally as an opportunity, and the old markets have shown signs of reopening under new patronage.
zygerrian.language: Zygerrians speak Zygerrian, sibilant and expressive, and speak Basic fluently for commerce. Their courtesy is elaborate and entirely instrumental, and a Zygerrian being especially gracious is usually assessing what you are worth.

lasat.name: Lasat
lasat.description: The Lasat are a tall, powerful people, agile despite their size and marked by prehensile feet that let them cross sheer surfaces as easily as level ground. Scattered across the galaxy after the fall of their homeworld, many became warriors, mercenaries, and wanderers.

jawa_aaa.name: Jawa
jawa_aaa.description: Small, hooded scavengers of the deep desert, Jawas are shrewd traders who prize salvage and drive a hard bargain. What they lack in stature they make up for in cunning and an uncanny eye for a deal.

tusken_raider.name: Tusken Raider
tusken_raider.description: The Tusken Raiders are a fiercely territorial desert people, hardened survivors who ride banthas and endure wastes that would kill most travelers. Outsiders rarely earn their trust.

ewok_aaa.name: Ewok
ewok_aaa.description: The Ewoks of the forest moon are a small, curious woodland people, easily overlooked and just as easily underestimated — keen of sense, adept at stealth, and quick to turn simple tools and their terrain to advantage.

csg_aalagar.name: Aalagar

special_abilities.name: Northern Islanders
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold or wet conditions, add setback for hot or dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add boost on auditory Perception checks. Double all sonic damage.

special_abilities.name: Tireless
special_abilities.description: Suffer no penalties for lack of sleep and only require 4 hours of light meditation per day.

csg_aalagar.physiology: Like other Bith-related races, Aalagar are highly advanced craniopods, a group of species with a large head. This oversized cranium has much space devoted to a massive brain that is highly adept at logical reasoning. Below the forehead are wide dark eyes protected by a translucent shell. They have no eyelids, as they have no need for sleep, surviving off only a few hours of light meditation. Just below the eyes are skin flaps in their cheeks, which hold their highly adept olfactory organs. Their mouth and nose are quite small at the bottom center of their face, and they only inhale through the nose. Air then goes to a single lung and is exhaled through their skin. Aalagar have a more pale yellow skin than most Bith. Despite the lack of visible ears, hearing is their strong suit, and they have a particular knack for detecting pitch. While they lack toes, they do have fairly long and bony fingers. They cannot reproduce naturally and require artificial conception, which usually involves careful genetic analysis. Such analysis has consistently shown Aalagar and Bith relationships to make sub-par offspring, so they are effectively their own species. Aalagar are further distinguished from the Bith by additional layers of fat in their skin, which protect them from cold temperatures.
csg_aalagar.society: Aalagar are similar to other Bith in most respects, with a powerful intellect and a meticulous mindset for detailed work, although they are more inclined toward visual arts. Whereas other Bith are known as engineers who manifest their knowledge as industrial titans, the Aalagar often stay in academia and ponder more abstract questions. While perfectly capable around tech, they are fond of small scale operations. For example, while Bith babies are gestated at designated Reproduction Centers, Aalagar couples generally rent the machines to put in their own homes and do it themselves. Aalagar are all hardier than other Bith, and they weren’t quite as impacted by the wave of pacifism that has overtaken the species in recent centuries.
csg_aalagar.language: Aalagar speak Y’oon and usually Basic or Bith. Their writing system can be encoded using knotted ropes.
csg_aalagar.homeworld: Clak’dor VII is an Outer Rim planet on the Rimma Trade Route. The Aalagar live in an island chain called Laga, which is north of the other Bith cities and much more frigid.
