The planet is a dangerous one, with genetically mutated fauna and a toxic atmosphere, so Bith must live in domed cities. Aalagar have not adapted well to this, and many have fled for colonies such as nearby Pyolli and its more pristine lakefronts.
csg_aalagar.description: One of the Bith-related subraces on Clak'dor VII, Aalagar are a more independently-minded group that is adapted to living on its more frigid and rural island communities. Compared to their more tropical-dwelling peers, they are more inclined toward the arts and an academic lifestyle.
csg_aalagar.sidebar_text: Before the Bith brought ecological devastation to Clak’dor VII, Aalagar were a gregarious people, travelling on ships not through space, but over the waters. They were fishermen, nomads, and often pirates in a life filled with both danger and adventure. The disaster brought on by Bith wars has forced modernization in recent centuries, but many feel cramped in the domes and long for their old ways. Some have left for other worlds, such as Pyolli, where they have built several cities on the coasts of its massive freshwater lakes. Others reminisce of olden days with ballads and tales of their greatest warriors.
csg_aalagar._provenance_note: The Aalagar species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_aaraa.name: Aar’aa

special_abilities.name: Cold-Blooded
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions. May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn in conditions below 10 degrees Celsius. When conditions are freezing or close to freezing, must make a hard Resilience check. If failed, treat the environment as a dangerous atmosphere of rating 1. Increase to daunting and rating 2 if below -10 degrees.

special_abilities.name: Camouflage
special_abilities.description: Add boost on Stealth checks.

csg_aaraa.physiology: Aar’aa are a species of predatory reptiles who are fairly large, making them dangerous in combat. Their body is covered by pebble-like scales that can change color in order to blend in with their environment, and their back has a narrow ridge protruding from it. Their visage features glowing vermillion eyes underneath a set of thick brows. Aar’aa are a cold-blooded species, making them very uncomfortable if they aren’t in a sufficiently warm environment. When cold, they become sluggish rather than shivering.
csg_aaraa.society: Aar’aa may be big with strong predatory instincts, but they are intelligent, valuing civility and restraint. They greatly revere whatever technology they have access to, and they seek to assimilate to other cultures when around them, with the exception of the Hutts. They work hard to keep their emotions under control, which has turned one or two of them into excellent Jedi throughout the centuries. However, Aar’aa are still hunters deep down, and they fight ferociously at times, particularly if their nest is threatened.
csg_aaraa.language: Aar’aa prefer to speak the hissing language of Aa’ast. Hutt servants also learn Huttese, but they find it painful to speak, and those who escape Hutt service usually refuse to use it again.
csg_aaraa.homeworld: The majority of the Aar’aa population is located on Ques, a swampy world near the Si’Klaata Cluster. Food is scarce, and while the winters are moderate compared to most places, the Aar’aa still find it colder than they like. They live in villages with pre-industrial technology, and only those who accept indenturehood are allowed to access its spaceports. A few Aar’aa have done this and escaped into the wider galaxy. Smaller populations have begun to resettle their original home, Aar, a rainforest Outer Rim world which is still recovering from the ecological disaster it suffered more than a millennium ago.
csg_aaraa.description: Aar'aa are a dangerous species of reptilian predators who are eager to prove their restraint and civility. However, this has been made more difficult for them by the fact that many now live on a Hutt-dominated world, where they are often forced into seedier occupations.
csg_aaraa.sidebar_text: Aar’aa come from the Outer Rim planet Aar, which was once a world of steamy rainforests with a thriving ecosystem. However, disaster struck during the New Sith Wars, during which they fell under rule of the Sith Lord Aathiel. While the Aar’aa revolted against him, they inadvertently brought further disaster when another Sith, a rival to Aathiel, devastated the planet with biological weapons. With nowhere else to turn, the population of refugees followed Aathiel, who took them across the galaxy to the planet Ques and then sold them out as slaves to the Hutts. While the Aar’aa on Ques have since gained a nominal freedom, the Hutts keep strict control over its spaceport, imposing steep taxes on any offworld trade and only allowing Aar’aa to leave if they do so as indentured servants, who work as bodyguards or hitmen. Aar’aa from Ques loathe their Hutt overlords, but some see service as the only way to escape their poverty. Their mythology has come to emphasize that they evolved from legless creatures, and they see the development of bipedalism as equivalent to becoming civilized.
csg_aaraa._provenance_note: The Aar’aa species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_abednedo.name: Abednedo

special_abilities.name: Sensory Tendrils
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for lighting conditions.

csg_abednedo.physiology: Abednedo are mammalian humanoids who have tan, cream, or brown skin, which occasionally has gray spots. They have a wide, elongated head, and their eyes, split far apart on their face, are also very dark. They have prominent nostrils split on their sides of their head, and their mouth is at the end of their pointed chin. Surrounding their mouth, they have two tendrils that droop downwards, and these act as extra sensory organs, which are helpful in conditions where they struggle to see. They have hair which is similar to human hair in color and placement, and their hands have five digits, but they have just three toes. Although they are typically similar to humans in size, they have more dramatic size differences than other species, so some can be significantly larger than other Abednedo.
csg_abednedo.society: Not unlike humans, Abednedo are a very common sight in the galaxy, and they can excel in a wide range of professions that includes politicians and pilots to scoundrels and technicians. They often travel offworld, as they are gregarious and also curious about the rest of the galaxy. They are accepting but curious towards other cultures. The Abednedo descend from a species that lived in massive underground cathedrals, which are interconnected by a complex tunnel system. When they formed a more civilized society than that of their precursors, they colonized the surface of their planet, and they built massive cities. Their precursors still exist underground, although the two species rarely interact with one another.
csg_abednedo.language: Abednedo have a knack for learning many different languages, so they typically know at least Basic and their native tongue of Abednedish, and many know even more.
csg_abednedo.homeworld: Abednedo come from Abednedo, a planet in the Colonies. The architecture, decoration, and organization of their cities is complex and erratic, featuring seemingly random flagpoles, decorative spires, and artistic carvings. These are typically confusing and overwhelming to outsiders, but the Abednedo find them to be entertaining.
csg_abednedo.description: A gregarious species of mammals, Abednedo are similar to humans in that they display a diverse set of abilities and can be found all throughout the galaxy, although they have had poor relations with the Galactic Empire.
csg_abednedo.sidebar_text: Abednedo are currently allies of the Rebel Alliance, but their loyalty will not be reinforced until after the Battle of Endor, when the Empire will fragmenting Empire will seen a variety of less-than-sane leaders briefly come to power. During this tumultuous time, Grand Admiral Grunger will use an orbital nightcloak to devastate Abednedo’s environment. After his death in the Corellian system, the Abednedo will become firm allies of the New Republic, and they will staunchly oppose the later efforts of the Galactic Alliance to have any sort of unity with the Imperial Remnant.
csg_abednedo._provenance_note: The Abednedo species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU.

csg_abyssin.name: Abyssin

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound. May also regrow lost limbs after a few weeks.

csg_abyssin.physiology: The Abyssin are large creatures who are extremely muscular. They have one eye that is typically white, yellow, or orange with a black pupil. They have pointed ears and black hair around their face. Most have no neck, as their entire upper chest is filled with muscle. They are not very intelligent but do boast powerful regenerative abilities. Aside from the elderly, the Abyssin can regrow nearly any body part, such as limbs and even organs. As such, they can live for about 300 years.
csg_abyssin.society: The Abyssin have a primitive tribal society that is very violent. They are a brutish people, largely a result of their regeneration. Many don’t realize that other species do not have their extreme toughness or fast healing. Since they lack stable resources, they are organized into nomadic tribes with no centralized government. Because life is so harsh for them, elderly Abyssin often voluntarily exile themselves to die alone rather than waste their tribe’s resources.
csg_abyssin.language: The Abyssin speak Abyssin, a hieroglyphic language of grunts and growls. Most do not know Basic.
csg_abyssin.homeworld: Abyssin come from the desert world of Byss, an Outer Rim planet in the Ash Worlds. It is very hot and very dry. It has twin suns, causing it to have a unique day-night cycle. Many Abyssin are taken offworld as slaves; others go as mercenaries.
csg_abyssin.description: Primitive but powerful, the one-eyed Abyssin boast incredible strength and toughness in addition to regenerative abilities. While some have found them useful as mercenaries, their violent culture makes interaction complicated.
csg_abyssin.sidebar_text: When Abyssin tribes encounter one another, their tradition allows for two options. If both have enough food and water to survive, the two tribes trade with each other in peace and fairness. However, if one tribe severely lacks food or water, that tribe will instigate a “Blooding.” This violent event is a brawl that involves all members of each tribe. It only ends when all the members of one tribe have surrendered, are incapacitated, or are killed. Once the Blooding is over, the surviving tribe takes all of the food and water. While this tradition has worked fine amongst the Abyssin, it is somewhat more problematic with offworlders. Arcona colonists first came to Abyssin, bringing food and water to exchange. However, the poorer Abyssin tribes would instead fight them.

csg_abugartte.name: Ab’Ugartte

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Unpleasant Demeanors
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Fearsome.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_abugartte.physiology: The Ab’Ugartte are a broad-shouldered species of humanoids known primarily for their smell, as they are not particularly hygienic. They are lagomorphic biologically, with long ears that droop beside their head. They have fur in shades ranging from golden to gray, and their nose is fairly small, sitting well above a mouth of sharp teeth. They have a pointed chin, and their eyes tend to be dark. Ab’Ugartte have clawed hands with four fingers, which they use to catch prey that they prefer to eat live.
csg_abugartte.society: Few species are looked down upon more than the Ab’Ugartte, who are notably lacking in terms of both hygiene and humor. Ab’Ugartte have had poor relations with the other species native to their system, which made them regard all aliens with a degree of suspicion. Most trust more in machinery, some to rather extreme degrees, growing unusually fond of completely ordinary tools and even naming them. They are adept as scavengers and repairmen, and they can also make capable starship captains, although they only ever haul cargo, since no living being would ever want to be their passenger. While they are extremely unpleasant for most species, Ab’Ugartte do enjoy the company of their own, and those who enter the wider galaxy tend to travel in small packs of closely-knit friends.
csg_abugartte.language: Ab’Ugartte speak Arttik, and they tend to have a deep voice. While they can speak Basic, many find it more useful to know Farangi or Root.
csg_abugartte.homeworld: Ab’Ugartte come from the world of Ab’Ugard in the Ab’Bshingh system of the southern Outer Rim. It is a double planet with Ab’Bshingh, home of the Farangs and Waroot. Both planets have relatively steamy climates, although Ab’Bshingh is distinctly smaller. Its spindly natives have little interest in dealing with the higher gravity of Ab’Ugard. The planets are tidally locked to one another, meaning that Ab’Bshingh stays at the same place in the sky, looking like an extremely bright moon for the half of Ab’Ugard that faces it.
csg_abugartte.description: Technology is often a better companion for the Ab'Ugartte than other living creatures, who often find them stinky and unpleasant. They often find themselves working as scavengers or in other positions that keep them away from other species, as they prefer to stick to their own kind.
csg_abugartte.sidebar_text: Ab’Ugartte have adapted to millenia of warfare in their star system between the Waroot and the Farangs, and they have come to thrive as scavengers. Swarming like vultures amongst the ruins, the Ab’Ugartte have begun to colonize areas left vacant by warfare, using their advanced technical skills to repair technology. Many now make a good living by reselling salvaged weapons or starships. Many also take up to eating the wasting corpses, as they can eat almost anything if needed. However, they still see meat from living rodents, crustaceans, or insects as a preferable luxury. Ab’Ugartte settlers are not particularly welcomed by either side, who see them as pests to get rid whenever they attempt to resettle.
csg_abugartte._provenance_note: The Ab’Ugartte species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_adarian.name: Adarian

special_abilities.name: Long Call
special_abilities.description: May create a low sound which can be heard up to 20 kilometers away by other Adarians. Once per encounter, may also use it to attack using an easy Resilience check, dealing 4 base damage as strain to all non-Adarians within short range. Have Crit 4, but suffer 2 strain when using this attack.

csg_adarian.physiology: Adarians are mammals distinguished by a tall, wrinkled head which has a large hole that goes through its side. Their skin comes in shades of brown, yellow, or blue, which is mostly dependent on caste. They have no nose or ears, but they have olfactory glands under their skin and thin hairs which can hear even more effectively than the ears of other species. They have a distinctive throat pouch which they can inflate and vibrate to emit a low sound called a long call. They can use it to communicate with each other over long distances, but it can be used as an attack against non-Adarians who are nearby.
csg_adarian.society: Highly intelligent, the Adarians will take a long time to consider before making any sort of decision, but once they have made their choice, they are incredibly stubborn. They place high value in financial success, which gives them a powerful drive to succeed in business, often at the expense of hobbies or relationships. This, when combined with their knack for technology, has ensured that they do well in mining and technology industries.
csg_adarian.language: Adarians have a rigid mouth with no lips, so they have a thick accent when they speak Basic. Their own language, Adarese, is based on pitches and tonal inflections.
csg_adarian.homeworld: Adarians come from the Inner Rim planet of Adari, although it is widely accepted that they immigrated to it thousands of years ago from an unknown homeworld. A cold world with forests and mountains, it is ruled by a government, which is headquartered in the Hall of Decisions, that acts like a corporation. It has prominent industries of mining and manufacturing, but many Adarians are sent offworld to find more business opportunities.
csg_adarian.description: A species with a stubborn focus on financial success, the Adarians have a strict caste system called screel'sara that defines their society. A hole through the side of their head gives them a unique appearance.
csg_adarian.sidebar_text: Adarians are arranged into a caste system called screel’sara, which almost all of them support. Any Adarian will support a member of a higher class and obey their commands. This structure is so successful that their civilization has been stable and avoided any sort of civil unrest. Their government is composed of members in the higher castes. Breaking away from the tiers of the caste structure is unthinkable, so any Adarians in the lower caste who want freedom must leave their planet.

csg_adnerem.name: Adnerem

special_abilities.name: Entrepreneurial
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Wheel and Deal.”

special_abilities.name: Narrow Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for brightness, add setback for darkness.

csg_adnerem.physiology: Adrenem are a species of humanoids with dark gray skin who are relatively slender and an average of two meters tall. Their head is triangular, somewhat similar to that of an Arcona: short on the forehead, wide around the eyes, and with a pointed chin. They have a single lump called an echo chamber atop their head, which functions as their ear. Their eyes, typically in shades of turquoise, are wide but thin in order to prevent them from being blinded by the two suns of their world. They only grow hair on the back of their head, near their neck, which they often braid or bejewel. Their hands have just four fingers, which are fairly dexterous, but they lack thumbs. They have quite sturdy fingernails, and those with more cushy jobs will grow their nails long to show off their status.
csg_adnerem.society: Adnerem tend to be calm and quiet with a rigorous devotion to their professions, and they have little interest in biological families. Talkative only in pursuit of professional connections, they arrange themselves into social units called steri, about five to a hundred Adnerem who generally share a homestead and a profession. They see the steris as their means of advancing their status, and they judge others by how powerful their steris is and how much they can contribute to it. The idea of a rank is foreign to them. Nepotism is also rare, since they have little connection with their parents. From the ages of six to fourteen, Adnerem are adopted into a school-steris, and they enter a professional steris for the decade after that. At the age of 24, they are cut loose and given the chance to join a new steris for their permanent career, although roughly half choose to remain in their original steris, in part due to incentives offered. Adnerem are allowed to leave their steris after that, but they forfeit all possessions, and it comes with a degree of stigma, so they will only change if offered significant incentives from their new steris. All steri interact with one another in a complex web of trading, but larger steri can occasionally abuse their influence, triggering brief raid wars to shift the balance of power. Adnerem prioritize seizing assets rather than destroying them, and they subdue rather than annihilate their enemies. Occasionally, large steri will voluntarily split in order to avoid being targeted by a raid. Adnerem rarely travel; those who do remain with their steris. Such steri usually operate merchant fleets, crime syndicates, or freelance business management teams. One steri has formed a high-end mercenary band called the Interstellar StrikeForce.
csg_adnerem.homeworld: Adnerem come from the hot Expansion Region planet of Adner. It has a fairly diverse economy, importing only specialty goods, although it has become known for tourist attractions like casinos and theme parks.
csg_adnerem.description: Triangular-headed humanoids, the Adnerem are a professional and diligent people who arrange themselves into groups called steri. Steri contain dozens of members who share a profession and live communally, and they value their steris's status over personal advancement.
csg_adnerem.sidebar_text: While Adnerem are notoriously quiet in large groups, their proclivity for social interaction increases in more intimate settings. The most extreme example of this is called the sterika, in which two Adnerem form an extremely close professional bond, something that usually follows periods of stress. Those involved are referred to as sterikai, and they are always from the same steris. Although the relationship is somewhat similar to marriages of other species, it does not involve children, and those who are not part of one do not actively seek it out. Only about a tenth of Adnerem are in a sterika.

csg_advozse.name: Advozse

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add boost on auditory Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Natural Skeptics
special_abilities.description: When assisting an ally, remove 1 uncancelled threat from the final roll in addition to the base benefit.

csg_advozse.physiology: The Advozsec are herbivores who have both reptilian and mammalian heritage. They have no hair and instead have a single black horn. They have blue-gray eyes and pale-yellow skin. Despite their vegetarian diet, they have fairly sharp canine teeth. Their head is fairly wrinkled for the most part. They have relatively good hearing thanks to their pointed ears. They can also see quite well in the dark, although they can adjust to bright lights. While they have opposable thumbs, they only have four fingers.
csg_advozse.society: The Advozsec are a selfish people in general, focusing on their own well-being above all else. While on the whole, they are difficult to be around, they can nevertheless be valuable. This is because the Advozsec are natural sceptics who have a knack for finding issues in plans. Of course, these holes don’t always come to fruition. In those cases, the Advozsec appear as simply paranoid or annoying. They are a very pessimistic people, planning for the worst and expecting the worst. Because they believe material possessions can be so easily lost, they tend to only value money. While they have sought to be part of the CIS, they were occupied by the Republic during the Clone Wars and unable to do anything about it. Of course, they have sought independence from the Empire that now occupies them as well, but the pessimistic Advozsec have acknowledged its futility. Assuming for the worst, few dare to speak up about their beliefs.
csg_advozse.language: The Advozsec speak Advb, a language which is known by almost no one else. Many know Basic.
csg_advozse.homeworld: Advozsec come from Riflor, a planet in the only known star system with three suns. It is in the southwest portion of the Mid Rim. The Advozsec eat fungi that grow around the Riflor’s hot springs. In addition to hot springs, it has many active volcanoes. A Yuuzhan Vong bioplague will later destroy the plant life and kill much of the Advozsec.
csg_advozse.description: Advozsec are yellow-skinned herbivores with a single horn. They come from Riflor, a geologically active planet. This caused most Advozse to learn pessimism and selfishness, traits that continue in the species to this day.
csg_advozse.sidebar_text: Many of Advozsec’s behaviors are a result of their planet’s geology. They have settled near hot springs for heat, but those generally occur in geologically unstable regions. As such, volcanoes are a common problem for them. The destruction of their homes has left them pessimistic and paranoid. However, they have come to understand that financial stability can allow them to rebuild back up to their previous lifestyle. This desire for acquisition of wealth and power makes many of them bureaucrats.

csg_aing_tii.name: Aing-Tii

special_abilities.name: Protective Plates
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Monks
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Forsee Basic Power and the Move Basic Power. When using the Move power, may teleport it instantly rather than move it. Still may not move objects farther than otherwise allowed. When using the Foresee power, may also see into the past.

special_abilities.name: No Vocal Cords
special_abilities.description: Cannot speak.

csg_aing_tii.physiology: Aing-Tii are a unique species of Force-sensitive mammals who are covered by a layer of protective plates. They typically paint their plates with motifs unique to the individual. They are similar in size to humans, but they have a long tail, and they lack a neck, as their head simply juts out perpendicular to their chest. Their hands have three clawed fingers, and their feet end in two claws as well. Their hairless head features two wide eyes and six green tongues which extend about half of a meter beyond their mouth. Aing-Tii are not capable of speech, but they speak using a combination of taste, smell, pheromones, and touch, all via their tongues.
csg_aing_tii.society: Aing-Tii are a people who are all Force-sensitive, and they are highly religious in how they view the Force. They do not call it the Force, and they see it as a gift from “Those Who Dwell Beyond the Veil,” but it is not a gift that they wish to squander by using in excess. They see themselves as completely subordinate to the Force, and they see the Force as having total control of their life. Often living as warrior monks, they spend their lives traversing the Kathol Rift on pilgrimages, only using the Force when absolutely necessary. Their connection to the Force is different than that of either the Light or the Dark Side, so their powers are also different. They are capable of teleporting objects, similar in practicality to telekinesis but instantaneous. Their other unique ability is that of flow-walking, which is much rarer among them, but those who are capable of it surrender their emotions to the Force in order to observe both the future and the past in a more detailed way than simple visions. However, they must be present at the location they wish to observe. Although their own actions can change the future, the Aing-Tii believe that the Force has predestined all things, so that the final outcome will ultimately be the same. Aing-Tii are extremely reclusive, and they have little interest in working with outsiders, learning their ways, or teaching their ways to outsiders. The one exception to this isolationism is the Aing-Tii’s view of slavery, which they detest so much that they will venture into the rest of the galaxy in order to attack slavers, let the slaves go free, and dissapear as suddenly as they came.
csg_aing_tii.language: Aing-Tii cannot speak Basic because they lack vocal chords, and they use their native language to communicate. Eventually, the smuggler Jorj Car’das will design a device that interprets Aing-Tii communication and reads it aloud in Basic.
csg_aing_tii.homeworld: Aing-Tii come from a very hidden planet in the Kathol Rift of the southern Outer Rim. It has a cooler climate than most, and its unique atmosphere means that some humans prefer to use a breath mask on it. The terrain is rocky, and it has several oceans.
csg_aing_tii.description: A unique species of monks, the Aing-Tii are entirely Force-sensitive but view the Force through a philosophy much different than the Jedi or Sith. They are also very xenophobic and keep to themselves.
csg_aing_tii.sidebar_text: Aing-Tii travel on Sanhedrim ships, which are living transports about the size of frigates that have a crew of about one hundred. They are covered by symbols similar to those on the Aing-Tii themselves, and they travel using both the Aing-Tii’s teleportation abilities and their own power. In addition to the unique technology being harder to detect, the living ships boast incredible firepower. Another Aing-Tii innovation is the Vor’cha stun stick, which appears as a wooden staff wrapped in wire and is capable of electrocution.

csg_akurian.name: Akurian

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_akurian.physiology: A larger species of primates comparable to Wookiees in build, the Akurians have thick, white fur in order to protect them from the snowy environment of their homeworld. Because of their ferocity, they are sometimes called Snow Demons or Snow Stompers. Their face, generally not covered by fur, is fairly humanoid with a short nose and a wide mouth, and they have a vertical crest of fur atop their head.
csg_akurian.society: A primitive people, the Akurians have the appearance of simple-minded brutes, and they can be intimidating to other species. They use little technology in their traditional lifestyle, which also involves isolation. As larger nomadic predators, they live on their own or in small units of immediate family, although there are a few occasions where they interact with one another. Some work as merchants, and there are a couple dozen judges across the planet who are paid to act as the government. Because they have little experience with seeing those outside their own family, they come across as strange in demeanor. Often, they are cold and unfriendly, forming cynical rivalries, but they will obey authority without question and expect the same from their subordinates.
csg_akurian.language: Akurians rarely ever speak Basic, as they have little contact with outsiders and cannot always differentiate between its vowels. Their native language, also named Akurian, comes in many dialects, many of which have not been properly studied.
csg_akurian.homeworld: Akurians come from the frigid planet of Akuria II in the Oplovis sector of the northern Outer Rim. It is a very backwater planet with little resources to offer the galactic community, but now that the Imperials have been driven away from it, a few smugglers and other criminals use it as a hideout.
csg_akurian.description: Akurians are large and intimidating primates with little technological development or interest in the outside world. They are independently minded, and while they have no love for the Empire, few have had interest in supporting the broader goals of the Rebel Alliance beyond their homeworld of Akuria II.
csg_akurian.sidebar_text: Akurians were once hunted by Imperials, who had a base on Akuria II and were oblivious to the fact that Akurians are sentient. The Rebel Alliance, which once wanted to make a base of their own there, has made various dealings with the Akurians to help them fight off Imperial rule, including supplying weapons and personnel, hoping that the Akurians would provide support to the Alliance after they emerge victorious. Unfortunately, such an optimistic venture has not worked out exactly as intended. After a longer than expected struggle, the Akurians have indeed earned their freedom, but few have developed genuine friendships with the rebels they fought with or have any interest in fighting in a galaxy-wide war. The vast majority wish to return to their primitive lifestyle, and those who do go offworld typically have a more selfish motivation.
csg_akurian._provenance_note: The Akurian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_aleena.name: Aleena

special_abilities.name: Sturdy Frames
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

csg_aleena.physiology: At 80 centimeters and 50 kilograms on average, Aleena are a small and fast species of warm-blooded reptiles. Proportionally, their body is rather long with short legs and arms. Despite their short stride, they have quick reflexes, and a fast metabolism gives them large amounts of energy: enough energy to outrun much larger predators. Though their hands have only four stubby fingers, they are nevertheless superior to many species in terms of dexterity. Their somewhat scaled skin is mostly blue-gray and typically grayest at the chin and chest. Their hairless head also includes a wide mouth of sharp teeth, downward-pointing ears, noseless nostrils, and a pointed forehead.
csg_aleena.society: Aleena are social creatures, thriving the most amongst their own families or with other closely-knit groups. They live in villages with large groups of their extended family members. They are very loyal and dedicated to their families and friends, travelling with them even if they leave the planet. They are also innately curious, eager to see new things. Their food is omnivorous and known for being extremely spicy.
csg_aleena.language: Most Aleena can speak Aleena, which is their native language, and Basic.
csg_aleena.homeworld: The Aleena homeworld is the Inner Rim planet of Aleen, which, despite its verdant terrain, is a very dangerous planet. Predatory sagcatchers continue to plague the Aleena because of their great speed, as do the scatalpens. Despite these troubles, the Aleena have built a well-functioning society, including a prominent sporting industry. However, because of their love of tourism and exploration, they are scattered throughout the galaxy.
csg_aleena.description: Aleena are adventurous reptiles who are very family oriented. They are small but very fast, and their advanced reflexes grant them an edge in many sports, such as Podracing.
csg_aleena.sidebar_text: Tourism is a preferred hobby of most Aleena, and their dedication to family means that Aleena families touring is common sight at many metropolises, historical sites, amusement parks, or sporting events. Podracing is a particularly common sport for Aleena, whose quick reflexes and dexterity grant an edge. The Aleen Classic is one of the most important races on their homeworld.

csg_amani.name: Amani

special_abilities.name: Dispersed Organs
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Poisonous Skin
special_abilities.description: When attacked by a Brawl check that generates threat, may make the attacker suffer wounds equal to the number of threat.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering one or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover one additional wound. May also regrow lost limbs after a few months.

special_abilities.name: Rolling
special_abilities.description: As a maneuver, may begin rolling. When rolling, must spend at least 1 maneuver per round moving, but this maneuver may move 2 range bands.

csg_amani.physiology: Amanin, also known as Amanaman, are a planarian race similar to worms. They secrete a minor poison onto their skin to deter predators. Their green and yellow skin helps to camouflage their body in rainforests, but their massive two or three meter stature makes them stick out. They have short legs, long arms, and a long, wide neck. Their hairless head is flat, and with keen nostrils and small, red, eyes that can see well in the dark. While they appear relatively slow and clumsy when walking, they can move very quickly when they choose to curl into a ball and roll. They are also effective in trees, swinging from their long arms. They are very difficult to kill, as all of their vital organs all have multiple copies that are dispersed throughout the body. In theory, an Amani could even survive being vertically cut in half, with each half regrowing into a full version of the original Amani. It is also speculated that Amanin reproduce hermaphroditically, as their genders have yet to be distinguished by scientists. Perhaps the most odd facet of their biology is that they remove waste through their mouth, although they have learned that this act is best done in private.
csg_amani.society: The Amani culture is very primitive, and they live in tribes of nomadic hunters led by lorekeepers. They love exchanging stories but are also a violent people, and tribes will fight each other for control of a forest in bouts called takitals. Despite the temporary violence, takitals still ultimately lead to understanding and peace between tribes. Despite their size, they prefer to be stealthy and unnoticed, although they do carry a very unsubtle staff that is often adorned with the heads of vanquished foes, sometimes earning them the nickname “Head Hunters.”
csg_amani.language: The Amanin cannot read, and few speak Basic. They only speak their native language, Amanese, and they have a deep voice.
csg_amani.homeworld: Amanin come from Maridun, an Outer Rim world of Amanin-inhabited rainforests and savannahs, which they call gruntak. With the Empire shifting their attention away, criminal factions now dominate it.
csg_amani.description: The Amani are large worm-like predators from the grasslands of Maridun, where they live as primitive hunters. While some have been taken as slaves, their large size and innate poison allow many to escape and become mercenaries or bounty hunters.
csg_amani.sidebar_text: One takital that changed the Amanin forever was the one that an Imperial mining operation inadvertently started. Called by outsiders as the Battle of Maridun, this takital saw Amanin and Imperials battle through several days of fighting. In the resulting stalemate, the Empire agreed to stay off of tribal lands in exchange for ownership of captives from further takitals. These captives became slaves offworld, introducing the Amanin who escape to the rest of the galaxy, where some now work as scouts, mercenaries, or laborers.

csg_amaran.name: Amaran

special_abilities.name: Demanding Negotiators
special_abilities.description: After making a Negotiation check, may suffer 2 strain to convert 1 triumph into 2 success.

csg_amaran.physiology: The Amarans are small-sized creatures that share vulpine and canine heritage. They are covered in fur, which is typically red-orange with a white spot on the chest. Their fur is relatively short aside from their bushy tail and tufted cheeks. They have a pointed white muzzle with a small mouth. They also have small black eyes and a black nose, and their ears are large and pointed. While the Amarans have no toes, they do have four-fingered hands with thin claws.
csg_amaran.society: The Amarans are a social people, so many work in roles related to leadership. They are a mobile species that likes to form colonies. Even more Amaran travel for business and job opportunities. Negotiation comes naturally to them, although they are notorious for spending far longer than other species in the process. While this long-winded bargaining can be a waste of time in some cases, many Amaran manage much better deals when they make others cave out of frustration. Many are also good at dealing with animals, so some find work as ranchers or beast charmers. Others combine these abilities to sell animals. Unlike some other furred creatures, they typically wear clothing.
csg_amaran.language: Amarans often know many languages, as they like to travel and be social. Typically, Basic is one of them.
csg_amaran.homeworld: The Amarans originally come from Amar, a terrestrial Inner Rim world. However, they are often seen on other planets. Many live on the watery Mid Rim world of Naboo, where they inhabit swamps and work as ranchers for the native bursa. These swamps also feature a primitive species, the Gungans. Those on Vulptereen and other worlds related to the Trade Federations mostly focus on business management, leadership, and other white-collar jobs. They can also be found on many other planets like Coruscant, often as merchants or traders.
csg_amaran.description: Small vulpines with a large tail, the Amarans are persistent negotiators and savvy ranchers. They often work in animal handling, business, or both. They have travelled to many planets and often learn many languages.
csg_amaran.sidebar_text: While the Amarans originally hail from Amar, their nature for business makes many of them travel offworld. In particular, many have worked with the Trade Federation as managers or middle men. One of the planets that many have come to for business is Vulpter. This highly polluted Deep Core planet had many Amarans, who made up about six percent of the population. It was used as a storage world for the Trade Federation, with its underground facilities managed by immigrant Amarans while the native Vulptereen handled menial labor. This arrangement meant that the Amarans were greatly disliked by the Vulptereen. The Amarans on Vulpter were also disliked by their own people, as their homeworld chose to stay with the Republic. After the end of the Clone Wars, the Amaran immigrants who worked for their Trade Federation suddenly lost their offworld benefactors in addition to being trapped on the planet by Imperial regulations regarding the Deep Core. With their hostile relations combined with poverty, the life for Amarans on Vulpter is now difficult.

csg_amorphiian_being.name: Amorphiian Being

special_abilities.name: Power Fluctuations
special_abilities.description: If a check generates threat, the GM may spend it to trigger a power fluctuation or glitch, which induces 1 strain per threat as well as 1 of the following penalties per threat. The penalties may be removed by rubbing or pulling on a body part, which requires a maneuver.

special_abilities.name: Power Fluctuations Penalty 1
special_abilities.description: Lose the free maneuver.

special_abilities.name: Power Fluctuations Penalty 2
special_abilities.description: Reduce a characteristic by 1.

special_abilities.name: Power Fluctuations Penalty 3
special_abilities.description: Become completely mute or have a dramatic change in voice.

csg_amorphiian_being.physiology: Amorphiian Beings appear as humans, completely indistinguishable at first glance, but what is inside them is very different, and it shows in how they act. They are very machine-like, making strange beeps and whirring sounds, and they tend to move in an inorganic, robotic fashion. They are also prone to power fluctuations that dramatically impair their functionality: Sometimes, one of their digits or facial muscles will rapidly twitch, other times it will slow down the movement of a particular limb. Their voice can also be affected, having rapid changes in pitch or volume. These glitches have strange fixes, and Amorphiian Beings can often recalibrate and return to normal functioning by providing sensory inputs. Pulling on a finger might make their voice normal again, or rubbing on their stomach might allow them to move a leg.
csg_amorphiian_being.society: Amorphiians tend to be efficient and emotionless, fitting their robotic appearance. They are polite with respect for protocols, and they tend to see through their plans. Though tech-savvy and intelligent when given time to think, they struggle to improvise and can be overwhelmed by the unexpected. They prefer solitude as they find other species to be very erratic.
csg_amorphiian_being.language: Amorphiians speak Basic as while as a unique machine language of beeps and whistles.
csg_amorphiian_being.homeworld: The planet of Amorphiia is a backwater world in the Western Reaches that has long been trying to establish itself in the technology industry. However, Amorphiian-run businesses have something of an image problem, so most of the planet works in mines or factories that are owned by offworld businesses.
csg_amorphiian_being.description: A strange species of cyborgs, the Amorphiian beings have modifications to the core of the bodies that run so deep, the machines even pass on their nature to the children. They are efficient and skilled with technology, but they are beset by occasional glitches to their own software.
csg_amorphiian_being.sidebar_text: The machine-like appearance and behaviors of the Amorphiian Beings is no ruse, for they are, in fact, part machine. Their species started off as an innocent experiment in advanced self-repairing cybernetics given to a wealthy amputee named Kella Hough, but the technology started to learn faster than anyone realized. Drawing power from her nervous system and even acquiring raw materials from metals in her diet, the cybernetics were able to take over her mind, body, and even genetic code, ultimately transferring to her children. Two of them died, one was infertile, but one was healthy and able to reproduce. Many saw the Houghs as bizarre and viewed the cybernetics like an infection, so the ostracized family made a colony on a world they called Amorphiia. A handful of curious humans followed, and within a few generations, the cybernetics had taken over the entirety of the colony. Glitches still exist, but the cybernetics are more stable now, thoroughly implanted into their genome to the point where Amorphiians can safely reproduce among their own but not with humans. Many humans are still deeply unsettled by the strange cyborgs, however.
csg_amorphiian_being._provenance_note: The Amorphiian Being species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_annoo_dat_blue.name: Annoo-dat Blue

special_abilities.name: Colored Scales
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Deception checks if eye scales aren’t covered.

csg_annoo_dat_blue.physiology: The Annoo-dat Blue are a species of reptiles with scaly skin in shades of light turquoise. They are big creatures, two meters tall on average and often heftier than humans, with a wide neck and bulbous chin. They have no hair, and their ears are pointed. They are distinguished by having three nostrils and spots on their cheeks, but of more critical importance are actually their heavy brows. The scales on these eyebrows can change color based on the Annoo-dat’s emotions, which often proves to be a valuable tell. Making up for this disadvantage, Annoo-dat benefit from extreme longevity, living about ten times longer than humans.
csg_annoo_dat_blue.society: Annoo-dat do not have a very high reputation in the galaxy, known mostly for being thugs and gangsters. Powerful crime families dominate society, particularly the Fromm Gang, which is known for their use of Spaarti cloning cylinders to grow a small army. The crimes of the Annoo-dat rarely involve much subtlety, thanks in part to their physiology, although a few have been known to find clever ways around this. This ability to deceive is also apparent when gambling, where a surprising number of Annoo-dat have taken interest in games of chance. Controlling the color changes in their scales is a very challenging feat for them to master, but those who do are often highly eager to show it off in games such as sabacc. Because of their longevity, the Annoo-dat are known for being excellent planners, and they always have long-term visions which many species perceive as slow-moving. This slowness has also applied to adapting technology. Since their first contact with offworlders was in 322 BBY, the days before it are still in living memory for the majority of their species.
csg_annoo_dat_blue.language: Annoo-dat once spoke Tra’ang’a, but they have since adopted the Annoo-dat Prime’s language, called Dat-an. While most young Annoo-dat are now taught Basic, those more than a couple centuries old have a hard time learning it. Many can’t manage its subtle vowel distinctions, and their voice is often gravelly.
csg_annoo_dat_blue.homeworld: Once known as Gelefil, the world of Annoo is a grassy agrarian planet just north of Hutt Space. Its southern hemisphere is more modernized than the north, though both deal with more than their share of government corruption. The Annoo-dat coexist with a substantial immigrant population of humans and other species wanting to avoid either the Empire or the Hutts.
csg_annoo_dat_blue.description: A criminally-inclined species of reptiles with blue-green skin, the Annoo-dat Blue are on the large side, but their ability for deceit is limited by their scales that change color with emotion. They consider themselves one species with the Annoo-dat Prime, an unrelated species that conquered their planet.
csg_annoo_dat_blue.sidebar_text: Annoo-dat is not actually the original name for their species, who once were the peaceful Ret native to Gelefil. This changed centuries ago, when their first meeting with offworlders began a violent conquest by the quicker and more technologically developed Annoo-dat. Once the Ret were subjugated, the invaders made Gelefil their new home, renaming it Annoo. For the most part, the Ret came to accept this change, considering it a lesson learned that pacifism was weakness. They even renamed themselves the Annoo-dat as a symbol of unity, hoping to participate in their conquerors’ glory. While xenologists often use the terms Annoo-dat Blue and Annoo-dat Prime to distinguish the two species, the Annoo-dat are quite happy to share the same name. However, a minority of Annoo-dat Blue are secretly happy for a different reason: They see the name change as a means to steal the identity of the Annoo-dat Prime after they annihilate the Prime and retake Annoo.
csg_annoo_dat_blue._provenance_note: Little is known about Annoo-dat Blue society. The remainder of this information has a few assumptions based on subtle comments but is mostly made up. However, I need to fill this page, and having societal information should make Annoo-dat Blue characters more interesting. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they imagine their own aspects of Annoo-dat Blue culture.

csg_annoo_dat_prime.name: Annoo-dat Prime

special_abilities.name: Extra Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Nimble Physiology
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Dodge.”

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_annoo_dat_prime.physiology: The Annoo-dat Prime are a species of lanky reptiles with an extra set of eyes that can see infrared, and strangely, a minority of the species also hatches with an extra set of arms. Whether they are of the two or four-armed variety, their arms have hands with four dark-clawed fingers. Annoo-dat average about two and a half meters in height, and they are exceptionally strong, with quality athleticism and quick reflexes that make them extremely dangerous in combat. They have ridged skin of hues of ochre, and their head is covered by sharp horns rather than hair. Their mouth is laden with incisors, and they have a long tongue that they use to smell. The species is further distinguished by their dark, lengthy hair, and they have a long tail.
csg_annoo_dat_prime.society: The Annoo-dat are a violent and direct people, inclined toward straightforward conquest of their most immediate goals. They display kindness only to whom they choose and when they feel like it. Around their enemies, there is little concept of showing mercy or trying to avoid collateral damage. This lack of control often makes them unpopular as mercenaries, so even though most would prefer a combative profession, they often end up as laborers. They have minimal social skills even among their own kind, so their difficulties finding mates has limited their overall population. Their young receive little care and are expected to be able to fend for themselves quickly after hatching.
csg_annoo_dat_prime.language: The Annoo-dat Prime’s language, which is called Dat-an, is the dominant language of Annoo, even among the Annoo-dat Blue. The Annoo-dat Prime are only slightly more inclined to learn Basic than the Blue, and they have a raspy voice.
csg_annoo_dat_prime.homeworld: The Annoo-dat Prime left their original homeworld, Annoo, and settled on the planet once known as Gelefil, which they renamed as Annoo in honor of their old world. It is a grassy agrarian planet just north of Hutt Space. Its southern hemisphere is more modernized than the north, though both deal with more than their share of government corruption. The Annoo-dat coexist with a substantial immigrant population of humans and other species wanting to avoid either the Empire or the Hutts.
csg_annoo_dat_prime.description: Annoo-dat Prime are a violent race of strong and lanky reptiles with infrared vision, sharp claws, and heightened reflexes. After destroying their world in a war, they conquered another planet which they renamed Annoo, whose natives are now also referred to as Annoo-dat.
csg_annoo_dat_prime.sidebar_text: The name Annoo-dat can actually refer to two species, the Prime and the Blue. They come from separate worlds, with the latter originally known as the Ret. This changed centuries ago, when the Annoo-dat Prime society on Annoo was torn apart by a series of violent coups funded by Hutt gangsters who were hoping to form shadow governments on the planet. Nobody won, and the bloody conflict resulted in ecological disaster, so the Annoo-dat fled for Gelefil. Being quicker and more technologically developed than the then-peaceful native Ret, they were able to quickly conquer them in 322 BBY. They made Gelefil their new home, renaming it Annoo. For the most part, the Ret came to accept this change, considering it a lesson learned that pacifism was weakness. They even renamed themselves the Annoo-dat as a symbol of unity, hoping to participate in their conquerors’ glory. While xenologists often use the terms Annoo-dat Blue and Annoo-dat Prime to distinguish the two species, the Annoo-dat are quite happy to share the same name. Ironically, the Annoo-dat Prime generally lack the leadership skills to run a government, so it is the Blue who mostly rule.
csg_annoo_dat_prime._provenance_note: Little is known about Annoo-dat Prime society. The remainder of this information has a few assumptions based on subtle comments but is mostly made up. However, I need to fill this page, and having societal information should make Annoo-dat Prime characters more interesting. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they imagine their own aspects of Annoo-dat Prime culture.

csg_anomid.name: Anomid

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: No Vocal Cords
special_abilities.description: May not speak without a vocalizer mask, which costs 100 credits.

special_abilities.name: Vast Wealth
special_abilities.description: Gain +1,100 starting credits.

csg_anomid.physiology: Anomids are humanoids with translucent skin that comes in varying shades of purple. They are typically somewhat thin, and they prefer technical work to physical labor. Younger ones typically have long dark hair, while older ones are bald or have very little hair. They have yellow or blue eyes that lack visible pupils. Their ears are flat and pointed. Most unique about their head is that they have no vocal cords whatsoever, so they cannot effectively speak on their own. Their hands have two end fingers, two middle fingers, and two thumbs, all of which end in claws.
csg_anomid.society: Anomids are technically gifted and have made great wealth because of it. They were quick to discover space travel, and they made contact with the rest of the galaxy in 15,000 BBY when a drought caused food shortages. They began to trade and became prominent in commerce thanks to their advanced technology. They are especially good at building computers, especially those that are small and light. They learned advanced agricultural techniques from the Ithorians, a gift that the Anomids remember to this day. They continue to have success in farming, which is the main industry on their homeworld. They are also very pacifist, as no major wars have been fought in their history. This makes them respect the Jedi, and some privately disagree with the Empire. A few even donate to the Rebellion.
csg_anomid.language: Anomids use a sign language, which only can be used by those who have six fingers. This means that those who communicate with offworlders must know Basic, which they speak via their vocalizer mask.
csg_anomid.homeworld: Anomids come from the wealthy Outer Rim agriworld of Yablari, which is ruled by a Central Council of prominent businessmen. Its legal system is complicated and cumbersome, as they never repeal any laws. Instead, they create new laws that counteract the older laws when needed.
csg_anomid.description: Anomids are a mute species, so they must use a vocalizer mask or sign language with their six-fingered hands. Despite this challenge, they have had great financial success thanks to their technical skills.
csg_anomid.sidebar_text: Anomids are distinguished by what they wear. Almost all have vocalizer masks, which read mouth movements and play sounds in response, allowing them to emulate spoken languages. These masks are often stylized or ornately decorated, and they show information such as wealth, heritage, and profession. Anomids also typically wear long, oversized robes, although this isn’t always the case. About 70 years ago, a nonconformist culture began that wore light, sleeveless clothes. These nonconformists also were often pacifists.

csg_anx.name: Anx

special_abilities.name: Anatomical Knowledge
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Lethal Blows.”

special_abilities.name: Socially Savvy
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

special_abilities.name: Mood Crests
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Deception checks if head crest isn’t covered.

csg_anx.physiology: Anx are very tall reptilians, and they can be four meters high. Their thin, hairless head has a crest extending upward and a chin extending downward. The crest can change color based on mood, so they have a very difficult time hiding their emotions. They also have no nose. To maintain balance on their high gravity world, they have a hunched posture and a tail extending backwards. Their feet are also larger, since they have toes pointing backward as well as two toes on each foot that point forward. Their skin is a leathery brown, yellow, or blue. Though their eyesight is poor, they can smell very well. They have three stomachs, which consume an entirely vegetarian diet of mostly leaves.
csg_anx.society: Anx are a sociable people who have evolved from herd animals. They live in large, complicated clans. They tend to obsess about people and get to know all of their family very well. For those offworld, this also applies to their friends and all sorts of other acquaintances. They are very curious in general, so many choose to explore other worlds. While Anx are normally peaceful, their curiosity about people has given them a reputation as warriors. This is because they are highly familiar with the biology of all sorts of sentients, so Anx can be surprisingly effective in combat, crippling or wounding opponents with one well-placed attack.
csg_anx.language: Anx speak the language of Anx, but many know Basic as well. They have a very deep voice.
csg_anx.homeworld: Anx come from Gravlex Med, but few live on it anymore. The Empire has badly mismanaged the planet’s resources, and industrial pollution has turned the savannahs into a hazardous wasteland. The Anx have fled offworld to their many colonies.
csg_anx.description: A very tall people who are sociable and peaceful, the Anx love to talk. While they may wear their emotions on their sleeve metaphorically, they literally show them on a crest above their head. Anx evolved from herd animals, so they are very attached to their large families.
csg_anx.sidebar_text: Anx value sharing emotions as a people, and they are often eager to talk about their feelings with their friends and family. (They are also very eager to listen to the feelings of their friends and family.) However, talking isn’t always necessary. Anx display their moods by the colors of their crests. This makes them struggle with hiding their emotions, and lying can be very difficult for them. Few even bother trying. Those that do must cover their crests with a cloak of some sort. However, covering their crests is seen as very odd and is almost a taboo when among their people. Among other sentients, many realize that a covered crest is an indication that an Anx cannot be trusted. This suspicion sometimes makes it just as difficult for an Anx to successfully lie, even if they cover their crest.

csg_anzat.name: Anzat

special_abilities.name: Advanced Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for darkness. Add boost on olfactory or auditory Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Unique Circulatory System
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for temperature.

special_abilities.name: Feeders
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 3 advantage to hit with proboscis, forcing the target to make a Discipline check opposed by Coercion. If failed, the target is subdued, becoming incapacitated and receiving the injury “Bleeding Out.” After feeding for the first time, receive 20 points of obligation for addiction to feeding in this way. May not select this obligation during character creation.

special_abilities.name: Hypnotic Telepathy
special_abilities.description: As an action, may make an opposed Discipline vs. Discipline check against a chosen target within short range. May reduce their Willpower by 1 for 1 round per success.

special_abilities.name: Recognition of the Force
special_abilities.description: When tracking a Force-sensitive target, add boosts equal to the target’s Force Rating.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 2 additional wounds.

csg_anzat.physiology: The Anzati are a near-human species who feed off of the “soup” of sentients. Beyond a more pale skin color and a larger nose with flared nostrils, an Anzat can easily pass as human against a brief inspection. However, when the time is right, Anzati release thin proboscises out of pores in their cheeks. Similar to tentacles, these can go into nostrils and take a delicious soup out of a victim. The soup goes by many names, including “luck” and “sea of memory.” Regardless, drinking it is almost certain to kill the victim, and the Anzati are addicted to it. They strongly prefer soup of those who are lucky, clever, or strong in the Force. They live for about a millennium, and they have a moderate form of hypnotic Force-based telepathy. They also boast a powerful combination of great athleticism, low-light vision, enhanced hearing and smell, immunity to hot or cold climates, and regenerative abilities. Perhaps most strangely of all, they have no detectable pulse.
csg_anzat.society: While most Anzati place their value and purpose in the quest for soup, there are still other characteristics and values that define them. Though not social and almost always alone, they can nevertheless be interested in the arts, although they tend to eventually find that the art is meaningless. Their longevity causes many of them to become very lonely, and most have a “kill or be killed” sort of mentality.
csg_anzat.language: Anzati speak Anzat, a very old language whose written form is now dead. Most Anzati use Basic to interact with others, and they have no given names, instead choosing aliases that help them best blend in.
csg_anzat.homeworld: The world of Anzat is a misty Mid Rim world that is rightfully avoided by most non-Anzati, who have hardly ever been known to return. The Anzati live in stone buildings and usually leave it to hunt.
csg_anzat.description: Perhaps no species is more feared than the Anzati. Though near-human, they have proboscises which can be used to "feed" off of the "soup" of other sentients. They boast a number of superhuman abilities such as incredible strength, immunity to heat or cold, and telepathy, all of which combine to make them nightmarishly dangerous.
csg_anzat.sidebar_text: Anzati are best known for feeding on sentients, which makes many distrustful of them, should they be recognized, as many species have terrifying legends of the Anzati. Once they have chosen a target, they are typically deliberate and secretive, blending into crowds before finally choosing to strike. However, they are highly obsessive, unable to think of anything but the hunt, especially as they age. Although they sometimes hunt in groups, these informal alliances are very rare. A few brave beings do intentionally choose to employ the Anzati as assassins or hunters.
csg_anzat._provenance_note: Since the Anzati are a mysterious species, some GMs may wish to consider one or more of their abilities as mere myths and adjust the profile accordingly.

csg_anzellan.name: Anzellan

special_abilities.name: Microvision
special_abilities.description: Add boost on checks to see tiny details up close.

csg_anzellan.physiology: Anzellans are one the galaxy's smallest sentient species, about a quarter of a meter in height. They have skin in shades of pink, tan, and gray, and they have three digits on each of their limbs. Their wide head lacks a nose but boasts two wide eyes, both of which have micro-lenses that are capable of seeing details which would be microscopic to other species. They typically have whiskers of some sort.
csg_anzellan.society: Tending to plan ahead extensively, Anzellans are a detail-oriented people. They believe that everything can be optimized, the concepts such as subjectivity or multiple valid approaches are generally foreign to them. Anzellans are a technically inclined species, so this is apparent in their work. They prefer to mass-produce, finding overarching solutions that are repeated to the letter in every scenario. Although most of their technology is rarely seen among other species because it is intended only for usage by smaller species, those who do utilise Anzellan technology will discover that it has been carefully planned and is almost never modified or revised in any way. Because of these tendencies, Anzellans excel in research and development work but are overwhelmed when needing to improvise with limited time or facing problems where their usual solutions do not work. Many Anzellans learn to trust the counsel of other species in these situations, while those who do not are often overwhelmed.
csg_anzellan.language: Anzellans rarely ever speak Basic, and they continue to use their native language of Nazellia. Even those who know Basic use Nazellia whenever they have the chance to, as they see it as the optimal language.
csg_anzellan.homeworld: Anzellans come from Zell, a mostly urban Mid Rim planet with sizable manufacturing industries. Their architecture is incredibly dull, having little decoration and being eerily uniform in its utilitarian style. Because it is designed exclusively for beings of their small size, offworlders spend little time on it beyond the spaceports.
csg_anzellan.description: A tiny species averaging a quarter or a meter tall, the Anzellans are adapted for technical work rather than anything physical, and they have eyes which can see incredibly tiny details up close.
csg_anzellan.sidebar_text: Although their small size can be a setback in many situations, Anzellans often take advantage of it by travelling offworld, where their cost of living is much lower than it would be for members of larger species. With their expenses much lower, Anzellans are often able to save up enough money to last a year during only a few months of work. As such, many of them are able to spend much of their time relaxing, vacationing, or working on hobbies. Unfortunately, this has created a stereotype that Anzellans are lazy or uncommitted to their work, and it has tainted their reputation in the corporate world.
csg_anzellan._provenance_note: The Anzellan species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU. Almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_aqualish.name: Aqualish

special_abilities.name: Blubber
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold or wet conditions, add setback for hot or dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Forest Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback when tracking outdoors.

special_abilities.name: Four Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater.

csg_aqualish.physiology: Aqualish are fairly average in height, but their body is well muscled and, in the case of the Aquala, insulated by a layer of fat. Depending on the subspecies, they can have hands or fins and two or four eyes. Either way, the Aqualish are a combination of arachnid and aquatic mammal species. Their two enamel-covered mandibles that extend from the jaw are resemblant of those on many large and can be used to dig or crack open shells. The tusks are extremely sensitive, and many often massage them against wood. Their black eyes do best in darker conditions, and doubly so for the Ualaq. They are amphibious, adept swimmers, and their blubbery skin, which comes in shades of green, gray, and black, has a rough, rubbery texture.
csg_aqualish.society: Aqualish culture centers on belligerence and strength, and they are unsubtly hostile when first meeting anyone as a means of judging their fortitude. For those who do not stand up, they will continue to bully. Aqualish were on the verge of wiping themselves out in a brutal race war before they were visited by offworlders, causing the races to unite in murdering the crew, stealing the ship, and starting a conquest of nearby worlds. However, Aqualish struggle with technology, and their haphazard contraptions were quickly outdone by the Republic’s engineering. After surrendering, the Andoan government was forced to accept guidance from offworld advisors. In recent decades, the Imperials have imposed martial law.
csg_aqualish.language: All subspecies speak dialects of a language known as Aqualish, which cannot be spoken by other species. When they speak Basic, their tone is abrasive.
csg_aqualish.homeworld: The Aqualish share the world of Ando, which is almost entirely water. Land covers just five percent of the planet, and it is shrouded by fog, with terrain devoted to rainforests, swamps, and rocky caves. A fairly minor world, it sits in the Mid Rim along the Corellian Run. The capital, Quantill City, is the home to Imperial legislation and the only major spaceport. Most of the planet is segregated by subspecies.
csg_aqualish.description: Racial separations divide the Aqualish, and they are often belligerent. Though they may lack subtlety, they make up for it with natural strength and aquatic abilities.
csg_aqualish.sidebar_text: The Aqualish have many racial differences. Most numerous and respected are the Aquala, who usually stay on Ando because their fins are not ideal for gripping outside technology. They prefer oceanic environments, where many make a living as fishers, and their skin in shades of dark turquoise helps them blend in with the water. The Quara, who live in the wetlands, are second in terms of power and the most humanoid. Their five fingers and two eyes make them fit in well offworld. They are also the fewest in number. They maintain better standing than the Ualaq, but are still blamed for the species' reputation as thugs. The Ualaq are the most persecuted and also the rarest. Their extra pair of eyes is adapted for night vision, which allows them to hunt in dark caves and forests. They have a variable number of fingers, ranging from three to five. Many have fled persecution, making them a very common sight offworld.

csg_araquia.name: Araquia

special_abilities.name: Medical Experts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Surgeon.”

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: May fill body with air and spend four maneuvers to prepare a wide sheet of web, which can be used to float. When floating, hover above the ground and move if pushed by the wind. May make an average Coordination check to move one range band in any direction, including upward.

special_abilities.name: Paralytic Bite
special_abilities.description: May spend 3 advantage on a successful Brawl check to bite. A target who has been bitten must pass an average Resilience check or become Immobilized for the rest of the encounter.

special_abilities.name: Webs
special_abilities.description: May shoot webs once per encounter, attacking within short range using Athletics. Deal no damage, but have the Ensnare 3 quality. May also use webs as a tool similar to rope.

csg_araquia.physiology: Araquia are six-legged arachnids who are about two meters tall. They have dark green skin, spindly limbs, and a large abdomen behind their limbs. They have six black eyes, each near a corresponding shoulder, and the front of their body features a mouth surrounded by two mandibles. They are omnivores, capable of eating vegetation as well as rodents, avians, and insects. They can catch their prey using a variety of natural weapons, including a poisonous bite, which has a paralyzing effect. Before using this bite, they typically restrain their prey by shooting sticky webs. Araquia can also use thick stands of web like a rope to lower themselves safely, or they can create large wings out of their silk. They can then fill themselves with air, and the wings are able to lift them off the ground. However, they have little control over their flight and must be carried by the wind.
csg_araquia.society: Araquia are pacifistic: They never kill sentient beings, and even animals they often leave alone should vegetarian food be available. They are expert healers and doctors, and they have extensive knowledge of the herbs and fungi on their homeworld which have medicinal properties. Doctors have a key role as leaders among them, although their tribes also have a governing council. Despite their skills in advanced medicine, they live simple lives, building homes in rural rainforest canopies and catching prey with their webs. For those not involved in medical industries, many become wilderness experts.
csg_araquia.language: Araquia can speak Basic, although most of them only know their chattering native language, Tep'Bo'Araquia.
csg_araquia.homeworld: Araquia come from Kirtania, a planet in the northern part of the Outer Rim. It is verdant but humid, particularly in the rainforests where the Araquia live. The humans are divided into three nations: Dulai, Surana, and Kinkosa, the latter of whom are allied with the Empire. Their largest city is Kinkosa City, which has a spaceport and an Imperial work camp.
csg_araquia.description: Rainforest-dwelling arachnids, the Araquia have developed the unique ability to float around by spinning webs that act as wings, allowing them to gently float through the air. They are very pacifistic, often vegetarian, and skilled in medical professions.
csg_araquia.sidebar_text: Araquia have always been fairly few in number, never having more than a million of them, but their population is now on the verge of extinction, with only around 1,500 remaining. This is because of human colonialism, as the new arrivals have damaged some of their habitats and even hunted them as a result of a cultural misunderstanding. Even worse, some humans sold Araquia territory to the Empire, which has begun a massive deforestation campaign while building a supply station. The famous Araquia doctor T’Jaleq Kith’Araquia tried to reason with them, but he was branded as a rebel and nearly killed. Currently, the remaining Araquia wage war on the Empire, but they refuse to take any lives. Instead, they destroy equipment, hoping that it will make Imperial operations too costly to continue.

csg_arcona.name: Arcona

special_abilities.name: Desert Natives
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for arid or hot conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Unique Senses
special_abilities.description: Add setback on visual Perception checks, but remove this penalty if smell or heat sensing can also be used.

csg_arcona.physiology: Arcona are cold-blooded reptiles with a triangular head and hard skin that comes in shades of gray, brown or dark terracotta. They have green eyes, but their vision is extremely blurred. To make up for this, the protuberance between their eyes, which resembles a nose, actually detects heat and is sensitive enough to distinguish particular species. They instead smell using their slender tongue, which they often flick in and out, to the annoyance of other species. They are adapted to eating a diet that is thoroughly contaminated by their planet’s ammonia, which they need to survive. When travelling offworld, they can make due with adding small ammonia supplements to their food. They can survive without them in the short term but will suffer long term health effects should they go too long.
csg_arcona.society: Arcona value community almost to the point of being a hive mind. Raising a family and being a part of one is considered both a vital duty and a prized privilege. Since marriage is such a sacred commitment to them, they take months or years of research before even beginning to court their future spouse. Males tend to be the primary caregivers, since, by Arconan standards, females tend to be more reckless and unreliable. They tend to put the good of their community before their own desires and expect the same from others. The nests that they organize themselves into combine to make Grand Nests, which meet every twenty days. Although Arcona are fond of tradition, and very few would separate from their families, they are actually quite common travellers. They enjoy visiting or colonizing new worlds, but they usually go with their families or even entire nests.
