csg_arcona.language: Arcona are practical, teaching their children Basic before they learn Arconese. They have a hissing accent and prefer to use “we” instead of “I.” Their names are also reversed relative to most species, with their family name before their individual name.
csg_arcona.homeworld: Cona is a hot and dry world in the Inner Rim with a blue star. There is no freestanding water, but its plant life can produce it via chemical reactions with the ammonia. Uniquely, it has no axial tilt or eccentricity in its orbit, so there are no seasonal variations. High levels of ammonia give it a bad smell, and other species need a breath mask.
csg_arcona.description: Arcona are a very community-oriented species of reptiles who are very restrained with one notable exception: They can become addicted if they have too much salt, which acts like a narcotic for them.
csg_arcona.sidebar_text: Although Arcona are generally known for restraint, they still have a weakness: sodium chloride. This compound, otherwise known as salt, is very common in the galaxy, but for the Arcona, it causes extreme hallucinations and turns their eyes from green to an unhealthy yellow. Arcona need 25 grams of salt per day if they become addicted but are generally not affected by “impure” salts, such as foods with an ordinary amount of salt. Should an unaddicted Arcona consume two or three grams of pure salt, he must make a hard Discipline check or receive two obligation points for addiction. Consuming salt disorients an Arcona for the remainder of the current encounter and all of the next encounter. On the other side of things, salt smuggling is a popular business on Cona. It is risky, however, as the substance is just as illegal as any narcotic, and Arcona who aren’t addicts will often kill anyone who distributes salt on Cona.

csg_ardennian.name: Ardennian

special_abilities.name: Brachiation
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for moving through forest or jungle terrain, add boost on checks to swing, climb, or jump.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. When hanging, treat feet as extra hands. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_ardennian.physiology: Ardennians are a shorter species of primates with an extra set of arms. They are incredibly agile and dexterous, and their feet are just as prehensile as their hands, so are able to easily climb around a thickly forested environment. They have gray-brown skin, and they have short fur. Their face, which is lighter in color than the back of their head, has a flat nose and a slight snout, and their eyes are black.
csg_ardennian.society: Ardennians are very social among their own, but their society is deeply split among a number of villages with about 50 members each. They are chosen for a particular job at a young age, and each village has a socialist economy. Unlike more individualistic species, Ardennian culture emphasizes the importance of societal good over individual good, and Ardennians see helping their group as the only way to benefit themselves. Such beliefs extend to those who live offworld, and they think of partners and allies like they would fellow villagers. Those who team up or join organizations view it as a permanent commitment, placing complete trust in their allies and expecting such attitudes to be reciprocated. Ardennians mostly live in canopies to avoid predators, although they operate farms and trap animals on the ground. Ardennians only joined the modern galaxy about two centuries ago, and although they have taken advantage of some new technologies, they have been doing so slowly. Its usage has been a controversial subject, and it has split some villages apart.
csg_ardennian.language: The nationalism of Ardennian villages has meant that every village has its own distinct language. They are united by a trade language called Norell, which a couple members from each village speak. Some regions have replaced Norell with Basic, which an increasing number of Ardennians are learning.
csg_ardennian.homeworld: Ardennians come from Ardennia, a hot Mid Rim planet that supports little life outside of its poles. They live in wooden treehouses near the south pole, and few outsiders visit them. However, a small contingent of Klytonian miners have recently found precious ores in scorching deserts far north of the Ardennians.
csg_ardennian.description: A smaller species of six-limbed primates, the Ardennians are nimble and coordinated, allowing them to swiftly navigate jungle environments. They tend to be outgoing and friendly, and they develop strong bonds with their allies.
csg_ardennian.sidebar_text: Ardennians have fierce rivalries between different villages, and they have a strong tradition of gambling land and settling disputes using annual games. Although such attitudes do not extend to those in their village, when they encounter those from outside their village, one of their first instincts is to brag or try to one-up. One of their most popular sports is the chaotic game of Yerik-Wrin, which is played between three villages in all three dimensions of a tree canopy. Each region has its own unique rules, but it generally involves five to seven balls, which they attempt to throw into bags defended by the other villages. Another of their sports is Podracing, invented by an Ardennian named Pod Phoebos about a century ago.
csg_ardennian._provenance_note: The Ardennian species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU. Almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_arkanian.name: Arkanian

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for darkness, add setback for brightness.

csg_arkanian.physiology: Arkanians are near-humans, having much in common with their human relatives. What makes them most distinctive visually are their silvery eyes without pupils and white hair. They also have four fingers, which are somewhat clawed. Offshoots have five normal fingers and human-resembling eyes. Their skin is much lighter. For both, their eyes are capable of both infrared and heat detecting sight, meaning that they can effectively see in the dark. They are also sensitive to light in general, meaning that they sometimes need sunglasses on planets with brighter suns.
csg_arkanian.society: Arkanian society is best defined by arrogance. They believe themselves to be the pinnacle of evolution and act like it. Though arrogant and often blatantly insulting towards outsiders, they expect politeness toward themselves. Insulting an Arkanian without a proper apology or gift to make amends can mean prison time on Arkania. They are often scientists, and brutal ones at that: Famed for genetic manipulation, they have created new species, made major medical discoveries, and also committed major genocides and atrocities. Though passionate about their field, they are still very slow to conduct their research. That being said, Arkanians are good scientists and not afraid to say so. Even the more modest ones acknowledge it. They are also competent when it comes to finances. Though not well-liked, they work with large corporations in order to maximize their own credit flows.
csg_arkanian.language: Arkanians speak Arkanian, though many know Basic as well.
csg_arkanian.homeworld: Arkanians live on the cold world of Arkania, which is mostly tundra. Rich in diamonds, it is used for mining as well as medical research. Though it is in the Core, it is not a commonly visited world thanks to the speciesist and arrogant ways of its natives.
csg_arkanian.description: Arkanians are arrogant and selfish near-humans who focus primarily on science. They are often seen as geneticists, and they have a track record of genetically modifying sentient creatures. They have even created species, such as the Quermians.
csg_arkanian.sidebar_text: Arkanians are known for genetic engineering, and it applies even to their own species. They have made several groups of genetically modified Arkanians, who serve as lower-class laborers. These are all distinguished by pale white skin, eyes with pupils, and five-fingered hands. They are better suited towards manual labor than the mainline counterparts. They are treated as second-class citizens with minimal rights, so many may seek to leave their discriminating homeworld.

csg_askajian.name: Askajian

special_abilities.name: Desert Natives
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Water Storage
special_abilities.description: May store up to 3 weeks of water in skin. May drink 1 week of water per day. Gain +1 soak but add setback on social checks for each week of water being stored.

csg_askajian.physiology: Askajians are near-humans who tend to be very bulky, as they store water in their skin. They can store up to three weeks of water and can drink a week’s worth in a single day. If they do not have any water stored in their skin, they are relatively normal in size. They have wrinkled skin on their face and two hearts. Female Askajians have six breasts.
csg_askajian.society: Askajans are very primitive, and most are still hunter-gatherers. They live in tribes which are nomadic, and each tribe typically contains one large extended family. They call their children “cubs.” The tribes occasionally unite and form military alliances. Dancing is an important aspect of their culture. The best dancer in a tribe acts as a storyteller and a shaman. Dance is used to re-enact history or legends and is also used as a form of worship to their god. Askajians believe in the Moon Lady, a goddess that values joy and happiness, even amidst death and tragedy. Another trait associated with Askajians is bravery, which some will proudly display.
csg_askajian.language: Askajians speak Askajian and some also know ancient Askajian. Those that leave their homeworld tend to learn Basic, although it isn’t ever used on Askaj.
csg_askajian.homeworld: Askaj is a desert Outer Rim world on the Rimma Trade Route. It has little technology and no central government. The tribes survive by hunting tomuons and gathering plants. Imperial control of the planet by Grand Moff Wilkadon has caused many Askajians to leave Askaj. They tend to head for other desert planets, like Tatooine.
csg_askajian.description: Primitive near-humans native to the deserts of Askaj, they Askajians are capable of storing large amounts of water in their body, which can make them very bulky.
csg_askajian.sidebar_text: Weaving is an important aspect of Askajian culture. The tomuons that they hunt are known for wool, although they also use the meat, hides, and horns of the animal. Tomuon wool is their only real industry, and it is a luxury even in the Core Worlds. Supposedly, it even makes up Palpatine’s robes. Weavers amongst the Askajans are very important, and their methods are a well-kept secret. Tribes have fought over the best weavers as well as access to the tomuon fur itself.

csg_asogian.name: Asogian
csg_asogian.physiology: Asogians are a smaller, more nimble sentient species with brown or yellow skin that is typically very wrinkled. They have short legs, but a longer neck and arms. They have four-fingered hands and three-toed feet. Many are hairless, but a few have patches of dark hair atop their head. Their head is short, flat, and wide, and it is dominated by large eyes, which can be blue or red. They have a short, pig-like nose. Asogians rarely wear any clothing.
csg_asogian.society: Asogians are known for their curiosity, which is almost childlike, and they are generally perceived to have a persona of innocence, which helps them get along in the galaxy. They can be overly naive at times, and they tend to speak their mind, even when it is best to keep silent. In particular, many have run afoul of the Empire for criticizing it too vocally. Despite this naivete in social situations, Asogians are nevertheless disciplined and restrained when they need to be, and they are also hard workers. They do a good job of planning for the future and thinking in the long term.
csg_asogian.language: Asogians typically speak Basic, given their frequent contact with other species. Their native language of Dwellig is mostly dead, known only by scholars.
csg_asogian.homeworld: The Asogian homeworld of Brodo Asogi lies near the edge of the civilized galaxy, in the northwestern Outer Rim. It is a lush, verdant planet, where plant life is dominant. It lacks native animal life, and the Asogians themselves are actually immigrants to the planet. Their original home, Nellik Asogi, is mostly barren.
csg_asogian.description: Asogians are a small species with a large head and short limbs, and they are known for their child-like curiosity and desire to explore. Their homeworld, Brodo Asogi, is on the edge of the galaxy, and they once founded a major exploration into the intergalactic void.
csg_asogian.sidebar_text: Because of their curiosity, Asogians are often explorers. In fact, one of their most noteworthy achievements was conducting an expedition to traverse the intergalactic void about 20 years ago, which remains unprecedented in scale. However, stable hypercommunications have not been established outside the galaxy, so its fate will not be known until lightspeed messages eventually reach back. More relevant to the rest of the galaxy are Asogians all over frontier worlds, from rural farming colonies to lawless trading outposts. Even on worlds with larger populations, they are almost always drawn to exploring the areas that are left unexplored.
csg_asogian._provenance_note: The Asogian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_avogwi.name: Avogwi

special_abilities.name: Paranoia
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Nobody’s Fool.”

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain.

csg_avogwi.physiology: Also known as Altorians, the Avogwi are an avian species with clawed fingers on the joint in the middle of their wings, allowing them some dexterity with which to use tools. Their legs are short but rather muscular, and they have a tail. Avogwi are quite large, similar to humans in height but boasting a wingspan of four or five meters. In addition to the claws on their wings, the Avogwi have clawed feet and a sharp beak, because they are entirely carnivorous. Their skin is generally red, but they are covered by orange feathers, which allow them to blend in with their planet’s hazy atmosphere.
csg_avogwi.society: Avogwi are solitary predators, living only with their mate and claiming vast tracts of land, often a square of around seven kilometers in length, as their personal hunting territory. They settle disputes among their own by ceremonial duels to the death, and they are drawn to violent professions when they are offworld. They have next to no technology and are totally primitive, focusing solely on finding food and water. All of these tendencies come from a surprisingly intricate philosophy which was allegedly developed by a legendary Avogwi named Toro-toral, the first of their species to fly. According to his sayings, the only way to survive is by killing, and those who refuse to kill will be killed. They recite these sayings often, ensuring that they are united in this grim outlook.
csg_avogwi.language: Given their relative isolation, most Avogwi have little interest in learning Basic and typically only speak their primitive native language.
csg_avogwi.homeworld: As their second name of Altorians indicates, Avogwi come from Altor 14, a planet composed of warm deserts and dry plains. It is on the fringe of galactic society, at the edge of the southeastern Outer Rim. It was discovered sixteen years ago, and its population is under one million sentients.
csg_avogwi.description: A solitary species of avian predators, the Avogwi are completely primitive, even preying on a fellow sentient species called the Nuiwit. They are paranoid and believe that mutually beneficial interactions are impossible.
csg_avogwi.sidebar_text: Avogwi are naturally paranoid, and they cannot understand the concept of a deal benefiting both sides. As such, they always believe that if someone is willing to offer a deal, that deal is bound to harm the other party in order to benefit the person offering it. Even mining rights to their land, which is rich with minerals, they have refused to sell. Avogwi share their home with the sentient Nuiwit species, whom they see only as an especially delicious species of prey. These tendencies have played to their disadvantage as they interact with modern society, because the Nuiwit, more entrepreneurial, have experienced more success and been able to expand their territory. As they have built cities and farms, Avogwi hunting grounds have become smaller, and they have been forced to adapt. A few have now left their homeworld in order to find work as bounty hunters or mercenaries.

csg_ayrou.name: Ayrou

special_abilities.name: Information Gatherers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Researcher.”

csg_ayrou.physiology: Ayrou are avians with skin in varying shades of lavender and eyes which can be crimson, azure, or emerald. They are slightly taller than most other species, but they are thin and relatively light. Their limbs are triple-jointed, which makes them much more flexible than other species, and they have four-fingered hands with claws. They have a flat face with high eyebrows and a long nose, and they have colorful feathers on top of their head. The precise characteristics of this plumage are essential to beauty and also reflect overall health and social standing. Although they are adapted to a thin atmosphere of slightly different composition than most, they can also survive in a normal environment.
csg_ayrou.society: Ayrou are a people who are obsessive in their desire to collect information. Many of them also extend this tendency to physical items, causing them to hoard various trinkets and never throw anything away. However, they are not especially greedy, and they consider their ways to be practical. They are strong-willed and determined, never giving up when they want something. However, they disdain combat and prefer to bargain for what they want whenever possible. To them, negotiation is an art, while combat is an alternative used only by the straightforward.
csg_ayrou.language: Ayrou can only speak their native language, Ayrou. Their voice is squawking and incredibly annoying to non-Ayrou. Some have compared it to a songbird being strangled, and a few species even find their blood-curdling sounds to be physically harmful. Although they cannot speak Basic, many Ayrou can understand it.
csg_ayrou.homeworld: Ayrou come from Maya Kovel, a very windy world in the Moddell sector of the Outer Rim. Its atmosphere has low pressure and an unpleasant smell, so most other species prefer to wear a breath mask.
csg_ayrou.description: Ayrou are thin, lavender-skinned avians with a squawking voice that are obsessive hoarders of trinkets. They also excel in gathering information, and they are savvy negotiators despite their annoying demeanor.
csg_ayrou.sidebar_text: In order to solve the many debates of religion and politics which can divide a society, the Ayrou have a very unique tradition: Two well-respected individuals, one from each side of the debate, meet together and discuss the issue over the course of decades. However, they eventually come to a single conclusion in which one or both of them change their beliefs. This agreement is upheld by both parties, and Ayrou who change their mind in these debates generally support their new beliefs for life.

csg_balinak.name: Balinak

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Light Filtering
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for lighting conditions.

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_balinak.physiology: Balinaka are exceedingly large ursine creatures, well over four meters tall. Wearing no clothing and boasting sharp claws, they give the appearance of straightforward predators to many, but their mind is actually quite keen. Despite their mammalian appearance, they are actually fully amphibious, with a dual respiratory system including both gills and lungs. They hunt a diet of fish in frigid waters, where their thick fur keeps them warm, and the webbing between their fingers makes them skilled swimmers. Balinaka have small ears but a prominent black nose, and they have wide cheeks. Their dark eyes are tiny but extremely advanced, with multiple membrane layers that they can extend or retract to adjust their vision to a wide range of light levels. They have a long neck and a flexible tail, and despite their height, they are actually quite nimble. Their hands and feet have four digits each, with opposable thumbs and one rear-facing toe on each foot.
csg_balinak.society: Balinaka live in cities called sewfes that are dug out of caves in coastal areas, where they use geothermal power. Each of their homes is centered around a large communal area that houses all of their technology, and the sewfes are also arranged around communal areas called heswe that they use to meet, play, trade, and conduct religious services. Balinaka tend to have playful personalities, fond of arts such as dance and sculpture. They are extremely laid-back, calm in crises to the point of aloofness. This has allowed them to be very quietly abused as strong but docile slaves by factions such as the Imperials or the Senax nobles. However, the Balinaka have been friendly with the Imperials on their world to the point that they are generally allowed significant autonomy.
csg_balinak.language: The Balinaka speak a very synthetic language, but they can also learn Basic.
csg_balinak.homeworld: A frigid world in the southern portion of the Outer Rim, Garnib is covered by thick glaciers and icy seas. The Imperials, centered around Garnib Station, are recent arrivals, setting up slave camps and collecting steep taxes. There are also a significant number of Vernol immigrants, whose own homeworld has been rendered uninhabitable. While the Balinaka are welcoming to the Vernols, the newcomers are still apprehensive toward their giant neighbors.
csg_balinak.description: Known for their dancing, sculpting, and overall playfulness, the Balinaka are an easygoing species of giant ursines. They are are well-adapted to frigid conditions on both land and water.
csg_balinak.sidebar_text: Of all the art forms that Balinaka enjoy, the most prominent are their ice sculptures. These traditional works were relatively obscure until one Balinak, Vornest Dep-thesel Digarsarg, began to incorporate shards of Garnab Crystals into his work, creating more colorful masterpieces. This innovation was noticed by a human businessman, Abram Zavict, who began to export the new sculptures to the wider galaxy, forming Galactic Crystal Creations, also known as Garnib Crystal Corporation. This venture, owned collectively by the entire planet, has pushed the Balinaka more into the galactic spotlight, as their work is renowned galaxy-wide. GCC hosts an annual celebration called wallarand, which lasts four days and sees basically the entire planet congregate in a single city. In addition to celebrating their arts, it serves as a business and political meeting.

csg_balosar.name: Balosar

special_abilities.name: Antennapalps
special_abilities.description: With extended antennapalps, remove setback from Perception checks. May also sense surges in emotion, adding boost on all initiative checks.

special_abilities.name: Poison Tolerance
special_abilities.description: Remove penalties for most toxins or reduce difficulty to resist toxins by up to 2 at the GM’s discretion.

csg_balosar.physiology: Balosars are near-humans, although they tend to be more pale and sickly than humans. Being exposed to a litany of pollutants on their world, they have evolved a resistance to almost every known poison, be it a narcotic, pollutant, or other toxin. However, even they have a relatively short lifespan on their homeworld because of its poor conditions. The most distinctive feature that separates them from humans are their antennapalps, which can acutely sense many things through their subsonic hearing. This can allow them to sometimes sense surges of emotion in others in a way that acts similar to a Jedi’s danger sense. The antennapalps can be hidden inside their head as well. Though they are useless when hidden this way, it does provide an option for the Balosars who want to hide their powerful ability or pass as human.
csg_balosar.society: Balosar possess a horrid reputation, as their society is one of crime, poverty, and decay. Stereotypes make them out to be weak-willed, manipulative, selfish, and deceitful. While such pictures aren’t entirely false, this is mostly because their hardships have forced them to take extreme measures to survive. This has come at the expense of distinguishing right and wrong, so many are criminals. Depression is common among them, which often manifests itself as a jaded sarcasm. Those who leave the poverty of the planet Balosar seem to have little luck elsewhere, as adapting to new worlds proves challenging, and the stereotypes often become self-fulfilling as they are treated with disdain. Those who thrive the most are Balosars who leave as young children to get an offworld education, and the sooner they do so, the better.
csg_balosar.language: Most Balosars speak Basic and their native tongue, Balosur, in a raspy voice.
csg_balosar.homeworld: While some choose to leave it, most Balosars find themselves in the urban mess of poverty, crime, corruption, and pollution that is Balosar. Although it is in the Core Worlds, it has a huge underworld, and the government is entangled with criminals. It is highly industrialized, so there is still legal work in sweatshop factories whose emissions blot out the sunlight.
csg_balosar.description: The Balosars are near-humans who live in a society that is defined by crime and poverty. They are extremely resistant to any form of drug or poison, but they do export death sticks. Most look somewhat sickly.
csg_balosar.sidebar_text: The only thing that the Balosars seem to have going for them is that their homeworld prominently grows the balo mushroom, which produces a narcotic called Ixetal cilona extract. This is often made into what are called “death sticks,” a drug with a sweet flavor that does little other than addict users and shorten their lifespan. Though their lifespan is short to begin with thanks to pollution, Balosars are actually immune to the side effects of death sticks, just not the addictive property. While death sticks do provide an industry that employs many Balosars, countless other Balosars are addicts, and many are both. Their industry was once dominant galaxy-wide, but it has grown smaller after Twi’lek crime bosses started gang wars, now allowing ryll to dominate the drug market.

csg_barabel.name: Barabel

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Natural Hunters
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Expert Tracker.”

special_abilities.name: Claws and Teeth
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3. May spend 4 advantage to bite, inducing a Critical Injury, adding the Vicious 2 quality, and immobilizing the victim for 1 round.

csg_barabel.physiology: Barabels are reptiles that are big and tall, averaging just over two meters in height and possessing great strength. As carnivores with two stomachs, they are completely built for killing a variety of deadly prey. Their thick skin is covered in a protective layer of keratin scales and come in many shades, including green, purple, gray, brown, and red, and their scales get darker as they age. Their red or black eyes see infrared and do well in the dark, but they cannot see blue or violet, and they struggle in bright conditions. They have five centimeter teeth which can crush bone, and their retractable claws are also good weapons. Their long tail, which is also effective in combat, can easily be shed and regrown.
csg_barabel.society: Barabels are territorial and aggressive, which reflects in their culture. They live in small communities of no more than 10,000, or even as small as a dozen. Their tribes also number up to 10,000. Communities center around a warren, which they hunt from. Always ready for combat, they’re aggressive and tend to have short tempers. Despite their violence, they still value wisdom and cooperation and are very loyal to their family. Families are female dominated, as children don’t even know their fathers. Barabel emotions are different from those of humans, and they fail to understand apologies. Apologizing, in fact, tends to make things worse. They do not comprehend guilt or sympathy and find mourning to be a strange tradition.
csg_barabel.language: Barabel, the language of the Barabels, is full of barks and hisses. They can learn Basic, but have a hissing accent and pronounce the letter “s” as a “z.” They also refer to themselves as “this one,” instead of using the first person singular pronouns, “I” and “me.”
csg_barabel.homeworld: Barab I is a world in the eastern part of the Outer Rim. A harsh planet, deadly radiation fills the daytime hours. Its caves are the only shelter, as few species can survive Barab I’s daytime. In the night, the hunt begins across the rocky badlands. The extremely hot day also evaporates the oceans and standing water, meaning that later in the night, sudden rainfall again forces the natives to take shelter. In recent years, it has built its first city, Alater-ka, named for the Imperial captain who designated Barabels as sentient. Alater-ka is an underground complex with primitive technology, although it does have a spaceport.
csg_barabel.description: A species of clawed reptiles with vicious jaws, Barabels are deadly. They deal with harsh conditions on their homeworld of Barab I and mostly live as primitive hunters. They do not understand some emotions like regret and grief, often causing major and even violent misunderstandings.
csg_barabel.sidebar_text: Barab I is a very isolated planet, so Barabels are not well-known in the galaxy. Their first notable outside contact was with a Jedi, who, according to legend, came to Barab I and stopped a heated clan dispute over hunting grounds. Ever since, Barabels have been highly respectful of the Jedi. Their second notable contact with the rest of the galaxy is more violent. Planetary Safaris Inc. began to organize hunting trips to Barab I, targeting the Barabels. Under Imperial law, Barabels were considered non-sentient and were hunted for sport. However, after a few Barabels were killed, a Barabel named Shaka-Ka organized hunting parties of her own, attacking the safaris. The safari ships were continuously destroyed until an Imperial investigation revealed that Barabels are sentient. Safaris now hunt the dangerous animals of Barab I, employing Barabels as tour guides.

csg_baragwin.name: Baragwin

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Advanced Olfaction
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks. As a maneuver, may sense the emotional state of anyone within medium range by passing an average Perception check.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_baragwin.physiology: Baragwin are hunchbacked reptiles with very thick skin that is typically brown, gray, or olive. This thick skin helps them to shrug off a great deal of damage, but they are heavy and slow. Such sluggishness is purely physical, however, as their mind is highly intelligent. They do sometimes hide their intelligence, as they can often take advantage of misconceptions. They have three-fingered hands and three-toed feet. Their head, typically very wrinkled, is large and roughly cylindrical with a flat face. They have small, black eyes, and their mouth is wide and slobbery. They have a very large, circular nose. This nose is extremely sensitive, and they can use smell to track targets or even decipher the moods and emotions of others. Because of these abilities, a number of them have found success as bounty hunters.
csg_baragwin.society: Baragwin are a people with a desire to move and explore, often migrating and forming colonies throughout the galaxy. They are also known to treat all people equally, regardless of societal background or wealth. This even applies to criminal Baragwin, who often exploit without prejudice. Their intelligence allows them to succeed in many careers, and they were one of the first spacefaring species. However, they have become especially noteworthy as weaponsmiths. They make weapons ranging from blasters to vibroblades, and they can be found on both sides of the Galactic Civil War.
csg_baragwin.language: Baragwin typically know Basic, and some know other tongues that are used on their planet of origin. They have a native language, Baragwinian, but most of them are not fond of it.
csg_baragwin.homeworld: The Baragwin originate from Old Barag, an Expansion Region planet. However, they were quick to discover space travel and have moved on to many other other planets. They have now completely forgotten Old Barag. Although their population is only in the millions, they have many small colonies. Such colonies include Tatooine, Denuhi-Eight, and Coruscant. Because of how widespread they are, they are a common sight and are very-well known throughout the galaxy.
csg_baragwin.description: Baragwin make natural colonists; they are found on so many worlds that their original homeworld is now forgotten. Though hunchbacked, slow-moving, and not particularly attractive, they are resilient and excel in mechanical professions.
csg_baragwin.sidebar_text: Baragwin are so inclined toward colonization that they have forgotten their old homeworld and have yet to unify on a single planet. They have a number of small settlements, most of which are relatively anarchic and have politicians selected by an informal democracy. Such politicos only remain in power for short periods of time, however. They affiliate themselves more with their colony of origin than their species, and their culture varies greatly based on which colony they are from. For example, the Baragwin on Denuhi-Eight are amiable yet cautious, but Baragwin on other worlds such as Tatooine are very different.

csg_bardottan.name: Bardottan
csg_bardottan.physiology: Bardottans are a species with saurian biology. Their neck is long, curved, and wrinkled. They have a duck-like head, with eyes on the sides and a narrow snout including nostrils and a mouth. They get around by hopping with their three-toed feet. Their knees bend backwards. Bardottans can look very different from each other in many ways. First, some have a tail, and some do not. They also vary greatly in height, from one meter to nearly two meters. Some have three-fingered hands, others have four-fingered hands. Some also have two skin colors, while others have just one. Their skin is often green, but it can also come in yellow, gray, purple, or red.
csg_bardottan.society: Bardottans are best known for being a very spiritual people. They are also disciplined and knowledgeable, and many tend to be scholarly. They are also very independent and take pride in being able to do things by themselves. Few ask for assistance in anything. They view education as privilege, not a right, and earning it requires intense study. Bardottans tend to focus on academics, and each city specializes in a different field of study.
csg_bardottan.language: Some Bardottans know Basic, but they almost always choose to speak in their own language, Bardottan.
csg_bardottan.homeworld: Bardotta is a mountainous world in the Colonies that most Bardottans call home. It is covered in many temples and academic facilities. Few Bardottans leave their homeworld.
csg_bardottan.description: Dimunitive saurians, the Bardottans are a species that are known for their reclusive, scholarly ways. They are also very spiritual, and some are members of the Force tradition known as the Dagoyan Masters.
csg_bardottan.sidebar_text: Bardottans have a rich Force tradition, although they long detested the Jedi Order for kidnapping children. (This opinion somewhat changed in 19 BBY after Mace Windu assisted the people.) Almost all Bardottans believe in Dagoyan ways, and Dagoyan beliefs are deeply ingrained into their culture. They practice peace, meditation, and study. However, long ago, the Bardottans were not so peaceful. They instead were ruled by the Frangawl cult, a violent group of demon-worshippers. While the Frangawl were barbaric and stuck fear into the hearts of many, they truly believed that their actions were moral and necessary.

csg_bartokk.name: Bartokk

special_abilities.name: Hardened Carapaces
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Compartmentalized Anatomy
special_abilities.description: Severed body parts may function normally for up to 8 hours.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Hive Minds
special_abilities.description: May form a hive mind with all other Bartokk within 500 meters, sharing all information. When part of a hive mind with more than 5 Bartokk, gain +1 Intellect and +1 Cunning.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 2 additional wounds. May also regrow lost limbs after a few days. May attempt to heal critical injuries 3 times more often.

csg_bartokk.physiology: Bartokk are insects with six limbs, four of which they can use for grasping and manipulation. They have six eyes on their head and more on their abdomen. Their sharp claws make them deadly combatants. Their body is black and covered in a spiky chitinous exoskeleton, which provides them with excellent protection. What damage they do absorb, they can regenerate very quickly, recovering from almost any injury after a few days. They can even generate an entire body using just half of their brain, meaning that they can recover from any injury other than complete disintegration of their brain. Furthermore, they have telepathy, which allows severed body parts to function normally, even allowing them to use their body after being decapitated. This telepathy also allows them to act as a hive mind. This hive mind is important, since they are barely sentient as individuals but much more intelligent as a group.
csg_bartokk.society: Bartokk possess little individuality, since they are almost always part of hives. They are not technologically advanced, but when they are in a hive, they are intelligent enough to make some progress in reverse-engineering technology. When they interact with the rest of the galaxy, most hives act as one and make a living as assassins. However, many facets of Bartokk society are shrouded in mystery.
csg_bartokk.language: Bartokk have no language of their own, since they are all capable of telepathy with each other. If they wish to communicate with outsiders, they are able to speak. However, individual Bartokk are not intelligent enough to possess a complete vocabulary. Because they lack individuality, individuals in a hive are nameless.
csg_bartokk.homeworld: Only the Bartokk know the location of their home planet, a rocky Outer Rim world. Its minor radiation can cause mutations for Bartokk.
csg_bartokk.description: A species of insects with a hive mind, the Bartokk are unintelligent on their own but can be more calculating in groups. They are often assassins, as their strange physiology allows them to regenerate quickly, and their limbs can function without being attached to their body.
csg_bartokk.sidebar_text: Bartokk who are part of a hive act collectively without individual freedom or personality. However, a hive mind is not automatic. In fact, a small minority of Bartokk lack the ability to join a hive mind entirely. Others are forcibly removed from a hive mind because of mutations, such as additional fingers or a slightly misshapen carapace. Bartokk who are without their hive often die in the wilderness of their homeworld, although some find kinship offworld. For those who follow either of these paths, they are barely sentient and act very much like animals, only capable of extremely basic logic.

csg_berrite.name: Berrite

special_abilities.name: Expert Survivalists
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

special_abilities.name: Sonar
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for lighting conditions. Add setback on auditory or visual Perception checks, but remove this penalty if sonar may be used instead.

csg_berrite.physiology: Berrites are quadrupedal, and they are typically lumbering and slow. Although they are only a meter tall, they are also chubby and have a thick layer of wrinkled green skin. They have some patches of black hair. Their feet have three claws each, but their hands are more humanoid, except with larger palms and longer pointer fingers. They store food in their cheek pouches, as it can take hours to chew. Berrites have a small nose and eyes, and their vision is very poor. Their hearing, also rather poor, is done through a number of small tubes on either side of their head, and they have no ears. However, Berrites overcome these sensory shortcomings using sonar, which typically is enough to compensate. Berrites are hermaphrodites, meaning that they are all capable of producing and carrying eggs as well as fertilizing them. Although this means they are capable of reproducing without a mate, they still generally find one. If they think it will cause them to receive better treatment, Berrites will arbitrarily assign themselves a gender when encountering other species. Because they lack true genders, they typically struggle to identify genders for members of other species. They typically have three babies at a time, who reach full size within a year, but they do not truly reach adulthood until the age of 60. Their lifespan is about 400 years.
csg_berrite.society: Berrites have a primitive and anarchical society, foraging to survive without any real government or civilization. Nevertheless, they are peaceful and cultured, cooperating with one another and enjoying storytelling in groups. Typically, storytelling sessions are also a time that they use to chew their food, which takes many hours. They spend the rest of their time as highly skilled foragers, but they also manage their resources carefully, and they are actually very intentional with their actions in order to achieve sustainability.
csg_berrite.language: Berrites have no known native language and typically speak Basic.
csg_berrite.homeworld: Berrites come from Berri, a hot planet with few natural resources and high gravity. It is primitive and has little trade or other offworld contact. It once had Imperial factories where the Berrites were enslaved, but it has been left alone after the Berrites passively resisted the Empire by feigning stupidity and intentionally making mistakes.
csg_berrite.description: A species of quadrupedal hunter-gatherers, Berrites are surprisingly cunning and use their ugly appearance and primitive lifestyle to make others underestimate them.
csg_berrite.sidebar_text: Berrites are extremely clever, and they are smart enough to know that their sluggish appearance and physical clumsiness often causes others to assume they are unintelligent. Those who encounter other species often take advantage of this, acting as con artists or playing dumb if they ever are put in a dangerous situation. When pressured, they prefer to respond in a manner that seems aloof, protesting cheerfully and pretending not to understand the situation’s severity.

csg_besalisk.name: Besalisk

special_abilities.name: Cold Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Extra Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_besalisk.physiology: Besalisks are strong, bulky humanoids with four arms. Some females have even more arms. Like humans, Besalisks only have one dominant hand, however. Some have a slight beak for a mouth, as they are technically avian. They have three-toed feet, but four-fingered hands. Their skin is typically a light brown. Their head is quite distinctive, with a bulbous throat, wide mouth, downward-drooping ears, and, in males, a hard crest. Just above their mouth, they have black whiskers with sensory capabilities. They reproduce by laying eggs, which are hatched during the warm seasons.
csg_besalisk.society: Besalisks are typically brave, adventurous, and friendly. They often seek thrills, even if it isn’t very safe. They also love to talk, gossiping often and trying to make friends with just about anyone. This makes them not the best employees for some jobs, but they quit due to boredom just as often as they get fired. Whether it’s prospecting for aurodium on Subterrel, working as a criminal enforcer on Nar Shaddaa, smuggling glitterstim spice on a freighter, or setting up a restaurant or Coruscant, Beskalisks are likely to switch jobs quite a bit, and they’ll also be willing to tell stories about these jobs. Despite this mobility, they still tend to form long-lasting friendships and will remain dedicated to their friends.
csg_besalisk.language: Besalisks speak their native language of Besalisk, one of barks, grunts, and growls. Since many travel offworld, quite a few know Basic.
csg_besalisk.homeworld: Ojom is an icy ocean world that the Besalisks inhabit. It is very hard to get to and from, as it is in the Deep Core. They have several space stations that they use to conduct business over the planet. Though the space stations are mostly designed for offworlders, who are less adapted to the cold, many Besalisks reside in the space stations as well. Their populations exceed that of the surface itself. It has very little Imperial presence, as the Besalisks have called in favors from various underworld connections to stay independent.
csg_besalisk.description: Besalisks are brave and adventurous avians with four arms. They come from the frigid glaciers of Ojom, where they live in relative isolation. Their bulk provides great strength and protects them from the cold.
csg_besalisk.sidebar_text: Besalisks live in relatively small communes instead of large cities, with none being larger than a thousand families or so. Each is ruled by a single elder. The idea of keeping the community sizes equal is to prevent war between communities, and it typically works. They are so dedicated to this size equality, in fact, that if one gets too big, families are asked to leave and start their own community. Each community has its own glacier to inhabit. They are still sparsely populated enough that they haven’t needed to colonize other worlds.

csg_bilar.name: Bilar

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Advanced Hearing
special_abilities.description: Add boost on all auditory Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Brachiation
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for moving through forest or jungle terrain, add boost on checks to swing, climb, or jump.

special_abilities.name: Multiple Individuals
special_abilities.description: Control 4 individuals who each have identical stats. May increase the amount of individuals controlled at a cost of 20 XP per individual, purchased at character creation prior to all other XP spending. For every 3 individuals purchased, receive +1 Intellect. Communicate automatically between individuals if within sight. If separated or split in any way, reduce Intellect by 1 for 1 day or until reunited.

csg_bilar.physiology: Bilars are a species of herbivorous, hairless primates with pink skin, an appearance which generally comes off as extremely cute or repulsive, with little in-between. They are chubby and can move both bipedally or quadrupedally. They are also skilled climbers and can move effectively swinging through a forest canopy. They are shorter than most species, about a meter tall, and they have a large head with wide ears and circular ears. They can see in the infrared and have capable night vision, and their ears, capable of hearing a broad range of pitches, are also able to rotate in order to home in on specific sounds. They have a slight snout with a wide, smiling mouth, and a short, black nose. Their most unique distinction is their form of telepathy, which is not entirely understood by scientists but is thought to include pheromones, visual cues, and physical touch.
csg_bilar.society: Bilars tend to have a child-like temperament brought on by the abundance of natural resources on their world. Offworld, scarcity of resources makes them frustrated, and they tend to complain if they don’t get what they want or need to work. On their homeworld, they are playful, although they are capable of using and developing technology. They are peaceful, especially among their own, and they tend to avoid combat. They are innately curious and are typically too naive to be truly afraid, so they enjoy exploring.
csg_bilar.language: Bilars need little language among their own claqas because of their unique telepathy, but they often know Basic in order to communicate with other species.
csg_bilar.homeworld: Bilars come from the tectonically volatile Mid Rim planet of Mima II. Although most of the planet is plagued by groundquakes and volcanoes, the Bilars live in an equatorial region which is more stable and has rainforests with an abundance of edible fruit. They do have a few natural predators, including large flying reptiles called the riams.
csg_bilar.description: A playful species of primates, the Bilars are distinguished by a powerful hive mind, or claqa, which unites them for life. They have an almost telepathic ability to communicate with those in their claqa, but they can go into shock if they are separated from it.
csg_bilar.sidebar_text: Bilars are distinguished by their claqas, a form of hive mind that lasts for life. They have no individual name, only one for the claqa. Bilar mothers give birth within minutes of others in their claqa, and the resulting newborns form a lifelong telepathic bond among themselves within a few minutes. If the claqa has only one Bilar, that Bilar is non-sentient, but two or three Bilars can achieve semi-sentience. Claqas of four are sentient, five take slightly more interest in technology and cities, and seven are geniuses. All members within a claqa are almost totally identical, staying together, learning together, and making decisions together. Although this unity has its benefits, it also comes with consequences. Many other species are unnerved by their strange hive-mind, making it hard for them to get along offworld. Additionally, they must remain within sight of their claqa at all times: Even temporary separation from a single member causes a shock that revokes their intelligence, and a death can render all others deeply depressed or even comatose.

csg_bimm.name: Bimm

special_abilities.name: Sociable
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

csg_bimm.physiology: Although the Bimms are both biologically unrelated, they are each very small, ranging from one meter to one and a half meters tall. The near-human Bimms are likely related to human immigrants, and they are only distinguished by being smaller and typically having a prominent beard. The furred Bimms are more unique. They have a long muzzle, pointed ears, and black eyes. They are covered in fur that is typically tan but can be darker. They have just four fingers on each hand.
csg_bimm.society: Bimms are a mild-mannered and peaceful people. This allows the two species to live together with no racial conflicts. Crime is minimized, as they are too peaceful for violent crime and detest cheating or deception. They revere the Jedi, although they quietly left the Republic during the Clone Wars. Both of their cultures almost identical, and intermarriage among the two groups is common, although such couples must adopt if they want children. There are small differences, however. The near-human Bimms are more prone to scholarly pursuits and enjoy storytelling, while the furred Bimms, for their part, value bargaining and have tendencies toward haggling and shopping. They also often wear the color yellow.
csg_bimm.language: Both Bimm species speak Bimmini, a melodic language that sounds like a five-part harmony. They are typically bilingual, as most also learn Basic from a young age.
csg_bimm.homeworld: The Bimms are united in that they both live on Bimmisaari, a temperature world in the Mid Rim. It is filled with jungles of asaari trees, although most of the cities are built over plains. Despite a small population in the tens of millions, it is a sector capital and a prominent trade world, exporting luxury goods such as wine.
csg_bimm.description: Bimms are two diminutive species who share a culture and a world. One is furred, the other is near-human, but both are amiable, peaceful, and have a strong sense of morality.
csg_bimm.sidebar_text: Just as the furred Bimms embraced the near-human immigrants into their culture, Bimms are a friendly and welcoming people. When they receive visitors, they conduct a silent welcoming ritual in which the visitors walk in a line and are touched on the head or back one by one. They are always very kind hosts, except they are not so welcoming to armed visitors, whom they do not typically allow on their world. The only weapons allowed are lightsabers carried by Jedi, whom they greatly respect.
csg_bimm._provenance_note: The Bimms are two genetically unrelated species. However, since they share a name, culture, homeworld, and language, they are both on this page.

csg_bith.name: Bith

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on auditory Perception checks. Triple all sonic damage and, at the GM’s discretion, increase sonic damage from 0 to 1.

special_abilities.name: Tireless
special_abilities.description: Suffer no penalties for lack of sleep and only require 4 hours of light meditation per day.

csg_bith.physiology: Bith are highly advanced craniopods, a group of species with a large head. This oversized cranium has much space devoted to a massive brain that is highly adept at logical reasoning. Below the forehead are wide dark eyes protected by a translucent shell. They have no eyelids, as Bith have no need for sleep, surviving off only a few hours of light meditation. Just below the eyes are skin flaps in their cheeks, which hold their highly adept olfactory organs. Their mouth and nose are quite small at the bottom center of their face, and they only inhale through the nose. Air then goes to a single lung and is exhaled through their yellow-tan skin. Despite the lack of visible ears, hearing is their strong suit, and they have a particular knack for detecting pitch. They cannot reproduce naturally and require artificial conception. While they lack toes, they do have fairly long and bony fingers.
csg_bith.society: Being highly intelligent and detail-oriented, Bith excel in arithmetic, linguistics, and the arts. Their society is one of the oldest in the galaxy, and they have developed advanced computer programs for almost every need, though their technology has grown stagnant in recent centuries. Computer programs control everything from who represents them politically to mating and breeding. The Computer Mating Service (CMS) matches potential couples together based on their DNA, and after the two negotiate the terms of their relationship and give their cells to their local Reproduction Center, their baby is delivered to their doorstep. Likewise in politics, they are led by a committee whose members are chosen via computer analysis. They tend to lean on the pacifistic side in politics, that was not always the case.
csg_bith.language: Bith learn to speak to speak and write both their language, Bith, and Basic from an early age. Bith is numerical in structure, indicating the mathematical nature of the species.
csg_bith.homeworld: Clak’dor VII is an Outer Rim planet on the Rimma Trade Route. Its swamps and jungles have become a toxic wasteland, and the atmosphere is poisonous. Most of the local fauna are dangerous and genetically mutated. Bith live in domed cities, with food, water, and any raw materials now needing to be imported.
csg_bith.description: Bith are a mathematical people who are experts in technology and music. They have a large yellow head that houses a powerful brain. They are very pacifistic thanks to major damage caused by bioweapons in a war that occurred 300 years ago.
csg_bith.sidebar_text: 300 years ago, the Bith city-states of Nozho and Weogar went into a cataclysmic war because Nozho blackmailed a judge in a patent case over a certain hyperdrive technology. Eventually, both sides turned to biological weapons, which ruined the ecosystem of their homeworld and devastated their infrastructure capacity. They learned their lesson: Bith now tend to be pacifistic and attempted to stay neutral during the Clone Wars. However, they were eventually forced to pick a side. When it became apparent that the Confederacy could offer them better economic opportunity, they made their choice, although they still chose not to fight and only supplied technology to the Confederacy’s efforts. Although they are horrified by the Empire’s militarist ways, a minority do appreciate its orderly nature. They have peacefully given their technological expertise to the Empire for now.

csg_bivall.name: Bivall

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_bivall.physiology: A thin species of aquatic ancestry, the Bivall have long limbs but are relatively weak. They have skin in shades of pink and light green, and they lack hair. Not unlike the Rakata, Bivall have a thin head with eyes protruding from its sides. They have a crest atop their head, and their somewhat beak-like mouth is covered by a thin strand of flesh drooping over it.
csg_bivall.society: Known mostly as academics, Bivall value knowledge above all else and tend to focus on understanding problems rather than solving them, so it is rare to see them doing work that isn’t highly theoretical. Although their abstract way of thinking makes them excel as theoretical physicists or mathematicians, many of them enjoy the arts. However, their tastes are so incredibly abstract that their arts and literature are incomprehensible and bafflingly random to almost all other species.
csg_bivall.language: Bivall have mostly adopted Basic as their language, aside from a few sects that try to preserve their native tongue, Viogesh.
csg_bivall.homeworld: Bivall come from the planet of Protobranch, a planet in the Core Worlds which is mostly plains. Although the Bivall come from its lakes, they have moved onto land in order to have more space. It is highly urbanized and has some agriculture, but its most notable businesses are laboratories and universities.
csg_bivall.description: Bivall are a thin aquatic species with a beak-like mouth and wide eyes. They are known more as academics than anything else, as they are seen across many universities and hospitals.
csg_bivall.sidebar_text: For Bivall, moral stances and philosophies are heavily dependent on which philosophical school of thought they follow. Every region or city has a different blend of belief systems, although many Bivall find a new philosopher to follow during their earliest part of adulthood. Many of their criminals follow the teachings of Dioenis, an ancient philosopher who preached that morality is an illusion and that total hedonism is the only rational behavior. The most numerous, encompassing about fifteen percent of their people, are the Akiyans. They believe in a concept of the Akiyus, who is similar to a deity but is abstract and without tangible details. They theorize that they were created with an intuition that understands morality and a corruption in their mind that is evil, and they believe that they must use logic to choose correctly and please the Akiyus. A rapidly growing sect are the Poelions, whose founder, Gionis Poeli, is still alive. He preaches that evolution is the source of morality, so their only purpose is to carry on their genetics as much as possible and expand the species. The Poelions generally have many children and focus on being frugal in order to stock up resources for future generations.
csg_bivall._provenance_note: The Bivall species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_blood_carver.name: Blood Carver

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_blood_carver.physiology: Blood Carvers are humanoids with gold skin, orange blood, and triple-jointed limbs who technically qualify as insectoids. Their combat capabilities are enhanced by both their sharp claws and innate quickness. They have nose flaps which are capable of both smelling and hearing along their beak-like snout. They can move these nose flaps and change their color in order to communicate. They have tiny, black eyes, and instead of hair, they have ridges on their skull.
csg_blood_carver.society: Blood Carvers have a primitive, tribal society. Their traditions include tattoos, especially on their upper lip, and they particularly detest flattery, greed, and vast wealth in general. Those who exhibit such traits are punished harshly; beatings or exiles are common. They can also punish via temporary exiles called extensions. They have very strong ties to their tribe, and they are extremely loyal. They also expect this in other relationships, so those who travel away from their people are often shocked by a comparative lack of loyalty. If they venture into the galaxy, they almost always form groups with other Blood Carvers. Most of them are warriors, although they demonstrate restraint in battle and avoid excessive mutilation. However, these skills did not help them enough when they were attacked by the Lontars, a species which nearly wiped them out in 110 BBY.
csg_blood_carver.language: Blood Carvers speak Batorese, a language which combines sounds with scents and nose flap colorations. Many of those who relocated away from Batorine learn Basic.
csg_blood_carver.homeworld: The forest world of Batorine, found in the Colonies, is the Blood Carver homeworld. The war against the Lontars devastated their population, and the near-genocide meant that many surviving Blood Carver relocated to planets such as Coruscant. Those who did so generally remained in their tribes.
csg_blood_carver.description: Blood Carvers have a tribal society and do everything for the good of their tribe rather than their own. They detest sloth and flattery, and they focus on constant improvement in all things, especially the sculptures that are the centerpiece of their culture.
csg_blood_carver.sidebar_text: Although Blood Carvers are known as warriors, sculpture is a far more essential aspect of their culture. They typically carve from the wood of a red tree, meaning their works have a blood-like color-hence their name. It is tradition that the sculptures are not complimented, which is actually seen as a grave insult. Conversely, a Blood Carver who makes a sculpture will show it expecting it to be critiqued harshly. This focus on improvement rather than praise reflects an overall outlook in their art: They only make it to benefit their tribe, never for personal gain.

csg_bosph.name: Bosph

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_bosph.physiology: Bosphs are a mammalian species with six limbs, four of which act as arms. Although they can be a bit shorter than humans, they tend to be thickly built, and their skin, brown-gray in color, is thicker than that of most species. Their hands and feet all end in three digits. Their hairless head is hemispheric, and they lack a neck. They have a pig-like nose and wide, multifaceted eyes. These eyes also act as tympanic membranes, meaning they are responsible for both hearing and sight. Right beside their eyes, they have two sharp horns which curl upward.
csg_bosph.society: Bosphs are a gregarious but antisocial people, a combination which makes them often go out of their way to avoid others. Although both of these tendencies have the rare exceptions, Bosphs tend to be polite yet indifferent when they are forced into social interactions. Bosphs respect other spacefaring species, and they value travelling amongst themselves. They often tattoo themselves with star maps, a tradition required of Force-sensitive Bosphs. Force-sensitives, called ela b’Yentarr, are all taken into factions at a young age. Factions act as the government, but factions are diverse in what they do and how they think: Some hunt animals, some are healers, and some are philosophers. All Bosphs tend to be more philosophical than other species, although their views on property are very distinct. Individual ownership of anything is only allowed for ela b’Yentarr, and everything else is shared among their entire society. Because of their unique views on property, Bosphs are often confused by offworld laws and get into legal trouble. Those allowed ownership claim objects using glyphs, although if multiple claims are made, they may fight for it. However, they are not especially violent otherwise. Bosphs rarely kill, and if they enter a conflict, the worst insult is to forget it and entirely ignore their adversary's existence.
csg_bosph.language: Bosphs are capable of speaking Basic, but they typically only speak their native language.
csg_bosph.homeworld: Bosphs come from the planet of Bosph, which is a planet of plains in the Outer Rin, and they have also colonized Bosph I.
csg_bosph.description: Bosphs are porcine mammals with four arms who dislike social interactions but tend to enjoy travelling. They are ruled by their Force-sensitives, so they were orbitally bombarded by the Empire.
csg_bosph.sidebar_text: Bosphs are a somewhat superstitious species, and all phenomena which are unexplained to them are referred to as the result of Yentarr, who is similar to a deity among them. The Force, referred to as abo b’Yentarr, is one example of this, although they associate it with rituals and ceremonies and struggle to use their powers without them. The Bosphs’ submission to Force-sensitives concerned the Imperial Moff, who orbitally bombarded their planet. Ever since then, they have ignored the Empire’s existence, and even the drastic damage from the Imperial bombardment has been attributed to Yentarr. Although individuals continue to traverse the spacelanes, they refuse to acknowledge any Imperial mandates, and their planet has taken an isolationist stance. The Empire has mostly ignored it ever since.

csg_bothan.name: Bothan

special_abilities.name: Spies
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Convincing Demeanor.”

csg_bothan.physiology: Bothans have keen senses and a small size that they use to their advantage. They have a tapered snout for their feline face, which includes a very sensitive black or brown nose. Their black or blue eyes have a greater range of focus, and their upward-pointed ears are twice as large as those of humans. Bothans are also somewhat small, averaging a meter and a half in height. While this means they aren’t as tough in a fight, they can sometimes fit into places far too small for a human. However, what may be the greatest asset to the Bothans is their fur, which they can use as a form of communication by rippling it. Their fur ranges in color from light tan to deep brown and usually covers their entire body except part of their face, which it surrounds as both a mane and a beard. A little-known fact about Bothan physiology is that they have retractable claws, as they rarely use them.
csg_bothan.society: Bothans are natural spies who base their society on the acquisition, manipulation, and selling of information. Unlike many other enterprising species, they are not driven by wealth as much as reputation. Prestige, they view, is really all that they can have or gain. This is hard to get, however, as Bothans are notorious for not trusting anyone. While open combat is incredibly rare, blackmail, gossip, and rhetoric are their weapon of choice. Bothans are skilled politicians, and they are governed by the Bothan Council. Their society is divided into a clan system, and about 600 of the major clans receive a representative on this body. This parliament then elects a Council Chief to lead it. The clans are large groups of families, and Bothans combine their family name with their clan name in order to form their last name, with an apostrophe separating the two. Despite their tendency towards subtlety, Bothans do have a limit: When faced with an enemy that is despicable enough, they will declare a total war, called ar’krai. Under an ar’krai, they will not stop fighting until their enemy is totally annihilated and wiped from history. Ar’krai has been declared twice ever, and no one knows its extinct victims. A third ar’krai will be declared against the Yuuzhan Vong.
csg_bothan.language: The Bothans almost all speak Basic, as well as their native tongue, Bothese. Its written form is Botha. Bothans also have another language: Wrendui. This language uses body language and ripples of the fur in order to subtly convey information. It is naturally coded, so it takes a cipher to understand.
csg_bothan.homeworld: Bothawui is a well-populated city planet in the Mid Rim known for its banking industries and many corporate headquarters. It has a temperate climate, and is of course a hub for information and spying. The Bothans also have colonies on Torolis and the water world of Kothlis, which have less political power.
csg_bothan.description: The Bothans are paranoid and rarely trust anyone. They are canines who use their small size and enhanced senses to their benefit when it comes to stealth. Since they run the Bothan Spynet, they are often seen in this role.
csg_bothan.sidebar_text: The Bothan Spynet is the most advanced and powerful network in the galaxy for intelligence. It is used to collect information on any potential enemies, which, to the Bothans, are pretty much anyone. It is diverse in nature, with some branches working for the Empire while others collect information for the Rebellion. It has knowledge about the criminal underworlds as well. It is active all over the galaxy and is devoted to the interests of the Bothans, although the lower ranks are more diverse.

csg_bovorian.name: Bovorian

special_abilities.name: Skeptical
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Nobody’s Fool.”

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Advanced Hearing
special_abilities.description: Add 3 boosts on auditory Perception checks. Quadruple all sonic damage and, at the GM’s discretion, increase sonic damage from 0 to up to 4.

csg_bovorian.physiology: Bovorians are a species of mammals with vestigial wings under their arms, harkening back to a day when they were flying creatures. They have a lanky build, and they are usually lighter than humans despite averaging over just two meters in height. Most do not wear clothing over their yellowish skin. Their head features white hair, prominent eyebrow ridges, eyes that can see infrared, widely set nostrils, and a long, pointed chin. Their ears are very wide, appearing as a massive fan-like membrane coming from just behind their eyes, which allows them to hear up to a kilometer away. Bovorian limbs have four digits, and their toes end in pointed nails. Similar to many avians, they have a somewhat flimsy biology and a very sensitive respiratory system.
csg_bovorian.society: Bovorians are a cautious and sensitive people who carefully examine all possible repercussions before acting. Though not always actively charitable, they are courteous when it comes to ensuring that they do not annoy or hinder others. They can be somewhat fearful, pessimistic, or outright paranoid, which has prevented them from having major roles in the wider galaxy, but they are loyal after relationships form.
csg_bovorian.language: Bovorians speak Bovorian, a high-pitched and often ultrasonic whistling language. Many also know Basic.
csg_bovorian.homeworld: The Bovorians call their world Razak, but it is Bovo Yagen on official records. They have also colonized Trellar Yagen, a world slightly further away from its sun. Both are hot and moist jungle planets. Industry is highly restricted on Bovo Yagen due to their sensitive hearing, but Trellar Yagen is more open to factories.
csg_bovorian.description: A cautious species of mammals that once had the ability to fly, the Bovorians are a generally isolated race apart from the small colony of refugees from the Empire that have settled in their system.
csg_bovorian.sidebar_text: The Bovorians have been a fairly isolated people, having been discovered by the wider galaxy during the New Sith Wars and immediately being exposed to the horrors of Sith tyranny. They found other planets to be noisy, dangerous, and polluted, so few ever travelled offworld. They resisted Republic settlement for so long that the records of the Galactic Empire had completely forgotten their system. This made it a prime destination for the Corellian former Imperial captain Bovo Yagen (whose name’s similarity with the species was coincidental). Despite the skepticism of the natives, he formed a settlement there, and over time the Bovorians came to appreciate his family, and now they’ve even opened up their system to more refugees from the Empire. Humans, Sullustans, Drall, and other non-Bovorians now number over a million. To keep the settlement discreet, Bovo Yagen never told the Empire about the six million native Bovorians. Painting himself as a colonist, he registered the Bovorian’s homeworld under his own name, Bovo Yagen, on official records, and he named the other worlds in their system after his family. Before Bovo’s death in 4 BBY, he and the Bovorians formed a colony on Trellar Yagen, which has quickly become a flourishing industrial world. Bovorians are slowly starting to appreciate the positives of the wider galaxy, and after the Empire’s fall, they will start openly accepting traders from the New Republic.
csg_bovorian._provenance_note: The Bovorian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_brizzit.name: Brizzit

special_abilities.name: Uniformity
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Indistinguishable.”

special_abilities.name: Swamp Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or wet conditions, add setback for cold or dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Enhanced Senses
special_abilities.description: Add boost on all Vigilance and Perception checks. May see in all directions.

csg_brizzit.physiology: To the human eye, all Brizzits look basically the same: They have gray-brown skin, a mouth with two mandibles, and gigantic compound eyes on either side of their head. They also have two sensory antennae protruding left and right from where humans would have a nose. Brizzits, it would seem, do not have a nose, judging by their taste in locales: They prefer hot, muddy homes that most species would consider unpleasant, like swamps and sewers. What Brizzits are capable of noticing is sudden movements, thanks to the sensory hairs protruding from their antennae and atop their head. Their lower body is mostly humanoid, although they have only four fingers on each hand. Younger Brizzits have fin-like structures over the backs of their hands, but these recede with age.
csg_brizzit.society: Brizzits have a somewhat unpleasant reputation, which can be partially explained by their stench and appearance, but they do little to help it with a dour, pessimistic attitude. They’re not particularly reliable, and their cautiousness leads them to often back out of commitments once a situation becomes difficult or dangerous. While Brizzits can act very quickly when the situation calls for it, they are generally quite patient, diligently planning their actions and never acting out of haste. Unlike many insectoid species, Brizzits do not have a hive structure and are actually quite independent. Even their larvae survive on their own by hunting other insects and small fish in the swamps, and once they crawl out of the water, they receive a brief government-organized education before becoming independent. The concept of family is foreign to Brizzits, and mates only know each other briefly before depositing fertilized eggs into a swamp.
csg_brizzit.language: Brizzits speak the buzzing language of Szivhz, and they struggle to speak Basic without adding buzz sounds, so many prefer to use translator droids.
csg_brizzit.homeworld: Brizzits hail from Ivvfis, a steamy Outer Rim planet along the northern part of the Hydian Way which exports a variety of rare fruits. They also have a few colonies, including Jandoon and Gulma, though the latter is being stripped of all resources by the Empire.
