csg_brizzit.description: Brizzits are a species of swamp-dwelling insects who boast twitchy senses thanks to their antennae, which can sense motion. They are independently minded with no concept of families, and they have a generally pessimistic attitude, as they are easily scared.
csg_brizzit.sidebar_text: Brizzits have a colony on Jandoon, a world whose native Edoonians mysteriously disappeared almost five centuries ago. In reality, the Edoonians grew afraid of the Republic becoming tyrannical and secretly relocated their entire society underground, only emerging in secret to gather food underwater or in the wilderness. Occasional encounters with these supposedly extinct Edoonians lead to persistent rumors that the planet is haunted, and many species avoid it. While Brizzits can be timid, they aren’t superstitious, and some have found mysterious things digging underground. Many search for the “Eye of the Beyonder,” an elaborate tapestry displayed in the Edoonian’s capital before their disappearance. It had cryptic inscriptions rumored to lead to the species’ secret treasure. In reality, these rumors were spread by the Edoonians themselves as a red herring.
csg_brizzit._provenance_note: The Brizzit species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_brubb.name: Brubb

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Camouflage
special_abilities.description: Add boost on Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Deafness
special_abilities.description: Add two setbacks on auditory Perception checks. Cut distances required to hear speech in half.

csg_brubb.physiology: Adapted to high-gravity conditions, Brubbs are a species of herbivorous reptiles who are strong and durable for their humanoid size. Their ears are mostly vestigial, as howling winds make hearing almost useless. They have thick but transparent membranes over their eyes in addition to their eyelids, and this extra layer can grant them protection from harsh sandstorms. They have dark hair which comes in one or more braids, and they have bony ridges at their eyebrows and lips. They smell with their forked tongue, and their nose is restricted to respiratory functions. Their skin, which is thick enough to make them more durable than other species, can also change color, granting them a limited degree of camouflage. However, its spectrum of colors is limited to shades of yellow, gray, and green. As reptiles, they reproduce by laying eggs once per year.
csg_brubb.society: Brubbs are a highly social people who live in tightly-knit communities of extended families called habas. These groups can contain as many as ten thousand or as few as ten individuals. Each haba is devoted to a particular business, such as a farm, mine, or factory. In their free time, Brubbs are almost always socializing, whether it is a communal dinner or a formal dance. To ensure that Brubbs end up where they are most well-suited and create a diverse population, children are raised communally by the haba, rather than only their parents, and they are then traded away to another haba once they are mature. Each haba gives and receives an equal amount of children when trading with one another, with the exception of the prestigious university habas. Sending children to university habas is seen as a great benefit, because members of the universities pass on their knowledge back to their original haba. Children sent to universities stay there for life, where they earn generous wages to develop new technologies.
csg_brubb.language: Given their near-deafness, the Brubbs’ native language is likely a sign language. Because of their love of social interactions, they typically know Basic.
csg_brubb.homeworld: A rocky Outer Rim planet with almost three times standard gravity, the Brubb homeworld of Baros is a harsh and isolated planet. It is mostly desert, and it is extremely hot and dry. Dust storms are common. None of its tangible commodities attract much trade interest, and the planet is fairly isolated, but many of the Brubbs themselves use their strength as guards or their color-changing abilities as entertainers.
csg_brubb.description: Although their hearing is very poor, Brubbs are a social people who enjoy parties, banquets, and dances. They combine their charms with a durability built to withstand a high-gravity desert with fierce winds.
csg_brubb.sidebar_text: Brubbs lay eggs every year, which is 567 days, and women are very selective about their mates. Typically, both mates will protect their egg together, but some males will abandon their nest to mate with multiple women. It is seen as humiliating for a woman to guard a nest on her own, so it is not uncommon for her to hunt down and murder the philanderer. Even when this does not happen, laying eggs is also very difficult work, and it does serious harm to the body of Brubb women, so they have a shorter lifespan because of this. Unfortunately for them, all Brubb habas are ruled by the ten eldest Brubbs, so this means that men are almost always in charge of their societies. To combat this, many women demand that the rulers be the five oldest males and five oldest females, but such cries have fallen on deaf ears. As such, many women now refuse to lay eggs in protest, and the two genders remain bitterly divided.

csg_brknaa.name: B’rknaa

special_abilities.name: Force Immunity
special_abilities.description: When being targeted by Force Powers, cause the check to automatically fail.

special_abilities.name: Hive Mind
special_abilities.description: Communicate telepathically and automatically provide or receive assistance with all other B’rknaa within extreme range. To act against the shared mind, must pass a Discipline vs. Discipline check opposed by it.

csg_brknaa.physiology: B’rknaa begin their lives as clusters of jagged blue-colored crystals, immobile and seemingly lifeless. However, they are intelligent, and once they become old enough, they develop the ability to control inanimate objects. Typically, they build a body out of rock for themselves, although it may be possible to use other materials if they are available. Their gigantic mineral shells are, of course, highly resistant to damage, and they are extremely strong physically, making them formidable foes in combat. Typically, their structure is humanoid, with pillar-like legs, broad shoulders, and an expressionless face. Their original crystal makeup still peers through two eye sockets in their head, and they have a gaping mouth as well. Their arms end in four-fingered hands, but they seemingly lack feet as their legs simply truncate.
csg_brknaa.society: B’rknaa are by all appearances very simple and primitive: They wear no clothing, build no structures, and develop no industries. Although they are capable of speaking aloud, they mostly communicate in silent telepathy via a single hive mind. All B’rknaa are part of this collective consciousness, sharing common goals and acting purely for the good of the species. As a culture, they are very peaceful despite their intimidating appearance, although they have on occasion been forced to take up arms. In particular, they will fight if their youth are in danger, which is not unheard of given that they appear as mere gemstones to other species. Because of their ability to control complex energy, B’rknaa crystals can be worth up to fifty thousand credits, and few offworlders are aware that they are actually sentient. However, whenever they try to mine the crystals, B’rknaa are quick to charge into battle and defend their young. While some in scientific circles are aware of the B’rknaa’s existence, they are regarded as only a minor curiosity and are otherwise isolated.
csg_brknaa.language: B’rknaa speak a raspy language which can be difficult to translate, and due to their isolation, none have ever been known to learn Basic. Because of their communal mind, they have no simple word for “I.”
csg_brknaa.homeworld: B’rknaa come from Indobok, a rocky moon of Kalarba, which is a mountainous Mid Rim world. In reality, Indobok itself is a giant B’rknaa and the forebear to the entire species. Indobok will be put in jeopardy when the Yuuzhan Vong will destroy Kalarba by causing it to collide with its other moon, Hosk Station, a cataclysm which will spew radioactive material throughout the entire system.
csg_brknaa.description: B'rknaa are crystals who share a telepathic hive mind, and they have a unique relationship with the Force. This allows them to assemble bodies made of stone for themselves, which their adult members use to move around. They come from the moon of Indobok which itself is a giant member of the species.
csg_brknaa.sidebar_text: Clearly, the mystical power of the Force is at work in allowing the B’rknaa to control inanimate stones and telepathically communicate with one another, but their relationship with it is a unique one. It is possible that, like the Yuuzhan Vong, B’rknaa interact with an entirely different facet of the Force. This theory is corroborated by the fact that they are entirely immune to all direct applications of the Force, including but not limited to telepathy, telekinesis, and healing. The Jedi of the Old Republic interpreted this ability as redirecting the flow of the Force, but it is also possible that they merely exist outside of the Jedi’s scope. In any case, it is unknown whether or not a particular B’rknaa could develop additional powers.

csg_caamasi.name: Caamasi

special_abilities.name: Skilled Mediators
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

csg_caamasi.physiology: Caamasi are furry mammals with a beak. Their furry down is light gray or golden brown and has a strong smell similar to that of Corellian whiskey, although they have spots of purple around their eyes and in stripes that start on top of their head before going down to their shoulders. Their two arms are long, but having only three clawed fingers means that they sometimes lack the dexterity of other sentients with five fingers. Their beak tends to be pink and has an acute sense of smell via the nose at the end of it. Their eyes are yellow, and their ears point off to the sides of their head.
csg_caamasi.society: Caamasi are a people with pacifistic ways who are almost universally beloved. In fact, their name, in some languages, translates to “trusted stranger,” or “friend from afar.” Their culture centers around the basic tenets of peace and justice, and they are naturally very artistic. They are among the most excellent mediators in the galaxy, with their wise words bringing peace to the hearts of all. It was the Caamasi who managed to even create peace between the Kubaz and Verpine. Furthermore, the Caamasi have strong ties to the Jedi Order. Their philosophies seem so similar to those of Jedi because the Caamasi ways, in fact, inspired the Jedi. The Jedi Scholars on Ossus first constructed the Jedi Code based on Caamasi ways. In 11,000 BBY, it was the Caamasi who first motivated the Jedi to take arms against the Puis Dea controlled Republic and Chancellor Contispex XIX. The Caamasi are, unfortunately, quite rare now. With their peaceful ways at odds with Imperial philosophies, the Empire arranged a bombing of Caamas in 19 BBY. The surviving Caamasi have since relocated, living on other worlds. While some suggest they use polygamy in order to create more members and regrow the species, the Caamasi are extremely monogamous.
csg_caamasi.language: Caamasi speak Caamasi in addition to Basic. After the devastation of their home, they also rely heavily on memniis to communicate with their relatives.
csg_caamasi.homeworld: The world of Caamas was a well-populated Core world. It had jungles, marshes, steppes, and rolling hills. This all changed in the Caamas Firestorm, in which Star Destroyers decimated the planet via Base Delta Zero. Only 200 Caamasi survived this incident, in addition to any others on other planets. These Caamasi were forced to leave, as the lack of vegetation has polluted the atmosphere. Ironically, many Caamasi relocated to Alderaan. One could say that they’re just looking for safe planets in all the wrong places. Some now survive on Kerilt, a rainforested planet in the Mid Rim.
csg_caamasi.description: Caamasi are extremely pacifistic mammals that are known for their abilities as diplomats. They are known for their strong moral compass, but that did not protect them from a vicious Imperial atrocity that resulted in the deaths of most Caamasi.
csg_caamasi.sidebar_text: All Caamasi are capable of memnii, which are particularly detailed memories. They are created in extremely emotional moments, both good and bad. Unlike regular memories, they do not fade with time. A Caamasi can perfectly recall these events as well as all of the emotions associated with them. A memnii can be transferred to close relatives or to Force-sensitives that they have a very close bond with. Some suggest that Caamasi may share memnii in their mating process, but they do not discuss that with outsiders. Because of their memnii, Caamasi who commit horrible acts or experience great pain have a hard time forgetting their actions.

csg_caarite.name: Caarite

special_abilities.name: Heat and Humidity Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or wet conditions, add setback for cold or dry conditions.

csg_caarite.physiology: Caarites are short humanoids (about one meter tall) with porcine features. They have an elongated snout with a large nose, wide cheeks, and pointed ears. They have pink skin and a wide smile with perfectly white teeth. They have no hair, so they are very vulnerable to the cold; however, they are well-adapted to their native environment on Caarimala, which is hot and steamy.
csg_caarite.society: Caarites are a greedy bunch who are willing to resort to any methods necessary to fulfill their goals. Although they are very selfish, they exude a friendly demeanor and a childlike smile in order to appease potential customers. Their small size prevents them from doing well in combat, so most of them prefer to use their charms and their wits instead of resorting to a fight. Very few of them support any cause beyond filling up their own pockets. They were once prominent in the Trade Federation, but they split away to form the Metatherian Cartel on Cularin following the blockade of Naboo, which they felt was bad for business.
csg_caarite.language: Caarites place very high value in the ability to communicate, so they are well-trained in at least three languages. Most know their native language of Caarimala, and they typically understand Basic as their second language. Their third language varies from Caarite to Caarite.
csg_caarite.homeworld: Caarites come from the Outer Rim planet of Caarimon, which is hot and humid. It used to have many rainforests, but an asteroid collision has caused many toxins to spread into the land. Now, the Caarites live in floating cities which are higher up in the atmosphere.
csg_caarite.description: Porcines adapted to a hot and wet environment, the Caarites have a mind for business, and they have a charm that makes them very savvy negotiators. They were once part of the Trade Federation but headed the Metatherian Cartel in more recent years.
csg_caarite.sidebar_text: Unfortunately for the Caarites, they have been crooked for long enough for the rest of the galaxy to understand their ways. Anyone who deals with a Caarite is always very careful, since the Caarites have a reputation for being deceitful. However, many Caarites manage to overcome these difficulties with their wide grins almost childlike demeanor, which they can use to overcome their reputation. Time and time again, Caarites use their charms to make people abandon their belief in stereotypes, and then they immediately take advantage by swindling their trusting, new friend.

csg_calibop.name: Calibop

special_abilities.name: All Talk
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

csg_calibop.physiology: Calibops are a lanky avian sentient species with vestigial wings along their arms. They cannot fly, but flapping their wings does help propel themselves forward and increase their sprinting speed. They have olive-yellow skin and similarly colored feathers along their head, back, and wings. Their face features a dark-colored beak and two nostrils on the sides of their snout. Caibops have blue eyes which are spread out on the sides of their head to enhance their peripheral vision, and also a tail, which they often move as part of their unique body language.
csg_calibop.society: It is widely known that Calibops are talkative and social, far preferring discussion and leadership to direct action, but what many do not realize is that their culture is distinctive in many other regards. Calibops generally form themselves into nomadic tribes of several dozen called “okals,” which roam the jungles and forage a variety of seeds, fruits, and grasses. Harsh seasonal changes require near-constant migration to match the seasons, so permanence of any kind is rare. This makes them highly adaptable and generally accepting of change, though they often recognize that the universe sways in cyclical patterns. Their tribes are fairly dispersed, so meetings are rare, but when they do happen, it is an important event. Generally referred to as a convocation, the okals use it as a chance to barter goods between the tribes, which is a negotiation that can take days. Even more important, it is custom that they must also swap members: At least one member of each okal must join the other, and the abilities of each member often factor into the negotiation. Thus, Calibops are very good at making new friends, although they can be somewhat shallow and struggle with the concept of permanent relationships. They see themselves as resources for the okal, not as an individual, for they have little freedom and no personal possessions. Nuclear families are also foreign to them, as children are raised communally, and polygamy is common.
csg_calibop.language: The constant mingling of cultures has ensured that Calibops speak only one language, Ongif. More modernized okals typically know Basic as well.
csg_calibop.homeworld: Calibops hail from the backwater Mid Rim planet of Melket, a steamy planet with particularly short years. Due to their sensitivity to minute temperature changes, Calibops require near-constant migration. Melket’s high precipitation results in swampy rainforests over its surface, and its lower gravity allows Calibops a limited ability to glide.
csg_calibop.description: Calibops are lanky avians who have the ability to glide on their low-gravity homeworld, and they migrate constantly in their nomadic tribes called okals to avoid its quick seasonal changes. The okals are collectivist, making the Calibops highly social creatures, and they have a reputation for being extremely long-winded.
csg_calibop.sidebar_text: Calibops may be nomadic for the most part, but they are hardly primitive, and they import a variety of technology from airspeeders and weapons to comlinks and scanners. In exchange, many okals are involved with exporting a valuable delicacy called kolomu berries, which cannot be cultivated effectively via intensive farming and must instead be gathered. A minority of okals do live in permanent cities, where they manage the planet’s spaceports or the growing industrial complexes. Many of these more modernized communities also dislike the conventional norms regarding trading, particularly the exchange of members. More traditional okals often look on them with disdain, but they are ultimately dependent on these cities and spaceports for imported goods, so they are thus forced to get along.
csg_calibop._provenance_note: The Calibop species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_carosite.name: Carosite

special_abilities.name: Esteemed Doctors
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Surgeon.”

special_abilities.name: Semi-Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_carosite.physiology: Carosites are species of long-necked mammals slightly shorter than humans on average who are covered in thin fur. Their eyes, nostrils, and ears are all on the side of their long head, and their senses are particularly acute. They have a beak-like mouth that often sports a goatee below it, and their diet consists of mostly seafood, as they are capable swimmers. They have four long digits on each foot, one of which is opposed, so they are often barefoot. Their hands are also dexterous, with five total fingers and two opposable thumbs on each. They can only reproduce twice in their lives, although each instance usually produces a litter with multiple children.
csg_carosite.society: Carosites are known primarily as healers, and their limited birth rate requires a great reverence for life. They are pioneers in a variety of medical techniques, but they are particularly known for treating mental illnesses, and they excel at designing and programming medical droids. They will use cybernetics to replace limbs, but they will not install cybernetic enhancements. Others take a more academic approach, and the Carosi XII Academy of Medicine is among the galaxy’s most renowned medical schools. Regardless of specialization, Carosites are honest, considerate, and often far too trusting, as they assume others will share their integrity. When it comes to medical treatment, they only charge patients for what they can afford. While this usually makes them well-liked, their obsession with health can make them overbearing at times. They despise alcohol, and they can be very critical about their friends’ diet or exercise. Carosites elect a leader democratically, but that leader has absolute power and reigns for a decade. Eleven oligarchs act as counselors. In general, Carosites are strict pacifists, fighting only to defend others who are helpless, although they are sympathetic to the Rebel Alliance. A small but vocal group called The Preventers believes that aggressive military action against the Empire is necessary to save lives over the long term. Some Carosites are curious about the Force for its healing powers, but the galaxy has yet to see a Carosite Jedi.
csg_carosite.language: Carosites can speak Basic as well as their own language. In either tongue, they use medical metaphors to describe a variety of situations.
csg_carosite.homeworld: 200 years ago, the star Carosi became a red giant, heating up its worlds. The Carosite homeworld, Carosi IV became scorched, but the ice planet Carosi XII became warm enough to live on, and their entire society moved over the course of two decades, although they continue to terraform their new home. These changes have led some Carosites arguing that they abandon past traditions and modify their society. Regardless, Carosi XII is a chilly, low-gravity world with glaciers and plains. Its single ocean, the Avuae Sea, is below freezing but stays liquid because of its high mineral content, and it hosts a variety of marine life, as well as many Carosite swimmers. The planet also features geothermal hot springs, which is a popular tourist destination and also useful for healing.
csg_carosite.description: Because of their low birth rate, Carosites are extremely diligent in taking care of the members they do have, and they make excellent doctors. These long-necked marine mammals have developed one of the galaxy's premier medical schools on their world, and they also operate mobile hospitals.
csg_carosite.sidebar_text: One of the most famous Carosite ventures is the Sudden Restoration, a KDY Class-C Frigate which travels the galaxy and offers free medical care, often showing up on battlefields. It cares for about 2,000 patients at once, healing rebels, Imperials, and ne’er do wells alike. With its great success and legendary recovery rate, Carosites are making more ships like it. Because of its popularity, the Empire dares not shut it down directly, but Imperials have blackmailed at least one physician into sabotaging the treatment of rebels.

csg_cathar.name: Cathar

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound.

csg_cathar.physiology: The Cathar are predatory felines who have great instincts as warriors. Though not incredibly large, they are fast and possess excellent reflexes. Further making them formidable in combat are their retractable claws and great healing abilities. They have pointed ears, a mane around their head, sharp teeth, and a black nose. Though their brown skin is similar in color to fur, they do not have fur over the rest of their body. There are two other subspecies, the Juhani and the Myr Rho, both of which are more similar to humans in terms of looks.
csg_cathar.society: Though Cathar are a passionate people known for their temper and emotions, they also strongly value honor and loyalty. They are as dedicated and as determined as anyone. They are organized into clans which are lead by “Elders.” These clans inhabit cities that are built into giant trees and have carvings that store their history. They greatly value monogamy, mating for life and never loving another, even for those whose spouses die. Their religion includes a ritual known as a “Blood Hunt.” In this dangerous rite of passage, a single Cathar goes into battle against a horde of kiltik. The kiltik are giant insectoids who are very dangerous. Blood Hunts are believed to teach courage and purge inner darkness, but they are also an important way to gain honor.
csg_cathar.language: The Cathar mostly speak accented Basic in addition to knowing their native language, Catharese.
csg_cathar.homeworld: The Cathar homeworld, Cathar, is a planet of mostly savannahs that is covered by giant trees. It is a dangerous world because of the giant kiltiks.
csg_cathar.description: Disciplined yet ferocious felines with sharp claws and fast healing, Cathar have a history as warriors, although they were once devastated by Mandalorians. They are religious and value honor.
csg_cathar.sidebar_text: Long ago, Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders devastated the Cathar and their homeworld: In the fateful Battle of Cathar, about 90 percent of the population was killed by the Mandalorians. While a few fled and survived, the rest were taken as slaves by their conquerors. Not only did the population suffer, but the ecological damage done lasted for a long time as well. It is now finally repaired, however. Before that, the Cathar settled on worlds like Ord Mantell and Taris. Their time as slaves to the Mandalorians has ended, but many are now enslaved by the Empire or other organizations. While females are prized as slaves, the males’ ferocious temper makes them too difficult to control.

csg_celegian.name: Celegian

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Cyanogen Breathers
special_abilities.description: Need a cyanogen tank to breathe in a normal environment. Receive a free cyanogen tank at character creation. Oxygen is a dangerous atmosphere of rating 8.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Natural Levitation
special_abilities.description: May float in the air and move in any direction without touching anything, but may only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

special_abilities.name: Telepathy
special_abilities.description: May communicate telepathically, projecting messages silently to one or more beings within 500 meters. May also receive messages telepathically from willing subjects.

csg_celegian.physiology: Celegians are crustaceans who look similar to jellyfish and generally float around using their form of natural levitation. Living about 3 times longer than humans, they can live in air or water but require complete submersion in cyanogen, a gas which is lethal to other species. They have a large, brain-like mass of more than a meter in diameter at the top of their body. They have four large tentacles, about two meters long, and several small tentacles which descend from their brain. Although they are not especially coordinated, they can use these tentacles to grasp objects. Their skin is a mottled mix of red, pink, and white. Despite their lack of clearly visible eyes or ears, they are still capable of sight and hearing. They are also telepathic, which lets them communicate silently with anyone nearby.
csg_celegian.society: Celegians are an intellectual species who are very wise and thoughtful. They typically enjoy puzzles and riddles, and they tend to be more logical than abstract. They almost always avoid combat, likely a result of the vulnerabilities presented by their physiology. However, they are not always cowardly, as they also enjoy exploration. Many Celegians in the galaxy find work as scouts or other explorers.
csg_celegian.language: Celegian telepathy operates without any language, meaning that they can communicate ideas with anyone.
csg_celegian.homeworld: Celegians come from the Expansion Region planet of Celegia, which is covered in seas. It has cyanogen dissolved underwater and in the atmosphere.
csg_celegian.description: Celegians are a species of large crustaceans adapted to cyanogen oceans, so they must surround themselves with a chamber of the substance when they are on other planets. They do not speak, instead using their natural telepathy.
csg_celegian.sidebar_text: All Celegians not in a cyanogen environment must use a cyanogen chamber in order to survive, and conventional breath masks cannot act as a substitute. They float around in the chambers, which are typically made of transparisteel and equipped with repulsorlifts to give them some mobility. A cyanogen chamber costs 6,000 credits and completely encloses up to 15 encumbrance, preventing any attacks from going in or out. However, it can be ruptured with 8 points of damage. It can only move once per turn and still requires a maneuver to move.

csg_cerean.name: Cerean

special_abilities.name: Intellectuals
special_abilities.description: Receive 2 free career skills of choice. These skills must be Knowledge skills. Still may not receive a free rank in them without spending XP.

csg_cerean.physiology: Cereans are near-humans, almost entirely identical to humans from the eyebrows down. However, they have a tall head that holds their large binary brain and a second heart. Most notably, this brain is excellent at multitasking and holding multiple trains of thought at once, as its two halves are strongly divided. This comes at the expense of compactness, and the weight from their large head can make them less coordinated and sometimes causes back problems later in life. Beyond this, differences from humans are minor: their long forehead has little hair, as they generally lack eyebrows and often prefer to wear their hair back. Their hands have five fingers, but the digits have slight claws at the ends.
csg_cerean.society: Cereans have a low-tech society on Cerea, which they are fine to keep relatively isolated, especially after being the site of vicious conflict during the Clone Wars. They are ruled by a Council of Elders, which is led by a president, careful to see issues from every possible perspective, and female-dominated. Male Cereans are very rare genetically, about five percent of their population, so a male will typically have several “honor wives” in order to sustain the population. However, they only have one “bond wife.” Cereans embrace the Force culturally, and their analysis can appear to others as precognition. Cerean male names are three hyphenated parts, which are derivatives of the names from their parents and grandparents. Females have only a single name, though bond wives will take a second name, that of their husband’s grandfather. Despite Cerea’s lack of tech, Cereans are quick to learn technology when offworld, and many have made excellent scientists, astrographers, engineers, or programmers. They tend to be detailed, fair, and rational by nature, and their philosophies are peaceful. Any aggression they have is spent on the art of traditional shyarn dueling, a battle of curved magnetic swords that can also be a choreographed dance.
csg_cerean.language: Cereans speak Cerean, a language of long compound words and many glottal stops. They also typically learn Basic, despite their isolationist nature.
csg_cerean.homeworld: Cereans come from the world of Cerea, which is notable for its lack of pollution and harmony with nature. The low-tech society keeps the planet in excellent shape, and the Cereans live in giant buildings to preserve space. The land is otherwise used for farming, which they do without the help of technology. It is isolated from the rest of the galaxy and covered in lush vegetation, mountains, rivers, and plains. Outsider technology is only allowed in the Outsider Citadels, and the Cereans are very touchy about any pollution. For the Cereans who are more fond of adapting to outsider technology, the Empire made means for them to relocate to Bavinyar, settling them on an archipelago once inhabited by human Separatists. After the human population fled their world to evade the Empire, the Cereans have taken over the planet. After the Emperor's demise, humans will return to Bavinyar, and the population will have an uneasy peace between the two peoples.
csg_cerean.description: A binary brain allows the Cereans to have powerful intellectual abilities and easily multitask. They have avoided technology on their home planet in order to protect from environmental damage.
csg_cerean.sidebar_text: Meditation is a very important ritual in daily life for Cereans, even ones without the Force. To focus during meditation, they use kasha crystals, which are calming and clear the mind of distractions. They have patterns engraved into them which help harness the full potential of their harmonic energy. When used as a lightsaber crystal, the kasha gives the user focus and calm, even in intense combat situations. Their inclination toward meditation has made many excellent Cerean Jedi, and those who do follow this path are allowed to have honor wives if they are male. Rumor has it that some Cereans have also been able to take advantage of their binary brain and contemplate the light and dark sides simultaneously.

csg_chadra_fan.name: Chadra-Fan

special_abilities.name: 7 Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks from Perception checks.

csg_chadra_fan.physiology: Chadra-Fan are rodent-like creatures. They average about a meter tall and are not particularly strong, but they make up for this with several other advantages. First, they have great senses. Not only are all of their senses more acute than a human’s, they also boast two extra: infrared sight from their large, dark eyes, and chemoreceptive smell from the inner two of the four nostrils on their flat, bat-like nose. Their fast metabolism also means that they need very little sleep and can survive off of a couple two hour naps each day. They have two hearts but still will die after a few days if either one stops working. Their body is covered in brown fur, and males and females are visually identical. They can identify the gender of other Chadra-Fan using their keen smell, which is also useful for sensing pheromones. Chadra-Fan show their emotions through these scents rather than facial expressions, although some of the pheromones are released involuntarily. Others they can control and use to send fairly complex messages. They mature in fifteen years and usually die by 40 years.
csg_chadra_fan.society: Chadra-Fan are amiable creatures, and they regard very few things as permanent, a result of the frequent tsunamis that devastate their coastal homes. What is left is to eat, drink, and be merry, so their outlook is generally positive. They constantly busy themselves and love to tinker or create unique devices, which are considered to be more art than useful tools. Some collectors take a keen interest in buying them as novelties. Coming from a water world, they have an instinctive fear of drowning, which is so strong that many relocate to arid worlds. A decade ago, their fears were strengthened when a massive tsunami wiped out much of the life on their planet, and on its anniversary, they now remember it by lighting billions of candles and sending them afloat into the ocean. Their ancient religion claims that a deity under the waves is responsible for such floods, although few modern Chadra-Fan take it seriously. They live in intimate clans, where all households are open, few keep track of their immediate family, and the entire clan shares responsibility for raising all children. Leadership is quickly passed on by situation. Trying to replicate this structure in the wider galaxy, they are not picky with friends and will avoid loneliness at any cost, as they can die of depression within weeks if alone for too long. They are also very forgiving and will only get angry from the most vile of acts.
csg_chadra_fan.language: Chadra-Fan speak Chadra-Fan. It is sensitive to pitch and very squeaky. The Chadra-Fan can speak Basic, but their voice is generally fairly high-pitched.
csg_chadra_fan.homeworld: Chadra-Fan come from the world known as Chad, also known as Chadra or Chad III, which is a watery world in the eastern Outer Rim with nine moons. It is fairly hot, very moist, and prone to flooding. Its orbit is eccentric, but the climate is fairly uniform across seasons because of its tiny axial tilt. Though a major planet in the dairy industry, it is still fairly primitive with technology, and the Chadra-Fan live in open-air buildings that are cheap to construct and move amid the trees of wetland areas, where they travel via methane-powered boats. A small population of immigrant humans also calls it home.
csg_chadra_fan.description: Chadra-Fan are optimistic and amiable, always seeing the best in others. They love to tinker with mechanics. They are very small rodents who are instinctively afraid of drowning, so many leave their homeworld of Chad.
csg_chadra_fan.sidebar_text: Many Chadra-Fan have been taken offworld as slaves. They generally don’t fight this and just follow along with whatever happens. This laid-back attitude makes them almost aloof to their mistreatment, so they are often content and can even view it as a big adventure, seeing new people and planets.

csg_chagrian.name: Chagrian

special_abilities.name: Scholars
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Knowledge Specialization.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_chagrian.physiology: Chagrians are an aquatic species, and they begin their life as tiny tadpoles before they can emerge from the water. As adults, they are amphibious and similar in size to most sentients. They have a skin that ranges in color from lighter shades of blue to cobalt. They have horns growing down the sides of their head and onto their chest which are quite elegant. Males also have two more horns called lethorns that grow upward. All Chagrians keep their horns very well cared for. They cannot taste at all as adults, so they eat purely for nutritional value.
csg_chagrian.society: Chagrians live in a very wealthy society, so they find poverty and inequality to be disgusting, surprising, and unjust. As a people they are normally very reserved and serene, however. They are sticklers when it comes to procedure and are very law abiding. Justice is an important concept for them, so their courts are incredibly meticulous. Those Chagrians that do commit crimes typically admit their guilt, however. Their relative affluence and comfort makes them stand up against injustice often, so many also join the Rebel Alliance. They have a strong desire to please others, which, when combined with their respect for traditions, makes them excellent as diplomats. One custom that doesn’t work as well for them is meals, as their lack of taste makes them find the practice to be a waste of time.
csg_chagrian.language: The Chagrian language of Chagri is rarely used off of Champala. Not all Chagrians know Basic, but they can learn it relatively easily.
csg_chagrian.homeworld: Chagrians are native to the water world of Champala, found in the Inner Rim. Its cities are built entirely underwater or in tidal zones so that they are submerged half the time. Spaceports are above water to appeal to its many tourists. While tourism on its coastlines and beaches has been a major industry, industrial pollution from Imperial mining operations have recently reduced it.
csg_chagrian.description: Peace and justice are extremely important to Chagrians, as they are reserved and serene. Their physiology is amphibious, so they are only aquatic as children before they can breathe on land. They cannot taste, so they eat only for nutrition.
csg_chagrian.sidebar_text: In the Chagrian spirit of compassion and fairness, killing civilians in a war is seen as a horrible mistake. As such, during their rare conflicts, soldiers wear a certain shade of maroon red to indicate that they may be attacked, thus reducing accidental attacks on civilians. While uniform standards mean that those in offworld militaries cannot wear entirely red, they still often incorporate it into the uniforms.

csg_chalactan.name: Chalactan

special_abilities.name: Staunchly Committed
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Nobody’s Fool.”

csg_chalactan.physiology: Chalactans are a near-human people with only a few differences. Their skin is a little bit darker than that of most humans, and they also generally have darker-colored hair. They are somewhat notable in that their females have a high rate of Force-sensitivity and are very often Jedi. These female Chalactan Jedi include Knight Sar Labooda, Padawan Klossi Anno, and High Councilor Depa Billaba. While they are not genetically compatible with humans, Chalactans are otherwise fairly similar to them in appearance and biology. Most are also distinguished by their facial piercings, which have religious significance in their culture.
csg_chalactan.society: Chalactans are a spiritual people who are focused on meditation, self-control, and discipline. While they focus greatly on knowledge and their mind, they are more philosophical than practical. They prefer to teach by using riddles. On the other side of this, they are a simpler people who are trusting and benevolent. Their spirituality and philosophy often makes them not get along entirely well, especially with those who do not share their values. However, they are a very calm people who are typically cool and collected. Because they can often avoid conflict by being that way, they are also very pacifistic. Their religious views further enforce that.
csg_chalactan.language: Chalactans generally know Basic as well as their own native language. The latter is often used for religious purposes.
csg_chalactan.homeworld: Chalacta is a planet in the eastern part of the Mid Rim that is the Chalactan homeworld. A terrestrial world of seas and plains, it is a refugee for the spiritual. It is the headquarters for the Chalactan Adepts and has the Temple of Illumination. When facing a big decision, many Chalactans will return home to consult those in the Temple of Illumination.
csg_chalactan.description: Religion is vital to the near-human species known as the Chalactans, as they are almost all members of the Chalactan Adepts. They are extremely strong-willed, as their beliefs center around self-control and discipline.
csg_chalactan.sidebar_text: Almost all Chalactans fall into the religion of Chalactan Adepts. The Chalactan Adepts focus on many of the views that distinguish the Chalactans as a whole. They are a mystical people with a complex philosophy. They strive constantly to receive illumination, also called Enlightenment. This is best defined as an understanding of the natural laws of the universe, which they also believe to exist in every single sentient person. All Adepts have a piercing near the top of their nose referred to as the Lesser Mark. It symbolizes their quest for Enlightenment. Once a Chalactan Adept has received Enlightenment, they receive a Greater Mark of Illumination in the lower middle of their forehead. Both these marks are small golden beads featuring the “Unclosable Eye” that are attached on by piercing. They are ruled by a Convocation of Adepts and study at the Temple of Illumination. On the more practical level, Chalactan Adepts are known to use their discipline to be nearly immune to manipulation and torture.

csg_chandrilan_human.name: Chandrilan Human

special_abilities.name: Intellectual Debate
special_abilities.description: When arguing persuasively, may add boosts equal to ranks in a relevant Knowledge skill at the GM’s discretion.

csg_chandrilan_human.physiology: Chandrilans are a culture of humans, so they differ more through culture than physiology. Some of the humans on Chandrila are immigrants who can have different genetics entirely. Those of mostly Chandrilan ancestry typically have lighter skin and hair.
csg_chandrilan_human.society: Chandrilan culture is well-known for its combination of debate and environmentalism. The former is related to a strong connection to democracy. The Chandrilans value the right to speak freely and participate in politics. They have unparalleled rights to protesting, but most express their beliefs in public debates. Every city or town has a debate rotunda where anyone is free to debate issues with others or with government officials. This greatly reduces corruption and makes the Chandrilans place high value in free speech. They use many tactics to debate, but most avoid personal attacks. Because of the great scrutiny related to debate, lies are also rare. They are very pacifistic politically. The Chandrilans have a strong preference for conservation that is almost equally noteworthy. While they prefer reduced roles for the government and increased freedom, the environment is an exception. Families are reduced to no more than two children so that the population stays around one billion. They let animals roam freely in cities and also protect them in preserves. Industrial pollution is essentially non-existent. Nature walks are a common hobby for Chandrilans, as are boating, fishing, and sun jammer racing. They are also an artistic people who value painting, dance, and theater.
csg_chandrilan_human.homeworld: Chandrila is Core world on the Perlemian Trade Route. It is a farming world of meadows and plains. Hanna City is the capital city; it is found near Lake Sah’ot. It has the Imperial garrison and the government buildings. The only place on the world zoned for industry is Emita, which has made many advances in clean technologies.
csg_chandrilan_human.description: Chandrilans are a unique human culture that have two notable things. First is their extreme pacifism, as most prefer to settle disagreements via debate. The other is their focus on protecting the environment, so their planet is in excellent condition.
csg_chandrilan_human.sidebar_text: Chandrilan beliefs run almost exactly opposite to those of the Empire. Their former Senator, Mon Mothma, is a known Rebel leader. With the Empire unable to use the Death Star on Chandrila, Palpatine has let Gerald Weizel govern the planet. Weizel attempted to blockade the planet, but underestimated the determination of the Rebel Alliance. The planet was freed by Rogue Squadron. However, the Empire has placed forces above its neighbors and used tariffs on food to hurt the Chandrilan economy. This indirect blockade has forced Chandrilans to rely on smugglers. While their orbital fleet is ready to defend the planet should the Empire attack, the people will not attack the Imperial garrison.

csg_charon.name: Charon

special_abilities.name: Natural Armor
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 3 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Webs
special_abilities.description: May shoot webs once per encounter, attacking within short range using Athletics. Deal no damage, but have the Ensnare 3 quality. May also use webs as a tool similar to rope.

csg_charon.physiology: Charon are hulking arachnids who are more than two meters tall. In addition to some hair, they are covered by a gray, brown, or turquoise carapace which is thick enough to offer them protection. They also have three sharp claws on each of their eight limbs. They have mandibles on their mouth and two large eyes which have slit pupils. Although their upper body is upright, their abdomen trails horizontally. They can shoot webs from their abdomen, which can be used like ropes or as an offensive weapon. They have a short lifespan, reaching adulthood at six and typically dying around 60. They have two castes: Warriors are distinguished by darker skin, while Bioscientists have colored cilia on their limbs.
csg_charon.society: Charon are simple-minded and obsessive, and they will do whatever it takes to get what they want. Many are extremely ruthless and immoral, and a majority desire nothing more than the murder of everything that they encounter. The technology that they developed is biological, although the organisms they use lack free will. Unlike the Yuuzhan Vong, they are willing to use mechanical devices when available, but simply believe that biotechnology is more effective. Bioscientists develop this technology, while the Warriors focus on combat.
csg_charon.language: The Charon language is composed of bizarre clicking and scratching, and a few other insect species can replicate it. Few have any reason to learn Basic.
csg_charon.homeworld: The Charon homeworld is unnamed, bleak, and barely habitable. It is surrounded by black holes, which means that it will soon be sucked in. The Charon live in a pocket of space called otherspace, which acts similar to another dimension. They have annihilated all other species in otherspace and generally do not know how to reenter the galaxy. However, there is a colony of other Charon on Kayri III, although there are only a couple dozen of them.
csg_charon.description: Eight-limbed arachnids with sharp claws and the ability to shoot webs, the Charon come from a pocket of space known as otherspace, where they are almost entirely isolated from the rest of the galaxy. This is a great relief, as their cult-like religion makes them wish to end all life in the galaxy.
csg_charon.sidebar_text: One of the most important figures in Charon society is the Prophet of the Void, the leader of the death cult that governs society. Their goal is to cast all life “into the Void of Death.” They have conducted many successful genocides under this desire. However, there is a smaller group called the “Cult of the Light,” which opposes the ways of the Prophet of the Void but acts in secret. These few Charon will discover the hyperdrive in a few years, but they will attempt to keep their discovery secret in order to prevent the other Charon from invading the galaxy. The Cult of the Light is peaceful, seeking to make colonies and contact other species. They are also unique in that members are given names.

csg_chawenhe.name: Cha’wen’he

special_abilities.name: Natural Explorers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Galaxy Mapper.”

special_abilities.name: Heel Spikes
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Three Heads
special_abilities.description: May see in all directions.

csg_chawenhe.physiology: One of the galaxy’s more uniquely built species, the Cha’wen’he are flightless and featherless avians distinguished by their three snake-like heads, each of which has a flexible two-meter long neck. Standing at about four meters tall with their necks fully extended, they have a wide body with two thin legs, and both legs end in a three-toed foot. Additionally, they have spikes on their heels that they use for self-defense. Their legs, necks, and body are all covered in scales. Unlike multi-headed Troigs or Paaerduags, each of their heads does not have its own consciousness. However, their heads are distributed evenly around the body, allowing them to see in all directions. Each head also has four digits around its mouth, which the Cha’wen’he use as fingers. This ability, combined with their flexible necks, means that any of their heads can act as limbs when needed. They are herbivores, and they are naturally very high-energy, preferring to stay on the move at all times.
csg_chawenhe.society: Facing a great deal of predators on their planet, Cha’wen’he are naturally hypervigilant, anxious, and easily scared. Their society is organized into flocks, all of whom are nomadic, and they lack a central government. Even fact, even the flocks have no official rulers and constantly shift between a number of informal leaders. This strange structure makes it hard for them to negotiate with offworlders, as changes in leadership can render treaties or contracts null and void. They also have no private property, and everything they own is shared among the entire flock. Most of them eventually learn such concepts in their dealings with other species, but the idea of private land is still foreign to them, and they will often trespass. Because of their wanderlust, those who leave their home tend to become explorers.
csg_chawenhe.language: Cha’wen’he have no known native language and typically speak Basic.
csg_chawenhe.homeworld: Cha’wen’he come from Wen’he’dinae, a backwater Mid Rim planet with no organized government. The Cha’wen’he are still hunted by many predators, and the Imperials have also attempted to rule the planet. However, because the Cha’wen’he have no real permanent cities or larger governments, Imperial rule has little effect on them.
csg_chawenhe.description: Cha’wen’he are a bizarre three-headed species that is constantly on the run, whether it be to escape danger or to satiate their wanderlust. They organize into flocks with a communal mentality, having little care for their personal advancement, and their leadership changes unpredictably.
csg_chawenhe.sidebar_text: Cha’wen’he learn skills through a strange sort of genetic memory in addition to learning them from their mentors. Their most primitive motor skills, for example, are so entrenched in their genetic code that they can walk, run, and grasp objects almost as soon as they are born. However, genes which grant them memories of more complicated skills can only be accessed later in life and activate almost randomly. As such, they can sometimes learn new skills almost immediately for no observable reason.

csg_chev.name: Chev
csg_chev.physiology: The Chevs are a near-human people who evolved from primates. They have pale skin and their hair, which is only atop their head, is blonde or white, similar to many humans. However, their hair is often dyed for identification purposes. They have two notable differences from humans, however. They have multiple hearts, which sometimes allows them to have a significantly longer lifespan. However, a majority of Chevs still live a fairly normal lifespan, around 75 years. The other distinction is that they lack eyelids.
csg_chev.society: The society of the Chevs is defined by their owners, the Chevin. On Vinsoth, slavery of the Chevs is widespread. Although the Chevin are their rulers, the Chevs give what little power they have to the oldest female, who oversees the other slaves and acts as the leader. The Chevs are a docile and submissive people, a result of evolution both genetically and culturally. As the Chevin are a nomadic people, the Chevs in bondage to them must also be nomadic. They fulfill a variety of roles, although many are especially good at technical work. Despite their oppression, the Chevs still have some freedoms. Most Chevin give them some free time and tolerate their cultural rituals. They also place high value in folklore and art. Some Chevin sell this art for profit, while others simply tolerate it as a way to keep the Chevs content. Legally, the Chevin can do whatever they wish to the Chevs they own, although harsher punishments are somewhat taboo.
csg_chev.language: Chevs all know their native language of Chev, and they also learn Chevin and Basic.
csg_chev.homeworld: The Chevs live with the Chevin on Vinsoth, a fairly flat Outer Rim world. Most of the Chevin live on the temperate plains. They are nomadic pastoralists, and the Chevs live in small villages for manufacturing or farming. There are seven dictators who rule on Vinsoth, each with their own continent.
csg_chev.description: Chevs are near-humans who are almost entirely enslaved by a much larger species called the Chevin. Their predicament is a more civilized one than that of other enslaved species, and harsher punishments are rare, but they are still ultimately in bondage.
csg_chev.sidebar_text: Like any species that is enslaved to a great extent, the Chevs look forward to the day when they can become free. This isn’t particularly likely, however, as only a handful of Chevin support emancipation- only because they believe the Chevin should learn to survive on their own, not over morality. A handful of Chevs do hold secret meetings in the night where they discuss possible rebellions. There are some escaped Chevs. These Chevs often fight for freedom as part of the Rebel Alliance, although others are more paranoid and seek to keep a low profile for fear of being recaptured. Almost all who escape use elaborate clothing or tattoos to separate themselves from their enslaved brethren. Eventually, in almost 50 years, the Chevs will be freed as part of the Freedom Flight movement.

csg_chevin.name: Chevin

special_abilities.name: Thick Hides
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Olfaxes
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks, add setback on tactile Perception checks.

csg_chevin.physiology: Chevin are big and tall creatures who can be up to three meters in height, and their thick, wrinkled gray-brown hide gives them a degree of protection from lighter blaster fire. This comes at the expense of sensitivity, so Chevin have a poor sense of touch. They make up for it with smell, as their massive snout features two giant nostrils which they use to sniff for smaller prey in the grasses. Disproportionate humanoids, their huge head makes up much of their mass, with their chin reaching knee level on their stubby legs. Protruding from their wide shoulders are arms long enough to touch the ground without bending down, and they have four-fingered hands. They have hair, typically blond or brown, on their chin and atop their head, and their eyes, composed of only dark pupils, have two lids to protect in sandstorms.
csg_chevin.society: For all of their cunning, Chevin are surprisingly honest. Their culture is obsessed with commerce, which relies on trust, so their moral code demands they fulfill their side of bargains to the letter. They expect the same from others and can be extremely vindictive to those who openly double-cross them. When not bound by the letter of the law, however, they are ruthless in business using whatever loopholes, coercion, or blackmail they can to acquire as many credits as possible. Their moral outlook is generally a grim “every man for himself,” which they find in themselves and expect from others. Chevin are ambitious, working well in leadership roles and possessing a knack for sniffing out potential in either people or markets. While they are willing to go just about anywhere to make a profit, they are especially good at navigating black markets and the underworld. Aside from their dictators, all Chevin are nomadic, and whole villages move on their homeworld as they search for the backshin, their primary prey. Their villages are built atop either wheeled or repulsorlift platforms known as lodges, which carry them and their goods every few weeks. This mentality continues when Chevin take to the stars, and they have eagerly traded with new worlds. Much of their technology is from offworld, and they only started wearing clothing after they were inspired by how other species flaunted their wealth via elaborate vestments.
csg_chevin.language: Most Chevin speak both Chevin and Basic fluently.
csg_chevin.homeworld: Chevin are native to Vinsoth, and their durable nature works well with its diverse climates, which include grassy plains, polar ice caps, and dry deserts. Vinsoth is an Outer Rim world in the northern part of the galaxy, and its seven continents are all ruled by their own dictator, who chooses a small panel of advisors.
csg_chevin.description: A selfish people who still practice slavery, the Chevin put business first. They are very large and tough, but most prefer to get what they want through commerce. While they may drive a hard bargain, they are still honest.
csg_chevin.sidebar_text: On Vinsoth, there are two native species: Chevin and Chevs. Long ago, the Chevin defeated the Chevs thanks to their size, toughness, and teamwork, and they’ve kept them as slaves ever since, even back in the days of the Old Republic, when slavery was illegal. Few Chevin see anything wrong with their arrangement, although there are extremist Chevin who disagree. However, most of them believe that abolition is only necessary because it would benefit the development of the Chevin by teaching hard work and independence while encouraging them to develop new technologies. Chevin who disagree with slavery on a moral basis often give up on persuading their fellows, and many leave Vinsoth to join the Rebellion.

csg_chironian.name: Chironian

special_abilities.name: Equine Athleticism
special_abilities.description: Move twice as quickly, and encumbrance threshold is equal to 10+Brawn.

special_abilities.name: Horns
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 2 advantage to hit with horns, adding the Pierce 2 quality.

csg_chironian.physiology: Chironians are centauriforms, possessing an equine lower body with four powerful legs with hooves and a humanoid upper body. They are large, as tall as a human adult even if they fold their legs underneath them in order to sit. They have a long tail behind them, and their skin Their upper body has arms and a head that are physiologically almost identical to a human, except they have horns. The horns fall off and regrow every year. They start off as knobs of furry velvet, which slowly grow until the horns pierce the velvet. The horns are shiny and smooth with ridges, and they can be used in combat. However, if the velvet is pierced artificially before the horns are long enough, the injury can actually be fatal. Chironians have red-brown hair, which they typically let grow down their back, and their skin is red-brown. Youth have orangish skin with white spots. They often do not wear clothing as youth, although adults typically wear clothing over their torso.
csg_chironian.society: Descending from herds of grazing herbivores, the Chironians are a communally-oriented people who are far less individualistic than many other cultures. Most live in small migratory herds of a couple dozen individuals, and the concept of families is almost entirely unknown to them. Children are raised by the entire community, and mates do not remain together. Chironians have few possessions of their own, and resources are shared by the entire herd.
csg_chironian.language: The Chironian’s native language of Re’ein uses a combination of gestures, including foot stomps and hand signals, to communicate, and it has no written form. As they modernized, Tartainians developed Relen’ein, a language that uses only sounds and can be written. Chironians who live a traditional lifestyle continue to learn only Re’ein, while Tartainians learn Basic and Relen’ein. When speaking Basic, they have a thick accent and a husky voice.
csg_chironian.homeworld: Chironians come from Chiron, a planet in the Ash Worlds covered by grasslands. The eastern part is more urbanized, including the capital city of Tartain, while the west is dominated by wilderness.
csg_chironian.description: An athletic species of equines, the Chironians are quadrupedal and have a fur-covered lower body, but their upper half is more humanoid. They also have sharp horns that they use in combat.
csg_chironian.sidebar_text: Chironians were discovered by the rest of the galaxy only 300 years ago, but they have been slow to adapt to modern technology. Most Chironians live in the wilderness, living in large tents and often moving their homes to match the seasons or find greener pastures. It is very rare for these Chironians to use any electronic technology or offworld goods. The only exception is Tartain, their only major city, which tried to embrace galactic culture when Chiron was discovered. Tartainians are increasing in number, but most Chironians view their modernity with suspicion.
csg_chironian._provenance_note: The Chironian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_chiss.name: Chiss

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for lighting conditions.

csg_chiss.physiology: Chiss are near-humans most notable for their blue skin and red eyes that lack pupils, which excel at seeing in low-light conditions. These features grow even more intense when in greater concentrations of oxygen. Their hair is jet black, but occasionally for females, and rarely for males, it can become silvery as they age. It is seen as a mark of distinction, and children of gray-haired parents are considered to be significant. Chiss reach maturity as young as thirteen, although this may be more cultural than genetic, and compared to humans, they tend to be physically well-built. According to genetic analysis, the two species are relatives, but the split is old enough that no records of these connections are known.
csg_chiss.society: Chiss are cautious, thoughtful, and highly cultured, with great advances in both artistic and scientific endeavors, particularly when it supports their military, the Chiss Expansionary Defense Force, which is beset on all sides by the Killiks, Ssi-ruuk, Vaagari, and even the Yuuzhan Vong. While they value this strength, it is strictly for defense and retaliation, as they tend to keep to themselves, and they have little outside contact. Even the rare Chiss that do somehow end up in the rest of the galaxy keep a careful respect for the rest of their species’s secrecy. The Chiss are so unknown that those who recognize them usually only know of them as the species of Thrawn, though the Imperial Grand Admiral is quiet about his origins. Like their most well-known member, most are not prone to emotion, planning their moves with diligence before taking action. They are excellent at predicting their opponents, and they view all outsiders with a deep-seated paranoia. While their culture values individual achievements in artistic and intellectual fields, they are not greedy and instead strive for contribution to their society, the Chiss Ascendancy. This government over their entire species is strictly authoritarian, and they have several ruling families, each with its own area of focus. The Nuruodo control their army and navy, Csapla their farms and colonies, Sabosen their schools and hospitals, and Inrokini their businesses and laboratories.
csg_chiss.language: Chiss are the only species that can speak the highly complex tongue of Cheunh. This language requires their unique vocal cords, and names are formed as three parts connected by apostrophes. To humans, they abbreviate them by only using a middle section.
csg_chiss.homeworld: Chiss hail from the Chiss Ascendancy, the organization that governs 28 colonies in the westernmost region of the galaxy. This region is cut off from the rest of the galaxy by a hyperspace tangle, making travel difficult. The Ascendancy has many worlds, but it originates from the icy planet Csilla. Covered in glaciers, the Chiss now live underground, with a large network of passages connecting the cities, the largest of which is Csaplar.
csg_chiss.description: Chiss are a very calculating people who focus on planning and analyzing ahead of time as much as they can. They are distant relatives to humans but are now distinguished by their blue skin and red eyes that have no pupils.
csg_chiss.sidebar_text: Chiss are taught to constantly plan for the future, to painstakingly analyze their situation, and to always be ready for any attack. So strong is their emphasis on defense and retaliation that preemptive strikes of any sort are forbidden, and to make one can result in exile, as was the case with Thrawn. Even among those who don’t command militaries, their adventures likely wait for the last moment to draw their blaster and won’t fight until first attacked. Force-sensitive Chiss, however rare, may see precognition as a dangerous temptation, as seeing an attack before it happens may prompt them to strike first.

csg_chistori.name: Chistori

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_chistori.physiology: The Chistori are saurian reptiles with skin that is blue or purple on the back and yellow or tan on the front. Their head points forward with a snout-like beak. They have a very wide mouth that features a handful of teeth sticking out. Their small, black eyes face off to the side. Although they are average in height, they are strong and athletic. As reptiles, they are cold-blooded and have scales, which afford them some level of protection. Their four-fingered hands also end in sharp claws.
csg_chistori.society: Chistori are an extremely violent people who are straightforward and impatient. They are also mean and bad-tempered, and they aren’t exceptionally moral. Because of their violent nature, they often become mercenaries or bounty hunters if they leave their world. However, such Chistori are relatively few in number, as a majority of them choose not to leave their homeworld.
csg_chistori.language: Chistori rarely speak Basic, as most of them only know their growling native tongue of Hrr’ost. The handful who do business with outsiders use a trade language, Bocce. Those of them who do speak Basic typically have a deep voice.
csg_chistori.homeworld: Chistori come from a rocky world in the Outer Rim called Isthu. It is a relatively rural planet completely outside of Imperial influences due to its relatively low population. They live in independent tribes which often go to war with each other. The Chistori tribes are largely nomadic and mostly survive through hunting, although a few have begun mining operations in recent years. Such tribes have traded the minerals, which has allowed them to build cities and have moderate levels of current technology. More traditional tribes look to these innovations with scrutiny, considering the modernized tribes to be traitors to their species.
csg_chistori.description: A very violent people, the Chistori are saurians known for their bad temper and straightforwardness. Their few Force-sensitives are persecuted out of fear, and most of them seen in the broader galaxy perform mercenary work of some sort.
csg_chistori.sidebar_text: Chistori have no knowledge of the Force as it is known to the Jedi or Sith, and they are far too undisciplined to know it as any other religion. Most of them fear the Force, so the few who are gifted with Force-sensitivity are feared and persecuted. Such persecution makes Force-sensitive Chistori eager to leave their world and seek new opportunities in the wider galaxy. One such example was Cydon Prax, a Force-sensitive who became a bounty hunter during the Clone Wars. Similarly, Desann will join Luke Skywalker’s Jedi Academy and later become a Dark Jedi.
csg_chistori._provenance_note: No knowledge exists regarding the homeworld or language of the Chistori. The remaining information is made up. Players are not obligated to follow this.

csg_clawdite.name: Clawdite

special_abilities.name: Changelings
special_abilities.description: As an action, may attempt to shape-shift by suffering 3 strain and making an average Resilience check. If successful, change appearance to match that of a previously observed humanoid silhouette 1 character. Any observers who would want to recognize the disguise must attempt a Perception check opposed by Deception. Boosts or setbacks can be added based on how much either have observed the individual, whether the clothing matches, or if imitating a species that is considerably different in physiology.

csg_clawdite.physiology: Clawdites are unique in that they can change almost all of their physical features at will in order to match the appearance of another. While they still have struggles with changing size or drastically altering physiology, such as impersonating a Dug’s physique. They enhance their abilities with special oils that improve their skin’s pliability, and some with training can even make their skin look like particular clothing or jewelry. Shape-shifting does require great concentration and put sufficient strain on them, so they revert back to their original form when asleep, badly wounded, or dead. This natural form has olive green or yellow skin, sunken cheeks, a small mouth, a narrow nose, and cream-colored eyes with slit pupils. As reptiles, they reproduce via eggs. Their young can simply change hues to communicate their needs, but schools help them tune their shapeshifting powers. It is noted that one particularly skilled Clawdite, Zam Wesell, was able to even manipulate her size, seemingly via removing or adding water, but her feats have not been known to be replicated.
csg_clawdite.society: Clawdites are quiet and solitary, and they aren’t particularly social. They are slow to trust anyone and harshly pessimistic. While they can work together when it benefits them, they aren’t natural team players, and loyalty is a foreign concept to them. Some do find purpose in military service, and they are often sympathetic to the plights of oppressed species.
csg_clawdite.language: Clawdites speak Clawdite, a modified version of Zolanese.
csg_clawdite.homeworld: Clawdites come from Zolan, a Mid Rim world. It was in great turmoil during the Clone Wars, since the Clawdites were eager to join the Confederacy, who promised them equality and liberation from the Zolanders. Imperial rule has allowed for continued subjugation of the Clawdites.
csg_clawdite.description: Shapeshifting is a powerful ability that defines the Clawdites. However, it also works to their detriment, as on their homeworld, the religious Zolanders find it to be heresy. However, their ability to disguise themselves as almost anyone is also extremely useful.
csg_clawdite.sidebar_text: While many have inevitably been jealous of the Clawdites, their lives are not as glamorous as one would think. The Zolanders who share the Clawdite homeworld have the same appearance as Clawdites in their natural form, and they are the ancestors of the Clawdites. The Zolanders are deeply religious, and they shun their offshoot species, whom they consider unholy and impure. The Zolanders have forced the Clawdites to live in secured ghettos so that they cannot spread. However, some have been able to enter into the ancient and highly prestigious Zolander warrior tradition, called the Mabari. Since the Zolanders fear the Clawdites, few let them access this elite warrior training. Those who do enter face harsh standards and are watched closely. Failure means permanent exile from Zolan, so this sets up many Clawdites to be bounty hunters in the wider galaxy.

csg_codru_ji.name: Codru-Ji

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_codru_ji.physiology: The Codru-Ji are six-limbed mammals who undergo metamorphosis to become adults. As children, they appear as six-legged canines called wyrwulves, in which they resemble animals more than sentients. wyrwulves cannot speak, although are smart enough to protect their parents and bond emotionally. They are covered in fur and have a tail, a snout, and pointed ears. However, once they reach puberty, the Wyrwulves encase themself in a cocoon, and they eventually emerge as a humanoid adult. They still somewhat resemble their animal-like forms with thick, tannish skin, claws, and pointed ears. Both can also hear very high frequencies undetectable to many other species. They have six limbs, four of which act like arms. Unlike most other species, they sleep standing up. They are excellent survivalists who are typically in good physical condition and able to survive for days without food or water.
csg_codru_ji.society: Codru-Ji are somewhat xenophobic, as their customs are typically seen as barbaric by outsiders. They are also concerned about external influences on their culture. This has kept their society very isolated. They typically maintain a relationship with wyrwulves similar to that of a human with a pet, and most wyrwulves will loyally protect their parents or caretakers. They do not receive a complete name until adulthood and only have nicknames as wyrwulves.
csg_codru_ji.language: The Codru-Ji speak Codruese, a language composed of barks, growls, and snarls. Although it is seemingly well-suited for young wyrwulves, it can only be spoken by the humanoid adults. Because of their isolation, a majority of Codru-Ji chose not to learn Basic.
csg_codru_ji.homeworld: The Codru-Ji homeworld, Munto Codru, lies on the edge of the galaxy at the northeast tip of the Slice. It is a mountainous planet with a temperate climate. It is extremely isolated and exports very little. Its capital, Capital Codru, has the planet’s primary spaceport.
csg_codru_ji.description: Codru-Ji have six limbs, and most live a relatively low-tech lifestyle. They are known for their strange custom of harmless kidnappings in politics and are seen as barbaric by many. Although the adults resemble humans, young Codru-Ji are very canine and barely sentient.
