csg_dug.physiology: Dugs are small mammals, averaging about a meter in height. Despite their small size, however, they have a well-muscled and athletic body. The most interesting feature of Dug physiology is the fact that they use their legs for grasping, carrying, and fine manipulation while walking on their arms. They are swift runners, climbers, and swimmers, and some prefer to move on all fours. Their legs (which they use as arms) have two knees each, allowing them greater dexterity. They have smooth and very loose-hanging skin that comes in shades of brown, gray, or purple. Dug males have a flap of skin over their neck, which they inflate during their mating rituals. Their face is unique as well: They have pointed ears with long earlobes and a snout with a piglike nose and a mouth that always seems to snarl. Dug eyes, somewhat on the side of their snout, are yellow or blue.
csg_dug.society: Dugs are aggressive creatures who like to establish dominance with their bullying ways. Naturals with insults, they are experts at angering others. They even will constantly berate their mates, though they are still deeply loyal in their marriages. Dugs value heritage, which they commemorate via beads on their ear fins, and they will fight to defend the honor of their family members. They are undisciplined and easily angered, and some psychologists see them as an insecure species. They hold grudges for generations, particularly toward the Gran, who conquered their homeworld and made the Dugs into little more than a slave species. They are paid minimal wages and treated as second class citizens thanks to the power that the Gran hold in politics. The Dugs have had to disband their military and been stripped of their weapons ever since, though some continue to make their own arms, such as the scooped, bladed b’hedda. Dug clans are ruled by a lone monarch, who is selected via ritual combat, and the monarch is usually the only being that they won’t ever insult. Their tribes still live in primitive villages in the treetops of their homeworld, which they call “tree thorps.” These towering constructions are difficult to climb for other species, not that the Dugs have interest in hosting them anyway. Experiences with the Gran have left them xenophobic, and they are rarely seen offworld. Those that do leave Malastare tend to be criminals, and they like to stay in groups with other Dugs.
csg_dug.language: Dugs speak Dug, a language that is mostly suppressed by the Gran, who prefer them to learn Gran on Malastare. Many Dugs choose not to learn Basic, so as to force the use of their own language, those who do speak Basic tend to have a deep voice.
csg_dug.homeworld: Dugs come from Malastare, a high gravity world in the southern part of the Mid Rim that is rich in fuel. The diverse terrain of forest, desert, and methane lakes make it ideal as a hub for Podracing. The Dugs have been forced to the continent on western part of the world by their Gran oppressors.
csg_dug.description: Dugs are small mammals that walk with their arms and use their feet for manipulation. They make natural bullies, and they constantly insult others. They have been treated as second-class citizens by their Gran conquerors.
csg_dug.sidebar_text: Under the oppression of the Gran, Dugs have few opportunities for fame or success. However, their innate coordination and piloting skill allows them one opportunity: Podracing. The sport is incredibly dangerous, but the Dugs like risk and, with little to lose, many choose to do it anyway. Malastare has become a hub for Podracing, allowing some lucky Dugs enough credits to get offworld, where they can compete on locations without the bigotry.

csg_duinuogwuin.name: Duinuogwuin

special_abilities.name: Cold Fusion
special_abilities.description: Once per week, may exhale superheated gases using Ranged-Light, dealing 20 damage at the planetary scale with short range and have Crit rating of 2. Have Blast 10 and Breach 6.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain.

special_abilities.name: Space-Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Do not take wound or strain damage due to vacuum, unbreathable atmosphere, or abnormal air pressure. When in space for long periods of time, make an easy Resilience check. For every success, may spend 1 month in space without penalty. After this span, suffer 1 wound per day.

csg_duinuogwuin.physiology: According to all known laws of aviation, there is no way that a Duinuogwuin should be able to fly. Its wings are too delicate to get its fat body off the ground. The Duinuogwuin, of course, flies anyways. Because Duinuogwuin don't care what humans think is impossible. Duinuogwuin can even fly through space, an environment that they are capable of surviving for equally mysterious reasons. Because they can survive in a vacuum, it is theorized that they are able to recycle everything in their body, surviving for months without needing to consume anything, They are also extremely long-lived, often living for at least six millenia. However, none of their abilities is as awe-inspiring as what is apparently some form of cold fusion, allowing them to exhale superheated gases in an awe-inspiring attack. Duinuogwuin have a snake-like body covered in small gray scales, and they are almost always at least ten meters in length. Their body is divided into segments, each with a pair of legs, and each leg ends in a foot with two clawed toes. Their last segment is their chest, head and neck, which they hold upright. Their head features floppy ears, sparkling eyes on the side, and a long snout with teeth sticking out. Duinuogwuin are theorized to be the distant ancestors of species such as Kadri’Ra and Krayt dragons. They have no distinct genders, but they are known to create haploid gametes and reproduce sexually. How their offspring are gestated is yet another mystery.
csg_duinuogwuin.society: Also known as Star Dragons, the Duinuogwuin are a wise people known to be philosophical and pensive. They are decisive, but not rash, and they are also extremely patient and detached. They are preoccupied with their thoughts and almost always ignore questions about their species or history. They also stay far from their own, never living in the same sector as another Duinuogwuin out of respect for one another’s territory. Some Duinuogwuin live in total isolation, but many interact with the rest of the galaxy. Despite their superior power and wisdom, they view other species as equals, and they often run organizations from behind the scenes, using their wisdom to guide others. Although it is almost impossible to find them, they will make themselves known when they are needed. At birth, most Duinuogwuin are savage monsters who are barely sentient, but such members of the species are killed immediately by their parents to protect the galaxy, and only those who are wise live on.
csg_duinuogwuin.language: Duinuogwuin speak a language of the same name that uses hisses and growls which cannot be reproduced by other species.
csg_duinuogwuin.homeworld: Duinuogwuin come from Xuaquarres, an Outer Rim planet in the Ash Worlds which is carefully hidden away from almost everyone. It is also home to one of Emperor Palpatine’s storehouses.
csg_duinuogwuin.description: A secretive and reclusive species that can survive in space, the Duinuogwuins boast mythical powers and are almost impossible to find. However, they will appear to intervene in galactic events when they are needed most.
csg_duinuogwuin.sidebar_text: As is fitting for their mystery, Duinuogwuin almost never die in public, and they have never once been successfully captured. Traditionally, a Duinuogwuin will return to their homeworld when it is time for them to die, a place they call the Graveyard of the Dragons.

csg_duros.name: Duros

special_abilities.name: Intuitive Navigation
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Galaxy Mapper.”

csg_duros.physiology: Duros are hairless humanoids with blue-gray or green skin. They have pupiless red eyes and lack a nose. They are somewhat thin in comparison to humans but make up for it with knowledge. Duros were one of the first (if not the first) to develop the hyperdrive, and they are naturals when it comes to navigation. They are similar to humans in height, but some are taller. Their head has sunken cheeks, a wide cranium, and is generally somewhat wrinkled. These wrinkles are horizontal at eyebrow level, though they lack hair for eyebrows, vertical surrounding where their nose would be, and dropping down to the edges of their lipless mouth. They still have a sense of smell, and the olfactory organs are directly underneath their eyes. Descending from reptiles, they lay eggs and are born in a larval grub stage.
csg_duros.society: Duros tend to be adventurous and gregarious but not typically violent, reckless, or thrill-seeking. They are also noted for their good memories and love for telling stories about their many travels, as they are often very outgoing. It is tradition for them to refer to one another as “traveller,” regardless of occupation, as journeys are hihgly important to them. One of their greatest heroes is Felanil De Brek, supposedly the inventor of the hyperdrive and the first interstellar starship captain, who went from Duro to New Plympto millennia ago. De Brek's journey is celebrated annually around the day of his birth, a nine-day holiday they call Berikos, which is traditionally spent going on a vacation with their family. Family is important to the Duros, who always care for their young and give them special attention, educating them in the home alongside extended family as a way of separating themselves from the Neimoidians. Economically, many Duros work as navigators, explorers, or pilots, while others stay in the Duro system and use their intellect to work in the many industries. The Duros’ starship industry is one of the most prominent businesses in their society and is entirely operated by its many shareholders. Duros also have important traditions around borrowing money, and failure to follow them can create a severe social stigma.
csg_duros.language: The Duros language of Durese is common as a lingua franca amongst spacers due to the prominence of Duros, and it is an influence in Basic. Since the Duros are so eager to travel, they generally learn Basic.
csg_duros.homeworld: Duros come from the highly polluted Core World that is Duro. They live in orbital cities, as the environment varies from barren to overgrown, although there are still some droid-operated facilities on the planet’s surface. The twenty orbital cities support most of the housing and industrial needs, in addition to the orbiting shipyards. The environment will actually be improved during the Yuuzhan Vong War.
csg_duros.description: Reptiles with blue or green skin who often travel the spacelanes, the Duros have left their homeworld because of industrial pollution. Though some stay nearby in orbital cities, many have left their home entirely. They value travelling so much that they often refer to one another with the title "traveler."
csg_duros.sidebar_text: Duros are relatives to the Neimoidians, who are a Duros offshoot that colonized Neimoidia. The relationship between the two species is somewhat strained, as many Duros look down on their cowardly relatives. It is a bad insult to mistake a Duros for a Neimoidian. While Neimoidians once showed great patriotism and desire to outdo their relatives, many Neimoidians now pretend to be Duros thanks to their humiliation in the Clone Wars. Most Duros metaphorically thumb their nose at any idea of blending the species, but by the time of the New Republic, a few will start to work with the Neimoidians and give them respect for their business skills.

csg_duuranh.name: Duu’ranh
csg_duuranh.physiology: The Duu’ranh are humanoids who are on the larger side, usually boasting a height over two meters. They have light blue skin, occasionally verging on lavender. Their forehead is short and sloped, and their cranium is bald, but their males do have two beards of blue hair going down from each of their ears. Their beards lighten and grow with age, and eventually, each of the two halves grow all the way to the center of their chin, merging into a single beard. Likewise, their ears grow with age, making them somewhat unique in that it is actually their elders who have the best hearing. It is believed that this adaptation exists so that older Duu’ranh can transition to ambush predators as their mobility is reduced, hiding beneath rocks until they hear small prey pass by. All ages of Duu’ranh have bright white eyes that are usually without visible pupils, and they have a prominent bony ridge for their brow, which wraps all the way up and around the back of their head. While they lack a nose, they have two nostrils directly under their eyes, and long wrinkles trace the path from the nostrils to their mouth.
csg_duuranh.society: The Duu’ranh have one of the more authoritarian societies, with a far-reaching government that has little value for individual freedoms. Crime and violence are kept at a minimum by a strict and powerful police force, and everything from a Duu’ranh’s career path to their mating and childbearing is selected by tests that are administered by their dizzying bureaucracy. Their homes are assigned based on job, and their children are quickly separated from their parents to be raised at public boarding schools called eurr’kat. Changes of power in their government follow a convoluted system where each department has authority to make appointments within another in a circular system of checks. They are ruled by a Diktat, who is selected by the managers of the various government departments. While the few members of other species to visit Or’ranh generally find their policies to be overbearing, most of the Duu’ranh themselves are happy with the system, as they notoriously struggle with self-guided ventures. In the wider galaxy, the lack of supervision often makes them lazy and aimless, and they can grow more violent if they have too much time on their hands. Those away from Or’ranh are often found in military or law enforcement professions.
csg_duuranh.language: Duu’ranh speak Akuthst but are usually educated in Basic, depending on the career planned for them.
csg_duuranh.homeworld: The Duu’ranh come from the Mid Rim planet of Or’ranh, which is not far from the Corellian Run, where they tend to cluster in dense cities with vast tracts of wilderness or farmland between them.
csg_duuranh.description: The Duu’ranh are a species of humanoids with light blue skin that are highly authoritarian in their society. Their Force tradition, the Ahj Olana, has strong ties to the Jedi Order historically.
csg_duuranh.sidebar_text: The Duu’ranh have a somewhat high rate of Force-sensitivity, and prior to the rise of the Empire, their members with high midi-chlorian counts were quickly sent into the Ahj Olana, a military order centered around practical usage of the Force. While they only numbered about a dozen at a time, they still had a prominent role in enforcing order among the Duu’ranh. Because the youth of the Ahj Olana were separated from their parents anyway, the Jedi Order signed an ancient treaty that made them historically lenient on allowing Ahj Olana to transfer back and forth from their Order. The handful who became full-fledged Jedi, such as Jastus Farr, often still spent significant amounts of time training and serving on their homeworld, and they favored the saberstaff due to its similarities with the electrostaffs of the Ahj Olana. The Empire targeted the Ahj Olana in the Jedi Purge, but most of them dispersed before they could be killed. The Inquisitorius has since attempted to restart the Ahj Olana under new dark side teachings.
csg_duuranh._provenance_note: Little is known about the Duu’ranh. This entire page is highly speculative and retcons Jastus Farr, the Jedi Brutes in the Revenge of the Sith game, and the unidentified native race in A Stranger in Town to be members. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they rewrite stats, imagining their own aspects of Duu’ranh physiology and culture.

csg_ebranite.name: Ebranite

special_abilities.name: Troglodytes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Six Arms
special_abilities.description: May have three times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Climbing Claws
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on checks to climb.

special_abilities.name: Rage
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl or Melee, deal +1 damage when wounded, or +2 damage when critically injured.

csg_ebranite.physiology: Troglodytes with brown or gray skin who are slightly shorter than humans on average, the Ebranites are skilled climbers because of their claws and prehensile toes. They have no visible hair, nose, or ears, and their dark eyes lack pupils. They have infrared vision and see well in the dark. They have six arms, each of which ends in a six-fingered, clawed hand. Despite their size, they are surprisingly tough and have a thick hide.
csg_ebranite.society: The Ebranites are a very determined people who are slow to trust outsiders and very easily angered. They are a primitive people, and they distrust technology because they associate it with the Empire. Although they were mostly ignored during the days of the Old Republic, they had offworld contact with Carosite traders. Recently, the Empire has taken a more active role in governing their planet. Those suspected of anti-Imperial sentiment are sent to lu-ramin mines in the Grythsorin canyons. However, the Ebranites have fought back very successfully, demonstrating surprising resourcefulness and ferocity. Although some have joined the Rebel Alliance, a majority choose to stay on their homeworld.
csg_ebranite.language: Ebranese is a spoken language of honks and grunts. The Ebranites do not have writing and use simple pictographs to draw past events.
csg_ebranite.homeworld: Ebranites hail from the Mid Rim planet of Ebra, which is in the Dousc system. It is covered in caves, canyons, and mountains, terrain in which they excel.
csg_ebranite.description: Eight-limbed cave dwellers, the Ebranites are primitive and slow to trust outsiders, but they are very loyal to their family and their clan, the latter of which is called a thilda. They rarely use technology, which they associate with Imperial oppressors.
csg_ebranite.sidebar_text: Ebranites are extremely loyal to their nuclear families. In their families, children get very little freedom, and although males take a leadership role, the mothers are more highly respected. 20 to 30 of these families will unite to form a “thilda,” in which they work together to protect each other. Although family loyalty is always the most important, Ebranites are also very loyal to their thildas, and they tattoo their thilda’s logo on their uppermost left arm. To betray or completely cut ties with one’s thilda is unheard of. Thildas are led by a council called the “ghantar.” Wars between thildas are relatively rare.

csg_echani.name: Echani

special_abilities.name: Quick Blows
special_abilities.description: Though damage is still dependent on Brawn rating, may use Agility with Brawl and Melee instead of Brawn. This cannot apply when using Melee weapons with 4 or more encumbrance, which still use Brawn. It is chosen at character creation, and can only be changed afterwards through significant training.

csg_echani.physiology: Echani are near-humans with lighter skin, silver hair, and silver eyes, while their Thyrsian subspecies has dark skin and hair. Aside from the Thyrsians, Echani are generally lighter in build, but also quick. This is more a result of cultural differences than genetic ones, but it is still prominent in almost all Echani. They are not very diverse in appearance, and all of them look very similar, especially to outsiders. Some theorize that Echani are the result of genetically modified humans, and there is some evidence to suggest that Arkanians, infamous as biologists, (also, ironically, silver-haired near-humans) are responsible.
csg_echani.society: Echani society focuses strongly on hand-to-hand combat but is surprisingly similar to that of many modern humans. It lacks the more brutal focus of other combat-respecting cultures and believes that martial arts are a skill to be respected. Though they might have disagreements, many Echani find that they respect each other more after a fight. Traditional Echani weapons and armor are light, to account for their lack of physical strength. Some prefer to not wear armor at all, as it can restrict their movement, and they are not inclined towards blasters culturally. This contrasts with their rivals, the Mandalorians, who use heavy armor, lots of gear, and plenty of blasters. Echani society is somewhat female dominated. Their cousins, the Thyrsians, are their opposite in many ways. They are a Force cult worshiping the “Son of Suns,” and some have turned to Sith ways. They also prefer heavier weapons and equipment.
csg_echani.language: The Echani have no unique language.
csg_echani.homeworld: Echani hail from the world of Eshan in the Inner Rim. Thyrsians are from Thyrsus, which is nearby.
csg_echani.description: Combat is not just a way of life for the near-human Echani. For them, it is also a way of communication. They value speed, so they rarely use armor or heavy weapons.
csg_echani.sidebar_text: Echani are adept at using combat as communication. Not only is martial arts important as a sport or hobby, it is also a universal way to understand someone. Even Echani generals can see into the emotions of their rival leader through a battle. Hand-to-hand combat is seen as expression and art. Since they look so similar, combat is even vital towards identification in their culture.

csg_eklaad.name: Eklaad

special_abilities.name: Thick Armor
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Defensive Ball
special_abilities.description: As a maneuver, may curl into a ball, reducing crit damage by 30.

special_abilities.name: Quadrupedal Structure
special_abilities.description: When carrying large objects or people on back, reduce their encumbrance by 3 to a minimum of 4. May carry small objects using prehensile trunk, but may not wield weapons that require 2 hands.

csg_eklaad.physiology: The Eklaad are a species of large, primitive herbivores adapted to a high-gravity environment. They are quadrupedal, but they can grasp objects using their prehensile trunk, which has three finger-like appendages at its end. Their back, face, and all of their limbs are covered by a multitude of plates that act as a heavy natural armor, protecting them when they are threatened. The Eklaad can become even more unkillable if they roll up into a defensive ball to ensure maximum coverage by their plates, which is their most common response when they are threatened or scared. They are shorter than humans, but they are significantly wider due to their hunched-over posture. Eklaad have no visible hair, and their face is distinguished by an eye on either side of their trunk and a small mouth below it. All four of their feet end in three hoof-like toes. Eklaad have eyes on the sides of their head, but their vision is below-average, and they rely more on tanking damage than on quickly responding to threats.
csg_eklaad.society: The Eklaad are not a particularly forceful or assertive people, and they are known for their relative timidity. When faced with danger or anything they dislike, their preferred response is to ignore it, curling into a ball until predators give up and go away. Should they be faced with a more serious danger, Eklaad prefer to flee. They will only fight if they’re backed into a corner and know that their armor won’t be sufficient to protect them. However, in these cases, the mighty Eklaad are surprisingly fierce, and they do not go down easily. In general, Eklaad tribes, ruled by hereditary chieftains, survive by foraging nomadically. Their population is now just a million and a half, and their technology is only at a stone age level, including bows and spears.
csg_eklaad.language: A few Eklaad have learned Basic by lurking around the Imperial training camps on their homeworld. The rest speak in a language of whistles and piping sounds.
csg_eklaad.homeworld: The Eklaad come from a harsh planet in the Arkanis Sector of the Outer Rim known as Sirpar, which has very little by way of natural resources or fertile soil. The vegetation is inedible to most other species, and the 25% stronger gravity poses a significant discomfort for offworlders. The climate is generally hot and dry, while the terrain is fairly diverse, with mountains, seas, lowland jungles, and high-altitude deserts atop the plateaus. The Empire has thousands of troops in training scattered across a dozen primary camps and a dozen more camps intended to train in specific environments.
csg_eklaad.description: Four-legged herbivores with a nimble trunk, the Eklaad live as primitive nomads on high-gravity Sirpar. They have been harmed by the Galactic Empire setting up stormtrooper training facilities on their world, but they are too pacifistic to fight back and are more inclined to run away or curl into a defensive ball.
csg_eklaad.sidebar_text: The Eklaad lived in isolation up until recently, when the Galactic Empire constructed training camps on their world. The Empire sees the Eklaad as largely irrelevant, as their pacificistic nature prevents them from forming any threat. However, Eklaad population has dwindled as a result of Imperial settlement, and their traditional Council of Chieftains has been suspended due to the dangers posed by Imperials. Many once-proud tribes are now reduced to foraging for scraps of waste around the Imperial camps. Due to the circumstances, they regard all offworlders with a very deep suspicion.

csg_elom.name: Elom

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Digging Claws
special_abilities.description: Spend 2 maneuvers to tunnel through loose soil, moving 1 range band.

csg_elom.physiology: Eloms are bulky humanoids who are completely herbivorous and covered in gray or brown fur. Not unlike Whiphids, their face is the only part of their body not covered in fur. This face is a wrinkled mess of high nostrils, black eyes that see well in the dark, and small twin tusks. They have no neck. Their claws may be sharp, but they are designed for digging, not combat. Each hand has three, including an opposable thumb. They also have three toes, one of which points backwards. It is not uncommon or surprising to see an Elom without clothing, although some do choose to wear it. While some Eloms have a tail, not all of them do.
csg_elom.society: Despite their brutish appearance, Eloms are peaceful creatures. They are simple and, to some, unsophisticated. Most are content to live a simple life, earning a primitive living and raising a family. They are social creatures with a strong desire for belonging. Unfortunately, many fall into the wrong crowds. Their naive nature makes them easily manipulated, so many end up working as criminals or enforcers if they leave their homeworld. They almost never hold grudges and tend to see the best in people. Not only are they forgiving, but they rarely expect misdeeds from others. While some work against the Empire, they continue to offer forgiveness. Eloms live in underground cities that are called cseria. These are generally small towns. Each cseria has a yearly meeting, where members resolve disputes and trade goods.
csg_elom.language: Eloms speak Elom. This language requires the unique structure of the Elom mouth, so they find it difficult to speak Basic.
csg_elom.homeworld: Eloms come from the chilly deserts of Elom, which is an Outer Rim world. They share it with the Elomin, descendants of Zabrak colonists. The mines are a source of Lommite. Most of civilization is in the A’driannamieq Mountains.
csg_elom.description: Simple creatures who mostly live in caves, the Elom are large, furry, and well-suited for digging. Imperial oppression has caused some to unite with the Elomin, going against millenia of separation. They are a very peaceful people.
csg_elom.sidebar_text: The Eloms share their world with the mathematically minded Elomin. These people once considered the Eloms to be non-sentient and held them as slaves. While few Eloms bear a grudge, some Elomin do find it unsettling that they are not the sole owners of their world. The two species kept a peaceful separation, split apart by cultural differences. Now, that has somewhat changed. Elomin are now slaves to the Empire, working in mines near Elom caves. Many Eloms have chosen to stand up to the Empire, sneaking themselves and others (both Elom and Elomin) into deeper, unexplored caves. Most Elomin now respond with gratitude. The actions of the Empire make some choose to leave Elom entirely and join the Rebel Alliance.

csg_elomin.name: Elomin
csg_elomin.physiology: Elomin have skin that is orange, red, or rusty brown and horns atop their head. A long lost offshoot of the Zabraks, they have four horns on top of their head and two more on the cheeks. Their physiology also includes neck wattles, spanchons, four stomachs, generative nodes, a six-chambered heart, and long hairs which grow behind their ears. They have somewhat long ears, their eyes are black, red, orange, or yellow, and they have no nose, only nostrils. They are somewhat smaller than humans, averaging five thirds of a meter tall.
csg_elomin.society: Elomin are obsessed with order and patterns. They seek to find patterns even where none exist and are compulsive when it comes to organization. One odd result of this is that they are unable to cope with a Marg Sabl maneuver, as demonstrated by Grand Admiral Thrawn in a skirmish over Obroa-skai. They are also extremely hygienic, polishing their horns and combing ear hair. They are also excellent at math. As one Elomin said, “Physical calculus is the foundation of logical analysis, and logical analysis is the foundation of Elom civilization.” They consider the logical, predictable, and completely accurate field that is mathematics to be very important. Under Imperial rule, the Elomin are mostly slaves in mines.
csg_elomin.language: Elomin can speak Basic without difficulty. They have their own language as well, Elomin.
csg_elomin.homeworld: The world of Elom is a cold and barren desert. It has long had struggles with a lack of water, but it has been able to trade away minerals from the mines in exchange for water.
csg_elomin.description: Distant relatives to the Zabraks who have reddish skin, the Elomin are obsessive when it comes to logic, hygene, and pattern-finding. They have now become Imperial slaves, but some find freedom with help from their furry Elom neighbors, a species that they were typically very separate from.
csg_elomin.sidebar_text: The Elomin live on the surface of their planet, initially unaware of the Eloms. These bulky creatures live underground, and they have had a strained relationship with the Elomin. While the Elomin were at one point Zabrak colonists, the Eloms have lived on Elom for all of recorded history. Even when the Eloms were discovered, the Elomin explorers never told the other Elomin. They found it difficult to accept that they weren’t the sole owners of the planet. While the Eloms planned for a peaceful yet isolated coexistence, the Elomin considered them non-sentient. A Republic study found the Eloms to be sentient and gave them rights to territory. The two species remained mostly isolated because of differences in lifestyle, but recent circumstances have caused some of the more moral Eloms to do battle with the Empire, freeing Elomin from the mines.

csg_emliy.name: Em’liy
csg_emliy.physiology: Em’liy are tall and muscular humanoids whose mottled skin can range in color from tan to yellow to blue. They have no body hair, but they have dark hair on top of their head which they braid into topknots. Their face is noseless and features fin-like protrusions to the sides of their small, yellow eyes. Their nostrils and ears are covered in permeable membranes to protect them from wind and sandstorms.
csg_emliy.society: Em’liy are survivors: a hardworking people who have an “every man for himself” mentality. They take nothing for granted, expect selfishness from others, and detest those who are lazy or dependent. They work hard to survive and built themselves a successful society. However, Imperial forces drove them from their cities years ago, and the Em’liy were disgraced. Considering themselves unworthy of the name they once held, they now call themselves the “Nomads,” and they became even hardier and more tenacious than before. Although they have begun to rebuild, many still feel lost and restless. Although they have lost their arrogance, they are still very hard to impress. However, once they are impressed, they are extremely loyal and will can even befriend former enemies. The Em’liy are also highly skilled warriors. In battle, they give themselves over to ferocity, handing control to their instincts in what they call the Spirit of Battle. They detest the Empire, but they have also been told lies which has many of them distrust all humans. However, nomadic Em’liy who have more experience with other species often learn that their prejudices were incorrect.
csg_emliy.language: Most Em’liy are bilingual, knowing their native language of Em’liy and Basic.
csg_emliy.homeworld: Em’liy come from Shalyvane, a desert planet in the Outer Rim. For many years, the Em’liy were nomadic or survived in Shalyvane’s wilderness, but now, some of them have begun to rebuild their capital city of Chinshassa.
csg_emliy.description: Em'liy are a hardy people with a devotion to their faith and their warrior ways. They were humiliated by the Empire, who drove them from their cities in a devastating invasion, and they have since been forced to live as nomads in their world's wilderness.
csg_emliy.sidebar_text: Em’liy are a religious people who worship a number of gods. Four of these gods, Argwin, Damilini, Criclamon, and Dojufi, are also names of their castes. Members of these four castes are distinguished by their amount of topknots, which ranges from one to three depending on caste. Each caste is led by its eldest member. Recently, the Damilini have been disliked, since they were the caste responsible for guarding a sacred place called the “Circle of Kavaan” when the Empire bombarded it.

csg_enso.name: Enso

special_abilities.name: Cold Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for cold conditions, add setback for heat at room temperature. At temperatures 5 degrees above this, add additional setback and must pass an easy Resilience check or suffer 1 strain per minute. Increase difficulty, setbacks, and strain penalty by 1 per 5 degrees. May negate penalties with a coolth suit, which has soak 1 and costs 600 credits.

csg_enso.physiology: Ensos are near-humans in terms of appearance, but they differ greatly in terms of temperature tolerance: They are so resistant to cold that they are comfortable below freezing but can easily overheat on warmer planets. As a result, they are often seen wearing air conditioned coolth suits when travelling the galaxy.
csg_enso.society: For anyone interested in the field of hydroponic farming, the Ensos are an unforgettable people responsible for many of the field's most important achievements. The majority of Ensos found in the wider galaxy do work related to hydroponics, but few choose to leave their homeworld at all. They are mild-mannered and cheerful, but they have little respect for privacy or personal space. They live in tightly-knit communities with large shared living spaces, and they are notoriously terrible at keeping secrets. They expect to make conversation with anyone they meet, and they discuss deeply personal issues as casually and cheerfully as they would the weather. They are direct in conflict as well, eager to confront but also quick to forgive. They are generous often to the point of naïveté, for swindlers among them have no place to hide. Enso criminals are very rare and usually end up being banished.
csg_enso.language: Linguists conclude that the Enso language, Sipeets, is a relative of Basic, as it has cognates with certain sounds shifted. Ensos need not learn Basic from scratch, they simply learn the patterns to reverse the sound changes. Unfortunately, some words have also shifted in meaning: For example, “hope” is only used to describe wishes that are impossible to fulfill.
csg_enso.homeworld: The Core World of Ensolica is a harsh planet, consistently frozen except for the most equatorial regions, which are coniferous forests with poor soil quality. As such, the Ensos built underground, digging into the glaciers and creating a society fueled by geothermal energy. Because of the difficulties creating cities this way, the architecture is notoriously compact.
csg_enso.description: Ensos are near-humans adapted to very frigid environments, so much so that many wear refrigerated coolth suits when visiting other worlds. Living in cramped cities, they have little respect for privacy and are known for their expertise in hydroponic farming.
csg_enso.sidebar_text: The Ensos’ near-human appearance is not merely superficial; genetic analysis points to them being relatives of humans with certain strands of alien DNA inserted. Where this DNA comes from is a mystery that none have been able to figure out, but it is clear that someone tampered with their genetics in the past. Archeological evidence indicates that Enso civilization is at least 9,000 years old, and a variety of mad scientists from just before then have been proposed to be the “creators” of the Ensos who altered their genes and abandoned them on Ensolica. The most infamous of these is Davin bon-Korich, an Arkanian criminal geneticist born in 11,578 BBY who killed thousands in his bizarre experiments. He at one point journaled that he wanted to create a new species and abandon them on an uninhabited planet, but there is no evidence that he was able to successfully do so. Nonetheless, about a tenth of Ensos worship him as their creator.
csg_enso._provenance_note: The Enso species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_equat.name: Equat

special_abilities.name: Poetic
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Respected Scholar.”

csg_equat.physiology: Equat are a mammalian species covered by fur in shades of tan, gray, or golden, except for their face, beard, and stomach, which have white fur instead. They have wide blue eyes without pupils, and the top of their head ends in their longest fur, which droops down to their back if unattempted to, but they usually weave it into an elaborate rigid headdress which widens into a fan at the back. Flanking the hairpiece is a pair of narrow pointed ears. Equat also have a long tail, which widens slightly at its end. Males and females are indistinguishable visually, and Equat do not usually wear clothing, although they are often adorned with various jewelry in addition to their hairpiece, such as earrings or a ribbon around the tail.
csg_equat.society: Equat are an artistically inclined race best known for their poems and writings, and they excel in academic fields such as linguistics, history, and xenology. They have a natural way with words that makes them highly coveted orators, and they’re at their best when the lights are brightest. Such high-minded academic gifts don’t always translate in every setting though, and they can display notable aloofness in situations that demand street smarts. They are careful planners more comfortable with rehearsed speeches than improvisation, so despite their overall charms, they don’t always make friends quickly.
csg_equat.language: Equat speak a variety of complex languages. While they can speak and write in Basic or Huttese, they find these languages to be insufficiently colorful.
csg_equat.homeworld: Equat are a fairly common sight as servants on a variety of Hutt worlds, but they originally come from the foggy jungles of Nirellia, where some still live in treetop villages. Located west of Hutt Space, Nirellia is fairly backwater, and free Equat often prefer to head for more academically prestigious Core Worlds.
csg_equat.description: Furry mammals native to a world near Hutt Space, the Equats managed a peaceful society of artists and poets before many were enslaved by the Hutts. Those with their freedom often find themselves at the premier academic institutions of the Core Worlds.
csg_equat.sidebar_text: The Equat once had a peaceful existence near the western fringes of Hutt Space, but things changed for them during the Kymoodon Era, as the Hutts were recovering from one of the most significant events in their own history: The Hutt Cataclysms, which rendered their homeworld of Varl uninhabitable. As the mourning Hutts formed a new society of kajidics on Nal Hutta, some took a newfound interest in preserving their history. Leading this movement, Ardustagg Nem’ro Oggurobb (remembered in history as Ardustagg the Immortalizer) sought among his servants anyone who could create a sufficiently glorious recounting of Hutt legends, but Weequays and Vodrans proved to have little skill with words. Exploring westward, his minions found a world whose mammals made worthy epic poems and operas. Spinning the Hutts as a race of auteurs, Ardustagg was able to trick thousands of Equat into coming to Nal Hutta, and overseeing their best writers, he constructed a corpus of epic mythologies that remain popular among Hutts to this day. These mixes of fact and fiction tell of battles against the Wardens, the Rebel Angels, the Demons, and Xim the Despot. Most notably, Death of a God tells the tragedy of the Hutts’ exile—but the Equat writer used clever metaphor to actually make it a reflection on his own people’s exile and slavery. Ardustagg ensured his Equat slaves bred quickly, growing the exiled population, though future generations never quite lived up to their forebears' work. Many Hutts continue to employ them as writers, but others are forced into more menial roles.
csg_equat._provenance_note: Little is known about the Equat. This entire page is highly speculative and retcons the unidentified mammalian species from The Art of Star Wars Episode I to be members. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they rewrite stats, imagining their own aspects of Equat physiology and culture.

csg_ergesh.name: Ergesh

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Swamp Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or wet conditions, add setback for cold or dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 2 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Poison Tolerance
special_abilities.description: Remove penalties for most toxins or reduce difficulty to resist toxins by up to 2 at the GM’s discretion.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_ergesh.physiology: The Ergesh are a unique species in that their biology is that of a massive plant rather than an animal. They are similar to humans in height but significantly wider, and that doesn’t include the system of roots that they have beneath them. Ergesh are still mobile, capable of floating in water or dragging themselves along with their tentacles, although they are not very fast. Their appearance is like a mound of leaves, vines, and assorted plant materials, all covered in a layer of slime that reeks of ammonia. Their skin is thick, making them well-protected, and it starts their life as a greenish shade, which becomes more and more dominated by patches of gray or brown as they age. They live for around two centuries, and they weigh half of a metric ton as adults. Ergesh are covered by a multitude of tentacles, which can serve many purposes. Some serve as their arms, while others have eyes, called opticstalks. Other tentacles are sensitive to sound, acting as ears. Without an obvious face, it is unclear how they eat, but it is known that their digestive tract is highly immune to toxins. They can easily cleanse themselves by drinking Kaloob, which causes them to secrete their fluids, flushing out poisons or harmful bacteria. Ergesh are genderless, reproducing by making one seed every two years, which they plant in a swamp called the Shoolbloorp, translating to the “Land of Beginnings.”
csg_ergesh.society: Ergesh are wise and peaceful, with a sincere interest in other cultures. They conduct business with integrity and fairness, and their society is devoid of crimes, classes, or discrimination. Their population is divided into 80 clans of about 10,000 each, and the government is composed of one representative from each clan, who is always the oldest. The government meets monthly for 40 straight hours at the Communal Pool, a swamp marked by its unique pattern of vegetation growth. The one exception to Ergesh level-headedness occurs for one day out of the year, when their planet’s moons align, causing them to behave in violent ways that can border on insanity before they suddenly return to normal.
csg_ergesh.language: The Ergesh language is a unique one that resembles the sound of water bubbling. Most Ergesh speak Basic, although they don’t use pronouns or articles. Their names are long and impossible to pronounce for other species, so most develop nicknames.
csg_ergesh.homeworld: The muggy, high-gravity planet Ergeshui in the southwestern Expansion Region is home to the Ergesh. It has dramatic tides, and almost half of the land, called tidal flats, are flooded at high tide. It has very rich soil and two sizable continents: Ersheg and Queesh. During the Clone Wars, Ergesh constructed the climate-controlled Outworlder City for visitors.
csg_ergesh.description: Massive botanical sentients native to the steamy swamps of Ergeshui, the Ergesh are serene and intelligent, making a multitude of unique organic technologies. However, their tendencies reverse once a year when their planet’s moons align, and they become dangerously psychotic.
csg_ergesh.sidebar_text: Ergesh are skilled scientists, and this is demonstrated best by their research into living technology, which is grown by a crew of about 2,000 farmers in the Industrial Swampfields. Their strange tech includes starships called Ergesh Starjumpers, which are no longer than a light freighter but require a crew of 800 Ergesh. The ships appear as blobs of vine-like appendages and can hurl plant buds as weapons. They also have organic buildings which can recognize the occupants, intelligently keeping out intruders.

csg_erkit.name: Er’Kit

special_abilities.name: Daredevils
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Confidence.”

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

csg_erkit.physiology: Er’Kits are fairly nimble humanoids of slightly above-average height with thick, bone-white skin that makes them more durable than the average sentient. Their head is hairless with a crest at the back, and they have long, downward-pointing ears. Their feet are wide and circular with tiny toes.
csg_erkit.society: Overall, the Er’Kits have a reputation of being a friendly, upbeat species who are optimistic to the point of carelessness. They expect the best in all of their ventures, taking on the galaxy with fearless ambition and few backup plans. Descending from speedy herbivores who grazed in large herds, they live in clans of several hundred and rarely travel alone. This social structure makes them generous and helpful, but they lack independence and can be too trusting at times. They voice the opinions that are popular, so once a clan makes up their mind, no one ever wants to speak out and be the first to question it. Clans often get involved in risky businesses together, and when things go sour, they usually just keep doubling down.
csg_erkit.language: The polysynthetic language called Er’Kit is a commonly used lingua franca among Er’Kit, although some know an additional native language. Most are literate in Basic, but they often struggle to pronounce p, b, f, or v sounds because their lips are too stiff.
csg_erkit.homeworld: Though once verdant, the Outer Rim planet Er’Kit is now a dying world, its ecosystem devastated by biological warfare. Once home to over 5 billion, only 3 million Er’Kit remain on the planet, and they have migrated to taigas near the poles. Most of the surviving Er’Kit population, about 800 million, is offworld on planets including Ciutric, Taanab, and Toprawa. The Yuuzhan Vong will terraform Er’Kit when they capture it, which will somewhat improve conditions and allow many to return home.
csg_erkit.description: Er’Kit are long-limbed humanoids with thick, chalk-colored skin and quick reflexes. This makes them skilled in areas of daredevil piloting, and they maintain an optimistic attitude. Their homeworld was devastated in the Clone Wars, so most of the survivors now take their chances in the wider galaxy.
csg_erkit.sidebar_text: Er’Kit was a world hit hard by the Clone Wars after the populace offered their support to the Separatists. Er’Kits used their mines and factories to support the war effort, bought war bonds, and many fought for the CIS directly. Their ace pilots served throughout the galaxy and defended their homeworld of Er’Kit. Unable to punch through their navy and land troops, Republic High General Sadiya Keldon turned to biological warfare, dropping trihexalophine1138 on Er’Kit from orbit. The contaminant devastated the planet’s ecosystem, rendering about half of it uninhabitable, but it also hurt the Er’Kits directly, causing respiratory problems for most of the population. Those who experienced particularly high doses also have psychological symptoms including memory loss, anxiety, and uncontrollable temper. Their lifespan is shorter and much of their land has been lost, so only a small population remains on Er’Kit to farm desolate, blighted lands and try to clean up the ecosystem. The Empire allows pirates and slavers to plague the planet, and Er’Kits blame Palpatine for their poverty, despising the Empire as much as they did the Old Republic. Even after seeing the CIS fail to gain independence, many still believe that a second rebellion will succeed.
csg_erkit._provenance_note: The Er’Kit species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_esoomian_zexx.name: Esoomian/Zexx

special_abilities.name: Tusks and Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_esoomian_zexx.physiology: Esoomians and Zexx are two names for the same hulking sentient species, which averages three meters in height. However, they often do not rise to their full height, preferring to stay in a squatted position, as they can run well on all fours. Their feet have four toes, and their hands also end in three clawed fingers. They have two long sharp tusks that can cut through flesh, and their head is conical at the top with a ridge along the center of their forehead. They have heavy brows, and their ears appear as slits on the side of their head. Most wear minimal clothing.
csg_esoomian_zexx.society: Esoomians and Zexx are both fairly unintelligent, and they tend to resolve all conflicts violently. While they are renowned as hired muscle, they make poor bounty hunters due to their lack of wits. Although they are highly aggressive with a strong emphasis on maintaining control over their property, they do not strongly seek independence, as they are just smart enough to recognize the value in having superiors who can maximize their specific skill set. Historically, this manifested as following tribal leaders, but now, Esoomians often join corporate-style hierarchies.
csg_esoomian_zexx.language: Neither Esoomians nor Zexx are fond of learning Basic. Their languages, Prazik and Esoomian, share a common ancestor but aren’t mutually intelligible. Esoomian is the only one with a written form.
csg_esoomian_zexx.homeworld: Esoomians come from Esooma, a world in the northern Outer Rim, while Zexx hail from Prazhi, an Expansion Region planet. Esooma has historically been the more technologically advanced and more involved in galactic trade, but this changed after an Esoomian revolt against the Empire in 12 BBY. Afterwards, the planet was quarantined, and the Empire found Esoomian slaves to be more trouble than they're worth. Both Esooma and Prazhi are relatively dry worlds with below-average gravity.
csg_esoomian_zexx.description: Zexx are a hulking species with sharp tusks and a highly combative focus. Millennia ago, some of their mercenaries settled war-torn Esoomia, where they have now become known as Esoomians.
csg_esoomian_zexx.sidebar_text: Originally, this species was known as the Zexx, and they hail from the Expansion Region planet Prazhi. However, this eventually became more complicated late in the Kanz Disorders: Just beyond the Republic’s northern frontier, the Argazdan Redoubt was establishing a brutal, expansive empire based around genocide and slavery. Worlds such as Esooma saw massive waves of emigration as civilians left their homes in fear of becoming the Argazdans’ latest victims. Meanwhile, Zexx travelled across the galaxy to fight as mercenaries on the frontier, defending the planets wealthy enough to afford their services. As the conflicts dragged on for centuries, Zexx came to find the largely abandoned cities of Esooma as an ideal place to rest between battles, and for many, it eventually became a permanent home. Once peace returned, the Zexx were so thoroughly entrenched on Esooma that they had opted to rename themselves to identify with it. Becoming the Esoomians, they saw their brethren on relatively peaceful Prazhi as cowards. The Zexx, by contrast, saw the Esoomians as having abandoned their heritage and assimilated into a human society. These sorts of stereotypes have lasted for over 3,000 years, and now, neither of them even acknowledge one another as being from the same species. Biologists will point out that the two should be genetically compatible with one another, but actual instances of this being tested are exceedingly rare due to their rivalry.
csg_esoomian_zexx._provenance_note: The Esoomian/Zexx species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_ewok.name: Ewok

special_abilities.name: Scent
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for concealment from combat checks if target is within short range.

csg_ewok.physiology: Ewoks are small creatures, though their bulk and fitness make up for this to an extent. Aside from eyes, nose, and mouth, they are covered in fur. This fur is mostly brown, though it can also be gray or black. They have three toes and fingers. Ewoks are distinctive for their large, black eyes and a small but sensitive nose. They are omnivorous in diet.
csg_ewok.society: Ewoks have a primitive society, but they are still sentient and intelligent. They are very superstitious, however, and have many religions, gods, and rituals. They hold the forests of their homeworld to be sacred, believing themselves descendants of the “Great Tree.” They are ruled by a chief and Council of Elders, while a medicine man handles most religious affairs. Ewoks are still practical and need to focus much of their time on getting food. For food, they aren’t opposed to eating sentients, either. Ewok villages are high in the trees, which are made of wood and connected by a series of bridges. Some live on the forest floor as fishers or hunters. Although they have demonstrated the ability to quickly grasp outside technology, their own technology is still basic. Innovations include hang gliders and fire.
csg_ewok.language: Ewokese is a primitive tongue, which is not known by many. Their vocal cords can handle Basic, just as humans can speak Ewokese.
csg_ewok.homeworld: Ewoks live on the Forest Moon of Endor, which is shared with several other sentient species. This includes the Yuzzum, which they have a strained relationship with. However, they mostly stay out of each other’s way. Later, it will be host to the construction of the Second Death Star, a major battle in the Galactic Civil War, and the death of Emperor Palpatine. The star system is currently backwater, obscure, and rarely traveled to by other sentients. Nearby astronomical hazards ensure that passing ships are highly likely to crash, which has given Endor its wide variety of immigrated species.
csg_ewok.description: Ewoks are primitive and seemingly irrelevant to the grand scheme of the galaxy. Living only on the isolated forest moon of Endor, they have yet to develop technology or space travel. Despite this, they will be vital to the Empire's defeat.
csg_ewok.sidebar_text: Though their small size and lack of advanced technology is indeed a major limit, Ewoks can be effective combatants on their own homeworld or anywhere with home field advantage. As primitive hunters, they know how to set traps for single animals, but they have other abilities as well. They have access to poison-tipped arrows and many are archers. Others use log based traps, which can trip larger foes. These are designed to fend off larger predators, but will later beat Imperial AT-STs. Even a primitive attack such as thrown rocks can work, since most armor isn’t designed to stop such an attack.

csg_falleen.name: Falleen

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 3.

csg_falleen.physiology: Falleen are cold-blooded reptilian near-humans with scaled green skin, although that color can temporarily change. They have a prominent spinal ridge starting at the back of their head. Females usually have lighter skin, lessened color changing, and a smaller ridge. The Falleen also have silky black hair, which males traditionally braid into a long topknot. While females have historically made more elaborate hairstyles for themselves, some in recent days choose to match the masculine style. With prominent cheekbones and a typically well-toned physique, Falleen are an attractive people, and they supplement this with pheromones and allelochemical transmitters, which have a hypnotic effect on the emotions of most species. Their skin color changes as they use these powers, however, so it is unsubtle. They are also gifted with a resistance to telepathic Force powers like mind tricks, and as distant relatives to aquatic creatures, they can hold their breath for a very long time. They also benefit from above-average reflexes, deadly talons on their digits, and a lifespan of over 200 years.
csg_falleen.society: Falleen are arrogant by nature and are organized into a feudal system of government. The lower classes include artisans, technicians, laborers, and slaves. Monarchs conduct business on behalf of the planet, and although they eagerly scheme and manipulate to maneuver themselves into positions of greater power, open warfare is rare. Falleen are restrained and known to be stoic, but this is not the whole story: While displays of emotion are seen as weak and immature, they are passionate in more private settings. In public, Falleen rein in their emotions with intense training, and they strive to make decisions based on rationality and careful planning. The social structures on Falleen prevent most Falleen from venturing into the galaxy, but there are a few reasons which can lead to exceptions: Lower class individuals can be sold to outsiders as slaves, while young nobles generally leave their home on a pilgrimage of sorts, learning to harness their manipulative abilities. Some Falleen also enjoy offworld art, although they consider the other species who create it to be inferior, and they are careful to keep it from influencing their own society.
csg_falleen.language: Falleen almost entirely know Basic in order to deal with outsiders, but they also view their own language, Falleen, as being superior.
csg_falleen.homeworld: Falleen is a Mid Rim world in the Slice. Since it is now blockaded by the Empire, the Falleen have been forced to prove their self-sufficiency. The terrain includes forests, mountains, and plains.
csg_falleen.description: Manipulation is the preferred weapon of the Falleen, and they combine natural effectiveness with powerful pheromones. They are arrogant and eager to take advantage of others. They are feared by the Imperials, so they now face heavy restrictions.
csg_falleen.sidebar_text: Falleen are very oppressed by the Empire, since the local Moff fears their manipulative abilities. The Empire has nationalized many corporations and taken profits. Years ago, they further angered Falleen when an Imperial biolab on the planet had an accident that spilled dangerous bacteria, and Darth Vader razed an entire city to prevent the spread. This killed over 200,000, including the family of noted crime lord Prince Xizor. The Empire has also restricted movement off of Falleen, with the only exceptions for pilgrimages and Imperial traffic. Some find ways to exploit those exceptions if they need to get offworld, while others go to the Rebel Alliance for help.

csg_farghul.name: Farghul

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_farghul.physiology: The Farghuls are a species that is very feline. They have fur covering their entire body, as well as fur on most of their head. This fur is typically brown. They also have pointed ears and greenish eyes. They have a prehensile tail and claws on their fingers. However, their most noteworthy physical capabilities come in terms of fitness. Farghuls are a very athletic people with great strength and speed who are typically in excellent physical condition. This, especially when combined with their sharp claws, means that many Farghuls are excellent fighters.
csg_farghul.society: Farghuls are known to be a people who are very oriented toward crime. This isn’t just a stereotype, however. It is very true that many Farghuls are smugglers, con artists, pickpockets, bounty hunters, and mercenaries. Although it would seem that this would make them opposed to the Empire, this isn’t always true: They’re often willing to fight for the Empire against the Jedi. Not unlike the Ubese, the Farghuls have developed a culture that fears the Jedi, who once destroyed a Farghul smuggling base. They still don’t trust politicians or governments of any sort, however. Similarly, they are also slightly xenophobic. Farghuls are also a species that is obsessed with appearance. They are extremely self-conscious about it, and they often wear fancy clothes and jewelry in order to look better. Although what they do wear is fancy, they wear relatively little clothing in comparison to many other species.
csg_farghul.language: Farghuls speak Farghul, and many of them also know Basic.
csg_farghul.homeworld: Farrfin, the homeworld of the Farghuls, is a temperate planet in the Core Worlds composed mostly of mountains and oceans. Its gravity is slightly below-average. It is a world devoted mostly to criminal activities of all sorts, such as spice smuggling, pickpocketing, and rigged gambling. Its main cities are Farlhu, Jahhnu, and Geltyu.
csg_farghul.description: Farghuls are notorious for their mischief, and although they are often criminals, they often seem to take their work lightly. They detest the Jedi, who at one point destroyed one of their smuggling bases.
csg_farghul.sidebar_text: Although many Farghuls are in fact criminals, they aren’t as serious as some. Most Farghuls who swindle will give back what they stole if they are caught. Whether this is for fear of repercussions or because of some strange moral code, no one knows. It is quite possible that they view crime and swindling as just a game, since they are known to be a species that is very playful and mischievous. Criminals or not, almost all Farghuls enjoy telling bad jokes and pranking those that they come across.

csg_feeorin.name: Feeorin

special_abilities.name: Dark Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Heat Tolerance
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions.

csg_feeorin.physiology: The Feeorins are large and tall humanoids who are very tolerant to heat. They are strong and also very fit, able to continue prolonged exercise without needing as much rest as other species. Their skin is typically blue or green, but it can also be gray or black. They have no hair, but they do have long tendrils which extend from their head. Similar to Nautolans, the tendrils are about half of a meter long. Their red eyes see well in the dark, and about half of them have a nose. Unlike many other species, they do not become weaker with age. Instead, they grow stronger, although they don’t learn wisdom as much as other species. Eventually, at some point between 300 and 400 years old, they drop dead, dying of old age without warning.
csg_feeorin.society: Feeorins resemble humans in that they can have a great diversity of personalities, but their spacers are typically selfish and grumpy. They are very easily angered, while they don’t make friends easily. They have a reputation of being very dangerous. Feeorins are a very religious people, and their dead elders are buried in the Sanctum of the Exalted, where they are believed to control the weather. Only the Exalted are allowed to enter this sacred necropolis, a title bestowed to the oldest and strongest of the Feeorin. Most Feeorin are very traditional, somewhat primitive, and have a tribal mindset, but their spacefaring members are often more practical.
csg_feeorin.language: Feeorin speak Feeorin, and many of them learn Basic as well.
csg_feeorin.homeworld: Feeorins have abandoned their home after climate change made it uninhabitable, but their largest colony is on Odryn. Odryn has plentiful jungles, and trees are used to build homes on its mountainsides. The planet is considered uncomfortably hot by humans, but the Feeorins have little issue with the temperature. Very few outsiders visit Odryn, and its natives rarely leave. Most of the nomadic Feeorin come from parents who were also nomadic.
csg_feeorin.description: Feeorins are a warlike people who never feel the effects of old age until they suddenly drop dead. All are strong, athletic, and resistant to heat, but their elders are the strongest.
csg_feeorin.sidebar_text: The original homeworld of the Feeorin has been rendered uninhabitable because of climate change, and it has been abandoned. The Feeorin population has suffered in response: Although they have sent out many colony ships to find a new home, they have struggled to survive as nomads. Not the best at peaceful interaction, they have been unwelcome on many of their new colonies. Native species often fight back by hunting them down, considering the Feeorins to be raiders. Now, there are fewer than 1,000,000 Feeorins who have survived. While some live in successful colonies, many others are nomadic.

csg_fefze.name: Fefze

special_abilities.name: Hardened Carapaces
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Acidic Spit
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter, may suffer 2 strain to attack using acidic vomit with Ranged-Light, dealing 4 base damage at engaged range. Have a Crit rating of 4, and may spend triumph to blind opponent.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Suffer 4 strain for every round spent flying.

special_abilities.name: Swarms
special_abilities.description: May become part of a swarm with other Fefze if within 100 meters of its other members, sharing all memories and gaining +1 Intellect.

special_abilities.name: No Hands
special_abilities.description: Reduce encumbrance threshold by 2 and may not carry items in hands. May not use technology requiring fingers, such as blasters. At the GM’s discretion, add up to 3 setbacks on checks where fingers are beneficial, such as Piloting.

csg_fefze.physiology: The Fefze are a species of insects who are protected by a hardened black carapace which is split down the middle, and they can extend it off of their body to form wings. Although they are not optimized for flight, they can manage it in short bursts. Their head and legs are less protected, but they can curl up under their shell as a defense mechanism. Like most insects, Fefze walk on six legs and have a body split between their head, thorax, and abdomen. Although they can use their front limbs for manipulation, they have no hands, so properly using technology is difficult. Their head features two prominent mandibles at their mouth, and they have wide compound eyes on either side of their head. They also have two antennae above their eyes, both of which fulfill three major functions. The antennae give them their sense of both hearing and smell, but they also can be rubbed together to produce unique sounds, which they use to communicate. They live for only ten years on average. Fefze also boast an incredibly advanced digestive system, with which they can gain nutrition from almost any carbon-based material, including dirt or mulch. They have a supply of acid in their mouth that they spit on their food before they consume it, which helps with digestion but also separates carbohydrates and proteins. Fefze consume both, but they can regurgitate the proteins at will. They do this if confronted by predators, as the predators will generally choose to eat the easily accessible protein rather than give chase. Additionally, the acidic spit itself can be used to attack.
csg_fefze.society: Fefze live only in swarms of ten to one hundred members, as they are unintelligent when alone but as sentient as any other species when studied as a group. They care little for themselves as individuals, as they place the good of the swarm above all. They have experienced great success with their lifestyle, because their unique digestive system gives them a bountiful supply of food. As such, they have had little reason to develop advanced technology, but they have created great art. Many are musicians, although their music is unique and unpopular among other species. They also enjoy visual art, but their works are rarely permanent. Mostly made of sand or small organisms, their works last for short periods of time.
csg_fefze.language: Fefze typically speak their native language of rubbing antennae together and rarely know Basic.
csg_fefze.homeworld: Fefze come from the hot Mid Rim planet of Fef, a primitive forest world with a thick atmosphere.
csg_fefze.description: Fefze are insects with an incredible digestive system that allows them to eat almost anything, and although they are unintelligent on their own, they can form swarms that are more intelligent. Fefze don't think for themselves, only for the swarm, which they are completely loyal to.
csg_fefze.sidebar_text: One of the most popular forms of Fefze art is their choreographed dances, which are respected even among other species. These dances are often done on their own as entertainment, but their original purpose is for mating. In these joyous events, two swarms get together to dance and mate. Afterwards, the females lay their eggs within a globute of protein paste secreted by the males. Most of the eggs remain within the swarm, allowing them to repopulate and keep the swarm alive for hundreds of years. Others, however, are kept separate and form a new swarm.

csg_felucian.name: Felucian

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Rancor Tamers
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Enhance Basic Power, the Move Basic Power, and the Influence Basic Power. When using an Influence Power check on an animal, add 2 boosts.

csg_felucian.physiology: An agile but resilient species of amphibious sentients, the Felucians are slightly taller and more athletic than most species. They are camouflaged with moist gray skin which is marked with colored stripes. Their brawny arms end in four webbed digits with suction cup tips, each evenly spaced. Additionally, they have smaller but more dexterous hands extending from their wrists, each with three fingers. Visually, their most distinctive feature is their face, a mass of tendrils with luminescent tips. Their eyes, appearing as a dark gap between the tendrils, see well in the dark, and their mouth is also a gap between their tendrils. All are Force-sensitive, and they have a strong connection to the Living Force. Conversely, they are very vulnerable to Dark Side degradation, which causes their tendrils to become dry and limp.
csg_felucian.society: Felucians have a primitive society in the wild jungles of Felucia, away from more industrialized Gossams, but they are united under a single tribe. This is because Felucians are barbaric by most standards and extremely unpredictable, so any independent tribes or individuals could put their entire society at risk. They live in small huts made of fungi, and they clothe themselves with only bones or scraps of plants, although most decorate themselves with beads, and some wear a traditional headdress. They use primitive weapons, and they extract poisons and medicines from plants. They have a symbiosis with the yerdua poison-spitter, a semi-sentient plant that guards their villages in exchange for being fed and cared for. Their planet’s ecosystem was damaged in the Clone Wars, but life grew back, and the Felucians thrived for a time. However, four years ago, the Empire began to attack them out of fear for their Force-sensitivity.
csg_felucian.language: Felucians rarely speak Basic, instead using their barking native tongue, Felucianese.
csg_felucian.homeworld: A steamy jungle planet, Felucia was somewhat industrialized by Gossams in the Commerce Guild, but much of the planet remains totally primitive. Composed of hostile animals and fungi, the jungle’s ecosystem and the Felucians themselves act as a single entity united by the Living Force.
csg_felucian.description: Entirely Force-sensitive, the Felucians have a deep relationship with their native environment via the Living Force. Although they are primitive, they are united under a single government, and they were once guided in the Force by Jedi Master Shaak Ti.
csg_felucian.sidebar_text: Felucians have a caste system, including mushroom farmers, warriors and scouts marked blue, shamans marked red, and chieftains marked yellow. Most are capable of using telekinesis for simple pushes, and warriors and scouts use the Force to enhance their physical skills, but shamans focus on more advanced techniques like healing and protection. Chieftains often specialize in taming the native rancors. Although chieftains have the most political power, shamans are trusted as spiritual leaders. Trained to resist the Dark Side, shamans will throw Dark-Siders into the Ancient Abyss, a sarlacc that kills them. In recent decades, Felucian society was dominated by a uniquely gifted chieftain in Jedi Master Shaak Ti, who trained them in the Force. Although her death at the hands of Galen Marek four years ago plunged their people into the Dark Side, they have since returned to the Light Side.

csg_fett_clone.name: Fett Clone

special_abilities.name: Scout Training
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent "Outdoorsman."

special_abilities.name: Strict Regimen
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent "Physical Training."

special_abilities.name: Loyal
special_abilities.description: After 1 month of serving a person or cause, may become extremely loyal. When doing things to serve that cause or person, add boost to all Willpower checks.

csg_fett_clone.physiology: Fett clones are humans with the base genome of Jango Fett, modified to make them into optimal soldiers. They share many traits as their template, including dark hair, a height of 1.83 meters, and their harsh training ensures that they are typically in excellent shape. However, they have a key difference in that their genome has been modified so that they age at twice the rate of normal humans. This allows them to enter battle at nine or ten years old, but their lifespan is essentially cut in half even if they survive battle. An even more dramatic change can be seen in clones made from Spaarti cloning cylinders, which saw use in the second half of the war and could produce a functioning adult in a single year. Spaarti clones are cheaper and even more robotic than normal clones, and they are trained via false memories injected into them with a process called "flash-pumping."
csg_fett_clone.society: During the Clone Wars, clone troopers were created as essentially slaves to the Republic with very little freedom in their lives. They were objects to their Kaminoan creators, who often terminated defective clones. For the rest, their training was a harsh life that often saw live-fire combat drills beginning as young as four years. Everything from their diets to their time was strictly overseen by others, so the idea of choices is essentially foreign to most clones. This unique upbringing combined with genetic modifications to make them more obedient created an army far unlike any normal humans. Though clones experienced better treatment under the Jedi and other officers in the Republic, their single-mindedness and loyalty remained. Only a small portion of clones were designed to be more independent, those including the Commanders, ARC Troopers, and Republic Commandos. Such clones, lacking the genetic modifications to be more obedient, were consequently capable of desertion and disobedience, something unthinkable for most clones. The rank and file clones transitioned seamlessly into stormtroopers as the Republic was reorganized, though the Empire slowed production of new clones and refilled their army with civilian recruits. Palpatine gave little to no consideration for the Grand Army’s health care, and the clones are cast aside once unable to serve.
csg_fett_clone.language: Normal clones are taught Basic, but those trained by Cuy’val Dar often learn Mando’a as well.
