csg_fett_clone.homeworld: The clones were created in secret on the rainy world of Kamino, which is found in Companion Aurek. The native Kaminoans are an emotionless bunch who built stilted cities over the oceans.
csg_fett_clone.description: Bred for combat by Kaminoan cloners, the clones of Jango Fett are highly trained warriors who have a narrow focus and little ability for independent thought. They have accelerated aging, which made them ready for battle more quickly, but it now hurts many as their body quickly wears down.
csg_fett_clone.sidebar_text: The Republic Commandos received unique training from a hundred mercenaries called the Cuy’val Dar, a Mando’a phrase meaning “those who no longer exist.” Selected by Fett, three quarters of the Cuy’val Dar were Mandalorian, and all passed on parts of their own culture to the commandos. Each trained 104 clones and often became father figures for them. Clones with Mandalorian heritage may supplement this profile with the Mandalorian stats.

csg_filordus.name: Filordus

special_abilities.name: Pincers
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3. When using Brawl with pincers, suffer 1 strain for every maneuver spent moving. May use pincers for Brawl even when holding other gear or weapons.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add boost on auditory Perception checks. Triple all sonic damage and, at the GM’s discretion, increase sonic damage from 0 to 1.

csg_filordus.physiology: Filordi are canines with six limbs who are covered in short, brown hair. Their uppermost limbs have three-fingered hands, their middle pair is used to help walk and have pincers, and their bottom pair are thick and used exclusively for walking. When they fight, they often use their pincers as weapons, but it is very hard for them to stand on only two legs. They are somewhat short, averaging under a meter and a half in height. Despite their smaller size, they are tough and very resilient. Their face has an elongated snout and large ears, the latter of which they can use to protect their black eyes from wind and rain. They all have blue stripes, although some have more prominent stripes than others. Filordi are asexual, so none of them have a gender. They reproduce by giving birth a week after they have died. An infant Filordus is a clone of his or her dead parent. They are able to crawl at birth and become adults by the age of fifteen.
csg_filordus.society: Filordi are a persistent, obsessive people who go to extreme lengths to get what they want in the short term. They are extremely opportunistic and highly resourceful, so they find a way to consume everything that is available to them. They are intelligent and adapt quickly. These abilities have given them some success in business, as they were once a prominent species in the Metatherian Cartel, a Trade Federation offshoot based on Cularin.
csg_filordus.language: Filordi speak Filordian, a language which lacks many of the consonant sounds that Basic has. They have a gravelly voice, and they often ignore certain consonants when speaking Basic.
csg_filordus.homeworld: Filordi come from Filordis, an Inner Rim planet with a ren sun. It is a rocky wasteland and has many thunderstorms. Many Filordi have attempted to terraform it.
csg_filordus.description: A canine species known for their fierce determination, the Filordi have six limbs, including two for walking, two for grasping, and two they can walk or act as weapons. Although they are opportunistic, they struggle greatly with long-term planning.
csg_filordus.sidebar_text: Despite their drive to succeed, the Filordi are almost completely incapable of long term planning, and their inability to think ahead has cost them. Their homeworld is a wasteland plagued by harsh weather, so they have needed to terraform it. Many others prefer to abandon it in favor of more habitable planets in the rest of the galaxy. Their foolishness can create other problems, too: Since they will become completely obsessed with their goals without thinking things through, they are very easy to swindle if given what they want.

csg_filvian.name: Filvian

special_abilities.name: Desert Survivors
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions. Can survive for 1 month without food or water due to reserve glands.

special_abilities.name: Naturally Quadrupedal
special_abilities.description: When bipedal, may only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn. May not carry items in hands or wield weapons while moving quadrupedally.

csg_filvian.physiology: Filvians are fur-covered quadrupedal ungulates, and they are adapted to survive in harsh desert environments. They have lumpy glands throughout their body which store additional food and water, allowing them to survive for up to a month without eating or drinking if they need to. Despite these adaptations, they are still more comfortable at the cooler temperatures which are preferred by humans. Although they move faster on four legs, they can be bipedal if needed, and their forelimbs each have three dexterous fingers that they can use to carry things or use technology. Their fur comes in shades of tan, yellow, or off-white, and they have a tail, humps on their back, and two pointed ears above their forehead. Their furry visage features a prominent snout and small eyes. They are shorter than humans, about one and a half meters tall on average if they stand on their hind legs.
csg_filvian.society: The Filvians are a highly intelligent and technologically advanced people. They are among the galaxy’s premier programmers and engineers, and they quickly pick up new technical skills. They are naturally very gregarious and enjoy travelling throughout the galaxy. Unfamiliar technology is of particular interest to them, and they make every effort to learn about the machines used in other societies as they go about their business.
csg_filvian.language: Filvians are capable of speaking Basic, and it is unknown whether or not they also use a language of their own.
csg_filvian.homeworld: Filvians come from the desert planet of Filve, a prominent trade world in the southeastern part of the Mid Rim. It has excellent spaceports and heavy investment in starship service and repair. An economically successful world, it holds branch offices for many major corporations such as Sienar and BlasTech Industries. It also has highly advanced infrastructure, with cities that are insulated and climate-controlled. An extensive system of tunnels allows for transportation between them without ever going outside. Days on Filve are remarkably short, at just 14 standard hours, and although seasonal weather variations have little impact on the Filvians, years on the planet are short as well, just 64 standard days. 6 billion sentients call it home, including a sizable population of immigrated species such as humans.
csg_filvian.description: Filvians are desert-dwelling ungulates who can be either quadrupedal or bipedal. They are highly skilled with all matters of technology, which makes them carefully watched by their Imperial rulers.
csg_filvian.sidebar_text: In part because of their success, Filvians now suffer under discriminatory Imperial policies. With such a large number of weapons and starship manufacturers located on Filve, it is no surprise that the Empire has made certain to keep a close eye on the planet. Any incidents of rebellion near Filve have been violently crushed, often with significant collateral damage. Although the Filvians do not like this, they tolerate Imperial rule for fear of reprisal. Even as they long for a new power to take over, most Filvians currently do everything that they can to placate the Empire and ensure that their situation does not become any worse. Not long after Palpatine’s death, they will quickly move to support the fledgling New Republic in 6 ABY.

csg_firrerreo.name: Firrerreo

special_abilities.name: Advanced Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for lighting conditions.

special_abilities.name: Supreme Regeneration
special_abilities.description: As an action, may make an average Resilience check to heal, recovering 1 wound per success. Outside of combat, after every hour of healing, recover 5 wounds and may roll to heal a critical injury. May reattach lost limbs in a few hours if the limb is set in place.

csg_firrerreo.physiology: Save for more prominent canine teeth and two-colored hair, Firrerreos are visually near-human. However, they have a very distinct biology internally. They are surprisingly strong from their size and incredibly resilient, able to recover from almost anything in a few hours. More minor wounds they can heal in a span of minutes, sometimes even at a speed visible to the naked eye. They have somewhat gold skin, but it can become more monochrome when they are angry or when the skin is recently healed. In addition to their remarkable durability, Firrerreos boast exceptional senses, including ultraviolet vision and hearing at higher frequencies than humans. No doubt as a result of their rapid healing abilities, they require a large amount of protein and eat mostly meat.
csg_firrerreo.society: A somewhat wild and animalistic species, Firrerreos have a distinct worldview that makes them struggle to interact under human social norms. They have clans, which they are loyal to, but they are indifferent to those who are outside of their clan or their race. They are also completely independent, never expecting to be helped and never helping others either unless something is offered in exchange. They place a high value on names, and they view saying another’s name as a demonstration of power over that person. As such, they usually operate under the pseudonym “Firrerreo,” and if they ever learn someone else’s name, they are certain to repeat it often.
csg_firrerreo.language: Firrerreos speak Firrerrese. When speaking Basic, they are prone to animalistic tendencies like snarls, growls, and barring of teeth. Traditionally, they say, “May you be shielded from the wind” when parting.
csg_firrerreo.homeworld: Firrerre was once the Firrerreos’ homeworld, but its sentient population has been wiped out, and no one has resettled it for fear of the virus. The Outer Rim world is still a rugged, mountainous planet with vast oceans, and the empty infrastructure remains.
csg_firrerreo.description: Firrerrreos appear human but actually have a very unique biology that gives them some of the most efficient healing of any species. They are loyal to their clans but have little concept of generosity, expecting all to take responsibility for their own needs.
csg_firrerreo.sidebar_text: The Firrerreos are one of many peoples to suffer atrocities under the Empire, but their most direct oppressor was actually one of their own. Hethrir, a Firrerreo dark Jedi who was instructed by Darth Vader, became an Imperial Procurator of Justice and betrayed his own people to prove his loyalty. The Firrerreo homeworld was knowingly infected with hive virus under his orders, and the planet was quarantined to avoid its spread. However, thousands of Firrerreos were evacuated by the Empire, and they are now kept in suspended animation aboard freighters that float through empty space. Hethrir intends to return to them after a millenia, awakening the prisoners and being worshipped as their savior and god. After Palpatine’s death, he will go on to lead the Empire Reborn, which will collapse in 14 ABY following his disappearance. After learning about the atrocities, the New Republic will discover and free many of the Firrerreos from their stasis. The species will then settle worlds like Kinooine and Belderone, although the settlements on Belderone will later be wiped out by the Yuuzhan Vong.

csg_flakax.name: Flakax

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for dry conditions, add setback for wet conditions.

csg_flakax.physiology: Flakax are bipedal insects native to a desert environment with a black body, and they have a distinct thorax and abdomen. They have large compound eyes on either side of their head, small mandibles surrounding their beak-like mouth, and two antennae atop their hairless head. Their arms have three pincer-like fingers, and their feet have two toes. Their abdomen is bioluminescent, which can flash on and off for use as a flashlight. They have three genders: males, females, and sterile drones. The latter make up most of their society and are parthenogenetic children of the queen.
csg_flakax.society: Flakax have a hive-based society, and they have little identity or purpose outside of their hive. Most are drones who exist solely to work. Males are responsible only for breeding, while females take up leadership positions. They are ruled by a female queen who is also solely responsible for laying eggs. Males are typically eaten by the queen after they reproduce. Queens are responsible for guiding the hive, providing direction, emotion, and creativity on behalf of its entirety. Most queens care little for anyone outside the hive, as do her subjects. Although many hives have little technology and no tools, their strong unity makes them excellent builders. They all live underground in massive colonies, and they hunt for food above ground at dusk. A few Flakax are without hives: This can happen after the death of a queen, and it is also not unprecedented for males to run away if they are about to be eaten. However, these individuals are rendered purposeless by their lack of a hive, so they are generally psychopathic, suicidal, or otherwise insane.
csg_flakax.language: Flakax typically speak their native language as well as Basic.
csg_flakax.homeworld: Flakax come from the backwater Expansion Region planet of Flax, which is tectonically very active, creating enormous mountains. Although it has many seas, this unique geography prevents moisture from reaching the land, and most of the planet is a desert.
csg_flakax.description: Although they are not capable of telepathic hive minds like some species, the Flakax are insects who are absolutely loyal to their hive. The majority of their species is infertile, simply acting as drones to perform labor for their queen.
csg_flakax.sidebar_text: Because of their work ethic and devotion to their hive, the Flakax are excellent in manual labor such as building and mining. The latter is especially common in the modern era, where, despite their onetime allegiance to the Confederacy of Independent Systems, they have mined much of their world in service to the Empire. They are willing to mine out their lands for little pay because the Empire is giving them protection in exchange, and the Flakax see this as a worthwhile sacrifice. Like all things, they approach their work with austere devotion.

csg_florn_lamproid.name: Florn Lamproid

special_abilities.name: Superb Reflexes
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Rapid Reaction.”

special_abilities.name: Constriction
special_abilities.description: May spend 2 advantage on a Brawl check to immobilize the target and induce suffocation. Escaping constriction requires an Athletics check opposed by Brawl. Constricted victims may be poisoned using stinger or fangs as a maneuver, which disorient the victim for and deal 2 wounds per round until the victim passes a hard Resilience check.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 3 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Eyestalks
special_abilities.description: Can see in all directions.

special_abilities.name: Pincers
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of any checks to use technology designed for species with fingers, such as most starship controls or blasters.

csg_florn_lamproid.physiology: Florn Lamproids are among the galaxy’s top predators. Related to reptilian parasites, they have a very muscular serpentine body that grows six meters long and is packed with muscle. They propel themselves using their tail, and they have six short arms, each with simple pincers that are ineffective for grasping most technology. They have a wide mouth surrounded by four large fangs, and they have four eyestalks above their head, which can see in all directions. Lamproids have brown, gray, green, or pink skin. They excel in stealth and can quickly wrap up a victim using their tail. Once constrained, the victim is finished off using a poisonous stinger and their poisonous saliva. Their teeth can easily chew up flesh, and they drink blood. Lamproids rarely wear clothing, and they identify other Lamproids using pheromones. Many are Force-sensitive, and they tend to excel in telepathy.
csg_florn_lamproid.society: Florn Lamproids are cunning enough to succeed as hunters and as members of galactic society, but they have little interest in the arts. Almost all live as hunters of some sort, whether they are primitive predators, assassins, or bounty hunters. Despite these shortcomings, many have been able to acclimate to modern technology, live in some civilized societies, and a few have even joined the Rebel Alliance.
csg_florn_lamproid.language: Lamproids who are more civilized generally speak Basic, but they have no language of their own. They have a hissing voice, and they convey emotions by shifting their fangs.
csg_florn_lamproid.homeworld: Lamproids come from Florn, a jungle planet on the fringes of the Outer Rim that has an incredibly dangerous wilderness. To the rest of the galaxy, their homeworld is a mystery, because they have many colonies as well. Most of these colonies are uncivilized worlds with vast sections of forest that they can hunt in.
csg_florn_lamproid.description: Many debate the sentience of the Florn Lamproids, who are clever hunters that communicate but have little civilized society. What is not up for debate is that they are top predators, combining strength and venom with stealth and reflexes.
csg_florn_lamproid.sidebar_text: Because they lack culture or art, the sentience of the Lamproids is often debated. Although they have not adapted much intelligence for social interactions, they are clever hunters and can solve many puzzles. As such, they are often legal to hunt, especially under the Empire. However, they pose an incredible challenge because of their natural fitness, stealth, weapons, and intelligence, so only the most skilled of hunters will prey on the Florn Lamproids.

csg_fluggrian.name: Fluggrian

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_fluggrian.physiology: Fluggrians are portly amphibians with olive-green skin. They average about a meter tall due to their short legs, which protrude from the sides of their abdomen. Each of their hands and feet have three digits which end in a purple spike, and these purple spikes are also scattered across their stomach, forearms, and scalp. They act as sensory organs and can process information very quickly, giving the Fluggrians excellent reflexes. They also have purple stripes along their neck, below their chin, and around their sunken yellow eyes. Their forehead protrudes forward, as does their snout, which has prominent pink lips with two large visible teeth behind them. While Fluggrians are aquatic and have gills on their neck to breathe underwater, they can also breathe air.
csg_fluggrian.society: Often found in criminal occupations, the Fluggrians are a clever people for whom deception comes naturally. They tend to be long-term thinkers, which often results in frequently worrying, pessimism, and paranoia. If they aren’t trying to deceive, they tend to think out loud, wear their emotions on their sleeve, and vent their many worries to whomever they can, a trait which exasperates most other species. While using others for emotional support is common, having them as financial support is not, and almost all Fluggrians strive to be self-sufficient at a young age. The Empire has exploited this tendency by luring Fluggrian youth into long contracts which are generous for their age but low-paying in the long run. Other Fluggrians are forced to work in debtor’s prisons, and former Separatists are enslaved as well.
csg_fluggrian.language: Fluggrians speak their native language of Klurrel, and although most can understand Basic, their unique teeth make it impossible for them to normally pronounce d, t, or th sounds.
csg_fluggrian.homeworld: Fluggrians come from the impoverished Expansion Region world Ploo IV, which is in the same system as Ploo II, the Glymphid homeworld. It is covered in bogs with floating cities and underwater tunnels.
csg_fluggrian.description: The amphibious Fluggrians are a people known for their worrying and desire for independence, and they value being able to plan far into the future. They have a fierce rivalry with the Glymphids that share a star system with them.
csg_fluggrian.sidebar_text: For generations, the Fluggrians have been at war with their neighbors, the Glymphids, a lanky species of reptiles. Tensions run deep between the two, and no Fluggrian or Glymphid would ever willingly work with one another. Both species are prone to criminal activity and will often try to assassinate one another if they encounter them offworld. However, what was once a stalemate took a dramatic turn during the Clone Wars, when the Fluggrians seceded, yet the Glymphids remained loyal to the Republic, and the Grand Army seized the Fluggrian homeworld during the war’s final year. The Empire demanded reparations from the Fluggrians and placed corrupt Glymphids in power over their former rivals. This turned out bad for nearly everyone involved, as the extremely sadistic Glymphid-run government was more concerned with tormenting and murdering the Fluggrians than getting any productive labor out of them. The Empire has since installed a new government with leaders from other worlds, but Fluggrians are still impoverished, heavily taxed, and often in borderline slavery. Many support the Rebel Alliance, which has made efforts to free them.
csg_fluggrian._provenance_note: The Fluggrian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_fneeb.name: Fneeb

special_abilities.name: Magnetic Sense
special_abilities.description: When in a strong magnetic field, know direction at all times and add boost on all Coordination or Piloting checks or 2 boosts on checks to navigate mazes or buildings.

csg_fneeb.physiology: Fneebs are small avians with a brown-feathered back and a white-feathered chest. They have a tail and an antenna, both of which manifest as a chain of ball-shaped mounds of flesh. The latter is used for sensing magnetic signals, which helps them with navigation. Their wide, circular eyes have yellow irises, and their bullseye shapes give the Fneebs what many consider a startled look. Just above them, their eyebrows manifest as two wide ridges, one on top of the other, and their mouth is a conical white beak that they use to crush their diet of seeds, grains, and nuts. Their young do not have the strength to eat these foods, so they feed them via regurgitation. Their hands have three fingers, and their feet end in three toes, which they use to walk with a digitigrade stance. Most Fneebs do not wear clothing.
csg_fneeb.society: Fneebs make up for their diminutive stature with a flamboyant personality, which often makes them excel in entertainment professions, although they are also known for their medical skills, and they have the energy to keep up with the demanding work of a doctor. But outside of work, they almost always like to travel the galaxy: While Fneebs have long lost the ability to fly, their psyche never quite let go of the desire. For some, this also manifests as an interest in piloting, be it starships, swoops, or even Podracers, the latter of which they are often brought into because of the Hutt influence on their planet.
csg_fneeb.language: Thanks to the strong Hutt influence on their world, Fneebs are more likely to learn Huttese or Bocce as their second language than Basic, though they can speak it. Their voice is higher-pitched, and their native language, Ismeeft, involves many chirps and whistles.
csg_fneeb.homeworld: Fneebs come from Fallowan, a fairly dry world of deserts, mountains, and plains. Located in the southeastern Outer Rim, it is backwater and rarely visited, except by traders from the Hutt kajidic Gorensla, who have influenced the planet’s economy to make it a hub for growing armudu spice. They also have colonies in the equatorial parts of Nedij.
csg_fneeb.description: Little avians, the Fneebs make up for their loss of flight with a flamboyant personality and eager desire to fly whatever vehicles they can. Prior to their first contact with the Republic, many developed a religious fervor for carbon-freezing themselves and taking to the stars via sublight spacecraft.
csg_fneeb.sidebar_text: The Fneebs’ desire to explore was most prominent in ancient history, before the wider galaxy made contact with them. They were able to discover sublight space travel on their own, and they were also significantly ahead of their time in the science of carbon-freezing individuals to preserve their lifespan. Combining these feats, they made plans to send hundreds of millions of Fneebs to the Nedij system, a journey projected to take over six thousand years initially. From 7,370 BBY until contact with the Republic in 2,347 BBY gave them the hyperdrive, Fneebs took to the stars in these sleeper ships. Many survived their journey and began to settle Nedij over the course of the Republic Golden Age, though their warmer climate preferences generally took them to different regions of the planet than its native Nediji. It’s still not uncommon for a couple ships per year to show up at Nedij with a hundred or so frozen Fneebs, who have established a tradition of showing off their age via a system of colored bands on their tail. In the past, Nedij held an almost religious significance to the Fneebs as a prophesied heaven, and arriving to a tyrannical Imperial rule there shatters their worldview. Some refuse to accept reality and insist on the Empire’s benevolence; others see it as a demonic force that they are destined to purge Nedij of.
csg_fneeb._provenance_note: Little is known about the Fneeb. The following information is almost entirely made up. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they imagine their own aspects of Fneeb physiology and culture, rewriting stats accordingly.

csg_fosh.name: Fosh

special_abilities.name: Unique Tears
special_abilities.description: Once per day, may make an Easy Resilience check to generate tears. If successful, may create a pheromonal liquid that can influence mood, a poison that deals 1 wound per success, or a medicinal salve that heals 1 wound per success.

csg_fosh.physiology: Fosh are small but nimble avians who are rather frail. Their skin is red, purple, or pink. They are further distinguished by a multitude of feathers that grow from the backs of their heads. These feathers change color by mood. Orange is indicative of contentment, while gray is more angry or dissatisfied. Green is used to show focused thought or amusement. Normally, the feathers are blue or purple. Their head also features two small red antennae, soft whiskers, red eyes, and a beaked mouth. Their arms and legs are thin and typically less feathered. Their feet have two clawed toes and their hands have four clawed fingers. They have two knees on each leg, with the lower one pointing forward. Fosh also have very unique tears, which females in particular can manipulate to create various minor pheromones. Those who are Force-sensitive can further enhance this ability, creating even more powerful liquids. This includes both poisons and powerful healing fluids similar to bacta.
csg_fosh.society: Fosh are a mysterious people who tend to be loners. They are secretive, private, and also very rare. So rare, in fact, that many have considered them to be extinct for the past 30 years. The average sentient likely wouldn’t even recognize them. They are a quiet people who prefer to listen rather than speak. When they do speak, however, it is usually for good reason. They are very manipulative, devious, and would likely be good in politics. Despite that, they have no political representation, as no one knows of their homeworld or government. While wise enough to appease should their lives be threatened, Fosh are often quite annoying. In conversation, they use riddles and analogies to confuse those that listen. They are selfish, arrogant, and sometimes even rude. Most notably, they are also quite speciesist. They view all other species as subordinate, merely toys within their own machinations. Fosh are difficult to predict, often pursuing complicated goals with even more complicated schemes. What exactly they hope to accomplish in these schemes is another one of the many mysteries surrounding the Fosh.
csg_fosh.language: Fosh speak a language called Fosh that is known by very few non-Fosh. Most also speak Basic.
csg_fosh.homeworld: The Fosh homeworld is not known to the rest of the galaxy. Some theorize that they come from the Corporate Sector. Considering the bias against non-human species in that region, it is possible that they were hunted to being nearly extinct.
csg_fosh.description: Light, mysterious avians from an unknown world, Fosh are an extremely rare sight. They are selfish, manipulative, and a bit annoying to some. Their tears are incredible chemicals which can range from miracle medicines to poisons.
csg_fosh.sidebar_text: Just because the Fosh are so secretive doesn’t mean their culture doesn’t exist. Players controlling a Fosh should consider the various mysteries of Fosh culture and try to better flesh out the species. While they should tell their GM, keeping it secret from the other players can provide many opportunities for interesting roleplaying as well. However, the detached nature of the Fosh may make it difficult to get along, so being a Fosh shouldn’t be chosen lightly.

csg_frenk.name: Frenk

special_abilities.name: Nimble Frame
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Dodge.”

csg_frenk.physiology: Frenk are thinly built reptiles of about two meters in height. They have spotted green, orange, or pink skin, and their dexterous body is extremely thin above the waist before widening at the shoulders. Their head is hairless and has extremely sunken cheeks, somewhat similar to that of the Rodians, who are their distant relatives. Their cranium is conical, and they have four nostrils between their large black eyes. Unlike the Rodians, they have four-fingered hands and lack suction cups on their fingers.
csg_frenk.society: Frenk value combative abilities and hunting, which makes many of them eager to be bounty hunters. They are also community oriented and often prefer to work in teams, which stems from their clans that survive together prowling the jungles. Despite their fondness for groups, they are very quiet in general, and they are not particularly sociable or friendly when interacting with other species. On their homeworld, their population is small enough to survive as nomadic groups of hunters, similar to their Rodian ancestors, and they succeed against fierce predators despite relatively minimal technology. Their government is handled by annual meetings between clans, although recent Imperial involvement has changed that somewhat. A small percentage of Frenk resist the Empire, but their primitive lifestyle has meant that most are unaffected by it.
csg_frenk.language: Frenk mostly speak Fen, a dialect combining Rodese and Basic. Some learn to speak both tongues.
csg_frenk.homeworld: The world of Gorobei is a terrestrial planet full of jungles. Vicious predators of many sorts fill it, while a single spaceport provides technological imports and transit offworld, used mostly by Imperials as well as the occasional Frenk who wishes to take up a hunt in the wider galaxy.
csg_frenk.description: Frenk are green-skinned reptiles that show relations to Rodians. They are tall and thin, and many are exceptional athletes. Those seen away from their homeworld are almost always bounty hunters.
csg_frenk.sidebar_text: Frenk and Rodians share similar culture, a never forgotten link from their past. Long ago, a group of Rodians hired Arkanians to genetically modify their clan by creating a superior genome. The experiment succeeded to an extent, giving the new Rodians an ability to speak Basic and better abilities as athletes. However, their intelligence dropped marginally in result, causing the Arkanians to consider it a failure. When they attempted to terminate the “experiments,” their creations escaped offworld before crashing on the far-off planet Gorobei. Thought dead, they created a society of their own, becoming known as the Frenk before eventual rediscovery. While some maintain a friendly rivalry with the Rodians, many hold harsh feelings over their species being seen as a “failure.”
csg_frenk._provenance_note: The Frenk species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_frozian.name: Frozian
csg_frozian.physiology: Frozians are tall and thin humanoids with an extra joint on each of their limbs. Because of this, their range of motion is different than other species, and their method of walking is seen as very off-putting. Despite their extra joints, they are clumsier than most other species. They are covered in brownish fur, and they have very long, black whiskers which can resemble a mustache. They have a feline head with a snout that features a small mouth and an identifiable nose. They can move their nose and whiskers at will when they create facial expressions. They have wide, brown eyes which have excellent peripheral vision and pointed fur at the back of their head.
csg_frozian.society: Frozians are strong-willed and moral. They are a kind and generous people, eager to give to those in need. They are also extremely diligent, working very hard and keeping their promises to the letter. Most of them are very intelligent and excel in technical work. This combination of integrity, charity, and tenacity makes them thrive in whatever societies they join. However, they have one trait that can make them very hard to befriend: Frozians are extremely pessimistic. Even though they don’t want to depress those around them, the melancholy outlook of a Frozian can sadden even the most optimistic of spirits. Many make a conscious effort to do otherwise when around non-Frozians, but few manage to succeed. Most enjoy the company of other species, and aside from their pessimism, they assimilate easily.
csg_frozian.language: Most Frozians speak Frozian, their native language. They also typically know another language from whichever society they integrate into. They have a tendency to repeat phrases for emphasis, a grammatical trend originating from Frozian.
csg_frozian.homeworld: Frozians come from the peaceful low-gravity planet of Froz, a world in the Corellian Sector with low gravity and unique flora that is necessary for them to breed. Years ago, it was decimated via Base Delta Zero, forcing the Frozians to disperse. Eventually, the New Republic will begin restoration efforts, and scientists will attempt to recreate Froz’s natural environment.
csg_frozian.description: Frozians are friendly and tenacious, but their charms are hindered by their extreme pessimism. They were one of the first species to resist the Empire, and their world was bombarded as a result. Infertile off of the homeworld, they now face extinction.
csg_frozian.sidebar_text: Frozians were one of the first people to defy the Empire, and many joined rebel movements. In response, the Moff governing their sector decided to bombard their planet from orbit, devastating all life on their planet. Immediately, almost all Frozians resorted to active resistance against the Empire, and almost all of them are now in the Rebel Alliance. However, the Frozians are infertile without the conditions on their homeworld, so the species' already slim population will only decrease. It is estimated that in about 100 years, they will all be dead. As is fitting for their personality, most have accepted their fate.

csg_galidyn.name: Galidyn

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain.

special_abilities.name: Sharp Teeth
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a crit rating of 3.

csg_galidyn.physiology: Galidyn are large but thin flying reptiles, ranging from two to five meters head to tail, and with a wingspan usually about twice their length. Their legs are thin, short, and too weak to walk with, so they must fly at all times. In combat, they often rely on their long tail or their needle-like proboscis, which is also lined with sharp teeth, and they are aided by their tough skin. Their head is thin, with a large eye on each side, and it ends in a pointed crest at the top. Their arms are attached to their massive wings, which make them relatively useless for grasping, and all four of their limbs have two digits. However, their appearance is actually far from the strangest thing about the Galidyn’s physiology. While they lay eggs like most reptiles, they only do so once per century, as their lifespan is massive: The oldest Galidyn currently is Ssseeeeseetek, who is about 4,000 years old.
csg_galidyn.society: While the Empire has made contact with the Galidyn’s planet, it is not aware of their presence, as the species is highly secretive and few in number, with only a few tens of thousands of them. Furthermore, their cities, which are only eight in number, are more than a kilometer underground, making them very hard to reach. The Galidyn are extremely technologically advanced as a race, and they educate their young well in all manners of science, linguistics and technology, such as medicine, cryptography, and aerodynamics. Children are only cared for by their immediate family for a short time before they are sent to a mentor for schooling. Once educated, they are allowed to join in their participatory government, which is headed by a single Steward in each of the cities. The oldest and most prominent Steward is Ssseeeeseetek. They enjoy debating and ideating, although in rare occasions, rogue Galidyn will have the desire to “go native” and survive by hunting. Either way, they are generally reclusive, hidden, and rarely keen to travel offworld, but they do often interrogate any offworlders who are seen on Fyodos, bringing them to a place called the Crater of Debate, where they are asked to explain their presence.
csg_galidyn.language: Galidyn are very well-educated and speak the same language as the Fyodoi, but they are fond of using such elaborate and archaic vocabulary that most of the humans can hardly understand them.
csg_galidyn.homeworld: Galidyn come from Fyodos, a far eastern Outer Rim world, which is also known as Tatrang IV. Galidyn live in underground cities powered by geothermal energy and grow large swaths of fungus, while primitive Fyodoi live on the mountains and plains above.
csg_galidyn.description: Galidyn are a long-lived species of thin reptiles with massive wings, and they live in hiding from both the Imperials and the now-primitive human colonists on their world called the Fyodoi. Their underground society is highly technologically advanced.
csg_galidyn.sidebar_text: While the Empire has only recently discovered Fyodos, they were not actually the first humans to arrive. It’s unknown where the first human colonists, called the Fyodoi, actually came from, as they had no recorded contact with the outside galaxy. In any case, these settlers did interact with the Galidyn, and the two collaborated well in a technologically advanced society up until recent centuries. Things changed when the Fyodoi started a war amongst themselves in 350 BBY called the Great Cleansing, which proved to be a devastating slaughter for everyone involved. Galidyn hid underground to flee the conflict, and then they hibernated for two centuries. While the Galidyn have forgiven the Fyodoi and are willing to make contact with their descendants, the feeling is no longer mutual. This is because in light of their war, the Fyodoi have become repulsed by the technology that ripped their society apart. They now live a primitive lifestyle, and they see the Galidyn as idolaters who are overly obsessed with their technology. Thus, the two species now mostly leave one another alone.

csg_gallaprixom.name: Gallaprixom

special_abilities.name: Stoic
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Convincing Demeanor.”

special_abilities.name: Poor Hearing
special_abilities.description: Add setback on auditory Perception checks, and may not hear ordinary speech from anyone beyond engaged range. May choose to spend 1,000 credits for cybernetic hearing implants to remove this penalty permanently, or 2,000 credits for advanced cybernetic hearing implants, which remove this penalty and also add boost on auditory Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Cyborgs
special_abilities.description: At character creation, gain up to 3 free cybernetic implants of up to 6,000 credits combined value. Additional credits at character creation may be used to increase the 6,000 credit cap. Have a cybernetic implant cap of 3+Brawn.

csg_gallaprixom.physiology: Gallaprixom are a sentient species that are rarely seen in their natural form, as most are quick to cover and modify themselves with cybernetic armor and implants. They are stockily built with broad shoulders and a wide stance, which makes them somewhat ungainly, though this can often be altered via cybernetics. However, the real reason that the Gallaprixom first got into cybernetics was actually to improve their poor hearing, which made it difficult for them to communicate as they started to enter the wider galaxy. Once they started with that, they just couldn’t stop upgrading themselves, to the point that they see the peak of privilege as being able to rid themselves of all organic parts except the brain, which is otherwise in their chest. Thus, it is not uncommon for Gallaprixom to even remove their head. Some don’t even replace it, instead putting photoreceptors and audioreceptors on other parts of their body. For those who can’t afford such advanced implants, many wear metal armor to cover up their organic nature, which is naturally yellow-skinned with no neck, a short bald head, undersized ears, and a wide mouth. On the other hand, the richest often purchase multiple modular cybernetics so that they can swap out limbs or even entire bodies.
csg_gallaprixom.society: Gallaprixom are technologically gifted not only in cybernetics, but also in the design and manufacture of droids and other devices, which has allowed them to find work on many worlds. However, they struggle to get along with other sentients, even when they can hear them, as they are generally humorless, overly pedantic, and emotionally detached. On the other hand, their coldness and inexpressiveness can help them to excel in criminal occupations, so they are not an uncommon sight as mob bosses. Because of their logical mentality, they generally make well-organized but inflexible managers of such operations.
csg_gallaprixom.language: Speech does not come naturally to the Gallaprixom because of their poor hearing, so their native languages are actually sign languages. Although many now have hearing implants to let them listen to Basic, they still tend to speak rarely and deliberately.
csg_gallaprixom.homeworld: Gallaprixom come from the high-gravity planet of Ord Gallapraxis in the southern Expansion Region. It is urban, somewhat frigid, and highly crime-ridden.
csg_gallaprixom.description: A silent species of yellow-skinned humanoids, the Gallaprixom are obsessed with technology design and almost always replace as much of their body as they can with cybernetic implants. They have poor hearing and generally communicate through sign language.
csg_gallaprixom.sidebar_text: While most Gallaprixom are content with just making cyborgs of themselves, a few of them want to share their gifts with others. On Niordi during the Clone Wars, one Gallaprixom named Tren Standian travelled to the war-torn Outer Rim world of Niorde, where he coordinated with the Niordi government to create an army of surgically-modified living weapons whose heads were replaced by cannons. He would get the attention of Republic officials in his time there and later be an advisor on the Dark Trooper project, supplying a few of his people as test subjects. But more horrifying was the criminal Dr. Bal Gandileen, a flame of Dr. Evazen who ran infamous experiments at a hidden lair on Poytta called the Singularity, where she would kidnap people and turn them into cyborgs.
csg_gallaprixom._provenance_note: Little is known about Feleen Bantillian’s species, including their name. The following information is almost entirely made up.

csg_gamorrean.name: Gamorrean
csg_gamorrean.physiology: Gamorreans are burly hogs with green or brown skin. They are similar to humans in height but weigh much more. Their mind is not advanced, and they are really only good at brutal melee… or so the stereotypes say. This isn’t all true, however. Many Gamorreans are indeed like this, but there are still exceptions. Some are more thin, similar to a human. (They are frowned upon and viewed as less than ideal.) Amongst the less warlike females, skin color can vary as well: black, brown, pink, yellow, and rarely white are all possible for them. They have two horns atop their head and sharp incisors on the lower jaw that tend to stick out. Their eyes are beady. Most notably about their face, however, is the nose. This snout, particularly hog-like, further enforces the “piggish” appearance. Their beady eyes are gold, brown, or black. Most are covered in parasitic bloodsuckers known as morrts. They actually show affection to these, viewing them as pets. They live to 45 years old, though their warlike way of living means that few males last that long.
csg_gamorrean.society: Gamorreans live in a clan based society, which is strictly divided by gender. The males, “boars,” simply fight. They devote their life to a constant cycle of training, going to war, and healing. The females, “sows,” do all of the productive work. This includes farming, hunting, manufacturing, and running businesses. Males are traded and switch between clans, while females stay in the same clan. Clans differ, but are mostly in double or sometimes triple digits. At birth, there are ten males to every female, but the males have such a short lifespan, making the number somewhat closer. Gamorreans call summer “wartime,” since it is when they fight. Fall, or “croptime,” sees the final skirmishes before they settle in for winter. In “coldtime,” they mostly stay in their homes as a family. Then spring, or “slushtime,” is for preparing for war, marrying, or giving birth.
csg_gamorrean.language: Gamorrese is a simple language that only Gamorreans can speak. Its runic alphabet is only known by sows. Gamorrreans cannot speak Basic.
csg_gamorrean.homeworld: Gamorreans come from Gamorr and have colonized Pzob. Procedure programs for visiting Gamorr consist of a single line: DO NOT VISIT GAMORR. It is average in climate and possesses diverse terrain. Prominent mushrooms are used as food.
csg_gamorrean.description: Brutal mammals related to pigs, Gamorreans focus their life on warfare. They are extremely violent and uncivilized, making interaction with other species difficult.
csg_gamorrean.sidebar_text: Gamorreans have strict beliefs about the combat that they so adore. They refuse to use ranged weapons in their wars, viewing them as insufficient for demonstrating their “boarness.” They still use them against outsiders or dishonored Gamorreans. However, wars are a game to them that has strict rules. They stick to their melee weapons or fists. They also strictly avoid the use of “magic,” which can include anything from the Force, stealth, or even superior tactics.

csg_gand.name: Gand

special_abilities.name: Lungless
special_abilities.description: Remove penalties for suffocation.

special_abilities.name: Ammonia Breathers
special_abilities.description: Need an ammonia mask to breathe in a normal environment. Oxygen is a dangerous atmosphere of rating 8.

special_abilities.name: Exoskeletons
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound. May also regrow lost limbs after a few months.

special_abilities.name: Rituals
special_abilities.description: Once per session when tracking a target, may make a hard Discipline check to meditate. If successful, receive a relevant (but ambiguous) vision.

csg_gand.physiology: Gand are an odd species of insectoids with almost a dozen varieties that puzzle xenobiologists. They are shorter than humans in size, typically have three fingers, and are covered in a brown, green, or purple protective exoskeleton. Whatever their exoskeleton cannot defend against, Gand can heal quickly, even regenerating limbs. Their face is dominated by a beak and large, silvery eyes which are sensitive in darker conditions while also perceiving ultraviolet light. Where Gand are most unique, however, is in their respiratory system: Most do not seem to need air at all, receiving everything they need from food and exhaling through their skin, emitting a musky odor of methane. Other subspecies have lungs and breathe ammonia, so they typically wear a respirator mask if they ever travel offworld.
csg_gand.society: Gand have a closed culture, just like their biology, so they are a mystery to everyone else. They are seen to be humble, soft spoken, and polite. This is because they rarely brag about themselves, but the Gand actually place achievement above all else and judge everyone by their feats. Religion, centered around the ammonia mists of their world, is prominent in their culture, and the Elders of Gand dispatch distinguished Gand called ruetsavii to observe the people. Gand have the name “Gand,” until a major accomplishment, as judged by the ruetsavii, allows them to use their family’s name. Further greatness, such as becoming a findsmen, allows them to use a first name. They live in small “pocket colonies'' that are ruled by a central government, and they also have a slave trade.
csg_gand.language: The clicking language of the Gand can really only be replicated by droids, and most Gand lack the vocal cords to speak Basic. Relying on mechanical translation devices, these Gand never use pronouns, since names carry such an important weight.
csg_gand.homeworld: Gand come from Gand, an Outer Rim world covered in ammonia and methane. It is closed to offworlders, and most trade is handled through space stations. Foreigners who are allowed on the surface almost always stay in the Alien Quarters, and only Gand of high standing are allowed to invite them.
csg_gand.description: One of the more distinctive species of insectoids in the galaxy, the Gand are a very mysterious species. Some have no lungs, while others breathe ammonia. They refer to themselves using their names, which they earn through accomplishments. Some have abilities that allow them to track targets via mysterious rituals.
csg_gand.sidebar_text: Gand culture is most well-known for the findsmen, a mystical sect of trackers. Some fight with electrified shockprod staffs or rarer Gand dischargers, and a few attack with sharp growths that sprout from their exoskeleton via genetic modifications or chemical baths. However, they are most known for looking in the strangest places for omens which can help them discover the location of the target. These bizarre rituals somehow work, which most consider to be a connection to the Force, even though the findsmen themselves claim otherwise. Recent importing of Imperial scanning technology has limited the need for findsmen, causing some to find offworld work.

csg_gank.name: Gank

special_abilities.name: Cyborgs
special_abilities.description: At character creation, gain up to 2 free cybernetic implants of up to 5,000 credits combined value. Additional credits at character creation may be used to increase the 5,000 credit cap. Have a cybernetic implant cap of 3+Brawn.

csg_gank.physiology: Ganks are a species of entirely cyborgs who augment their skills and physique with mechanical devices. In addition, they almost always cover their entire body in their traditional body armor. Those that see a Gank outside of his or her armor, which is very rare, will see a furry yellow body. Their head is squared-off and their mouth is almost in a frown or snarl. Their eyes, not far above the mouth, are small. Though short, they are heavy, with broad shoulders and thick limbs. The cybernetic implants also allow for silent communication with other Ganks.
csg_gank.society: Ganks are a brutal people with a reputation as such. Aside from the Ganks themselves, no one really knows much about the species. They almost all view battle and mercenary work as their calling in life and have no qualms about murdering anyone. This earns them the name “Gank Killers.” Few seem to object to it. They can be violent as a result of any perceived or real insult, although they can get along better with employers. Even for those who successfully approach a Gank, they are cold and mysterious. They have a taboo against exposed flesh and entirely cover themselves in armor. Although they almost always travel in packs, evidence of a society or leader remains yet to be seen.
csg_gank.language: Since Ganks can communicate silently, the nature of their language remains yet another mystery. They can understand and speak Basic, however, if they need to get a point across.
csg_gank.homeworld: The original Gank homeworld is unknown, but they came to Nar Shaddaa and made it their homeworld. Nar Shaddaa is the Hutt-controlled moon of Nal Hutta, covered in cities that house all sorts of illicit activities. They seem to live with their Hutt crime lord employers, or they may be nomadic entirely. Such mysteries, just like the others, can only be answered by the Gank Killers themselves.
csg_gank.description: A violent and serious species typically devoted to mercenary work, the Ganks are prominent in Hutt Spaces as thugs and hired guns. They are covered in cybernetics and armor, so they give off a mysterious and almost droid-like aura.
csg_gank.sidebar_text: The use of Ganks as bodyguards by Neimoidians is one of the few notable cases in history in which the Bounty Hunter’s Guild did not maintain complete control of the field. Such is not the only notable feat by the Ganks in mercenary fields. Their overall history as hitmen, enforcers, and mercenaries is well known, and they have good relations with many Hutt crime lords. Their abilities seem far superior to that of any competition. The Hutt relations, as well as their overall nature, makes them seen as immoral and low-class to most citizens of the galaxy. For this, or perhaps some other unknown reason, they organized, fought, and lost in a war against the Republic over 5,000 years ago.

csg_gendai.name: Gen’Dai

special_abilities.name: Decentralized Organs
special_abilities.description: Receive 2 ranks in the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Advanced Nervous System
special_abilities.description: May make tactile Perception checks from up to Long range as if Engaged. Difficulty to perceive the subject is upgraded once per range band of distance.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: Recover 1 wound per round or minute at all times, and may attempt to heal critical injuries once at the end of each encounter or once per 2 hours minimum. When healing the “Maimed” injury, reattach the limb.

csg_gendai.physiology: A boneless species, the Gen'Dai are virtually a formless jumble of corded muscle and nerve bundles. Because of this, they typically inhabit heavy armor made for humanoids to give themselves a form to pass as any number of species in the galaxy. The only distinct part of a Gen’Dai is their head, which is typically bald, has two eyes, nose slits, and a mouth full of razor-sharp fangs. Gen’Dai also have two large, wing-like ears, but they are usually folded below their jawlines to hide distinguishing features. Gen’Dai are completely void of vital organs, allowing them to survive injuries unthinkable for other species, giving them a reputation of being virtually immortal. The Gen’Dai also have a decentralized nervous system, giving them near-instantaneous reflexes. This also allows them to function after sustaining heavy injuries and to have an absurd sense of touch: For example, they can feel a human heartbeat from up to 200 meters away. The only known way to kill a Gen’Dai is to atomize their body all at once.
csg_gendai.society: The Gen’Dai are a peaceful people who practice a philosophy of “perfection of permanence,” meaning that all change is an illusion. This leads philosophers from their species to preach that taking an active role in anything is pointless and detrimental. Since their homeworld’s destruction long ago, the species has taken to a nomadic lifestyle, journeying the stars in isolation.
csg_gendai.language: The Gen’Dai speak their own native language of Gen’Dai. As they are an ancient species, each living 4,000 to 7,000 years, they have a low birth rate and population. Thus, Gen’Dai is rarely used and has been all but forgotten, and most know Basic.
csg_gendai.homeworld: The homeworld of the Gen’Dai was razed long ago by the Sith Empire, leading the race to their current nomadic lifestyle. While the planet still exists, no one knows where it is, and it is unlikely that it could support life, even if it were to be rediscovered.
csg_gendai.description: A boneless species with no centralized organs, the Gen'Dai can live for millennia and heal from almost any injury almost instantly. Although they are peaceful by nature, their mind degrades before their body does, sometimes making their eldest members psychotic.
csg_gendai.sidebar_text: Despite all their durability, the regeneration abilities of the Gen’Dai do not extend to their mind, which deteriorates over time. This psychosis leads to older members of the species becoming extremely violent. These members of the species often take jobs as mercenaries or bounty hunters, giving the species as a whole an image of savagery to the wider public.

csg_geonosian.name: Geonosian

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

csg_geonosian.physiology: Geonosians are tough insectoids who are only partially sentient. In many ways, they are a conundrum. While they are barely intelligent enough to manage sentience, the Workers are excellent in mechanics. They are thinner than most other sentients, but the Soldiers are surprisingly strong. Even the Nobles are devious despite their lack of complete sentience. The Nobles and Soldiers have wings, while the drones do not. Most other traits are more uniform across castes: hard, brown skin, three fingers and toes on each hand and foot, and double-kneed legs. Their hairless head points down and forward, and their eyes are red.
csg_geonosian.society: Geonosian society is best defined by its caste system: A majority are Worker drones, who live in poverty as slaves for the projects of the Nobles. Though the Soldiers receive a higher status, they are still nevertheless put in dangerous conditions and fight in wars that they have no stake in. The Nobles control all and are typically selfish in nature. Differences in psychology are notable between castes. Workers are not typically ambitious; they only do what they’re told to. Soldiers are just the opposite and can be very competitive. All of them have little value for life, and ritual combat is important as entertainment. Some lucky lower-class ones can even acquire a higher status by winning as a gladiator. They are not very friendly towards other species and don’t trust them. Most also prefer to stay on their homeworld amongst their own people.
csg_geonosian.language: Geonosians speak Geonosian, a clicking tongue. Although all Geonosians are capable of speaking Basic, only Nobles are likely to learn it.
csg_geonosian.homeworld: An Outer Rim world near Tatooine, Geonosis is a dry, dusty planet of red rock. It is plagued by radiation, so most Geonosians live underground or in stone buildings. It is, of course, the site of the first battle in the Clone Wars, where the Republic took over Geonosian factories. While it used to be successful in the business of arms manufacturing, association with the Separatists has ruined its reputation. The planet is also surrounded by an asteroid belt.
csg_geonosian.description: Geonosians are flying insectoids notable for helping the Separatists in the Clone Wars. They enjoy violence, but a majority of the Geonosians are worker drones whom the nobles use for manufacturing.
csg_geonosian.sidebar_text: The bold move of aligning with the Confederacy cost the Geonosians. Losers in the war, they are now not on very good terms with the Empire. While Geonosian Nobles remain rulers, many others are now slaves to the Empire. The handful of revolts have been quickly put down.

csg_geranite.name: Geranite

special_abilities.name: Atmospheric Requirement
special_abilities.description: Require a mask supplying trace amounts of hydron-3 to survive in a normal environment. The mask must be supplied with a canister of hydron-3 daily, which has Rarity 2, Encumbrance 0, and costs 50 credits. If deprived of hydron-3, begin to suffocate after 1 hour.

csg_geranite.physiology: Geranites are near-humans distinguished by their skin’s bluish or pinkish tint, and they tend to have darker hair. They have five digits on their hands and feet and fairly standard proportions. However, there is a key difference between them and humans in that they require a gas called hydron-3 to survive. In a standard atmosphere, they typically wear a helmet which supplies them with the gas, although they can go without it for short periods of time.
csg_geranite.society: Geranites tend to be a very disciplined species, rarely giving into their emotions or short-term desires, which makes them well-suited to work as soldiers, hunters, or mercenaries. They tend to be very formal, direct, and almost robotic in social situations, and they prefer solitude. Many find this in the outdoors, where they are most at home. The deities whom the Geranites worship, called the Sky Seraphs, further enforce this tendency. The Sky Seraphs are believed to have created the natural world, and they conclude that man-made indoor spaces like buildings and starships are therefore less holy. To occasionally fly on starships or have a job that requires being indoors is by no means forbidden, but there is a strong expectation that if given the choice, Geranites should experience the outdoors. The religious fervor also tends to make them honest and trustworthy. They are a very grateful people, never forgetting what others have done for them, and they usually express thankfulness with actions rather than words.
csg_geranite.language: There are two major languages on Geran, Ellist in the west and Byakt in the east. Most Geranites also learn Basic, although their voice is typically distorted by their breath mask.
csg_geranite.homeworld: Geranites come from Geran, a temperate Outer Rim world with an atmosphere containing hydron-3, which is not toxic to other species. It has a small axial tilt, and they live near its lush equator, so seasonal variations are minimal. This allows them to have many open air constructions, and their towns are not particularly dense, leaving room for parks and forests.
csg_geranite.description: Due to their unique atmospheric requirement of hydron-3, the Geranites must almost always obscure their near-human form beneath a helmet. They are disciplined, formal, and highly religious, which emphasizes the importance of the outdoors.
csg_geranite.sidebar_text: Although Geranites are typically not ones to draw attention to themselves, some do end up in the spotlight due to their sport of Otil, which has garnered interest from throughout the Outer Rim. It is of huge significance to Geranite politics, as all 35 nations on their homeworld have a government-sponsored team, and traditionally, these nations would resolve disputes and formulate trade agreements based on the results. Increasingly, governments find it silly to decide their economic fate over Otil, but there are still many nations who continue to uphold this tradition. In any case, it is hugely successful as a business, as many games see billions of spectators tune in over the HoloNet. It is extremely complex, with three teams, each having thirteen players, four balls, and five goals to defend. At its core, teams try to carry balls into their opponent’s goals, but they are governed by a system of wagers which limit where offensive and defensive are allowed to go and how many points are awarded.
csg_geranite._provenance_note: The Geranite species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_gigoran.name: Gigoran

special_abilities.name: Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_gigoran.physiology: Gigorans possess enough intelligence to match that of many sentients, although they still are very primitive in their technology. They are large, furred creatures with white fur. They have a wide mouth, pig-like nose, and tiny eyes. They have three-toed feet and four-fingered hands which have claws on both. They are strong enough to be excellent for combat or physical labor.
csg_gigoran.society: Gigorans are very family-oriented, and most are more than willing to sacrifice for their relatives. Though they have a very fierce appearance, they are actually quite peaceful. Though dangerous as predators, they are kind and docile when with other sentients. Gigorans are arranged into groups called home-clans, which are tribes of hunter-gatherer nomads who live in caves. They further organize themselves into smaller family groups.
csg_gigoran.language: Gigorans who are taken offworld learn Basic fairly quickly. While they are capable of speaking it, they still prefer to use their native language of grunts when they can.
csg_gigoran.homeworld: Gigorans come from the snowy planet of Gigor, an Outer Rim world. Its only sentient inhabitants are Gigorans. They live a primitive lifestyle, using stone-age technology to hunt through the mountains and caves.
csg_gigoran.description: Furry primitives from the snowy world of Gigor, almost all Gigorans who leave their homeworld do so as slaves. Unlike the short-tempered Wookiees, their nonviolence makes them easier to control.
csg_gigoran.sidebar_text: Tragically, their lack of technology and weak wills have made Gigorans easy prey for slavers. Their natural strength makes them quite valuable as well. This mostly occurs in the Mytaranor sector, which also includes Kashyyyk, the Wookiee homeworld. (Another large and furry slave species) Almost all of the Gigorans seen off of their homeworld are escaped slaves or current slaves. Those that escape are often on the run from bounty hunters. Many still live in peace on their homeworld, but more and more are also forced to leave their homeworld each day. Because of their size, Gigorans are effective fighters. Many fight to end the slavery of their people, while others hope to end slavery galaxy-wide by joining the Rebel Alliance.

csg_givin.name: Givin

special_abilities.name: Exoskeletons
special_abilities.description: Do not take wound or strain damage due to vacuum, unbreathable atmosphere, or abnormal air pressure.

csg_givin.physiology: Givin are covered in a bony exoskeleton that is chalk-white and bears striking similarities to the human bone structure, meaning that Givin can appear to be very creepy for many humans. They have triangular eye sockets and a mouth that appears as a permanent frown, and their strangely alien gait somewhat resembles a string puppet. But beneath this odd aesthetic is a brilliant mind with incredible mathematical aptitude, which the Givin developed to predict the harsh tides and sudden air pressure changes caused by the rapid orbits of their world’s three moons. But constant fleeing from danger proved challenging, so the Givins’ exoskeleton also gained the ability to seal itself off, allowing them to even survive total vacuum or other conditions involving air pressure and poisonous atmospheres. In order to maintain these advantages, they need to eat three times as much as humans. They are similar to humans in height and have five-fingered hands and three-toed feet.
csg_givin.society: The highly intelligent Givin are a deeply religious people whose faith is centered around mathematics. They study to earn entrance into monasteries, and their best mathematicians become priests who have the responsibility of predicting the weather. They are governed by the “Body Calculus,” a group of Factors, and planetary governor who is determined by a contest that requires calculating multidimensional differentials. All their leaders then make decisions based on null-modal probability, and they often find alliances to be economically beneficial, even if their culture remains fairly isolated. Givin use their skills to build what they deem to be the best ships, spending ages designing them and often using them to run successful cargo transit companies. However, these starships are often incompatible with outsiders, as they lack pressurization systems or navicomputers, since the Givin need neither. They respect other shipbuilding species, like Duros and Verpine, but they can stand organic Mon Calamari design and have a subtle arrogance toward anyone who cannot survive in a vacuum.
csg_givin.language: Givin speak the language of Givin, though many know Basic. Its written form includes mathematical symbols and requires a knowledge of calculus to read.
csg_givin.description: Math is the cornerstone of Givin society. They are very logical and intelligent, even if their skeleton-like facial features are very unnerving to some. Their homeworld, Yag'Dhul, is prone to sudden loss of air, so they can survive in a vacuum.
csg_givin.sidebar_text: Givin apply math even in their greetings, which is traditionally a simple quadratic. Even though these roots are often rational, some outsiders cannot find them in their heads, so Givin often look down on them. When meeting new people for the first time, they are more likely to employ more advanced questions to gauge the stranger’s knowledge.

csg_glymphid.name: Glymphid

special_abilities.name: Savvy Underworlders
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Plausible Deniability.”

csg_glymphid.physiology: Glymphids are lanky reptilians with unique proportions. Averaging around a meter and a third in height, they have very short legs and long arms, and their long neck leads to a mouth with a flat snout. This long snout has nostrils on top and is flanked by two large red eyes. Glymphids have tiny feet, but their hands are long and have fingers which end in suction cups. Their skinny neck has two flaps of flesh extending from either side, and they have occasional black spots on their scaly skin. The rest of their scales vary in color between shades of yellow or tan on their stomach and turquoise blue on their back, and they typically do not wear any clothing.
csg_glymphid.society: Glymphids are sly creatures who value making plans and seeing them through. While they can have criminal tendencies, they are typically very measured, setting aside their violent ways if it won’t benefit them or if the danger is too great. The only time they attack out of emotion is when Fluggrians are involved, a species with whom they have a longstanding rivalry. Although they can come across as cowardly, they still have a strong military tradition, as they believe that a well-organized fighting force is needed to protect their interests. They have no qualms about using violence, intimidation, or deception to get what they want.
csg_glymphid.language: Glymphids have a number of native languages depending on region, so they have adapted Basic as a lingua franca even among their own.
csg_glymphid.homeworld: Glymphids come from Ploo II, a planet in the northern Expansion Region, which is in the same system as Ploo IV, the Fluggrian homeworld. Glymphids live in coastal wetlands, where they have built compact multi-level cities that often require crawling.
csg_glymphid.description: A spindly species of reptiles with a long snout, the Glymphids are sly and untrustworthy, though they place importance in restraint even in their criminal occupations. They make an exception for this when it comes to their bitter rivals, the Fluggrians.
csg_glymphid.sidebar_text: For generations, the Glymphids have been at war with their neighbors, the Fluggrians, a squat species of swamp-dwelling amphibians. Tensions run deep between the two, and no Glymphid or Fluggrian would ever willingly work with one another. Both species are prone to criminal activity and will often try to assassinate one another if they encounter them offworld. However, what was once a stalemate took a dramatic turn during the Clone Wars, when the Fluggrians seceded. Naturally, Glymphids remained loyal to the Republic in response, and ultimately their loyalty was paid off when the Grand Army seized the Fluggrian homeworld during the war’s final year. The Empire demanded reparations from the Fluggrians and placed corrupt Glymphids in power over their former rivals. This turned out bad for nearly everyone involved, as the extremely sadistic Glymphid-run government was more concerned with tormenting and murdering the Fluggrians than getting any productive labor out of them. The Empire has since installed a new government with leaders from other worlds, and some of the Glymphids were even charged with crimes. Meanwhile, the Empire has forced the Glymphids to demilitarize. At least two years of military service was once a requirement for all males, but this is no longer the case, and many Glymphid veterans despise the younger generations who have not been to war. Such veterans now point to the Rebel Alliance (which, of course, has been freeing Fluggrians) as an enemy they must now defeat. Their economy has also struggled to adapt to peacetime, and they have entered into a recession.
csg_glymphid._provenance_note: The Glymphid species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_gorax.name: Gorax

special_abilities.name: Incredible Power
special_abilities.description: Receive 2 ranks in the talent “Feral Strength.”

special_abilities.name: Nocturnal
special_abilities.description: Add boost on auditory Perception checks, add setback on visual Perception checks. In very bright conditions, add setback on all checks.

csg_gorax.physiology: Gorax are immense humanoids which span from 6 to 30 meters tall. Their thick matted fur can manifest as black, brown, or gray. Inexplicably, some Gorax have hoof-like feet, while others have long toes, and either a long, narrow heel, or a backward-pointing fourth toe.  Their hairless face is defined by a protruding lower jaw full of teeth. While their teeth and stomach support them being omnivorous, they generally prefer to eat meat.
csg_gorax.society: Gorax may be extremely strong, but their intelligence is limited, and they only show the beginnings of developing sentience. They have begun to use basic stone tools and weapons, build very basic structures in their cave homes, and adopt pets they find endearing. Despite this, they have yet to form any prominent communities or societies, preferring instead to keep their own solitary patrols of territory in which they hunt.
csg_gorax.language: Gorax cannot speak any languages other than the animalistic grunts and growls that allow them to get basic ideas across to one another.
csg_gorax.homeworld: It’s unknown exactly where Gorax come from, but there are two leading theories. Some believe they are native to Endor despite having a population of approximately twenty. Others believe they crash-landed on the moon along with Phlogs, and that the two share a homeworld. Until they join the galaxy at large, no one can know for sure. The Forest Moon of Endor is shared with several other sentient species, including native Yuzzums and Ewoks. Later, it will be host to the construction of the Second Death Star, a major battle in the Galactic Civil War, and the death of Emperor Palpatine. The star system is currently backwater, obscure, and rarely traveled to by other sentients. Nearby astronomical hazards ensure that passing ships are highly likely to crash, which has given Endor its wide variety of immigrated species.
csg_gorax.description: Gorax are barely sentient predators from the Forest Moon of Endor, where they use their massive size to torment a variety of prey. While they have not developed language, many have managed tool use, and they often keep pets for themselves.
csg_gorax.sidebar_text: Gorax are undisputed as the most powerful predators of Endor’s forests, and although they are extremely rare, they are highly dangerous if encountered. However, they do not just kill everything they see, as they are known to sometimes take victims as pets. Young boar-wolves in particular they will raise as their own after killing the mother, and once the baby matures, Gorax use the boar-wolves to help hunt. Ewoks they will also take as prisoners, keeping them in hanging cages in their lairs.

csg_gormak.name: Gormak

special_abilities.name: Technical Sophistication
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Gearhead.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_gormak.physiology: The Gormak are green-skinned humanoids with no nose or hair. Their most unique visual feature is their frills, which line the sides of their head, just above the ears. They have clawed, three-fingered hands, making them formidable fighters. They have red, orange, or blue eyes, and males have a pattern of small concentric circles between their eyes.
csg_gormak.society: Gormak are a unique society in that they are culturally very primitive, but they excel with technology. Despite their inability to achieve space travel, the Gormak are among the best in the galaxy at building, modifying, and scavenging technology.
