They are often miners, taking advantage of the many valuable minerals on their world to build technology. Gormak live in camps of small tribes, typically as nomads. Each clan is ruled by a Shaman, who is chosen based on technical skills. They excel with cybernetics, which they typically test on trapped animals, turning them into cyberbeast. Gormak are extremely competitive and hostile, often resorting to warfare or combat to solve their problems.
csg_gormak.language: Gormak have a simple native language called Gormak, and very few of them know Basic.
csg_gormak.homeworld: Gormak come from Voss, a mining planet in the Tion Cluster. It has a rocky landscape with a few forests and a hazy, yellow sky. During their war against the Voss, they were mostly found in the Gormak Lands. Their largest settlement of Gorma-Koss, a mountainside city with about 10,000 Gormak ruled by their King, Jokull.
csg_gormak.description: Technologically advanced nomads, the Gormak were at one point the sworn enemies of the Voss, but millennia ago, the two species put aside their differences to fight off the Sith Eternal Empire. They have green skin and frills on the sides of their head.
csg_gormak.sidebar_text: The Gormak are suspicious of all outsiders, but they were especially hateful of the Voss, their distant ancestors. In the time of the Old Republic, the Gormak were at war with the Voss, and they viewed the Voss as an abomination that needed to be destroyed if their species were to prosper. Although they outnumbered the Voss, the Voss have many Force-sensitive prophets, which granted the Voss the edge they needed to survive. Although the Voss defended themselves well, it was prophesied that the Voss would all die if the Gormak became extinct, so the Voss were never too aggressive. Foresight allowed the Voss to fight off the Sith Empire, forcing both the Empire and the Republic to fight against the Gormak in order to earn the Voss’s favor. However, when the Eternal Empire took over the Voss system, the only way for the Gormak to survive was to forget their long-standing hatred and ally with the Voss. Both species had heavy losses, but each survived, validating the Voss’s prophecy.

csg_gossam.name: Gossam
csg_gossam.physiology: Gossams are a diminutive reptilian species that reproduces by laying eggs, and they are a little over a meter tall with a thin build. They balance on their toes, of which they have three for each foot, just as they also have three-fingered hands. Their skin, coming in shades of turquoise and slate blue, has a ridged texture. They have gray hair, widely set yellow eyes, pointed ears, and no visible nose.
csg_gossam.society: Gossam society values appearance, reputation, and pleasing others. This is demonstrated prominently by their elaborate clothing, and their females also usually use fancy creams to sculpt their hair, pointing it back to form a cone-like shape that curves up at the end.  Young Gossam parents also show themselves off in how they handle their eggs. Though eggs require little practical care, there is strong tradition and social pressure to provide additional comforts, dressing them with elaborate nests of fine fabrics. Before they are hatched, the eggs get shown off at “egg parties,” where friends and relatives come to see. These ceremonies tend to be late in the incubation period, in hopes that the birth can be shown off as well. Gifts are given to the parents, especially if they have a high status. Credits matter a great deal to the Gossams, and they make for extremely shrewd businessmen. However, they are selfish and extremely dishonest, so they have a bit of a reputation for being untrustworthy. Things produced by Gossams tend to be extremely cheap for manufacturing. These flaws often prevent them ascending to positions of true power.
csg_gossam.language: Gossams speak Gossam, a croaking language. Due to their knack for business, most speak Basic as well. Gossam words and names tend to be short.
csg_gossam.homeworld: Gossams come from the urban, industrialized world of Castell. It is in the Colonies, a wealthy region of space, and sits on the Perlemian Trade Route. They also have colonized Felucia.
csg_gossam.description: The Gossams are small reptiles with blue-gray skin. They place extreme value in appearance and pleasing others. They were also very prominent in the Confederacy of Independent Systems, so they are now hunted by the Empire or live as slaves.
csg_gossam.sidebar_text: Though they tend to be independently minded, many Gossam once ended up working for the Commerce Guild. In the decades before the Clone Wars, it was the Commerce Guild who saved their world from a severe economic depression by buying out most of its land. Gossams were then typically locked into ten year contracts with the Guild, with their housing and food being provided as part of it. During the Clone Wars, the Commerce Guild was in strong favor of secession, but Castell was surrounded by Republic territories and soon retaken, and the Commerce Guild was dissolved at the end of the war. Amid the conflict, Gossams were banned from Coruscant, and those already on it were not warned. Thus, they became fugitives, forced to hide, smuggle themselves offworld, or rebel. While they once fought the Republic, many now fight the Empire under the banner of Whiplash. While independent from the Rebellion, this secretive organization has had great success rebelling from the Coruscant underworld. Others now fight the Empire from elsewhere, as the Empire has enslaved Castell and used its industries to support the Imperial Navy.

csg_gotal.name: Gotal

special_abilities.name: Energy Sensitivity
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as a maneuver, sense the presence and emotional state of everyone within short range. May use this ability to upgrade the difficulty twice when opposing a Deception check. When around droids or other electromagnetic radiation, but no more than four times per encounter, suffer 1 strain at the GM’s discretion.

csg_gotal.physiology: Gotals are burly humanoids that have evolved from hunter tribes on the plains of their homeworld. They are covered in coarse, dense fur, which can be brown, tan, or gray. Their beady red eyes are above average at handling dark conditions, but they have overall poor eyesight, and their tiny nostrils are just for breathing, as they cannot actually smell. However, all of their sensory deficiencies are more than made up for by the two conical horns on their heavily knobbed brows. These organs can detect electromagnetic waves and many other types of energy, and they act as the Gotals’ primary sense. For the most part, they can sense and read the feelings of any nearby life. This is useful for both hunting their equine prey and more easily understanding fellow sentients.
csg_gotal.society: Gotals used to live a nomadic lifestyle to avoid the unpredictable nature of their moon. Unable to plant crops, they hunted animals called quivry instead. Though they now have been able to form cities, many still honor the pastoralist lifestyle. Gotals are one the few species that have managed anarchy successfully, since their ability to read emotions gives them a natural empathy, and their ability to detect anger makes them naturally averse to conflict. Only a few rare Gotals have enough psychopathic tendencies to necessitate the use of their bare-bones court system. Most Gotals find love at first sight, and they make excellent parents, even though their children are highly temperamental due to sensory overload. Being bombarded by energies causes discomfort that takes time for them to learn to manage. Though their own starships are free of electromagnetic emissions, there are a litany of offworld technologies that they find uncomfortable, particularly droids. Eventually, a Gotal businessman will invent a very expensive cone sock which filters out unwanted radiation, making it easier for wealthy Gotals to travel. Those found offworld are highly coveted as hunters, although the Empire finds that they are prone to quickly empathizing too much with their targets. Others make good social workers or diplomats, and they’re good at gambling to the point of being banned from high-stakes tables.
csg_gotal.language: Gotals speak Antarian, a language that lacks words to describe emotion and relies on their ability to sense brain waves. When speaking Basic, they are very monotone and rarely use words to describe emotion.
csg_gotal.homeworld: Gotals come from Antar IV, one of the six moons that orbits the gas giant Antar. It is 60% water, and the mineral-rich land is mostly plains. It has a highly unpredictable climate because of its twin suns and orbit, and light level changes quickly with eclipses. Gotals are also prominent spacefarers, and they had colonized Antar’s other moons even prior to first contact with the Republic. Their system was very loyal to the Confederacy during the Clone Wars.
csg_gotal.description: The ability to sense emotions has had a major impact on Gotal culture. Their head-cones detect energy fields, which allow them to detect emotions but also make them vulnerable to other forms of electromagnetic radiation, which can cause discomfort. Though extremely empathetic, the idea of expressing emotions through speech is foreign to them.
csg_gotal.sidebar_text: One mildly Force-sensitive Gotal, after not getting into the Jedi Order, created the Antarian Rangers, who are now filled with members of many species, but still are based on Antar IV. This paramilitary organization was volunteer funded to assist the Jedi in logistics, exploration, combat, and funding. Now labelled co-conspirators with the Jedi, Antarian Rangers are almost extinct, with the remnant surviving in hiding.

csg_gran.name: Gran

special_abilities.name: Keen Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks from Perception checks. Remove 2 setbacks for concealment in combat.

csg_gran.physiology: Gran are three-eyed creatures with leathery brown or tan skin. Their head is further defined by four upward-pointing appendages and small horns on the back instead of hair. They have a wide neck, large ears that droop down, and prominent nostrils. All three of their large-dark eyes protrude from their head and are superior to those of humans, seeing into the infrared spectrum as well. Especially among their own kind, they are very adept at detecting minute changes in physiology and understanding the moods of those among them. They have six-fingered hands and six toes on each foot, though some have malformities on their digits, which render them into outcasts. In terms of diet, Gran are grazing herbivores, using their two stomachs to methodically eat a variety of grasses.
csg_gran.society: All Gran have a community-based outlook, and on Kinyen, this goes to the point of socialism. They raise their children to do specific jobs, which means that Gran from Kinyen can have a very narrowly-focued education. Few find this to be an issue, and onky rare exceptions stray from their predestined path. It is difficult to rebel against their communities, however, as Gran also have deep psychological dependence on their family and friends. They prize long, deliberate meals with their fellows, spending much of the day slowly chewing on grasses together. This outlook goes back to their earliest history, when they lived in herds for safety. In modern times, the harshest punishment is exile, and leaving their kin behind forever is seen as a fate worse than death. Not having them for emotional support can drive them criminally insane. Other species find them very chatty, often in a pleasant way, though some find their insistence on pacifism to be somewhat annoying. Gran on Kinyen are almost entirely followers of the Doellinist religion, which forbids not only violence, but also addictions to gambling, liquor or spice. Despite its prominence, most Gran view its creation account as metaphorical.
csg_gran.language: Gran typically are good linguists, learning Gran, Basic and any other language that their travels necessitate.
csg_gran.homeworld: The Gran are scattered throughout the southwestern parts of the galaxy. Their homeworld, Kinyen, is the Western Reaches of the Expansion Region. On it, they have built colorful cities which delight their keen sense of sight, and it features silvergrass, their favorite food. Malastare, a high-gravity Mid Rim world, is their largest colony and has a strong fuel industry. Other colonies include Hok, a tidally locked planet in the Slice where various crystals are mined, and Fenis II, a rainforest planet known for its manufacture of pharmaceuticals.
csg_gran.description: Gran are social and community-oriented herbivores best distinguished by their three eyes. They are very often colonists, abiding on many planets. Though the Gran on Kinyen are socialist, those on other planets sometimes demonstrate more racist or aggressive tendencies.
csg_gran.sidebar_text: The Gran possess a combination of adaptability and curiosity that makes them excellent colonists. These new settlements usually start off as microcosms of Kinyen, but they rarely stay that way as colonists adapt to their new surroundings. For example, on Malastare, conflicts with the native Dugs rendered the Gran more shrewd and conniving. Dugs, who saw Gran as invaders, once went to war, which the Gran won through their superior political influence. With the Republic on their side, they turned the Dugs into slaves and second-class citizens. The Gran on Kinyen find this abhorrent and essentially consider the less benevolent Gran of Malastare to be a different species culturally. About a millennium ago, Kinyen began to cut itself off from its colonies, limiting emigration and isolating visitors. As such, colonies such as Hok, Fenis II, and Malastare now diverge even further.

csg_gree.name: Gree

special_abilities.name: Atmospheric Requirement
special_abilities.description: Need a breath mask to breathe in a normal environment. Oxygen is a dangerous atmosphere of rating 3.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_gree.physiology: A very alien species of gray-skinned cephalopods, the Gree have six tentacles instead of limbs. Four are used as manipulators, while two drag along the ground for locomotion. Because of this structure, they are much shorter than humans, generally about one meter tall. Gree breath a Type II atmosphere and require a spongy breath mask to survive in a normal atmosphere, and they have no visible mouth. They instead communicate by releasing sounds through the fleshy folds under their gray eyes. Above their eyes is a tall, sloping forehead, and they have a drooping sac behind their head that stores some of their brain.
csg_gree.society: At the zenith of Gree society, there were four castes: Administrators, Crafters, Operators, and Researchers, each distinguished forehead tattoos, but only the Operators, who use but do not create technology, remain. As such, their technological knowledge has plateaued. The Operator caste is subdivided into guilds, which Gree are also born into. Their society has been redefined into a hierarchy: At the top are the grandmasters, the most wealthy and powerful Gree, who are recognized as being highly skilled. Guildmasters rule local guilds, which are then composed of masters. Masters have the most direct control over technology, so the masses, referred to as lesser Gree, are almost mindless and must perform menial labor for a master in order to earn food or shelter. Before a Gree can become a master, they must learn as an apprentice and then become a senior assistant, but most lack the drive or attention span to do this and simply remain in the masses. Being an apprentice is very difficult, as most masters hoard their knowledge, which is why so much of the best Gree technology has been forgotten. Traders facilitate negotiations between masters and other species, and although they are looked down upon as members of the masses, they perform a vital role.
csg_gree.language: The Gree language, Gree, is a strange tongue in that it is based almost entirely on combinations of colors and shapes that have secondary metaphorical meanings in addition to their literal definitions.
csg_gree.homeworld: Gree have isolated themselves in a northern part of the Outer Rim called the Gree Enclave, which contains their homeworld, Gree, as well as Asation, Licha In, Lonatro, Malanose, and Te Hasa. They allow few visitors and are known to almost no one. Some Gree use large vessels such as the Rokak’k Baran as mobile cities that travel within the Enclave.
csg_gree.description: Once a great species, cephalopods called the Gree had some of the most advanced technology the galaxy had ever seen. However, no one, including the Gree themselves, knows how to properly use it anymore, and the species has become isolated and forgotten.
csg_gree.sidebar_text: Although Gree are still a technologically skilled people, their society and their technology most flourished 100,000 years ago, an era they refer to as “the most ancient and forgotten days.” At this time, they were far more technologically advanced than even modern society, but they have since forgotten their past secrets of highly advanced navigation devices, dimensional engineering, terraforming, and quanta-technology. They were heavily reliant on droids, especially for military roles, but their version of droid technology was unique, and they have a distaste for modern droids. Gree technology has a unique philosophy in that their devices are “played” similarly to musical instruments. In fact, they often create music in addition to their primary function. Gree technology is therefore very alien to outsiders, just as their own ancient technology is alien to them.

csg_gungan.name: Gungan

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove penalties for underwater movement. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: High Jump
special_abilities.description: Able to jump very high or far. Once per round as a maneuver, suffer 3 strain to move 2 range bands either vertically or horizontally.

csg_gungan.physiology: Most Gungans are the lighter and orange Otalla; some are the bulkier and green Ankura. As amphibians, both subspecies start as tadpoles before developing the ability to go on land. Their strong legs are adept at running, swimming, and jumping, and they have cartilage instead of bones, which makes them very flexible. The Otalla have haillu, which act as earlobes, but are long and fin-like. Haillu are among many tools that Otalla Gungans use for expression, as well as flaring nostrils, a wide mouth on their bill, and yellow eyestalks that are partially retractable. Though Ankura have a more humanoid facial structure, they are equally expressive. Both also have a long tongue, which they use to catch insects, and their strong teeth help with eating shellfish and smaller amphibians. While hairless, some grow whisker-like tendrils with age. They have four fingers and three toes. Although they have compound lungs that can breathe underwater, they can also hold their breath for longer than most if needed. Because they are suited to the swamps, they are not well-adapted for any dry places, where their skin dries quickly.
csg_gungan.society: Gungans are reverent toward nature, so although they have advanced technology including unique shields that allow them to make bubble domes in their cities, they generally seek to minimize its role. Though they can be generous and peaceful in some contexts, their law is very harsh in punishing. In addition to caning or stoning for even fairly minor crimes, Gungans can be exiled, and it is difficult to return unless one achieves great deeds in order to undo the punishment. They have many gods which can have an effect on their life, and these gods enforce any life-debts that they fall into. Their lifestyle is sedentary, but they still are mostly hunter-gatherers in the swamps. They can be very hospitable, but they are suspicious of other species until trust is established. They take pride in their military might, particularly the warriors who fight on kaadu. Entire schools are devoted to teaching mounting combat, and Gungan officers treat their animals as family.
csg_gungan.language: Gungans speak Gunganese, but they learn a pidgin of Basic that they speak around outsiders. It is different enough to make them sound unintelligent, but still similar enough to be understood by most.
csg_gungan.homeworld: The Gungan home of Naboo is a water world in the Mid Rim. It is most notable for being the homeworld of Palpatine and the place of a protest by the Trade Federation that led to his election as Chancellor. The Gungans also colonized Naboo’s moon Ohma-D’un, but this settlement was wiped out in the Clone Wars.
csg_gungan.description: Gungans are reverent for nature and relatively primitive. They come from Naboo, the homeworld of Emperor Palpatine. They are amphibians, so most of their cities are underwater.
csg_gungan.sidebar_text: Gungans share their homeworld with the human colonists on Naboo, who have avoided them even though the two have no record of conflict against each other. For their part, the Gungans also chose to stay very isolated by hiding underwater. While the two cultures made progress reconciling after the Naboo Crisis in the waning days of the Republic, the Imperial presence now on Naboo has made the Gungans once again hide themselves. Though most have never met a human, they see them as cowardly, and humans imagine the Gungans to be barbaric.

csg_gupin.name: Gupin

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: If carried encumbrance is below encumbrance threshold by at least 2, can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

special_abilities.name: Gupin Powers
special_abilities.description: May shapeshift into creatures that cooperative engaged characters are thinking of. Shapeshifting requires those imagining to pass a number of consecutive successful Discipline checks equal to the creature’s silhouette. These checks may be done in succession by one person who imagines or distributed between multiple people who are imagining. Performing this check uses the character’s entire turn. May increase the number of checks required by 1 to gain the Claws or Aquatic ability, and may increase it by 3 to gain +1 to any characteristic. When increasing silhouette, gain +7 encumbrance threshold per 1 silhouette. After those imagining have finished, the Gupin may spend an action to shape-shift. They revert back to normal form at the end of the encounter or sooner if desired.

csg_gupin.physiology: Gupins are small furry humanoids that come in a variety of colors, though most often their fur tends to be a mixture of two colors: a warm color such as orange or tan for their head and a cooler color such as blue or dark purple for their body. Once a Gupin reaches adulthood, they also develop the ability to manifest wings on their normal form, allowing them to fly short distances. Gupins also have the notable ability to shapeshift, but they are limited to forms that those around them are concentrating on. When shapeshifting, they gain the traits of their new form, but they retain their blue and orange fur.
csg_gupin.society: Gupins are a social people, as they need to work together to allow for their abilities to manifest. Because of this, they are well known for their festivals and celebrations in which they make a point to get to know any strangers they come across. These festivals seem like planned holidays to outsiders, but in reality, Gupins only celebrate one holiday and find the idea of planned celebrations strange. They simply celebrate when their society feels they have something to celebrate, and because of this they are always prepared to have a celebration.
csg_gupin.language: Gupins are capable of speaking Basic and typically learn it in addition to their native tongue, Elegsh.
csg_gupin.homeworld: Gupins are from a southeastern Outer Rim called Gupin. Gupin is an agrarian world of vast plains, and they are scattered across its surface in small villages.
csg_gupin.description: Gupin are small flying creatures that have a limited ability to shapeshift that depends on aid from those around them.
csg_gupin.sidebar_text: Gupins attribute their shapeshifting abilities to magic shared by their people. Each colony or city of Gupins is ruled by a king who possesses a special chest. Once a year, Gupins find their powers begin to ebb and fade, and they must return to their home to participate in the Renewal Ceremony. This ritual involves the current king attempting to open the magic chest with a magic key. If the chest opens, that king has been found worthy and shall rule another year, and all nearby Gupins have their abilities restored. If the chest does not open, any Gupin in attendance may attempt to open the chest. The first to succeed becomes the new king for the year. Legend has it that occasionally a hero will come along who can open the magic chest with no key at all. Researchers are still unaware if this ceremony has any real connection to their abilities or if the power loss is mostly placebo.
csg_gupin._provenance_note: The Gupin species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_hapan_human.name: Hapan Human

special_abilities.name: Manipulators
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

special_abilities.name: Nighttime Blindness
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for brightness, add setback for darkness.

csg_hapan_human.physiology: Hapans are a race of humans who have evolved two distinct traits. Their first is their beauty, which they are well-known for. Furthermore, they have very poor vision in the dark, because there is a great deal of starlight on their worlds.
csg_hapan_human.society: Hapans have a very hierarchical society, and they are capable of incredible cruelty to gain power. Assassination among nobility is common in order to advance, and their politics are incredibly cutthroat. As such, most Hapans are extremely paranoid. In their society, men are seen as inferior and unintelligent, with their value mostly restricted to breeding. Servants occupy the lowest tier, while farmers are above them, and businesswomen occupy a middle tier. The highest status belongs to the nobility, who are ruled by the Queen Mother. The Queen Mother is seen as almost god-like, and every noble house vies to gain power by offering one of their men as a consort to the Queen Mother. Oftentimes, noble families assassinate the Queen Mother or her offspring in order to get their preferred successor. Hapans can be incredibly haughty, viewing those of lower status as innately inferior. They value beauty and appearance, and they see physical deformities as worse than death. Hapans are a wealthy people who have built an isolationist society with a large, but mostly untested, military. They consider themselves pacifists, but they fiercely defend their territory from all outsiders. However, Hapans have actually had a peaceful relationship with the Empire, which has made no serious attempt to annex them, perhaps because Hapans are humans and dislike the Jedi. Their technology is unique, and although their turbolaser technology is poor, they have some unique inventions. The most notable is the Gun of Command, a weapon that generates an electromagnetic field which disables thought processes, rendering its victim confused and susceptible to manipulation. They also excel in making prosthetics.
csg_hapan_human.language: Hapans rarely know Basic because of their isolation, and they typically speak their native tongue, Hapan.
csg_hapan_human.homeworld: Hapans come from the isolated Hapes Cluster in the Transitory Mists, and hyperspace travel entering or leaving the Cluster is difficult. Their capital is on the planet Hapes, a temperate, urban planet. The cluster is densely packed with hundreds of stars, meaning that their planets are always well-lit, even at night. They rule 93 star systems and 63 inhabited planets.
csg_hapan_human.description: A matriarchal culture of humans isolated in the Hapes cluster, the Hapans are known for both their beauty and their wealth. Their politics are literally cutthroat, as assassinations among the noble families are incredibly common.
csg_hapan_human.sidebar_text: The matriarchal society of the Hapans is not unexplained, and neither is their beauty. Hapans descend from the Lorell Raiders, a band of pirates from 4,000 years ago that discovered the Hapes Cluster and used it as a retreat. Furthermore, they took their most beautiful female prisoners to Hapes, whom they often raped. Over many generations, a sizeable population of Hapan women, selectively bred for beauty, became prisoners in the Hapes Cluster, while their sons became pirates once they were old enough. However, the Hapans were ultimately freed when the Jedi defeated the Lorell Raiders, and they established their own isolated society. When they did so, they vowed to never be ruled by a man again, and Hapan men have been servants ever since.

csg_harch.name: Harch

special_abilities.name: Six Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness or brightness.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 3 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Venomous Bite
special_abilities.description: May spend 3 advantage on a successful Brawl check to bite. A target who has been bitten must succeed in a hard Resilience check or receive the critical injury “At the Brink.”

csg_harch.physiology: The Harch are spider-like creatures with eight limbs. They use two for walking and have six to use as arms. These arms are clustered together, three on each side. The front two arms have two elbows each. Each hand has three fingers, which includes an opposable thumb. They have two toes on their feet. Harch are larger than most sentients, similar to their Aqualish cousins. With extra eyes, they are, in particular, related to the Ualaq subspecies of Aqualish. (Harch consider the debate on the intricacies of their genetics to be obscene, however.) They are tough and resilient to go with this strength. They are covered in brown hair, which grays at the face. This face lacks a neck and is very circular in nature. They have six red eyes, arranged in a semi-circle, two large mandibles that they keep neatly groomed, and a mouth with four teeth. These teeth have a bite that is somewhat venomous but can only slow down a victim. This mouth also tends to make a clicking sound that they use when they think.
csg_harch.society: While the Harch are just as aggressive as their Aqualish relatives, they also have more restraint. As much as they value strength and aggression, they also focus on resilience and patience. They are smarter than the Aqualish, but negotiation and diplomacy do not come naturally to them. However, they are cunning enough to find ways to rule over the Aqualish. They live in the Spiverelda, a region of space that refers to their and the Aqualish worlds. Their history with the Aqualish is an ugly one, complete with all the turbulence of the two species being aggressive in nature. When there weren’t wars going on, the Harch have served many roles. Sometimes, they have been cunning manipulators from behind the scenes. In others, they were dictators ruling over both peoples. Every once in awhile, they have been a cast down species.
csg_harch.language: The Harch speak Basic, and many know an Aqualish dialect or two.
csg_harch.homeworld: The Harch come from Secundus Ando, a Mid Rim world in the Spiverelda.
csg_harch.description: Arachnids of distant relations to the Aqualish, the Harch are long-lived, tough, and ambitious. They have a poisonous bite and six arms, providing impressive capabilities in combat.
csg_harch.sidebar_text: Though the Harch do not live on the Aqualish world of Ando, they were firmly aligned with Ando in the battles against the Andoan Free Colonies. When the Republic stepped in to save the Andoan Free Colonies and demilitarized Ando, the Harch and Aqualish grew dissatisfied. This resulted in both being eager to leave the corrupt regime and join the Confederacy. Though they lost, their drive for independence continues. Now, many Harch continue to fight against the Empire.

csg_hepsalum_tash.name: Hepsalum Tash

special_abilities.name: Swamp Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for wet conditions, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_hepsalum_tash.physiology: One of the galaxy’s stranger-looking species, the Hepsalum Tash are gigantic, at least eight meters tall. They have folded, leathery skin in shades of red, brown, and gold, and they have stripes or spots which can be used to distinguish age and gender. They are herbivorous, with a diet of many roots and nuts, and they are mostly sedentary because of their cumbersome physiology. Their left hand is roughly humanoid, useful for grasping, but their right has claws designed for digging in the mud. Their feet have two toes. They have a long neck, giving them a worm-like appearance, and their face features a large nose with no forehead, tiny eyes, and drooping ears. Their mouth is often surrounded by a layer of white whiskers, and they can have a small amount of hair atop their head as well.
csg_hepsalum_tash.society: Hepsalum Tash, sometimes referred to only as Tash, are a calm and peaceful people. They avoid interpersonal conflict and are indifferent whenever possible. They are loners, forsaking their mates after children are born. They generally use about a square kilometer of swampland, protecting it with wooden barriers, and they rarely trespass on others’ territories. As tool use has made it easier to find food, they have used their spare time to advance in the arts, crafting songs or stories to fill their time. Despite being ordinarily relaxed, they approach these fields with a perfectionist mentality. They will work for years before daring to reveal their handiwork, and to do otherwise is seen as insulting.
csg_hepsalum_tash.language: Despite their limited territory, the Hepsalum Tash have developed three major languages. In the unofficial borders between languages, creoles are common.
csg_hepsalum_tash.homeworld: The Hepsalum Tash hail from the world of Dagobah, a very backwater planet in the southern Outer Rim not far from the Rimma Trade Route. Its surface is covered in muddy swamps, although the territory of the Hepsalum Tash has fewer trees and more grasses in comparison to most of the rest of the planet.
csg_hepsalum_tash.description: The Tash are a species of gentle giants native to the swamps of Dagobah, where they are highly diligent artists and creators in their lonely abodes. They currently have no contact with the outside galaxy, but even once they do, few will take interest in leaving home.
csg_hepsalum_tash.sidebar_text: The Tash are mostly content in their environment, and though kind and curious, they have little interest in changing anything about their current lifestyle. Not that having such desires would matter anyway: They have yet to make any contact with an offworlder. Dagobah itself is not entirely isolated, as it is the home of Jedi Master Yoda, and just before the Clone Wars, a group of children were stranded on the world when their parents were killed by a fever. Now cannibalistic, The Children have a small, primitive society. However, the Hepsalum Tash are totally isolated from these inhabitants, since their society is solely on a peninsula in the western hemisphere, with a mountain range blocking off the other end, and they have never explored the rest of Dagobah, where these foreigners live. The first offworld contact for the Tash will be in about two decades, when a Jedi survey team will uncover their society while attempting to study Yoda’s exile. The Tash will agree to send a single member, Makuursh, offworld to study the galaxy for a year and report back. Finding urbanized planets built for smaller beings and disliking the constant bustle, he will mostly discourage his people from leaving. Only a handful of rouges will ever do so, most notably Ploutonshaa, a musician whose mellow songs will gain minor popularity for a few years following the Yuuzhan Vong War.
csg_hepsalum_tash._provenance_note: The Hepsalum Tash species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_herglic.name: Herglic

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_herglic.physiology: Herglics, sometimes called Koodans, are whale-like creatures native to the world of Giju. They breathe through a blowhole and still have fins instead of hands. Although fins make it somewhat difficult to use human technology, it is not completely impossible. Their smooth and mostly hairless skin occasionally has white portions but is mostly a darker color, such as black, purple, or dark blue. They are tall, up to three meters high, and especially wide in comparison to other large sentient species due to both their thick blubber and well-muscled physique. They don’t have much of a neck, and their head has a wide mouth and small black eyes. They are comfortable in aquatic conditions but cannot breathe underwater, instead relying on a blowhole and their impressive ability to hold their breath.
csg_herglic.society: Herglics are gentle, easygoing creatures and are always ready to explore, travel, and be social. However, they are very sensitive about their size, as they are too large for some human accommodations. For this reason, many form their own communities, and they stick together if they travel on worlds where they are a minority. These groups are called “pods,” or “pakk” in Herglese. The one flaw that many Herglics have is gambling. Addicted to Sabacc and other games of chance, they are a common sight at casinos. When not gambling, Herglics are very active in galactic trade, and many work in the technology business as well.
csg_herglic.language: The Herglic language is known as Herglese. Most Herglics know Basic and can speak it without issue. Thanks to the influence of the Herglics, many Herglese words are incorporated into the vocabulary of nearby worlds in the Tapani sector. One, a “hauum” sound, is that of a Herglic clearing his blowhole. It is used to begin a significant remark.
csg_herglic.homeworld: The Herglic homeworld of Giju is a wet world in the southern portion of the Colonies. It is on the Rimma Trade Route, which its Herglics helped to create. Its islands are covered by cities, which are hubs for the technology manufacturing industry. Its many spaceports make it great for all kinds of trade.
csg_herglic.description: Herglics are friendly and gregarious, but their large size makes it difficult for them to fit in with things designed for smaller humanoids. They are aquatic and descend from whales. Many become addicted to sabacc and other forms of gambling.
csg_herglic.sidebar_text: The Herglics were one of the first species to create hyperspace technology and used their innovations to create a powerful empire centered around trade and technology. Herglic technology from that time is long lost, but it is considered to be at a level that goes unparalleled, even in comparison to that at the current time. This early empire collapsed, and the technology was lost. Herglics continued on and were prominent as scouts and explorers in the galaxy. Their Trade Empire rose again and stayed separate from the Republic for a while, although it eventually joined around 13,000 BBY. Heglics again rose to greatness in 5,500 BBY, when they proved instrumental in developing the Rimma Trade Route. Now, the Herglics have become less successful under the Galactic Empire, although Giju is still prominent in the technology industry.

csg_hiromi.name: Hiromi

special_abilities.name: Victory Lap
special_abilities.description: When healing strain at the end of an encounter that can be considered successful, heal 2 additional strain.

csg_hiromi.physiology: Insectoids with brown or olive skin, the Hiromi are on the shorter side but relatively stocky. They have no hair, but they do have two white antennae atop their head. They have large, yellow eyes with green pupils, and they have a tongue, which is rare among insects. On both sides of their mouth, they have a loose flap of skin in a triangular shape. They also have a sharply pointed chin.
csg_hiromi.society: Hiromi are an extremely cowardly people; they have an incredibly strong instinct for self-preservation. Whenever presented with a chance to fight, they will almost always suggest some sort of alternative- bringing in reinforcements, hiding, or even abandoning the conflict altogether. Although they will ultimately do what is required of them, they always prefer to take on the easiest possible tasks, even if these tasks do little to contribute to their goals. For whatever reason, they have an image of themselves which is the exact opposite of this reality: They consider themselves to be a species of conquerors, and describe themselves as “glorious” and “ruthless.” They enjoy cheering and will celebrate even the most meaningless of achievements whenever they have a chance. Another obstacle preventing them from reaching their goals is an extreme lack of patience, as they will often quit a task in order to eat or play. All of these oddities ultimately stem from the unique logic of the Hiromi. The Hiromi excel in creative thinking and lateral logic, and they have the mental capabilities to solve incredibly complex problems, but they lack much of the more basic logic that other species take for granted. As such, even their most elaborate plans are plagued by seemingly obvious issues.
csg_hiromi.language: Likely because of their time spent trying to conquer the galaxy, a majority of the Hiromi know Basic as well as their native tongue.
csg_hiromi.homeworld: The location and name of the Hiromi homeworld is unknown, but they are one of the few species that has contact with the Tofs from Companion Besh as well as the rest of the galaxy. They consider their territory an Empire, although it is likely quite small.
csg_hiromi.description: Hiromi are insects from the Unknown Regions with a baffling psychology: They have a knack for outside-the-box problem solving and engineering, but they are blind to incredibly obvious facts. They are also extremely cowardly, but they see themselves as the opposite.
csg_hiromi.sidebar_text: For about 2,000 years, the Hiromi have been waiting for the opportunity to take control of the entire galaxy, but when they do so, their attempts will be abysmal. Their current plan is to force the galaxy into a civil war, which they intend to start by pitting the Lahsbee and the Ewoks against each other. Although both species are obscure and relatively harmless, the deceptions of the Hiromi will ultimately fall apart. They will then invade Zeltros, successfully conquering the palace kitchens because the Zeltrons won’t care enough to bother fighting them. At that point, they will be certain that the entire galaxy will soon follow, and they will celebrate by eating lunch. They will work alongside the Zeltrons and Luke Skywalker to defeat the Tofs, a violent species whose invasion will pose a legitimate threat. However, upon realizing that their conquests mean nothing, the Hiromi will return home.

csg_hoojib.name: Hoojib

special_abilities.name: Energy Feeders
special_abilities.description: May survive off of absorbing electrical energy.

special_abilities.name: Telepathy
special_abilities.description: Cannot speak. May communicate by telepathically “broadcasting” speech to all beings within short range. May also “whisper,” broadcasting only to those who are engaged.

csg_hoojib.physiology: Hoojibs are a species of smaller, quadrupedal rodents distinguished by a long antenna, floppy ears, and wide eyes. They are covered in fur, which is typically tan or yellow, but it can also be blue, white or pink. What they lack in size they make up for in speed and agility, and they are able to navigate their native forests with ease. Hoojibs do not need to eat other animals or plants, and they instead survive by consuming energy directly, similar to plants. Hoojibs can sustain themselves by receiving energy from droids or other electronic devices that produce or use significant amounts of power. Hoojibs are also telepathic, able to broadcast their thoughts into the minds of nearby sentients.
csg_hoojib.society: The Hoojibs are a deeply communal society, valuing friendship and camaraderie amongst their own. Their government is led by a single spokesmind, who communicates on behalf of their people. They rarely use technology of any sort, but they are nevertheless a civilized people with a rich culture. Hoojibs have telepathically connected with underground being called the Darker, which was created when another sentient species, the Arbrans, who are now extinct, attempted to rid their minds of all evil thoughts using advanced technology. They succeeded, but the evil became manifested in the Darker. Hoojibs see the Darker as the embodiment of evil, and he will be killed in a few years with help from the Rebel Alliance.
csg_hoojib.language: Hoojibs cannot speak any verbal language, although they can make simple sounds like yelps or cries. Their telepathy can be understood by beings who know any language. They typically understand Basic.
csg_hoojib.homeworld: Hoojibs come from Arbra, a planet which has many environments, including rainforests, mountains, and caves. It is a primitive world on the surface, but underground, it has devices capable of harvesting the core’s geothermal heat. This energy is released as electricity throughout the Hoojib’s cave, and they feed off of it.
csg_hoojib.description: Small quadrupedal rodents who lack technology, the Hoojibs may be mistaken for non-sentient creatures, but they are sentient, and they have a very communal society. They do not speak, but they can communicate amongst themselves or with others via telepathy.
csg_hoojib.sidebar_text: Hoojibs will first encounter offworlders when the Rebel Alliance will scout their homeworld in search of a location to build a base following the Battle of Hoth. The relationship between the two will be tense at first, but they will eventually unite after the rebels help kill a Yuuzhan Vong monster called the Slivilith, which will attack their home. The Rebel Alliance will build a base in the cavern where Hoojibs live, and the two will interact with each other frequently, thus providing the Hoojibs with opportunities to travel offworld and enter the wider galaxy.

csg_houk.name: Houk

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

csg_houk.physiology: Houk are an extremely large and strong race. They average more than two meters in height, very few species can rival their incredible strength, and they have thick skin which protects them from many types of harm. Their skin is blue or purple with splotches of orange or beige on their head and chest, and they have a ridged forehead instead of hair. Although they lack a visible nose or ears, their face is distinguished by prominent jowls on their chin and beady, yellow eyes.
csg_houk.society: Houk are a fundamentally selfish people who are disliked by almost all. They have a reputation to be bullies, and they are very short-tempered. They are also completely without honesty, as they are willing to backstab anyone and do not respect contracts or promises that they have made. They expect to get what they want, and most of them demonstrate great tenacity in doing whatever is necessary to fulfill their desires. Despite their violent tendencies, they’re smarter than they look. Although they are not especially skilled in technology or book smarts, their cleverness can be comparable to that of a Hutt. Despite their willingness to be violent at a moment’s notice, many of them prefer to use stealth and deception in combat. Still others devote their stubbornness and perseverance toward hard work. Of all of their wars, their most notable conflict is with the Weequays, a species native Sriluur, where the Houk set up a colony. They have recently begun a ceasefire, but tensions on Sriluur are still very high.
csg_houk.language: Houk speak Houkese, a grunting language which uses precise differences in pitch to distinguish different words. They have barely invented a written language, as they still use pictograms to represent most nouns.
csg_houk.homeworld: The Houk come from Lijuter, a planet in the Reibrin system of the Outer Rim. Although it is dry and unwelcoming, its many space stations and two moons see a very deal of traders, smugglers, and other underworlders. They also have 31 nearby colonies, all of which answer to the Lijuter Congress.
csg_houk.description: Houk possess a powerful combination of stubbornness, cleverness, and raw strength. They have had a long-standing conflict with the Weequays, and they have also been drawn into conflict with the Galactic Empire.
csg_houk.sidebar_text: The Empire felt that the Houk had the potential to become perfect slaves: burly but willing to submit. Although the former assessment is correct, the latter is very wrong. Houk are a strong-willed people who do not give up, and they are also clever enough to fight back effectively. These factors caused the program to fail. Of the hundreds of Houk who were captured, most refused to obey and were killed. At least one Houk escaped and joined the Rebel Alliance out of spite. However, Houk are not idealistic, so those present in the Alliance are almost certainly motivated by revenge.

csg_hodin.name: Ho’Din
csg_hodin.physiology: The Ho’din are taller than two and half meters, with some being up to three meters tall. Despite their size, they are thin creatures. They have varying colors of skin which can be orange, yellow, green, or blue. They have long and thin limbs and their suction-cupped fingers are also long and thin. They have large black eyes. Most unique about their appearance is their strange version of hair. Their “hair” is thick and snake-like, red or maroon in color. These tubes are actually covered by scales. Yet another unique feature about them is that they have two hearts. While they claim to be related to plants, they are likely of reptilian origin.
csg_hodin.society: The Ho’Din are generally peaceful and enjoy focusing on the studies of ecology and botany. Their society has three ranks that individuals achieve through time, experience, and training. The youngest and least experienced are known as Learners. The more knowledgeable Ho’Din can be Healers. Finally, the greatest title is that of Master Gardener. They developed an interest in ecology when their society industrialized, which brought an unexpected ecological consequence: parasites. After that time, which the refer to as the Great Rape of the Land, they returned to a simpler lifestyle and devoted themselves to ecology. While they are willing to use technology on planets that are “already damaged,” they avoid bringing it to planets that are free of tech. Gardening and ecology often take up much of their money and time, as they work to improve the ecosystem of their own planet and even to create “garden worlds” on other planets where they can commune with nature. They are also excellent healers, particularly when it comes to herbal therapies.
csg_hodin.language: The Ho’Din speak Ho’Din, a croaking language. They often use plant-based metaphors and idioms.
csg_hodin.homeworld: The Ho’Din come from the rainforest planet Moltok, which they have terraformed and filled with ecological wonders of all sorts. It mostly focuses on an herbal industry. It also has volcanoes, whose ashes give the world a crimson sky. The Ho’Din share it with the Makurth, a species often employed as bodyguards and mercenaries in the criminal underworld.
csg_hodin.description: Ho'Din specialize in all things related to plants and botany. They are tall and thin with snake-like protrusions on their head. They have an extreme focus on preserving environments and being eco-friendly, which is emphasized in their religion.
csg_hodin.sidebar_text: The Ho’Din are ruled by a theocracy, the priests of the [Dinante Fli’R]. This religion worships nature, particularly plants. According to their history, the Ho’Din were once mobile plants themselves, before being turned into animals af punishment for going against [Dinegia]. Much their actions are done in hopes of completing the [Flik’a kirki], or Virtuous Cycle of Nature. Those who do enough to complete this can be supposedly reborn as plants. Their customs follow along with this. For example, conception is done in a ceremony that mimics the conception in plants. Even in funerals, they give the body as a gift to the soil on the forest floor.

csg_hrakian.name: Hrakian
csg_hrakian.physiology: Hrakians are near-humans distinguished by yellowish skin, and they also lack hair. Instead, they have golden ruffs of feathers which are atop their head and just above their eyes. They are also fairly durable with above-average stamina. Otherwise, they are very similar to humans.
csg_hrakian.society: Hrakians are generally known to be a people who are very determined yet straightforward. They thrive when they are given simple, menial jobs, but they don’t always have the drive to go above and beyond. However, they are extremely persevering and will always ensure that at least the bare minimum gets completed no matter what.
csg_hrakian.language: As Hrakians embraced the wider galaxy, their language of Hrakian evolved and borrowed a significant amount of vocabulary from Basic. The two languages are now so similar that Hrakian is essentially a dialect of Basic, Hrakians rarely bother to learn the standard version of Basic.
csg_hrakian.homeworld: Hrakians come from Hraki, an Outer Rim planet near the Perlemian Trade Route. A prominent hub for commerce, it features towering mountains and dense, humid jungles. However, Hrakians are often spacers, so they can be found on their many colonies throughout the Vorzyd Cluster and all throughout the rest of the galaxy.
csg_hrakian.description: Yellowy near-humans, the Hrakians make up for their lack of tech-savviness through determination and hard work. They enjoy space travel and can be found on a variety of worlds.
csg_hrakian.sidebar_text: Hrakians are a spacefaring species with a natural desire to explore the stars, and they are common sight on bulk freighters throughout the Vorzyd Cluster. What they lack in intellect, social skills, or cleverness, they make up for with hard work, and so long as they can look forward to a cantina full of Elba beer at the end of the day, they will happily take on any job. Their prevalence as travelers has turned their homeworld into something of a trading hub, and Hrakians can easily mingle with the crowds of other nearby species. Unfortunately, they are still handicapped by their lack of technical skills. Hrakian technicians are an extremely rare commodity, and the many Hrakian ship captains will gladly pay a steep wage in order to hire one of the few who do exist.

csg_huhk_lahsbee.name: Huhk/Lahsbee
csg_huhk_lahsbee.physiology: The Huhks and Lahsbees are bipedal felines with pointed ears and yellow eyes. They have a short nose and sharp teeth. They are also covered in fur, which can range in color from shades of red, pink, and yellow to shades of blue, gray, and brown. They have two separate names because they undergo a dramatic transformation once they reach adulthood. Lahsbees are the children, and they are even smaller than human children, while the adults, Huhks, grow to a whopping three meters tall.
csg_huhk_lahsbee.society: Lahsbees and Huhks each have their own society, and each has a distinct culture. Huhks are mindless savages, roaming around cities or wilderness in search of prey and almost never interacting with other sentients. Although the Huhks will typically try to murder Lahsbees if they ever encounter one, they can be temporarily calmed using music, a technique that the Lahsbees employ frequently. Conversely, the Lahsbees are actually quite civilized, living in rural communities where they cheerfully play for much of their youth. Although they use some simple technology, they detest all forms of advanced electronic technology, and they wish to be far away from modern conveniences.
csg_huhk_lahsbee.language: Both Lahsbees and Huhks share the language of Huhk, and they rarely speak Basic.
csg_huhk_lahsbee.homeworld: Lahsbees and Huhks come from Lahsbane, a primitive planet with jungles and canyons. They travel using simple hot air balloons or gliders. It is backwater enough that it is rarely visited, and spacers are further deterred by a pollen which can clog the intake valves of starships.
csg_huhk_lahsbee.description: A species of primitive felines, the Lahsbee undergo such a dramatic metamorphosis at puberty that they take a new name: Huhk. Lashbee are tiny and playful, while Huhk are large and ferocious.
csg_huhk_lahsbee.sidebar_text: Puberty dramatically changes the Lahsbees, and if a a Lahsbee PC wishes to undergo this transformation, they must spend five XP and wait several months. After that, they increase Brawn by two, decrease Intellect by one, decrease Presence by one, increase Wound Threshold by five, and decrease Strain Threshold by one. Additionally, they become Silhouette 2, receive a rank in Brawl, and reduce ranks in Charm by one.

csg_human.name: Human
csg_human.physiology: Human physiology is very versatile and is a baseline from which other species are often described. Very few features set them apart from any other species, and have entirely the “common” ones. They have two arms, two legs, and stand a bit below two meters in general. They have five-fingered hands and five-toed feet, with an opposable thumb on each hand. Their head has hair in varying shades of brown or blonde, or gray or white with age. Their skin is tan, peach, or brown. Their eyes are blue, green, or brown with dark pupils, and typically have eyebrows. Unlike many other species, they sometimes have hair around their mouth and on their chin.
csg_human.society: Over time, humans have developed into multiple societies across thousands of planets and have merged and travelled so much that they are said to represent the average of all other cultures in the galaxy. Still, human culture is a very complex subject. Almost all have a unique background from whatever planet they may come from. Those from some may come from a culture of extreme peace, while others may come from a planet valuing battle and military service. Others may come from one of recklessness and independence, with others may come from a culture valuing conformity. The species as a whole is notable for being very diverse, and humans, more than most other species, tend to vary in personality. This makes them more widespread than any other species, and also a fascinating subject for many geneticists.
csg_human.language: While some humans learn other languages to communicate with other cultures, Basic is the only one that most use.
csg_human.homeworld: Humans have no specific homeworld, though they are theorized to hail from Coruscant itself. They have spread to nearly everywhere, from bustling Core Worlds to Mid Rim settlements to Outer Rim shadowports. The former in particular is very common, as many Outer Rim worlds are dominated by existing populations of native species.
csg_human.description: The most common species in the galaxy, humans are widespread thanks to being adaptable and well-rounded. They have been the benefactors of speciesism from the Empire and Republic and are typically the standard from which other species are judged.
csg_human.sidebar_text: Humanity has gotten a particularly large advantage under the Empire. Though the course of history has been dotted with some degrees of human superiority, the Empire has been the most blatant major government in supporting humans since the Pius Dea controlled Republic over 20,000 years ago. Not only are humans less likely to be oppressed by the Empire, they are ideal candidates for dealing with Imperials, who will often dislike non-humans. These opportunities do come with a cost, however, as some non-humans resent the species over their past transgressions. More than any other species, humans have backgrounds relating to being a part of or allied with the Empire. These experiences often involve a whole lot of injustice, which can shape them for their lives.

csg_huralok.name: Huralok

special_abilities.name: Master Manipulators
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Plausible Deniability.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_huralok.physiology: Huraloks are reptiles who are bulky but short, averaging around one and a half meters tall. They have scales that come in shades of brown, and stripes of brittle black hair wrap around their body and on top of their head. Their head is triangular in shape, thin around their mouth but with eyes that are spread wide apart. These eyes are quite large and mostly yellow in color with orange irises. Their hands and feet have three digits on each, and these digits end in black claws which can be used for combat. Huraloks are an extremely long-lived species, not becoming adults until the age of 45 and often living past 300. However, their claws frequently become dull as they get older. Nonetheless, they retain an intimidating appearance that most other species find unsavory.
csg_huralok.society: In short, there are few redeeming traits for the Huralok species. They never forget a grudge, and they are vicious and merciless in their typical occupations of being pirates, con artists, or mob bosses. Huraloks are completely selfish, and they pursue their ends with complex schemes that usually involve manipulation and betrayal. On the occasions when they aren’t being cruel bullies, it’s usually a fake kindness to carry out a con. They are also rather lazy, much preferring to let minions carry out their work than doing anything themselves. Even as their treacherous plans unfold, they are usually hidden away behind the scenes, far beyond the reach of any potential repercussions. If there is one good thing about the species, it’s that they are extremely few in number, as they rarely reproduce. This is because their loathing extends even to their own kind, and they avoid interacting with other Huraloks whenever possible. Only when the species is on the verge of extinction do they reluctantly come together with other Huraloks to mate, and they are quick to separate afterwards.
csg_huralok.language: Huraloks speak their native language of Huralok and usually learn Basic as well.
csg_huralok.homeworld: The Huralok homeworld is Djurmo, a volcanic planet in the Mid Rim.
csg_huralok.description: The Huraloks are a widely despised species of treacherous, unforgiving bullies. They make natural con artists, but their reputation has been so sullied that few would ever trust them anymore, so now they often turn to less subtle violence, such as piracy.
csg_huralok.sidebar_text: Unfortunately for them, Huraloks suffer from a rather unsavory image, and as much as they may try to manipulate, many species know better than to trust a Huralok. Indeed, this may be why they so often feel the need to use emissaries and underlings in order to pull off their various cons. In some ways, the Huraloks have no one to blame but themselves for their reputation, but the situation is exacerbated by Imperial holodramas, which depict the Empire heroically standing up to the villainous Huralok pirates. These films are extremely popular, and for many average citizens, it is how they are first introduced to the Huralok species.

csg_hutt.name: Hutt

special_abilities.name: Fat
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Stubborn
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Nobody’s Fool.”

special_abilities.name: Awkward
special_abilities.description: Add 3 setbacks to all Brawl, Coordination, and Melee checks.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 2.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_hutt.physiology: Hutts are slug-like creatures with skin that is green or brown. Their body is thick and well-covered in fat, and they lack legs. Their arms are also short, and the four fingers on each hand are quite chubby. Despite all of their physical limitations, Hutts are not to be underestimated. Behind the ugly, chubby exterior lies a devious mind, (which is also resistant to the Force) and their influence is also great. Not only that, but they can make surprisingly formidable combatants thanks to their bulk and mass. Their neckless head has a wide mouth and yellow eyes, lacking hair or a nose. While some Hutts are so large that they are completely immobile, most can manage to slowly slither about if needed. Their skin is slippery, and they lack bones. Hutts are also known for their smell, which can be sickening to a particularly sensitive person and disgusting for most. They are hermaphrodites, allowing them to reproduce with or without a mate. They can live for 1,000 years.
csg_hutt.society: Hutts value cunning and good business, and most are completely immoral. They also tend to be paranoid. Hutts view all other species as subordinate, so they have no reservations about slavery, spice dealing, and extortion. Almost all tend to be crime lords. Beneath their business oriented exterior, what many fail to realize is that Hutts feel threatened and make most actions out of fear. Though ruthless, they are not prone to war. They instead view violence as wasteful and accomplish control by more cunning means. This will change after the Yuuzhan Vong war in 25 ABY, in which their holdings will be badly damaged. While Hutts are far too savvy to be manipulated and persuaded by others, they tend to be extremely offended if they are not flattered. Almost all keep slaves, who they use for most manual labor. For large-scale operations, however, they prefer indentured servants.
csg_hutt.language: Though Hutts can speak Basic, most choose not to. Their own language, Huttese, is somewhat of a lingua franca on the more illicit parts of the Outer Rim.
csg_hutt.homeworld: While their influence brings them all over Hutt space, they mostly call Nal Hutta home. It is fairly urban and extremely swampy.
csg_hutt.description: No species is more well-known for crime than the Hutts. They are massive, slug-like creatures who lead many of the most powerful crime rings in the galaxy. What they lack in coordination they make up for in deviousness, heartlessness, and bulk.
csg_hutt.sidebar_text: In addition to being naturally savvy, Hutts also hold great political power. As the controllers of Hutt space, the Hutt Council is almost impossible to oppose. It is a very independent region, as not even the Empire can control Hutt space. Species native to the region have mostly been subjugated as slaves. Hutts are the only law in that portion of the galaxy.

csg_hyallp.name: Hyallp

special_abilities.name: Six Arms
special_abilities.description: May have three times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Tunnel Vision
special_abilities.description: When in combat with multiple adversaries, must designate a single one to be the Hyallp’s only target. If the target is defeated while combat is still ongoing, a new target must be designated immediately. All adversaries who are not the target add boost on attacks against the Hyallp.

csg_hyallp.physiology: Hyallp are arthropods with twelve limbs, half of which are legs that end in a single sharp chela that they walk atop. Their other six limbs are arms ending in three-fingered hands that do have opposable thumbs. Hyallp have a maroon and black carapace, but despite its hardness, it is fairly brittle, making them surprisingly fragile. However, they are still fierce in combat, thanks to their extra arms and significant size. They average over two meters tall, although they have a somewhat spindly build. This keeps them light, allowing them to move quickly on their long legs. Hyallp cannot smell and rely primarily on their single large eye, which is yellow or green. This eye dominates the face of their diamond-shaped head. The majority of Hyallp are genderless, infertile drones.
csg_hyallp.society: Hyallp are secretive, single-minded, and vicious. Inclined toward a combative lifestyle, they make deadly and inexorable hunters, but they are slow to adapt and infamously narrow in their focus. They make few friends outside their own nests, which are composed of a few dozen members. Nests are mostly worker drones who serve the rare fertile Hyallp: one queen and a handful of males per nest. Unlike many insect species, the queen enjoys little power. Though she is pampered to ensure that she produces enough eggs, it is the fertile males who enjoy both privilege and power, and they are often cruel toward the drones, whom they see as highly dispensable. The nests are built underground, protecting the Hyallp from larger predators, and they can become very cramped. Aside from weapons, modern technology has made few inroads in their backwater society.
csg_hyallp.language: Hyallp speak a language known as Iyallp, but they are very careful to avoid speaking it around anyone who could be recording, as they do not want the wider galaxy to study it and make a translation. Those who leave their world can learn Basic, but their voice is very soft. Drones are referred to with the pronoun “it.”
csg_hyallp.homeworld: The Hyallp have managed to keep their homeworld a secret after they only entered the wider galaxy by repairing a starship that crash-landed on their homeworld, which they call Riome-Eso. Riome-Eso is a low tech planet in the Outer Moddell systems, and much of its plains are dominated by megafauna such as the gyutch, which Hyallp hunt for food.
csg_hyallp.description: Hive dwelling insects, Hyallp are rarely seen in the wider galaxy, and they are deeply distrusting of all other races, who have yet to even locate their homeworld. These one-eyed arthropods make dangerous warriors, but their narrow focus is a major limitation.
csg_hyallp.sidebar_text: It is highly dangerous for Hyallp to remain on their homeworld without a nest, so such individuals often attempt to flee offworld. The only ways are via two shuttles, a YG-4210 managed by the Fay nest, and a modified Wayfarer-class freighter by the Nillysch nest. The shuttles usually ferry about a dozen Hyallp to a small spaceport (never the same one twice, for fear they could be tracked back to their homeworld), and the passengers have no say in their destination. Some drones will try to flee on them if their queen dies without a successor, as the males start ambitious wars to kidnap a queen from another nest. They usually leave in pairs, as their singlemindedness makes them vulnerable alone. Males will sometimes flee alone if their political machinations unfold. In rare cases, an ambitious queen will leave seeking adventure as she abandons a life of comfort.
csg_hyallp._provenance_note: Little is known about the Hyallp. This entire page is highly speculative and retcons Krutch to be a member. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they rewrite stats, imagining their own aspects of Hyallp physiology and culture.

csg_hdrachi.name: H’drachi

special_abilities.name: Gifted Seers
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Forsee Basic Power. When purchasing a Strength or Duration upgrade for Forsee, double that upgrade’s effects.

csg_hdrachi.physiology: H’drachi are smaller mammals with yellow skin and short, brown hair. Their arms and legs are relatively thin, and they have three-fingered hands and two-toed feet. All of their digits end in sharp nails, which provide traction but do little in combat. They have a forward-pointing snout and typically have a white beard. They have an unusually strong connection to the Force.
csg_hdrachi.society: H’drachi are peaceful, and they are subservient to a population of human colonists. They have very little interest in galactic politics, and their homeworld has remained out of most wars. Because the H’drachi Seers can often predict the future, most of them value patience and worry very little.
csg_hdrachi.language: The H’drachi have no known language of their own, and most of them know Basic.
csg_hdrachi.homeworld: H’drachi come from M’haeli, a planet that is ruled by human monarchs and occupied by the Empire. An agriworld in the Expansion Region, it has vast plains and a few mountain ranges. Most of civilized society is at the more temperate equator, such as the capital of N’croth, since other parts of the planet are very cold. Human colonists have most of the planet’s wealth, and the H’drachi typically live in ghettos. Although the Rebel Alliance once sought to take over the planet, and the humans have begun guerrilla warfare against the Empire, both have been unsuccessful. Grand Moff Lynch and his forces currently keep the planet under Imperial control.
csg_hdrachi.description: H'drachi are peaceful and spiritual mammals that rarely worry about anything, and many are gifted in the Force. They often excel in precognition, but very few are gifted with any other powers.
csg_hdrachi.sidebar_text: As a very religious people, the H’drachi have developed their own views of the Force. The vast number of Force-sensitive H’drachi refer to their ability as being able to perceive the time-stream. They call themselves the H’drachi Seers, since most of them only exhibit precognition, with other Force abilities being extremely rare. However, what they lack in telekinesis or physical augmentation, they make up for with precognition. They can see the future with extreme precision, especially with multiple H’drachi. As such, the H’drachi are well-aware that the Empire will fall, and they decided to simply wait out the war. Most H’drachi Seers are distinguished by a colorful tunic, a large turban, and a multitude of charms.

csg_hnemthe.name: H’nemthe

special_abilities.name: Sharp Tongue
special_abilities.description: Deal +2 Brawl damage as wounds, and have the Pierce 2 and Vicious 1 qualities.

special_abilities.name: Heat Sensitivity
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as a maneuver, sense the presence and emotional state of everyone within short range.

csg_hnemthe.physiology: Reptilians of a rough pink, orange, or blue-gray skin, the H’nemthe are best known for one trait: the females have tongues that are as sharp and as deadly as swords, which they use to kill the males after mating. 95% of H’nemthe are male at birth, although the females make up for this with a significantly longer lifespan. Their face has large black or green eyes and a notable beak above their mouth. Their face is also very bony and ridged, with four head cones at the top. These cones can sense minute heat differences and allow a H’nemthe to read the emotions of others and predict weather. They have four-fingered hands with claws.
csg_hnemthe.society: H’nemthe are mostly peaceful, artistic, and philosophical. Poetry is a venerated tradition, and their literature and music are popular galaxy-wide. They live in a highly structured direct democracy, and virgin females are especially protected due to their rarity. Most of their leaders are also female, as males often don’t survive long enough to fulfill their duties. The society is closed off and somewhat a mystery to the rest of the galaxy. Though they rarely leave their homeworld, those that do are often musicians or artists. Under Imperial control, a handful have also joined the Rebel Alliance. It is almost exclusively males who are found offworld, as they can grow upset by their inability to find a companion amongst their own kind. Females mating with other species is much rarer, with the first ever known exception being fairly recent in M’iiyoom Onith, who mated and killed a Gotal named Feltipern Trevagg. This unique event has made her into a celebrity on H’nemthe.
csg_hnemthe.language: H’nemthe is also the name of their language, which is one of squeals and squeaks. This makes it irritating to most other species, so their popular musical compositions are mostly instrumental. The written form is much more visually pleasing, written in a continuous line. As they are generally well-educated, H’nemthe typically learn Basic.
csg_hnemthe.homeworld: H’nemthe come from a planet of the same name. It is very green due to its heavy forests, but it has a rapidly fluctuating climate due to the tidal pulls of its three moons. It includes the carnivorous plant m’iiyoom, which is also called the Nightlily.
csg_hnemthe.description: H'nemthe are pacifistic, romantic, and philosophical. However, they only view death as a change in form prior to their afterlife, so they are willing to die very easily. There are 20 males to every female, but this difference is reduced by the fact that males are killed after reproducing.
csg_hnemthe.sidebar_text: For all their brutal ways, H’nemthe are surprisingly romantic. Males are willing to face certain death in order to reproduce, which they believe gives them major rewards in their afterlife. Though otherwise timid, males devote much of their lives towards finding a partner. They believe that after death, they become angels with the sacred duty of guarding their offspring. Females have strictly vegetarian diets until their first time mating, in which they get their first meat: their lover’s eviscerated body. The H’nemthe do not find this to be brutal and view death as a mere change in form. Prior to their mating, H’nemthe couples traditionally write epic poems for one another, which are then recited publically in a last tribute to the groom, then reproduced in ornate calligraphy.

csg_iakaru.name: Iakaru

special_abilities.name: Brachiation
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for moving through forest or jungle terrain, add boost on checks to swing, climb, or jump.

csg_iakaru.physiology: Iakaru are a species of arboreal primates covered in fur that is mostly thick and dark brown, but they have patches that are lighter-colored and softer on their belly and face. They have a short neck supporting their head that features small eyes with red pupils and a scrunched nose. They have thick eyebrows and whiskers. Iakaru are an agile, gymnastic people who have excellent balance and can easily swing between branches.
