These treetop athletics have given them superb three-dimensional spatial awareness and an innate understanding of distances and relative motion, skills that make them great pilots.
csg_iakaru.society: Iakaru live in clans of about 50, led by the eldest female, that occupy the canopy of a single large tree, which is often a kilometer high. They generally control a territory with a handful of nearby trees but stick to only one as their home. Males stay with their tree-clan for life, but females can change clans when they marry. They have no individual possessions, everything they use belongs to the entire tree-clan and is stored in the tree trunk, although they can brawl over food. They have some technology, including solar-powered repulsorlifts, as a few clans near mountains have been able to mine. They have developed agriculture, farming both fruits and insects.
csg_iakaru.language: Iakaru speak using a chattering tongue called Iakari, and those who learn Basic can only speak it with a very thick accent. They tend to squeal or bark in arguments or when threatened, and they will howl if they are away from home at night.
csg_iakaru.homeworld: Iakaru hail from Iakar, a lush jungle planet with many mountain ranges that is in the Elrood sector. They live at the top of the giant trees, while rodents, felines, and giant spiders live below the canopy.
csg_iakaru.description: Relatively primitive primates, the Iakaru's arboreal nature gives them great coordination, reflexes, and spatial awareness, which makes them excellent pilots. An Imperial invasion of their planet, mining for compounds that can be used in pharmaceutical drugs, has driven many Iakaru from their homes.
csg_iakaru.sidebar_text: Iakaru were only discovered during the Clone Wars, when pharmaceutical companies came to their planet in search of compounds with medicinal use. Corporate security for companies like Chiewab, Fabreth Medical, and Merisee Prime quickly forced the Iakaru to concede a small amount of their territory and retreat back further into the forests. The Imperials continued this trend and doubled down on it, occupying the planet, burning forests to make way for garrisons and labs, and capturing many Iakaru for study. Losing their homes has caused the Iakaru to become desperate and frustrated, so many have decided to leave their home behind by stealing starships and venturing into the larger galaxy.
csg_iakaru._provenance_note: The Iakaru species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU.

csg_icehead.name: Icehead

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Frozen Bodies
special_abilities.description: Remove all setbacks for cold conditions, add two setbacks for hot conditions. Double damage from fire or fire-based weapons.

special_abilities.name: Ice Skating
special_abilities.description: Immune to movement penalties due to snow. When on a slick surface, such as ice, may begin ice skating as a maneuver. When ice skating, must spend at least 1 maneuver per round moving, but this maneuver may move twice as far. Must spend a maneuver to stand up after ice skating.

csg_icehead.physiology: Standing at about one and a half meters tall on average, Iceheads have a thin, wiry body covered in sleek, black skin. Their hands have three clawed digits, and their legs each end in one large, pointed foot. As their colloquial name suggests, Iceheads have a head that, to many, resembles a block of ice. Every part of their head is slick, shiny, and white, even down to the inside of their mouth. The species is seemingly immune to any form of cold conditions and can move completely unhindered in any amount of snow. When on a slick surface, the Iceheads can use their quickest form of locomotion: flipping onto their head and sliding along the surface in a process similar to how one might ice skate. This allows them to move at high speeds while on ice and is their preferred mode of transportation.
csg_icehead.society: On their arctic homeworld, Iceheads have a rigid feudal system, with most members of a community serving as a warrior, a guard, or a hunter. If they fail in one of their combative roles, they are given another role in society, which labels them as too weak to be a true warrior. The only respectable members of their society that don’t revolve around combat are the sorcerer nobles, who are strong in the Force, manipulating the ice and snow to their whim. Those who are warriors use the Icehead traditional clubs, which are flat wooden boards with a paddle-like end. Iceheads must constantly regenerate the layer of ice protecting their head, which they do by dousing their head in water on a daily basis. In social situations, they are gruff, rarely speaking unless there is something important to say.
csg_icehead.language: Iceheads can speak Basic but prefer to use their own language, Ivigysh, or the language of whoever is employing them at the time.
csg_icehead.homeworld: Located near Companion Besh, Crylonis IV is a planet totally covered by frozen tundra, and its distance from the wider galaxy means that Icheads are a rare sight. Crylonis IV is populated by many savage arctic beasts, which the Iceheads continue to struggle against. The cities, made with assistance from the nobles, are made of bricks of snow.
csg_icehead.description: The name "Icehead" says it all: Their face does indeed appear to be made of ice. Adapted to colder climates, Iceheads often use their slippery head to skate across the ground.
csg_icehead.sidebar_text: Iceheads have been stranded on Endor for many years, where they have fallen into the service of a ruler called the Snow King. Living and working around his Snow Palace, the Iceheads are happy, and they show their worth by hunting and fighting in the name of this powerful sorcerer.
csg_icehead._provenance_note: The Icehead species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_iktotchi.name: Iktotchi

special_abilities.name: Precognition
special_abilities.description: May sometimes receive visions of the future. These can be handled by the GM and may have varying degrees of ambiguity. When making Initiative checks, may spend triumph to gain +3 success.

special_abilities.name: Telepathy
special_abilities.description: May silently communicate with other sentients of choice within medium range.

csg_iktotchi.physiology: Iktotchi are hairless near-humans with tough red-tan skin and downward-curving horns that can regenerate. The horns are not actually useful for combat but nevertheless come across as intimidating to some. They possess very powerful psychological abilities, including precognition and telepathy. While the former loses some effect once they go off of their homeworld, it is nevertheless prominent enough to keep most Iktotchi banned from gambling. Their telepathy allows them to communicate with others. They have rather large hands and fat fingers, which somewhat limit their dexterity. Despite this, reflexes and foresight more than make up for this when they are in a pilot’s seat or handling weapons.
csg_iktotchi.society: Iktotchi are known to be stoic and unemotional, but this is somewhat a façade over a more sensitive interior. They rarely interact with other species and aren’t very good at it when they do. Both telepathy and precognition can often harm more than help, painting them as crazed wizards with mysterious powers that should be feared.
csg_iktotchi.language: Iktotchi are perfectly capable of speaking Basic, but they also have their own language of Iktotchese.
csg_iktotchi.homeworld: Iktotch is the third moon of the gas giant Iktotchon, an arid moon of windy deserts in the Expansion Region. The Iktotchi developed their precognition, in fact, to predict the winds and storms. It is highly separated from the rest of galactic society and blockaded by the Empire. This is thanks to the wishes of both Iktotchi and Imperials. The precognition is strongest for Iktotchi when on Iktotch and decreases with distance.
csg_iktotchi.description: Iktotchi give off a harsh and cold appearance, and they are very intimidating thanks to their horns. They are gifted in both precognition and telepathy, which gave them a good relationship with the Jedi Order.
csg_iktotchi.sidebar_text: Just because they possess abilities similar to Force-sensitives does not mean all Iktotchi are Force-sensitive. However, they do have strong traditions in the Force, as first taught them by the Kwa long before they were civilized. Precognition has served them well throughout history: When Republic scouts first discovered the planet, the Iktotchi had already inscribed the Republic logo into the planet’s surface to welcome them. While they maintained a good relationship with Jedi and many served the Order, they lived in relative isolation. They foresaw the Clone Wars and rise of the Empire but could do little to stop it. They did, however, prepare for a massive wave of immigration as people fled Imperial rule. They now live in isolation, safe from the Empire. While Iktotchi can very well have predictions of a number of future events, the Yuuzhan Vong War is one notable exception, as they are entirely disconnected from the Force.

csg_inleshat.name: Inleshat

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater, but may not breathe in air. Treat air as a dangerous atmosphere of rating 1.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on auditory Perception checks. Double all sonic damage and, at the GM’s discretion, increase sonic damage from 0 to 1.

csg_inleshat.physiology: Though Iskalonians have a humanoid build, they are actually fully aquatic, and they suffocate in an oxygen atmosphere outside of the water. If they need to travel offworld, they must wear a suit that provides them with a water-filled helmet. Their skin comes in shades of lime, yellow, and orange, and their hair is usually in lighter shades of yellow or green. Their large circular eyes, on the other hand, can come in just about any color. While Inleshat lack a nose, the males have fleshy protrusions above their mouth or on their chin somewhat resembling human mustaches and beards. They are further recognizable by their excellent smiles with teeth that are straight and pristine white. Their ears are pointed and highly attuned, to the point that they can hear some underwater sounds as far as kilometers away. Inleshat are typically tall and well-built, and they have webbed hands that aid in their swimming. While most have three fingers, it is also possible for them to have four or five fingers.
csg_inleshat.society: Inleshat have a natural charisma and leadership ability, which has over time made them into the most prominent species on their planet Iskalon. They share with sixteen other sentient aquatic races and together, are known as the Iskalonian School. The School is currently led by an Inleshat named Primor, who casts himself as a conduit for the people’s wants rather than a monarch. All Inleshat are eager to please others and improve their social standing, even the members of the species that are seen as the most rebellious. They are very friendly to strangers, often too friendly, especially since they often have a hard time understanding the words and customs of species who dwell on land. They aren’t shy about anything and have little respect for privacy, perhaps because of their superb hearing. While their society is currently fairly prosperous, some of them have been historically targeted as slaves, such as by Hugo Bartyn.
csg_inleshat.language: Like all species in the Iskalonian School, Inleshat speak Iskalonian, although almost all of them also know Basic. They refer to children or youth as “fries.”
csg_inleshat.homeworld: Though they hail from Drexel II, Inleshat now have Iskalon as their homeworld. It is a temperate world completely covered by oceans, although its sea levels briefly lowered during the Cold War between the Sith and Republic, allowing a few land masses with caves to breach the surface. It currently has a city called Pavillion which includes a spaceport where the aquatic species and air-breathers can interact, but this town will be destroyed by a tidal wave. It will actually be the Empire behind this incident, causing it to attempt to kill the visiting Luke Skywalker. Afterwards, the Iskalonians will be significantly more isolated from galactic affairs.
csg_inleshat.description: Aquatic near-humans, the Inleshat immigrated to Iskalon, where they have become natural leaders in a diverse School of fellow aquatic species. They are outgoing and always eager to please.
csg_inleshat.sidebar_text: While the Inleshat have a prominent role on Iskalon, this was not always the case. In fact, they actually originated on another ocean planet, Drexel II. However, their society there suffered from a horrible cataclysm about five millennia ago, and they were on the verge of extinction. They were saved by unknown benefactors who helped to relocate the bulk of the entire species and resettle them on Iskalon, alongside the other species of the Iskalonian School, who also came from different planets and were dealing with disasters of their own. In any case, the move has seemed to be for the better, and Drexel II remains without sentient inhabitants to this day.

csg_iotran.name: Iotran

special_abilities.name: Militaristic
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Body Guard.”

csg_iotran.physiology: Iotrans are a people with brown or black skin. While they have no visible ears, they are capable of hearing. They also lack hair. Iotrans have yellow eyes and a broad but flat nose. While bald, their head is decorated by small horns around their eyes. These spikes also appear on their elbows, shoulders, and hands. Their skin is covered in spots that have a slightly different color. They are also often wrinkled. Their hands have just four fingers, although they are perfectly capable of effectively gripping technology. Their feet have just two toes each. While they are fairly average in size, Iotrans tend to be strong and tough thanks to their military-based culture, which ensures that almost all of them are in excellent physical condition.
csg_iotran.society: Iotran society values strength and stability above all else. In most ways, this is reflected through their incredibly large focus on military and police occupations. This can still create conflict in their political views, however. For example, most support the Empire, as it exemplifies the centralized strength and military power that the Iotrans find necessary. However, others consider the Republic to be a more stable form of government, simply because it lasted for longer. Their technology is still very primitive, and many still use slugthrowers or surface vehicles. Their droids and computers are also much simpler. Iotrans prefer military occupations in stunning numbers. At most times, about half of their homeworld’s population is somehow involved with the Iotran Police Force, or IPF, which enforces the laws on their planet. From an early age, they are trained for the military or police. They are ruled by the highest ranking officials in the IPF. Many Iotrans are inducted after 14 seasons, which is about 18 standard years. Since there is such a great supply of law enforcement on their homeworld, most venture offworld as mercenaries, policemen, or bodyguards.
csg_iotran.language: Iotrans speak Tranese, a very precise language. While Iotrans find Basic to be imprecise and confusing, they typically understand the benefits of learning it.
csg_iotran.homeworld: Iotrans come from Iotra, a windy Outer Rim world that is mostly industrial. It is the fifth planet in its star system.
csg_iotran.description: The Iotrans are militaristic and value order and justice. They have extremely high numbers employed as soldiers or policemen, and the Iotran Bracemen bring “justice" (often controversially) on other planets.
csg_iotran.sidebar_text: Many of the more notable Iotrans are those who are the Iotran Bracemen. These people are often taken from the best of the best in the IPF. The Iotran Bracemen bring justice on other worlds according to Iotran laws, without respect for where they have jurisdiction or when there are different laws on other planets. While they sometimes track down fugitives and bring them to local law enforcement, the actions of Iotran Bracemen often include incidents of vigilante justice that are far more morally questionable. Especially considering their lack of any jurisdiction, the Iotran Bracemen create a great many diplomatic incidents.

csg_ishi_tib.name: Ishi Tib

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove penalties for underwater movement. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Water Dependence
special_abilities.description: For every 24 hours without bathing in salt water, reduce wound threshold by 2. Remove penalties after bathing in salt water.

csg_ishi_tib.physiology: Ishi Tib are aquatic creatures with green skin. They have a head that strongly resembles a five-pointed star: A beak forms one point, the golden eyes on stalks atop their head make the next two, and their cheek pouches also resemble two more points. Their lungs act as gills, which they do not have externally. They have an acute sense of smell from their two nostrils, although they have no nose. The Ishi Tib are best in humid conditions and need water to survive. If they do not bathe themselves in salt water similar to that of Tibrin for more than a day, their leathery skin begins to crack, and they bleed both internally and externally. Eventually, this will cause death. Their feet are flat for swimming, and their hands have only two stubby fingers each.
csg_ishi_tib.society: Ishi Tib live in underwater cities on coral reefs, evolved to farm for food such as fish, seaweed, and crustaceans. Like fish, they call their communities “schools,” which have up to 10,000 Ishi Tib. The schools have a community oriented culture, as they have no families or marriages. The school governs reproduction, and after the fertilized eggs are hatched in mass hatcheries near the reefs, children are then raised communally. Ishi Tib are quiet, disciplined, and meticulous in their work. Many find work as accountants, executives, or managers thanks to their drive to get things done, careful planning, and almost perfectionist nature. Offworld, they can be somewhat naïve, often bonding quickly with whomever they can find. This can be to their detriment, as other species aren’t always as communally-oriented as the Ishi Tib.
csg_ishi_tib.language: Ishi Tib speak Tibrinese, a language of squeals and honks with a hieroglyphic alphabet. They can also speak Basic.
csg_ishi_tib.homeworld: Ishi Tib come from Tibrin, a Mid Rim planet of shallow oceans. It has almost no axial tilt, so its seasons are extremely stable, and currents efficiently circulate heat, making it temperate almost everywhere. They mostly live in coral reefs and sandbars, and environmental concerns mean that the planet still has very little technology. Tibrin was aligned with the Confederacy during the Clone Wars, since the Republic let the brutal dictator Suribran Tu hold power, and he was publicly executed by Dooku. It is now under Imperial control.
csg_ishi_tib.description: Aquatic creatures who live in large schools, the Ishi Tib are known for their organizational abilities. They are extremely reverent for nature and place way more value than other species in ecological sustainability.
csg_ishi_tib.sidebar_text: Ishi Tib are well known for showing a reverence for the environment. To most outsiders, this is viewed as more of an obsession, which holds them back. To Ishi Tib, it is simply a motivation and a purpose. Any Ishi Tib who does not share these values would likely be an outcast and might wish to find a new life elsewhere. On Tibrin, they focus their laws on how to best protect the environment and not waste natural resources. New technologies are carefully tested for their impact on the planet. Although their organizational skills put them in high demand, Ishi Tib are often unwilling to take on certain jobs over concern for a company’s environmental policies.

csg_ithorian.name: Ithorian

special_abilities.name: Ithorian Bellows
special_abilities.description: May attack using Resilience, dealing 6 base damage as strain to all within short range, and have a Crit rating of 4. Have Concussive 1 and Slow Firing 2, but suffer 3 strain when using this attack.

csg_ithorian.physiology: Ithorians are large, mammalian herbivores that average two meters in height. Their leathery skin is brown, and they have a long neck that curves upward before reaching a T-shaped head, so some give them the nickname Hammerheads. Females have two humps at the back of their head; males have one. At the sides of their head are black eyes, and they are hairless. They have four throats and a mouth on either side of their neck, which allows them to speak in stereo and roar loudly enough to damage the ears of those nearby. They have four-toed feet and five-fingered hands and tend to be less coordinated.
csg_ithorian.society: Ithorians are extremely peaceful creatures who are very respectful of life. They especially value plant life, treating vegetation with excellent care as part of their worship to Mother Jungle, which is led by their herd’s High Priest. They both befriend and worship the semi-sentient, telepathic bafforr trees in the jungles below them, in addition to caring for a multitude of other flora. They are completely pacifistic, and most devote their life towards ecology or the study of plant life. Despite their unique focus, they are still quite conversational and sociable, possessing a curiosity and respect for the beliefs of others. They are gregarious by nature, so many explore and make new gardens across the galaxy. In order to protect their world, they organize into massive, self-sustaining, autonomous herd ships that float above the surface. The garden-filled ships have no weapons, but they do boast powerful shields that were coveted by the Empire until High Priest Momaw Nadon was forced at gunpoint to give away the designs. The herds participate in a communal government and gather together at the Herd Meet each season, which is every five standard years. In this grand gathering, they hover their ships within meters of the treetops and celebrate with a festive, regal ceremony. The Ithorians are generous and many have trading centers that give away things to the poor.
csg_ithorian.language: Ithorese is a musical, harmonious tongue that requires four throats to speak, but many Ithorians can also speak Basic with a “stereo” effect.
csg_ithorian.homeworld: Ithorians come from the lush rainforests of Ithor, a Mid Rim world. They hold their planet to be sacred and protect it carefully. It is pristine, without any touch of civilization, as Ithorians now live in floating cities known as herd ships. The surface is so protected that going down to it is forbidden unless an Ithorian has “heard the call” of their deity, Mother Jungle, in which case they tend to the surface forever as a priest. It will be rendered barren during the Yuuzhan Vong War, and the bereaving Ithorian herd ships will disperse.
csg_ithorian.description: While many live in space for practical reasons, the Ithorians do so in order to protect the sacred jungles of their homeworld. They are peaceful and pacifistic, so few ever kill. When they do need to fight, they often use their four powerful throats to bellow.
csg_ithorian.sidebar_text: The Law of Life is one of the most sacred Ithorian values. It states that for every plant harvested, two shall be grown to replace it. However, it also extends to animals and sentients: Should an Ithorian kill anyone, they will attempt to create two clones. In one case, they captured “Spore,” a person who murdered hundreds. Since they could not clone him, they only imprisoned him and buried him when he died.

csg_iyra.name: Iyra

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Camouflage
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on all Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Extra Eyes
special_abilities.description: Add boost on visual Perception checks. May see in all directions.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn when on land.

csg_iyra.physiology: Iyra are symmetrical, aquatic creatures who grow tentacles and eye stalks in pairs as they age. At birth, they have only four tentacles and four eyes. Their build is unique, with a large mouth on their underside and all of their organs in a single central body. They are about half of a meter tall, but their tentacles can span a diameter of one or two meters. As aquatic creatures, they can breathe underwater, thrive in humid atmospheres, and swim very quickly. However, they are vulnerable to dry conditions, and they cannot move very effectively on land, as they must slowly drag themselves with their tentacles. Because they lack bones, they can somewhat contract and expand their body. They can also control their skin color and even create textures or patterns on their skin.
csg_iyra.society: Iyra are wise and philosophical, but they are also extremely arrogant. They typically don’t like other species, although they are somewhat more amiable toward species with extra limbs. They mate twice each year in a ritual in which males change their skin color and perform elaborate dances. The females then choose a partner, although they do not remain together for long, and the children are raised by others of the four-tentacled caste.
csg_iyra.language: The Iyra speak a native language whose written form contains swirls and dots. Those who need to can also speak Basic.
csg_iyra.homeworld: The Iyra hail from an Outer Rim water world, F’tral. It is a successful trade world that exports gravity projectors and inertial compensators. Because carnivorous plants dominate the few land masses, their cities are underwater. Those who leave F’tral almost always live on water worlds, although they sometimes settle for low-gravity planets. Those living on land often use “floating ponds,” repulsor chairs equipped with a tank of water.
csg_iyra.description: Cephalopods with radial symmetry who struggle dramatically on land, the Iyra have a caste system based on the number of tentacles they have. All are wise but arrogant, yet they are subservient to those with more tentacles. Since they grow more tentacles with age, this is seen as a fair system.
csg_iyra.sidebar_text: Iyra society is divided into strict castes based on the number of tentacles that they have. Those with fewer tentacles always defer to those who have more, but few disagree with this arrangement: Since they gain tentacles as they grow older, they all can move up in society. Those who lose tentacles move down a caste, as the Iyra believe that such events demonstrate carelessness. They also cut off the corresponding eyestalk after losing a tentacle. When Iyra with the same amount of tentacles disagree, they often discuss peacefully. However, they sometimes settle matters via duel, which ends when one of them loses a tentacle and is forced to defer. One side effect of this system is that when among other species with four limbs, even young Iyra almost always consider themselves to be superior.

csg_jawa.name: Jawa

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Utinni!”

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Olfaxes
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks, and may identify other Jawas using smell.

csg_jawa.physiology: Jawas are short, rodent-like creatures with glowing, yellow eyes. They are almost always entirely shrouded in dark brown robes, and only their furred hands are visible. They have a shrunken face, though few have ever been able to see them. Jawas are well-known to be odorous. Most species find the smell repulsive, but this potent odor means a lot to the sense of smell of a Jawa. It can tell lots of things, ranging from mood and maturity to ancestry and lineage. They can even tell health or their last meal based on this one simple sniff. This is mostly the result of an aversion to bathing, which Jawas consider to be a waste of water. They also boast exceptional night vision and a strong immune system. Their high body temperature results in a fast metabolism, and an efficient digestive system allows them to survive almost entirely off of one food: the hubba gourd. Though sour, they grow well on Tatooine.
csg_jawa.society: Jawas are timid scavengers that live communally. They travel Tatooine in search of scrap, which rusts very slowly due to a lack of moisture. They have a reputation for being good with mechanics and for finding a use for anything. They also are known as scavengers and thieves, though they find this to be a compliment. They travel in Sandcrawlers, old vessels that are big and slow. They interact to trade with other clans at swap meets, where they trade scrap, navigation data, and even marriages. These are arranged by parents in order to ensure genetic diversity and make a good profit while they’re at it. The Great Swap Meet is held annually, where every Jawa clan travels to the Dune Sea just before storm season. In addition to sandcrawlers, Jawas have large fortresses that protect them. They almost never fight anything directly and instead hide within their fortresses or sandcrawlers. Jawas have a complex clan system and a hierarchy through which information is passed.
csg_jawa.language: Jawaese is the high-pitched Jawa language, which requires scents to create. The more simplified Jawa Trade Language is used to interact with customers. They cannot speak Basic.
csg_jawa.homeworld: Jawas come from the desert world of Tatooine. It is a backwater Outer Rim world with twin suns. This heat, combined with a lack of water, makes it inhospitable to almost all who come. In addition to Jawas, there are the warlike Tusken Raiders, some moisture farmers, and a large criminal element.
csg_jawa.description: Jawas are extremely timid nomads who prowl the deserts of Tatooine in massive sandcrawlers. They are skilled mechanics and expert scavengers, talents which they use to trade for what they need.
csg_jawa.sidebar_text: Shamans are a powerful influence in Jawa clans. Each clan has a Shaman to oversee all of the major day-to-day operations. While Shamans are always female, females otherwise receive very little respect in Jawa society. The Shamans are often consulted for their wisdom, since they are believed to possess many abilities. This includes foresight, spells, hexes, and blessings. To become a Shaman, a Jawa must either have a Force ability that they can use to perform magic or overcome an illness while receiving a hallucinatory vision. Some Shamans are also trained by a current Shaman and chosen as a successor.

csg_jenet.name: Jenet

special_abilities.name: Low-Light Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Accurate Memories
special_abilities.description: Never forget anything, even trivial details.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Brawl +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks. Remove penalties for eating spoiled or rotten food.

csg_jenet.physiology: Jenets are a species of rodents notorious for sheer ugliness. Shorter in size and typically thinner, the Jenets are also very flexible: They can even dislocate limbs and separate bones in their cranium when needed. This allows them to squeeze through a gap as wide as the distance between their whiskers. Their digits all in end claws, and they have four-toed feet. Their skin is pink and oily, but the back of their head and chin is covered in white, gray, or red hair. Their head features an elongated muzzle and includes a sensitive nose at the front, keen red eyes that see well in the dark, sharp yellow teeth, and pointed ears. They have an incredible memory which is accurate, detailed, and completely infallible. As scavengers, they can eat almost anything. Even though they live for about 70 years, they can reach adulthood in a decade and produce multiple litters of babies every year.
csg_jenet.society: Jenets are known to be very obnoxious, and they are obsessed with trivialities. They never discard anything, and they typically store their garbage for later use. As they are scavengers by nature, most of them survive by sorting through large piles of garbage called Community Heaps. They do not hunt for survival, although they will scavenge off of corpses which are already dead. They dislike manual labor, although they have a healthy work ethic and great attention to detail. Although they were typically prey, their cunning allowed them to kill off all of their predators in an event called the Great Conquest, which is remembered through long ballads.
csg_jenet.language: Jenets speak Jenet, a language with no written version. It is composed of high pitched squeaks and squeals. Their name typically includes a list of their accomplishments. To prevent deceit, Jenets never introduce themselves; they can only be introduced by two third parties who know their name.
csg_jenet.homeworld: Jenets hail from the Outer Rim planet of Garban, which is in the Tau Sakar system. It is covered in Community Heaps which are managed by their incredibly complex bureaucratic government. An Imperial presence takes some Jenets offworld as slaves, and these Jenets have been selectively bred to be unintelligent and obedient.
csg_jenet.description: Rodents who typically live as scavengers, the Jenets have a number of unique customs, and their impressive memory allows them to be obsessive about all of them. They always greet one another with insults, which they take with pride: As they see it, being famous enough to be insulted is a good thing.
csg_jenet.sidebar_text: Although it is common knowledge that Jenets care little for tact, this isn’t entirely true: In fact, they have an entirely different standard for politeness. It derives from their incredible memory, which allows Jenets to hold grudges indefinitely. This means that many Jenets will begrudge someone over gossip that they heard years ago. Since they have little reservations about insults, Jenets will constantly bring up these criticisms, even if they are untrue. As such, they typically greet each other with insults, and they take pride in it: The way they see it, every insult is a demonstration of fame.

csg_kaleesh.name: Kaleesh

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

csg_kaleesh.physiology: The Kaleesh are reptilian humanoids who typically have red or brown skin. Their hands each have four claws, two of which are opposable thumbs. Their feet have five toes. They also possess excellent night vision from thermal pits beneath their yellow eyes. Almost all of them keep their face hidden behind a traditional mask, but those that don’t reveal two upward tusks in their mouth, nostrils without a nose, a hairless scalp, (though they do have eyebrows) and upward pointing ears. Their chin also has downward pointing tusks. While the notable Kaleesh cyborg General Grievous had a digitigrade stance, most Kaleesh who do not have such cybernetics use a plantigrade one.
csg_kaleesh.society: Kaleesh are a warlike people, through and through. They are also highly spiritual. Perhaps a result of the frequency of war, death is very important in their society. From skeleton-like masks to elaborate burials, and even worshipping dead Kaleesh as gods if they have done great things, it is clear that death is relevant. Though many of these gods are ancient ancestors, General Grievous is one of the more recent additions. Their holiest temple is called Shrupak, and they have fiercely defended it during conflicts. Of all the rituals, war may be the most sacred. Most view it as their calling in life, and war between tribes is both sacred and essential. The tribes do sometimes unite against a common enemy, which they can find relatively easily in the various nearby planets. Despite this, they have little by way of unified government. A more unique aspect of tir culture is that they are polygynous, a practice in which males can have multiple wives.
csg_kaleesh.language: Kaleesh speak Kaleesh, and some know Basic. Because of their isolation, Basic speakers are few and far between.
csg_kaleesh.homeworld: Kalee is a humid world of rainforests and beaches in Wild Space. It also has some more arid regions as well as rocky ones of cliffs and canyons. Animals such as mumuu and karabbacs act as prey for the Kaleesh, who use them for meat, hides, and bones.
csg_kaleesh.description: Most notable as the people who brought the great warrior General Grievous into the galaxy, Kaleesh are a warlike people who worship death as part of their religion. They are organized into tribes that occasionally unite against a common enemy.
csg_kaleesh.sidebar_text: Kaleesh have always been a primitive people, mostly fighting with spears and swords. This changed, however, when they were armed by the Republic. This was done as a way for the Republic to indirectly attack the Bitthævrians, an independant planet that the Kaleesh also feared. The Kaleesh again found war shortly before the Clone Wars, but this time, they were not aided by the Republic. Invaded by Yam’rii slavers, the Kaleesh fought back in a brutal war. Their leader, Qymaen jai Sheelal, then invaded the other Yam’rii colonies. In desperation, the Yam’rii used their political influence to wager a corrupt bargain that would cause the Republic to step in on behalf of the Yam’rii. The Kaleesh could not defeat both, and victory turned to defeat. The Yam’rii retook Kalee, continuing to take Kaleesh as slaves. Harsh punishments by the Senate then created an even more strained relationship between the Kaleesh and the Republic. Sheelal would go on to become Grievous, and Kalee a CIS world. For their part in the war, the Kaleesh are punished by the Empire.

csg_kalleran.name: Kalleran

special_abilities.name: Hypersensitive Antennae
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Heightened Awareness.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic Heritage
special_abilities.description: Remove all movement penalties for being underwater.

csg_kalleran.physiology: Kallerans are a tall, thin, and flexible people who have a distantly aquatic heritage. They cannot breathe underwater, but they swim well and have retained the ability to breathe directly through their greenish skin. Because of this ability, they have no need for a nose. Kallerans have excellent senses thanks to their antennae, which smell and hear, and the fins on their head, which are actually giant ears. Kalleran are strong despite their slim build because they have very dense muscles, but this compact nature also makes them far less durable. They have three prehensile digits on both their hands and feet, so they rarely use shoes in order to use their toes.
csg_kalleran.society: Kallerans are known to be extremely individualistic, with little focus on collective success or teamwork. They are typically selfish, rarely acting out of moral responsibility, and they care little about ideological causes, including governments. They have little interest in galactic politics, and they have never even united under one government as a species.
csg_kalleran.language: Kallerans almost always know Basic, but they still learn one of their native languages, which are specific to regions but share many similarities. Imperials generally refer to these languages as Kall languages. Much of their vocabulary uses antennae movements, so Kallerans can communicate silently, but with limited vocabulary.
csg_kalleran.homeworld: Kaller is a temperate but somewhat dry planet with two suns. It has very unpredictable weather because of this strange orbit. They mostly live in smaller towns near rivers, and traditional homes are made from stone in order to withstand the harsh weather.
csg_kalleran.description: Though surprisingly frail, Kallerans are athletic and have both prehensile toes and sensitive antennae. They are an independent people, so they have mostly ignored the many governments and organizations that have tried to colonize their homeworld.
csg_kalleran.sidebar_text: The Kalleran planet of Kaller has never had a single ruler, but many offworld organizations have held power on smaller parts of it. Because of its location and natural resources, it is worthwhile to have a stake on it, and the Kallerans have dealt with every type of colonist under the sun, including the Pykes and the Mandalorians. Some offworlders have ruled territories as warlords, some have taken over land peacefully to conduct business, and some have worked alongside the Kallerans to benefit mutually. Some areas with little to offer have been left alone, and the Kallerans have owned them for all of their history. Many Kalleran organizations and governments have worked to profit off of the offworlders, pitting them against one another, striking deals, or taking part in new industries. All Kallerans have benefited in some ways from technology imports and overall advancements to society because of offworld influence. Recently, one organization to take a claim on Kaller was the Confederacy of Independent Systems, but they were repelled by the Republic. Surprisingly, the Imperials have mostly ignored the Kallerans. Most Kallerans accept the offworlders as an inevitability, and they have become tolerant of other species. Regardless, many have come to dislike the constant drama, and such Kalleran will often take to the stars in search of a more stable life.
csg_kalleran._provenance_note: The Kalleran species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU.

csg_kamarian.name: Kamarian

special_abilities.name: Cavers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Water Storage
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for arid or hot conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions. Can survive for 25 days without water.

special_abilities.name: Water Storage
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for arid or hot conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions. Can survive for 50 days without water.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Extra Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_kamarian.physiology: Kamarians are insects with a segmented prehensile tail and six bracia: two legs and four arms. Their exoskeleton stores water, allowing them to survive for several weeks without drinking, and their hardy physiology is adapted for hot desert environments. Their legs end in clawed, four-toed feet and they also have two clawed fingers on each hand, making them dangerous warriors even when unarmed. They have large compound eyes dominating their visage, and their mouth has mandibles surrounding it. They come in various colors depending on their subspecies, and most are about a meter and a half tall on average, although the light-colored Kamar Badlander race is a few decimeters shorter. The Badlanders also boast an even greater tolerance for arid climates.
csg_kamarian.society: Kamarians live in various feudal cities called tk’skquas, and they are prone to warring against one another. The races each have their own cultures and levels of technological development. The most numerous group, known as the mountain dwellers, built homes in cave systems and developed atomic level technology prior to their recent first contact with the Galactic Empire. On the opposite end, the Kamar Badlanders are the most primitive, using only simple tools and weapons such as spears.
csg_kamarian.language: Kamarians have their own language and rarely learn Basic.
csg_kamarian.homeworld: Kamarians come from the Wild Space planet of Kamar, which is near the Corporate Sector. It is an arid, sun-baked world covered by both mountains and Badlands, and it features a variety of deadly fauna, such as bloodsniffers, howlrunners, and nightswifts.
csg_kamarian.description: Four-armed insects with varying races that have their own cultures and technologies, the Kamarians are adapted to harsh desert conditions, and they can survive for weeks without water.
csg_kamarian.sidebar_text: In 2 BBY, enterprising smugglers Han Solo and Chewbacca set up a small holotheater on Kamar among the Badlanders in exchange for local crafts. He showcased a boring documentary called Varn, World of Water to the locals, who didn’t even understand its language. However, the Kamarians were in awe. Solo got his friend Sonniod to bring a new film and keep the revenue rolling but failed to realize they’d developed a cult-like reverence for the original: Varn and its waters were seen as the afterlife, and they destroyed the sacrilegious holoprojector when it played the new film. Solo fled, becoming known as the Solohan the Deceiver, an angelic traitor in the restless Badlanders’ new mythology. Sonniod would eventually return with a new projector and a copy of the original film, setting up a priesthood and helping the Cult of Varn spread. Some attempted revenge on Solo, but he escaped their capture.

csg_kaminoan.name: Kaminoan
csg_kaminoan.physiology: Kaminoans are tall, thin creatures who have evolved from aquatic swamp dwellers. Their skin is a bright white, and they have a long neck. While Kaminoans are hairless, males have their head topped with a spiked ridge. They have nostrils but no nose, and their mouth is tiny, as they need little food. Their almond-shaped eyes are black with colored pupils, and they can see in the ultraviolet spectrum. This means that the whites that appear on their skin and in their architecture are actually several different colors to them. They have long, three-fingered hands, as well as very long legs and a small torso. Genetically speaking, the Kaminoans are one of the galaxy’s most homogeneous species. All are created via a cloning process that introduces only a limited amount of genetic variance.
csg_kaminoan.society: Kaminoans are polite but quietly believe themselves to be better than all other species. They are cold and calculating, not prone to displays of emotion or empathy, which is an advantage in business. They sell their creations as slaves, sending them to work dangerous jobs in armies or mines. The Kaminoans are obsessed with genetic perfection and willing to do anything to help evolve their species to be better. They only respect others who feel the same about their species, but they rarely let it show in their dealings. Otherwise, they look down on the “frail” species who tolerate deformities in their genome, only interacting with offworlders for business in most circumstances. The Kaminoan cloning industry was most famous for their highly successful work creating a Grand Army of the Republic, but neither them nor others have been able to reach such greatness again. A decade after the Clone Wars, they attempted to use Fett clones for their own purposes, seceding from the Empire, but the rebellion was quickly crushed by stormtroopers led by one of the Kaminoans’ own creations: Boba Fett. A few cloners were captured and brought back to Coruscant to serve the Empire.
csg_kaminoan.language: Kaminoans speak Kaminoan, but since they need raw materials from the wider galaxy, most know Basic. They typically speak it with a gentle tone.
csg_kaminoan.homeworld: Kamino is a watery planet off of many maps and outside the galactic disk. Kaminoans treasure its rainy autumns, loathing the heat and bright sunlight in other seasons. Their cities were once on land, but increased rainfall has now flooded the entire globe, and Kaminoan cities must now float above the waves. Their submerged former dwellings remain preserved as sacred places, and pilgrimages to these ruins are some of the only times they show any sentimentality.
csg_kaminoan.description: The Kaminoans are obsessed with genetic perfection more than anything else. They're cloners (good ones, too) who have no qualms about the enslavement of whatever sentients they create. They are extremely cold and emotionless.
csg_kaminoan.sidebar_text: Kaminoans have a caste system based on eye color, which they consider to be an important trait. Gray pupils are the best, and Kaminoans with these are given important roles in leadership and administration. Yellow eyes make up the middle class, filling jobs in the sciences that they are so well known for. Blue eyes are the lower class, doing manual labor. Green eyes are the worst, and babies with green eyes are quickly executed. These roles are a well-established part of Kaminoan society, and any who would speak out against them would quickly become an outcast.

csg_kari.name: Kari

special_abilities.name: Hardened Carapaces
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Hive Minds
special_abilities.description: May form a hive mind with all other Kari within 100 meters, sharing all information. When part of a hive mind with more than 5 Kari, gain +1 Intellect, and when part of a hive mind with more than 50 Kari, gain +2 Intellect.

csg_kari.physiology: Kari are bipedal insects with a black protective exoskeleton. At only one meter tall on average, they are relatively short, but they have a bulky, pear-shaped body supported by thick hind legs. They also have a stubby tail and thinner arms which end in small opposable thumbs plus two more fingers on each hand. They also have small spikes on their knees and on the backs of their shins. A roughly cylindrical shape makes up the Kari head, with their shell hanging over the top half. Their brain has a very limited capacity, and a lone Kari is barely sentient. However, they possess the ability to form hive minds, with the resulting combination becoming more intelligent than any of its individual members would be on their own. Like many insects, they have a very high birth rate, but in an industrialized society with fewer dangers, there is little to prevent them from rapidly increasing their population.
csg_kari.society: Kari society is massive and densely populated, and feeding their entire planet is a massive job that consumes much of their collective focus. This is not to say that they are entirely agrarian, as many hive minds have used their significant intelligence to develop electronic devices and various appliances. However, the devices are mostly for exporting, as few Kari can afford to keep their own luxuries and need all the money they can get to feed themselves. Their society is organized into families called Hatches, which generally include 20 to 30 individual Kari forming a hive mind together. Because they can grow their species at such a massive rate, the Empire has a serious fear of the Kari. To keep the population in check, Kari are strictly forbidden from developing space travel, and the freighters which visit their planet to trade with them are not allowed to transport the Kari either. While it certainly could be possible for one or two Kari to slip through the cracks, they aren’t particularly competent when they’re in such small numbers.
csg_kari.language: The details of the Kari’s native languages are unknown, but given their isolation, it can be assumed that few know Basic.
csg_kari.homeworld: Kari hail from the Outer Rim world of Karideph, which is located in the Minos Cluster. All land area on the planet has been settled, where it hosts either gardens or massive cities, which can reach so high that they need to be pressurized. With over 88 billion Kari, only a small percent can regularly experience these heights, and many live in the depths of the cities’ lower levels, where the sun does not reach, or even in an extensive network of underground tunnels. These tunnels house the majority of the population and can go as deep as twelve kilometers. All trade goes through the single massive spaceport in Capital City, and the planet has just one college called the University of Universal Thought.
csg_kari.description: Kari have a massive but isolated population on Karideph, where the bulky, hive-minded insects live in cramped cities that extend deep underground. They have massive farms devoted to feeding their planet and export many electronic appliances.
csg_kari.sidebar_text: The Kari are not a culture known for writing, and much of their history is still preserved orally. Every Hatch is careful to preserve their own history, which is a serious responsibility generally given to their greatest singer. The history of the Hatch is turned into a song, which is memorized and passed down through generations of Bards, who are also responsible for singing their history to other Hatches, should they need to introduce themselves.

csg_karkarodon.name: Karkarodon

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Powerful Jaws
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 3 advantage to bite, inducing a Critical Injury and also adding the Pierce 1 and Vicious 2 qualities.

csg_karkarodon.physiology: Karkarodons are shark-like humanoids who are deadly predators. Their large body is very muscular, making them very effective in a brawl. However, Karkarodons are carnivorous predators, so these brawls often purely serve the purpose of subduing or distracting prey before their jaws do the real damage. Karkarodons have a large mouth with dozens of small but sharp teeth. Their head is flat at the top with nostrils in between their grayish eyes. They also have gill slits, which allow them to breathe both underwater and on land. Their hands and feet and webbed to allow them to effectively walk on land as well as swim. Their body is blue on their back and white or gray on the chest and front, which helps camouflage them.
csg_karkarodon.society: Karkarodons value independence and determination. Children are hatched from eggs without knowing their family and have the instincts to survive on their own by nomadically hunting fish. Many are solo predators for their entire life, but a few make contact with their rare settlements, where they take advantage of basic technologies that they often acquire from offworlders in exchange for work as hired muscle. But for all their fearsomeness, Karkarodons in the wider galaxy are also known as fierce champions of democracy. This is because, to them, monarchs are highly dangerous. Karkarodon psychology causes them to become extremely sadistic and egotistical should they have a chance at power, even if they were once benevolent.
csg_karkarodon.language: Many Karkarodons in the wild do not have a concept of language or speech, and while most of their settlements have learned Basic from offworlders.
csg_karkarodon.homeworld: Karkaris is a water world in the Outer Rim with a few small towns and scattered islands, but mostly open oceans that the Karkarodons hunt alone. Transit to or from the planet is carefully monitored by the Empire, who is wary of the Karkarodons’ prowess. The largest of the settlements is Skreej’s Landing, a mostly underwater fishing colony on an island coastline. It has Karkaris’s only major spaceport, allowing human and Vurk colonists to live alongside the Karkarodons.
csg_karkarodon.description: Karkarodons are aquatic predators descending from sharks. They are physically strong and have powerful jaws, making them very dangerous. Some can be power hungry, so they have learned the hard way how dangerous monarchies and dictatorships can be.
csg_karkarodon.sidebar_text: Once the Clone Wars started, the Karkarodons became shocked that the Republic wouldn’t allow planets the right of self-government. They showed widespread support for the Confederacy, and many joined their forces. While some fought as soldiers, others became an elite group known as the Wigg Assassins, who tried to kill monarchs and dictators of all sorts in the name of the Confederacy. Most notably, one was successful in assassinating a Mon Calamari monarch. Many also tried to kill Suribran Tu, a dictator on Tibrin. Most of the Wigg Assassins have been executed by the Republic or Empire for war crimes, but some still live in hiding.
csg_karkarodon._provenance_note: The Karkarodon species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_kel_dor.name: Kel Dor

special_abilities.name: Helium Breathers
special_abilities.description: Need a helium mask to breathe in a normal environment. Oxygen is a dangerous atmosphere of rating 4. Need goggles to see in a normal environment.

csg_kel_dor.physiology: Kel Dors are vermillion-skinned creatures that are poisoned by oxygen, which causes irritation and eventually suffocation. They require helium along with another gas specific to Dorin to breathe, and they need goggles to protect their eyes in other atmospheres. Without the goggles, they have dark eyes, although Force-sensitive ones have silver eyes. They also wear a tightly sealed mask over their face to breathe and amplify their voice. Behind it is a nose that is just short of beak and a gaping opening that transitions into a large mouth. They have no teeth, instead having upper and lower hard palettes, which are only visible when their lips are pulled back. Their wrinkled head has no hair, and there are extrasensory organs to the sides of their head which contain part of their brain and give them quicker reactions. These terminate in four small gray tusks that surround the mouth. They have four-fingered hands with dark nails, and they are weaker than most species.
csg_kel_dor.society: Kel Dors are quiet and unassuming, but they value justice and use it firmly. Viewing morals in black and white, they punish harshly, as even stealing food to stay alive can result in a death sentence. Despite this, Kel Dors are also known for hospitality, and they get along well in large households. They often live with at least three generations, and it is very common practice for children to take one of their parent’s professions. They offer free public education, and their society is highly proficient in the sciences, particularly when it comes to making atmospheric containment devices. They also have very high rates of Force-sensitivity and have developed a Force tradition called the Baron Do Sages. While the Sages only used their power to control weather at first, they became more versatile, and at their peak, they were very commonly employed as advisors to government officials and wealthy families. The Baran Do have an affinity for using the Force to predict and can stop conflicts before they happen, and their practices of sensory deprivation in training help them develop advanced telepathic and sensory skills.
csg_kel_dor.language: Kel Dors speak both Kel Dor and Basic. It is simple, as they express creativity visually and tactilely.
csg_kel_dor.homeworld: Kel Dors come from Dorin, a dark, dusty world in the Mid Rim. Its atmosphere, containing helium and a gas unique to it, has extremely violent, unpredictable storms. Humans visiting it must wear a breath mask or they will quickly pass out.
csg_kel_dor.description: Kel Dors are a harsh people who view morality in very black-and-white terms. They have tough orange skin but cannot survive in a normal environment off of their homeworld, Dorin. They must instead rely on masks and goggles.
csg_kel_dor.sidebar_text: The Baron Do had good relations with the Jedi Order and lost many members to it. Now, however, the Do’s small numbers now make the group obscure enough to survive under the rule of the Empire. Nonetheless, one subsect created by Tokra Hazz, the Hidden Ones, remains fearful of facing the same fate as the Jedi. Composed of less than fifty members, they are ruled by the Hidden One. Their culture revolves around a Baron Do Sage willing himself to die. While this is common among the Baran Do, to become a Hidden One, a sage must fake their death. After a ceremony, they are carried to caverns, where they receive a new name and are considered dead. The Hidden Ones are very traditional in their ways, and though they may preserve knowledge, they do nothing to seek new knowledge or learn new skills. They refuse to let any members leave the caverns. The Hidden Ones will return to living society in forty years thanks to an intervention by Luke Skywalker and his son, Ben.

csg_kentra.name: Kentra

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

csg_kentra.physiology: The Kentra are a large sentient species which exhibits feline traits such as a tail, pointed ears, and claws for traction. They are very muscular, and they have a long, snake-like torso. A pair of large, bat-like wings are mounted on their back. Their species comes in four different races, each distinguished by the color of the fur that covers their body. The brown folk have brown fur and are mainly farmers. The jungle folk, who have black fur, are avid and cunning hunters. The spotted folk, who have spotted fur, live as nomads on the plains, and they rely on their speed to chase their prey while hunting. Finally, there are the well-camouflaged striped folk, who live near rivers and are very patient hunters.
csg_kentra.society: Kentra are a simple yet jovial people with a strong cultural emphasis on honesty. Honor is the primary social measure in Kentra culture, and dishonorable acts can result in banishment. Typically, the Kentra live in villages among the branches of the colossal buntra trees, and their homes are built out of wood. However, some larger cities are built alongside mountain ranges. Their social structure is based around nests, families, and village folk. Nests are organized into regional clans and racial flocks. The major cities often have lords who are then placed in national councils to aid King Jerius in ruling the planet. Soldiers are chosen and trained from an early age when they are taught honor, and they only use their skills for the benefit of the nest, rather than in the name of the individual. Soldiers who violate this code are dismissed and banished. Soldiers typically carry primitive weapons like swords and spears, but they are also proficient at using bows and arrows.
csg_kentra.language: Mimicking the recordings left behind by the Jedi Knight, the Kentra merged their own language and basic together, creating a language they referred to as Bas’c which they speak to this day.
csg_kentra.homeworld: Their homeworld, Orellon II, is a planet in the Mid Rim that is covered in jungles, plains, and volcanic mountains. About a third of the planet’s surface is covered in water.
csg_kentra.description: Primitive yet amiable, Kentra are large felines capable of flight. They are unique in that they have been relatively isolated, but their culture was formed based on a brief interaction with a Jedi Knight, so they have developed a religion based on Jedi ways.
csg_kentra.sidebar_title: The Holy Order of the Je’ulajists
csg_kentra.sidebar_text: The religion of the Kentra people is known as the Holy Order of the Je’ulajists, and they worship the prophet Tandre. In reality, the ‘prophet’ was a human Jedi Knight from the Old Republic, who crash landed on the planet 200 years ago and decided to teach them the ways of the Jedi. As he taught the Kentra, he created computer programs to continue their training after he left, and his lightsaber is also kept safe as the Sword of Honor. The name of their religion was a corruption of the word “geologist,” which they heard in his recording.

csg_kerestian.name: Kerestian
csg_kerestian.physiology: Broad-shouldered and over two meters tall, the Kerestians are typically a strong species. They have tan skin and green eyes with slit pupils. They have a single nostril which connects to their mouth, and they lack ears. They also have air holes along their cheekbones. Their dark hair is long and thin, and it grows along two stripes atop their head.
csg_kerestian.society: Kerestians are a savage people; they are not civilized, and they resort to constant violence in order to survive. They are often cannibals, and they mostly live as primitive hunter-gatherers. For those who do leave their home, they almost always work as mercenaries of some sort. They enjoy wilderness hunting for sport, although a majority of them also do it out of necessity to survive. Their barbarism is so great that it is difficult to mate: When Kerestians are approached by one of their own, it is likely because they are being hunted for food. They have a mythology which describes an afterlife in the Great Darkness. They believe that the only thing they can bring with them into the Great Darkness is a weapon called a darkstick.
csg_kerestian.language: Kerestians speak the complicated language of Kerestese, a tongue with many rules. Although many lost Kerestians are willing to learn Basic, they typically only speak Kerestese when they are first discovered.
csg_kerestian.homeworld: Kerestians come from Kerest, a cold and inhospitable Outer Rim planet which is covered in glaciers.
csg_kerestian.description: Kerestians are a savage people, their bulkier size helping them in combat, but they were not always that way: Much earlier in their history, they were more civilized. A few civilized Kerestians escaped into space by freezing themselves in carbonite before their society collapsed, and they continue to be found.
csg_kerestian.sidebar_text: The current state of Kerestian society is not how it always was. More than 1,000 years ago, they were a more civilized society with advanced technology such as nuclear power and space travel, although they never invented the hyperdrive or had any offworld contact. However, a massive ice age devastated ecosystems and changed life as they knew it. Their society collapsed, and they had to compete with each other for food, bringing about the brutal culture they have now. However, as things fell apart, many Kerestians chose to flee, flying into deep space at sublight speed. Using carbonite to freeze themselves, these Kerestians survived for centuries, and some are still flying through space today. Some died when their ships malfunctioned, but others have been found and reawakened. When these ancient Kerestians are discovered, they are typically very civilized. “Lost” Kerestians are a compassionate people, saddened by the decline of their society. They are well-educated, and most of them enjoy various arts. Just as they took to the stars millenia ago, many lost Kerestians continue to be explorers or colonists.

csg_kerkoiden.name: Kerkoiden

special_abilities.name: Refined Strategies
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Clever Commander.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_kerkoiden.physiology: Kerkoidens are a shout species with ancestors who were quadrupedal predators. They have thin hips but strong limbs and wide shoulders, and their four-fingered hands have sharp claws that they use in combat. Kerkoidens have green or blue skin and no hair, their head features both a long snout with sharp tusks and a large crest at the top. They have red eyes, and they lack obvious nostrils. Despite their bulk, Kerkoidens are on the shorter side, generally less than a meter and a half tall.
csg_kerkoiden.society: Kerkoidens are naturally aggressive, but they belay their more animalistic tendencies using their natural cunning, and they place very high value on being recognized as a civilized and intelligent species. As such, they often combine these tendencies through military occupations, which sate their aggressive psyche while still demonstrating discipline and intelligence. Otherwise, Kerkoidens generally appear calm, intelligent, and dignified, but they are quick to lose their temper and often start fights. Economically, they have become very industrialized and believe strongly in capitalism, which they see as an indicator of a true civilization. They specialize in narrow fields of work, and they typically begin schooling for their specific career as early as ten years old.
csg_kerkoiden.language: Kerkoidens generally speak their native language of Kerkoidese. Although some can speak Basic, most prefer their native tongue because of their growing sense of nationalism.
csg_kerkoiden.homeworld: Kerkoidens come from the Expansion Region planet of Kerkoidia, which is a temperate industrialized world with mostly savannas and jungles. The Empire rules the planet with an iron fist.
csg_kerkoiden.description: A shorter species with blue skin, the Kerkoidens have a ferocious appearance but value civility. They were prominent in the Confederacy of Independent Systems, where many of them made effective military commanders.
csg_kerkoiden.sidebar_text: Kerkoiden society, like most industrialized ones outside of the Core Worlds, fell on the wrong side of Republic taxation and saw tariffs rob them of some of the vast profits that could have further bolstered their economy. Being burdened by the distant Galactic Republic piqued the natural aggression of the Kerkoidens, and they were quick to voice their support for Count Dooku’s secessionist movement. Wanting to protect the Confederacy, a militarist fervor polarized the Kerkoidens against the wealthy humans of the Core Worlds, only for an aggressive Republic military campaign to subjugate their planet early in the war. Kerkoidens are now occupied by the Empire, with harsh restrictions punishing them for their role in the war. Militarism has not died down in recent decades, and most Kerkoidens are now longing for a chance to take revenge on the Empire.
csg_kerkoiden._provenance_note: The Kerkoiden species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_keshiri.name: Keshiri
csg_keshiri.physiology: Near-humans with purple skin, the Keshiri are typically seen as attractive by human standards. They are not capable of interbreeding with humans, but they are similar to humans in most other respects. They have red or mauve eyes which are, on average, larger than those of humans, and their hair comes in shades of brown, silver, or violet.
csg_keshiri.society: The Keshiri are a people who live in an isolated society mostly dominated by human Sith. Without offworld contact, they have developed a unique culture, and although their world lacks any accessible metals, they have made surprising advances in science. However, they are best distinguished by their art and appreciation of beauty. Keshiri and humans on Kesh alike excel in glassblowing, and they also are often interested in theater and other visual arts. In all things, they are typically focused on appearance. Despite their lack of electronic technology aside from what the Sith brought to the planet when the Omen crashed, they are fairly prosperous. For transportation, they have flying reptiles called uvaks, wooden boats, and gas-filled airships. They have ventilation, elaborate aqueducts, and even warning sirens that use hydraulics. They use their glass for many decorations, including lights, and they also have glass-based weapons, such as daggers. They have society on two continents, Keshtah and Alanciar, which were once isolated and distinct, but they have somewhat merged once the cultures collided. Those from Keshtah were once deeply religious, but their religion eventually evolved to worship their Sith overlords, and in more recent millenia, it has disappeared entirely. The Alanciari were once very militarized in order to protect themselves from a Sith invasion, but once the Sith encountered them, war was averted, they were manipulated into disarming themselves, and the Sith ended up ruling both as a single society. Currently, their society is entirely cut off from offworlders. In about four decades, they will begin to acquire a fleet and travel offworld to wage war against the Jedi, but they will keep their homeworld’s location a secret.
csg_keshiri.language: The Sith brought a knowledge of Basic to the Keshiri, but they still also know their native language, Keshiri.
csg_keshiri.homeworld: Keshiri come from the isolated planet of Kesh, which is mostly ocean but with a few continents. Located in eastern Wild Space, its strange magnetic field restricts hyperspace travel to it. It has two moons, and its landmasses include plains, forests, and mountains, with a diverse range of native fauna. The capital is Tahv, an ornate town known as the City of Glass.
csg_keshiri.description: Purple-skinned near-humans, the Keshiri value beauty and the arts. They are cut off from the rest of the galaxy and ruled by a population of Sith whose ship crashed on their world millennia ago.
csg_keshiri.sidebar_text: Despite the once-great divide between human Sith and subservient Keshiri, the two have formed a somewhat more egalitarian meritocracy. Intermarriage between the two species is common, even though they cannot breed. Force-sensitivity amongst Keshiri has increased, and many now number among the Sith Lords. There is still, however, a strong hierarchy based on the Force. The Circle of Lords rule, including a single Grand Lord, seven High Lords, and thirteen Lords. Beneath them are Sith Masters, then Sith Sabers (who are analogous to Knights), and then Apprentices, all above commoners. The youngest Force-sensitivities are called Tyros, who train in the Force together but often return home to their families until they begin an apprenticeship.

csg_khil.name: Khil

special_abilities.name: Entrepreneurial Spirits
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Wheel and Deal.”

special_abilities.name: Hullepi
special_abilities.description: May survive off of absorbing bacteria and organic debris for food.

csg_khil.physiology: The Khil are humanoids with gray-green skin. They have wide variation in height, as some adults aren’t much higher than a meter, while others are two meters tall. They have pointed ears and dark gray eyes. Their most notable features are their hullepi, which are similar to tentacles. Each Khil has six hullepi that they use to breath, speak, and absorb liquid nutrients. Very uniquely, they only consume water, organic debris, bacteria, and juices.
csg_khil.society: Khil are a people who are hardworking and ambitious. Though not particularly greedy, they do value success in their careers, and they detest laziness and wasting time. Their mentality is also very arrogant in that they believe they can achieve anything if they are willing to work hard enough. They are business-oriented, and many find work in management positions. From corporations to individual traders, they are a people who have made a massive impact on the economy of the galaxy. Further encouraging their impact on the galaxy is the fact that they are a friendly people who are polite and willing to embrace other cultures. Despite their many successes, their extreme tenacity has the drawback of sometimes causing mood swings or nervous breakdowns.
csg_khil.language: The Khil speak Khilese, an extremely musical language that only they can speak. Most of them also know Basic.
csg_khil.homeworld: Khil come from Belnar, a swampy world in the Colonies. The cities on Belnar aren’t as urban as those on other worlds. Instead, they are lower in density and have a number of parks. These parks are in wetlands, and Khil value them for aesthetic purposes as well as a place to feed.
csg_khil.description: A species that has been rather successful in galactic commerce, the Khil are gifted with a combination of friendliness and work ethic. They value unifying the galaxy, so they often travel to other planets, welcome foreigners to their own homeworld, and detest the Empire's xenophobia.
csg_khil.sidebar_text: As a very social people, the Khil consider themselves as “citizens of the galaxy.” They place more value in galaxy-wide unity than unity of their own species. Because of this welcoming perspective, many Khil are found offworld, and their cities are often filled with other species. They value peaceful interaction, but they have a strong military to ensure that they aren’t attacked. All Khil are called to military service at least once in their lifetime. Although the Khil valued the unity provided by the Republic, many now oppose the Empire, as it violates their peaceful and democratic values.

csg_khommite.name: Khommite

special_abilities.name: Optimization
special_abilities.description: May train any 1 skill up to 3 during character creation.

csg_khommite.physiology: Khommites are a species of near-humans that believe their genetics are perfect. All Khommites are clones, so they all have others who share their genetic material. They still have some genetic diversity, as there are plenty of different individuals that they can be cloned from. All of these individuals were viewed as having “perfect” genetics. All Khommites have skin that is somewhere between tan, brown, and green. They can be as tall as two meters or as short as barely over a meter. Their digestive system is extremely specified and is only able to consume certain processed wafers. They have no hair and lumps on their forehead and scalp. They have no biological genders. Despite this, they are referred to with masculine pronouns for the sake of simplicity.
csg_khommite.society: Khommites value organization and mathematical perfection. That is why their society is so uniform. They are extremely adverse to change, so their society has remained the same for the past millennium. This will eventually change when Admiral Daala will attack the Khommites in 12 ABY, forcing them to adapt.
csg_khommite.language: The Khommites generally speak both Khomm and Basic.
csg_khommite.homeworld: Khommites come from Khomm, a world on the edge of the Deep Core. It is isolated and has mostly ocean and plains. It is perfectly organized into cities of uniform grids that are unchanging. Many visitors are driven crazy by the blandness of the planet.
