csg_khommite.description: The Khommites once decided that their species achieved optimal genetic structure. As such, they ceased to reproduce normally and instead created new members by cloning the best of their society. They are very fond of uniformity and are slow to adapt.
csg_khommite.sidebar_text: Though their expertise is not as well-known, Khommites have been extremely good cloners for about 1,000 years. However, they refuse to adapt and innovate, so their expertise is limited to cloning the certain individuals that they have chosen. Although clones are theoretically all the same, and cloning Force-sensitives is thought to be impossible, Khommite practices will break both these laws very rarely. Every once in a while, a Khommite will be Force-sensitive. The Dorsk clones are particularly prone to becoming Force-sensitive, as evidenced by Dorsk-81 and Dorsk-82, beings who will eventually join Luke Skywalker’s Jedi Order. They view them as undesirable flukes. All clones are given the name of the person they are cloned from followed by a number showing the order of their creation.

csg_kianthar.name: Kian’thar

special_abilities.name: Animal Affinity
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Beast Wrangler.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Empathy
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as a maneuver, sense the presence and emotional state of everyone within short range. May use this ability to upgrade the difficulty twice when opposing a Deception check.

csg_kianthar.physiology: Kian’thar are a species of semi-aquatic reptiles with maroon or pink scales. Instead of a nose, they have two dangling tentacles, and they have drooping tendrils extending from their eyebrows. Their eyes are yellow and lack pupils, and their neck is protected by multiple keratin plates. They are bulky, and their hands have four thick fingers, making them somewhat uncoordinated. Their most unique ability is their empathy: Similar to Gotals and Zeltrons, the Kian’thar are capable of sensing the emotions of the people around them.
csg_kianthar.society: On the whole, Kian’thar are a kind and peaceful people. This is partly because their ability to sense emotions makes it much easier for them to empathize with anyone. Although they are prone to mood swings, they are disciplined and hardworking. They show constant determination, and it was this drive that caused them to take up a somewhat nomadic lifestyle. They continue to enjoy exploration, and many relish the challenge of assimilating with offworld cultures. For those who remain on their homeworld, controlling animals is essential: They ride flying bentails and herd an aquatic species known as the derlac. Offworld, their empathy makes them excel in any role that requires social interaction, such as being an ambassador, counselor, or con artist.
csg_kianthar.language: Kian’thar speak Kian’thar, a language which uses bubbling sounds and croaks. Many Kian’thar can also speak Basic.
csg_kianthar.homeworld: The Kian’thar come from Shaum Hii, a backwater Outer Rim world with relatively few people. It is swampy, and the Kian’thar have built their villages along the shores.
csg_kianthar.description: A hardworking species of reptiles adapted to living in swamps, the Kian'thar are gifted with empathic abilities that allow them to sense the emotions of those around them. As such, they get along well with others, and many enjoy exploring the galaxy despite originating from a backwater world.
csg_kianthar.sidebar_text: The Kian’thar come from a region of space which is very hard to navigate, so it took a long time for them to be discovered by the rest of the galaxy. About 300 years ago, a group of Shistavanen scouts finally made contact with the Kian’thar, and the concept of interacting with the galaxy has been a major controversy among their people ever since. A faction known as the Lllun advocate trading with the galaxy, joining the Republic, and encouraging immigration. The Iith’lon want isolation and wish to avoid the exploitation that is common in the Republic. However, the two sides are more peaceful than many other political factions, and both sides understand that the other has good intentions. For what it’s worth, more than 2,000,000 Kian’thar have left their home galactic community, and Shaum Hii has developed ties with Black Sun and the Hutts.

csg_kiffar.name: Kiffar

special_abilities.name: Psychometry
special_abilities.description: When using the Foresee power while touching an inanimate object or corpse, may see events relating to the object’s past rather than the future.

csg_kiffar.physiology: The Kiffar are very closely related to humans, enough that they can interbreed. The biggest visual difference between the two is that the Kiffar always wear tattoos that represent their clan. Kiffar typically have dark hair, and they generally style it into long dreadlocks. Kiffar are more likely to be Force-sensitive, which is typically manifested in psychometry, a rare Force power that about one percent of the Kiffar population can use. Using psychometry, Kiffar can touch objects and receive visions from the Force that show them the object’s past.
csg_kiffar.society: Kiffar are a people who value their own independence, staying out of galactic affairs and being ruled only by themselves. They see outsiders as dangerous and are generally nationalists. They are organized into clans, and clan heritage is very important to them. Their markings, which they call qukuuf, are passed down through the family maternally, but Kiffar with a human mother will typically use their father’s tattoos. Conversely, clan membership is passed down paternally, and those with a human father can join their mother’s clan. Clans were once constantly in tension with one another, typically through complex alliances, while others engaged in open warfare. This changed 3,500 years ago under the reign of the Sith Empire, who brought tyranny to the Kiffar and killed many of them. With a far smaller population ever since, the Kiffar have been mostly united.
csg_kiffar.language: Kiffar do not use a native language, and all know Basic.
csg_kiffar.homeworld: Kiffar inhabit the Azurbani System, which contains the planets Kiffu and Kiffex. The two planets orbit each other, generating electric storms that the Kiffar use to generate energy. Kiffu is their somewhat arid homeworld, while Kiffex is an agricultural world that also has their prisons.
csg_kiffar.description: An individualistic species of near-humans, the Kiffar are capable of breeding with humans but are still considered to be their own species. They value their independence, are loyal to their clan, and have mostly stayed out of galactic affairs.
csg_kiffar.sidebar_text: Kiffu Guardians, also known as the Guardians of Kiffu, are an important Kiffar institution that acts as a police force in their space. The Kiffu Guardians wear black armor, and they share a symbol with clan Vos, which is a gold five-pointed star outlined by a circle. The leader of the Guardians is known as the sheyf, and the sheyfs have absolute power over Kiffar society. One of the most prominent sheyfs in recent history was Tinté Vos, who began her career as a Kiffu Guardian and rose through the ranks. In order to take the throne, however, she needed to defeat two rivals, Pethros and Quian Vos. She sacrificed them to the Anzati Dark Jedi Volfe Karkko and adopted their son, Quinlan Vos. He was eventually taken from Tinté by the Jedi, who trained him, but Quinlan would encounter her again after he joined Count Dooku during the Clone Wars. During this encounter, Quinlan uncovered the truth and killed Tinté in his rage. In the resulting power vacuum, the Confederacy was able to rule Kiffu and Kiffex, although the Vos family would retake power after the war.

csg_killik.name: Killik

special_abilities.name: Chitinous Exoskeleton
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Hive Mind
special_abilities.description: Communicate telepathically and automatically provide or receive assistance with all other Killiks of the same hive within extreme range. To act against the nest, must pass a Discipline vs. Discipline check opposed by the nest.

csg_killik.physiology: Killiks are a species of eusocial insects who organize themselves into hives known as nests, each of which is a distinct subspecies. Depending on the nest, their size and other characteristics can vary dramatically. What all Killiks generally have in common is that they have a segmented body with two powerful legs and four arms, three-fingered hands with claws, and a protective exoskeleton made of black or green chitin. They have antennae, mandibles, and glowing, red eyes on the side of their head. Killiks can reproduce quickly, with females being able to lay thousands of eggs and larvae reaching adulthood in a few years, but they rarely reproduce so quickly unless there are enough resources. Almost all Killiks are females, and the males are only used for reproduction. The most unique ability of the Killiks is that they can form a hive mind: Using pheromones and electromagnetic waves, they can communicate telepathically. Furthermore, with enough exposure, Killik pheromones can alter the structure of non-Killik brains, seducing aliens and granting them telepathy, so they become part of the hive as Joiners. Telepathy has limited range, but they can form chains of Killiks to extend its signal. Each nest has different castes, including warriors, assassins, attendants, and membrosia givers, who secrete a potent form of alcohol called membrosia.
csg_killik.society: Killiks, who call themselves the Kind, act as a nest rather than distinct individuals, and all are controlled by what they call the nest’s Will. The nest absorbs the skills and knowledge of every individual, and it also averages their personalities. While each nest has its own personality, they are typically peaceful but seek to increase their numbers. Killik nests do not care about individuals, only the entire nest’s success, so they are extremely industrious and will sacrifice lives on a whim. Their combined memory makes them very knowledgeable, but they cannot distinguish which memories are true and which are memories of fiction.
csg_killik.language: Killiks use telepathy for most communications, but they also have a native language, Killik. It is a visual sign language, using dance to convey meaning.
csg_killik.homeworld: Killiks originate from Alderaan, but the species migrated to the Unknown Regions around 30,000 BBY. There, they control a number of planets in their pocket of space and are unknown to all but the Chiss.
csg_killik.description: Originally from Alderaan but now living in the Unknown Regions, the Killiks are hive-minded insects who arrange themselves into nests, each of which has its own genetics. The hive minds they form are capable of telepathically influencing both its members and outsiders.
csg_killik.sidebar_text: In 27 ABY, the Jedi Raynur Thul and Dark Jedi Welk and Lomi Plo crash landed on Yoggoy, a Killik colony, and they became Joiners. Raynur Thul helped the Killiks expand, while the Dark Jedi formed the Gorog secretive nest and manipulated Killik politics to start a war against the Jedi, Galactic Alliance, and Chiss. The Killiks ultimately lost, and the Gorog nest was exposed, so they returned to the Unknown Regions. From then on, the Jedi placed nanotechnology on their colonies that would sabotage them if they attempted to overpopulate again.
csg_killik._provenance_note: Every Killik nest has different genetics, which may translate into different stats. This stat block should serve as a base but may be modified as needed.

csg_kilmaulsi.name: Kilmaulsi

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: When using claws, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Battle Frenzy
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as an incidental, may enter a frenzied state. When in this state, deal +1 Brawl and Melee damage and gain +2 WT, but may not use any skills or perform activities that require concentration or patience. May remain in this state for up to 5 rounds.

csg_kilmaulsi.physiology: Kilmaulsi descend from avians, but they have long lost their wings and ability to fly as they became bulkier. They are now humanoid in terms of size and stature, but they still retain gray or purple plumage on their neck and forearms. They have lime green skin with orange on their eyelids and the underside of their pointed beak. Kilmaulsi have no hair, and their blue or red eyes are wide. Their hands have four fingers which end in talons, while their feet have three toes, and they use a digitigrade stance with high ankles and long feet.
csg_kilmaulsi.society: Kilmaulsi tend to be direct, straightforward, and humorless. Once they set their minds to a task, they are extremely resolute and determined to see it through. They are often driven by a strong curiosity and wanderlust, so a significant portion of them have left their homeworld. While they can have violent tendencies, they are more than willing to put them aside in order to assimilate with the wider galaxy, and they have adapted to modern technology.
csg_kilmaulsi.language: Kilmaulsi speak a language of the same name and typically know Basic as well. They tend to have a shrieking voice and often squawk.
csg_kilmaulsi.homeworld: The Kilmaulsi inhabit multiple planets in the Kilmauls system of the Outer Rim, and their homeworld is Kilmaulsias, a forested planet which is carved with many canyons.
csg_kilmaulsi.description: The Kilmaulsi are straightforward and direct avians who have warring tendencies that they mostly subdued in order to embrace contact with the wider galaxy. However, when their fury comes out, it is a fight to behold.
csg_kilmaulsi.sidebar_text: Historically, the Kilmaulsi were a very warlike people, as a number of rival tribes with religious differences engaged in frequent conflicts. While this could’ve led them to extinction, they survived thanks to their world being discovered by Hrakian, Paigun, and Vorzydiak explorers. The opportunity to explore the wider galaxy was simply too good to pass up, so the Kilmaulsi put aside their violent ways and became more civilized in order to take to the stars and make peaceful contact with other species. Nonetheless, this warrior past still remains in the hearts of the Kilmaulsi, and they can be deadly in combat. They are a common sight as mercenaries in the Vorzyd Cluster, and once they enter into the frenzy of combat, they lose all sense of civility and transform into a terrifying blur. Their soldiers traditionally wear green heavy battle armor with elaborate decoration.

csg_kitonak.name: Kitonak

special_abilities.name: Thick Hides
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Desert Survivors
special_abilities.description: May go up to 2 months without eating and 4 hours without breathing.

special_abilities.name: Diggers
special_abilities.description: May spend 2 maneuvers to tunnel through loose soil, moving 1 range band.

special_abilities.name: Methodical
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver per turn moving. This does not apply when digging.

csg_kitonak.physiology: Kitonaks are chubby but small humanoids with pink, off-white, or tan skin, which is thick and leathery, keeping them quite well protected from harsh desert windstorms. They can go for weeks without eating and four hours without breathing, but this comes at the cost of extremely low energy. Kitonaks are as slow as any sentient species, and they don’t actually move their legs to walk, instead just pulling their body along with their toes while upright. On the ground, they often move by slithering, and they are adept diggers. Their eyes, ears, and mouth are small and covered by folds of skin, and their head also lacks hair. A nearly cylindrical portion of flesh wraps around their head, which ends in what looks like a nose. However, they actually smell from their feet, which have two toes. Their hands have three fingers, and all of their digits are quite pudgy.
csg_kitonak.society: Kitonaks are extremely patient and painfully slow to interact in social situations. This makes many mistake them for being asleep or non-sentient, although the Kitonaks are typically too simple to take advantage of this underestimation. They are calm and take a long time before deciding anything. Though democratic, their lack of technology and slow communication between tribes makes the government a negligible force. They often lose their possessions to the desert winds, and they live nomadically, following groups of prey called chooba. They hunt by mimicking the sulfaro plant until a chooba wanders into their mouth, which can then feed them for a month. Kitonaks ritually mate during the Great Celebration of Life when there are rains, which occur once every standard decade. The deluge forms brief ponds and rivers in which the couples perform their Dance of Love. The couples then return to the river in the next decade to be together for the birth, which is also underwater.
csg_kitonak.language: Kitonaks speak Kitonese, and many also speak Basic very slowly. They are generally silent.
csg_kitonak.homeworld: Kitonaks wander the deserts of Kirdo III, an incredibly windy planet in the southern Outer Rim. The Kitonaks are very scared of its caves, which are considered passages to the Realm of the Dead.
csg_kitonak.description: Kitonaks are one the slowest species in the galaxy. They are incredibly meticulous, so much so that many mistake them for being asleep. They are relatively small and often move by burrowing or slithering.
csg_kitonak.sidebar_text: The highlight of the day for Kitonaks is the storytelling session. At dusk, the tribe gets together to tell a story, which serves to educate their youth. Each member takes turns adding their own details and plot twists, and the story slowly progresses over the course of days. For the youth of crowded tribes, another bold adventure can be taken. Some choose to become wanderers, in search of less populous tribes. These nomads play their flutes, called chidinkalu, to attract attention as they wander the desert. Some have become renowned musicians in the wider galaxy, while other wanderers have been caught by slavers.

csg_klatooinian.name: Klatooinian
csg_klatooinian.physiology: Klatooinians are an ancient species of humanoids with a dog-like face and no hair. Their skin is brown, tan, or olive green, and their face has heavy brows over their dark eyes, with pronounced jowls and a blunt nose. Their hands are strong and have natural dexterity, giving them an edge with blasters. They are roughly the height of a normal human, although sometimes a bit taller, and their males and females are roughly identical.
csg_klatooinian.society: Klatooinians value loyalty, perseverance, and tenacity. As one of the older civilizations in the galaxy, they have a long history. Like the Weequays, another Hutt servant race, they let religious beliefs dominate their culture. They celebrate time, and they are ruled by elders, who form the Council of Elders. Membership is judged by age and their understanding of Klatooinian culture, the latter of which is measured in ceremonial debate. This council rules the planet from a palace which is situated near the Fountain of Ancients. Klatooinian education teaches their youth Huttese, their Klatooinian history, and lore about the glories of their time in Hutt servitude. Stripped of independence, by ten years old, they are transferred into slavery for a Hutt and are given a more practical education on what they need to know for their job. Although they have learned many different crafts, the Hutts generally prefer them in bodyguard or mercenary roles, where many excel. Troublemaking youth are sent to do hard labor in mines, mills, shipyards, or quarries. Because they value tradition, most Klatooinians prefer simpler weapons such as slugthrowers and swords.
csg_klatooinian.language: The Klatooinian language, Klatooinian, is now dead. Although a few ancient texts have been found, it has yet to be fully resurrected, and the Hutts forbid its use. Otherwise, Klatooinians know Huttese and can speak Basic if needed, though they are usually illiterate.
csg_klatooinian.homeworld: The Outer Rim world of Klatooine is an arid world consisting of deserts and savannas. It is in the Si’Klaata Cluster at the northern tip of Hutt Space. The primary feature is the Fountain of Ancients, which is a gap in the crust of the Derelkoos Desert that has sprayed out liquid wintrium. The wintrium freezes on contact with air and looks like water in mid-flow. Nearly indestructible, it has never been harvested, as the Klatooinians forbid it.
csg_klatooinian.description: A ridiculously unfair treaty that has been around for millennia keeps the Klatooinians in service to the Hutts. The Klatooinians are canines who place extreme value in age, loyalty, and tenacity. They consider time to be the most powerful force in the universe.
csg_klatooinian.sidebar_text: Klatooinians have been in Hutt servitude for millennia and have been mostly content to do so. This is because of the Treaty of Vontor, which was signed by Barada M’Beg, placing the Klatooinians in the power of the Hutts, whom they see as near deities. In exchange, the Hutts have vowed to protect the sacred Fountain of Ancients. This remains a generally popular treaty, and many Klatooinians to this day are named after M’Beg. They consider the fountain to be a gift from their gods known as the Ancients, and the Klatooinians forbid anyone from touching or nearing the structure. Modern technology must stay at least a kilometer away, so as to keep the area as it was in ancient days. Klatooinians revere time, however, and believe that everything else must wither away in its face, even their treaty. The Fountain grows with time, and many believe that their race, the children of the fountains, has grown strong enough to shake off the shackles of servitude and earn their independence. Some hide in secret enclaves and try to revive their dead language and culture; others make silent protest with a simple orange scarf. The Hutts have responded with harsher restrictions, only to find that this just increases resistance.

csg_klytonian.name: Klytonian

special_abilities.name: Cold-Blooded
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, and setback for cold conditions. May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn in conditions below 10 degrees Celsius.

special_abilities.name: Radio Communication
special_abilities.description: May communicate with technology or other Klytonians through radio waves, which have a range of up to 100 meters depending on the frequency.

csg_klytonian.physiology: Klytonians are a reptilian species with leathery scales that come in shades of lime to orange depending on their race. They have spindly legs, so they need to either move on all fours or more commonly support themselves by dragging their long, thick tail. The tail is covered in small spikes, which they evolved to use for defense against packs of canine predators that would otherwise attack from behind. Notably, Klytonians have a massive frill around their neck, which actually acts as a focusing dish for their keen ability to sense radio waves. They communicate using these radio waves, which they can naturally emit from an organ just behind their eyes. They all have a preferred frequency to hear and emit, which is mostly genetic, so they communicate best with their relatives, especially their twin. Quite strangely, almost all Klytonians share their egg with an identical twin that they naturally split with. It is suspected that this developed to increase their birth rate, as egg-laying is a risky process for their females even with the advancements of modern medicine. Klytonians also struggle with the cold, becoming sluggish in it due to their cold blood. Their hands have three fingers and no thumbs, so they struggle with tech.
csg_klytonian.society: Klytonians are detail-oriented and willing to work hard even for small payouts. They make better followers than leaders, but their employability is limited by their tendency to steal. This skulduggery is motivated much more by thrill than greed, and they enjoy setting up shrines of their most impressive heists. Thus, they excel most as underlings in criminal organizations, but their managers must keep them occupied at all times, or else their mischief quickly turns against their boss.
csg_klytonian.language: Klytonians communicate via electric field vibrations which function similar to telepathy, although their signals can be picked up on by droids. Pairs of twins can communicate most easily, silently conversing even through walls or across several dozen meters. Strangers who are less adept at hearing one another’s frequencies need to move closer or send messages more slowly. Those of different races often take minutes to convey even simple phrases to each other. While they can learn Basic, speaking feels unnatural to them, and they are raspy and quiet.
csg_klytonian.homeworld: Klytonians come from the rocky desert world of Klytonia in the eastern Outer Rim. While nominally independent, their government has become strongly influenced by Hutt mob bosses.
csg_klytonian.description: Frilled reptilians who come in pairs of twins, the Klytonians have the rare ability to naturally communicate via radio waves, especially with their twin. They make diligent workers but are prone to kleptomania.
csg_klytonian.sidebar_text: Klytonians rarely part from their twin, who is their partner in almost all matters, almost like a hive mind. While they can operate independently for a tome, twin pairs heavily depend on being within radio distance of one another both emotionally and practically. They often study different but complementary things, so individuals often have rather surprising blind spots if ever put in a situation where their twin can’t clue them in. Even in marriage, twins stay together, forming a household of four adults. It is common for Klytonians to commit suicide after their twin’s death. If one twin dies while in the egg, the other, known as a Singular, is a social outcast. It is common for Singulars to be adopted by other species shortly after they hatch.
csg_klytonian._provenance_note: Little is known about the Klytonians. This entire page is highly speculative and retcons the unidentified frilled reptiloid species from The Art of Star Wars Episode I to be members. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they rewrite stats, imagining their own aspects of Klytonian physiology and culture.

csg_kobok.name: Kobok

special_abilities.name: Natural Armor
special_abilities.description: Increase Ranged Defense by 1.

special_abilities.name: Foreclaws
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 2 advantage to hit with foreclaws, forcing the target to make a hard Resilience check. If failed, the target suffers 8 strain, plus additional strain per threat. On any check, may spend despair to suffer a self-inflicted foreclaw wound at the GM’s discretion.

special_abilities.name: Wide Vision
special_abilities.description: May see in all directions.

csg_kobok.physiology: Spindly insectoids, the Koboks are usually a bit shorter than humans and half as heavy, but they are strong for their size. They are relatively fragile, although they have a carapace that protects them from some damage, including radiation. It is covered in a layer of thin fuzz, and its color changes depending on the region a Kokok is from. Yellow is the most common color, but shades of olive, crème, umber, darker green, and orange are all possible. They have three red-orange eyes, two in front of their head and one atop it, granting them a combined field of view that is essentially 360 degrees. They have mandibles surrounding a mouth of humanoid teeth, and they can grow their fuzz longer as facial hair. They have four fingers and three toes, and their limbs also feature four spikes on their forearms and three spikes on their shins. These spikes, usually called foreclaws or stingers, contain a potent venom that can render a victim unconscious for hours. Unfortunately, the Koboks themselves are also vulnerable to its effects, so they can knock themselves out if they are careless. Most Koboks wear little clothing, save for a few scraps of cloth.
csg_kobok.society: The Koboks are hardy and calculating, and they tend to favor violent professions. They developed sublight space travel on their own, but they mostly kept to warring amongst themselves until the formation of Kobok Union centuries prior to the Battle of Yavin. Unifying the species, the Kobok Union was able to form trade agreements with nearby Trianii and Hiitians. They have always been independent, never a part of the Republic or Empire, although they have had skirmishes with the Corporate Alliance.
csg_kobok.language: The Kobok language, Kobothi, is a language that relies heavily on a wide variety of fricatives in unusual consonant clusters. Although their language is difficult to translate, it is possible for Koboks to learn Basic. The Kobothi S-Corps has developed several additional code languages known only to them.
csg_kobok.homeworld: Koboth is a harsh, barren world on the northern edge of the Tingel Arm, just west of the Corporate Sector. The planet, particularly its sea-covered southern hemisphere, receives a heavy bombardment of radiation due to frequent solar flares. They control a wider region of space, including their planet’s three moons as well as other star systems, but most of their society remains on Koboth’s northern hemisphere. They rarely travel far from Kobothi Space, save for Roon, which has a colony of about 20,000 Koboks.
csg_kobok.description: Three-eyed insects with venomous spikes and thin limbs, the Koboks are cold and naturally violent, though they have little interest in the outside world. They fought fiercely to preserve their independence from the Empire and have since reverted to isolation.
csg_kobok.sidebar_text: Shortly after the Clone Wars, the Empire attacked rebels in the Mavva system, which included a number of Koboks. As the battles dragged on, the Empire turned to biological warfare, introducing the rooze virus. Unfortunately, both sides were devastated, Imperials and Rebels alike falling victim to the disease. The only exception was the Koboks, who were immune to it. Koboks made up the majority of the remaining rebel force and successfully retained their independence, earning them a fierce reputation. The battles led to the formation of the elite Kobothi S-Corps, and veterans of the conflict distinguish themselves with a blue cape. The Empire, for its part, discontinued the rooze virus as a bioweapon.

csg_koorivar.name: Koorivar

special_abilities.name: Savvy Liars
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Plausible Deniability.”

csg_koorivar.physiology: Koorivar are near-humans, but they are distinguished by a tall horn atop their head and different skin color. Their skin can be yellow or green in males and purple or red in females. Though they are often hooded, they actually have several horns which surround their large, spiralling horn. Horns are an important status symbol to Koorivar. Large horns are very prominent in the upper class, while those with smaller horns end up in the lower class. Those who lose their horns can be banished. Their skin is scaled and their eyes are yellowish.
csg_koorivar.society: Koorivar value financial prowess and business success above all. Even marriage is entirely focused on getting optimal financial benefit. In school, Koorivar learn little other than how to trade, conduct business, and negotiate. They almost always focus on being business administrators, traders, or merchants. Many start their own business at the age of ten or earlier.
csg_koorivar.language: Koorivar speak Koorivar, although the language also requires hand gestures. Many also know Basic, as it is important for business.
csg_koorivar.homeworld: The original Koorivar homeworld is long-lost, and though many are dispersed, their homeworld is now Kooriva. It is a jungle planet in the Inner Rim. It has economically struggled under Imperial rule.
csg_koorivar.description: A difficult past has caused the near-human species called the Koorivar to become greedy, shady, and business-oriented. Because of a great deal of work, they have managed to settle on the world of Kooriva.
csg_koorivar.sidebar_text: For all their wealth, Koorivar long struggled to gain what other species take for granted: a homeworld. Their own home planet has long been uninhabitable due to an unstable star, so they searched the galaxy for a new home. They eventually decided to lease the planet of Kooriva. After several centuries, they named themselves the Koorivar and petitioned the Senate to buy the world. They were turned down and were forced off of Kooriva shortly after. For more than 500 years, they travelled the galaxy and worked together to gain influence. Learning the shady ways that they are now known for, they eventually got enough power to overturn the vote. However, even after owning Kooriva, it wasn’t all perfect. The Republic cracked down on them for illegal activities of all sorts, they dealt with a blockade over Kooriva, and they faced sanctions. During the Clone Wars, the Koorivar on Republic worlds faced newfound troubles. The Koorivar held great power with the Corporate Alliance, which sided with the CIS, so Kooriva joined the Confederacy, Thanks to that, the Koorivar on Republic planets like Coruscant were persecuted and many were forced to leave. The species has suffered greatly under Imperial rule as further punishment for the Clone Wars. The dwindling Corporate Alliance has fled to the Corporate Sector.

csg_korun_human.name: Korun Human

special_abilities.name: Animal Tamers
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Influence Basic Power. When using an Influence Power check on an animal, add 2 boosts.

special_abilities.name: Poison Tolerance
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on Resilience checks to deal with poisons, and reduce ratings of dangerous atmospheres by 1.

csg_korun_human.physiology: Korunnai are a group of primitive humans who descend from a line of Jedi. All are Force-sensitive to some extent, and they also boast a tolerance to toxins. Otherwise, they are genetically identical to humans, but they are less diverse, having exclusively darker skin and black hair.
csg_korun_human.society: Korunnai live a primitive lifestyle among clans of their extended family that they refer to as Ghôshes. They refer to those within their Ghôsh as Dôshallai, meaning clan-brothers. They survive by herding animals called grassers, and they use akk dogs for protection. In order to tame these animals, they use the Force, which they know as the Pelekotan, an entity that controls nature itself. They view themselves as products of the Pelekotan, which they exist to serve. They excel in using the Pelekotan to guide animals, and their powers in that domain are often superior to those of Jedi. Their spiritual leader is called the lor pelek, a shaman who is also a skilled warrior. Although they were allies of the Republic during the Clone Wars, their population was decimated by an Imperial bombardment shortly after the war, and few Korunnai survived.
csg_korun_human.language: Korunnai speak Koruun, also known as Korunni, and they have a distinct way of communicating even when they use Basic. They always measure distances using travel time, and they shift their head to the side rather than shrugging.
csg_korun_human.homeworld: Korunnai come from the volcanic planet of Haruun Kal, a planet with a toxic atmosphere, especially in the lowlands. As such, the Korunnai live in the jungles on mountains and plateaus, where the toxins are at a low enough concentration for them to survive. It also has many fungi which destroy metals, although coating metals in portaak amber allows them to survive for short periods of time. It is governed mostly by offworlders, whom the Korunnai call Balawai.
csg_korun_human.description: Force-sensitive humans from the planet Haruun Kal, the Korunnai were nearly wiped out by the Empire. They are loyal to the herds they own, their family, their extended family, and their sense of courage and integrity, in that order.
csg_korun_human.sidebar_text: One of the most important aspects of Korunnai culture is the Four Pillars, a guide to their morality. The most important pillar is Herd. As they depend on the grasser herds to survive, they are expected to place Herd above everything else, including other pillars. Beneath it is Family, for whom they are expected to defend, caring for their elders and teaching their children. Beneath Family is Duty, which is their commitment to work hard and serve their entire Ghôsh. Finally, there is Honor, which is beneath all other pillars. Honor is a commitment to integrity and courage.

csg_kowakian.name: Kowakian monkey-lizard

special_abilities.name: Foragers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Camouflage
special_abilities.description: Add boost on Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Excellent Stomachs
special_abilities.description: Suffer no penalties for eating spoiled or rotten food.

csg_kowakian.physiology: Kowakian monkey-lizards are small but noisy arboreal creatures, averaging two thirds of a meter tall, with relatively long limbs and, for some subspecies, a prehensile tail. They are reptiles, although they have a beaked mouth, no teeth, and a small mane of hair growing around their neck. Their reproductive habits are not well-studied, but it is believed they lay eggs. They also have very keen senses from their long ears and from the yellow eyes on their triangular head. They have clawed hands and feet, which they use for climbing, and they are extremely nimble creatures. Making them further difficult to catch, they can slightly shift their own skin color as a form of camouflage, although they most naturally have hues of orange or clay brown. They survive mostly by scavenging and have a stomach that allows them to eat even the most rotten of foods. Preferring quantity of food over quality, their stomach is often bloated.
csg_kowakian.society: Kowakian monkey-lizards live in large groups that share a nest. They are of debated sentience, but they are nonetheless playful and often enjoy swinging through treetops or exploring. Most of them are scavengers, although they also hunt smaller prey like insects, worms, or rodents. Barely sentient, they are quite mischievous and greatly enjoy destruction. They also enjoy mockery through their well-timed laughter, by throwing things, or by pulling pranks. They are cruel even to other monkey-lizards and will never share food. They have very minimal structure to their society, though each member of the nest is given a particular role, be it to scavenge, guard, or scout. The oldest female is their leader.
csg_kowakian.language: Kowakian monkey-lizards have a chirping language of their own, but they are also skilled mimics. It is unclear just how much they understand when they parrot back languages such as Basic or Huttese.
csg_kowakian.homeworld: Kowakian monkey-lizards come from rainforests on the Outer Rim world of Kowak. A population of Zygerrians and their slaves also live on the planet.
csg_kowakian.description: Tiny, annoying sentients that many consider to be animals, the monkey-lizards are primitive scavengers who have begun to explore the galaxy by stowing away on ships. They enjoy mockery and pranks, so many are used as court jesters.
csg_kowakian.sidebar_text: Stowing away on ships has allowed Kowakian monkey-lizards to traverse the galaxy. They have infested the swamps of Baroonda, for example. They are also taken offworld as pets, most often by crime lords. While their noisiness and destructiveness is frowned upon in civilized society, they seem to get along better with more shady figures. They have been seen around the underworld as pets, court jesters, and even spies. While they are too stubborn to be properly trained, they are cunning enough to understand what owners want. Because of this, they will behave if they realize their well-being is at stake.

csg_krevaaki.name: Krevaaki

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Stoic
special_abilities.description: Add boost on all Deception checks, add setback on all Charm checks.

csg_krevaaki.physiology: Krevaaki are shallow-water crustaceans who are protected by a tough, red-brown shell. They have eight tentacles, although these tentacles become increasingly specialized as they age. Once they become adults, six of their tentacles can only be used for walking. Their upper two have opposable thumbs but lack fingers, so the Krevaaki somewhat struggle with using technology. Their head is hairless and has pointed ears near the top of it, and they have large, blue eyes. On their chin, they have six tiny tentacles that they use as olfactory organs. Because of their unique appearance, most species have a hard time understanding their facial expressions, and it is harder for them to interact with others. Their unique body structure is also unsettling to some species, so they often cover up their six tentacles that act as legs using long robes, so that they can assume a more humanoid posture.
csg_krevaaki.society: Krevaaki are a philosophical people who value wisdom. Not unlike the Jedi, they are peaceful, resolving conflicts when necessary but doing so humbly and nonviolently whenever possible. Furthermore, they seek to purify themselves of negative emotions like hatred or jealousy and find inner peace. They meditate frequently and constantly seek wisdom, and very few of them are truly interested in money or fame. Many enjoy exploration, so they are often found expanding the frontier as scouts or colonists.
csg_krevaaki.language: Most Krevaaki know both verbal and written Kreva, and those who explore the galaxy also generally learn Basic.
csg_krevaaki.homeworld: Krevaaki hail from Krevas, an Outer Rim planet. Krevaaki inhabit its shallow swamps, and the rest of the planet is covered in oceans.
csg_krevaaki.description: Crustaceans protected by thick plates, the Krevaaki have eight tentacles, but they often conceal all but two of them beneath their robes to have a humanoid posture. They are similar to the Jedi in many ways: Force-sensitivity is common among them, and even those who lack the Force are deeply philosophical.
csg_krevaaki.sidebar_text: Krevaaki have a strong connection to the Force, and even those who cannot truly sense it seek to understand its power or even feel its calling. Many Krevaaki leave their home in order to learn more about the Force, and countless others obey what they sense to be their destiny. They can make bold decisions that make little sense rationally because they believe that is what they have been called to do by the Force.

csg_krish.name: Krish

special_abilities.name: Skilled Hunters
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Expert Tracker.”

csg_krish.physiology: Krish have a muscular, athletic body and gray-brown skin. Their wiry hair at the back of their head is typically dark red, although it can vary in color. They have a bony ridge going along their skull that starts at the nose and goes all the way around their head. Their face is very wrinkled, and their eyes are red. Whenever they are even mildly amused, Krish will smile prominently.
csg_krish.society: Krish are by nature extremely aggressive and competitive. They have come to love sports and other games, and they place high value in entertainment. They also enjoy puzzles, and many are gamblers. They respond extremely well to adversity, but they are prone to boredom when faced with easier tasks. As such, many Krish will intentionally handicap themselves in order to provide a challenge with certain tasks. Their love of excitement and sport has prevented them from experiencing real success in the galaxy, as they can be lazy and distracted in many jobs. Although they can be excellent hunters when focused, they are easily goaded, and their tendency to handicap themselves can become an issue.
csg_krish.language: The Krish have a gruff language which uses grunting and bellowing. Their written language is extremely complicated, as their alphabets are optimized to minimize the amount of symbols needed.
csg_krish.homeworld: Krish come from the Mid Rim planet of Sanza, which is also known as Krish. It has many rainforests, but a majority of habitable land that isn’t used up by industry has been devoted to making stadiums, resorts, or race tracks. This can make it a popular tourist destination.
csg_krish.description: The Krish are obsessed with competitions and games of all sorts, and they bring a competitive approach to everything they do that often allows them to conquer difficult tasks. Many are hunters, a field where their exceptional athleticism is particularly useful.
csg_krish.sidebar_text: Krish can be surprisingly successful in many businesses or even politics, as they can treat these fields like any other game. This tendency to game the system gives them a reputation of being very selfish, deceitful, or corrupt. Although these tactics are often successful, their short attention span makes it hard for them to achieve any real wealth or power. Once they have what they want, they will often retire or move on so that they can focus on new challenges.

csg_krytollak.name: Krytollak

special_abilities.name: Hardened Shell
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

csg_krytollak.physiology: Krytollaks are mammals with an exoskeleton in addition to their internal bones, granting them extra protection. Because of this brown, black, or green shell, they are often mistaken for insectoids. They are actually capable of growing their exoskeleton, which they keep for their entire life. They also live a bit longer than humans and never stop growing, so elder members of their people can be up to three meters tall. Females are generally larger than males by a decimeter or two in height. Both their mouth and their dark eyes are visible through slits in their shell, and they have no distinct head. They have three-fingered hands, and they have front-facing and rear-facing toes which are both clawed. Krytollaks do not eat meat, but they do consume vitamins and minerals by eating rocks to supplement their diet of vegetables. They consider rocks or plants from other planets to be delicacies.
csg_krytollak.society: Unified by a single planetary government, Krytollaks believe in the need for monarchy and order and are all ruled by Empress Devir. They also have a racial hierarchy in which those with green shells, about one in 25 Krytollaks, are royals, while the rest are workers. They all place high value in hand-to-hand combat, often brawling to resolve disputes. These brawls are relatively harmless because of their shells, so they are quite friendly. Serious disputes are resolved in duels with weapons, although ranged weapons of any kind are forbidden. Although they have these violent tendencies, they are still very restrained in most situations. They are patient, listening carefully and remaining silent or responding passively before coming to a decision, but they are slow to forgive.
csg_krytollak.language: As they have only been discovered by the galaxy very recently, Krytollaks generally don’t speak Basic and only know their native language.
csg_krytollak.homeworld: Krytollaks come from Thandruss, a planet with two moons that is in the Expansion Region. It was discovered very recently by the rest of the galaxy, when their technology was only steam-powered. Now, they have quickly embraced new technology, but it is hard to acquire. They view vibroblades as a rare commodity and seek to own their own hyperdrives.
csg_krytollak.description: Shell-covered mammals who eat vegetables and rocks, the Krytollaks are psychologically inclined to support monarchs and value order. This makes them supporters of the Empire, although they have only had limited contact with the outside galaxy.
csg_krytollak.sidebar_text: Because of their cultural inclination toward monarchy, the Krytollaks practically worship Emperor Palpatine. However, they recognize the failures of his subordinates, and many are frustrated by high Imperial taxes. As such, they hope to inform Palpatine of their plight so that he can rat out corruption and improve his Empire. Nevertheless, they still see the Empire as a necessity that exists for the greater good, and they see the Rebel Alliance as a dangerous organization that will bring anarchy or a very corrupt democracy if they succeed. Empress Devir has many Imperial advisors, and Krytollak nobles now dress in way based on the attire of Imperial nobility, typically wearing the gray uniforms of the Imperial Military.

csg_kubaz.name: Kubaz

special_abilities.name: Born Spies
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Stalker.”

csg_kubaz.physiology: Kubaz are insect-eating mammals with green or black skin, a little bit on the taller side but fairly lanky. Their head is similar in shape to that of Rodian’s, with a long snout that acts as a highly sensitive nose and as a mouth with two rows of teeth. This snout also has the size and dexterity to effectively find and grab bugs and suck them out of small crevices, which the Kubaz eat. However, the snout is also highly expressive, as they can curl or vibrate it to show emotion. Their eyes are sensitive, both in terms of recognizing details and being damaged by some types of light. Therefore, they are almost always seen wearing goggles of some sort if they are on any worlds with a red or yellow star. Their black hair is short and bristled. Their feet are two-toed, and their hands have broad fingers.
csg_kubaz.society: Kubaz live underground nests that have a clan structure. With each clan ruled by a Queen, Kubaz take the name of the Queen that they have descended from. They value their families, doting on children constantly until they’re sent to the crèche at five years old. At the crèche, unwed females educate the children, while parents come in to check on their young over shared meals. Though extremely nosy and prone to asking constant questions, Kubaz are otherwise obsessed with tact and decorum, strict in their proper courtesies. With their keen eyes, Kubaz are adept at reading body language, and they are highly observant. They value culture and have a love for art and literature, though their odd moral codes do not consider thievery of such things to be wrong. The highlight of their culture, however, is their meals of insects, which rely on a variety of carefully mutated strains to form delicacies. The earliest conflicts in Kubaz history were the Hive Wars, fought over their insect farms. It was modern genetic engineering, a field that they called “insecticulture,” which ended it. These sciences allowed them to create insects that grew bigger and tastier, as well as color coding them by clan to eliminate disputes over ownership.
csg_kubaz.language: Kubazian is the language of the Kubaz. Most learn Basic as well, but with a nasally accent. They tend to be only literate in their own tongue. They also have a non-verbal language, which involves hand signals of touching the head, nose, or shoulders, as well as subtle motions of their trunk.
csg_kubaz.homeworld: Kubaz come from the world of Kubindi, an Outer Rim planet not far from Hutt Space. Their system’s sun is a blue giant, which makes the world sun-baked and lacking in vegetation. For this reason, Kubaz mostly live underground, eating insects out of their burrows. It is home to a multitude of insect species, many of which are mutated by radiation.
csg_kubaz.description: The Kubaz are insect-eating mammals who place extremely strong emphasis in protocol, family, and art. Because of their diet, they consider all insects to be nothing more than food, even the sentient ones. This has caused many governments to keep them isolated on their homeworld of Kubindi, away from the likes of Verpine, Geonosians, Gand, and X'ting.
csg_kubaz.sidebar_text: Kubaz eat insects and view all insectoid creatures as mere food. This includes Verpine, Geonosians, Gand, Killiks, and Fefze. They also eat non-sentient insects, and many Kubaz travel the galaxy to bring their clans information about the cuisine on other planets. When Kubaz first began to explore, they were very violent towards the Verpine. That incident required Republic intervention in order to stop it, and the Republic has since kept the Kubaz trapped on their homeworld, discouraging them from developing the hyperdrive. The Empire has continued this policy, often blaming the Republic or the Rebel Alliance for sabotage of Kubaz starship engineers. Some joined the Empire to take revenge, though more recently, some of the Kubaz were able to expose these lies. Many are now beginning to join the Alliance.

csg_kulless.name: Kulless

special_abilities.name: Expert Modders
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Tinkerer.”

csg_kulless.physiology: Kulless are portly creatures with short legs and a thick tail, and they have off-white skin with brown-pink pigmentation around their eyes, on their tail, and in stripes along their arms. Their feet are quite small with three forward-facing toes and one rear-facing toe on each. Their hands also have four digits but are very large by comparison. Their visage lacks a nose, with two nostrils situated just below their black eyes. Their mouth has no lips, leaving their teeth visible. Despite their ungainly appearance, they have quick reflexes and are surprisingly nimble.
csg_kulless.society: Kulless are a cautious and deliberate people, not very prone to risk taking. This preference also makes them dislike change, but on the positive side, it makes them very loyal. In their friendships and in their careers, once they find something which is comfortable enough, they prefer to keep it that way, so they never abandon their friends or coworkers. They also tend to be very honest, but to the extent that they become overly literal and extremely pedantic. They have little use for euphemisms or pleasantries, so their extremely frank speech can often make interactions with other species a bit awkward. However, this way of speaking is exactly how machines think, so many of them make excellent programmers or engineers, and they usually find interactions with droids to be refreshingly straightforward. They believe an understanding of mathematical logic and physics is of utmost importance, and they have a tradition that if logical debate cannot resolve a disagreement, they settle it by comparing math skills. In order to determine who has more credible judgment, they each attempt to solve puzzles and math problems, typically supplied by a third party, although there are also HoloNet resources which can select a random question out of a large library.
csg_kulless.language: Notrami typically speak Onis and Basic, while the Abivites speak Kornakian and are less likely to know Basic.
csg_kulless.homeworld: Kulless come from a Mid Rim planet called Gerres Gule, a relatively dry world with vast windswept plains. It is agrarian around the equator and to the north, with small villages stretching across the vast tracts of farmland, while the more densely populated cities are further south.
csg_kulless.description: Kulless are squat mammals who are generally averse to risk. They are literal and pedantic, which helps them understand droid programming, and they also have good reflexes should they have a chance to pilot.
csg_kulless.sidebar_text: There have always been two major political groups among the Kulless. In the north and in equatorial regions are the Abiv nations, and to the south is the Notrami Union. By comparison to the Notrami, Abivites tend to be somewhat more slender with a sharper chin, wider eyes, and more frequent splotches of pink on their skin. They have formed tightly-knit farming communities and are the more traditional of the two peoples, with a culture that leans more collectivist. They are very loyal to their hometowns and are less likely to venture into the wider galaxy. On the other hand, the Notrami are more individualistic, likely to travel, and modernized. They thrive in many high-tech industries, particularly droid programming and manufacturing. Tensions between the two societies are strong. Both races have their share of rebel sympathizers, but so far, the Empire has prevented uprisings by pitting the two against each other. During the Clone Wars, it was a similar story, where both groups joined the Separatists, but Republic agitators attempted to plunge the planet into civil war.
csg_kulless._provenance_note: The Kulless species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_kushiban.name: Kushiban

special_abilities.name: Camouflage
special_abilities.description: Add boost on Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Mood Fur
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Deception checks opposed by someone who understands the significance of fur colors.

special_abilities.name: Superb Mobility
special_abilities.description: May leap up to a meter with no check. May climb up steep surfaces.

csg_kushiban.physiology: Kushibans are a very small species of lagomorphs who are typically less than a meter long. Although they run best when standing on all four limbs, they can stand on two limbs in order to use their front limbs for manipulation. They are excellent leapers for their size, and they can jump higher than a human and climb many surfaces. In general, they are nimble and quick. They have a soft, bushy tail and long ears, but their face has more in common with primates than other lagomorphs. Their wide eyes can change color, and they often change to match the eye color of whomever they’re looking at. One of the most unique abilities that Kushibans have is color-changing fur. They can change it to match a particular environment for camouflage, but it also changes naturally based on their mood if they don’t try to control it. It is white when they are calm or asleep, gray when they’re upset, and black when they’re mourning.
csg_kushiban.society: Kushibans are a very simple people who have very little technology. They have negligible industrialization and are mostly agricultural. They use fire to defend themselves and farm silkweed to make fabrics. They rarely choose to leave their home planet or embrace the technology of the rest of the galaxy. They are a communal people who are very generous and kind. However, they are quick to anger and have little tolerance for bullies and cynics. Although they aren’t completely isolated from the rest of the galaxy, they are not a commonly seen species. Because of their appearance, many assume them to be pets or vermin. The Kushibans are very reverent toward the Jedi, and they are honored when Jedi search among them for apprentices. A number of Kushiban have become Jedi. However, most Kushibans find the idea of a Kushiban Jedi to be laughable.
csg_kushiban.language: Because of their isolated nature, few Kushibans speak Basic. They typically only use their own language, Kushiban.
csg_kushiban.homeworld: Kushibans come from Kushibah, a planet in the northern part of the Outer Rim. It is isolated and obscure with almost no advanced technology. It is the home of a species of animal called the xinkra, who often attempt to eat the Kushibans but are easily scared away by fire.
csg_kushiban.description: Kushiban are small lagomorphs who have a simple society based around small-scale agriculture and weaving. They are kind, pacifistic, and generous, and they have a reverence for the Jedi.
csg_kushiban.sidebar_text: Kushibans have an economy based primarily on agriculture and weaving. They grow silkweed and mix it with their own fur in order to make tapestries in a variety of colors. The silkweed harvest is a very important date on their planet. Most impressive about their success is that they do it almost entirely without technology, using only rakes, scythes, spindles, and torches. Despite the value in their tapestries, the Kushibans still make a relatively small impact on the galactic economy.

csg_kyuzo.name: Kyuzo

special_abilities.name: High Jump
special_abilities.description: Able to jump very high or far in normal gravity. Once per round as a maneuver, may suffer 3 strain to move 2 range bands either vertically or horizontally.

special_abilities.name: High-Pressure Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Need a breath mask in a normal environment. Without a breath mask, become disoriented.

csg_kyuzo.physiology: Kyuzo are a physically strong species, having adapted to the high gravity of their homeworld, so they can pull off impressive physical feats in ordinary gravity. They are large, as well, often above two meters tall. They have a wrinkled green skin, which can vary from olive and almost brown to a more bluish turquoise. Their wide eyes are black, and they have yellow irises in the center. Kyuzo have four fingers and are adjusted to breathing in high-pressure atmospheres, so they often need to wear a breath mask on other worlds.
csg_kyuzo.society: Kyuzo society is centered around honorability and loyalty. Oaths are considered unbreakable. They have a strong sense for justice, which they often execute using the clovocs. The clovocs are similar to a police force and uphold the warrior traditions from the Kyuzo. Local governments hire the clovocs to keep the peace, and they also battle for spectacle, though not to the death. Their clovocs vary greatly in terms of culture: Some, for example, revolve around offworld mercenary work, while others forbid it entirely. Large islands and continents form their own political entities, which are bonded by a relatively loose alliance. Despite their rigid honor, Kyuzo do have a respect for rogues and social outcasts, which are predominantly featured in their myths and stories.
csg_kyuzo.language: Kyuzo speak the language known as Kyuzo. Its words are very short and aren't particularly difficult for humans to pronounce. Kyuzo are capable of comprehending Basic, but they find it difficult to pronounce and the grammar to be fairly confusing.
csg_kyuzo.homeworld: The Kyuzo homeworld of Phatrong has high gravity and high atmospheric pressure. Its oceans are divided by long, thin, continents which are fairly mountainous. Some of these mountains are bordered by plains and hills, while others surround fjords and canyons.
csg_kyuzo.description: An honorable, loyal species known for their combative skills, Kyuzo have built up strength as an adaptation to their high-gravity homeworld of Phatrong. Some are organized into clovocs, which act as police and militia while also fighting for show.
csg_kyuzo.sidebar_text: Kyuzo war helmets can act as a shield, a thrown weapon, or a melee weapon. As a shield, the wearer gains +1 melee defense when holding or wearing it. As a thrown weapon, it uses Ranged-Light, has short range, deals 4 damage, has Knockdown, Disorient 1, Cumbersome 3. For 3 advantage, it may ricochet back to the thrower. As a Melee weapon, it has engaged range and deals damage of Brawn +1, but otherwise keeps the qualities of the thrown version. It has Encumbrance 3, Rarity 8, and costs 750 credits. Encumbrance decreases to 1 when worn.

csg_laboi.name: Laboi

special_abilities.name: Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Advanced Olfaction
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks. When smelling to find the general direction of a target, make difficulty equal to distance in kilometers.

special_abilities.name: Limbless
special_abilities.description: Reduce encumbrance threshold by 6 and may not carry items in hands. May not use technology requiring hands, such as blasters or vehicles. When wielding Melee weapons with tail, add 3 setbacks.

special_abilities.name: Sharp Teeth
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Telekinetic Powers
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Move Basic Power and its Strength upgrades.

csg_laboi.physiology: The Laboi are fur-covered canines with a serpentine body structure. Their fur is colorful, coming in shades of green, indigo, and crimson, but it loses its color in the daytime and becomes white, making them less vulnerable to bright sunshine. They have sharp teeth for combat, and their canine muzzle also features a large nose with four nostrils. They have an excellent sense of smell, allowing them to track prey with ease. It also helps to identify food, although this makes them picky eaters. They have wide eyes and prominent circular ears atop their head. Even as adults, their body can be as short as two meters or as long as ten meters, and their tail is somewhat prehensile, allowing them to grasp objects such as simple sticks. Laboi larvae are known as worms, and the amount of worms per birth increases as the mothers age. Young, short mothers generally give birth to a single worm, while the older, longer mothers can give birth to up to twenty at one time. Laboi have a relatively high rate of Force-sensitivity, as older females will occasionally develop telekinetic powers.
csg_laboi.society: Laboi have a deep respect for age, and they see their shortest members as almost worthless. This is in part because smaller Laboi are most vulnerable to predators. They are a philosophical society, and a few follow a religion that connects to the Force. However, they are still very aggressive, and food is their biggest priority, even over their companions. A few have no qualms about eating sentients, a minority that has severely harmed their overall reputation. When they are not hunting and fighting, the Laboi are an artistic sort: They enjoy music as well as tending to gardens of multicolored crystals. Many have no interest in the rest of the galaxy, but for those who take part in offworld work, their lack of arms means that they often work behind the scenes. Many are scholars or philosophers, while others find work as businessmen, both legal and illegal.
csg_laboi.language: Because of their isolation, most Laboi only know their native language.
csg_laboi.homeworld: Laboi come from the unique Outer Rim planet of Laboi II, which has a very slow rotation, so daytime and nighttime last for a little less than three standard months each. Strong winds provide some moderation to the temperature, but nighttime is still freezing, while many rocks melt because of the extreme heat during the day. This melting means that the geography is constantly changing, so it has no plant life. However, it has a rich diversity of animal life and features a number distinct minerals and crystals. These rare crystals attract the planet’s only offworld trade.
csg_laboi.description: Fur-covered canines who lack limbs, the Laboi are adapted to temperature extremes, many are Force-sensitive, using telekinesis to make up for their physical shortcomings. They value age, so their longest members are seen as the most valuable.
csg_laboi.sidebar_text: Laboi are organized into hunting packs, each of which is ruled by its longest (and therefore oldest) male called the pack leader. The pack leader then sends out smaller groups called hunts, each of which is also ruled by the largest available male, who is called the chief. Most of the dangerous work is carried out by smaller Laboi. They typically hunt ovalyans, an animal the size of a bantha. This is dangerous, as ovalyans will also prey on smaller Laboi if given the chance.

csg_lannik.name: Lannik

special_abilities.name: Indomitable
special_abilities.description: Remove setback from critical injuries, fear, or the disoriented condition.

csg_lannik.physiology: Lannik are short humanoids with pinkish-tan skin. They stand just over one meter tall. While many hold a grizzled look of battle scars, the only feature otherwise distinguishing them are wide ears, which droop downward off of either side of their head. Despite their size, these ears actually provide very little unique benefits as sensory organs. While some consider the Lannik to be possible relatives of Yoda’s species, such claims are without evidence.
csg_lannik.society: Lannik are brutal and primitive but nevertheless intelligent and strong-willed. They are known for being excellent in battle and at keeping a clear head, staying calm despite fear or emotion. They can often find solutions out of dangerous situations, thanks to this ability. For all their strengths, they are also known to be bellicose, not to mention arrogant. Lannik never back down in a fight. Now, this fight is often the Empire. While the Lannik have long been independent, this goes strictly against Imperial views, which have been seeking to annex the planet. They have yet to succeed. The Lannik are also known for their many traditions, which outsiders generally find to be strange and primitive.
csg_lannik.language: Most Lannik speak Basic as well as their native language, Lannik.
csg_lannik.homeworld: Lannik come from a world of the same name which is in the Mid Rim. It contains mountains and forests primarily. It is unique in that it has large amounts of resources that are not yet tapped into, since it is so isolated and the Lannik have little interest in mining. It has been separate from many galactic governments in peace, though that is now threatened by the Empire.
csg_lannik.description: Lannik may be small, but they are some of the toughest, most confident, and bravest people in the galaxy. They are very violent, and some see them as rather primitive. Imperial control has kept them isolated on their homeworld of Lannik.
csg_lannik.sidebar_text: Lannik history is filled with strife and conflict, dating back to their first contact with the Republic. Corellians and Duros first came to the planet bringing high technology. The Lannik became split on how to use it. And so, factions were created and war began. As conflict raged, only criminal groups came in to stop it, which was to no avail. Eventually, the Republic itself intervened, ending the conflict. While they sought to reduce technology imports, it was unsuccessful, and technology became prominent. This has led to several criminal groups controlling the planet as well as smuggling in devices. They have also been ruled by an oppressive monarchy, with the only thing close to liberation being a terrorist group known as Red Iaro. Under Imperial control, fewer Lannik have left their home. While not as warlike as some, the tradition of war affects every Lannik, and many find it to be their calling. Some turn instead to the thrill of sports, such as Pugil.

csg_lasat.name: Lasat

special_abilities.name: Ears and Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold or hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

csg_lasat.physiology: Lasat are a sentient species of carnivorous mammals with a humanoid body structure, but they are covered in light brown fur. Females also have tan fur, but theirs is much shorter than that of males. Because of this, male Lasat are often mistaken for Wookiees, especially in the case of their biggest members, but they are much shorter, thinner, and their facial structure is significantly different. Lasat also have a tail. They have no fur or hair on their face, and they have a very small nose. Their yellow eyes are very large, allowing them to see well in the dark, and they have long, pointed ears. These ears actually help them to dissipate heat off of their body. Combined with their insulating fur, Lasat are adapted to a wide range of temperatures.
csg_lasat.society: Lasat are a cunning people, typically setting up traps in order to catch their prey. Their cleverness gives them a knack for mechanics, including the construction of explosives. They have a strong tradition of oral storytelling, which generally emphasizes the importance of cunning. They are almost entirely nomadic, but a few of them do inhabit city-states, typically living in mud-brick buildings. City-states often go to war, hiring the nomads as mercenaries. Their rulers are mostly religious figures, whose roles are hereditary.
csg_lasat.language: Lasat generally speak Basic, but when they do, they refer to themselves in the third person, rather than using pronouns.
csg_lasat.homeworld: Lasat come from Lasan, a very arid planet in the southern part of Wild Space. It has some mountains, but almost all Lasat have chosen to live in its flat deserts.
csg_lasat.description: A species of carnivorous mammals with fur, wide eyes, and pointed ears, the Lasat's most valuable asset is their cunning. They excel in building and setting traps when they hunt, and their ingenuity has made it difficult for the Empire to enslave them.
csg_lasat.sidebar_text: Many Lasat are slaves, and that is basically the only way that they ever leave their homeworld. However, they make for very poor slaves, because they are often able to outwit their captors and find ways to escape before they provide any real value to their owner. Additionally, they lack the strength of the Wookiees whom they resemble, so they are far less suitable for menial labor.

csg_leffingite.name: Leffingite

special_abilities.name: Large Ears
special_abilities.description: Add boost on auditory Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Pack Instincts
special_abilities.description: When performing the assist maneuver, grant 2 boosts instead of 1.

csg_leffingite.physiology: Leffingites are an ovine sentient species with large leaf-shaped ears and four horns atop their head, each of which is directly above an eye. Their two smaller horns are in the center of their forehead, just as their two smaller eyes are also at the center. Their nose is long and flat with large nostrils, and their mouth is wrinkled with sharp teeth. Their skin is wrinkled and tan in color, and they tend to be short in stature due to their hunched posture.
csg_leffingite.society: Leffingites tend to be group-oriented and collaborative, tendencies that can also make them naïve and too quick to to trust. They rely on their herds for safety and psychological support, and those separated from their own kind often enter a deep depression. As such, Leffingites are not a very common sight in the wider galaxy. They are averse to conflict and tend to hide from their problems, rarely standing up to those they disagree with. For some, this can mean creating intricate webs of dishonesty, flattery, and secrecy, juggling a variety of different aliases and identities depending on their situation. Among their own, Leffingites are usually either too naïve or too passive to call out these deceptions, which can often make young Leffingite criminals overconfident in their cunning. Those criminals unfortunate enough to take their business offworld typically end up being in over their head.
csg_leffingite.language: There are a variety of Leffingite languages, the most common of which include Oub and Ermenian, but Basic is widely accepted as a lingua franca.
csg_leffingite.homeworld: Leffingites hail from the large, high-gravity Outer Rim planet of Almak, which forms a double-planet system with drier Iyilis. Almak is a backwater planet, with an agrarian society on its flat plains save for the occasional textile factories, which make most of their exports. Dense cities are very rare, with almost all of the land covered by vast farmlands or suburban towns. A small number of Leffingites live on Iyilis, but it was first colonized by the Lutrillians, and the two societies generally leave one another alone.
csg_leffingite.description: Leffingites are ovine mammals that excel at getting along in herds, and they rarely do anything that would risk stirring the pot. Some of them on Almak have formed a collectivist subculture called the Great Flock.
csg_leffingite.sidebar_text: Many Leffingites are a part of a unique society that they call the Great Flock, which has hundreds of millions of members. They preach collectivist ideals and shun individualism, advocating for selflessness, charity, and teamwork. Their five leaders, collectively referred to as the Daropaas, hold positions for life and are worshipped with cult-like reverence. They seek to function like a sovereign nation, holding a vast tract of land across the plains of Almak. Those in this region who are not members of the Great Flock are ostracized, bullied, and stolen from, thus bringing the group into tension with the wider government. Such persecutions occur often underneath its seemingly utopian surface, and those who speak out against it are quickly silenced. Over the past few years, the Empire has been negotiating with the Great Flock, as Moff Sulamar believes that he can easily control the entire Leffingite population if he can win the allegiance of the Daropaas. He has given weapons to the Great Flock, allowing them to violently expand their territory.
csg_leffingite._provenance_note: The Leffingite species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_lepi.name: Lepi

special_abilities.name: High Energy
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Dodge.”

csg_lepi.physiology: Lepi are furry green creatures that have distinctive buck teeth and long ears. They have large feet and strong legs. This, combined with a fast metabolism and a skinny frame, gives them impressive speed. They have a tail that varies greatly in length. Their face also has black eyes and whiskers. While there is a misconception that the Lepi eat space carrots, they are actually carnivorous.
csg_lepi.society: Lepi are known for their flightiness; they descended from skittish herbivores and like to stay moving. This is enhanced by their curiosity and desire to explore. They are impulsive and typically have very aggressive goals for adventure and fame. They are also very prideful creatures who like to brag and show off. Going with this is the fact that they can be very sensitive, in particular when it comes to insults about their families or their rodent-like appearance. These insults can bring about violence or anger from them. Despite this issue, many get along well. Humor in particular is one of their strong suits. They are a religious people, which they often take with them through lucky charms.
