special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Hard Headed.”

special_abilities.name: Desert Natives
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for arid or hot conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_nazren.physiology: Nazren are tall humanoids with long arms and wide shoulders but short legs and thin hips. They are slow-moving but strong, resilient, adapted to the harsh conditions of their windy desert homeworld, and over two meters tall. They have yellow-brown skin with knobs on their back and lack hair or a nose. Their mouth is wide, and their hands and feet have four digits. Nazren age slowly, reaching adulthood around 30 and often living to 300.
csg_nazren.society: Nazren tend to be quiet and reclusive, and they are mostly peaceful but will stand up to injustice and defend the weak. Family is of utmost importance to them, as their harsh homeworld, Nizon, frequently destroys material possessions. They live in tribes that make decisions collectively, deliberating extensively until every adult can come to an agreement. It can be a long process, but Nazren are patient and don’t mind it. These tribes are nomadic on Nizon, and they have a sense of wanderlust that makes many of them enjoy travelling the galaxy. After being enslaved by the Empire, they are very careful to never again lose their freedom. Nazren have a long history, having been around for close to a million years, and they have an oral religious tradition that claims Nizon was once lush, but that they took it for granted, so the gods punished them: The sun grew bigger, and flaming rocks fell from the sky, turning it into a barren desert. Scholars believe that this cataclysm occurred hundreds of millenia ago when a large celestial body collided with Nizon and pushed it closer to its sun. They also speculate that this may have been a good thing, as the past abundance led to corruption and warfare. Only by being forced to spread out and live simpler lives did Nazren become peaceful. Their current technology is very primitive: They have made excellent moisture vaporators and breath masks to keep out sand, although their hardy physiology also reduces the need for the latter. They do occasionally trade between tribes, meeting up every two years to make deals. In recent years, Nazren have somewhat modernized, scavenging Imperial technology and learning about offworld arts and sciences.
csg_nazren.language: Nazren speak a native language of the same name, and those who are former slaves typically know Basic.
csg_nazren.homeworld: Nazren come from Nizon, an inhospitable desert planet in the Mid Rim. It is a very dusty planet, so other species are recommended to have a mask, especially in the badlands, which also features dangerous blade scorpions. Sheltered by a mountain, there is a single city called Ahdjok. It has a spaceport as well as stone buildings that average a dozen stories high, and it is a site to which Nazren from all around the planet make pilgrimages to. They visit Martyr’s Plaza, an ancient dome which is surrounded by crumbling statues and covered by scrolls that tell Nazren history. Of practical importance, Ahdjok has a turbolaser and shield for defense, and it is almost impossible to navigate the asteroid field around the planet without aid from its communications center.
csg_nazren.description: Nazren are a species of desert-dwelling humanoids who live in primitive nomadic tribes. They value their family more than wealth, and they deliberate carefully before making any major decisions.
csg_nazren.sidebar_text: Shortly before the rise of the Empire, Nizon rose in galactic prominence as valuable ores were discovered. However, this attention turned out to be unfortunate when Nazren were enslaved by the Empire shortly after its formation and deported en masse to the nearby planet Centares. They won their freedom in a revolution, but they were not far from extinction due to the harsh treatment, and the population is still dramatically reduced. However, they are now much more dispersed, with some slaves and many former slaves roaming the galaxy.

csg_nazzar.name: Nazzar
csg_nazzar.physiology: The Nazzar are large equines, distinguished by their elongated snout, mane, and eyes on the side of their head. They also have four-fingered hands and long ears. They are an athletic species, both agile and physically powerful, and they stand about two meters tall. Their skin is dark and covered in fur that ranges in color from gray to brown to blue. They have prominent nostrils and their eyes lack pupils. Although they mature at a normal rate, they live for several decades longer than humans.
csg_nazzar.society: Nazzar are a very noble and trustworthy people, and they have a strong moral compass. They are also a very spiritual people, united by their belief in the tenets of Ulizra, although they are divided into fourteen sects. One of the most important aspects of their spirituality is selflessness, as they believe the group is more important than the individual. They abhor other cultures, and they seek to keep their beliefs untainted by the rest of the galaxy. As such, they are very isolated on their homeworld, only interacting with the rest of the galaxy when absolutely necessary and being very cold toward outsiders if they travel. Very few Nazzar live away from their people, especially since the Empire came to power, an event that caused many of them to return home. Occasionally, a Nazzar preacher will attempt to bring their religion of Ulizra to other societies, but their message is rarely accepted, and they typically give up eventually. A few Nazzar abandon Ulizra entirely, and they typically leave their home to become a fanatical follower of some other religion, cult, or political fringe group.
csg_nazzar.language: Nazzar typically speak and read their native language, Nazzar.
csg_nazzar.homeworld: Nazzar come from Nazzri, a temperate Mid Rim planet covered by plains with dense vegetation. They have also colonized three nearby star systems, all of which form their own isolated cluster. Although they were once part of the Republic, the Empire has yet to interact with the Nazzar, and they will ignore their invitation to join the New Republic. Their government, once a monarchy, is now run by a group of religious oligarchs.
csg_nazzar.description: Athletic equines who are tall, durable, and nimble, the Nazzar are known best for their religion of Ulizra. Through their faith, they all have a strong moral compass, but they have isolated themselves from the rest of the galaxy in order to protect their culture.
csg_nazzar.sidebar_text: One of the other reasons that a Nazzar can be found off of their homeworld is by going on a boqeri. The boqeri is almost like an exile, although it is self-imposed and typically only done by those who are wealthier and in good standing. A boqeri is ultimately a search for spiritual truth, and the seeker traditionally returns home once they have reached the understanding that they seek. However, some find the galaxy to be a very interesting place and decide not to return home.

csg_neimoidian.name: Neimoidian
csg_neimoidian.physiology: Distant relatives to the more successful Duros, Neimoidians have a noseless face that is gray-green in color. Their red eyes have pupils that still split horizontally, and their cheeks are somewhat sunken. Neimoidians are distinguished by their lumpy forehead and mouth that naturally frowns. They lack a nose, instead smelling using organs that are just below their eyes. Their lungs expand and contract wildly when a Neimoidian is under stress, leading to the phrase that Neimoidians are the only species with an organ devoted to worrying. Neimoidians are very prone to disease, and they have carried many diseases to other parts of the galaxy. While their hands are humanoid, their feet have two claw-like toes. As young, they are born live in a larval grub state, and at death, their body desiccates rapidly.
csg_neimoidian.society: Neimoidian society values greed and places finances above all else. Up until age seven, Neimoidian children are grubs who must fight for the little food that they receive. This begins to teach them greed, which they see as a virtue. Even after this, the continuing education of Neimoidians also ensures that greediness is rewarded, although many still put on altruistic façades. Because of this harsh upbringing, many Neimoidians come to hate their homeworld and are quick to leave it. They are immoral by nature and use any methods necessary to get what they want, including deception and extortion. Although they are excellent businessmen, perhaps the most infamous characteristic for Neimoidians is cowardice, which makes them a laughing stock to other cultures—most notably, their distant relatives, the Duros, who are much more eager to seek adventure. Neimoidians used to respond to this with a planetary pride, considering their culture more successful and trying to distinguish themselves with every opportunity. However, the collapse of the Trade Federation and their losses in the Clone Wars have left the Neimoidian culture humiliated, and the species is portrayed as villainous, lazy, greedy, and cowardly. Now, many Neimoidians pretend to be Duros.
csg_neimoidian.language: The staccato croaks of Pak Pak are the Neimoidian tongue, but most know Basic as well.
csg_neimoidian.homeworld: Neimoidia is a world in the Colonies, but many Neimoidians come from their purse worlds of Cato Neimoidia, Deko Neimoidia, and Koru Neimoidia. It centers around fungus farming and is ruled by a Trade Monarch.
csg_neimoidian.description: Shrewd and greedy, the Neimoidians are the more cowardly relatives of the Duros. Though they are poor and will starve unless they are greedy enough as children, they are often very wealthy as adults, which they flaunt with ornate clothing.
csg_neimoidian.sidebar_text: Their focus on status is especially portrayed in the complex rituals of Neimoidian clothing, which they use to show rank, wealth, and prestige. Symbolic meanings are hidden in the fabrics, patterns, and colors of the robes and hats. Neimoidians rarely part with their fancy clothes, especially their hat, which they are only separated from in death.

csg_nelvaanian.name: Nelvaanian

special_abilities.name: Cold Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_nelvaanian.physiology: Nelvaanians are lupine mammals who have blue-gray fur to protect them from the cold. They are predators, and their fingers and toes have claws for combat. Their head has a pointed chin and long ears, and they have long, black hair. Their snout also features a dog-like nose and a mouth full of sharp teeth. Their eyes are black. Most Nelvaanian warriors have tattoos, which are geometric and typically have spirals composed of rectangles.
csg_nelvaanian.society: Nelvaanians are a warrior people, and they are highly spiritual. They live in hunter-gatherer tribes, and their lifestyle is very primitive. Males are typically responsible for fighting and hunting, while females focus on building, gathering, and raising children. Raising children is considered to be a sacred duty and a great honor. Their religion worships their planet itself, which they know as the “Great Mother.” Tribes are ruled by one Chieftain and one Shaman, the former of whom leads them in practical matters, while the latter deals with spiritual rites.
csg_nelvaanian.language: Nelvaanians speak Nelvaanese, although many of the mutant ones have a noticeably different accent.
csg_nelvaanian.homeworld: Nelvaan is a frigid Outer Rim planet with below-average gravity. It has many mountains and glaciers, most of which are covered in trees. It has an abandoned Techno Union laboratory, which was destroyed during the Clone Wars. Many Nelvaanians live in small villages, although they do not farm, so they must travel to find food.
csg_nelvaanian.description: A nomadic species of blue-skinned warriors native to the frigid lands of Nelvaan, the Nelvaanians combine their physical prowess with spiritual devotion. This attracted the attention of General Greivous, who, with help from the Techno Union, mutated many of them to become hulking monsters.
csg_nelvaanian.sidebar_text: Although the Nelvaanians were mostly isolated and had little interaction with the rest of the galaxy, they caught the attention of General Grievous because of their similarities to his own people, the Kaleesh. The respect was mutual, because the Nelvaanians believed him to be a figure from their mythology. Skakoan engineers from the Techno Union experimented with cybernetic augmentations for the Nelvaanians, using steroids as well as microelectronics to turn many of the males into 3-meter tall giants. Unfortunately for the CIS, the Nelvaanians involved came to regret their involvement. The facility was attacked by Anakin Skywalker, and most of the subjects destroyed their cybernetics to fight against the CIS and return to their tribe. Although the mutant Nelvaanians were small in number, epigenetic changes during the experiments caused their male descendants to retain some of the mutations.

csg_neti.name: Neti

special_abilities.name: Massive
special_abilities.description: Receive 2 ranks in the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Photoautotrophic
special_abilities.description: Do not require normal food, surviving only off of sunlight, Carbon Dioxide, and small amounts of water for long periods of time, especially in a tree-like Silhouette 3 state.

special_abilities.name: Shape-Shifters
special_abilities.description: As an action, may attempt to shape-shift by suffering 2 strain and making an average Resilience check. If successful, may choose to be bipedal, quadrupedal, or Silhouette 2. May also make a hard Resilience check to become Silhouette 1. When quadrupedal, may only spend 1 maneuver per turn moving, but increase encumbrance threshold by 2. Be fully mobile when bipedal. When Silhouette 1 or 2, remove the effects of Massive. May revert to tree-like Silhouette 3 without a check.

special_abilities.name: Tree-like
special_abilities.description: Still possess arms, but may not walk, run, or become prone. Add up to 4 boosts on Stealth checks in forests or among foliage.

special_abilities.name: Wooden Body
special_abilities.description: Double damage from fire or fire-based weapons.

csg_neti.physiology: Neti are a plant-based species with the ability to change their shape relatively freely. The Neti cannot shape-shift like the Clawdites or Shi’idos in order to disguise themselves, but they can move in incredible ways to become a humanoid biped, a hunched quadruped, or a structure resembling a tree. They are incapable of walking as a tree and slow as a quadruped, but they always retain their branch-like arms. They can also increase or decrease their size, becoming as small as a human or as large as ten meters. When resting, they tend to be tree-like and about five meters tall. Regardless of size and shape, their skin is always tough, gray, and bark-like, and they have photosynthetic foliage at the top of their body that can be green, black, or brown. In the short term, they can survive entirely off of photosynthesis, even though they only drink a tenth as much water as other species. Neti live for about 3,000 years, and their seeds, released every few centuries, often lie dormant for over 1,000 years.
csg_neti.society: The Neti are secretive and secluded, but they are also philosophers, explorers, and intellectuals. They enjoy pondering deep mysteries, and they can be friendly to those willing to discuss with them. Because they only reproduce once every few centuries and live for a very long time, their population is small, and they rarely leave the areas they call home.
csg_neti.language: Neti are taught the Neti language from birth, a language made very complex by its combination of verbal and gesture-based communication. Many of them also know Basic.
csg_neti.homeworld: Neti were first found on Ryyk, a planet which was destroyed by a supernova 4,000 years ago. Many now live isolated on Nerit, a temperate moon of Ossus, while others are found on Myrkr, a jungle planet which has been historically kept secret. No research has proven their true origin, and many consider the species to be mythical.
csg_neti.description: Neti are Force-sensitive plants with a long lifespan who are capable of shape-shifting. They are reclusive and mysterious, and they are few in number, as their homeworld was destroyed millenia ago.
csg_neti.sidebar_text: The Neti are entirely Force-sensitive, although their secluded nature means that not all of them are trained to use their powers. Many of them excel in using trances, and photosynthesis allows them to sustain themselves much more easily than other species. Combining the Force with their plant-like physiology, they can elongate their lifespan and hibernate for millenia. Many Neti did this after the destruction of Ryyk, awaiting rescue in remote locales. Some remain undiscovered to this day.

csg_nikto.name: Nikto

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3. Add boost when climbing surfaces that can be pierced by a claw.

special_abilities.name: Heat fins
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for temperature by adjusting fins.

special_abilities.name: Island Natives
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for wet conditions, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Desert Natives
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Ultrasonic Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove setback from Perception checks.

csg_nikto.physiology: Nikto are reptilians that have many races, all of which are humanoid in size and have leathery skin. Their eyes are black and protected by a membrane, and they tend to have a rather blank expression. Despite this, many are more observant and cunning than they would seem at first glance. They have five subspecies, the most common of which are the desert-dwelling Red Nikto. They have red-brown skin, forehead ridges, a flap over their nose, eight facial horns around their eyes, and two on their chin. The Green Nikto, coming from the forests, have scaly olive or brown skin, a multitude of small facial horns around their eyes, and claws used for climbing. The Mountain Nikto have blue-gray skin, facial fins to regulate heat, and a flap over their nose. The Pale Nikto, coming from islands, have white skin, facial horns like the Red and Green Nikto, and smaller facial fins than the Mountain Nikto. The Southern Nikto have white, yellow, or orange skin, a flap over the nose, and tubes on the back of their head that sense ultrasonic waves. All subspecies can interbreed, but a Nikto of mixed parents will typically end up with one race or the other, only being visibly mixed about seven percent of the time. These mixed Nikto are the most outcast.
csg_nikto.society: The Nikto have had a bloody history of wars between subspecies, but they eventually united to deal with more pressing issues, such as the harsh nature of their homeworld. They have nevertheless developed a culture of fierce warriors, and all are effective in combat. Particularly dangerous is the tradition of the Morgukai, a secret society of warriors known for their cortosis weapons who formed as early rebels against the Hutts. Their founder, an ancient Red Nikto named Morguk, attempted to free their race via any means necessary during the Hutt-Xim Conflict. All Nikto are tenacious and determined, willing to do what it takes to survive, and are almost entirely without humor.
csg_nikto.language: Nikto learn Nikto as their native language, but all eventually learn Huttese as well.
csg_nikto.homeworld: The Nikto have been molded by the harsh nature of their world, Kintan. It has a diverse ecosystem, including forests, archipelagos, magma fields, swamps, rocky wastelands, deserts, and mountains. Most eventually are taken off of it to serve on Nal Hutta or other Hutt worlds.
csg_nikto.description: A species that are mostly enslaved by the Hutts, Nikto are strong and tough. They have many races which have evolved for different environments. They are also very serious and prone to violence.
csg_nikto.sidebar_text: Nikto are one of the many species that are almost entirely enslaved by the Hutts. Few resist it, as the life on their homeworld is even more arduous, and the Hutts helped liberate them from the death cult of M’dweshuu in their ancient history. The great Churabba the Acquisitioner brutally executed the high priests, and the Nikto became eager to serve their goddess in the stars. Over the subsequent millennia, the Hutts have encouraged the Nikto to become powerful warriors, and they have done little to resist it. A few Nikto have escaped from their Hutt masters, but doing so is very dangerous. They are often captured and brought back into servitude before they can leave Hutt Space.

csg_nimbanel.name: Nimbanel
csg_nimbanel.physiology: Nimbanels are a species of herbivores who are warm-blooded reptilians. They are humanoids with gray-purple skin, but they are best distinguished by two fleshy lumps which hang over their mouth and resemble a human mustache in shape. Their nostrils are also on these lumps, and their eyes are dark and circular. Although many are bald, some have a bit of dark hair behind their head or on their cheeks. Additionally, they boast a highly advanced mind which is adept at puzzle-solving. From a genetic standpoint, nothing prevents them from being physically strong, but a majority of them strongly prefer to use their mind rather than their body.
csg_nimbanel.society: Nimbanels are a people who excel in mathematics, puzzle-solving, and bureaucracy of all sorts. A majority of the plants they once ate required complex tool usage to access, which prompted cultural value for such skills. They compete in clan rivalries with forms of information stockpiling, complex paperwork, and convolution of all sorts. Nimbanels are also an extremely competitive people who value success and have little tolerance for those who stand in their way. These traits made them excel in the bureaucratic webs of the Republic, while many others found success as a part of BoSS. Eventually, BoSS attempted to cut ties with the Nimbanels, but they found a way to retain power by making a deal with the Hutts. The outcome of this deal included Hutt annexation of Nimban and Hutt access to Nimban’s databanks, although the Nimbanels managed to maintain much of their internal freedom. In exchange, they received Hutt backing in their venture to remain a part of BoSS. To this day, they are the only species to have petitioned the Hutts requesting to be annexed. Although they can be involved with business ventures of all sorts, many work for the Hutts.
csg_nimbanel.language: Nimbanels are gifted with snouts that can effectively articulate many languages. Among these tongues are their own native language of Nimbanese, Basic, and Huttese. Most Nimbanels know all three of these languages.
csg_nimbanel.homeworld: The Nimbanels come from Nimban, a terrestrial planet that is now on the border of Hutt Space. It is divided into multiple states, which are each ruled by a coalition of clan councils.
csg_nimbanel.description: Mathematically-inclined reptiles, the Nimbanel are highly adept puzzlers, and they excel in jobs that involve finance or data analytics. They voluntarily left the Republic and joined Hutt Space in order to remain a part of the BoSS while retaining relative independence.
csg_nimbanel.sidebar_text: The most important form of competition in Nimbanel society is the muhndee. In a muhndee, rival clans compete with each other in a way that resolves heated conflicts via a simple game. Rival clans, which are common among Nimbanels, challenge each other with a riddle, paradox, arithmetic problem, or other puzzle, and each clan gets one year to solve it. In more recent years, they have also used muhndees to resolve elections: Every five years, family heads hold electoral muhndees to grant positions on clan councils.

csg_noehon.name: Noehon

special_abilities.name: Arboreal
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on checks to climb.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Scent
special_abilities.description: Unless thoroughly washed multiple times per day, produce a strong scent, adding a setback on Stealth checks. This scent may also linger on items, clothing, or even other people after close contact.

csg_noehon.physiology: Noehons are a species of short insects with four arms and two legs. Averaging just above one meter in height, they are nimble but not very strong. Their green carapace is relatively soft, lacking the chitin that protects other insects, and it is covered in short bristles. Their red eyes are enormous and multifaceted, and they have two small antennae instead of hair. Their mouth also has two prominent mandibles which each have a gland for producing scents. Because of these glands, Noehons emit a powerful, musky odor that they can use to identify themselves and mark their property. Since they are arboreal, Noehons are excellent climbers.
csg_noehon.society: Noehons are an obsessive people, willing to go to great lengths to fulfill their goals and letting nothing stand between them and their destiny. They are organized, wasting nothing, and they are highly adaptive to new challenges. Noehons live in tribes known as welds, which are isolated groups of 200-10,000 led by a dominant male. Often, adolescent males will attempt to seize power in their weld by killing the leader once they come of age. Welds often trade goods and technology with one other, and adolescent females are sometimes traded as well. Some welds prefer to steal from the smaller or more vulnerable welds. Industrialization from offworlds has allowed for more advanced warfare using blasters.
csg_noehon.language: Noehons speak Noehonese, a language which uses clicks from their mandibles and skreaks as well as scents. Because of this unique method of communication, they struggle with learning other languages. However, they see many offworlders, so learning Basic is usually worthwhile.
csg_noehon.homeworld: Noehons come from the jungle planet of Noe’ha’on, which is located in the Expansion Region. Using spacecraft from offworlders, they have begun to colonize nearby worlds.
csg_noehon.description: Small but nimble insects who live in trees, the Noehons have a musky scent that they use to mark their property. They are organized into a hierarchy, and they are notoriously obsessive in getting what they want.
csg_noehon.sidebar_text: Noehons have a hierarchical society, making slavery seem very natural for them. Frequently, Noehons are taken as slaves or transferred offworld as indentured servants. They sheepishly obey, for the most part. Conversely, when Noehons are free, they are unnecessarily cruel. Even those who do not practice slavery are very abusive and harsh toward their underlings. They also use their scent to mark subordinates, just as they would label their territory or property.

csg_noghri.name: Noghri

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Olfaxes
special_abilities.description: Add boost on olfactory Perception checks, and may identify bloodlines using smell.

special_abilities.name: Superb Reflexes
special_abilities.description: Add 1 success on all initiative checks.

csg_noghri.physiology: Noghri are hairless reptiles, although they have blue-gray skin instead of scales. They are on the small side, but they more than make up for it with a well-muscled frame and extremely fast movements. Their black eyes are constantly darting around in search of threats, although their nose is very effective as well, which they use to identify the clans of their fellow Noghri. They have ridged eyebrows and a mouth full of sharp teeth. They have extremely sharp claws on both their fingers and toes, but perhaps their most powerful ability is their reflexes, which are among the best in the galaxy.
csg_noghri.society: Noghri society places heavy value on honor and loyalty. Many will serve their entire life as a bodyguard or assassin for a particular employer. Although they make devoted employees and do their best to adapt to the customs of those around them, they are hardly ever sociable or fun-loving. They instead devote their entire focus to being ready for their deadly work, although they prefer not to involve too much advanced technology. Instead they rely on stealth, timing, and primitive blades. Noghri once ferociously fought each other in clan wars, but in more modern times, the clans are better at getting along. Their clans center around a meeting center called a “dukha,” where they do most of their business, and all of the families in it are ruled by an older female “maitrahk,” who acts as a lore keeper.
csg_noghri.language: The Noghri native language is Honoghran, although many learn Basic to interact with Imperials. Their voice is raspy and quiet.
csg_noghri.homeworld: The Noghri homeworld of Honoghr is an isolated and ecologically devastated Outer Rim world near Hutt Space. Once a world where they could farm on the plains and hunt in the rainforests, it is now a desert. Some are starting to form small oases, such as a hidden canyon called The Future of the Noghri.
csg_noghri.description: Small reptiles with sharp claws, the Noghri are renowned for their reflexes and combative abilities. They are excellent as assassins and bodyguards. The Empire has used manipulation to acquire their services, and the Noghri essentially worship Darth Vader.
csg_noghri.sidebar_text: Many Noghri now work for the Empire as a result of a disaster going back decades: During the Clone Wars, a ship full of a chemical weapon, trihexalophine1138, crashed onto the Noghri homeworld. Ecological disaster ensued, and the Noghri faced extinction as their farms ceased to produce. Only an intervention by the Galactic Empire saved the people. Darth Vader offered to provide Imperial help in fixing the planet as long as the Noghri were to serve the Empire during that time. Little do the Noghri know that the repairs have been sabotaged by the Empire so as to continue indefinitely and put the Noghri in indefinite servitude. For now, many serve the Empire as elite assassins, calling themselves the Noghri Death Commandos. All are very loyal to the Empire and practically worship Vader himself. After Vader's death, they will transfer their service to Jerec, and then start working for Thrawn just prior to Jerec's demise. Eventually, the Imperial treachery will be exposed by the New Republic, and the Noghri will then serve as bodyguards to Vader’s heir, Leia.

csg_nosaurian.name: Nosaurian

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Claws and Horns
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds, and have a Crit rating of 3. May spend 2 advantage to add the Pierce 2 quality by hitting with horns.

special_abilities.name: Sing Down the Sun
special_abilities.description: On homeworld, must bray at the setting sun, or may feel compulsion anywhere by rolling a despair. Braying incapacitates for 2 rounds, and resisting requires a hard Discipline check.

csg_nosaurian.physiology: Nosaurians are a species of smaller reptiles best distinguished by their horned head. Their feet are birdlike, with three toes pointing forward and one pointing back. Both fingers and toes are clawed, making them formidable when unarmed, despite a smaller size. Their tough hide is scaled, typically light green or brown. They can also be black, gray, green, yellow, orange, or red. Their scales are lighter at the chin and belly. Their eyes, near the top of their hairless head, cannot see color. They have two nostrils but no nose, and their wide mouth has sharp teeth. Their mouth has a further distinguishing ability: emitting light at will.
csg_nosaurian.society: Though not the most friendly when around outsiders, (particularly humans) Nosaurians are typically level-headed and congenial. They live in clans, which sometimes stay on their own as independent towns, while others make larger city-states. They are a proud people, very set in their ways.
csg_nosaurian.language: Nosaurian is a tongue that is mostly high pitched, but it is lower-pitched if a Nosaurian is angry or upset. The written form uses many metaphors related to nature. While Nosaurians are capable of speaking Basic, many dislike the language for association with human oppressors.
csg_nosaurian.homeworld: New Plympto is a swampy Core World that is home to the Nosaurians and a small human population. Native crustaceans called rikknit are the only major source of industry, as their eggs are edible. Reduced numbers of rikknit have significantly reduced the Nosaurian population. Homes on the world are domed mounds of soil, arranged in rings to provide a central community space.
csg_nosaurian.description: The Nosaurians are stubborn and proud, but they have dealt with great troubles under the Republic. Their attempts to secede during the Clone Wars have made them victims of Imperial oppression, which is even worse than that from the Republic. They are horned and tend to bray at a setting sun.
csg_nosaurian.sidebar_text: Nosaurians were first introduced to the galaxy through contact with Corellians. From then on, they were represented in the Senate by the Corellians, and Corellians held economic control. Losing all profits from trade, Nosaurians came to dislike the Corellians. After the Republic banned the export of rikknit eggs, their main product, Nosaurians joined the Confederacy. With help from the droid army, they attempted to fight back the Republic attackers. The deactivation of the CIS army sealed defeat, and they are now oppressed by the Empire. Mostly enslaved, resistance still continues but with little success.

csg_nuiwit.name: Nuiwit

special_abilities.name: Cold-Blooded
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for arid conditions, add setback for wet conditions.

special_abilities.name: Bulging Eyes
special_abilities.description: Can see in all directions.

csg_nuiwit.physiology: Also known as the Altorians, the Nuiwit are typically quadrupedal lizards who have scaled skin which is gray-green or gold-brown. They have a long tail, which they can detach in order to escape predators. If they do this, the tail regrows in about a month. Additionally, they can use their tail for balance, allowing them to stand on their two back legs and use their hands for manipulation. Even standing up, they are still shorter than other species, about one and a half meters tall. They have clawed hands and feet for traction when they move, although they provide few benefits in combat. Their front limbs also have a rear-facing digit in addition to the three front-facing digits. The Nuiwit have bulging eyes on eyestalks, granting them 360 degree vision with which to recognize predators. Their head also features a long tongue, and they have nostrils but no nose. They do have a row of spikes from the back of their head to along their neck and all the way down their back and tail. Nuiwit are adapted to a hot and dry environment, as they are cold-blooded. Nevertheless, they are still only awake at morning and twilight, when the temperature is reasonably cool. They are also entirely herbivorous, a trait which has no doubt caused their diminutive stature and lack of combative abilities.
csg_nuiwit.society: Nuiwit are extremely pacifist, becoming horrified by violence of any type. They live a simple life in closely-knit communities that survive off of agriculture and industry. Even before they were discovered by the wider galaxy, the Nuiwits had a reasonable degree of advanced technology, including highly refined agricultural sciences, basic droids, and extensive mining. When their world was first discovered by Rego Mineral Company about sixteen years ago, they were quick to engage in commerce. Their traditional handicrafts have sold well on the wider market, and they also experienced financial success by trading away mining rights to the offworlders. Their politics are fairly civilized, as they are ruled by a Council of Elders who typically have the best interests of the entire society in mind.
csg_nuiwit.language: Given their recent discovery, Nuiwit tend to use their native language, although their frequent contact with offworlders means that most of them also know Basic.
csg_nuiwit.homeworld: As their second name of Altorians indicates, Nuiwit come from Altor 14, a planet composed of warm deserts and dry plains. It is on the fringe of galactic society, at the edge of the southeastern Outer Rim, and its population is under one million sentients.
csg_nuiwit.description: Small herbivorous lizards who live in a hot and dry desert, the Nuiwits' total pacifism has done them a great deal of harm. Another sentient species, the primitive Avogwi, prey on them frequently, but the Nuiwit refuse to exterminate them.
csg_nuiwit.sidebar_text: To the Avogwi, the other sentient species native to their homeworld, the Nuiwit are just a species of prey who may be killed without remorse. However, the Nuiwit refuse to take any offensive action against the Avogwi, even to fight in self-defense, because of their strictly pacifistic nature. The Nuiwit are technologically far superior to the Avogwi, and their use of commerce has allowed them to control an increasingly large amount of territory that they use to farm and mine. This territory was once the hunting grounds of the Avogwi, but Nuiwit civilization prevents them from hunting. As such, even though the Nuiwit refuse to take direct action against the Avogwi, they are nevertheless responsible for the Avogwi’s declining population. As the Nuiwit see it, this approach may cost them their own lives in the short term, but it will ultimately result in prosperity once the Avogwi are forced to relocate or change their brutal ways. Indeed, many Avogwi now look offworld to find work.

csg_nuknog.name: Nuknog
csg_nuknog.physiology: Nuknog are short reptiles who are just more than one meter tall. They have leathery skin which is wrinkled and red-brown in color. Nuknog have a unique shape with very short legs, a wide stomach, and a long neck. They have a tall, bumpy, ridge atop their hairless head, and their head is widest at the jaw and near the eyes. Their nostrils are flat on their head, lacking a nose. Their eyes are black, and they have a series of bumps along their jawline. They have three toes on their feet, and they have four-fingered hands.
csg_nuknog.society: Nuknog are a short-sighted people, irrational and quick to complain. They are extremely petty, getting upset over everything and rarely showing gratitude to anyone. They are highly suspicious of everyone, and they are quick to find scapegoats. They are eager to get out of difficult situations, but they are generally unwilling to do any work for it in the short run. As such, they typically end up trading one problem for another. This also makes them easily manipulated.
csg_nuknog.language: Nuknog speak Nuknog, a language with a simple alphabet. It is gruff, and it uses a number of barks and squeaks. Those who sell themselves as slaves also typically learn Basic.
csg_nuknog.homeworld: Nuknog come from the Outer Rim planet of Sump, a planet which has been dramatically polluted by extensive mining. It is humid, and most of the surface is covered in swamps which are extremely toxic. It can barely sustain life, and the pollution dramatically reduces the lifespan of the Nuknog.
csg_nuknog.description: Ill-tempered reptiles, the Nuknog are shorter with a ridge on their head but are better known for their constant complaining. They are incredibly short-sighted, focusing only on their most immediate wants with no plan for the future.
csg_nuknog.sidebar_text: The Nuknog were once a people who were employed and, for the most part, satisfied. They sold their planet to a mining company in exchange for jobs, food, and shelter, and this arrangement lasted almost 1,000 years. Although the jobs were dangerous, food was relatively scarce, and the barracks were small, the Nuknog were employed and the situation became relatively stable. This changed when the Republic arrived, forcing the mining companies to dissolve over the mistreatment of the Nuknog. The Nuknog society collapsed. Although the Republic provided emergency food supplies in order to appease popular opinion sympathizing with the Nuknog, they did nothing to rebuild the society that they destroyed. The Nuknog were left unemployed, and life on their homeworld is completely terrible. Few can survive for more than half of their lifespan, and they have no real industries. As such, the only hope for most Nuknog is by selling themselves into slavery in exchange for passage offworld, an exchange which usually improves their quality of life. Because of how much the Republic destroyed their economy, Nuknog were strong supporters of the Separatists. However, they end up under Imperial control after the war.

csg_oliar.name: Oliar

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_oliar.physiology: Oliar are smaller avians who live in aquatic environments, where their webbed feet aid them in swimming. While they have lost their wings, they retain their feathers, which can come in a wide variety of hues. They have a bill that aids them in catching fish and crustaceans, although they can also eat a variety of plants and their seeds.
csg_oliar.society: Family is important above all else to the Oliar, who often have migratory patterns that make it hard for them to get too attached to their possessions. They know even their most distant of relatives, living in groups known as clanholds that often include many distant cousins and raise children communally. Each clanhold has their own clanhall that is stationary, but Oliar often migrate, and most have some sort of relative in another clanhold that is willing to host them at their clanhall. They are talkative and very friendly beings, although on the downside, gossip also spreads quickly. Most Oliar hold countless grudges over various things that they heard were done to their distant cousins. Their marriages are very important to them, with extravagant weddings leading into highly loyal lifelong partnerships. While fond of travel, particularly after being widowed, it is rarer to see Oliar making friends with those beyond their own race, so some other species find them a bit rude. Few make permanent homes on other worlds, as they always return to their clanhall. Those who find work offworld are most often noted for their abilities in culinary and medical professions.
csg_oliar.language: Due to their frequent travels, Oliar have all come to speak a single language, Vheliar. Many of them also learn Basic, which they can speak albeit with a somewhat nasally tone.
csg_oliar.homeworld: The Oliar homeworld of Anatoo is a damp Inner Rim planet with shallow oceans and vast marshlands, the latter of which they’ve made their homes in. Well-integrated with galactic society, it is a major exporter of seafoods and a few pharmaceuticals.
csg_oliar.description: The most important thing to Oliar is their family, which they view as being very vast, even including distant cousins. These avian creatures live together in clanholds, those they are often found traveling.
csg_oliar.sidebar_text: Currently in a quiet exile underground due to their Jedi connections, the Oliar have a tradition of Force-sensitive shamans who follow teachings known as the Flowing Path. They see the Force as embodied by the tides and currents of their world’s waters, with bioluminescent shrimp as manifestations of the light side and the various dangers in murkier waters as scepters of the dark. After first contact with the wider galaxy, many shamans became Jedi, but some stayed behind to continue their tradition. In more recent times, the Imperial Inquisitors have sought to destroy the Flowing Path, so a few shamans allowed themselves to be caught in order to satisfy them. The remainder have survived and are now in hiding, waiting while they are protected by their families.

csg_omwati.name: Omwati

special_abilities.name: Technical Skills
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Gearhead.”

csg_omwati.physiology: Omwati are thin humanoids distinguished by their light blue skin. Their thin face, which often gives off a youthful appearance, typically features blue eyes and a sharp chin. Instead of hair, they have feathery threads which sparkle and can appear iridescent. These threads naturally come in shades of orange, yellow, or white, but many Omwati dye them in other colors. They have a highly advanced brain which is extremely pliant during youth. If properly trained and encouraged, a young Omwati can become a brilliant scientist or engineer.
csg_omwati.society: Omwati are gifted with an excellent memory, which makes them intelligent and perceptive in most cases. It also gives them wisdom, as they apply lessons from the past. Additionally, they are gifted artistically, and they excel in music. They place very high value in their relationships with friends and family. Thanks to these traits, society on their homeworld was highly successful. Unified under a single government, they maintained peace while advancing technology and stewarding their resources.
csg_omwati.language: The Omwati speak Omwatese, a very musical language with a flowing written form. Tone is vital to the language, so they struggle with Basic.
csg_omwati.homeworld: Omwat is a world in the Southern part of the Outer Rim which features savannas, mountains, and cities which resemble honeycombs. It has no contact with the rest of the galaxy. Many Omwati live offworld on planets like Coruscant.
csg_omwati.description: Omwati are blue-skinned avians who are relatively thin but boast an incredible mind for engineering. Although some live as members of the civilized galaxy, their homeworld was kept isolated by Grand Moff Tarkin, who ruled it and recruited many Omwati as engineers.
csg_omwati.sidebar_text: Currently, a very small number of Omwati live in the larger galaxy, as their homeworld was lost from all records long ago. However, little do these Omwati know that their planet was rediscovered during the waning days of the Galactic Republic, which chose to keep it secret. Tarkin controlled the affair, and he gave them Republic technology to study. After more than a decade, Tarkin returned as a Grand Moff, and he had the power he needed to exploit the Omwati. Distracting them with diplomats who told them of the rest of the galaxy, Tarkin constructed an orbital education facility to conduct his operations. Once it was completed, he ordered the Omwati to give him hundreds of their most promising youth, who would be trained in modern engineering. For those who failed to develop as Tarkin hoped, they were executed and their home cities were destroyed. The ten who succeeded were taken offworld, like Qwi Xux, went on to help design the Death Star. With Tarkin dead, the Omwati are again isolated. However, around 15 ABY, they will reach the orbital facility, where they will discover hyperdrive technology. After making contact with the New Republic, many will attempt to find their kidnapped children. The Omwati from the rest of the galaxy will welcome their brethren.

csg_ongree.name: Ongree

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_ongree.physiology: Ongree are an amphibious species that many find odd because of a face that seems upside down. They have no hair, but their tall head has a wide, lipless, mouth near the top. Their eyes, resembling those of Mon Calamari, are on stalks near the bottom of their head that go off to the side. They have red irises and a triangular pupil. On their chin, they have small tentacles extending down. Their skin is yellow, orange, or red in most cases. They have just two wide fingers, but they can still manage decent dexterity with small objects. As humpbacks, they are somewhat awkward when walking on land.
csg_ongree.society: Ongree are a peaceful people known to be content with observation and study. They are often excellent judges of character, and many consider them to be an excellent source of wisdom or impartial judgment. They have a love for poetry and literature, but they prefer metaphors so complex that the significance and meaning in their art is usually lost on non-Ongree readers. They much prefer this role of observation and study rather than action. This restrained approach usually results in them being stereotyped as advocates of the middle ground, for they rarely show extreme devotion to any cause. Though some say that this ability to have multiple perspectives is a result of their spread-out eyes being able to see from multiple angles, this connection is coincidental.
csg_ongree.language: Because of their isolation, many Ongree only speak Ongreenen. However, it is impossible to speak outside of water, so some have learned Basic.
csg_ongree.homeworld: Ongree come from the ocean planet of Skustell, an Outer Rim world that has a history of neutral isolation. Not hostile to anyone, Skustell has become known as a safe pace among Imperials in a region that is otherwise teeming with rebels. Each city on Skustell is divided into “suruael” sections of above the water and “suouael” portions that are underwater. They also have an extensive population on the nearby ocean planet Qiqos, where many work as fishermen.
csg_ongree.description: Ongree are amphibians with eyes on the side of their head and a high mouth, which makes them look very odd. They are diplomatic and reserved, often preferring to carefully observe situations from all angles.
csg_ongree.sidebar_text: Though Ongree are known for having neutral, unexceptional viewpoints, their extreme open-mindedness can allow them to engage with a wide variety of viewpoints that other species would quickly dismiss. Many Ongree who meet cultists give them legitimate consideration, and after murmuring in indecision for too long, some end up falling sway to strange beliefs. Some of the notable instances involving Ongree cultists include a group that worshiped Revan on Nar Shaddaa during the Cold War and the infamous “777 Attendees,” the majority of whom were Ongree. (The cult used base eight, so this holy number is what most sentients would know as 511). All 511 members attempted to kill a deity named Shi’lak by committing one of the galaxy’s largest mass suicides. The cult is extinct, but the bizarre incident received so much media attention that Ongree are still known for it, and many expect them to be in awe if the numbers 511 or 777 come up in everyday business.
csg_ongree._provenance_note: The Ongree species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_opquis.name: Opquis

special_abilities.name: Extra Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Low-G Natives
special_abilities.description: May not move in a normal gravity environment without mechanical assistance. May spend 1,000 credits on a basic repulsorlift chair, allowing the character to move but only once per turn, or 2,000 credits on an advanced repulsorlift chair, allowing the character to move normally.

csg_opquis.physiology: The Opquis are bulky, neckless, egg-shaped creatures with six limbs, all of which end in three digits. Used to a low-gravity environment, their legs are no stronger than their four arms and cannot support their meter-high body in normal gravity. Thus, those offworld must move around on repulsor chairs. Their blue skin is smooth, hairless, and oily, and most do not wear clothing save for perhaps a vest. Their visage is dominated by a large mouth that they use to swallow their reptilian prey whole. They have wide, dark eyes, and their nostrils are widely spaced as well. Most uniquely, however, are their ears. Opquis have eight of them, four on each side of their head, which appear as tubes jutting out of it. Each pair of ears is dedicated to a specific frequency band, which allows them to listen to a wide range of ultrasonic sounds. The upper and lower sets of ears are processed in separate parts of the nervous system.
csg_opquis.society: While the Opquis’ appearance comes across to many as very friendly, they actually make for fairly dour and serious company. Most have little interest in casual conversation, staying focused on their work at hand or preferring solitude in their rare time off. They find other species’ mealtime customs particularly strange, as they gorge themselves notoriously quickly. Despite their physical and social limitations, Opquis are highly appreciated around many industries for their hardworking attitude and algorithmic problem-solving abilities. They are particularly prominent in software engineering professions, and many program droids that they personally find to make better company than living beings. While quiet, Opquis are not deceptive, and they have a particular distaste for criminals. Their own legal system is quite harsh, and many see the Rebel Alliance as troublesome, even though most have their quiet gripes about the Empire.
csg_opquis.language: Opquis language is made unique by their hearing. Since high-pitched and low-pitched sounds are processed in different areas of their brain, they get very confused when trying to parse speech that involves both, as it does when most humans casually speak Basic. While they can speak Basic in either all-high or all-low tones, they usually need a translator to hear it. They prefer to use either their deep language, Grudos or their squeaky language, Teesii. Most remarkably, an Opquis can listen without difficulty to one person speaking Grudos and another speaking Teesii at the same time.
csg_opquis.homeworld: The Opquis come from Opquili, a small, sun-baked world in the Thoran system of Bothan Space. Most other species find its low gravity to be awkward, so the population is almost all Opquis, who gather in high-rising cities well south of the equator, where the summer heat is a bit more manageable.
csg_opquis.description: A blue-skinned species adapted to low gravity, the Opquis’ legs aren’t strong enough to support their body in normal gravity, so they rarely travel. Those who do are known for their hard work, honesty, dour attitudes, and hatred of Bothans.
csg_opquis.sidebar_text: In many ways, the opposite of the aboveboard but cold Opquis are the sly, smooth-talking Bothans, who originate not far from them and colonized a planet in their system, Thoran, much to the chagrin of the Opquis. While Opquis are far less prominent in the galaxy than their canine neighbors, they nonetheless maintain something of a one-sided rivalry. Even their most stoic members will swear colorfully at the mere mention of Bothans. Most Opquis purport that a brutal pirate attack in 116 BBY was caused by Bothan spies selling their shield deactivation codes to the attackers.
csg_opquis._provenance_note: Little is known about the Opquis. This entire page is highly speculative and retcons Ellam to be a member. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they rewrite stats, imagining their own aspects of Opquis physiology and culture.

csg_orgon.name: Orgon

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Photoautotrophic
special_abilities.description: Do not require normal food, surviving only off of sunlight, Carbon Dioxide, and water for long periods of time.

special_abilities.name: Chemical Weapons
special_abilities.description: May spend 2 advantage on a successful Brawl check to apply poison. A target who has been poisoned must pass an average Resilience check or become Disoriented and Immobilized for the rest of the encounter. After being engaged with an Immobilized target for 2 rounds, may secrete digestive acid as maneuver, which deals 1 wound per round per application until it is cleaned off.

csg_orgon.physiology: Orgons are a unique species of sentient mobile plants who can actually be predatorial. They have radial symmetry, with six to eight tentacles sprouting from their circular body in all directions. The tentacles, which can be up to two meters long, have several key functions: They are used like legs for locomotion, but they can also be lifted upward to grasp objects like hands. The tentacles also contain venom and adhesives which can be used to restrain their prey, and once that is complete, they also contain a significant portion of the Orgon’s digestive tract. They can secrete digestive acids and absorb nutrients. However, if prey is scarce, Orgons can also resort to photoautotrophy. The bulk of their body is contained within a hard circular olive green or yellow shell that is about half a meter in diameter. While Orgons don’t have any visible eyes, they are capable of sight. Although its purpose is unknown, they also lay clusters of red goo which can rupture when bumped and cause skin irritation to humans.
csg_orgon.society: Orgons are patient and solitary creatures who will fiercely defend their hunting grounds from any rivals. Though primitive, they are still sentient, and they have annual swap meets to trade resources, labor, or land. However, they are cautious to the point of paranoia.
csg_orgon.language: Orgons have a sign language and can write but are physically incapable of speaking any verbal tongue.
csg_orgon.homeworld: A few Orgons can be found in the rural swamps of Shaum Hii, but they come from Gorsh, a wilderness planet in Wild Space far north of the galactic center. Due to high carbon dioxide, breath masks are helpful but not required for other species, and Gorsh also has high gravity. Its surface is dominated by oceans with a few swampy islands, and the climate is hot and humid. It is owned by a pharmaceutical company, Genetech Laboratories, which has found a number of valuable compounds produced by the unique flora and fauna. About 100,000 offworlders work in the system, although most of their operations occur in a crowded but well-equipped orbital facility.
csg_orgon.description: Multi-tentacled plants, the Orgon are not recognized as a sentient species by the offworlders who have stumbled into them, but they can collaborate and hunt together.
csg_orgon.sidebar_text: Genetech Laboratories has sought to capture a live Orgon but has yet to succeed, although about a decade ago, a group of Orgons was successfully able to ambush a Genetech ship as it landed. They killed the entire crew but were unable to actually fly the vehicle and abandoned it. However, unknown to everyone, a few of their spores were scattered about the ship and hitchhiked their way to Shaum Hii, where the young Orgons now interact with civilized Kian’thar.
csg_orgon._provenance_note: The Orgon species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_ortolan.name: Ortolan

special_abilities.name: Advanced Olfaction
special_abilities.description: When smelling for food, make difficulty equal to twice the distance in kilometers.

csg_ortolan.physiology: Ortolans are a chubby race slightly smaller than most humans. They have large, floppy ears and a long snout. While Ortolan skin may appear to be smooth and rubbery, it is actually covered in a thin layer of velvety fur. This fur is naturally blue, but many choose to dye it in other colors, like pink. (This actually started when they wanted a use for food dyes, since they view dying food as a waste of time.) Their hands have four chubby fingers that end in suction-cup like tips. Their thumbs are not opposable, giving them some difficulties when it comes to coordination and manipulating technology. Ortolans also have beady black eyes and a trunk that is well-adapted to eating and smelling. This smell can sense food from two kilometers away. Their large ears also give them an excellent sense of hearing, which can sense things in the subsonic range.
csg_ortolan.society: Ortolan society puts an emphasis on the family unit, as education is entirely the responsibility of the parents. Since this is sometimes impractical, gifted children are occasionally sent to other families. Though their lifespan is similar to a human one in length, they reach adulthood by seven and are then kicked out of the family. Ortolans barter for goods and do not have a system of money. They still understand the concept, however, and use credits to trade with offworlders. Ortolans are not warlike in nature and attempted neutrality in the Clone Wars. This did not last, however, when financial administrator Belo Tusus decided to place Orto in the allegiance of the Separatists. Though droids liberated the planet from Republic rule after a brief skirmish, war returned to Orto. The Jedi Knight Nem Bees sabotaged many Ortolan factories while undercover as an ordinary citizen. Bees and his clones then fought a long battle to take over the planet that only ended when the droid shutdown was issued.
csg_ortolan.language: Ortolans speak Ortolan, and most are fluent in Basic. Ortolan consists of grunts and hoots.
csg_ortolan.homeworld: Ortolans come from the frigid Outer Rim world of Orto and are under Imperial rule. The frozen wasteland is populated by cities and mines for radioactive fuels and heavy metals. While the growing season is short, they import plenty of food. Despite being technically under Imperial rule, the Empire mostly leaves it alone in exchange for its resources from mining.
csg_ortolan.description: Ortolans are chubby creatures with an amazing sense of smell, which they use to find food. Ortolans have fur which they often dye and are known for being obsessed with music, food, or both.
csg_ortolan.sidebar_text: Ortolans are known for two obsessions: music and food. In addition to consuming food with their mouths, they can also absorb it in their fingertips. While their chubby fingers and lack of opposable thumbs make them unsuitable for many musical instruments, they can still play one very well: the organ. While their sense of smell makes them excellent chefs as well (a bit on the perfectionist side) they sometimes take up unfavorable contracts when offworld, working hard and only being paid in food.

csg_ossan.name: Ossan

special_abilities.name: Thick Fat
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: High-Gravity Adaptations
special_abilities.description: After spending 3 months in a high-gravity environment, temporarily gain +1 Brawn. After spending 3 months in normal or lower gravity, redact this benefit.

csg_ossan.physiology: Ossans are a larger species of rodents who have a wide upper jaw forming a snout, and they have long, drooping ears. Their nose has a single nostril, and their eyes are dark. They have short legs and long arms, and they are typically very well-muscled. However, they are adapted to a high-gravity environment, and they lose much of their musculature after a few months in normal gravity. After that, they end up extremely chubby. Their fingers have slight claws, and they have a thin layer of fur over most of their body.
csg_ossan.society: Ossans have a cheerful attitude and tend to see all things from a ridiculously optimistic perspective, even to the point of delusion. In fact, they are rather dim-witted and tend to fall for cons, despite the fact that they see themselves as incredibly cunning. For example, they routinely fall prey to an animal called the cucul because it somewhat resembles a floating log. Although this prevents the Ossans from financial success, it does not prevent them from being happy: No matter their predicament, they always see themselves as perfectly capable of succeeding in it. On their homeworld, they are primitive, not even possessing bows and arrows, and their villages struggle to survive because of the Ossans’ general incompetence. Some Ossans manage to land good jobs offworld because of their strength, but once their muscle deteriorates, they are often left unemployed.
csg_ossan.language: Ossans typically speak their native language as well as Basic.
csg_ossan.homeworld: Ossans come from the primitive Outer Rim world of Ossel II. It has high gravity and is known for the resilient syp wood.
csg_ossan.description: Ossans are rodents who boast an impressive, muscular body, but this musculature turns to fat if they spend enough time in normal gravity. They are extremely unintelligent, being irrationally suspicious of good deals while accepting other bargains where they gain next to nothing.
csg_ossan.sidebar_text: Ossans may fancy themselves as masters of commerce, but that couldn’t be farther from the truth. They are so unreasonably suspicious that they will back out of many good deals, refusing to sell anything in exchange for credits and also frequently turning down reasonable offers of goods in exchange for other goods. However, they can also be oblivious to extremely one-sided deals. Oftentimes, they will sell their wood in exchange for being granted a tour of day on trading ships. Despite giving away both their goods and labor in exchange for next to nothing, Ossans nevertheless always think they got the better end of the deal. As such, Ossans encountered offworld are often indentured servants or willing slaves, and many have been taken to the Senex-Juvex sectors. However, their unintelligence means that they are often let go from their duties prematurely.

csg_paaerduag.name: Paaerduag

special_abilities.name: Multiple Heads
special_abilities.description: Must be attached to a smaller part Paaerduag character. The two can act as separate individuals in terms of personality, stats, actions, initiative order, and critical injuries. They share a wound threshold, which is the average of their two wound thresholds. They may communicate telepathically with each other.

csg_paaerduag.physiology: Paaerduags start off life as two distinct types of individuals: Some of smaller creatures with green skin and four eyes, others have yellowish skin and a hunchbacked posture. As they grow up, these two beings fuse together and form a single being, with the smaller part attached to the back of the larger. The larger part is responsible for movement, while the smaller being provides two extra sets of eyes, granting their combination omnidirectional vision. Each being has two-fingered hands, and the larger part has two-toed feet. Although they can think independently, the beings can coordinate telepathically with one another.
csg_paaerduag.society: Paaerduags are a haughty people who tend to keep to themselves, for the partner attached to them is often all the company they need. They take pride in their unique physiology, often boasting about the superiority of having two heads to other species. As such, they respect species of similar physiology, like Troigs, Yuvernians, and Cha’wen’he. Although they can be clever, they are vulnerable to overconfidence and tend to underestimate their adversaries.
csg_paaerduag.language: Paaerduags speak Brun’grraun, a language which uses the harmony between both beings. The larger part speaks in a voice that is too low for humans to hear, while the speech of the smaller part is audible to other species. The smaller part is biologically capable of speaking Basic, although they rarely learn it.
csg_paaerduag.homeworld: Paaerduags come from an Outer Rim planet which is referred to as Sorjus in Basic, although its true name is only pronounceable by them. Sorjus is a backwater planet that partakes in little trade.
csg_paaerduag.description: Paaerduags are a species where two separate beings, one large and one small, attach to one another during adolescence. The larger part is responsible for all motion, while the smaller part is the only one that can speak Basic.
csg_paaerduag.sidebar_text: Paaerduags are not born connected, so they have some choice in who they spend their lives attached to. This takes place at the young age of eight during the fall, during which the larger parts gather in a city center, and smaller parts climb atop the back of their preferred partner. If the larger part dislikes the potential partner, they may shake the smaller part off, thus beginning another round of searching. Those without a partner at the end die by the age of ten.
csg_paaerduag._provenance_note: The Paaerduag species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_pacithhip.name: Pacithhip

special_abilities.name: Thick Hides
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Omnidirectional Vision
special_abilities.description: May see in all directions, adding boost on visual Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Claws and Tusks
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds, and have a Crit rating of 3. May spend 2 advantage to add the Pierce 2 quality by hitting with tusks.

csg_pacithhip.physiology: Pacithhips are a species of pachyderms, a physiology shared with the Ortolans and the Cragmoloids. Similar to these species, they are slow and bulky. Despite their mass, they are stocky and much shorter than humans on average, because of their very stubby legs. They have eyes on either side of their head, optimized to give them 360 degree vision. They also have a trunk with a nostril and tusk on either side of it, and the tusks are sharp enough to use in combat. However, the tusks are also thin and elegant, providing them with an important aesthetic. Their gray skin can be mottled with varying shades of blue or yellow, and it is also very wrinkled. In addition to their arms and legs, they also have a long tail. They have a long neck, and the back of their head is protected by a thick ridge of bone.
csg_pacithhip.society: Pacithhips are a people who are quick to accept the status quo, and they are generally very passive. They almost never question authority, which makes them well-adapted to assimilate into many different cultures or become colonists. One way this manifests is that to better fit in in humanoid-dominated societies, many use stilts to give themselves more height and a longer stride, making them seem more humanoid. They greatly enjoy meeting people from very different species, and they are willing to accept a variety of unique customs. This makes them very skilled in social situations, and many excel as merchants or traders. While the Pacithhips have been travelling into the wider galaxy for some time, their homeworld of Shimia was only recently settled by Imperial-backed scouts, and the locals were defeated relatively easily by their technologically superior conquerors. Once the Empire is defeated, these Pacithhips will begin to reverse-engineer Imperial technology and emigrate offworld in larger numbers.
csg_pacithhip.language: Almost all Pacithhips learn Basic from an early age, which they speak without issue. They also still use their own language of Shimiese, which includes snorts and bellows and has a pictographic alphabet.
csg_pacithhip.homeworld: The Pacithhip homeworld of Shimia is somewhat primitive, relying mostly on fossil fuels and only recently using hyperdrive or repulsorlift technology brought by the Empire. It is an Outer Rim planet not far from the Corellian Run, and its terrain includes grasslands, mountains, and oceans.
csg_pacithhip.description: Pacithhips are pachyderms who are slow to accept change, although they maintain an outgoing demeanor. They are relatively primitive and were discovered only recently by the Empire, but many enjoy exploring the galaxy, and they make excellent merchants.
csg_pacithhip.sidebar_text: Pacithhips have a caste system which features three roles: the farmer, the warrior, and the scholar. The farmers are an all-encompassing group of manual laborers who have been expanded to include manufacturers as well as people who make food or textiles. Scholars include lawyers, politicians, engineers, and teachers. Warriors mostly act as police or soldiers. None of the three castes are seen as objectively better or of higher importance than the others. A Pacithhip’s caste is determined by tusk shape, which can only be determined once they are fully-grown adults. The tolerance of the Pacithhips allows for a great deal of flexibility in the caste system, especially in modern times. Although everyone on their homeworld is expected to somewhat comply with the role of their caste, those who cannot fit in are encouraged no matter what, even if their destiny is elsewhere.

csg_paigun.name: Paigun

special_abilities.name: Avid Theorists
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Researcher.”

special_abilities.name: Tough Hide
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

csg_paigun.physiology: Paiguns are a species of thin, toad-like sentients. They average just over two meters in height, with females typically taller than males. They have shriveled green skin which is thicker than that of most species, improving their durability. Their hairless head is tall and thin, and it has no visible ears or nostrils. They lack eyebrows and have small blue-gray eyes without pupils. Their lithe hands have just four fingers on each.
csg_paigun.society: One of the galaxy’s most logical species, Paiguns are experts in mathematics and engineering, although they tend to focus on the theoretical side. They apply this mentality to all aspects of their life, staying detached and emotionless whenever they can. They personally prefer nonviolence but usually have no issues with conflicts as long as someone else is doing the dirty work.
csg_paigun.language: The Paigun language is called Paigun, and it is rooted in mathematics with a script that resembles equations. It is extremely precise and logical, with little use of metaphor or even imagery. They can speak Basic, usually with the same preference for clear, unambiguous terminology.
csg_paigun.homeworld: Paigu is the Paigun homeworld, an urban planet in the Vorzyd Sector of the northeast Outer Rim. On it, they have built incredible skyscrapers that reach multiple kilometers high. The planet sees extremely frequent lightning storms, which the Paiguns are able to harness as a source of power. This crucial operation is managed by a group of engineers who are called “amptechs.”
csg_paigun.description: Paiguns are a very logical and mathematical species of tall toad-like creatures, literal and humorless in their speech. They excel at technological development, but outside of trading, they have little interest in engaging with the outside galaxy, whose people they generally look down upon.
csg_paigun.sidebar_text: While Paiguns aren’t exactly xenophobic, they possess a sort of arrogance and tend to look down on species who do not share their logical skills. This tends to sour their relations with other species, but few Paiguns have much desire to explore anyway. While they can usually understand the benefits of trading and doing business with the rest of the galaxy, they are perfectly fine doing so from a distance. Paigun adventurers are exceedingly rare, but they can occasionally be found offworld as scientists.

csg_pan_preneur.name: Pan-preneur

special_abilities.name: Performers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Smooth Talker.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn when on land.

csg_pan_preneur.physiology: Widely speculated to be distant relatives of the more well-known Mon Calamari, Pan-preneur are an amphibious race who have gills to breathe water as tadpoles and later develop lungs. They can be distinguished from Mon Cals by their skin tone, often in lighter shades of orange, and the females can be differentiated by their bluish spots. Also unlike the Mon Cals, their gills do not lose any effectiveness with age, enabling many to live their entire lives underwater. Just above these gills, their lime-colored eyes are large, widely-set, have dark pupils, and can see the ultraviolet spectrum, but they have red-green color blindness. Above the eyes, their hairless cranium is covered by several layers of bony ridges. Pan-preneur have four-fingered hands that have long fingers which end in suction-cups. Their legs end in large fins that are ill-adapted to walking on land, so most of them stick to the seas, where they farm a variety of underwater life forms for food. Some call them vegetarians as their food is generally stationary, although most biologists think a few of the species they eat should technically be classified as animals.
csg_pan_preneur.society: Pan-preneur are hardworking but highly social creatures, living in large schools that distribute food, property, and work, including the care of children, amongst their members. In modern times, schools have grown in size, often having thousands of members, but they still operate on principles of direct democracy, where every member of at least 32 local years (21.5 standard years) has a vote in every single group decision. They live and work in large underwater complexes with very few interior walls, as they have little desire or respect for privacy. This trait combined with their limitations on land makes it very difficult for them to adapt to life in the wider galaxy, where they can be nosy, gossipy and overbearing.
csg_pan_preneur.language: Pan-preneur speak Ort-ineur or Poli Opilian, both of which are polysynthetic languages with base eight counting. Neither of their tongues can be properly pronounced out of the water, so Basic and Mon Calamarian are common second languages.
csg_pan_preneur.homeworld: The Pan-preneur homeworld of Sonn Vilmari is a chilly water world just a dozen parsecs above the end of the Perlemian Trade Route.
