The Pan-preneur live almost entirely underwater, but a sizable population of offworlders, including many Mon Calamari, inhabit burgeoning floating cities. The offworlders’ fishing industries make the planet a major food supplier for the Colundra sector, and a few schools of Pan-preneur are starting to get involved in the trade.
csg_pan_preneur.description: Pan-preneur live in tightly-knit communities, and they work diligently when their schools aren’t taking holidays to devote to grand orchestral performances. As distant relatives to the Mon Calamari, they are adept in the water, but their finned feet are ill-adapted to walking on land.
csg_pan_preneur.sidebar_text: Pan-preneur are a very musical people, with entire schools traditionally taking one day out of every eight off work to host parties called Raukii-Fol centered around orchestra, choir, and ballet performances. It is very rare for any to have an entire career as a professional musician, but all are expected to chip in and be involved in these events. Twice per local year, there are even more elaborate celebrations where multiple schools join together. Increasingly, these have been dominated by anti-Imperial messaging.
csg_pan_preneur._provenance_note: Little is known about the Pan-preneur. The following information is almost entirely made up. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they imagine their own aspects of Pan-preneur physiology and culture, rewriting stats accordingly.

csg_pantoran.name: Pantoran

special_abilities.name: Cold Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_pantoran.physiology: Pantorans are blue-skinned near-humans with yellow eyes. Their hair is black, blue, lavender, or silver. They are resistant to low temperatures as well, only needing light clothing in frigid climates.
csg_pantoran.society: Pantorans are from a region of space that is infested with slavers, spice merchants, crime lords, and other shady characters. More reputable in nature, they have developed a proud tradition and are fiercely independent. Pantorans tend to be determined, prideful, and eager to demonstrate their skills. Though teamwork is not their strong suit, they are still excellent in roles like leadership and, for some, manipulation with their charms. Pantoran nation states are organized into a democracy, and politics are considered to be an art form. Ruled by the Pantoran Assembly, most of the power is given to the Speaker. The Chairman is second-in-command, checking the Speaker’s powers. Under Imperial rule, Pantora has now been cut off from the rest of the galaxy. Three main groups suggest solutions to this predicament. The Appeasers believe that joining the Empire is the only option and the best one. They point out economics as the biggest benefit. The Republicans favor independence, citing the atrocities of the Empire and its opposition to Pantora’s core values. The Expansionists are small in number, and the most oppressed. They favor banding with the nearby spice dealers and slavers.
csg_pantoran.language: The language of Pantoran has so many dialects by region, so it is fairly impractical. Most Pantorans know Basic, and many also know Huttese.
csg_pantoran.homeworld: Pantorans come from Pantora, an Outer Rim world of marshes and plains. It is very cut off from the rest of the galaxy but still technologically advanced. The nearby moon of Orto Plutonia has been viewed as a good resource to many Pantorans, but a treaty with Talz colonists during the Clone Wars has prevented Pantoran interference on it. Some Pantorans, however, seek to open trade with Orto Plutonia and intermix the two cultures.
csg_pantoran.description: Pantorans are near-humans with blue skin and yellow eyes who are adapted to the cold. They are typically proud and independent; most Pantorans are eager to demonstrate their skills. They are not great as team players, but they are excellent leaders.
csg_pantoran.sidebar_text: Though Pantorans, like most species in the modern galaxy, are democratic, they still have their feudal traditions. They use yellow markings on their foreheads and cheeks to symbolize lineage. This is mostly because of a cultural interest in genealogy, lineage, and history. Other Pantorans treasure different relics, like art or jewelry from their ancestors.

csg_parwan.name: Parwan

special_abilities.name: Electric
special_abilities.description: After hitting with a successful Brawl check, may shock an opponent, dealing 5 strain. The shock attack ignores soak. (Note that the Brawl attack itself does not.)

special_abilities.name: Gasbags
special_abilities.description: Float, ignoring movement penalties for terrain, and may move upwards as well. Do not suffer fall damage. May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_parwan.physiology: Parwans are lightweight gasbags with thin, tentacle-like limbs. Their skin varies in color, from orangish-brown to a blue-gray. They have four tentacles that act as legs, extending from their thin waist. They use these for propulsion and tethering as they float through the air. Their upper two tentacles start at the shoulder, and these long, thin appendages act as arms. Their arms have three fingers each and are nimble enough to grasp technology like blasters excellently. However, most Parwans who fight use a much different weapon: electricity. Parwans are electrically charged, so merely touching adversaries can shock them enough to subdue. A Parwan head is thin, and, instead of hair, it has a mushroom-like top. They have three eyes, but the arrangement of their face is otherwise quite humanoid.
csg_parwan.society: Parwans place value in emotion and expression, viewing it important to have and share their feelings. For this reason, they live in a tightly-knit family that sticks together for life. Since sharing negative feelings can have negative effects for everyone, they tend to lean on the optimistic side. They tend to work well in teams or groups and interact with people closely, often sharing their feelings but expecting the same from others. This nature makes many of them find interest in art, music, or literature.
csg_parwan.language: Parwans can speak Basic as well as their own language, Gu’waru, which sounds like gibberish to most outsiders.
csg_parwan.homeworld: Parwa is a gas giant, where the Parwans first began to float around. They are herbivores, floating around and feeding on colonies of photosynthetic, floating plants. It has a few cities, which float via repulsorlift. The Empire doesn’t allow most Parwans offworld, but doesn’t bother to control much of the planet.
csg_parwan.description: Electric gasbags with tentacles, the Parwans are so light that they can float on the air. Their electrically charged bodies give them a powerful combative ability, as they can shock enemies into submission.
csg_parwan.sidebar_text: Their natural weapons and unique movement makes many Parwans naturally fit for the profession of bounty hunting. They are also hunted, however. Many Parwans tend to like art and literature to the point of stealing, so they have a reputation for being untrustworthy, and this makes it a good business to hunt and kill the thieves. Some are even killed “preemptively.” Many Parwans will claim that their obsession with arts is so great that they literally cannot resist stealing and barely have a choice in the matter.
csg_parwan._provenance_note: The Parwan species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_patrolian.name: Patrolian

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove penalties for underwater movement. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Electric Resistance
special_abilities.description: Reduce damage from electric shocks by 2.

csg_patrolian.physiology: Patrolians are small aquatic creatures. Their skin is mottled with dots, slippery in texture, and lavender or pink for one race, while yellow or lime for the other. They are hairless, although they have frills at the back of their head and lining the underside of their jaw. These frills actually serve as their auditory organs, as they otherwise have no visible ears. Their eyes are red with black pupils and slight eyestalks. They also lack visible nostrils, and their nose instead transitions straight to the mouth, which is low on their face, very close to the chin. They have lanky limbs save for fins on their wrists to help them swim, and they are also more resistant than other species to electric shocks.
csg_patrolian.society: Patrolians have strong values in teamwork and being social, even though they have no families. They instead travel together in large schools that contain hundreds of members. Politically, their people are subordinate to a group of human colonists, who have slowly developed a complex tax code that charges the Patrolians higher rates, imposing penalties for large social structures and particular crops they farm underwater. While some Patrolians have sought to radically overturn their social structures in order to regain economic advantage, others have emphasized crime as a way to retaliate. To this, the colonists have responded with harsher rules, building up a growing tension as some entire schools are now forced into outright Imperial slavery. Many Patrolians now head offworld, though they often retain their criminal ways.
csg_patrolian.language: Patrolians are practical, speaking Basic in a gurgled tone. They have abandoned their native language.
csg_patrolian.homeworld: Patrolia is a primarily ocean planet, with about a tenth of the surface covered by jungle islands. It is in the far west edge of the southern Inner Rim and known economically for its fishing, mining, and underwater farming. Human colonists dominate the planet politically and make up about half of the population.
csg_patrolian.description: Patrolians are small amphibians who seem to be involved in crimes whenever they are seen off their homeworld. They have skin that is either lavender and pink or lime and yellow. They are also a species that places high value in teamwork.
csg_patrolian.sidebar_text: The subunit of the Patrolian school is the squad. Being born in mass hatcheries, they have no knowledge or interest in their immediate families, they do organize into squads that function somewhat similarly. The exact nature of a squad depends on the particular school, but they tend to consist of five to ten individuals who share a profession. Patrolians are sorted into them from birth based on genetic analysis, but some schools do allow for them to change based on certain assessments and the votes of their squadmates. Ordinarily, though, they stick together: Their squads act as families in most regards, sharing property and also providing a highly specialized education to young members. When offworld, they tend to form new “squads” as well, seeking to become close friends with other people of their profession.
csg_patrolian._provenance_note: The Patrolian species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_pauan.name: Pau’an

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness.

csg_pauan.physiology: Pau’ans are tall, gray-skinned humanoids. At two meters, they are still similar enough to humans to be humanoid. They have no hair, and their skin is gray. As carnivores, they have jagged incisors to chew meat. They prefer it raw. Augmenting their intimidating appearance, their eyes are black, sunken into red eye sockets. Their skin has vertical lines and wrinkles from a lack of sunlight. The lighting conditions also give them excellent vision in darkness. They live up to 700 years, so they are nicknamed the “Ancients.” Despite their great height, they are thin, making them relatively weak.
csg_pauan.society: Pau’ans naturally prefer leadership and government roles. Many first begin working with managing small teams of laborers before they move up. They are empathetic as leaders, understanding and respecting the desires, perspectives, and needs of their subordinates. This allows success in which each city is controlled by a single Master of Port Administration, a hereditary title. The Administrators are advised by several other councils. Each Administrator additionally serves on the Utapauan Committee, which is the planetary government. However, the cities are mostly autonomous, and the Committee rarely makes major decisions. Pau’an society varies greatly by city. Most tend to like art, something that shows in their unique architecture. They also prefer to use elaborate clothing to impress and demonstrate status. They are currently under the control of the Empire, which has not cared about the Pau’ans. Utapau is having its resources harvested, and some Pau’ans are now taken as slaves.
csg_pauan.language: Utapese is the Pau’an language. They tend to speak Basic as well. The Utai have their own language, which some Pau’ans also know.
csg_pauan.homeworld: The site of the final battle in the Clone Wars, Utapau is a minor Outer Rim world covered in rocky sinkholes. The surface is very windy, so both species are forced to live in the sinkholes. 95% of the planet is powered by wind. Native animals are useful for many roles, so airspeeders and other means of transit are replaced by the lizard-like varactyls who can climb walls and the flying dactillions.
csg_pauan.description: Natural leaders with a long lifespan, the Pau'ans are intimidating thanks to their gray face. They only eat raw meat, which some other species find unnerving, but despite this, they get along well and are typically liked by those who they lead.
csg_pauan.sidebar_text: Pau’ans share their homeworld with the Utai. The two are thought to be distant relatives. They co-exist peacefully, and they complement each other well. This first began thanks to Timon Medon, a Pau’an leader who first experimented in merging the species. Just as the Pau’ans have a strong preference for leadership, the Utai typically prefer simple, menial labor. They get along well because of this. More common conflicts are the ones between cities, which tend to result in societal and economic rivalries or embargos rather than outright bloodshed. Each city has great pride in their unique culture.

csg_palowick.name: Pa’lowick

special_abilities.name: Tusks
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_palowick.physiology: Pa’lowick are aquatic creatures with long limbs. They are somewhat scrawny but boast some of the best lungs in the galaxy. These lungs are contained in a chubby torso, which transitions to the head in a neckless blob. Their head contains eyestalks that surround a long proboscis, which eventually ends in human-like lips. The younger ones have tusks in a second, lower mouth as well. Their skin is yellow mottled with green-blue spots. Their limbs end in four fingers or toes, each with an opposable thumb or backwards toe. While humanoid in size, an air-filled bladder makes them very light.
csg_palowick.society: Pa’lowick have a simple society, and most are content to keep it that way. They are shy, patient, and have many proud traditions. These are very important to them, and, while they are respectful to outsiders, they always uphold their own ways. Their government is feudal, and communities are large but independent of one another. They rarely travel offworld, and most prefer the simplistic life of a farmer, fisherman, hunter, or storyteller. Storytellers are very important to Pa’lowick and hold a high place within society. Most of their knowledge and history is stored orally through the storytellers.
csg_palowick.language: The impressive vocals of Pa’lowick can speak Basic just fine. (Loudly at that) They also have their own language, Lowickese.
csg_palowick.homeworld: Pa’lowick come from the marshy planet of Lowick, which is also filled with rainforests. It is notable for isolation, staying unaligned in galactic affairs. It is also a relatively recent addition to the galactic community, still just a few centuries in.
csg_palowick.description: Powerful lungs help the Pa'lowicks to dive deep underwater, but they also help to sing. They are notable for putting high value in music. Though some travel the stars, many live much more simple lives as fishermen or farmers.
csg_palowick.sidebar_text: Few things define the Pa’lowick better than their love for song. Even their first major appearance on the galactic scale was through singer Larisselle Chatruni. Their biology makes them well-equipped for it, but even those who are not skilled nevertheless enjoy singing. Music and storytelling is seen as the pinnacle of entertainment. However, it also isn’t just for entertainment: Music is also very sacred, and singing is a vital rite of passage. Those that struggle with music find themselves outcasts in Pa’lowick society. For many others, music provides a way offworld and an eventual career, where they have more opportunities than they could ever dream of on their isolated homeworld.

csg_phindian.name: Phindian

special_abilities.name: Tinkerers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Gearhead.”

csg_phindian.physiology: Phindians are brown-skinned beings who are a touch shorter than humans. They are thin, and they have very flexible arms which are long enough to reach down to their knees. Their eyes, yellowish in color, are generally surrounded with white splotches. Some Phindians have these white spots all over their body. Their wrinkled head is hairless, and they have a large nose and a snout. They have four-fingered hands, and their feet have 3 claw-like toes. They generally prefer simple clothing with little decoration.
csg_phindian.society: Phindians typically get along very well with their family and close friends, coming across as affectionate and emotional. However, they are less friendly with strangers, distant friends, or business associates. Though highly perceptive, they typically come off as aloof in these circumstances because they are so unwilling to speak, and interacting with them can be exasperating. They are grumpy and irritable, frequently sarcastic and far too fond of hyperbole. Ultimately, these traits stem from their near-universal desire to focus on technology rather than other people. They greatly enjoy tinkering, and many of them would much rather talk to an obedient droid than have to deal with a fellow sentient. As such, many Phindians found offworld are technicians or engineers.
csg_phindian.language: Phindians generally speak both Phindian and Basic with a soft, raspy voice. Phindian has very long groups of vowels and sounds very soft.
csg_phindian.homeworld: Phindians come from the technologically advanced Outer Rim planet of Phindar, which is temperate and mostly urban.
csg_phindian.description: Phindians are shorter beings with brown skin, yellow eyes, and a snout. They are only amiable around family and close friends, and they are very closed off around anyone else. Given their mechanical skills, most of them prefer interactions with droids as opposed to organics.
csg_phindian.sidebar_text: One of the most unique inventions of the Phindians is a device which is capable of erasing memories, and this device made its owner, the Syndicat, incredibly powerful. The Syndicat was a criminal organization, and it used control over resources as leverage against the Phindian people. Oftentimes, they would erase the memories of their enemies and then exile them. However, the Syndicat did not last forever, and it was overthrown during a democratic revolution more than 30 years ago, which began with help from the Jedi. The new government, which supported the Separatists during the Clone Wars, ended after the takeover of the Empire, but democracy will return to the Phindians shortly after the Battle of Endor, and they will end up joining the New Republic a year after their liberation.

csg_pho_pheahian.name: Pho Ph’eahian

special_abilities.name: Thermal Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.” Add boost on checks to climb.

csg_pho_pheahian.physiology: The Pho Ph’eahians are a species of rodents who are similar to the Chadra-Fan with their bat-like face, which has large ears, a black nose, and small eyes. However, they are distinguished by being larger, and their fur is blue-gray rather than brown to provide better camouflage. Most notably, they have four arms, and these extra limbs are particularly advantageous in helping them to climb.
csg_pho_pheahian.society: Pho Ph’eahians are amiable and outgoing, not unlike the Chadra-Fan they resemble. They enjoy getting fame or attention and generally do their best to make friends. They are best known for their technical skills, and their society already possessed a great deal of technology such as nuclear power, sublight space travel, and repulsorlifts when the rest of the galaxy made contact with them. After reverse-engineering the hyperdrive, they joined the greater galactic community to do engineering of all sorts. Their technical skills travel well, making them a common sight on many worlds.
csg_pho_pheahian.language: The Pho Ph’eahians have created a language known as Pho Ph’eahese, which is considered to be very sophisticated. Every spoken syllable, typically a squeak or bark of some sort, translates to a single written character, and their voice is very high-pitched if they speak Basic.
csg_pho_pheahian.homeworld: The adaptations of the Pho Ph’eahians toward cold, mountainous environments are, of course, reflections of their homeworld’s terrain. They are native to the mountainous regions on Pho Ph’eah, a frigid Outer Rim planet. Pho Ph’eah has a very elliptical orbit, so it warms up briefly before going through a long season of darkness. Although Pho Ph’eahians have travelled to many planets throughout the galaxy, they are most prominent in regions close to their homeworld, such as the Corporate Sector.
csg_pho_pheahian.description: Mechanically inclined rodents with four limbs who are distantly related to the Chadra-Fan, the Pho Ph'eahians share their relatives' outgoing spirit. However, they are distinguished by their obsession with hygiene.
csg_pho_pheahian.sidebar_text: Pho Ph’eahians are extremely superstitious when it comes to staying clean, mostly because they try to be the center of attention. Pho Ph’eahians believe in a strong connection between their physical body and their soul, considering the body to be a “sacred manifestation of the spirit.” As such, they fear that any dirt, wound, or stain on them could transfer over to the soul. They consider anything related to hygiene or cleaning to be extremely important.

csg_phuii.name: Phuii

special_abilities.name: Gifted Racers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Shortcut.”

csg_phuii.physiology: Phuii are a rather dexterous saurian species that has a lean body and a long neck. Although they can be as tall as humans, many are significantly shorter, some being only one meter tall. Their legs have a knee that bends backwards, and they move around by hopping around on their three-toed feet. Although some also have three fingers on their hands, others have four digits. They show similar sorts of diversity in that some have a tail while others do not, and they also have varying skin colors in light green, yellow, and gray. Some have a single skin color, while others have a significantly lighter color on their chest and on the front of their face. Their face features a duck-like beak that they sometimes use to peck in a brawl, and they have red, orange, or yellow eyes on the sides of their head. Even young Phuii have wrinkles on their skin, especially their neck, and they also have a lumpy crest at the top of their head.
csg_phuii.society: Phuii are best known for their love of sports and gaming, industries which most of them work in on their homeworld. Fitting with their competitiveness, they tend to be overconfident and arrogant, often focusing on threats and intimidation when they interact with others. Because of this lack of tact, they tend to be more practical instead of being focused on their appearance, often choosing to wear simple attire like coveralls.
csg_phuii.language: Given their relatively frequent interactions with the rest of the galaxy, Phuii generally speak lingua francas like Basic or Huttese in favor of any native language.
csg_phuii.homeworld: The Phuii homeworld, Phu, is known for its gaming and sports industries. It is relatively small in population, is of very little consequence politically, and was neutral during the Clone Wars. However, it is in the Colonies, has technology up to the galactic standard, and has been a part of the greater galaxy for millenia.
csg_phuii.description: The Phuii are shorter but nimble saurians, and they are known for their love of sports and games. They are extremely competitive and can be arrogant, so they are not always well-liked, but they can make excellent Podracers.
csg_phuii.sidebar_text: One of the most popular sports among the Phuii is Podracing, a sport where they have earned notoriety thanks to famed Phuii Podracers such as Mars Guo and Chros-filik. Many Phuii take up Podracing as a hobby or as professionals, and Phuii who leave their homeworld are very likely doing so because of Podracing or another sport.

csg_phydolon.name: Phydolon

special_abilities.name: Symbiotic Resilience
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound.

special_abilities.name: Symbiotic Isolation
special_abilities.description: When healing strain at the end of an encounter, heal 1 fewer strain if no other Phydolons are present.

csg_phydolon.physiology: Phydolons are actually a symbiote of two other non-sentient species that have coevolved: humanoids known as the Agarans and a rhizome known as the Orucytes. Their overall body structure is that of the mammalian Agaran, but most of their tissues are made of the Orucyte fungus. Their consciousness is shared between the two organisms, and neither species can achieve sentience on its own. In some ways, they act as a single mind, but at times, they act more like a pair of distinct individuals. Their fungal tissue has a white or pink color, while their body structure is very long and lean. They also have long limbs and fingers. They have draping tendrils of flesh instead of hair, and their large, black eyes are near the top of their flat face and spread out near the sides of their head. They have a small mouth and no nose.
csg_phydolon.society: Phydolons are a quaint people who live together in very closely-knit groups, and they are very provincial. Their social order is informal, but they are generally ruled by the wisest among their people. Their unique biology grants them a sort of gestalt consciousness with the other Phylodons, allowing them to convey emotions, even without words, via their shared connection to the Orucytes. They also have a very strong sense of community and belonging, so they selflessly contribute to the needs of the group. The fungal part of their biology, which is the more social part, feels very isolated if they ever leave their own people, so they rarely leave their homeworld. Privacy is not a concern for them, so their homes are often without walls or doors.
csg_phydolon.language: Because of their innate empathy, Phydolons have little need for a complex language, and their tongue is very simple. They typically dislike Basic, as they find it to be unnecessarily complicated.
csg_phydolon.homeworld: A backwater planet in the Outer Rim, Mydasos is a lush planet that is home to the Phydolons. Its terrain includes swamps, small seas, vast forests, and jagged mountain ranges. It was discovered relatively recently, within the past century.
csg_phydolon.description: In an incredible biological phenomenon, the Phydolons are the combination of two separate species, one mammalian and the other fungal. Coming from a backwater world, they are deeply spiritual and incredibly reliant on their community.
csg_phydolon.sidebar_text: Phydolons are deeply spiritual, almost monastic, and they are more likely to be Force-sensitive than other species. They have a very strong connection to the Living Force because of their superb empathy and deep connections to those around them. Force-sensitive Phydolons see the Living Force as very welcoming and familiar, using it as a source of interconnectivity and understanding. Using it for power is unheard of to them.
csg_phydolon._provenance_note: The Phydolon species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU.

csg_polis_massan.name: Polis Massan

special_abilities.name: No Vocal Cords
special_abilities.description: Cannot speak.

special_abilities.name: Telepathy
special_abilities.description: May communicate by telepathically “broadcasting” simple thoughts and feelings to all beings within short range. May also “whisper,” broadcasting only to those who are engaged.

csg_polis_massan.physiology: Polis Massans, also known as Kallidahins, are short and thin. They have a long neck, and growth rings cover their smooth, gray skin which seems to have come from an aquatic ancestry. Their face is flat, with the only features being emotionless black or red eyes. It is also covered by a smooth osmotic membrane, which absorbs their nutrients. They have four-fingered hands. What makes Polis Massan most unique is their telepathy. Only a few rare members, known as Speakers, have vocal cords. All can communicate telepathically, making their words heard in a broadcast manner.
csg_polis_massan.society: Polis Massans are kind and extremely respectful of life, which they value in all forms, as they possess a great curiosity about biology. They are not aggressive, avoiding direct confrontation, and they keep quiet about their society to avoid unwanted attention from pirates and other criminals. They are gifted in intellectual fields, like medicine and archaeology, and they tend to be good workers, enjoying the job that they choose and finding fulfillment in it. They are also a very communal people, focusing on the good of their society instead of individual goals.
csg_polis_massan.language: Polis Massans have their language of Massan, which requires hand signs as well as audio that is created via telepathy or vocal cords.
csg_polis_massan.homeworld: Though no records of it exist, the Kallidahins originate from Kallidah, hence their original name. After entirely moving to Polis Massa, they have become known as Polis Massans. The planet itself is gone, but the largest of the remaining asteroids has taken up the name “Polis Massa.” These asteroids are well-settled by the Polis Massans, and many are the site of archaeological digs.
csg_polis_massan.description: The Polis Massans are a species that has devoted themselves to discovering their long-lost ancestors in the Polis Massa asteroid field. Most cannot speak, but they are all capable of telepathic broadcasting.
csg_polis_massan.sidebar_text: Polis Massans have a great curiosity towards other species, and many devote their life to researching others. Given their lack of diplomatic skill, they do this at a distance. This is best demonstrated by their desire to research the extinct species called the Eellayin, who were the original inhabitants of Polis Massa before it was destroyed. The Polis Massans purport the Eellayin to be their ancestors, and since they have uncovered a significant amount of genetic material, many now wish to clone one. Despite the high quality of Polis Massan cloning facilities, the material was too incomplete to successfully clone an Eellayin on their initial attempts. Recently, they have asked for help from the Kaminoans, a species of expert cloners. With help from their specialists, the teams continue to make progress. Most Polis Massans work for this massive operation that requires cloners, spelunkers, archaeologists, and miners.

csg_priapulin.name: Priapulin

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 3 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.” Have 2 hooked limbs, 2 spatulate limbs, and 2 thorny limbs. May not perform complex manipulation such as using ranged weapons with spatulate or thorny limbs.

special_abilities.name: Thorny Limbs
special_abilities.description: When using thorny limbs, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_priapulin.physiology: Priapulin are gastropods, a group of sluggish creatures with no skeleton who move around by slithering. They are four meters long on average, and they typically have about half of their length flat on their ground. They have five notochords on their back, each of which is visible as a circular bump. They are orange in color and have darker red spots on their back. Separating their stomach from their back are a number of thin, hair-like cilia, appendages which can extend up to their chin. They have no facial hair, but their face features three sets of prominent eyebrows, each of which has two purple eyes below it. They also have no nose. On the sides of their body are multiple limbs. The uppermost of these limbs end in thorny balls for combat, the middle set has hooks for grasping, and the last two are flat to help with moving. They have additional limbs below their main six which are smaller. The Priapulin are also an aquatic species, and they can swim well and breathe underwater.
csg_priapulin.society: Priapulin are a very peaceful race; they have gone centuries without war and avoided the many controversies of galactic politics. They follow an extremely rigid code of honor which emphasizes loyalty. Priapulin are also known for their sense of humor. Although they typically stay on their homeworld, the Priapulin can be very good pilots.
csg_priapulin.language: Priapulin speak Pria, a language which non-Priapulin have a very hard time pronouncing. They can speak Basic in a whisper, although they have a few unique measurement conventions: They measure time in 10 hour “tides,” and measure distance in “salt pans” which are just longer than a kilometer.
csg_priapulin.homeworld: Priapulin rule the water world of Priap, a planet which is in the Arrowhead of the Core Worlds. It is home to multiple sentient aquatic species, all of whom interact peacefully with each other.
csg_priapulin.description: A species of aquatic gastropods, the Priapulin have a peaceful rule over their planet of Priap. They move by slithering their snake-like body, leaving their six limbs available for grasping objects.
csg_priapulin.sidebar_text: Despite their apparent kindness and pacifism, there is a dark symbiosis that sustains the Priapulin. It involves the Crast, a sentient species of crustacean that the Priapulin refer to as the food-kin. The Priapulin eat the Crast, who willingly sacrifice themselves. This is because the eggs of the Crast can only be properly incubated inside the stomach of a Priapulin. Once hatched, the Priapulin raise the Crast children as their own. The Priapulin are at the top of their planet’s food chain, and they collaborate symbiotically with a number of the sentient species on their planet.

csg_psadan.name: Psadan

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Obstinate
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 2.

csg_psadan.physiology: Psadans are large creatures with very high shoulders and a wide torso, but their arms and legs are stubby, thus limiting their speed and dexterity and making them somewhat shorter than humans on average. Their tan-gray skin is thick and leathery, providing them with excellent protection. They are particularly well-defended from behind, where they have rock-solid plates for their skin. They have two-toed feet and four-fingered hands. Their scalp is bald, but some have brown hair on their chin and below their red eyes. Their small nose sits directly between their eyes, and they have a wide mouth. Their simpler brain is quite resistant to telepathic Force Powers.
csg_psadan.society: The simplistic nature of the Psadan brain has made them extremely stubborn, and they are also very eager to solve problems by fighting. Psadans partake in various forms of nature worship, and one of the more notable tenets that they follow is never wasting anything. Psadans are almost all hunters, and they neve let any part of their prey go to waste. Most Psadans wear various bones and sections of skin, which can be used as armor or simply act as a decorative trophy.
csg_psadan.language: Psadans speak Psadan, a language with grunts and groans. They typically have a deep voice, and many Myneyrshi learn the Psadan language as well.
csg_psadan.homeworld: Psadans come from Wayland, an obscure arboreal planet in the Outer Rim. It is mostly wilderness, and it has little contact with the rest of the galaxy. The Imperials have a base at Mount Tantiss, where slaves of both species work to build a storehouse for the Empire. This storehouse will be protected by the Guardian, who will be succeeded by Joruus C’baoth.
csg_psadan.description: Primitive hunters, the Psadans have a combination of bulk and simple stubbornness that aids them in combat. They have a long-standing conflict with the Myneyrshi, who also inhabit their homeworld of Wayland.
csg_psadan.sidebar_text: Given their warlike tendencies and stubbornness, it is no surprise that the Psadans have not gotten along well with the Myneyrshi, the other sentient species found on their homeworld. However, that changed when the Empire came to Wayland, and they attempted to enslave both species. The Psadans and Myneyrshi were united by their common enemy, but their attempts to fight off the Empire were unsuccessful, and many Psadans were forced to work carving the Empire’s secret base in Mount Tantiss. Ultimately, the Psadans will be left alone in 9 ABY when Palpatine’s base is destroyed, although their population will be threatened again by the Yuuzhan Vong, as most of them are too stubborn to evacuate their homeworld.

csg_pulra.name: Pulra

special_abilities.name: Binding
special_abilities.description: May attach to other Pulras as a maneuver, communicating telepathically with them so long as they remain attached. Automatically provide and receive skilled assistance. If providing unskilled assistance, grant 2 boosts instead of 1. May attach to willing members of other species, temporarily losing autonomy and morphing into an organ or limb.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

special_abilities.name: Shape-shifting
special_abilities.description: May shape-shift as an easy Discipline check, changing shape and general proportions or gaining up to 2 arms. May also increase the difficulty by 1, and for every increase, may choose 1 of the following benefits upon success. At the end of each encounter, must reroll the Discipline check or remove Amorphic Benefits and revert to a limbless blob.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 1
special_abilities.description: Negate the Ponderous ability.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 2
special_abilities.description: Form more than 2 arms, gaining the ability to have 3 times as much gear in their hands and not needing to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 3
special_abilities.description: Reshape 1 limb into a simple tool such as a dagger, backpack, or lock pick. May not form items larger than 3 encumbrance or items involving technology such as a blaster or datapad.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 4
special_abilities.description: Change colors, adding 2 boosts on Stealth checks.

special_abilities.name: Sonar
special_abilities.description: May sense using sonar, negating the effects of the Blind ability in most cases and gaining further benefits when applicable.

csg_pulra.physiology: Pulras are omnivores with a unique, highly variable physiology. They can range from being a few centimeters long to being more massive than humans, and they can shape-shift to change their form. They generally appear as a roughly cylindrical blob, but they can add limbs, and their skin can change color in shades between black, brown, and green. They cannot change size, but there is otherwise no real limit to what shape their limbs and body can take, making them highly adaptable. They also lack conventional senses, but they make up for it with a form of sonar. Finally, Pulras are capable of binding with one another and forming colonies. They typically are seen in this form, and they act like cells in this bigger organism. They reproduce by fission, which occurs without conscious intent so long as they have sufficient resources. Pulras in a colony also share a combined set of skills, knowledge, and goals. They can also bind with other species, but in these cases, they tend to lose their autonomy, becoming simple limbs or organs in service of their host.
csg_pulra.society: Pulras live in colonies with dozens or hundreds of members, and they are highly cooperative, although they can sometimes have disputes with other colonies. Such conflicts, handled collectively, can be extremely bloody. In general, Pulras prefer to interact with groups, as that is the form more familiar to them.
csg_pulra.language: It is unknown if Pulras can speak Basic, but they can communicate telepathically with their colony.
csg_pulra.homeworld: Pulras come from the backwater Outer Rim planet of Kuras III, which they call “Host.” It is highly dangerous to other species due to its combination of volcanic activity, atmospheric toxins, and dangerous bacteria. Pulras rarely want to leave, but those who do must get past the Kuras Drift, a gas cloud in nearby space that makes travel to and from the planet difficult.
csg_pulra.description: Pulras are a strange species of shapeshifters who cannot see but make up for it with sonar. They generally form colonies where they attach to other Pulras.
csg_pulra.sidebar_text: Pulras share their homeworld with two other sentient species: the Aganof, who are long with dozens of small legs, and the Hairy Savages, who are violent primates. Of the two, they have more contact with the Aganofs, who are highly intelligent and recognized by the Pulra as fellow sentients. However, the two species have been unable to effectively communicate with one another, and as such, the cave-dwelling Aganof mostly stick to themselves.

csg_pyke.name: Pyke

special_abilities.name: Underworld Connections
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Black Market Contacts.”

csg_pyke.physiology: Pykes are thin humanoids with green or gray skin. They have a long neck and a pod-shaped hexagonal head that is wider at the bottom. They have a small face in their head’s center that typically has purple eyes. They also have two tentacles coming down from their chin and two small spikes coming out of the back of their head. They have two large toes per foot and three fingers on each hand.
csg_pyke.society: The Pykes are a clever species that are not trustworthy and have what it takes to succeed in the underworld. They are superb liars but are capable of improvising if their deceptions break down. As such, it is no surprise that they are notable for their presence in the Pyke Syndicate, also known as the Pyke family. The Pyke Syndicate was very prominent more than thirty years earlier, around the time of the Naboo Crisis, when they held a near-monopoly on Kessel’s glitterstim. They continue to operate major spice-mining operations on Kessel.
csg_pyke.language: The Pykes typically speak Basic in a way that sounds slow and almost robotic. Like the Gand, they avoid pronouns. Some know other languages like Huttese if they need them.
csg_pyke.homeworld: The Pykes come from Oba Diah, a rocky, cliff-covered world not far from Kessel and on the Kessel Run. This has set them up well to profit in the glitterstim industry. It is fairly urban and has been under the influence of the Pyke Syndicate. Lom Pyke was once leader of the Pyke Syndicate and Minister of Oba Diah before he was killed and replaced by Marg Krim.
csg_pyke.description: Criminal enterprises are very important to the Pykes. They live not far from Kessel on their homeworld of Oba Diah, which puts them in prime position to handle much of the spice smuggling. Their prominence has somewhat dwindled with time, and they are no longer as powerful as they once were.
csg_pyke.sidebar_title: The Pyke Syndicate and the Sith
csg_pyke.sidebar_text: The Pyke Syndicate has dealt multiple times with the Sith, starting with their early deal with a man named Tyranus. A Jedi named Sifo-Dyas ordered the creation of a clone army as a result of manipulation from the Sith by Darth Plagueis, known as banker Hego Damask. The Sith Darth Tyranus needed Sifo-Dyas killed as a way to take control of the clone project. As Sifo-Dyas was on his way to meet with the Pykes, Tyranus paid them to shoot down and kill Sifo-Dyas’s shuttle. They did so, but took Silmann, Valorum’s aide and Sifo-Dyas’s partner, alive. This backfired when the Jedi discovered the matter during the Clone Wars, and Tyranus, revealed to be Dooku, killed Pyke leader Lom Pyke as cover-up. Around that time, the Pykes were involved with the Sith as members of Darth Maul’s Shadow Collective, which briefly took over Mandalore.

csg_pweck.name: P’w’eck

special_abilities.name: Natural Armor
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Force-Blind
special_abilities.description: May not become Force-sensitive.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Olfaxes
special_abilities.description: Add setback on visual Perception checks, but remove this penalty if smell can also be used. May also smell emotions, upgrading the difficulty when opposing a Deception check.

csg_pweck.physiology: Like their Ssi-ruuvi masters, the P’w’ecks are bipedal Saurischians, and they share many other traits with the Ssi-ruuk. They have protective scales and claws that help them in combat, and they are blind to the Force. They have bad eyesight but make up for it using their sense of smell, which is more advanced than human smell and can sense emotions. To smell, they use two tongue-like appendages that come out of holes above their mouth. They are smaller than Ssi-ruuk, closer to humans in terms of physical strength, and the Ssi-ruuk believe that the P’w’ecks are also less intelligent. P’w’ecks have brown scales, which look similar to scales of Ssi-ruuk who are born from mixed castes.
csg_pweck.society: The P’w’ecks are slaves to the Ssi-ruuk, who justify their prejudice using a religious text called the G’nnoch. Both species live in an isolated region of space on the edge of the galaxy known as the Ssi-ruuvi Imperium. Although the Ssi-ruuk wish to expand their territory, they fear dying on unconsecrated worlds, so they will not expand. Young P’w’ecks are slaves who do menial labor, typically acting as beasts of burden or crewing starships. Once they are fifteen years old, the P’w’ecks are enteched. This is extremely painful, leaving them conscious and eventually driving them to madness. During entechment, the P’w’ecks are bound and used as a mechanical power source, generally powering battle droids or starships. After the Battle of Endor, the Ssi-ruuk will begin an invasion of both the known galaxy and Chiss space, mostly using the P’w’eck-powered droids on their front lines. However, the invasion will be repelled on both fronts, and Chiss retaliation will lay waste to their homeworld, Lwhekk.
csg_pweck.language: P’w’ecks speak the melodic language of the Ssi-ruuk, which is called Ssi-ruuvi. A few P’w’ecks learn Basic so that they can act as translators for the Ssi-ruuk.
csg_pweck.homeworld: P’w’ecks are from Lwhekk, a steamy jungle planet in the Ssi-ruuk star cluster.
csg_pweck.description: The P’w’eck resemble a smaller version of the more fearsome Ssi-ruuk, who keep them as slaves. At the age of fifteen, they are forced to undergo the painful process of entechment, where their mind is transferred into a droid body that can by used by the Ssi-ruuk in their crusades.
csg_pweck.sidebar_text: Following the Chiss counterattack, the Ssi-ruuk will rebuild their society, even advancing the entechment process so that it becomes painless, allowing the P’w’ecks to last much longer. During the Yuuzhan Vong War, they will be ready to invade again, this time with the plan of sending a diplomatic mission to Bakura that will claim to be the P’w’eck Emancipation Movement, arriving with news that the P’w’ecks had won. The team’s true purpose will be to peacefully consecrate Bakura, which the Bakurans will allow the P’w’ecks to do. After that, the Ssi-ruuk will be able to invade. However, they will ultimately be undone by the P’w’ecks themselves, who will conduct a real uprising with help from the Galactic Federation of Free Alliances. At the same time, the Ssi-ruuvi Imperium will be crippled by a Yuuzhan Vong invasion. The P’w’ecks will be victorious, and most of them will resettle on Bakura, where they can live free.

csg_qiraash.name: Qiraash
csg_qiraash.physiology: The Qiraash are a near-human species with pale skin in shades of chalk-white or pink, and their dark hair grows only out of the back of their neck. Their elongated cranium is bald, although many Qiraash women tie their hair in thin braids that they pull over the top of their head. The only other feature setting them apart from humans is their higher-than-average cheekbones, although the two species are generally genetically incompatible. Only in the cases of genetic manipulation are Qiraash/human hybrids possible.
csg_qiraash.society: As evidenced by their enlarged brain, the Qiraash are a scholarly people with a knack for the world of academics. They particularly excel in finding patterns and identifying underlying causes in what they observe. This makes them valuable in mathematical roles as analysts or forecasters, but the Qiraash are not merely egghead intellectuals who never see the real world. Their ability to recognize trends also extends to people—even though they are keenly aware of the fact that many sentients are quite illogical. By observing what makes people respond in particular ways, they are quite persuasive and adept at oration. They are adept at hiding their own feelings of arrogance when it’s necessary to get what they want. Other Qiraash take interest in the arts, which are often highly abstract. Many take an interest in what they call “algorithmic art,” where they construct multivariable vector functions whose graphs are pleasing to the eye. Where the Qiraash most lack is in physicality. Their schools train only their mind, and their religion teaches that the conscience will be freed from the body after death. Thus, they have little use for physical exercise, and they view more blue-collar labor as beneath them. As a fairly wealthy society, they can always program droids or hire someone else if they have a more manual job at hand.
csg_qiraash.language: While the Qiraash are good at many mental things, rote memorization is not one of them, so most are monolingual. Those on Tag-Narrl only speak one of their native tongues, such as Orlain, while those born offworld usually only know Basic.
csg_qiraash.homeworld: Qiraash come from Tag-Narrl, a world in the eastern part of the Colonies with a fairly diverse ecosystem. It boasts many prestigious universities, such as Gaimor Classical University, and the population lives in relative comfort while droids tend to their farms and factories. Its government is in good standing with the Empire, and the Qiraash maintain strict law and order to make sure that it stays that way.
csg_qiraash.description: The Qiraash are a species of pale near-humans whose expanded brains give them excellent pattern recognition. They are skilled analysts and predictors, and they can also use their mental prowess toward understanding social situations, making them highly convincing speakers.
csg_qiraash.sidebar_text: Not all Qiraash are so pleased with their abilities, and some find that the constant in-depth analysis of their surroundings is overwhelming. Most cope by heading to familiar places they've already understood, shutting themselves off from the outside world, but a sizable minority are known so coping in less-than-healthy ways. It is said that just the right amount of alcohol can dull a Qiraash’s perceptions enough to make them psychologically similar to a human, but they have a reputation for taking the drinks too far overboard. Others take an interest in different spices, though they much prefer depressants to stimulants or hallucinogens. They are also uniquely affected by phareen flour. While it is a common and safe food product for most species, it has relaxing properties for the Qiraash, who find it highly addictive.
csg_qiraash._provenance_note: The Qiraash species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_quaple.name: Quaple

special_abilities.name: Thick Hide
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Powerful Bite
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 4 advantage to bite, dealing +1 damage as wounds and inducing a Critical Injury with the Vicious 2 quality.

special_abilities.name: Battle Frenzy
special_abilities.description: When betrayed or when family is threatened, enter a frenzied state. When in this state, deal +1 Brawl and Melee damage and gain +2 WT, but may not use any skills or perform activities that require concentration or patience. Require an average Discipline check to leave this state, or an easy Discipline check after all enemies are eliminated.

csg_quaple.physiology: The Quaples are a large species of herbivores, usually well over two meters tall. Though their ancestry is mammalian, they are well-adapted to living in rivers and marshlands, where they can hold their breath for up to half an hour. They have extremely tough, leathery skin, which comes in hues of gray ranging from bluish or lavender to dull pink. Their visage features a snout with wide, powerful jaws that they can use to fend off predators, and they have widely-spaced nostrils and eyes. They have no hair, and their ears are atop their head.
csg_quaple.society: The Quaples’ size and fearsome appearance actually hides what is usually an honest and quite gentle giant. They get along well with other nearby species, and they are frequently seen traveling the galaxy, as they often have a great wanderlust. They care deeply for their families, which are usually nuclear, and they are highly protective of their homes. These homes, built on the banks of rivers or in wetlands, are low tech and partially flooded, with a dry level and a submerged level. They also use a mix of elevated platforms and waterways to get around their cities. Those who go into space are often merchants or use their musculature for manual labor, although a few find their way into more thuggish roles. However, even these enforcers are careful to ensure that they only target specific victims without involving their families. Harming or threatening their family is one of the few things that can make them lose their tempers and go into a ferocious berserking rage. Betrayals also enrage them deeply; thus it is a well-known piece of advice to never double-cross a Quaple.
csg_quaple.language: Quaples have a handful of languages on their planet, the most prominent of which are Okwal and Nion. In the towns nearest the spaceports, it is common for them to learn Basic, but more rural settlements usually just stick to their own language.
csg_quaple.homeworld: Quaples come from Rivva, a world in the Outer Rim quite close to the Perlemian Trade Route. While prominent in galactic trade, its technology is not particularly advanced outside of the spaceports. It has very strong fishing and logging industries, while there have also been burgeoning mines for valuable underground gasses, such as tibanna.
csg_quaple.description: The Quaples are semi-aquatic mammals who are typically gentle giants, but their friendly demeanor is quickly reversed should their family be threatened or they find that they’ve been lied to.
csg_quaple.sidebar_text: While the Quaples themselves are fond of travel and adventure, they were much less excited when the Galactic Empire attempted to turn their world into a tourist hotbed without their consent. The Quaples felt betrayed by the Empire, and their rage made itself manifest at a species-wide level unseen before. The Empire was stunned as the previously passive herbivores proved to be deadly, and their forces were entirely annihilated in a devastating uprising. Only a few hundred Quaples were killed over the course of the planetwide conflict, and they even managed to destroy an entire star destroyer by crashing it into their moon. While the Empire has made talk of returning to the Rivva system to get revenge on the Quaples, they will not ever have the ships to spare, and the Quaples will survive and remain independent until they have the chance to join the New Republic.

csg_quarren.name: Quarren

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_quarren.physiology: Descending from cephalopods, Quarren are aquatic creatures. Thanks to the conical nature of their hairless forehead and their downward-pointing ears, Quarren have a head that is very triangular in shape. Three mandibles line a tiny mouth that sits near the chin, and four prehensile tentacles sit right next to it, dropping down to the chest. Above their tentacles, they have two alluring eyes of turquoise or blue. They have no visible nose or hair. Their skin is a leathery orange, sometimes pink, brown, or gray-green, and they have the ability to slightly change its hue in their mating rituals. Quarren typically have three suction-cup fingers on each hand, but some have five fingers or claws.
csg_quarren.society: Quarren are determined and stubborn, always trying to adhere to tradition and only changing when absolutely necessary. They are also slot to trust and pessimistic by nature, particularly toward more idealistic species, such as the Mon Calamari, who share their home. Though the Quarren had peace in the ocean depths for untold ages, their first encounter with the Mon Calamari started a feud that lasts to this day. War after war broke out, and the Mon Calamari frequently came out on top. Having nearly a million prisoners of war, the Mon Calamari eventually set them free but kept control over the generation of the young Quarren who had been born in captivity. These Quarren were schooled in Mon Calamari culture and arts for a decade before sending them back to their parents in the deep. These individuals were seen as brainwashed by their elders, but as they grew, they shifted Quarren culture into accepting an uneasy peace. With Quarren miners and Mon Cal engineers working together, the society was able to advance greatly, building floating cities and even starships. Nonetheless, the animosity never fully resolved itself, and the Mon Calamari remained wealthier and more politically powerful. Tensions boiled over in the Clone Wars when the Quarren Isolationist League attempted to secede against the Mon Cal’s wishes. Their efforts failed, and their support of the Separatists even resulted in a Republic cruiser rendering their shipyard colony of Pammant uninhabitable. Many Quarren do not see their ventures into space as a particularly good thing, and their literature shows a longing for simpler times in the ocean depths.
csg_quarren.language: Quarren speak Quarrenese, but it is difficult to speak in air, so they also can speak Basic in a gurgled tone.
csg_quarren.homeworld: Quarren come from the oceans of Mon Cala, an Outer Rim world that is also known as Dac. They mostly live in mining colonies beneath the sea, although some live in cities that float higher, such as Coral City, Quarren City, Morjanssik, or Foamwander. The planet is free from Imperial rule after a hard-fought struggle.
csg_quarren.description: Quarren are pessimistic, paranoid, and slow to trust. This has made it hard for them to get along with the Mon Calamari, who have attempted to remold Quarren culture. They finally have something that resembles freedom with a more egalitarian government and freedom from the Empire. Quarren live deep underwater on Dac, as they are an aquatic species.
csg_quarren.sidebar_text: It is said that the Empire seized Mon Calamari by fitting the two species against each other, having the Quarren sabotage planetary defenses. Although the Mon Calamari were mostly responsible for upsetting the Empire, both species were made into slaves under a brutal Imperial rule. Many Quarren who escaped this fate tended to just run. Others, however, make the difficult choice of fighting back. Even collaborating with the Mon Calamari, they were recently able to turn on their captors and successfully free their homeworld. However, many still loathe the Rebellion for upsetting the Empire in the first place.

csg_quermian.name: Quermian

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Body Language Readers
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter, may make a Perception check opposed by the Deception of a chosen NPC. If successful, add boost on all social checks made against that NPC for the rest of the encounter and know that NPC’s current emotional state. May also silently converse with other Quermians by reading body language, although more complicated or specific messages may require a check at the GM’s discretion.

csg_quermian.physiology: More or less, Quermians are a tall version of the Xexto species. They have a long neck, extremely pale skin, and four long arms. Though large, they are not actually that strong, and most are weaker than average humans because of their thin nature. Their hairless head has yellow eyes. Though they lack a nose, they can smell via their four-fingered hands. They have two brains, which has benefits in terms of intellect but drawbacks when it comes to developing split personalities. Their mouth is almost permanently in what humans generally consider to be a knowing smile. Interestingly enough, this knowing smile actually describes the Quermian personality quite well.
csg_quermian.society: Quermians were herbivores without predators when they developed their culture, so they are mostly peaceful. This has also given them plenty of time to develop philosophies, making them prominent as philosophers. They are capable of reading body language very well, something many recognize as telepathy. Some xenobiologists believe this claim, but the Quermians themselves claim otherwise. Since they are so good at reading body language and recognizing emotions, many become diplomats.
csg_quermian.language: Quermians typically know Basic, as well as their own melodious, vowel-filled tongue of Quermian. They also tend to be literate in both.
csg_quermian.homeworld: Quermia is a peaceful Outer Rim planet not far from the Xexto homeworld of Troiken. It has lush vegetation and very few animals.
csg_quermian.description: The Quermians are a taller version of the Xexto species that has been genetically created on Quermia. They are very peaceful because Quermia lacks predators, and they are prominent as diplomats and philosophers.
csg_quermian.sidebar_text: Long ago, when Xextos were in hunter-gatherer tribes, an Arkanian geneticist began experimenting with Xextos, hoping to make them taller so as to grant better vision. He brought them to the nearby world of Quermia, and these GMO cousins became known as Quermians. The Quermians are very tall, even in comparison to species like Wookiees. Though they  once denied the fact that they were related, the Xextos now hold a grudging respect for the Quermians and their intellect, who get along very well for their part.

csg_quockran.name: Quockran

special_abilities.name: Bulk
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Droid Experts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Deft Maker.”

special_abilities.name: No Differentiated Organs
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

csg_quockran.physiology: Slug-like creatures with mottled dark skin, the Quockrans are bulky but a bit less than two meters tall on average, with a long tail for locomotion in lieu of legs. Their arms are short with four fingers, and they lack the dexterity of humans. While their bulk makes them durable, they are still very unathletic and lack strength. They have a chubby stomach, sagging breasts, and a drooping chin that usually forms jowls. Their visage features a mouth of pointed teeth and wide set eyes to either side of it, with a large nose dominating their forehead. Internally, their organs are more versatile than those of other species, and this unique biology ensures that a single wound is almost never fatal.
csg_quockran.society: Quockran society has moved below the ground into tunnels, and few offworlders even know that they exist. Far fewer still have gotten the chance to actually interact with the Quockrans, who are deeply xenophobic and want nothing more than to be left alone. They are a stubborn and secretive bunch, and they become extremely uncooperative when others try to interact with them. If they have no choice but to interact with the wider galaxy, they can be perceptive when they need to be, and they will always be extremely slow to speak. Quockrans boast excellent technical skills, particularly when it comes to droids, but they have very little interest in other areas of scholarship.
csg_quockran.language: The details of the Quockran language are unknown, and none have any interest in learning Basic. Presumably, some of them know the machine language that their droids use. If such a Quockran needs a translator, the droids which are imported from offworld know the machine language in addition to Basic.
csg_quockran.homeworld: Situated in the backwater Minos Cluster of the Outer Rim, Quockra-4 was once swampy and moist, hospitable for life such as the Quockrans. However, the climate warmed in the distant past, its waters evaporating and giving way to featureless salt flats. Afternoons are scorching, but the nighttime can be freezing. Quockrans occasionally venture up to the surface at night, relaxing on the sand when it is cooler and the air feels more damp, but they try to avoid any outsiders when they do so.
csg_quockran.description: The Quockran are a highly reclusive species of slugs who have hidden underground in order to avoid interaction with the outside world. They have built a litany of droids to serve as their emissaries.
csg_quockran.sidebar_text: Although the Quockrans themselves live in isolation, they understand the benefits of trade, so when the Old Republic colonized the Minos Cluster, the Quockrans built a society of more than 10 million droids who live in a single city on the surface. These droids serve them and act as their public representatives, often buying and selling goods with offworlders. If the visitors get too nosy, the droids are programmed to ignore their questions and force them to leave, violently if necessary. At the apparent top of the droid society are repair droids designated by yellow paint who tend to have three arms, and beneath them are red-painted worker droids. Within these categories are literally thousands of variations, but all of them speak a beeping and whistling machine language that is not used anywhere else. There are also a number of droids recognizable as being imported from Imperial worlds, but they seem to have the lowest status, and many do not enjoy their jobs. These droids are the only ones who speak Basic, so they are usually used as interpreters, and as such, they are kept unaware of the Quockrans’ existence.

csg_quorsav.name: Quor’sav

special_abilities.name: Protective Instincts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Body Guard.”

special_abilities.name: Beak and Legs
special_abilities.description: When using beak, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a crit rating of 3, but have the Inaccurate 1 quality. When using legs, deal +1 Brawl damage.

special_abilities.name: Frail Constitutions
special_abilities.description: Add 2 setbacks on checks to resist poisons. Double penalties induced by air quality and develop illnesses caused by air quality much more frequently.

csg_quorsav.physiology: Quor’sav have an avian appearance, although they share many characteristics with monotremes. They are very large, at three to four meters tall, and they have long legs and powerful muscles. Excluding their legs, their body is covered in yellow feathers, and they have short arms that somewhat resemble wings. They have a very long neck, and their head has blue eyes on its sides and a sharp, orange beak that they use for combat. They sleep and relax by perching rather than laying down or sitting, for which they use a specialized seating rack or resting rack, and they are known to have very vivid dreams. They have a unique internal biology, and their heart is in their lower abdomen. They are very vulnerable to diseases, especially those related to air quality. Quor’sav reproduce by laying eggs, which take a year to hatch.
csg_quorsav.society: Quor’sav are known for their paranoia and anxiety, and they are rarely calm. They have strong protective instincts, particularly among females. Since they are so large, those who connect with non-Quor’sav view them like children, so they often attempt to take up a parental role in such interactions. They express emotions visually in ways that are different than other species, often through their feathers. Their feathers are smooth when calm, stiff when surprised, and can shake with anger. When very happy, they tend to grimace, an expression which typically confuses other species. Quor’sav have long been independent, but they have joined the Empire in response to an economic recession. Although their economy has improved, some are now mandated to join the Imperial Military.
csg_quorsav.language: Quor’sav typically do use a language of their own, and they generally speak Basic with a high-pitched voice.
csg_quorsav.homeworld: Quor’sav come from Uaua, a planet in a rural part of space called the Centrality. It is known for its many insects, which the Quor’sav eat.
csg_quorsav.description: A large species of avians, the Quor'savs' strange appearance makes them an easy target for racism, and they fear outsiders after their first contact resulted in the outbreak of a virus. They are a paranoid species, constantly on the lookout for danger, and they have strong protective instincts.
csg_quorsav.sidebar_text: The Quor’sav have had strained relations with outsiders, a fear that dates back to their first contact, over 3,000 years ago. When mammalian offworlders first encountered the Quor’sav, they brought with them a virus that the Quor’sav were devastated by. Ever since then, they have been wary of outsiders and try to maintain an isolationist stance. Although they can be friendly to other avians, they tend to dislike mammals, especially primates. Conversely, their strange appearance often prompts prejudice or jokes from humans. They also have troubles with the Yam’rii, a sentient species of carnivorous insects who greatly enjoy eating Quor’sav eggs.

csg_qwohog.name: Qwohog

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe in freshwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions. When breathing saltwater, suffer 1 wound per minute.

csg_qwohog.physiology: Qwohog are also known as Wavedancers, because they are aquatic and very nimble in the water. They are very short, just over a meter high on average, but they are still fairly athletic for their size. Their smooth skin is covered in scales, some of which stick out on top of their head and around their wrists and ankles. These scales are typically tan or silver in color. They have gill slits in their armpits that allow them to breathe underwater, although their lungs do not work in saltwater. The Qwohog do not have nostrils, but they can still smell using a ridge of skin above their mouth. Their greenish eyes have no visible pupils, and their long ears point upwards.
csg_qwohog.society: Driven and energetic, the Qwohog can be playful but also very devoted to whatever task is at hand when they need to work. They are a very social people, and they place great value in their communities. In the greater galaxy, they try to meet new people and often enjoy trade, and they are driven by a desire to explore. They are extremely amiable to strangers, but they can be unforgiving and surprisingly ferocious when wronged. On their homeworld, they are technologically primitive but can make many useful things to trade, including textiles, food, and medical products.
csg_qwohog.language: The Qwohog have a native language which only works underwater. They can use sign language to communicate on land, but recently, Anomid technicians have created a vocalizer mask for the Qwohog. This device, costing 100 credits, analyzes jaw movements and can be programmed to play corresponding sounds from almost any language.
csg_qwohog.homeworld: The Outer Rim planet of Hirsi is covered in freshwater lakes, and it has very little land. While the Qwohog are primarily aquatic, the land is prized by offworld interests, currently Imperial, who mine the rudic crystals to use them in sensors.
csg_qwohog.description: The Qwohog, known to some as the Wavedancers, are an aquatic species that is energetic and charismatic. They were first discovered by the Rebel Alliance, but after the Empire discovered their world, they have had little interactions with outsiders.
csg_qwohog.sidebar_text: The Qwohog’s homeworld was actually first discovered by the Rebel Alliance, who came to it in search of valuable rudic crystals. For a brief period of time, the Qwohog’s only contact with the outside galaxy was to trade with the Rebel Alliance. However, their planet was later discovered by the Empire, who forced the Alliance offworld and began their own mining operations. Although neither the Qwohog nor the Empire like each other very much, they coexist mostly peacefully, and they barely interact, leaving the Qwohog isolated again. The Empire will withdraw from the planet as they decline following the Battle of Endor, allowing the Rebel Alliance to establish a permanent base. Many Qwohog will travel offworld via Rebel ships, and they will form colonies throughout the galaxy in the following years.

csg_rakata.name: Rakata

special_abilities.name: Savages
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Lethal Blows.”

special_abilities.name: Islanders
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for wet conditions, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Severed Connection
special_abilities.description: May not become Force-sensitive.

csg_rakata.physiology: Rakata are smooth-skinned humanoids of aquatic ancestry that have a tall cranium. They have eye stalks protruding from the sides of their head and a multitude of sharp teeth. Their hands have three digits, each tipped with a sharp claw designed for combat. The species is typically slender and very uniform in height. Most Rakata have gray or red-gray skin, although more rare subspecies exist such as the blue-skinned Droot, the red-striped Ikalik, and the black Bukesek. The Rakata are carnivores, even feeding on other sentient species or each other.
csg_rakata.society: Rakata were once savages, but they were gifted with knowledge of the Force and technology by the Kwa. The Rakata took this knowledge and betrayed the Kwa. Rather than finding balance in the Force as instructed, the Rakata channeled only darkness. They began spreading, using their Force-based hyperdrive technology to form their Infinite Empire. However, this technology was limited and could only reach worlds that were strong in the Force. They conquered any species they met, driving many to extinction. However, some races, especially those strong with the Force, were taken as slaves. With or without their technology, the Rakata are an immoral and cruel species. They are xenophobic but prone to infighting, and they are relentless conquerors who are unwilling to compromise. They are divided into the priest and warrior castes, and the two castes are constantly at odds with one another. Modern Rakata feel a profound emptiness after being cut off from the Force, and a majority live as primitive cannibals.
csg_rakata.language: Typically, Rakata only speak Rakata. However, they are fast learners and able to speak other languages.
csg_rakata.homeworld: The original Rakatan homeworld is Lehon, a tropical world in a remote portion of the galaxy known as the Tempered Wastes. The surface of the planet is almost entirely covered in oceans, with a number of islands and archipelagos dotting the surface. Although their population on Lehon is extinct, they have scattered colonies in a region of the Unknown Regions known as the Rakatan Archipelago.
csg_rakata.description: Once savage primitives, the Rakata were gifted with the Force by the Kwa, and they ended up turning to Dark Side and building an Empire. However, they fell from glory when a plague cut them off from the Force.
csg_rakata.sidebar_text: Suddenly and mysteriously, as quickly as they grew their Empire, it fell.
