csg_srrorstok.sidebar_text: One of the most unique facets of Srrors’tok morality is that of the life debt, which states that if someone saves their life, the Srrors’tok then owes their life to serving that person. They will do anything to fulfill their life debt, even serving someone who they see as evil, and if they cannot fulfill the life debt, they are expected to commit suicide as punishment. Generally, life debts mean they act as a bodyguard of sorts, although it can also mean fulfilling another role for the organization that the beneficiary is a part of, and the debt lasts for life. Life debts can be cancelled if a Srrors’tok acquires a second life debt: Although they generally try to fulfill both contracts, this is typically not possible when the two beneficiaries are enemies of one another. Should this happen, they generally cancel the older debt, but they sometimes cancel both. However, it is seen as incredibly dishonorable to intentionally take up a second life debt in order to get free of the first. They speculate that allowing Srrors’toks to intentionally get into life debts would lead to a complex network of debts and the end of their society.

csg_ssi_ruu.name: Ssi-Ruu

special_abilities.name: Natural Armor
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Force-Blind
special_abilities.description: May not become Force-sensitive.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Olfaxes
special_abilities.description: Add setback on visual Perception checks, but remove this penalty if smell can also be used. May also smell emotions, upgrading the difficulty when opposing a Deception check.

csg_ssi_ruu.physiology: Ssi-ruuk are a species of large Saurischians who are fierce warriors. They are bipedal and have clawed hands and feet. Although they are taller than most species and weigh a whopping 350 kilograms on average, they are extremely agile for their size. Ssi-ruuk have a protective layer of scales, which come in varying colors depending on caste. These scales are thick and can protect them from blasters. Ssi-ruuk have poor eyesight, but they have an excellent sense of smell using two tongue-like appendages which can also sense emotions.
csg_ssi_ruu.society: Ssi-ruuk are a very spiritual people, and they have built the Ssi-ruuvi Imperium based on their beliefs in a book known as the G’nnoch. Although they wish to expand, they fear dying on unconsecrated planets, so they rarely ever leave their isolated star cluster. They use a unique technology known as entechment, in which captured organics can be used as a power source. Although the Ssi-ruuk claim otherwise, this process leaves them conscious and is extremely painful. Only “inferior beings” like slaves are enteched. Soon, Emperor Palpatine will make contact with the Imperium, ceding a few Outer Rim worlds to the Ssi-ruuk in exchange for entechment technology. After Palpatine’s death, the Ssi-Ruu will invade Bakura, but they will be driven back by the Alliance and devastated by the Chiss. They will manage to consecrate Bakura during the Yuuzhan Vong War, but a slave uprising will topple Ssi-ruuk society.
csg_ssi_ruu.language: Ssi-ruuk speak a melodic language called Ssi-ruuvi, which humans cannot reproduce. They rarely learn other languages and prefer to use droid translators.
csg_ssi_ruu.homeworld: Ssi-ruuk come from Lwhekk, a steamy jungle planet in the Ssi-ruuk star cluster that they rule.
csg_ssi_ruu.description: Ssi-Ruuk are a very prejudiced religious people, and they have a strict caste system which includes slaves. They control a small Empire in the Unknown Regions, southwest of the galaxy, but they are hesitant to invade any new planets because they fear dying on an unconsecrated world.
csg_ssi_ruu.sidebar_text: Ssi-ruuk are a highly prejudiced people. At the top of society are blue-scaled nobles and gold-scaled priests, while those with yellow scales work as scientists. Those with black scales work as assassins, and those with red scales make up the military. Most Ssi-ruuk have green scales, and they are used as workers. Marriage between castes is forbidden, and children from multiple castes end up brown. Such brown-scaled Ssi-ruuk are often killed at birth or used as slaves. There is also a species called the P’w’ecks, who are similar to the Ssi-ruuk but are smaller and always have brown scales. The P’w’ecks are seen as inferior and often enteched. Similarly, the Ssi-ruuk seek to conquer all other species.

csg_stenax.name: Stenax

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Fearsome Countenances
special_abilities.description: Add advantage on all Coercion checks.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

special_abilities.name: Adept Targetters
special_abilities.description: If using a ranged weapon while in flight, treat its range as being one range band further.

csg_stenax.physiology: Stenaxes are terrifying creatures of reptilian ancestry, towering well over two meters. They have skin in shades of puce, maroon, and magenta and an extremely well-muscled physique, even over their face, which pushes their brows to point upward. Their chin also has two drooping muscular cords, and they have pointed ears. Their eyes are mostly white with small pupils, but their sight is aided by another organ: the Kleti gland. This gland appears as a crest on their hairless cranium, which gives them an enhanced ability to recognize the movements of prey over great distances, homing in on them while in flight. However, Stenaxes no longer fly naturally, having vowed as a race to no longer use the massive wings on their back. Even without the advantage of flight, they are still dangerous fighters, as sharp spikes line their body along their shoulders, arms, and behind their knees. They also have sharp talons on all of their digits, which number three for each hand and foot. They live for two or three centuries.
csg_stenax.society: The Stenaxes are a brooding and violent people, although they are not without discipline. In fact, their culture is deeply spiritual, and they have built countless temples in honor of their god, Vol. The object of highest reverence to them is a stone idol of Vol, which they lost in an earthquake centuries ago. As a result, they became greatly ashamed and refused to fly until it was found. Only recently was the idol rediscovered by the Rebel Alliance, and which has prompted the race to take to the skies once again. Though they were once Imperial slaves, their joyous rediscovery of flight has allowed them to revolt and kill the Imperial governor, taking their planet for themselves and allowing them to largely ignore the offworlders.
csg_stenax.language: Stenaxes speak Stenax, and they are also capable of learning Basic.
csg_stenax.homeworld: Stenaxes come from Stenos, though they have started to travel through the Gordian Reach. It is a verdant green world with towering mountains and ruins of ancient buildings. The world is fairly lawless, with a substantial immigrant population that is mostly involved in criminal activity. The Stenaxes generally have little to do with these offworlders and prefer to keep to themselves.
csg_stenax.description: A grim species of massive, terrifying reptilians, the Stenaxes are more isolationist than conquest-minded, at least for now. They are devout followers of a god named Vol, even at one point forsaking their ability to fly for centuries as a show of grief.
csg_stenax.sidebar_text: A few Stenaxes have begun to travel offworld, generally using their musculature as mercenaries or menial laborers. However, they have actually been sent by their people to carefully observe the wider galaxy as the race contemplates a conquest of new worlds. In places such as Hunter’s World, Kabray, Delrakkin, and Cilpar, they have become more adept with understanding technology and are now prepared to strike against their enemies. Their hour will come about ten months after the Battle of Endor, when they will overrun Imperial strongholds before turning against civilian populations. Millions will be killed in the ensuing conflict, and only the New Republic will ultimately be able to subdue the Stenaxes, culminating in a final battle at Tharkos. Afterwards, perpetrators will be imprisoned, while the rest of the species will be observed closely to ensure they do not strike again.

csg_sullustan.name: Sullustan

special_abilities.name: Large Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Born Pilots
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Skilled Jockey.”

csg_sullustan.physiology: Sullustans are small near-humans, about a meter and a half tall, with a mouse-like appearance. They have tan, gray, or pink skin, with little hair. A few grow hair on their face, while rare females have it on top of their head. Their eyes are large, black, and highly sensitive to light, which causes them to get corneal defects at about 30 years old. They have very large ears granting them quality hearing, and they have facial jowls which are known as dewflaps. Their dewflap patterns and cranial ridges are slightly variable, allowing them to easily tell their own kind apart. Navigating the cave systems gives them an innate sense of direction, which also helps them when navigating through hyperspace. They are also very resistant to alcohol.
csg_sullustan.society: Sullustan society is very outgoing, and amiable, always looking to interact. They are curious in nature and looking to explore the galaxy. As they prefer to learn through mistakes and experience, some consider them to be reckless. Sullustans organize themselves into Warren-clans, which include one polyandrous female maintaining the home and several males, as well as their young. Despite their large families, they are overall quite individualistic, especially with how they look, often adding unique tattoos. Sullustan economy is very capitalist, and in addition to its notable starship industry, they also attract tourists for their high-tech underground cities. Some Sullustans prove to be skilled musicians due to their hearing. Perhaps the most unique business is hairstyling, where the generally hairless Sullustans are surprisingly renowned. The Empire has put SoroSuub corporation into power on Sullust, which employs half the population. The move is mostly opposed by the democratic Sullustans, and many look to join the Rebel Alliance.
csg_sullustan.language: Sullustans speak Sullustese, a chattering language with fairly short words. The pronunciation is somewhat difficult, but not impossible, for humans. Since Sullustans are a common sight amongst the stars, many spacers speak Sullustese. Many but not all Sullustans know Basic.
csg_sullustan.homeworld: The Outer Rim world of Sullust is a volcanic planet, and can be found on the Rimma Trade Route. It has rocky deserts and mountains as well. A wealthy world and a major hub of trade, especially with the starship industry, it “shines as a nova of capitalism.” The Sullustans live almost entirely in the underground caves, which are cooler, more humid, and free of the large predators that roam the surface. While the volcanoes aren’t very active in some parts of the planet, few are completely gone. The atmosphere is barely breathable thanks to volcanic pollution, but this does not affect the underground caves,
csg_sullustan.description: Sullustans are a small and mouse-like people who are very eager to explore and be outgoing. They developed a great sense of direction living in tunnels on Sullust, so they are excellent navigators.
csg_sullustan.sidebar_text: Sullustans have very unique burial rites, and death, known as “Eternal Sleep,” is treated with reverence. They have vast crypts and vaults, which are guarded by crypt masters. The most elaborate of their rites is referred to as “tomb walling.” The bodies are covered in stone bricks, which are placed one at a time, with the close relatives placing first, and minor friends going last. The placer of the final block is their spouse or closest friend, who then gives a short forward-looking address, with a number of words equal to the age of the deceased being in years.

csg_sunesi.name: Sunesi

special_abilities.name: Unique Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Can breathe a cirrifog atmosphere. Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Mystical Healers
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Heal/Harm Basic Power.

csg_sunesi.physiology: Sunesi are turquoise-skinned amphibians who undergo a radical metamorphosis at the age of 15. Their young are hairy and unable to speak, and although they are intelligent, their nervous system is diffused throughout their body. They form a cocoon in a reaction with cirrifog crystals in their planet’s atmosphere, inside of which they become gangly bipeds without hair who can speak. A few of them do not ever reawaken, but most survive to become adults. They have no nose, dark eyes, and enlarged craniums which emit ultrasonic sounds that mess with electronic listening devices or Gotal head-cones.
csg_sunesi.society: Sunesi are a deeply religious people with a strong moral compass. They once were divided amongst themselves, but they have since united under a common religion overseen by a single Priest-Prince. The Priest-Princes usually serve as long as they want and then hand power to one of their children. They worship the Maker, and they believe in an afterlife, viewing death as similar to their own metamorphosis in life. Many are Force-sensitive, and they are usually healers. They value honesty and prefer pacifism, but they will fight when it is necessary to achieve liberty. They are also a very inviting people, accepting not only offworlders but droids into their society and treating them as equals.
csg_sunesi.language: The Sunesi language uses both ultrasonic sounds from their skull and verbal sounds from their mouth, so humans cannot replicate it. However, most Sunesi can speak Basic.
csg_sunesi.homeworld: Sunesi come from the Mid Rim planet of Monor II, also called Kline’s Colony, and few of them venture into the galaxy. It is terrestrial, but it has a unique atmosphere of hazy cirrifog which is toxic to non-Sunesi.
csg_sunesi.description: A highly religious people, the Sunesi are skilled doctors and devout followers of their Maker. Their current Priest-Prince is Force-sensitive and a vocal critic of the Empire, so he now writes while in hiding.
csg_sunesi.sidebar_text: Imperial operations on Monor II are currently harvesting the cirrifog crystals in the atmosphere, which is making it more difficult for juvenile Sunesi to form their cocoons. The current Priest-Prince, Agapos IX, is a Force-sensitive and a vocal critic of the Empire who strongly advocates for rebellion in literature that circulates throughout the HoloNet. The Empire put up a bounty on him, so he was forced to flee Monor II and write while in hiding, aided by recent convert Daye Azur-Jamin.

csg_svivreni.name: Svivreni

special_abilities.name: Stubborn
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Nobody’s Fool.”

csg_svivreni.physiology: Svivreni are short equines who make up for their small size with musculature. They also have long arms for their size and hooves that allow them to run only slightly slower than a human. Their skin is pinkish, and their head features wide eyes and a projecting snout as well as two pointed ears. They typically have copper-colored hair on their forearms and atop their head, which they rarely cut. They typically only braid it, and this braid can go as far as their knees, especially among older Svivreni. They live for about 125 years and are very resilient.
csg_svivreni.society: Svivreni are one of the galaxy’s most stubborn species. They rarely change their mind about anything and react adversely whenever someone attempts to persuade them. Younger Svivreni will often defend their viewpoints via brawl. Although older ones are even more uncompromising, they fight less. They resist outside influences in their culture, so many of them do not like the Empire. Although they are currently under Imperial control, they will eventually join the New Republic and put up an incredible defense against Thrawn through sheer determination. Despite capabilities for violent resistance when needed, they are harsh on crime. They ban weapons, and violent crimes on their homeworld are punishable by death. This tends to ward off most criminals. One of the most unique aspects of their culture are their complex greetings and farewells. For example, they consider saying “goodbye” to be bad luck and instead use the phrase “as the journey begins, so go.”
csg_svivreni.language: The Svivreni language can only be spoken by Svivreni, although they are capable of speaking Basic. Not all Svivreni know Basic, however.
csg_svivreni.homeworld: Svivreni hail from Svivren, a mountainous Outer Rim world with a harsh climate. Despite the challenges that the Svivreni face, it is a prominent trade world that exports technology and other metal products. It is ruled by the Svivreni Trade Alliance and has a population of eight billion, including many immigrant humans, Sullustans, and Ewoks.
csg_svivreni.description: The greatest asset of the Svivreni is their incredibly stubbornness and determination. Despite their small stature, they are resilient and tough, making excellent miners and metalworkers.
csg_svivreni.sidebar_text: Svivreni are renowned throughout the galaxy for their abilities as miners and metalworkers, which helped make their backwater home into a successful trade world. They also run the Svivren Xenomineralogy Institute, which is considered the best college for xenomineralogy. They have a natural talent for recognizing a mineral’s value and are employed in all levels of mining. Most Svivreni miners wear sleeveless clothes so as to maximize flexibility and have many pockets to carry tools. Svivreni also value recognition from peers, although there is no consensus among them as to who is the best mineralogist in history.

csg_swokes_swokes.name: Swokes Swokes

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Reduced Sensitivity
special_abilities.description: Add two setbacks on tactile Perception checks. Remove two setbacks for pain.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound. May also regrow lost limbs after about 10 days.

csg_swokes_swokes.physiology: Swokes Swokes are chubby creatures with white or gray skin and no hair. Their wide mouth cannot frown and features several pointed teeth in a seemingly random arrangement. They have small bluish horns around their neck and atop their head. Their nostrils vary in number from one to three. Their eyes are blue, red, or white, and they have black eye sockets. This overall facial appearance is unattractive to almost all other species in the galaxy, although some instead view them as comical. Many Swokes Swokes have a tail which ends in four knobby spikes, while others lack this feature entirely. Swokes Swokes are among the galaxy’s hardest to kill creatures. They are absolutely relentless in combat because of a number of factors. Their thick, blubbery skin acts as excellent protection, they have greatly reduced sensitivity to pain, and quick regenerative abilities ensure that any wounds they do suffer, even lost limbs, can be healed in a little over a week.
csg_swokes_swokes.society: Swokes Swokes are a people who are viewed as brutes. This is very true: They are a violent people who are quick to fight and often try to solve their problems with straightforward combat. They are typically very selfish and use wealth as an important measure of status. One way to demonstrate this wealth is to surgically embed gemstones. Many buildings operated by Swokes Swokes use bioscanners to detect such gemstones and determine the wealth of its occupants. Aside from their wealth, they care little for hygiene or outward appearances. For example, they eat loudly and messily with all parties sharing from a wide trough. Cannibalism is a common punishment, but they view being eaten by family as better than being eaten by strangers.
csg_swokes_swokes.language: Swokes Swokes speak their guttural native language called Swoken, and most also know Basic. They repeat names of things that are great, so successful Swokes Swokes often have names like “Yeb Yeb.”
csg_swokes_swokes.homeworld: The Swokes Swokes come from Makem Te, an arid world in the Outer Rim with snake-like creatures called schingas that are domesticated as mounts. It exports spice and is also rich in a number of metal ores. The latter has attracted foreign mining companies, and many Swokes Swokes are suspicious of these firms. It is ruled by a Council of Caliphs, and its largest city is Thousand Thousand.
csg_swokes_swokes.description: Chubby and incredibly ugly, the Swokes Swokes are incredibly durable and unrelenting with incredible regenerative abilities. They are religious and place a great deal of importance on correctly burying the dead and often carrying the body parts of their ancestors with them.
csg_swokes_swokes.sidebar_text: The Swokes Swokes are a very religious people. They are divided into a number of sects which each fight for the devotion of the people. One sect, the Temple of the Beatific Razor, stressed violent and zealous devotion and demonstrated their piety by flaying parts of their skin. However, this sect is now illegal. Most sects have a number of features in common. They venerate their ancestors and often carry pieces of their bodies as relics. Funeral planning is an art form to the Swokes Swokes. Whether buried or cremated, the remains of ancestors are stored in a giant graveyard known as the Tract. Each person is stored in a monument called a “stela.” Each stela is contained in a two meter square of white polished stone. The Tract Conviction, a government branch responsible for the Tract, employs millions.

csg_sy_myrthian.name: Sy Myrthian

special_abilities.name: Bulky Physique
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

special_abilities.name: Vast Wealth
special_abilities.description: Gain +1,500 starting credits.

csg_sy_myrthian.physiology: The Sy Myrthians are a species of gastropods that move their body around by slithering on their single giant foot, with a body structure quite similar to that of a Hutt. However, the species are not related, as the Sy Myrthians are actually hairy mammals, with their pinkish skin covered by fur that is white on their front and darker on the back. This dark fur ranges in hue from a yellowish brown to steel gray, and both males and females also have a “beard” of longer, darker fur on their chin. Their head is elongated backwards, with a pair of triangular ears surrounding their large brain. They have wide nostrils that are flanked by red eyes. While they have a fatty body, it is not quite as bulky as that of most Hutts, and their arms are much longer. Sy Myrthians have four-fingered hands with dark nails.
csg_sy_myrthian.society: Ironically, of all the vices that one could accuse the Sy Myrthians of, sluggishness is not one of them. Greed comes naturally in their highly productive society, and while they crave comforts, they are willing to do whatever it takes to get them. Sy Myrthians bring a unique combination of hard work and more underhanded means to the problems at hand. They are bullying and crass by nature, although they have their ways of getting people to do what they want. They make generally detached parents, focusing on their work while confining the young Myrthlets to pods where they are supplied with a screen-based education. They only involve themselves to supply harsh words when the Myrthlets struggle, but this is surprisingly effective for their psyche. Sy Myrthians are highly motivated by criticism even as adults, while surrounding them with too much praise is the one thing that can make them complacent. They’re at their best when faced with difficult circumstances. Such hard times have now come to fruition: A formerly Separatist species, the Sy Myrthians doubled down on fighting for independence even after the loss of the droid army, and they continue to pay the price. Nonetheless, many Sy Myrthians have continued to find ways to wriggle out of new taxes, and some discreetly support the Rebel Alliance.
csg_sy_myrthian.language: The Sy Myrthians speak Basic with a bellowing voice. Although they are educated in their native language, Myrthian, it is rarely used even on their own planet.
csg_sy_myrthian.homeworld: The Outer Rim planet Sy Myrth was once an economic powerhouse with a prime location on the Triellus just off the Perlemian. As one of the Separatists’ key foundry worlds, it was bombarded badly and is now a shell of its former prestige. Many now try to take their businesses to greener pastures.
csg_sy_myrthian.description: A slow-moving species of gastropods, the Sy Myrthians are greedy and willing to do whatever it takes to secure wealth, whether it be honest or dishonest work. As notable Separatists, they have little love for the Empire that has devastated their world.
csg_sy_myrthian.sidebar_text: While Sy Myrthians are not typically ones for adoring words, they actually have a surprising fondness for many of the very same creatures they consider ugly. Whether it be pets of bizarre physiology or employees with genetic deformities or of species they call ugly, every powerful Sy Myrthians seems to end up with a strange entourage. Perhaps this habit is to make themselves seem more attractive by comparison, but the Sy Myrthians are not keen to explain. In fact, they are known to react with stunning hostility should someone agree with an insult they just said, as they want to be the only ones to use such words.
csg_sy_myrthian._provenance_note: The Sy Myrthian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_skytri.name: S’kytri

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: If carrying 5 or less encumbrance, can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

csg_skytri.physiology: S’kytri are tall and thin, muscular but light. They are mammals but share many traits associated with avians, so they have hollow bones and a thin body. They have very large wings attached to their shoulder blades, which are feathered. Otherwise, they have a humanoid body structure. They have no hair on the sides or back of their head, only a spike of hair resembling a feather at the very top of their scalp. This hair is between dark red, orange, yellow, or white. Generally, they have deep eye sockets and large lips. Their skin is typically blue for males or green for females, but less than one in every hundred S’kytri hatch with reverse pigmentation matching the other gender. These babies are considered to be horrific abominations, and they are typically killed immediately after they hatch. Additionally, the Outland Clans have red or orange skin.
csg_skytri.society: Known as “the Windborn” in their native language, the S’kytri are a proud people. To them, flight makes them an innately superior species in comparison to any other flightless sentients. They place very high value on tradition and “old world” values, which are enforced by a prominent patriarchy. They do not care for advanced technology and prefer a more primitive lifestyle, and they are very environmentally conscious. They view their homeworld as a living being and nurture it as such. They are a peaceful people, but they will fight courageously when absolutely necessary. To accomodate flight, they wear relatively little clothing and prefer tighter garb rather than anything that might create unwanted air resistance. Males generally also wear anklets which show their clan’s insignia. There are three types of clans: Highland Clans, Lowland Clans, and Outland Clans, the latter of which are distinguished by their red or orange skin and are seen as outcasts.
csg_skytri.language: Basic is the language of the S’kytri for all practical purposes, as their native language of S’kytric died. However, the folk revival places a heavy emphasis on returning to S’kytric, so it is now seeing renewed usage in those arts.
csg_skytri.homeworld: The Outer Rim planet of Skye is the S’kytri homeworld, although many offworlders, particularly Imperials, refer to it as Marat V. It is a mountainous planet with a mostly temperate climate. As loyal allies of the Jedi, Skye was a Republic ally that was later conquered by the Empire. It is currently ruled by Majestrix Kharys, a cruel Dark-sider appointed by Darth Vader. Under her rule, all other S’kytri are enslaved. After the fall of the Empire, Skye will become relatively isolated, refusing to join the New Republic and avoiding offworld contact.
csg_skytri.description: Strong but delicate mammals who can fly, male S'kytri are blue while females are green. They are currently enslaved by the Empire, but their society has also become divided between elders who support a traditional patriarchy and a youth counterculture.
csg_skytri.sidebar_text: Although much of S’kytri society is traditional and subservient to the elder patriarchs, young adults have pride of their own, and it has created a growing youth counterculture. Increasingly, they refuse to abide by the norms set by their elders. Simultaneously, the S’kytri are slaves to the Empire, and its harsh rule encourages a change toward Imperial doctrine and human culture, which has upset almost all S’kytri. In response to these dramatic changes to society, many are demanding a return to tradition. Folk songs and traditional art of all types have been making a comeback in S’kytri society.

csg_talid.name: Talid

special_abilities.name: Cold Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Extra Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_talid.physiology: The Talids are a species of lanky equine mammals with an extra set of arms. Though they are not particularly agile at their height, they have a layer of thick, bristly fur to protect them from the cold of their homeworld. Their fur is usually white, and those born with brown or tan fur tend to bleach it. They have a narrow equine face with four nostrils, and their cheeks are quite sunken. Their eyes are very narrow.
csg_talid.society: Talids are nomadic but not exclusively primitive, as they often partake in salvage of offworlder technologies. They are capable of using slugthrowers to defend their territory, and they can trade with credits if need be. However, they prefer to avoid the human colonists, and they generally only visit the Podraces until after they’re over to pick up the scraps. They have a complex system of negotiating that involves an opening ceremony followed by a long but direct sequence of bargaining until equilibrium is reached. Few other species understand its nuances, so they can sometimes have misunderstandings in the negotiations. While the Talids are cold and no-nonsense in these interactions, they have a more lighthearted and playful spirit that comes out among their own company. Their own society is quite ancient, and their tribes are adept at using reptomammals called tantas as mounts.
csg_talid.language: While Talids can speak Basic, verbal languages do not come particularly naturally to them. They instead use a language of hand and arm signals that are referred to as “Talid signalling.”
csg_talid.homeworld: The Talids come from a planet called Ando Prime, which is the third world in the Ando system that they share with the Aqualish. It is frigid, mountainous, and best known among other species as a place where Podraces are hosted. There are a few offworlders that settle there to mine vontium, but even Elesa, the town that is technically the planet’s capital, has only about a dozen buildings.
csg_talid.description: A species of six-limbed equines adapted to the frigid mountains of Adno Prime, the Talids live simple yet devout lives. Their religion of Dai Bendu monks was actually a key part of the foundation of the Jedi Order.
csg_talid.sidebar_text: The Talids have always been a religious people, and their tradition of the Order of the Dai Bendu monks is among the oldest extant groups to study the Force. Millennia ago, it was the Dai Bendu who encountered one of the Tho Yor and journeyed to the planet Tython. These Talids would be among the first Je’daii, and their ways would influence the Order over its lifetime—most notably creating their logo of an eight-pointing ring. Though the Dai Bendu who went to Tython would be largely forgotten apart from their Jedi heirs, not every monk left Ando Prime aboard the Tho Yor. The faith has continued strong in the mountaintop monasteries where it originated. They wear long and simple robes, but their wisest, the High Priest, is given more colorful orange vestments. They pump sacred water from the mountains and live in simple tents. They chant haunting songs in a very deep voice, and the number nine is sacred to them, representing the unity of the Force. While they preach against confrontationalism, they have no problem with commercialism, as they occasionally interact with Podrace organizers and sell the artisanal carpets that they weave.

csg_talz.name: Talz

special_abilities.name: Four Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness or brightness.

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_talz.physiology: Talz are snow-dwellers who grow over two meters tall. Their white, light gray, or cream-colored fur blends in well with the snow on their homeworld and, alongside a layer of blubber, protects them from the cold. Their noseless face is distinguished by having shorter and darker gray fur and four black eyes. The larger two see well in darkness, while their smaller eyes can handle bright reflections off snow in the daytime. Near the chin, a proboscis extends, which they use to eat, breathe, and communicate. Their large hands have sharp claws, making them effective brawlers and skilled at digging through layers of ice. Talz reproduce like insects, hatching from eggs as larvae and growing in a cocoon for their second year of life before cracking out of it as adult sized-Talz. After that, they live for about fifty years.
csg_talz.society: Despite their combative advantages, Talz are peaceful creatures. Although they defend themselves when needed, they are generally quite gentle, kind, and quiet. They prefer to satisfy their innate curiosity through observation rather than vocalizing their questions. They are diligent workers, though so primitive that more than once, the Talz have been considered to be non-sentient. However, they can construct simple shelters for warmth and do understand offworld technology like starships or blasters at a basic level. Their one complicated thing is a complex system of extended families within their clans. Organizing the clans are sophisticated rules, which are designed to distribute resources as effectively as possible. They have no formal schools, but parents will sometimes group up in educating their large children. Because the Talz are strong, peaceful, and not considered to be sentient, the Empire has enslaved them as miners on Alzoc III. Although they hope for freedom, violence is not a response that the Talz use. However, many now distrust all humans or other species that resemble them. A few Talz still live free on their other small colonies, such as Hoth.
csg_talz.language: The Talz speak Talzzi, a language of chirps and buzzes. Pitch is very important for determining the words as well. Due to the structure of their proboscis, the Talz cannot speak Basic.
csg_talz.homeworld: The Talz homeworld, Alzoc III, is a snowy planet with minimal greenery, like their colony on Hoth. It was discovered by the Empire and kept off many records, so few people know of the slavery of the Talz. It is in the southern Outer Rim and rich in minerals.
csg_talz.description: Talz are peaceful but physically powerful creatures adapted to the cold. They are very simple and do not understand the concept of ownership. Many are Imperial slaves.
csg_talz.sidebar_text: Since property is communal to the clan, the Talz fail to understand the concept of ownership. They will innocently borrow someone else’s things but allow others to do the same to them. This creates a perception that Talz tend to be thieves, and those familiar with the race learn to thoroughly lock up their possessions when around a Talz. Many have tried and failed to explain the concept of ownership to Talz, but few ever succeed. Talz will often give away objects they perceive as being “unused,” which often include decorations or things of sentimental value.

csg_tarasin.name: Tarasin

special_abilities.name: Cold-Blooded
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Color-Changing Skin
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Deception checks, but add boost on Stealth checks. May also communicate with other Tarasin by changing skin colors.

csg_tarasin.physiology: Tarasin are slightly undersized reptilian humanoids  who have translucent scales and color-changing skin. They can change colors to better camouflage themselves, but they also change colors based on their mood. They have enough control over it that they can communicate with other Tarasin by changing colors, but it is also a tell that makes it harder for them to lie or bluff. Similarly, they have a thin fan of skin around their neck that spreads out when they are agitated. They lack a nose or ears, and their face is distinguished by a wide mouth, prominent cheekbones, and large, black eyes. They are cold-blooded, mostly adapted for a warm climate, and they have a tail for balance.
csg_tarasin.society: Tarasin have moved past a nomadic life and formed tribal communities known as irstats that have a few dozen members and are generally a day’s journey apart. The chieftan, known as the Irstat-Kes, is typically the second-oldest female, while the eldest female, known as Mother, is revered as perfect. Tarasin are intelligent and curious by nature, and generally amiable in their interactions. Such traits allowed them to welcome Republic explorers when they first arrived on their planet, but tensions grew when natural resources were plundered by offworld factions generally interested in mining. Tarasin tribes and Trade Federation droids escalated violence against one another, and the Tarasin demonstrated surprising competence with offworld weapons. Eventually, the Jedi intervened and negotiated the Cularin Compact with both sides, a peace treaty that greatly limited corporate interests on Cularin. From then on, the Tarasin were mostly left alone, and the scale of industry, mostly conducted by the Metatherian Cartel, was greatly reduced.
csg_tarasin.language: Tarasin speak Tarasinese, but they often choose to communicate by changing skin colors, which is silent and can often go unnoticed.
csg_tarasin.homeworld: Tarasin come from the steamy rainforests of Cularin, an Expansion Region world which is full of life and strong in the Force. It has a few small cities operated by offworld interests such as the Metatheran Cartel. In 32 BBY, the usage of a Sith Artifact caused the planet to seemingly disappear for the next decade, which passed by in a blink for those on Cularin.
csg_tarasin.description: Humanoid reptiles with color-changing skin, the Tarasin are naturally spiritual and have a strong connection to the Force. They were once plagued by corporate interests, but they have since been left alone.
csg_tarasin.sidebar_text: All Tarasin have some connection to the Living Force, although few possess the ability to use it in very tangible ways. For most, it allows them to connect with nature in ways that other species cannot. Their entire planet is strong with the Force, so they value its natural resources. They are mostly vegetarian and rarely hunt for food, only medicinal compounds or skins. In particular, the hardwood ch’hala trees play an important role in their religion and are sacred to them. In 119 BBY, a Jedi Academy opened near Cularin, which many Tarasin joined. Although they hide their connection to the Force from the Empire, it is likely that many surviving Jedi now take refuge among the Tarasin. A few of the Tarasin who are strongest in the Force will join the New Jedi Order.

csg_tarc.name: Tarc

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions. May go for 2 weeks without water.

special_abilities.name: Hardened Shell
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: When using claws, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

csg_tarc.physiology: Once aquatic crustaceans, the Tarc have evolved into predatory desert dwellers. Their exoskeleton is made of chitin, and it can protect them as well as store water, thus allowing them to survive for weeks without access to fresh water. This contributes significantly to their bulk, making them slow-mowing, although they are strong and have quick reflexes. While they have six limbs, two of them are bulky pincers that only are suitable for combat. The upper pair of arms ends in three-toed fingers, but they have a variable number of toes. They have a wide mouth with no lips or tongue, and they also lack a stomach. Instead of swallowing, they have hollow spikes similar to teeth which can absorb food directly in their mouth, but only soft meat. They are a bit taller than humans, rarely wear clothes, and are also distinguished by having two antennae on their forehead.
csg_tarc.society: Tarc tend to be logical and straightforward, repressing their emotions whenever they can. They are extremely decisive, but they struggle to think in the long term and usually only want to deal with immediate problems. Tarc will be violent if there’s a clear benefit to doing so, but they will rarely attack out of rage. When in combat, they try to overwhelm their opponents quickly with direct offense, and they are not particularly merciful. Occasionally in combat, it brings out their repressed emotions, and they can get carried away in the thrill of violence.
csg_tarc.language: Because of their unique mouth, Tarc are incapable of pronouncing most of the galaxy’s languages. Their own language uses grunts, groans, and clicks.
csg_tarc.homeworld: Tarc come from the planet Hjaff in the Colonies, which has oceans as well as three arid continents. They control twenty other nearby systems, which are mostly military bases.
csg_tarc.description: A species of crustaceans with extra arms, the Tarc have massive claws and excellent water storage that lets them last in harsh deserts. Their nations are isolationist and independent of the Empire.
csg_tarc.sidebar_text: A multitude of nations and cultures have always been present among the Tarc, and they often went to war with one another. With war came technological progress, and their economy became more interconnected. They at last made peace among the nations, unifying under an elected leader called the Keddek. Each continent elects one advisor, but only the constitution limits the Keddek’s power. All serve for ten years (about eight standard years), and all Tarc are legally required to vote. Once war was set aside, the Tarc were able to take to the stars, and they began to colonize nearby worlds. Their empire spanned twenty star systems once they finally encountered other sentient life. Scared that another culture would erase their own, the highly xenophobic Tarc mostly returned home, now using their colonies as a buffer. None are legally allowed to leave, and intruders are shot on sight by their navy, called the Ivlacav Gourn. The Empire has attempted to invade, and while the Tarc have repelled them thus far, it only encourages the Empire to return in greater numbers. As the war escalates, a small minority of Tarc now suggest working with the Rebel Alliance.

csg_tarnab.name: Tarnab

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_tarnab.physiology: Tarnab are six-limbed bovine mammals, walking quadrupedally with a front side that curves upward. Each of their limbs has three digits that end in black hooves or nails. They have tan to gray fur that covers their entire body except for their hands and face, which is adorned by a dozen horns of various sizes. Each of their ears has a line of six horns above it, which surround a sloped forehead. Their mouth is near the bottom of their snout-like jaw, while their blue or purple eyes are widely set around a large, arch-shaped nostril. Tarnab are not particularly powerful athletes, but their four-legged stature gives them a strong anchor, and they are exceedingly durable due to their thick fur and leathery skin. This also protects them against the cold, and they are adept at surviving snowy environments.
csg_tarnab.society: Tarnab are notoriously stubborn, rarely changing their mind once it is made up and being entirely indifferent toward the opinions of others. They have little concept of shame and are essentially immune to mockery, which on occasion makes them prominent influencers who do not fear to set bold trends. However, to the Tarnab, such adoration is only as useful insofar as they can profit off it. Despite how it may seem, they are not aloof, merely indifferent. Because they are a rather forgiving people when they are criticized or insulted, Tarnab tend to be blunt and to the point. It is this honesty and objectivity that makes them valued in a wide range of analytical occupations, from news column editors to actuaries. However, their lack of tact has dramatically hindered the ability of Tarnab-ran businesses to succeed in interplanetary commerce, and their planet is consequently rather impoverished. For many decades, Tarnab have blamed their economic woes on taxes, overregulation, and other species’ inability to bargain objectively. Perhaps these complaints were once somewhat overblown, but the Empire now places an aggressive tax burden on the Tarnab to punish their discontent.
csg_tarnab.language: Tarnab have a low-pitched voice and generally speak Basic, in addition to one of their native tongues. Iblit speaks Iblis, and Vanball speaks Akrian.
csg_tarnab.homeworld: Tarnab are native to Narrell, a world in the Merel Sector of the Outer Rim. They are from its frozen tundras in lower latitudes, within 30 degrees of the south pole, a region known as Iblit. While they colonized its north pole, called Vanball, no one has use for the temperate regions, which are covered by vast oceans and rocky wastelands. Narell’s most prominent industry is tibanna gas mining, of which there are plentiful pockets deep beneath its ice.
csg_tarnab.description: The Tarnab are strong-willed bovine mammals with four legs. They are extremely blunt, with little use for politeness, and they tend to blame all their problems on those around them.
csg_tarnab.sidebar_text: Tarnab are known for their elaborate textile products made from toonbat fur, an animal they frequently ranch. They export high-end jackets and blankets, as well as purely decorative tapestries. Its thin strands allow them to crochet highly detailed patterns to tell stories. Value is placed on creating fabrics that can show multiple scenes by refolding, as each configuration reuses the elements in clever ways.
csg_tarnab._provenance_note: The Tarnab species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_tarong.name: Tarong

special_abilities.name: Advanced Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness and add boost on auditory or visual Perception checks.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. When flying, move twice as quickly.

csg_tarong.physiology: Tarongs are a species of large, flying reptiles with clawed feet and hands. Additionally, they have prominent wings with a wingspan of ten to twenty meters, although they can fold them up to enter smaller spaces. The wings are leathery, but they have a few feathers on the bottom. Similarly, they have a distinctly avian head which is also feathered. They have a beak, and their eyes, which see in the infrared, granting them excellent low-light vision, are on the side of their head. Tarongs also boast excellent hearing, although they do not have any sense of smell. Their feathers come in shades of brown and olive, and their skin typically matches its color. In addition to their wings, they have a wide tail to help them fly, and they move exceptionally quickly while flying. They are also carnivorous, preying upon small mammals such as rodents and marsupials. Tarongs never wear clothing unless they are in a cold environment, although they will wear simple jewelry.
csg_tarong.society: Tarongs are an extremely talkative people who enjoy conversation of any sort. They always try to talk to their prey, as they would never eat anything that can talk to them. Because of this trait, they are endlessly amused by protocol droids, whom they often treat as family. They are peaceful whenever it is possible, and their prefered tactic if they need to defend their home is to pick up the adversary and fly them to a remote or inaccessible location. They are also known for their love of gems and jewelry, which they typically decorate themselves and their protocol droids with. Despite access to offworld technology such as droids, they are otherwise fairly primitive, living in small huts in the treetops. They live with a larger extended family, and twelve to thirty families combine to form a tribe.
csg_tarong.language: Tarongs tend to be good linguists, as they can naturally pick languages up by mimicking them. They typically know Basic as well as at least one other language.
csg_tarong.homeworld: Tarongs were first discovered by the Republic on two worlds, Iri and Disim, and it was unclear which was their original home or how they spread to another planet. They were genetically almost identical, and they have since interbred extensively, thus totally eliminating any differences between the two species. Both Iri and Disim are both rural forest planets with some mining industries that are found in the Epidimi system of the Mid Rim.
csg_tarong.description: The Tarong are large flying reptiles with talons and a sharp beak who are peaceful despite their predatory heritage. They are a very social people, often living with many extended family members, and they have a fascination with protocol droids.
csg_tarong.sidebar_text: None of the Tarong tribes have any sort of formal government, although they meet with nearby tribes every season. Presiding over these meetings is the closest thing they have to political leadership, although they change leaders every meeting. They dislike the Empire, mostly because Imperial governors are less interesting in conversation, so they avoid interacting with the Imperials. They do enjoy exploring the galaxy and learning about offworld politics, although they have little interest in replicating them in their own society.

csg_tarro.name: Tarro

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Loners
special_abilities.description: Add setback when targeted by a Leadership check. May not perform the assist maneuver.

csg_tarro.physiology: Tarro are tall humanoids with clawed hands that have seven fingers each. This combination of size, athleticism, and natural weapons make them formidable combatants. They have a high forehead and lack eyebrows, and their nose is quite flat. They have pointed ears, and their mouth is full of sharp teeth. They have gray-green skin and yellow eyes, while hair color is dependent on sex. Males have navy blue hair, while females have reddish brown hair.
csg_tarro.society: Tarro are not especially immoral, but they are generally rude and not very friendly. Tarro are loners, and they are extremely self-centered. They expect others to leave them alone, and they often get frustrated that others are in their way. They are also extremely stubborn, always sticking with doing things their way. Despite these attitudes, the Tarro managed to build a very technologically advanced society, and they are highly intelligent. They cannot stand bureaucracy or paperwork, so they generally choose to live on the fringes of the galaxy, where legality is of little concern. They generally live on the move as mercenaries or bounty hunters, avoiding any long-term attachment to people or places.
csg_tarro.language: Tarro have managed to preserve their native language, Tarrese, a tongue that is very similar to Basic, but it is harsher-sounding and has a wider variety of sounds. Most of them know some Basic, since they rarely encounter other Tarro.
csg_tarro.homeworld: Tarro come from Tililix, an isolated planet in the Unknown Regions that has now been destroyed. They have not adopted a new homeworld, and they have now scattered throughout the Outer Rim.
csg_tarro.description: A taller species of near-humans with red hair, pointed ears, and claws, the Tarro are loners who are focused only on their own business. Their homeworld was destroyed, so they are scattered, and many go to the Outer Rim, as they detest bureaucracy.
csg_tarro.sidebar_text: Almost a century ago, the Tarro’s star system was destroyed when their sun exploded without warning. Many have speculated that this catastrophe was caused by the Tarro themselves, that they may have built some sort of superweapon could have destroyed the star system, but any evidence regarding the system’s destruction has been destroyed in the cataclysm. Only a few hundred Tarro survived, and they have scattered, leaving the species on the verge of extinction. Down to about 350 members, a few of them now look for lost Tarro colonies that are currently lost to time. Similarly, the dispersion of the Tarro has caused them to lose almost all of their original culture, although their attitude as obstinate loners remains unchanged.

csg_taung.name: Taung

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_taung.physiology: A now-extinct species of humanoids who had gray-green skin, the Taungs were bigger, taller, heavier, and stronger than humans. Their hairless head had tendrils and was typically hairless, and they had a pointed chin. They had glowing eyes and lacked a nose. Taungs also boasted claws to further enhance their combative abilities, and they matured quickly, reaching adulthood at thirteen.
csg_taung.society: Taungs were a warlike group of people who were all expected to be warriors first and foremost. Their god, Kad Ha’rangir, is a destroyer who brought growth through the cycle of death and rebirth. As such, warfare was seen as the instrument of the divine. Sloth, personified by a deity called Arasuum, was seen as the worst vice. Religion and politics were intimately intertwined, and their laws were known as the Canons of Honor. They typically fought to resolve disputes in unarmed combat to the death. Despite their codes of honor, Taungs were ruthless and loyal only to their own kin. Their clans were nomadic and mostly independent, although they were governed by a single ruler called the Manda’lore. Although Taungs were primitive by modern standards, they sought to use as advanced technology as possible, and they constantly innovated to reverse-engineer their opponents’ technology. However, ancient Taungs wore little armor, unlike later Mandalorians, as they saw it to be more honorable.
csg_taung.language: The Taungs’ original language was a very archaic form of Mando’a, although it has changed little over recent millennia. Although the Taungs often learned many other languages, they strongly preferred to use Mando’a when possible. Their names were almost always Mando’a words intended to describe them.
csg_taung.homeworld: The Taungs were native to Coruscant, which was then known as Notron, before they moved to Roon. Their final home, Mandalore, was and is a rural planet composed mostly of forests, grasslands, and deserts.
csg_taung.description: An ancient species that is now extinct, the Taungs are the cultural ancestors of the Mandalorians. They were a group of warriors that fought over Coruscant in its early history before they colonized Mandalore and developed the culture that the Mandalorians follow to this day.
csg_taung.sidebar_text: The Taungs were very prominent more than 100,000 years ago, before the creation of the Republic or even the Infinite Empire. At this time, they battled the Zhells, a species theorized to be the ancestors of modern humans, for control of the planet Coruscant. Ultimately, the Taungs were defeated and mostly fled to Roon, where they lived for tens of thousands of years. Eventually, a Taung known as Mandalore the First led them to conquer a new homeworld, killing native beasts known as Mythosaurs. Their homeworld became known as Manda’yaim, or Mandalore in Basic, and they dubbed themselves Mando’ade, or Mandalorians in Basic, meaning Children of Mandalore. As the Mandalorian Crusaders expanded their territory, they subjugated, enslaved, or exterminated many species, but some members of other those species voluntarily sacrificed their past lives to be reborn as Mandalorians. Over time, other species became prominent among the Mandalorians. Almost 4,000 years ago, the Taung population was decimated by the Mandalorian Wars, and they became extinct shortly thereafter. However, their culture lives on among Mandalorians of other species.

csg_tchuukthai.name: Tchuukthai

special_abilities.name: Natural Armor
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Quadrupedal Structure
special_abilities.description: When carrying large objects or people on back, reduce their encumbrance by 4 to a minimum of 4. When bipedal, add setback on all checks that use Brawn or Agility.

csg_tchuukthai.physiology: Tchuukthai appear as ferocious beasts, and they boast immense size and physical strength. They have a quadrupedal structure, but they can stand on two feet and use their forelimbs to grasp things if needed. They are two meters tall when quadrupedal, and three meters tall when bipedal. Further complementing their combative abilities is their natural armor, which is made out of thick, green plates that cover their head, back, and joints. Even where they lack armor, their leathery skin is thicker than that of most species and provides them with some protection as well. Many Tchuukthai do not wear clothing, although those who interact with other species frequently will typically do so. Both their hands and feet have prominent claws on their digits. The Tchuukthai are ceratopsia, and they have a tail as well as a beaked face. Their head is also distinguished by their head-fins, which extend out of their beak, pointing sideways before curving upwards, and they have small eyes without pupils. Some Tchuukthai have small patches of white or light gray fur on their chin, on the end of their tail, or on the backs of their limbs, but their scalp is always completely hairless.
csg_tchuukthai.society: Tchuukthai are thoughtful and philosophical. Some of them prefer to be left alone with their thoughts, but it is also not uncommon for them to be more sociable. Despite their appearance, Tchuukthai are actually extremely peaceful, and they detest violence of any sort. They are best known for their romantic poetry, an art form that is very important to them. However, these renowned poems are difficult to translate into Basic, and outsiders typically struggle to appreciate or even comprehend their poems’ true meaning and depth.
csg_tchuukthai.language: Tchuukthai typically speak Tchuukthese, a guttural language. Many of them who interact with the rest of the galaxy speak Basic as well.
csg_tchuukthai.homeworld: The Tchuukthai homeworld is a subject of great mystery to the galaxy. Although it is speculated to be in the Unknown Regions, they refuse to disclose any more specific information about their planet of origin. All seem to come from elsewhere, as none have been born in the broader galactic community.
csg_tchuukthai.description: A mysterious species likely hailing from the Unknown Regions, the Thuuckthai are giant quadrupedal beasts protected by green natural armor and sharp claws. Although they are philosophical and romantic by nature, they often use their fierce appearance to scare outsiders who try to pry into their business.
csg_tchuukthai.sidebar_text: Tchuukthai are shrouded in mystery, and the rest of the galaxy does not even know their name. To the rest of the galaxy, they have been labelled as Wharls, which they generally accept without comment. Tchuukthai ignore or refuse to answer the many questions they receive about their origins, and only a handful have been known in the galaxy. Many more have been sighted briefly, in ways that have crafted legends and myths about their people. Tchuukthai have actually encouraged these myths, and many work to create a more intimidating reputation. Although they refuse to fight directly, their threatening appearance that they can easily scare off others without conflict, a solution that they find easier and more peaceful. To accomplish this, they generally use dramatic displays of strength or act like ferocious animals, and anyone who gets too curious is almost always scared into disregarding them once they witness such incredible acts.

csg_temolak.name: Temolak

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Utinni!”

special_abilities.name: Thick Skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

csg_temolak.physiology: Temolaks are a bulky species protected by tough, clay-colored skin. They boast many redundant organs, which allows them to survive more punishment than other species. Their face is compact, with small eyes and a short nose with large nostrils. They have vertical ridges on their chin and small horns on their cheeks. They have fin-like protrusions on their forearms, but they have lost all major benefits of their aquatic heritage.
csg_temolak.society: 2,000 years ago, water evaporated on the Temolaks’ homeworld, so they took to the stars in order to harvest ice from the planet’s rings. Since then, they have acquired hyperspace technology, and they have essentially abandoned their homeworld to live as scavengers amongst the stars. They live aboard packed starships built from scrap metal, and they are remarkably thorough scavengers. They are typically timid and quiet, but they can be fiercely stubborn if someone attempts to steal their salvage. Even the majority of pirates know that fighting with Temolaks is rarely worth the effort. Many Temolaks also operate space stations that were once abandoned, using them as headquarters or warehouses. They rarely do business with technologically advanced species, as they generally prefer to trade with the primitive species who see simple technology as precious valuables. Among other advanced species, they are generally far too quick to trust and too easily manipulated.
csg_temolak.language: Most Temolaks speak Temolish, their guttural native language, as well as Basic.
csg_temolak.homeworld: Spacefaring Temolaks are typically nomadic and have little reason to return to their homeworld of Zirulast, which is now a backwater planet with a small population. It is a dry planet found in the Expansion Region.
csg_temolak.description: Temolaks are known mostly as scavengers, and they are very stubborn, which they back up with durability. They generally sell their technology to primitive peoples, as other advanced species often take advantage of them.
csg_temolak.sidebar_text: During the Republic Classic Era, the Temolaks would often fight amongst themselves, fighting over garbage in long skirmishes that were clearly counterproductive. Since then, they have formed the Temolak Salvage Consortium, an organization responsible for maintaining peace among the salvage crews. The Consortium assigned specific territories to each crew, reducing conflict. However, it has become highly regulated under the Empire, so many Temolaks have now left it to work independently.

csg_terrelian_jango.name: Terrelian Jango Jumper

special_abilities.name: High Jump
special_abilities.description: Able to jump very high or far. Once per round as a maneuver, suffer 3 strain to move 2 range bands either vertically or horizontally.

csg_terrelian_jango.physiology: Terrelian Jango Jumpers appear as very skinny humanoids with long legs, weighing only fifty kilograms on average. They have red eyes, blue or turquoise skin, and red hair. However, they are actually very unique as incredibly gifted athletes, superior to almost all other species and even rivalling Jedi with their combination of long-jumping abilities and stamina on foot.
csg_terrelian_jango.society: The athleticism of the Terrelian Jango Jumpers is a result of their ancestors’ nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyle, where they would wander in search of food and chase prey on foot. Their leaping abilities proved essential in traversing valleys and catching prey over short distances. Although modern members of the species are more civilized, they never truly felt the need to develop permanent homes. As such, they continue to live in large speeders or other portable communities, and they prefer to take their jobs with them, making migrations back and forth based on the seasons, the job market, or their own whims. This tendency for travel has also made many of them take to the spacelanes, and many enjoy tourism as a hobby. However, their culture is cautious of most outsiders, and some, fearing racism, disguise themselves as humans using face paint. This stems from their first contact, in which unsavory Corellian colonists took advantage of their people. These past events did give them strange fondness for the Devish, who allied with them in a brief conflict to boot out the colonists, which the Terrelians celebrate to this day.
csg_terrelian_jango.language: Terrelian Jango Jumpers are generally bilingual, speaking their native language of Erreli as well as Basic.
csg_terrelian_jango.homeworld: Terrelian Jango Jumpers come from the Inner Rim planet of Terrelia. It is a mountainous planet with few permanent settlements, although its technology is otherwise up to the galactic standard. Imperial mining interests have taken a recent interest in the world, but the mobile natives have generally been able to avoid the new arrivals.
csg_terrelian_jango.description: Terrelian Jango Jumpers are a species of very athletic near-humans who are light and skinny. Their skin is generally blue-green, and they have red-orange hair.
csg_terrelian_jango.sidebar_text: Although Terrelian Jango Jumpers are excellent athletes, they are too skilled for their own good in some ways: In most sports, their exceptional physiology is seen as an unfair advantage, so they rarely compete against humans. However, they have developed their own sports leagues, many of which attract excellent viewership because of how gifted their athletes are. The Terrelian Smashball League has gained galaxy-wide attention in particular, but the vast majority of the Terrelian Jango Jumpers themselves actually find such sports to be boring and overcomplicated. They prefer more straightforward contests of athleticism, such as sprints, distance runs, or vaulting competitions.
csg_terrelian_jango._provenance_note: The Terrelian Jango Jumper species originates from TCW, and almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_thakwaash.name: Thakwaash

special_abilities.name: Multiple Personalities
special_abilities.description: Must have at least 2 distinct personalities. For each personality, choose a unique skill. Gain +1 ranks in that skill when using that personality. At the beginning of each encounter, choose a personality randomly. Once per encounter, may roll an average Discipline check to switch to a particular personality. May gain or lose personalities over time.

csg_thakwaash.physiology: The Thakwaash are a species of large equine sentients. They are incredibly strong, often possessing three times the strength of an average human. They are also very large at around three meters tall. They have a long face that features pointed ears, prominent nostrils, and black eyes. They have hair on much of their body, including atop their head and on their neck. This hair, like their skin, is typically brown. They all have multiple personalities, so they consider it to be a normal behavior rather than a disorder.
csg_thakwaash.society: Thakwaash are known to be a very unpredictable people, which is mostly a result of their psychology. They are one of the few peoples who remain completely apart from the Empire, mostly because their incredible strength makes them very tough to defeat in a fight. Although they have fought the Empire, they now remain isolated and lack hyperdrive technology. They will be discovered by the larger galaxy shortly after the Battle of Endor.
csg_thakwaash.language: Thakwaash speak Thakwaese, a language whose verbal form consists of growling, snorting, and neighing. Because of their multiple personalities, most Thakwaash choose to refer to themselves in the plural form.
csg_thakwaash.homeworld: Thakwaash hail from an Outer Rim planet known as Thakwaa, which is a temperate world consisting mostly of plains and grasslands. It is independent from the Empire and completely isolated.
csg_thakwaash.description: The Thakwaash are a very strong species of equines who all have multiple personalities. Although some of their older members can change personalities at will, most simply change between them at random.
csg_thakwaash.sidebar_text: Thakwaash are a very unique people in that they all have multiple personalities. They generally develop more over time, and some can even create particular personalities at will. They view these personalities as entirely different people. Like two separate individuals, these personalities often have different skill sets. It also helps them see from other points of view and better predict other people. Oftentimes, one or more of these personalities is insane. However, they still have some control over their personalities. Especially among older Thakwaash, it is possible to switch between them at will.

csg_theelin.name: Theelin

special_abilities.name: Performers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Distracting Behavior.”

csg_theelin.physiology: Theelin are colorful near-humans, but their genetics have been problematic of late. A series of mutations first started during the waning decades of the Republic, and those mutations have made almost all members of the species infertile amongst each other. Rare already, fully blooded Theelin are almost extinct. Those remaining are very old. Recent attempts at cross breeding with humans have had some success, but their numbers continue to dwindle, and infant mortality is high. Crossbreeding makes Theelin a diverse species. Most have mottled skin of some bright color, often pink, red, or lavender. They also have brightly colored hair in most cases. Many have outward-pointing horns at their forehead. Otherwise, they are mostly human, but some have features such as hooved feet or three-fingered hands.
csg_theelin.society: Theelin are artistic and outgoing, often enjoying the performing arts. Many also are into fashion. The Theelin Divas are among the best singers in the galaxy, so many Theelin take the name Diva to honor them. Regardless of craft, almost all tend to be optimistic and happy. As social creatures, they work best in teams.
csg_theelin.language: All Theelin speak Basic, favoring it over their now-dead native language.
csg_theelin.homeworld: Theelin come from Suggero, a Mid Rim planet on the Hydian. A hub for fashion and art, it attracts enough immigrants to refill its dying population.
csg_theelin.description: Art is very important to the Theelin. Pink-skinned near humans who are typically quite charming, the Theelin are a dying people. Mutations have made many of them infertile, and they have had to resort to crossbreeding with humans.
csg_theelin.sidebar_text: With pure-blooded Theelin slowly dying away and only partial success with crossbreeding, the Theelin are approaching what many consider to be an inevitable extinction. Despite this, they continue to make the most of their situation. For many, this sense of impending doom is almost poetic, and the emotions associated with it make for some of the best art yet from the species. For others, it can make for great fear, knowing that their time is short. Perhaps others may desperately seek a child to continue the species at all costs. Still others may become deeply saddened by this reality.
csg_theelin._provenance_note: No knowledge exists regarding the homeworld or language of the Theelin. The remaining information is made up. Players are not obligated to follow this.

csg_thisspiasian.name: Thisspiasian

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: When using claws, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Tails
special_abilities.description: When using tail, have the Knockdown quality. May also carry 1 object of up to 6 encumbrance with tail that doesn’t count towards encumbrance threshold.

special_abilities.name: Meditators
special_abilities.description: Require only 2 hours of sleep, but must meditate at least 5 hours throughout the day.

csg_thisspiasian.physiology: Thisspiassians are creatures distinguished by their hairy, somewhat humanoid head and long, scaly reptilian tail. Their skin is naturally an olive green, but their face is hidden behind a prominent beard that leaves only their mouth, red eyes, and nostrils exposed. This hair is black, brown, or blond in youth, graying and whitening with age. Instead of legs, they have a thick tail, which is strong enough to slither on top of, carry large objects, or fight with. They coil it beneath them when they sit. Thisspiasians do shed their skin, like most reptiles, cycling at a rate of once every few years. However, they generally prefer to peel it off in small pieces, a little bit each day. Though hidden to many, Thisspiasians actually have four arms, each ending with a sharply clawed hand. While working-class Thisspiasians have roughly equal strength in each set of arms, the lower arms of the wealthiest class are smaller and weaker. In the prestigious parts of Thisspiasian society, it is taboo to use or or even show these limbs, which they strap to their waist. Though they only sleep for about two hours per day, Thisspiasians do require a five or six hour meditation. Most of them live for about a century.
csg_thisspiasian.society: Thisspiassians are proud warriors who hold fighting as very honorable. At times, they use ritual unarmed combat to settle disagreements, such as when Jedi Master Oppo Rancisis used it to force the planet’s Blood Monarch into providing military support for the Republic. This Monarch is a hereditary position that some Thispiassians see as archaic and out of touch, and the elected parliament has always handled most day-to-day affairs anyway. As a people, Thisspiasians are disciplined and have a facade of tranquility most of the time, but they are still fueled by a fierce inner rage that they must subdue via meditation. If they omit it, they are prone to emotional swings.
csg_thisspiasian.language: Thisspiasian is a hissing tongue spoken by most Thisspiasians. Most can speak Basic as well.
csg_thisspiasian.homeworld: Thisspias is a rocky Expansion Region world that is currently controlled by the Empire. After the murder of the Blood Monarch and bombardment of the planet, the Empire enslaves most Thisspiasians and has been subduing its many rebel movements. The Thisspiasian crown prince has escaped Imperial captivity, and some now slip through the quarantine to fight for the Rebel Alliance.
csg_thisspiasian.description: Thisspiasians are snake-like creatures with a martial history who are fierce warriors. They have four arms and are extremely intimidating to most other sentients, especially considering their carnivorous diet.
csg_thisspiasian.sidebar_text: Though omnivorous, Thisspiasians prefer to eat live birds, rodents, and insects. For larger animals, they can unhinge their jaw. Typical meals have the animals caged at the center of the table before being dipped in seasonings and eaten whole. They have learned to change such tastes when around outsiders. Only reluctantly do they consume cooked food.

csg_tholothian.name: Tholothian
csg_tholothian.physiology: Tholothians are a near-human species. Their most notable distinction is that they live much longer than humans, so many are very wise. Visually, their skin is much darker and they have white tendrils protruding from their head. Their eyes are generally blue or indigo. Most females cover their hair in a traditional headdress. The species is very rare, but they do have an exceptionally high rate of Force-sensitivity.
csg_tholothian.society: Tholothians are a peaceful people known for having an elaborate system of social customs and traditions, which focus on forging and preserving strong connections with their family. They live in large groups of extended families, which all share a household, which ensures that Tholothians tend to know all of their distant relatives very well.
