Particular dates and times are assigned for people of different relations to bond in different ways: For example, families separate by generation on the first day of their eight-day week, with groups of siblings and cousins dining together. However, these large households never contain pets, a concept which they find inhumane. Because of their close community, few try to leave their homeworld, but those who do often try to transfer their community-focused mentality to friends and allies instead. Longing for family was a particular challenge for their many Jedi. A serene appearance does not come very naturally to them, and Tholothians are fond of expression, though their understanding of art is much more abstract than other species.
csg_tholothian.language: The Tholothian language of P’olothin is considered somewhat archaic and impractical, so it is mostly used in formal situations among their own. Otherwise, Basic is generally used by them.
csg_tholothian.homeworld: Tholoth is an urban world in the Colonies. Almost the entire population is contained in a single massive city, called Rossdoa, which has become relatively crowded. It has few resources and very poor soil for farming, so most of their economy is centered around academic fields or technological design. Imperial rule on Tholoth is relatively benign, as Tholothians look near-human enough and have caused little trouble.
csg_tholothian.description: The Tholothians are a near-human species known for their Force-sensitivity. They have extremely long lifespans, and that extra time often allows them to become very wise.
csg_tholothian.sidebar_text: Though Tholothians not raised among their people can be exceptions, many of them strictly follow several unwritten laws of conversation. Advice is considered valuable, and a wise quote is considered fair compensation for help, rather than “thank you,” which has no direct translation in their own language. When greeting, mutual bowing is common, regardless of status differences. A final one that occurs often is the tendency to always address an elder outside their family as “Dovosan,” a word from their own language.
csg_tholothian._provenance_note: The Tholothian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_tintinna.name: Tintinna

special_abilities.name: Digging Claws
special_abilities.description: Spend 2 maneuvers to tunnel through loose soil, moving 1 range band.

csg_tintinna.physiology: Tintinna, also known as Tin-Tin Dwarves or T’iin T’iin, are small rodents with brown, gray, or green fur and pink skin. They are biologically very similar to the Ranats, and they are bipedal, just under a meter tall on average, and they have a long tail as well as claws on their hands and feet which they use for digging. They have small ears and eyes, both of which are rather perceptive, and their face is also distinguished by a snout. Not unlike the Ranats, their teeth grow constantly, so they must chew on things often in order to keep them at a reasonable length.
csg_tintinna.society: Tintinna are quite friendly, unlike many other species of rodents. They are curious and amiable, and many of them enjoy exploring the galaxy or meeting new people. Because of this, those who explore the galaxy often find themselves on tramp freighters or otherwise involved with space travel. On their homeworld, they live in underground burrows that they dig manually, although a few farmers and traders live above the ground. They are divided into tribes, each of which is ruled by a chief and a shaman.
csg_tintinna.language: Tintinna typically speak Basic if they are found off of their homeworld.
csg_tintinna.homeworld: Tintinna come from a rural backwater planet called Rinn, which is the Baxel sector of the Outer Rim. They live in its mountains, and they typically build using only wood, although some offworlders have begun to mine on the planet. It is near Hutt Space, and because it has little government of any sort, it is a haven for smugglers. As such, most Tintinna who leave Rinn and explore the galaxy start their journey with a smuggler.
csg_tintinna.description: Tiny rodents who hail from a backwater world, the Tintinna are amiable and often enjoy exploring the galaxy. Their own technology is very lacking, but they can be surprisingly capable mechanics if given the chance.
csg_tintinna.sidebar_text: The technological skills of the Tintinna are unique, in that they have a knack for mechanics and technology, but their own society is relatively primitive. Prior to offworld contact, their world was no more advanced than using steam power. Even now, they are still fairly primitive on their homeworld, mostly working with wood and still delivering news by word of mouth. Those who see them often assume that they are non-sentient. However, Tintinna are indeed sentient, and they are completely capable of using and understanding advanced technology if they are given the chance.

csg_tissshar.name: Tiss’shar

special_abilities.name: Technical Skills
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Gearhead.”

special_abilities.name: Trustworthy
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Convincing Demeanor.”

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Claws and Teeth
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3. May spend 2 advantage to hit with teeth, gaining the Pierce 1 and Vicious 2 qualities.

csg_tissshar.physiology: Tiss’shar are carnivorous therapods who appear to be a very primitive species, but the bipedal reptilians are surprisingly intelligent. In addition to their keen mind, Tiss’shar boast excellent night vision, sharp teeth and claws, and capable strength despite their shorter stature. They have a long neck, a noticeable beak, and a tail for balance. Although their hands are four-fingered, they have just three toes on each foot. Most do not wear any clothing. Tiss-shar have fairly durable scales whose coloration is dependent on subspecies. Sil-ar have diamond markings behind their head, ask-ar have red facial markings, orl-ar are green with orange strikes on their back, nil-ar have red bands around their eyes, ankles, wrists, and tail, kal-ar have concentric bands, and isk-ar have white scales.
csg_tissshar.society: Tiss’shar are a focused people who are shrewd and efficient. In everything from business to recreation, they have a strong drive to succeed, but they are very detached. They plan their steps carefully and execute them with cold-blooded precision. They are highly successful entrepreneurs, generally focusing on the technology industry, but their businesses are unique in that employees get very little salary but very high benefits. Among the Tiss’shar, businesses pay for their employee’s housing, education, food, and health care. Their world is ruled by the most successful businessmen, who make up the Tiss’sharl League. Not all Tiss’shar have lost their more primitive instincts, so many are assassins. Tiss’shar are renowned as very professional assassins, and they honor their contracts to the letter. In Tiss’shar business and politics, assassination is very common.
csg_tissshar.language: Tiss’shar is a lispy language of hisses and shrieks, and most Tiss’shar also know Basic. They have a hyphenated name with three short parts.
csg_tissshar.homeworld: Tiss’shar come from Tiss’sharl, a rainforest world near the Corporate Sector. Their knack for business has brought many Tiss’shar to the Corporate Sector.
csg_tissshar.description: Bipedal reptiles with sharp claws and teeth, the Tiss'shar are focused and emotionless, carrying out business with cold precision. They have many subspecies, each of which is the most gifted in a certain area, but all display excellent technical skills.
csg_tissshar.sidebar_text: Unlike species such as the Aqualish, subspecies has little to do with status among the Tiss’shar, but each subspecies boasts a slightly different skillset. Sil-ar, the most common subspecies, are more likely to focus on business than other Tiss’shar, as are the kal-ar. The isk-ar are the most mechanically inclined, while the Tiss’shar’s reputation as excellent assassins comes mostly from the nil-ar. The most athletic of the bunch are the orl-ar and the ask-ar.

csg_tognath.name: Tognath

special_abilities.name: Cybernetic Enhancements
special_abilities.description: Receive free cybernetics that upgrade all Coordination and Perception checks. Count as 1 implant toward the cybernetic implant cap.

special_abilities.name: Atmospheric Requirement
special_abilities.description: Need a pressure suit and breath mask to breathe or speak in a normal environment. Receive a free pressure suit at character creation. Standard pressure with oxygen is a dangerous atmosphere of rating 5.

special_abilities.name: Underdeveloped Nerves
special_abilities.description: Add two setbacks when targeted by a Coercion check. Remove two setbacks for pain.

csg_tognath.physiology: Tognath are one of the more primitive sentient species in the galaxy. They have both insectoid and mammalian physiology, including an endoskeleton and an exoskeleton. Their sensory system is far less advanced than that of most other species, so to compensate, they use cybernetic implants to help them with hearing, sight, and coordination. Their ability to sense pain is also very weak, but this plays more to their advantage than anything, allowing them to fight through pain more easily. They also require a breathing apparatus and pressure suit on most planets, as they are adapted for a high density atmosphere rich in sulfur. Additionally, their voice is too low to be heard by most other species, so they require devices to raise its pitch. Their eggs grow in a suspension jelly, and they hatch in a larval state, and they feed directly off a parent’s bloodstream for six months before they enter a cocoon and undergo metamorphosis, emerging as a bipedal child.
csg_tognath.society: Not particularly amiable, the Tognath are an extremely quiet and secretive people, and they are renowned for their confidentiality. They focus almost exclusively on their career early in life, and only lay eggs once they retire, allowing them to raise their children very attentively. They live in homes on stilts over volcanic mountains, because the mountain region is the only one with access to fresh water. Most Tognath are miners, and a few are farmers on the plains, but some conduct the very dangerous and highly romanticised job of float farming. Float-jellies are massive, air-filled creatures that float around eating volcanic ash, and the secretions on their back create a rich soil which can grow prized fungi and mosses. The best float farmers are Egg Mates, because they can communicate very easily.
csg_tognath.language: Tognath speak in a very low voice and cannot be heard without an amplifier in their mask.
csg_tognath.homeworld: Tognath come from Yar-Togna, a volcanic planet with a high-pressure atmosphere full of fumes. Violent fault lines create rare compounds that are valuable to mine, so the Empire nationalized the industries and enslaved the Tognath. Even those who escape Yar-Togna resent the Empire, because they cannot nurture their larvae without Yar-Togna’s nurseries.
csg_tognath.description: Possessing both mammalian and insectoid physiology, the Tognath cannot breathe or speak in a normal atmosphere, and their senses are dulled, making them less vulnerable to pain. They keep to themselves, and most of them are miners.
csg_tognath.sidebar_text: Sometimes, two or even three eggs from the same clutch fuse while in suspension jelly, and although they separate once they hatch, resulting larvae form a very close emotional bond. The term for this cannot be properly translated, but the closest term for it is “egg mates.” Depending on when they fused, some egg mates have a very weak telepathic bond, allowing them to sense each other’s emotions and location as long as they are within a few hundred meters.
csg_tognath._provenance_note: The Tognath species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU.

csg_togorian.name: Togorian

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_togorian.physiology: The Togorians are a species of predatory feline creatures who have sharp claws and are very tough. This combination makes many of them work in combat-oriented jobs, a role that they excel in. While the females aren’t much larger than humans, the males can grow from two and half meters to three meters tall. They have black, brown, white, or gray fur covering their entire body, which is sometimes striped. They have four fingers and three toes, all of which are clawed. Their head is elongated forward at the mouth, chin and nose. They are further distinguished by green eyes, whiskers, sharp teeth, pointed ears, and a black nose.
csg_togorian.society: Togorians believe in survival of the fittest, and they are always ruling by the strongest member. They are merciless, crushing opposition with no regrets. Males find face-to-face combat to be honorable, although they do not always extend this courtesy to non-Togorians. Togorian society is completely separated by gender, as the males and females are too stubborn to agree on a way of life. The males live as nomadic hunters, using their fierce strength and natural claws to hunt and survive. They have progressed little, as most dislike technology. The females have chosen a safer style of life, being sedentary farmers for both crops and livestock. Now, they are demanding negotiators who are quite clever and value material possessions. Many enjoy access to luxury goods. With these differences, even mates see each other just one month per year. The males are more isolated, trading very little and hating outsiders. While females trade out of necessity, most still don’t trust outsiders.
csg_togorian.language: Togorians have a harsh-sounding language called Togorian. Most females know Basic.
csg_togorian.homeworld: Togoria is the Mid Rim planet which is home to the Togorians. It contains plains, forests, and hills. Outsiders are only allowed in the capital city, Caross. The planet has allied with the Confederacy and is now showing support for the Rebel Alliance.
csg_togorian.description: Togorians are so stubborn that when males and females couldn’t agree between a hunter-gatherer lifestyle or one of a sedentary farmer, the two genders split and only come together to mate. They are dangerous feline predators with sharp claws.
csg_togorian.sidebar_text: While their natural instincts put them in a good position to be deadly warriors, the people that they have interacted with have also brought them down that path. Early in their history, they were unsuccessfully invaded by Mandalorian Neo-Crusaders. However, the Mandalorians were so impressed by the Togorians’ skills in defending their planet that they recruited them. Many of the Mandalorian Togorians never returned home after the defeat of the Neo-Crusaders, returning to Mandalore or becoming mercenaries, bounty hunters, or pirates. Many of their descendants still work in those jobs.

csg_togruta.name: Togruta

special_abilities.name: Pack Instincts
special_abilities.description: When performing the assist maneuver, grant 2 boosts instead of 1.

csg_togruta.physiology: Togrutas are a carnivorous species of mammals who prefer to eat their prey live. It is commonly misconceived that their incisors are venomous, a myth they rarely bother to correct. They have skin that tends to be red or orange but can stray towards yellow or purple. They naturally have white pigmentation forming stripes all over their body and face, an adaptation to blend in with the grass of their home. The patterns do vary slightly by individual. They have gray lips and eyes of all sorts of colors. Aside from color, the only obvious visual difference between Togruta and humans is their montrals, which they have instead of hair. Looking somewhat similar to Twi’lek lekku, these head-tails are colored in a pattern of white and blue stripes. Two short ones spike upward, while three long ones extend down, two in front over their chest, and one down their back. For adults, the montrals extend down to waist level, but young Togrutas have shorter ones. They act as ultrasonic sensors, allowing them to sense the space around them via echolocation.
csg_togruta.society: Togrutas value teamwork, unity, and togetherness. Since most creatures on their homeworld are fellow pack animals, they need to work together to beat such numbers. Some Togrutas have a hard time fulfilling personal goals, since they focus on the needs of their group. They tend to be peaceful and quiet but still long for companionship, especially with fellow Togrutas. While some can get along excellently with other cultures, many struggle with feelings of loneliness if they enter the wider galaxy. They can be clingier friends than most other species are used to. They have a spiritual connection to the land bolstered by their ability to sense the environmental space. One way that they follow this is by not wearing shoes, so they do not break the bond between them and the ground. They wear many teeth and pelts of animals that they kill, especially the dangerous predator called akul, if they can kill one unassisted.
csg_togruta.language: Togrutas are typically fully fluent in Basic, although some may use rather strange metaphors and expressions from their native tongue, Togruti.
csg_togruta.homeworld: Togrutas come from Shili, a temperate world in the Ehosiq Sector. They hunt herbivores such as thimiar in the scrublands while sleeping and living in forest canopies. Most still survive with this primitive lifestyle.
csg_togruta.description: Togruta are mammals with strong instincts for working together and living in packs. When not among their own people, they are typically extremely lonely. They are near-humans who scan sense via echolocation in their montrals.
csg_togruta.sidebar_text: In their tightly knit communities, Togruta distribute food and resources equally to everyone. In exchange for this, everyone is expected to do their part and fulfill the role that they have been given. Even young children are quickly given weapons to join on hunts. Considering it to be nature’s way, Togruta packs break ties with those who fail, and they are left behind to fend for themselves. Not only is it dangerous for those Togrutas who are left behind, but such events have a great psychological impact on any Togruta that this happens to. Those continuing on feel little remorse, as they see the abandonment only as an inevitable result of nature.

csg_toong.name: Toong

special_abilities.name: Social Anxiety
special_abilities.description: No more than once per session, the GM may trigger a social anxiety attack, and the character becomes terrified of a particular social encounter. If this occurs, cannot say anything more than basic pleasantries for the rest of the encounter without passing an average fear check. May spend 5 XP during or after character creation to remove this penalty.

csg_toong.physiology: Toong are odd fellows, yellow-colored creatures with long limbs, a tiny body, and a huge head. Their head has three protrusions similar to antennae, pointing upward as sensory organs. At the top of their face are small but wide eyes which surround an equally small nose. Below it, their head widens into large cheek pouches which store food before thinning down into a diamond shape with a jowled chin.
csg_toong.society: Toong society is mostly peaceful, and although Toong can get along well, they are often terrified of social interaction. (Or, at the very least, do not enjoy it.) Though not widely known enough to severely hinder them, it is no secret that the Toong will almost always give in when in an argument. While they can get along with others, they really only feel safe when with family. They also are often afraid of large open spaces, and they have only very reluctantly travelled off of their homeworld to explore the galaxy. Despite these challenges, one Toong, the podracer Ben Quadinaros, managed to achieve significant fame in his sport.
csg_toong.language: Toong speak Toongese and Basic and are known to stutter nervously in both.
csg_toong.homeworld: Toong’L is the actual Toong homeworld, though it was hit by a poisonous comet in 45 BBY. Since it is now barren, many Toong now come from Tund. Tund is in the Centrality and has a long history of ancient civilizations such as the Sharu and Rakata. It is a world strong in the Dark Side as well, home to cults of outcast Sorcerers. While once lush and beautiful, the final Sorcerer of Tund badly damaged the planet via an electromagnetic torpedo. It is now nearly permanently poisoned by radiation, and none inhabit it. The surviving Toong have again been dispersed.
csg_toong.description: Toong are creatures with a massive head that have came into the galaxy to flee disaster on their homeworld. They are absolutely terrified of any form of social interaction, and they avoid arguments at any cost.
csg_toong.sidebar_text: The Toong first had their only world war triggered by a surprising event: first contact with the rest of the galaxy. Shocked by the existence of other sentients and superior technology, the Toong homeworld somehow plunged into war from it. It took intervention from Jedi and a first contact specialist to save the species. Luck would have it that the Toong weren’t in the clear yet, however. A poisonous comet collided with their world, devastating it. In addition to the many deaths, it also caused mass immigration to the nearby planet Tund. Tund suffered a catastrophic event of its own during the time of the Empire.

csg_toydarian.name: Toydarian

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 2.

csg_toydarian.physiology: Toydarians are small creatures who fly via the wings on their back and the light gases in their inflated belly. Their skin ranges in shades of teal to pink, and it usually is more cream-colored on their stomach. Their face is best distinguished by a small wrinkled trunk surrounded by a pair of tusks protruding up from their wide mouth. Their thin arms and legs have three fingers and three webbed toes. Their legs have two knees each, though they are rarely used thanks to their preference for flying, which they are capable of even immediately after birth. Because Toydarians burn plenty of energy with their rapid flapping of their wings, they constantly need food and eat in large quantities whenever possible. While they mostly rely on high-energy processed goods to fill their needs, ancient times saw them fight over food very often. This metabolism also gives them a pleasant odor, similar to sweetspice. The Toydarian brain, though similar in structure to most other species, is strangely immune to any manipulation by the Force.
csg_toydarian.society: Toydarians were subjugated by the Hutts long ago, yet they are shrewd and have fared well compared to other slave species. Their standard of living increased under Hutt rule, and it ended up being, for all intents and purposes, a business merger. It has allowed them to keep their distance from government oversight in the rest of the galaxy, protecting their often unsavory financial interests. They still mostly live in Hutt space, working under the kajidics. They generally tend to be good at interacting with people but still capable when it comes to betrayals or thievery. This makes them excellent in many roles for their Hutt masters, such as accounting, business managing, or even serving as majordomos. Many also choose to trade elsewhere, carving out a niche for themselves and going to work as merchants or traders. Bargaining is ingrained deeply into their society, so these negotiations come naturally to them. However, they are fond of risk and can be overly ambitious in their businesses. While physical combat does not come naturally to them, in times of famine, their confederacies have been known to fight vindictive wars over their food supplies.
csg_toydarian.language: Toydarian is their native tongue, but Hutt rule has ensured that almost all Toydarians know Huttese. Still, the Toydarians are enterprising as ever, so most learn Basic to interact with any human customers.
csg_toydarian.homeworld: Toydaria is a swampy world in Hutt space whose space traffic is highly limited to avoid collisions with the Toydarians themselves. It is full of muck and mud, with both insects and algae found in large quantities. These aren’t the only bad things about Toydaria, either. Monsoons are common, fungi of all types break out as plagues, and the grabworms are dangerous carnivores. The boggy terrain is generally unsafe to set foot on, aside from the sparse algal mats, which are relatively safer. Regardless, the Toydarians place great pride in their home planet.
csg_toydarian.description: Toydarians are chubby creatures to get around by hovering. They are ruled by the Hutts, but they have thrived under the crime lords thanks to their business skills. They use scheming naturally as a way to separate the clever from the foolish.
csg_toydarian.sidebar_text: Toydarians have a feudal society ruled by a king, but there are plenty of other nobles to bicker over the other roles. These lower vassals are often quite wealthy, and they constantly scheme against one another to earn the king’s favor. The king keeps an extremely close eye on it, viewing the competition as an important and practical way to separate the strong from the weak and the clever from the foolish. Most Toydarians take to the intrigue effortlessly, and it teaches their society to value wealth and power.

csg_trandoshan.name: Trandoshan

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

special_abilities.name: Infrared Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness.

special_abilities.name: Regeneration
special_abilities.description: When recovering 1 or more wounds through natural rest or a bacta tank, recover 1 additional wound. May also regrow lost limbs after a few months.

csg_trandoshan.physiology: Generally about two meters tall, Trandoshans (referred to as T’doshok in their own language) are cold-blooded reptiles. Their scales, which they shed annually, vary greatly in color, with shades generally including olive, brown, or ochre. They have three-fingered hands and three-toed feet, all of which end in spiked claws. They generally don’t fit into shoes, and their lack of thumbs means that they have some difficulties when using technology like blasters, but many can make up for it with focused training and specialized equipment. Their vermillion eyes are keenly sensitive and also boast infrared vision, and they can heal much more effectively than most, even regrowing limbs. Their face is distinctive for its maw of sharp teeth and a forked tongue, and they also have small spikes instead of hair. Trandoshans reproduce by laying clutches of four eggs, and these eggs must be kept warm until they hatch. Even just after birth, they can walk and have basic hunting instincts.
csg_trandoshan.society: Trandoshan society is competitive, focused on strength, hunting skills, self-reliance, and resilience. Their children are raised by their mother, and hunting with her at age two and independent at age ten. Most go on to become bounty hunters or big-game hunters, but a few rebels take different paths that they consider as hunts, such as “hunting” for scientific answers or product designs. All hunts are judged by providing jagganath points, or “divine marks,” based on their difficulty. Humiliation can cause a Trandoshan to lose all of their jagganath points, which they can earn back by getting revenge. At the end of their life, their deity, a female named Scorekeeper, tallies the jagganath to determine their status in the afterlife. Jagganath points are the means by which Trandoshan females judge potential mates, but males rarely remain in the home for long after the eggs have been laid.
csg_trandoshan.language: The Trandoshan language of Dosh sounds to humans as a series of hisses and snarls. Trandoshans are also capable of speaking Basic in a low hissing voice.
csg_trandoshan.homeworld: The Trandoshan’s homeworld is known as Hsskhor, but in Basic it is referred to as Trandosha. It shares a star system with Kashyyyk, the forested Wookiee homeworld. It is a sun-baked, mountainous, and arid world, but the Trandoshans generally prefer to stick to its coastlands, where they can hunt Dosian jellyfish, their favorite food. The gravity is exceptionally low at 62% standard, and it has a highly elliptical orbit that gives it harsh planetwide seasonal extremes.
csg_trandoshan.description: The arch-nemesis of the Wookiees, Trandoshans are reptilian hunters who focus their lives on hunting to please their goddess, Scorekeeper. They are an effective combination of physical strength, sharp claws, and regenerative abilities.
csg_trandoshan.sidebar_text: Trandoshans have long been at odds with the Wookiees, a species that shares their star system. Quite strangely, they do share one aspect of culture: the life debt. Like Wookiees, Trandoshans will pledge service to anyone who saves their life. However, the two species have constantly feuded ever since Wookiees brutally murdered a Trandoshan scouting party on Kashyyyk. Retaliatory raids by Trandoshans have often sparked further wars, and the Old Republic sided with the Wookiees time and time again. Their world has faced economic sanctions as a result. Emperor Palpatine finally listened to the Trandoshans, allowing them to represent their own system in the Senate and buying Wookiee slaves from them. Most Trandoshans will be happy with this arrangement until the New Republic comes to power and demands the Trandoshans leave the Wookiees alone.

csg_trianii.name: Trianii

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: When using claws, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3. Add boost on checks to climb.

special_abilities.name: Prehensile Tails
special_abilities.description: May carry 1 object of up to 3 encumbrance with tail that doesn’t count towards encumbrance threshold. May not use tail to fire blasters.

csg_trianii.physiology: Trianii are slender felines with short fur that can come in many colors and patterns. The males are smaller and weaker than most other species, but females are average in build. Both boast sharp claws and a prehensile tail, which assist them in combat. Their face is distinctly feline, with pointed ears, glowing eyes, and whiskers. Trianii rarely wear clothing unless it is necessary to protect them or carry gear.
csg_trianii.society: Trianii are a very individualistic and curious people, and they are stubborn when it comes to achieving their goals. They don’t easily submit to authority and generally prefer to be left alone. Such attitudes are reflected in their politics, as they have warded off all attempts to annex them by the CSA thanks to the Trianii Rangers, an elite force devoted to policing and defending the Trianii’s sector of space. They have refused to join all major galactic governments, and live in their own isolated region of space. Trianii are a very technologically advanced society, and they are highly intelligent. Mostly because of their superior strength, the females rule the Trianii. Their government is mostly composed of local, all-female tribunals known as yu’nar.
csg_trianii.language: Trianii speak Trianii, a language with growls and purrs, and their written language has characters for each syllable.
csg_trianii.homeworld: Trianii come from Trian, a world just north of the Corporate Sector, and they have many nearby colonies. Trianii space is mostly isolated.
csg_trianii.description: Trianii are fur-covered felines with claws and a prehensile tail, and the males are smaller and weaker than most species. They are adept at using technology, but they have taken an isolationist stance as a result of their preference to be without authority.
csg_trianii.sidebar_text: Trianii are an extremely spiritual people, but their differing beliefs nearly lead to a holy war. Thousands of different religions were a problem for a Trianii, so many of their leaders got together to discuss one unifying religion that all could agree on. Now, all Trianii believe in the same common principles, but they also believe in their traditional religions, which tend to focus on minor details. Such traditional religions are numerous, with each tradition held by only a few families. Spirituality is important in all aspects of a Trianii’s life, including business, art, and recreation.

csg_triffian.name: Triffian

special_abilities.name: Thermoregulator Flaps
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Webbed Feet
special_abilities.description: Remove all movement penalties for being underwater.

csg_triffian.physiology: As expected for creatures who are just over a meter tall, the Triffians are nimble but weak, though they are hardy for their size. They tend to be chubbier with a tail extending from their abdomen between their legs. In order to swim, they have digitigrade webbed feet, and they have flaps extending from the neck which they use to release extra heat. Their skin is usually a mix of two shades: Creamy yellow or white dominates the stomach, hands and around the eyes, while a shade of blue or gray covers their tail, neck, forehead, and sides. They have hair in shades of blue, brown, and gray on their back and on their thermoregulator flaps, and they usually do not wear clothing. Their visage is dominated by a thin, pointed snout, and they have yellow or lime eyes above their pointed nostrils.
csg_triffian.society: Triffians are an affluent, aristocratic people who have built an efficient, well-organized network of droids that handles almost all of the manual labor on Triffis. They have a reputation for being somewhat lazy, usually working part time in a white-collar office job. The powerful in their society are the business owners, who are called “katriomik.” (Singular katriomi) These businesses have lasted for hundreds of generations, and the katriomi gives ownership to their oldest child when they die. The katriomi is expected to supply the needs of their entire family, and in exchange, their family does whatever work is needed. This structure means that Triffians who dislike their family cannot simply get jobs elsewhere, because all businesses only hire family members. Triffians can only enter another family by marriage, with the younger spouse joining the older spouse’s family. Because of this structure, Triffians offworld are incredibly loyal to their employers, and they think of coworkers like family members. At work, they also value delegation and organization to the extreme. To them, doing something means figuring out who the best candidate for the job is and convincing them to do it. In the free time that they’re left with, Triffians tend to become very well-read, and many are aficionados for the fine arts such as opera, painting, and sculpture.
csg_triffian.language: Pretty much every family on Triffis speaks a unique dialect or a unique language. Being a well-educated people, Triffians are expected to learn Basic as well as Okioli, which is the lingua franca of Triffis.
csg_triffian.homeworld: Triffis is a world of steamy bogs in the Mid Rim. It is known for a distinct architecture with organic curves and bright colors which is present in huge, ancient buildings. Factory floors, storefronts, and warehouses take up the lower levels, while the family who owns it lives directly above in the same building. These tall, multipurpose buildings are compact, leaving plenty of space for gardens and ponds even in the cities.
csg_triffian.description: The Triffians are quick little creatures, and their society is affluent and a bit lazy. They prefer to organize rather than act, and most of their businesses are family operations.
csg_triffian.sidebar_text: Triffis is dominated by old money passed down through generations, but there are some who want to make their own living. Starting a business on Triffis is almost impossible because the only way to hire a non-family member is to marry them into the family. Countless Triffians take their entrepreneurial ambitions offworld, but they often struggle with the long hours and non-family employees. As such, investors are very skeptical of Triffian businesses.
csg_triffian._provenance_note: The Triffian species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_trodatome.name: Trodatome

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: No Arms
special_abilities.description: May not hold any objects with encumbrance greater than Brawn.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn when on land.

csg_trodatome.physiology: Trodatome are large semi-aquatic creatures with a smooth tan body. They have no limbs, although they have four sensory antennae on either side of their head which are prehensile. Their face is composed of two bulbous eyestalks which extrude slightly from the top of their head, and a mouth with a split upper lip which allows them to speak their complex language. This face is mounted on a large muscular trunk which undulates, allowing them to propel themselves by tensing and relaxing their muscles. This allows them to better walk using their legless flippers. One can often hear a Trodatome coming by the flopping of their flippers against the ground.
csg_trodatome.society: Trodatome are deeply principled and full of integrity, eager to call out injustices in the galaxy. However, they can be less eager when it comes to acting out these beliefs and are often flustered once troubles arrive. Trodatome morality is rooted in their religion, Oko-Ugo, which worships the deities Otet (god of the past) and Ubem (god of the future). This unique system of belief ensures that they are reflective while also dreamers, though often at the expense of being in the present. They view history and archeology as an act of worship, and they also see planning and preparing as a godly endeavor. Just as their gods form a diad, Trodatome also value marriage as a similar union. They have more gender distinction than humans, with females thinking very abstractly and often being future-oriented. Males think in more concrete ways and are extremely reflective. Homosexuality is strictly forbidden, as both male and female are necessary to form a complementary pair.
csg_trodatome.language: Trodatome speak a language of the same name which is mostly made up of complex atonal yells and hums. It is almost impossible to speak without their split upper-lip. Conversely, they are unable to create the sounds required to speak Basic.
csg_trodatome.homeworld: Trodatome come from the Outer Rim planet Follok Prime, a tropical world which is four fifths ocean. Almost all the land on the planet is made up of sandy beaches, with most vegetation being moss and algae. They use algae to create a highly buoyant material on which they build their modest tethered cities.
csg_trodatome.description: Armless slugs with aquatic heritage, the Trodatome are intelligent and mechanically gifted despite theri physiological limitations. They are deeply principled beings with a religion that emphasizes a balance between past reflection and future planning, often at the expense of their present circumstance.
csg_trodatome.sidebar_text: Trodatome, despite their lack of useful gripping appendages, have made a name for themselves throughout the galaxy as skilled repairmen. Using the tools they can hold using their antennae, even inexperienced Trodatome are able to deftly repair a hyperdrive fairly easily. This confounds and attracts people from all over the galaxy who seek out Trodatome as ship mechanics, or simply to chuckle to themselves while watching them work.
csg_trodatome._provenance_note: The Trodatome species originates from Disney Canon, but can fit into the EU. Almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_troig.name: Troig

special_abilities.name: Multiple Heads
special_abilities.description: Must be attached to one other Troig character. The two can act as separate individuals in terms of personality, stats, actions, initiative order, and critical injuries. They share a wound threshold, which is the average of their two wound thresholds. They must always remain in the same location, only moving when both spend a maneuver to move in the same direction. They may communicate telepathically with each other.

csg_troig.physiology: Troigs are very unique in that they have two (or, in rare cases, more) heads, each of which can act as an independent being to an extent. The heads have separate personalities and often argue with each other. Separation via surgery is possible, but at least one head is always killed. The heads do have telepathic communication with each other, and they typically share most knowledge. Their heads, both atop long necks, are roughly conical. Some have hair, horns, or both. They also vary in that some have tentacles and the back of their craniums. They all have prominent brows, and their skin can come in many colors. Often, each side of the body is a different color. They have a tail that ends in a spiky lump and an egg-shaped chest. Their legs are spread far apart and have no feet. Each head has control over two arms, but only one of the four arms is dominant. Most Troigs do not wear any clothing.
csg_troig.society: Troigs are typically outgoing and curious. They can focus on a number of occupations, but they are especially good at those that require social skills. Their ability to multitask also helps with many industries, even though they lack advanced technology. They are often enthralled by a desire to leave home and explore the galaxy, such as AndroosinLiann, who hosted a popular talk show called Essence.
csg_troig.language: Troigs are talented linguists, and if one head knows a language, both know it. Their unique physiology creates many unique grammatical rules. First, they typically refer to the two heads in the singular as one body. They also combine names of each head by putting the infix “sin” in between them.
csg_troig.homeworld: Troigs come from Pollillus, a world in the western part of the Core Worlds near the Koornacht cluster. It was discovered relatively recently, shortly before the Battle of Naboo. Despite its isolated location, many Troigs are able to leave Pollillus and explore.
csg_troig.description: The Troigs have two heads, and each head displays a moderate level of independence from the other. This makes them excellent multitaskers, and they are also a very outgoing people who are charismatic and adept in social situations.
csg_troig.sidebar_text: The individuality of the heads is up for debate. They each think independently and have separate personalities, but they have a telepathic connection and almost always work together. However, this isn’t always the case, and that sometimes brings about moral conundrums. One head can sometimes exhibit extreme mental illnesses while the other is unaffected, which may make it necessary to separate heads and kill one of the Troigs. The left head, known as the Saprah, is typically more emotional, while the right, called the Saprin, is more logical. Rarely, there are Troigs with three or more heads, and they are often revered as celebrities.

csg_tunroth.name: Tunroth

special_abilities.name: Quarry Sense
special_abilities.description: Once per session, when tracking a quarry, may make a hard Perception, Streetwise, or Survival check. Which of those skills is chosen by the GM based on circumstances. May reduce difficulty to average for targets who are known about. If successful, get a general sense of the direction that the target is in.

csg_tunroth.physiology: The Tunroth are strong creatures who are natural hunters. They have two opposable thumbs on each hand with one central digit. Their feet are similar to that. They have tough, brown skin. They have an elongated, hairless skull that slopes backward. Their head also has sunken, black eyes and a mouth full of fangs. They have no nose. They have four spikes on their lower jaw, which they often replicate in their clothing. Tunroth skin is leathery and can come in various colors. Normally, it is dark brown or yellow, but a rarer race has orange skin. They have natural instincts as hunters, which combine to make what they refer to as quarry sense. Through quarry sense, they have an uncanny ability to know what general direction a target has gone.
csg_tunroth.society: Tunroth value hunting above all else. It is a profession, a way of life, a hobby, and even a spirituality. Children learn to hunt from their parents at a very early age before they typically become hunters themselves. They intimidate many other sentients because of their aggressiveness and confidence. The latter comes from their generally optimistic outlook. The Tunroth are also very determined and hard-working. They have faced near-extinction when they were attacked by the Lortans, but help from the Galactic Empire has allowed them to survive. They are still fairly primitive in terms of technology. Most fight with bows or melee weapons.
csg_tunroth.language: Tunroth speak Tunrothese, a simple language of grunts. Many can speak Basic, although few are literate in it.
csg_tunroth.homeworld: Tunroth come from the Jiroch system in the Mid Rim, where they live mostly on three planets. These planets are Jiroch-Reslia, Kalok, and Salok.
csg_tunroth.description: Tunroth are almost entirely devoted to hunting and boast the uncanny ability known as quarry sense. They are confident and aggressive, mostly working with bows and swords.
csg_tunroth.sidebar_text: While almost all Tunroth are hunters in one way or another, not all belong to the Tunroth Hunters. This group does include a fairly large percent of Tunroth, however. The Tunroth Hunters are an elite organization, joining it requires a three month rite. They are judged by hunting prowess as well as character. It is composed of 27 levels, and all Tunroth seek to increase their level. The highest level, Stiilran, has not been achieved for millennia, however. The three members who have the highest levels, known as the Assemblage of the Three, govern the Tunroth and lead the organization. Tunroth Hunters are often sent offworld as bounty hunters.

csg_tusken_raider.name: Tusken Raider

special_abilities.name: Desert Dwellers
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot or dry conditions, add setback for cold or wet conditions.

csg_tusken_raider.physiology: Precious little is known about the physiology of the Tusken Raiders. While a few are kidnapped humans assimilated into the culture, most Tuskens are a species of their own. They are almost always covered in robes, including their hands and feet, and their visage is bandaged or helmeted with a primitive breath mask and goggles protecting their eyes. Their hobbled-together scraps of clothing are tightly held together by leather belts of dewback hide. For all the curiosity surrounding Tuskens, few have had the opportunity to find out. They are known to be humanoid in stature, though stronger, and they also are more resistant to the heat than most species.
csg_tusken_raider.society: Tusken ways are brutal and violent, doing whatever is necessary to survive. This includes covering all skin to protect from heat and preserve moisture. They clean their body in the privacy of their tents, and only show themselves to their mate. To do otherwise is punishable by death. They are organized into clans of 20 to 30, with each clan living a nomadic life together through the desert. Having few possessions of any kind, they do not produce technology of their own, and they tend to be afraid of foreign devices. Although some have become familiar with stolen cycler rifles, their preferred weapon is the gaderffii, an ax-like weapon made from scavenged metals. Tusken children are known as Uli-ah, before they go through rites of adulthood at fifteen years old. This ritual can include travelling with only their bantha into the wilderness or completing a “bloodrite,” where they capture a creature and torture it to death over the course of weeks. The most skilled do it on humans, while others do it against dewbacks or hulak wraids. They form extremely close bonds with the massive furry banthas that they ride in single-file lines, and riders whose mounts die before them generally banish themselves into the wilderness to die alone.
csg_tusken_raider.language: Tuskens have a guttural language called Tusken. It has no written form, and none speak Basic.
csg_tusken_raider.homeworld: Tuskens come from the desert world of Tatooine. It is a backwater Outer Rim world with twin suns. In addition to Tuskens, there are diverse criminals, timid Jawas, and moisture farmers. Moisture farmers and Jawas both fear the Tuskens, who often raid them for food, supplies, or sentient prisoners. On other occasions, the farmers have moved to wipe out the Tuskens, who have retreated deeper into the desert.
csg_tusken_raider.description: Primitive and mysterious humanoids who lurk in the Tatooine wilderness, Tuskens are extremely brutal and have tense relations with nearby scavengers and farmers.
csg_tusken_raider.sidebar_text: Tusken history is entirely oral, passed down through a single member who is known as the storyteller. The storyteller can recite their history in perfect accuracy, though the ordeal is more than an hour long. Reciting even a single word incorrectly in the history is punishable by death, so only the storytellers will ever say it. Even apprentice storytellers are not allowed to practice, only listening until they are confident they can recite it fully. The histories include accounts of the coming-of-age rites for each clan member, as well as a mythology that tells how Tatooine’s two suns have been cursed, one for blasphemy by revealing his face, the other for failing to punish his brother’s sin.

csg_twilek.name: Twi’lek

special_abilities.name: Desert Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for dark, hot, or dry conditions, add setback for bright, cold, or wet conditions.

csg_twilek.physiology: Twi’leks are a species of near-humans distinguished by their head-tails, called lekku or tchin and tchun, and skin that can come in every color of the rainbow. These colors indicate ancestry, region of birth, and clan. Their lekku project from the top of their head and droop downwards, and they are partially prehensile, able to be moved as a form of silent communication. The lekku also are used for memory. Male Twi’leks have human-like ears, but females have small conical protrusions instead. They are otherwise near-human in appearance. Their eyes, while appearing quite human-like, boast above-average night vision.
csg_twilek.society: Twi’leks tend to value their family above all else, and they are organized into clans. Their government is an alliance of head clans, which each control a small town or region of a larger city. Each head clan is ruled by the five most important male Twi’leks in them, and the power is given based on influence or bloodline as opposed to voting by merit. Tradition states that when one of the five leaders in a head clan dies, the other four are exiled into the dangerous, sun baked, Bright Lands, where vicious lyleks prowl. Although some clever Twi’leks find ways around these exiles, it is generally the case that an entirely new generation takes power all at once. The clan system also leaves a vulnerable lower caste. These individuals of unfortunate bloodline are used as fodder in the slave trade by their own clans. While any Twi’lek leader would publicly deny accusations of slavery, shifting blame to other clans, almost all of them sell out lower-class citizens in “contracted indenturehood.” Such is their way, remaining loyal to immediate family but surprisingly sly and corrupt when dealing with others. Charming yet shrewd, they make natural businessmen. Their technology is limited, with windmills harvesting energy from vicious heat storms that power their agrarian society. They have no spacecraft of their own and are dependent on unsavory visitors if they want to go offworld.
csg_twilek.language: Twi’leks speak Ryl, yet they are skilled linguists, and almost all of them also know Basic. The more special language of the Twi’leks is Lekku, or Twi’leki. Using subtle movements of their lekku, they can add emphasis to everyday speech. In some cases, they choose to rely entirely on Lekku, communicating in perfect silence.
csg_twilek.homeworld: Twi’leks come from the Outer Rim world of Ryloth just south of Hutt Space. It is plagued by slavers, spice dealers, and crime lords because it is the source of a spice called ryll. Ryloth is tidally locked, with the day side called the Bright Lands and the night side called the Nightlands. Fierce winds encircle the planet, and unpredictable heat storms can occur in the Bright Lands. Most of society is in the temperate twilight band, and they often live underground or in cities carved into the mountains. The surface is rocky and mountainous with a thin atmosphere.
csg_twilek.description: Colorful near-humans with head-tails called lekku, the Twi'leks are often seen as attractive to others. Despite their social skills, they have been unable to escape oppression from the Hutts: Many are now slaves.
csg_twilek.sidebar_text: Twi’lek dance is considered to be among the best art forms in the galaxy, and it is graceful and sensual. However, this has tragically resulted in many becoming slave dancers. Despite this, there are Twi’leks who began a path to success that all started when the slave trade first forced them off of Ryloth. Twi’leks of the lower caste are never truly safe from slavery, and many try to flee Ryloth out of fear that their leaders would eventually sell them off. Twi’lek women in particular are common targets for the slave trade, as they are seen as subservient afterthoughts.

csg_tynnan.name: Tynnan

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_tynnan.physiology: Small mammals of aquatic ancestry, the Tynnans have thick, brown fur that protects them from frigid waters. Although they once used their long teeth to create dams for homes, they no longer do this, and their buckteeth have been becoming shorter and shorter with each generation. Their head also features a snout, on which are whiskers and a black nose. Their eyes are small, and they often need ocular enhancers, but they have large ears that hear very well. They are excellent swimmers with webbed hands, webbed feet, and a tail. They can hold their breath for a very long time, and many spend a majority of their time in the water. Although they are often less than one and a half meters tall, they are fit and surprisingly strong for their size. Because of their fur, most Tynnans do not wear clothing. However, most have pouches or belts to carry things.
csg_tynnan.society: Tynnans are a very patient people of careful planners who are detail-oriented and prepare for everything. They are enthusiastic in carrying out these plans, but they lack such enthusiasm over religion- they are too pragmatic for such beliefs. Politically, they joined the Confederacy of Independent Systems during the Clone Wars and have stood up to the Empire. Although they pay some taxes to the Empire, their formidable defenses have prevented a complete Imperial takeover. However, such defenses will not be effective enough when the Yuuzhan Vong invasion targets their planet.
csg_tynnan.language: Tynnans speak their native language of Tynnan, and they are also capable of speaking Basic.
csg_tynnan.homeworld: Tynnans come from the wealthy Expansion Region world of Tynna, which is an important business partner to the Corporate Sector. It is arboreal, cold, and full of many seas and lakes. The environment is very well-protected, and it is considered to be a beautiful planet by many. The population, mostly Tynnan, is relatively small, as it has less than one billion residents.
csg_tynnan.description: Small mammals covered by thick fur, the Tynnans are adapted to icy waters. They are patient and detail-oriented, but they have such a wealthy economy that they no longer need to work.
csg_tynnan.sidebar_text: The Tynnan government is essentially socialist, as all industrial profits are taken by the government and given to society. They preserve the environment carefully and are surprisingly wealthy, so there is enough money for the government to pay everyone the cost of living. Most incredibly, they are not required to work, and they have a great deal of free time to devote to sports such as water wall or other hobbies such as travelling. Even more strange about their government is that anyone can be forced into political service via a random lottery. Although Tynnans are typically well-informed in political affairs because of this, not all wish to govern. Such Tynnans typically have no choice other than fleeing the planet or entering politics for one year.

csg_tsurr.name: T’surr

special_abilities.name: Four Eyes
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness. Add boost on all Ranged-Light, Ranged-Heavy, and Gunnery checks.

csg_tsurr.physiology: T’surr males are giants, generally about two and a half meters tall, and they are extremely strong. Incredibly strong and thickly built, the T’surr are made even more intimidating by the crown of long horns and lipless mouth full of sharp teeth. Female T’surr lack the horns, and they are also much smaller in stature than the males, making them far less intimidating. For all T’surr, their four eyes are small, red, and see well in the dark, and they also have excellent hearing. The extra eyes give them great depth perception, which is highly advantageous when using blasters. Their blue skin has a shine similar to marble. They have three-fingered hands as well as a pair of smaller arms with pincers at the end, but these extra arms are so small that they are virtually useless.
csg_tsurr.society: Forged by the harsh living conditions on their homeworld, T’surr are as heartless as anyone. They are absolutely ruthless rulers, and almost all are slavers, pirates, or both. They view all other species like livestock, and they do the same to their own kind if given the opportunity. As dangerous as they may be, they are extremely few in number, so they have not achieved as much infamy as other slavers. They make little technology of their own, but they can capably use the technology that they steal and often keep trophies. However, in the eyes of the T’surr, no amount of material wealth can match the value of slaves. Without slaves, they have nothing.
csg_tsurr.language: T’surr speak T’surrese, and they tend to learn Basic as well so that they can command their slaves more easily.
csg_tsurr.homeworld: T’surr come from a planet of the same name, a high-gravity planet in the Expansion Region. It is cold, windy, and has little water. The sun is distant and provides little light, which is why the T’surr see so well in darkness.
csg_tsurr.description: The T'surr seen in the galaxy are exclusively male, and they are blue-skinned giants with extra eyes, sharp teeth, and horns. These T'surr are brutal pirates, and they value slaves above all else.
csg_tsurr.sidebar_text: The galaxy has yet to see any female T’surr, who are confined to the home. Although males may seek to conquest offworld, they are subject to the females in the home. For this reason, male T’surr generally prefer to leave their homes once they have had children, as they are subject to no one once they take to the stars. Males describe the females as small, timid creatures that are too scared to leave their homes, but the galaxy has yet to hear how the females respond to these claims.

csg_ubese.name: Ubese

special_abilities.name: Low-Oxygen Adaptations
special_abilities.description: Need a mask to breathe in a normal environment. Regular oxygen levels have a dangerous atmosphere of rating 2. Cannot speak louder than a raspy whisper without a microphone.

csg_ubese.physiology: Ubese are near-humans who appear fairly humanoid but actually have several major differences. They have fair skin and their narrow face is characterized by large green or blue eyes and high cheekbones. They have dark hair on their head but cannot grow facial hair. It is their respiratory and vocal systems that vary the most in comparison to humans: They cannot breathe in normal Type 1 atmospheres but are instead adapted toward breathing air that is parched and low in oxygen. Their vocal cords are less effective than most, as they cannot speak louder than a whisper. Almost all wear a special mask with an air filter and a microphone to accommodate for these differences.
csg_ubese.society: Ubese are a violent and xenophobic people, but this is not entirely by nature. They were once sophisticated and peaceful despite a relatively primitive level of technology. However, with advances in technology brought on by contact with the Republic thousands of years ago, their society flourished. A massive population boom caused them to colonize their system and form individual nations. However, they also became very prideful and rejected diplomacy as they began a military buildup. In response, the Republic sector authorities conducted orbital bombardments that devastated their society. Their original home, Uba III, was destroyed. Uba I, II, and V were rendered uninhabitable. Uba IV remained barely habitable. To this day, the Ubese remain bitter over this event, hating the Republic and the Jedi who served it. They rarely befriend any non-Ubese but are loyal to each other. Despite being very nomadic, they have little respect for customs or laws on other planets. They typically choose careers where they cannot carry out violence without repercussions.
csg_ubese.language: The Ubese have a hard time speaking, so they often use a sign language called Ubeninal. They can also speak Ubese, although they have no written language. They typically choose not to speak Basic.
csg_ubese.homeworld: The Ubese are nomadic, but they originate from either Uba IV or Ubertica. Both worlds have low amounts of oxygen. Uba IV is a toxic wasteland that is barely habitable, while Ubertica features plains and hills. Evidence of the Uba system has been wiped from most records, so only True Ubese know its location.
csg_ubese.description: Violent near-humans who need a mask to speak and breathe in a normal atmosphere, the Ubese have become mostly nomadic after their homeworld and colonies were orbitally bombarded. They detest the Republic, who was responsible for the event, so most find work on the fringes.
csg_ubese.sidebar_text: Just as the Ubese hate the rest of the galaxy and are only loyal to their own, they also hate those of the other race. It started shortly after the bombardments of the planets in the Uba system when a number of Ubese were transported away from the inhospitable Uba IV to a planet dubbed Ubertica. The Ubese who remained considered them to be cowardly and impure, and they called those on Ubertica the “yrak pootzck.” Ever since then, the True Ubese and the yrak pootzck have been engaged in a blood feud. However, they still hate outsiders, especially Jedi, more than those of another race.

csg_ugnaught.name: Ugnaught

special_abilities.name: Dependable
special_abilities.description: Remove setback from Computers and Mechanics checks.

csg_ugnaught.physiology: Ugnaughts are porcine humanoids who are short but bulky enough to compete with larger species when doing manual labor. Similar to humans in most respects, they have a distinctive snout with two prominent nostrils. They also have two sharp buck-teeth protruding from their lower jaw. Their skin is tan or pink. Their white or gray hair appears on their chin and head. Ugnaughts are also resistant to pain and able to go through long periods of discomfort. Despite their small size, they live for an average of 200 years.
csg_ugnaught.society: Ugnaughts are dependable and industrious, naturally suited to hard work and manual labor. They often find jobs as mechanics and technicians. Ugnaught parents pass down their occupation to their children, so all Ugnaughts have a “blood profession.” They will always do this job, unless there are too many laborers. If this happens, they enter a “blood duel,” which is fought to the death. The winners, of course, can keep their job. Otherwise, Ugnaughts are peaceful. Ugnaught children, or Ugletts, learn their job from their parents, and only a small portion get schooling elsewhere. Their greeting is to bow silently, which is responded by a guttural purring. They take personal offense to the common greeting of yaa-yaah and tend to throw things when greeted that way. Ugnaughts are organized into tribes, which are frequently sold into slavery together. Ugnaughts are often seen as slaves, thanks to their mechanical inclinations, industrious nature, tolerance for pain, and peaceful ways. They are ruled by elected councils called “terends,” which is made up of members that they call “ufflors.”
csg_ugnaught.language: Ugnaughts speak Ugnaught. It has grunts and squeals, making it difficult to learn but not impossible for humans to speak. Ugnaughts generally don’t bother to learn Basic, though they can do so if needed.
csg_ugnaught.homeworld: Ugnaughts come from Gentes. It has a somewhat poisonous atmosphere and is filled with swamps and volcanoes. It is in the Anoat sector, not far from Bespin. It is sparsely populated, since many Ugnaughts are scattered as slaves throughout the galaxy or live free on Cloud City.
csg_ugnaught.description: Ugnaughts are dependable laborers with porcine physiology. They have often been slaves, but some tribes earned their freedom by agreeing to build Cloud City, a place where many now live and work.
csg_ugnaught.sidebar_text: The Botrut, the Iscred, and the Irden are the three tribes that mostly inhabit Cloud City, an obscure tibanna mining station on the world of Bespin. They were purchased by Ecclessis Figg, the architect of Cloud City. He offered them a deal: If they built and maintained the city, they would receive freedom, a share in profits, and residence on Cloud City. To this day, they inhabit Cloud City, and most work as the mechanics maintaining it. Others manage businesses there. To feel more at home, they have their own labyrinth of small, red-lit tunnels that only they can navigate. They receive a share of Cloud City’s profits, but what they spend it on is anyone’s guess.

csg_ugor.name: Ugor

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Utinni!”

special_abilities.name: Amorphic
special_abilities.description: May shape-shift as an easy Discipline check, changing shape and general proportions or gaining up to 2 arms and 2 legs. Furthermore, may reduce up to 3 characteristics by 1. With each reduction, may choose 1 Amorphic Benefit to possess until that characteristic is increased. At the end of each encounter, must pass an average Discipline check or remove Amorphic Benefits and revert to a limbless blob.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 1
special_abilities.description: Increase 1 characteristic by 1.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 2
special_abilities.description: Form more than 4 limbs, gaining the ability to have 3 times as much gear in their hands and not needing to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 3
special_abilities.description: Reshape 1 limb into a simple tool such as a dagger, bag, or lock pick. May not form items larger than 3 encumbrance or items involving technology such as a blaster or datapad.

special_abilities.name: Amorphic Benefit 4
special_abilities.description: Create advanced sensory organs, adding 2 boosts on all Perception checks and removing setbacks for lighting conditions.

csg_ugor.physiology: Ugors are one of the galaxy’s most unique sentient species, as they are unicellular protozoa. Their brain, a highly evolved nucleus, works with individual molecules, making it much more efficient than that of another species. Instead of blood, they have cytoplasm. Instead of organs, they have organelles and pseudopodia, the latter of which can be created at will. This makes them capable of shape-shifting, which they use to specialize in certain abilities. For example, they can create limbs or enhance their physical power. They can also create facial features such as a smiling mouth or even a simple tool when needed. All of these abilities, however, require concentration and use up pseudopodia, so they must sacrifice an ability for every one they gain. Internally, they are capable of digesting almost anything, particularly garbage. However, their physiology is not without flaws. Their most comfortable form, a limbless blob, is very slow, while humanoid structures cannot be maintained indefinitely. They are generally unattractive, with slimy skin and a bad smell, and they require a great deal of food to survive.
csg_ugor.society: Ugors are greedy and selfish, and they are excellent negotiators. However, they are pompous, hard to get along with, and have a reputation as swindlers, so most prefer to avoid doing business with them. Most Ugors are obsessed with food and garbage, and their cuisine is incredibly complex. They worship salvage, which they consider to be holy relics that they must acquire with violence if needed. Many Ugor salvage teams patrol the galaxy in dreadnaughts, all of which are controlled by the Holy Ugor Taxation Collection Agency. Once salvage is brought back to the Paradise System, they are willing to give their relics to “pilgrims” who provide a “donation.”
csg_ugor.language: Ugors mostly speak Ugor, but they also typically know a trade language such as Basic or Bocce, and many know Squibbian. They often mispronounce words; for example, “give” is pronounced “gib.”
csg_ugor.homeworld: The Ugors control the entire Paradise System, which is filled with their salvaged technology.
csg_ugor.description: The Ugors are sentient protozoa, and although they are technically a single cell, they can form pseudopodia to act like limbs or organs. They are greedy scavengers by nature, and they have rivalry with the Squibs.
csg_ugor.sidebar_text: Ugors have a mortal enemy in the Squibs, a fellow scavenger species that they find sinful. They do not allow Squibs in their system and desire the complete extermination of the Squibs. However, some corrupt Ugors will tolerate Squibs if given an “exorcism fee.”

csg_umbaran.name: Umbaran

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for darkness, add 2 setbacks for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Supernatural Influence
special_abilities.description: Add boost on Coercion, Deception, and Negotiation checks.

csg_umbaran.physiology: Umbarans are a near-human species adapted to low-light conditions. They are tall, thin, and can be mistaken for stunningly pale humans. Further adding to this “almost human” idea are sunken eyes and hairless head. While they boast excellent vision when in low-light and can see the ultraviolet spectrum, Umbarans are just the opposite in bright conditions, where they are easily blinded.
csg_umbaran.society: Umbarans make natural spies: They are known to never reveal their own views and intentions, hiding behind layers upon layers of deception. They, in turn, can see through the deceptions of others in most cases. In combat, stealth and subterfuge are their allies, and they do anything in order to avoid direct confrontation. They are also manipulative, and many excel in leadership. Their abilities with persuasion are seemingly supernatural, and their gaze is very unnerving to most sentients. They tend to hold power and influence above all else, using it to measure their worth. These grim views and lack of kindness often lead to an extremely cold and dark sense of humor. Umbarans held high standing in the Republic because of their manipulative skills, and they are now close allies of the Empire. Many use their skills as spies to hunt Jedi.
csg_umbaran.language: Umbarans speak Umbarese, and most are literate and fluent in Basic as well.
csg_umbaran.homeworld: Umbara is a dark planet. Its nature earns Umbarans the nickname “shadow people.” It is an Expansion Region world in the Ghost Nebula with dense fog and perpetual darkness, where the Umbaran’s night vision is very necessary.
csg_umbaran.description: Umbarans are bald near-humans with pale skin adapted to darkness. They make excellent spies and are extremely manipulative. Their society is organized into more than 100 castes, which most Umbarans devote themselves to rising in.
csg_umbaran.sidebar_text: Umbarans arrange themselves into more than 100 castes, but these castes are not rigid enough to always contain the wily Umbarans. For Umbarans, rising up in caste is a game that consumes their lives. Hard work is rarely the option for them, and they instead attempt assassinations, blackmail, trickery, and deception to rise through the ranks. While failed attempts are punished harshly, the rewards for success appeal to any Umbaran. Failed attempts also often result in punishment to the family, causing many Umbarans to hold very hard feelings towards relatives. Only the top ten levels are allowed to leave their homeworld and the top level rules the planet, as the “Rootai.”

csg_utai.name: Utai

special_abilities.name: Tamers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Beast Wrangler.”

special_abilities.name: Dark Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: Natural Followers
special_abilities.description: Add boost when targeted by a Leadership check. When performing the assist maneuver, grant 2 boosts instead of 1.

csg_utai.physiology: Utai are relatively short, but they are stoutly built. Their skin is a pale pink or tan and is leathery in texture. Their oblong head has no hair and points backwards, with eyestalks on either side holding a pair of large, dark eyes that can see well in the dark. They have no nose, and their head ends in a puckered mouth. They have two-fingered hands and four-toed feet. Their fat fingers end in tips which look like suction cups. Unlike their Pau’an neighbors, they prefer their meat cooked.
csg_utai.society: Utai find their worth typically through manual labor, handling animals in particular. They possess an almost innate gift when it comes to the handling of animals, whether it be the flying dactillians or sprinting varactyls. The Utai have spent their time in the tunnels and caves on the sides of sinkholes, where they continue to live. They are currently under the control of the Empire, which has not cared about the Utai. Utapau is having its resources harvested, and some Pau’ans and Utai are now taken as slaves. While the nature of the Utai makes them more capable of dealing with slavery than others, some do step up for freedom. Rebel strike teams have had a decent track record in stirring up Utai revolts.
csg_utai.language: The Utai language is one of burbling glottal hoots. Most also know Utapese, the Pau’an language.
csg_utai.homeworld: The site of the final battle in the Clone Wars, Utapau is a minor Outer Rim world covered in rocky sinkholes. The surface is very windy, so both species are forced to live in the sinkholes. 95% of the planet is powered by wind. Native animals are useful for many roles, so airspeeders and other means of transit are replaced by the lizard-like varactyls who can climb walls and the flying dactillions.
csg_utai.description: Natural followers, the Utai are often seen as manual laborers. They are especially good at all things related to taming animals, a useful talent with the varactyls and dactillions found on their sinkhole-covered homeworld of Utapau.
csg_utai.sidebar_text: Utai share their homeworld with the Pau’ans, who are thought to be their distant relatives. They co-exist peacefully, and they complement each other well. This first began thanks to Timon Medon, a Pau’an leader who first experimented in merging the species. Just as the Utai typically prefer simple, menial labor, the Pau’ans have a strong preference for leadership. The Utai get along well with the Pau’ans, as they are treated fairly by Pau’an employers and taken into account by Pau’an lawmakers. More common conflicts are the ones between cities, which tend to result in societal and economic rivalries and embargos rather than outright bloodshed. Each city has great pride in their unique culture.

csg_vaathkree.name: Vaathkree

special_abilities.name: Gifted Traders
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent "Wheel and Deal."

special_abilities.name: Hardened Plates
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent "Enduring."

special_abilities.name: Volcanic Home
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for hot conditions and suffer no penalties for inhaling smoke.

csg_vaathkree.physiology: A distinct species that consumes minerals in order to develop a very thick armor, the Vaathkree live for about three centuries. For their first two decades of life, they are known as Stonesingers and are essentially non-sentient. At that age, they roam their planet’s lava flats, and their physical form is highly variable. However, once they mature and gain intelligence, their body stiffens, and they must choose a particular form. They are generally similar to humans in size, and although many choose to be humanoid in shape, others choose different forms to suit their profession. All are covered in incredibly hard scales which are in shades of navy and dark gray, and this grants them a great deal of protection from physical attacks. They have a unique diet and are capable of metabolising minerals.
csg_vaathkree.society: Although their unique physiology makes them incredibly durable and very intimidating, Vaathkree actually are known for their skills as merchants. A knowledge of economics, salesmanship, and negotiation is ingrained into their culture. For them, almost everything is about business and profitability. They are the namesake of the Vaathkree Trade Corridor: This prominent hyperlane that bridges Corsin and Gizer is dominated by their merchants.
