Not all of them are exclusively traders, however, as some are capable of art, such as Flatsculp.
csg_vaathkree.language: Vaathkree almost always know Basic for purposes of commerce, and they also have their native trade language, which is complex and difficult to translate, a feature that they use to keep secrets.
csg_vaathkree.homeworld: The Vaathkree share a name with their homeworld, an Outer Rim planet which is very dangerous thanks to its oppressive heat, high gravity, frequent meteor strikes, and vast lakes of lava. This makes its atmosphere unbreathable for non-Vaathkree, and radioactive metals are also prevalent. It has some mining industries, and there exist semi-organic towns called vnals to protect offworlders. These creations are impressive feats of engineering, although the concept of a living building is unnerving to most. Vaathkree can also be found on many worlds as merchants, and particularly Garnib.
csg_vaathkree.description: Merchants made of stone, the Vaathkree are adept travellers who can grow into a variety of forms during youth. They worship The Deal and pursue profits at all cost.
csg_vaathkree.sidebar_text: The name of the Vaathkree religion roughly translates to “The Deal,” reflecting their view that everything is a negotiation. Young Vaathkree are first instructed in The Deal at the age of nine, which is also when they first develop sentience.

special_abilities.name: Ultimate Protection
special_abilities.description: Receive an additional rank in the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn. Increase encumbrance threshold by 5.

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_vagaari.name: Vagaari
csg_vagaari.physiology: Vagaari are humanoids who are shorter in stature thanks to their stubby legs. They have violet eyes and dark hair, and their ears are very high on their head. Most notably, their chin splits, and they have two separate mouths on each cheek. Their skin borders between hues of tan and purple. Vagaari have large hands, and their feet have four toes.
csg_vagaari.society: Vagaari are a people who prefer to act rather than speak, and they are extremely warlike. They have developed little technology of their own, but they are a prominent spacefaring species because of their abilities as pirates and slavers. Vagaari boast a dangerous combination of cruelty and ingenuity that has allowed them to enslave other species throughout Chiss space who make up for the weaknesses. They are generally nomadic, but they have begun to make a military buildup on hidden planets in order to gather strength after their forces were decimated by Chiss Commander Thrawn prior to the Clone Wars. Their government, the Vagaari Empire, is ruled by a leader called the Miskara. Although they may be seen as simple brutes wanting only to loot for pleasure, they are still prideful and value their appearance: Most wear elaborate robes and a decorative mask to compensate for their lack of height.
csg_vagaari.language: Vagaari speak a number of languages, including their native language, Vagaari, as well as trade languages such as Minnisiat, Sy Bisti, and a pidgin form of Basic.
csg_vagaari.homeworld: Vagaari come from Vagar Praxut, a planet in the Unknown Regions near the Chiss Ascendency, although they have adopted a nomadic lifestyle.
csg_vagaari.description: A fierce species with two mouths and purple skin, the Vagaari have pillaged the Unknown Regions, occasionally coming into conflict with the Chiss. They are typically slavers, and they have very little grasp of morality, often using their slaves as living shields on their ships.
csg_vagaari.sidebar_text: Although much of their vessels are stolen or built by slaves of smarter species, Vagaari do use a number of living things, both sentient and non-sentient, in their own unique innovations. They are known to use their slaves as living shields, holding them in transparisteel cages on the hulls of their ships so that the vessels cannot be attacked without killing innocents. Although they fashion themselves as warriors, they often prefer to attack using trained animals. These include stinging insects called schostri and speedy yet resilient canines called wolvkil. Wolvkil can be held in stasis and carried around by a single Vagaari but are easy to unleash in combat. Perhaps because of these tendencies, they will form alliances with the Yuuzhan Vong, and the Vagaari Empire will expand after the Yuuzhan Vong War weakens the rest of the galaxy.

csg_veknoid.name: Veknoid

special_abilities.name: Attention Grabbers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Distracting Behavior.”

csg_veknoid.physiology: Veknoids are reptilian bipeds who are about a meter and a half tall on average. They have leathery brown skin and are somewhat stocky in build. They have three-toed feet and four-fingered hands, and their face is most distinguished by an underbite with four prominent upward-pointing teeth that extend outside of their wide mouth. Long floppy ears extend from the top of their hairless head, and their white eyes lack irises. They also have a tail which can reach about as far as the ground.
csg_veknoid.society: Veknoids are one of the galaxy’s most patient and disciplined species, traits that have made many great Veknoid Jedi. They have excellent self-awareness and are typically able to keep their emotions in check. Their only real vice is alcohol, which is extremely addictive to them, so the majority of Veknoids know to abstain from it completely. Their government is a matriarchal hierarchy, with a Queen who has absolute power and Countesses who handle the day-to-day governing for smaller regions. An elder matriach manages family affairs, including marriages, which are typically arranged. As long as they’re sober, Veknoids have little concept of romance, and they see marriage strictly as a practical necessity. However, they can certainly act the part of a smitten romantic, because in general, they make excellent showmen who excel when the spotlight is on them. Many become actors, while others use their excellent speed and reflexes to become star athletes or use their focus to become prominent chefs.
csg_veknoid.language: Veknoids speak Mandellian in everyday affairs, while their archaic language of Ekamo is reserved for religious matters. Many know Basic as well.
csg_veknoid.homeworld: Veknoids come from the Mid Rim planet of Moonus Mandel, a large world with high gravity and relatively few oceans. Veknoid society is very spread out across its giant continents, so they have few large cities. It is an excellent place to ranch imported nerfs and native ungulates called teeps, so it exports lots of meat.
csg_veknoid.description: Veknoids are patient and religious, although they have a knack for performing in the spotlight. They treat all life with deep reverence so long as they’re not falling into alcoholism.
csg_veknoid.sidebar_text: Religious fervor is a trait that almost all Veknoids share, and they believe in a pantheon of eleven gods called the Opeerd. These gods have a very finite amount of power but live eternally, and Veknoids hold that the universe was slowly constructed over the course of trillions of years by these gods. Similarly, they believe the gods are responsible for creating the “life energy” which is responsible for their existence, which also takes them decades for each person. Clearly, the Opeerd cannot create new life energy quickly enough to match the huge population, so the Veknoids hypothesize that they are using up a finite backlog of life energy, and that a day will come when the galaxy runs out and the population dramatically reduces. Regardless, all life and the natural world around them is a masterpiece that took decades to make according to Veknoids, and they treat it with due respect. Whenever they encounter an admirable person, natural wonder, performance, or artwork, they usually take time to appreciate it and praise the gods for their handiwork. Overall, their unique theology ensures that they are deeply principled, although it can also make them inflexible and judgemental.
csg_veknoid._provenance_note: The Veknoid species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_vernol.name: Vernol

special_abilities.name: Scavengers
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Forager.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_vernol.physiology: Despite their somewhat amphibious, frog-like appearance, the Vernols are actually a mammalian species. They have blue skin, though it also has splotches of orange hues around their eyes, their lips, their palms, and the soles of their feet. They are somewhat diminutive, averaging just a meter and a half in height, and their appearance is overall unthreatening to most species. They have an extremely wide face with a large mouth, while their eyes and ears are small and widely-spaced as well. The top of their head is short and hairless, though it does have a few appendages sprouting off the back-center. They have stout arms with four-fingered hands, and their digits are quite stubby.
csg_vernol.society: Vernols tend to be a highly clever and adaptable people, and as scavengers, they are very adept at making the most of things that others see as useless. While they are most skilled at finding food and shelter in the wilderness, some are also able to adapt their tracking abilities to work as private investigators or detectives. Because of their unassuming appearance, Vernols maintain a generally good reputation, which some choose to use to their advantage in work as merchants or con artists. These professions have allowed their race to expand across the galaxy, but they nonetheless have an extremely skittish and fearful personality. Vernols are actually quite territorial, and they prefer to try to stick to their own kind rather than venturing off too far. This largely stems from major calamities on their original homeworld: A devastating collision with a large meteor caused major damage to their population, and within fifty years, their world’s orbit had also shifted, rendering it effectively uninhabitable. As such, the Vernols have now had to establish new colonies.
csg_vernol.language: Vernols speak methodically in a deep tongue called Orvit, and most of them also learn Basic. In recent years, a few have also taken to learning the language of the Balinaka.
csg_vernol.homeworld: With their homeworld tragically no longer livable, the Vernols have established Garnib as their new home. A very chilly planet in the southern part of the Outer Rim, the Vernols and Balinaka live beneath a harsh Imperial rule. The Imperials are centered around Garnib Station and have enslaved some Balinaka. Because of the Vernols’ timidity and the Balinaka’s laid-back tendencies, their oppression has resulted in little violence. The planet is otherwise ruled by GCC, a corporation in which all citizens of Garnib are shareholders. This organization controls the Balinaka’s production of ice sculptures for export, and they oversee all over their business in an annual four-day festival and meeting called the wallarand, which the entire populace is expected to attend.
csg_vernol.description: Blue-skinned mammals of semi-aquatic origin, the Vernols are stout, unassuming, and smiley, but they are actually an extremely cunning people. Ecological disasters have forced their race to relocate, and they have since become quite skittish.
csg_vernol.sidebar_text: The Vernols’ most notable colony is on Garnib, a frigid world they share with the furry Balinaka, who are about three times their height. Perhaps because of this, or just because of their overall psyche, the Vernols are quite nervous around their neighbors. Despite their visitors’ icy attitudes, the Balinaka have been extremely agreeable and welcoming.

csg_verpine.name: Verpine

special_abilities.name: Hardened Carapaces
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Microvision
special_abilities.description: Add boost on checks to see tiny details up close.

special_abilities.name: Radio Communication
special_abilities.description: May communicate with technology or other Verpine through radio waves, which have a range of 100 kilometers.

csg_verpine.physiology: Verpine are insectoid creatures with an expertise for technology. Though thin-limbed, they average nearly two meters in height. Their body is covered in a flexible yet hardened carapace, which is a dark green with a plated texture, giving a wrinkled appearance. They have no heart, and unlike many other insects, they only have four limbs and lack wings. They have two-toed feet and three-fingered hands. A Verpine head has an elongated snout with small mandibles surrounding their toothless mouth. Their large red or black eyes are split to either side of their head, giving them enhanced peripheral vision. They do not have a nose, but they do have an extra sense from the two antennae that protrude from behind their eyes, each pointing backwards and down. These are extremely sensitive to radio waves, allowing the Verpine to communicate with one another over many kilometers. They often program technology to respond to these radio waves, thus allowing them to silently communicate with their devices.
csg_verpine.society: Verpine have nearly instant communication from their antennae, so the hives act as a consensus democracy. Instead of electing a government, they vote on every single issue. Because of how they communicate, their antennae are vital to their membership in society, and those who damage their antennae tend to be outcasts and criminals. In any case, their constant voting carries over into their interactions with other species, where they tend to constantly deliberate on even minor issues. Verpine aren’t known for fighting and tend to compromise instead, but they do build excellent weapons. They are now under the control of the Empire but openly support the Rebel Alliance. Their pacifistic nature prevents them from directly fighting off the Empire, but they do manufacture technology for the rebels, such as the B-Wing starfighter.
csg_verpine.language: Verpine can communicate with radio waves using their antennae, although it is relatively straightforward to translate this language into sounds that they can replicate verbally. This language is known as Verpine, and most Verpine are fluent in it as well as Basic.
csg_verpine.homeworld: Verpine do not know their original homeworld but now inhabit the Roche asteroid field, which includes Nickel One, Slayn, and Korpil. Roche is in the Mid Rim and is populated by mostly Verpine, and the Empire keeps a close watch on the system.
csg_verpine.description: Verpine are green-skinned insects with several benefits in their physiology. Perhaps most notable is their incredible intelligence, which they use to build excellent technology. In addition, they boast instant radio communication with their antennae, a hardened carapace, and microvision.
csg_verpine.sidebar_text: Verpine are hermaphrodites, meaning that every member can both lay and fertilize eggs. To ensure genetic diversity, they typically do not have anyone lay and fertilize the same egg. Naturally, about five percent of Verpine are intelligent, while the remainder were drones who were barely sentient and used only for manual labor. However, modern Verpine can now manufacture an enzyme that when applied, ensures that all of the eggs end up being intelligent.

csg_vimbexian.name: Vimbexian

special_abilities.name: Animal Experts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Hunter.”

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

csg_vimbexian.physiology: A genderless hermaphroditic species, Vimbexians have a two-phase life cycle tied to their homeworld’s seasons, which are very long due to their planet’s orbit taking almost a century. The sentient form known to the galaxy is called the medusa, which only lives during the winter. The medusa contains half the chromosomes of its parent, which is called the polyp and lives during the summer. Polyps are completely immobile, living as plants on the tropical ocean floor. They live about 44 standard years before the fall, when they die, and the medusas emerge from their innards. Medusas then swim around, hunting for small fish. They come onto land after about six standard years, at which point they become integrated into modern society. By about fourteen years they become adults, and once the climate warms again, when they are about 51, they bury themselves in the depths of the sea, where they fuse with a partner to recreate the full chromosome set needed to make new polyps. The polyp form is that of a plant with a hard stalk and yellow-bristles on top, living in the warmer parts of coral reefs where they can get sufficient sunlight. Genetically identical polyps grow in clusters, all connected by a shared root system. When the medusas are released, they have a small, hairless body without fully developed limbs, but as they grow, they gain four nimble limbs with fin-like frills and a layer of insulating white fur. Their snout features a mouth full of sharp teeth and a sensitive black nose.
csg_vimbexian.society: Though fierce hunters, the Vimbexians are a cautious and honest people. Raised by droids and holographic communiqués from the previous generation, they have a relatively strict upbringing that teaches them to control their natural instincts and become civilized. They still apply their animal knowledge, but in new ways: The flocks of caitons that they once mauled are now herded for their wool, and schools of flukefish that they once hunted are now fished at an industrial scale using giant submersibles. They are generally very reserved, seeing emotion as immature, and criminals are also considered unsophisticated. All are now about 35 years old, and interacting with other age groups is foreign to them. Expatriates don’t usually go far, as they must return home to mate.
csg_vimbexian.language: Dedicated to assimilating with the galaxy, Vimbexians generally speak only Basic.
csg_vimbexian.homeworld: The high gravity Mid Rim planet Vimbex distantly orbits a very bright red giant, resulting in its very long years. The planet is covered by ocean, but due to its elliptic path, it experiences a planet-wide winter where the whole ocean is covered by a layer of ice.
csg_vimbexian.description: The Vimbexians are a strange species that alternates between generations of stationary underwater plants in their planet’s summer and predatory amphibians in the winter. The latter are eager to prove their sophistication and adapt offworld technologies.
csg_vimbexian.sidebar_text: Vimbexians have unique difficulties when it comes to passing on their knowledge and resources to the next generation. Due to their decades-long time as plants when all the foundations of their society melt into the ocean, they must rely on a network or droids and hired hands. Currently, Vimbexians in equatorial regions look to begin going underwater in about a decade, while those in colder places will have up to six extra years. For now, it means there isn’t too much point in building anything more, and all of their buildings are of relatively cheap wooden construction designed to biodegrade once they sink. Many Vimbexians are now working to program the droids who will educate the next generation or investigating firms who can be trusted to build homes and schools in the distant future. In the next handful of years, some Vimbexians will begin seeking out a partner with whom they will fuse during the spring. However, it is generally seen as desperate to find a partner so early, and most will wait until it is within a few months or weeks of their mutual burial.
csg_vimbexian._provenance_note: Vimbexians are entirely homebrew, but they can fit into either continuity without contradiction.

csg_visk.name: Visk

special_abilities.name: Advanced Eyes
special_abilities.description: May see in all directions, adding boost on visual Perception checks. Remove setback for darkness.

special_abilities.name: Proboscis
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl, may spend 2 advantage to hit with proboscis, adding the Pierce 2 quality and consuming a small amount of the victim’s blood.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. Must land every 5 rounds.

csg_visk.physiology: Viska are a species of large, blood-drinking winged creatures. They are two or three meters tall, and their full wingspan is an impressive five meters. This wing membrane extends from their pointed tail all the way to their upper limbs to which it is attached. To keep such a large body in flight requires tremendous energy, so the Viska get their nutrition from a unique diet of only blood. Their digestive tract cannot handle other foods, and their mouth is a long, thin proboscis, called a blossug. The blossug takes the form of a sharp bone which can penetrate the flesh of their victims, then a layer of surrounding muscle that efficiently slurps up their meal, averaging about two liters total per day. While the blossug is sharp enough to use in combat, only a select few animals native to their world have blood that is safe for Viska to drink. Behind their blossug are dark, widely-set eyes which can see in the infrared and have a 360-degree view, and behind those, at the back of their narrow head are pointed ears. Viska use their lower limbs like arms for grasping, and all of their limbs have four digits.
csg_visk.society: Because of their world’s volatile tectonics, the Viska have developed an aerial society, building their cities around massive repulsorlift towers even since the Republic gave them the technology in the 300s BBY. Each column is a hundred meters in diameter, and the cities above can go kilometers high. Their workers are near the ground, living on the cities’ lowest levels and ranching animals such as drivveb and kessarch. As their world has sparse vegetation, they need to import massive quantities of grass to feed them. Industry and commerce are handled on mid levels, while their upper classes reserve the high places for themselves. Every Visk seeks such standing, as they are a highly ambitious, hardworking, and driven people. They can be very ruthless in their methods, and they do little to dispel the fears that they drink the blood of sentients. Offworlders often know them as “the great bloodsucking fiends of Rordak.”
csg_visk.language: Viska speak Durmdakst, a language that most other species find challenging to pronounce. About half of their population learns Basic as a second language.
csg_visk.homeworld: Visk come from a low-gravity Outer Rim planet called Rordak, which closely orbits a red giant star, giving it violent tectonic activity and a hostile atmosphere full of ash and carbon dioxide. The planet is one of extremes: Days, which last only fourteen hours, are scorching at noon, averaging 45 degrees, but nights are near freezing. Mountains are towering, but gorges are deep. Rain is rare and highly acidic. It has many Imperial prison camps, such TR-8, where miners with life sentences live on the ground beneath an orbital nightcloak, slaving for Viska nobles.
csg_visk.description: Mamals with giant wings, the Viska drink only the blood of the animals that they herd, and they’ve formed an airborne society. They are ambitious, but their clan leaders, chosen by ritual combat, have absolute authority over every individual.
csg_visk.sidebar_text: Counteracting their ambitious nature, Viska are held in place by a rigorous system of government. A Visk who seeks power through backhanded means, such as assassination, is punished by the killing of their entire family. Each family must submit entirely to their clan’s leader, called the calsk, who micromanages as far as picking out occupations for everyone in the clan. After a calsk’s death, their children fight a battle to the death to become the new calsk. A new family can only take power if the calsk dies childless, in which case they nominate a member to fight for the position against other families’ representatives. Similarly, most clans are lurinn clans, whom the three to six calsedra clans have absolute authority over. The calsedra clans are chosen by a monarch called the caleisk. Similarly to calsks, the caleisk rules until death, at which point their children fight for power.

csg_vodran.name: Vodran

special_abilities.name: Loyal
special_abilities.description: After 1 month of serving a person or cause, may become extremely loyal. When doing things to serve that cause or person, add boost to all Willpower checks.

csg_vodran.physiology: The Vodrans are reptilians who are similar to humans in terms of size and proportions. They have leathery skin that is brown or olive, and they lay eggs. The remaining notable differences from humans that Vodrans have are in their head. They have no hair and instead have horns. There are two horns on their chin and four more on either side of their black, sunken eyes. They have no nose and only tall slits for nostrils. Their face has very weak muscles in it, limiting their capability for facial expression.
csg_vodran.society: Vodrans are a people who are very selfless and trusting. They easily devote themselves to a cause, and almost all do everything in their power to support “the value of the many.” The other side of that coin is that they are very gullible, assuming benevolence in all others. Because of their communal nature, they struggle with some of the social intricacies such as innuendo or etiquette. In general, they are a straightforward people. They have a deep respect for any authority and strongly chastise nonconformity. They generally have very little individuality or desire for innovation. As for their culture, Vodrans have essentially no unique culture.
csg_vodran.language: The Vodrans have abandoned their native language in favor of Huttese, the Hutt language. Huttese is a major language among illicit parts of the galaxy.
csg_vodran.homeworld: Vodrans come from Vodran, a swampy world in the Si’Klaata Cluster of Hutt Space. They typically only travel when commanded to do so by their Hutt master. As such, many are taken to work on Nal Hutta or Nar Shaddaa, but few ever leave Hutt Space. Vodran itself has been given advanced technology from the Hutts. It is also noteworthy in that it is the homeworld of the dianoga species.
csg_vodran.description: The Vodrans are reptiles known for their gullibility. Given their location in Hutt Space, they were an easy target to become ruled by the Hutts. They have lost their previous culture and now believe they have only ever existed as Hutt servants.
csg_vodran.sidebar_text: A multitude of societal factors has made the Vodrans an easy target for manipulation. This, combined with being in Hutt Space, makes them one of the many species that is devoted to serving the Hutts. Unlike the others, however, they are very loyal to their masters and view the relationship as mutually beneficial. They have never attempted to revolt. Hutts have essentially redesigned Vodran culture from the ground up to fit their own desires. They have even written history so that the Vodrans didn’t even exist until they became Hutt servants. They have adapted much of Hutt culture into their own, although they believe their role is to serve rather than be served. Vodrans are organized into clans, each of which corresponds to a Hutt clan that they serve.

csg_vor.name: Vor

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Biology
special_abilities.description: Double penalties induced by air quality and develop illnesses caused by air quality much more frequently.

csg_vor.physiology: Vors are a winged sentient species with green skin that has avian and reptilian heritage. They are a graceful people with natural dexterity and agility, although they have thin bones and lack the strength of other species. However, their light bones allow them to fly with their leathery wings. They have a superb understanding of weather, and they fly exceptionally well in strong winds. They wear very little clothing, as it interferes with flight. They have webbed hands on the end of their wings, but their thumbs are only partially opposable. Their head is pointed with a beak and obsidian eyes on either side. They are extremely sensitive to pollution, as they are adapted to a very pure atmosphere that is on their homeworld. They are a very intelligent people, and their mental capacity is particularly exceptional when it comes to coordinating with other Vors. They can work together with little to no verbal communication. Some suspect this to be a telepathic ability, while others believe it is a skill that they have.
csg_vor.society: Vors are a hardworking people who are seen as very emotionless to most. This is not entirely true: Such reactions are just done in a way that non-Vors cannot recognize them. This seeming austerity makes them excellent at lying or gambling, but that is not what most of them do. Instead, they put their intellect toward work such as art or music. They are calm and peaceful, focused on the bigger picture more than any one moment. As such, they place the needs of their society above their own desires. They rarely leave their homeworld and prefer to avoid the rest of the galaxy.
csg_vor.language: Vors speak Vortexlex, a language featuring squawks and whistles. They often sing when working.
csg_vor.homeworld: Vors come from Vortex, a world in the northern part of the Mid Rim. Because of the tilt in its axis, it has very strong winds. They are arranged into tribes on their homeworld. Their homes resemble bunkers in that they are small and partially underground. Each settlement contains homes in a concentric circle.
csg_vor.description: A frail species of avian, the Vors are calm and austere to most other species except in their music, which is renowned throughout the galaxy. They are highly intelligent, and they excel in coordinating with others of their species.
csg_vor.sidebar_text: The Vors are renowned for their music, which is their only form of emotional expression comprehensible to outsiders. The most prominent example of their music is found at the magnificent Cathedral of the Winds, in which the building itself is used as an organ. It is one of the Twenty Wonders of the Galaxy. The Vors themselves fly around and cover up holes with their bodies, acting with incredible synchronization. Especially since it isn’t recorded, their annual Concert of the Winds is renowned throughout the galaxy. However, as protest for the rule of the Empire, they have sealed all openings in the Cathedral and refuse to perform for non-Vors. Unfortunately, once the Vors finally begin to perform the Concert of the Winds again, it will be destroyed because of Imperial sabotage.

csg_vorzydiak.name: Vorzydiak

special_abilities.name: Skeptical
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent "Nobody's Fool."

special_abilities.name: Inflexible
special_abilities.description: When performing a task in a way that is different from what the character is used to, add setback and suffer up 3 strain at the GM's discretion.

special_abilities.name: Specialized
special_abilities.description: Gain free ranks in 6 skills from career instead of 4, and 3 from specialization instead of 2.

csg_vorzydiak.physiology: Vorzydiaks are lithe near-humans with bright yellow skin, and they also have long antennae. Depending on the Vorzydiak’s mood, these antennae can droop down or lash around. They also have large eyes and a sharp chin.
csg_vorzydiak.society: Vorzydiaks are loyal and dedicated, and they boast an extremely hardworking society. On Vorzyd IV, children go to school seven days per week, and by age ten, they begin working. They take on more hours every year, and by seventeen, they work every day of the week, which lasts until they retire in their seventies. Although they have little time for relaxation, they find joy in their closely-knit families. Vorzydiaks are also extremely rigid thinkers who are skeptical of anything that is not their norm. This makes them very skeptical toward alien cultures, and they struggle to adapt their ways to new circumstances. As such, social changes are very rare, but when they do get enacted, there’s no going back.
csg_vorzydiak.language: Vorzydiaks typically speak their native language, Vorzydiak, as well as Basic.
csg_vorzydiak.homeworld: Vorzydiaks were a spacefaring species even before they were discovered by the Republic, but the gift of the hyperdrive allowed them to expand their society even further and make contact with the other species in the Vorzyd Cluster of the northeast Outer Rim. Their largest population is on their industrial homeworld, Vorzyd IV, but Vorzyd V is of more prominence on the galactic scale. Once in decay, Columexi businessman built a multitude of casinos in the capital city, Efavan, several decades ago, turning the planet into a hub for gambling and recreation. Corrupt bargains ensure that most of the money goes to the Empire and poverty still remains, but the planet is now bustling nonetheless.
csg_vorzydiak.description: The Vorzydiaks are hardworking but close-minded humanoids with yellow skin. They are skeptical of other species, although they do have a history of spacefaring.
csg_vorzydiak.sidebar_text: In stark contrast to the hardworking ways of most adult Vorzydiaks, their societies are in conflict with a nonconformist youth underclass called the “Freelies.” Among other things, Freelies oppose their elders’ work ethic and want to see Vorzyd society become less business-oriented. They go to dramatic lengths to make their message heard. Vandalism is commonplace among the Freelies, but many engage in shockingly violent crimes such as robbery, sabotage, and even murder.

csg_voss.name: Voss

special_abilities.name: Martial Arts Training
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Feral Strength.”

csg_voss.physiology: Voss are a near human species, and they display notable sexual dimorphism. Males have blue skin with glowing orange eyes, while females have crimson skin with glowing blue eyes. They have no hair or pupils, but their face is distinguished by markings of maroon and blue for females or navy blue and white for males. Force-sensitivity is very common among their species. Their strangest biological trait is that they cannot sexually mature until they perform particular rituals during their marriage ceremony.
csg_voss.society: Voss are reserved and quiet: Instead of using words, they are more likely to express themselves through symbolic art, which is traditionally black and white. All adults are required to perform a term of military service, becoming known as Commandos. They learn martial arts and survival skills, and even those who return to civilian life afterwards typically retain the skills. The most important group of people in their society are called the Mystics, who are Force-sensitive. Mystics must undergo years of training, culminating in a dangerous pilgrimage, but once they do, Mystics are extremely skilled as healers and prophets, although none expand their skills beyond those two powers. Mystics are revered, but they live isolated in either the Tower of Prophecy or the Shrine of Healing. Those gifted with foresight have infallible visions, but the Interpreters, the group that debates and meditates on these visions, can be fallible. Once the interpreters come to a conclusion, their word is law, and it is enacted to the letter by their government, which is called the Three. Voss never disobey laws and are completely loyal to their government, even accepting major destruction in the short term if it is necessary to survive in the long run.
csg_voss.language: Voss typically speak their native language, Voss, and Basic. They have a slightly robotic voice.
csg_voss.homeworld: Voss come from Voss, a mining planet in the Tion Cluster. It has a rocky landscape with a few forests and a hazy, yellow sky. During the war against the Gormak, the Voss were only in the mountaintop city of Voss-Ka. Offworlders are not allowed in Voss-Ka proper and are restricted to embassies.
csg_voss.description: Longtime enemies of the Gormaks, the Voss are a species whose Mystics excel in using the Force to predict the future and heal. The remainder of the species are Commandos, devoted to warfare and outdoor survival.
csg_voss.sidebar_text: In the time of the Old Republic, the Voss were at war with the Gormak, their distant ancestors. Although they were outnumbered, the ability to see the future granted the Voss the edge they needed to survive. Although they defended themselves well, it was prophesied that the Voss would all die if the Gormak became extinct, so the Voss were never too aggressive. Foresight allowed the Voss to fight off the Sith Empire, forcing both the Empire and the Republic to fight against the Gormak in order to earn the Voss’s favor. However, when the Eternal Empire took over the Voss system, the only way for the Voss to survive was to ally with the Gormak. Both species had heavy losses, but each survived, validating the prophecy.

csg_vratix.name: Vratix

special_abilities.name: High Jump
special_abilities.description: Able to jump very high or far in normal gravity. Once per round as a maneuver, may suffer 3 strain to move 2 range bands either vertically or horizontally.

csg_vratix.physiology: The Vratix, also known as Thyferrans, are six-legged insectoid creatures with green and white ridged skin. Their skin color changes slightly due to the chemical denin, which is released based on emotion. They are fast jumpers, using their four powerful legs to leap great distances. While their back legs are very thin, their front legs are very thick and have three toes. Both these legs have thighs that point up and shins that go back down. They have a tail that points up and back. They have a long, thin torso and a long neck; both are white on the front. They have thin arms with two elbows each and three-fingered hands that they use for manipulation. Their short and wide head has large, black or brown eyes, antenna, and four small mandibles. Vratix have minor telepathic abilities, as they can transmit thoughts to those who are closely related to them. They are a species of hermaphrodites, which means that they have no genders and can reproduce with others or create perfect clones of themselves on their own.
csg_vratix.society: Vratix are a very logical species. They can solve complex problems and puzzles, so many make great mathematicians, engineers, or scientists. In those fields and others, they are very detail-oriented but frequently fail to recognize the bigger picture. Despite their technological inclinations, they find it impolite to communicate through technology, as they instead prefer to converse in person. Their intelligence often fails to comprehend the mysteries related to art, literature, or music. These abstract concepts are incredibly foreign to them. They are still socially capable, however. They have a mentality similar to that of many hive minds, sacrificing their own desires for the good of their society.
csg_vratix.language: Vratix speak Vratix, a clicking language that uses pitch for meaning. Almost all also know Basic, although they avoid the use of singular pronouns.
csg_vratix.homeworld: Vratix come from Thyferra, a planet in the Inner Rim. It is a moist world that imports most of what it needs by selling bacta.
csg_vratix.description: Vratix are six-limbed insects that are notable for producing bacta, which is easily available on their homeworld of Thyferra. They are excellent at logic and puzzle-solving, but they struggle with abstract concepts like art.
csg_vratix.sidebar_text: The Vratix have had great economic success in the galaxy thanks to valuable resources present on their planet, which can be used to make bacta. Bacta is a potent healing liquid that is prominent throughout the galaxy. While bacta exported to the rest of the galaxy is cheaper and diluted, the bacta on Thyferra is incredibly potent. The business is entirely controlled by the two companies in the Bacta Cartel: Zaltin and Xucphra. This monopoly exists thanks to Imperial regulation and has caused highly increased prices from the trust. Since prices are so high, smuggling the bacta is popular. It is also taken up by the Rebel Alliance. While a small group of mostly humans manage the production and get profits, most of the manual labor is done by millions of Vratix. The Black Claw group has been working to restore Vratix control through sabotage for years.

csg_vulptereen.name: Vulptereen

special_abilities.name: Natural Hardiness
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for temperature, humidity, or air conditions. Add boost on Resilience checks to withstand such conditions.

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

csg_vulptereen.physiology: Vulptereens are short but bulky reptiles best distinguished by a very long snout. They have teeth pointing down out of their mouth on their snout, and they have six tusks on the snout as well. They have pointed ears and yellow eyes on the sides of their head that are adapted to darkness. They have poor depth perception but make up for it with echolocation. They also have an antenna-like feeler atop their snout. They have clawed hands for traction, and thick skin for protection. Their skin comes in a mix of yellow on their underside and green or gray elsewhere. They are durable in harsh environments, but their lack of a centralized brain means that they can lose mental capacity if they are maimed.
csg_vulptereen.society: Vulptereens are not a particularly intelligent people, and their biggest strength is their hardiness. They are also known to be decent pilots, a profession that many of them take part in.
csg_vulptereen.language: Vulptereens speak Vulpterish, and they often learn Basic in order to do business with offworld companies.
csg_vulptereen.homeworld: Vulptereens come from the Deep Core planet of Vulpter. It has been highly industrialized for a long time, so the once very verdant world is now highly polluted and colder than most planets on average. It cannot sustain agriculture, so they import food and export their technology. It is mostly urban or toxic wasteland, with vast tracts of land devoted to waste dumps. One of the planet’s most unique features is the Orbital Advertisement Ring, a giant structure surrounding the planet composed entirely of billboards. Leaving the planet is almost impossible, as the Empire has cut off access to the Deep Core.
csg_vulptereen.description: Vulptereens are reptiles distinguished by a long snout, and they are short but surprisingly hardy. They live on the Deep Core planet of Vulpter, which has become highly polluted by industry.
csg_vulptereen.sidebar_title: Vulptereens, Amarans, and the Trade Federation
csg_vulptereen.sidebar_text: Many Amarans have worked with the Trade Federation as managers or middle men, often conducting business on the Vulptereen homeworld of Vulpter. Amarans made up about six percent of the population, and the planet was used as a storage world for the Trade Federation, with its underground facilities managed by immigrant Amarans while the Vulptereen had to handle the menial labor, typically drilling tunnels. This arrangement meant that the Vulptereen strongly disliked the Amarans, whom they saw as aristocratic. After the end of the Clone Wars, the Amaran immigrants who worked for their Trade Federation suddenly lost their offworld benefactors in addition to being trapped on the planet by Imperial regulations regarding the Deep Core. As such, the two species are still forced to live together and reconcile their differences.

csg_vurk.name: Vurk

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can breathe underwater and remove all movement penalties for being underwater. Remove setback for humidity, add setback for dry conditions.

csg_vurk.physiology: Vurk are green-skinned amphibians. They can breathe both water and air with equal ease, though their body isn’t entirely adapted to land-based life. They are roughly humanoid in proportion, though males are marginally taller. Vurk have a hairless head, which is instead topped by a crest, pointing up and back. Their eyes are black and bulbous, spread to the sides of their head to maximize field of vision. Their skin is leathery, and their hands have just three fingers.
csg_vurk.society: Vurk live a nomadic lifestyle, causing many other sentients in the galaxy to view them as primitive. This is very much false, however. Vurk are actually highly sophisticated, and many follow a complex philosophy. This philosophy particularly emphasizes personal freedom and honesty. This is a view shared by most Vurk, who will seek to avoid being controlled and possess a strong personal integrity. They are also very calm and cool. This makes many find diplomacy as a possible career path. Though they tend to get along very well, some also become formidable warriors. Defending integrity is seen as very important, so some Vurk, normally calm, can burst into angry action. Vurk are also well-adapted to travel the galaxy, as their nomadic ways greatly reduce any desire for a permanent home. Others use their intellect to find jobs as mechanics or doctors.
csg_vurk.language: Vurk speak Semblan, and many also know Basic. They are also typically literate in both. Semblan is a deep language of croaks.
csg_vurk.homeworld: Vurk come from Sembla, (historically known as Utavurk) a world of archipelagos and shallow seas of warm water. For all its potential as a resort planet, its volcanic nature forces a continual choice to be nomadic. Some deposits of coral and crystal provide a source of credits. It is relatively isolated, backwater even for an Outer Rim world. It also holds a reputation for neutrality, which it has protected with its many excellent diplomats.
csg_vurk.description: Vurk are nomadic amphibians with green skin. They are often very philosophical and emphasize honesty and integrity. They are very calm and measured. Despite this sophistication, being nomadic makes other species look at them as primitive.
csg_vurk.sidebar_text: For all its sophistication, Vurk culture still possesses a rather outdated system of marriage, in which families control the children. Males in particular often find themselves married off by their families, though time, as always, threatens to change the traditional ways. Those that are not married by adulthood typically remain bachelors. While most Vurk are content with this arrangement, some do seek change. Since this can make them outcasts in society, many choose to leave, attempting to start afresh in the larger galaxy, where opportunities are abundant.

csg_vuvrian.name: Vuvrian

special_abilities.name: Extra Eyes
special_abilities.description: Add boost on visual Perception checks. May see in all directions.

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Skin
special_abilities.description: May detect minute changes in air currents or air temperature to sense. May get a general sense of the amount of people in a room with an average Perception check. May recognize movements with a hard Perception check.

csg_vuvrian.physiology: Vuvrians are thin insectoids with twelve eyes. They are about as tall as humans, but they are much lighter. They have an oblong head with flexible antennae, and they typically have gray or brown fur. The most powerful abilities that Vuvrians have are their senses. Having twelve eyes benefits them in many ways and gives them powerful omnidirectional vision, but they also have extremely sensitive skin that can detect minute changes in air currents or temperature. This allows them to do many impressive feats, such as recognizing the amount of people in a room via its temperature. On the other side of this coin, they are extremely sensitive to pain.
csg_vuvrian.society: Vuvrians are peaceful, intelligent, and curious. Despite their odd appearance, they are very outgoing and often manage to be effective in social situations and even charming. They are known to be skilled in matters of argument and debate, and they have a knack for making others sympathize with them. This is in part because they are skilled at recognizing quirks in other cultures and typically have a genuine interest in understanding other peoples. They have had good relations with the Jedi, and many Vuvrians have become Jedi. Despite persistent xenophobia, many Vuvrians work with the Empire as negotiators and diplomats.
csg_vuvrian.language: Most Vuvrians know and are literate in Basic and Vuvrian.
csg_vuvrian.homeworld: Vurdon Ka is an Inner Rim world that is peaceful and picturesque. It is moss-covered and known for its gardens. Most Vuvrians consider it to be a perfect paradise.
csg_vuvrian.description: Vuvrians have twelve eyes and can see in all directions. They are insects and are also known for having sensitive skin, which allows them to have incredible sense via touch. They often are tourists because they are very interested in learning about the galaxy and its peoples.
csg_vuvrian.sidebar_text: Though many Vuvrians enjoy observing the sights of the galaxy and meeting new people, they are only motivated by curiosity. They are often seen as travellers and tourists, but they have little desire to live anywhere other than Vurdon Ka. This is in part because of the fact that they are almost never satisfied with living conditions off of their homeworld. Those that do settle have the puzzling habit of gravitating to planets with a harsher climate.

csg_weequay.name: Weequay

special_abilities.name: Thick skin
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Pheromones
special_abilities.description: May communicate silently with members of the same clan within long range in a way completely undetectable to other species that lack advanced olfaction.

csg_weequay.physiology: Weequays are stoutly built humanoids of about two meters in height. Forged by the harsh desert winds, their skin is rough, generally wrinkled and in shades of brown, gray, or black. To provide protection from the harsh desert sunlight, their eyes are sunken back. For males, their hair is long and typically braided into a single topknot, while females usually shave their head completely. Those offworld have individual braids in the topknot representing the number of Sriluur years spent away from home. On their chin and jawline, small bones stick out, similar to horns.
csg_weequay.society: Weequay society is complex but cold, pitiless, and brutal. They live in clan units whose members do not even have individual names, and they are expected to worship and make sacrifices to their gods. The gods represent both forces on the planet and native animals. The most important is Quay, representing their moon, and second is Am-Shak, the god of thunder. They must sacrifice worthy opponents to these gods, generally a large beast of some sort. Given the recent end to their war with the Houk, Weequays are more trained in modern technology and tactics, and some are now less satisfied by their primitive ways. These factors have caused a recent increase in the number of Weequays who live abroad in the galaxy. Such Weequays are notably silent, as they prefer to only speak among their own kind, and some will even go as far as hiring a non-Weequay to speak on their behalf. However, most are willing to name themselves when among non-Weequays.
csg_weequay.language: Between clans, Weequays speak Sriluurian, but within their clan, they use pheromones to communicate. Since this is completely silent, they often give a foreboding appearance. Those who leave Sriluur generally can speak Basic, although they generally have a deeper voice than most humans.
csg_weequay.homeworld: Weequays live on Sriluur, which is their homeworld as well as a Houk colony. The two species have fought over the planet for the past 200 years, and are now in an uneasy peace after ten years of open violence. It is inhospitable by most standards. A hot and arid planet, it is filled with deserts, acidic seas, and volcanoes. The planet, located on the Sisar Run just Coreward of Hutt Space, is on the edge of the Outer Rim. Sriluur is under constant intrigue, with the Weequays, Houk, Imperials, and Hutts all wrestling for power.
csg_weequay.description: Weequays mostly follow their god known as Quay, who gives them advice via simple toys. While lacking in technology, they are by no means straightforward. Many work for the Hutts. They can communicate with pheromones.
csg_weequay.sidebar_text: The name “Weequay” literally translates to “Follower of Quay,” and that is what most Weequays are. Most have a spherical totem that is considered to be a part of the god himself, and when shaken, it will give simple responses to their questions. They are expected to consult Quay before doing anything, even letting it control their marriages. Most other sentient races view Quay as a superstition and the totem to be nothing more than a clever child’s toy. Because of this, Weequays in more public positions will deny their use of Quay. On their homeworld, however, there is strong social pressure in favor of their god. Their religious shrines are called thal, and they are not allowed to be constructed offworld.

csg_whaladon.name: Whaladon

special_abilities.name: Aquatic
special_abilities.description: Can hold breath for a very long time and remove all movement penalties for being underwater, but may not move on land. Treat air as a dangerous atmosphere of rating 1.

special_abilities.name: Night Vision
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for darkness, add setback for brightness.

special_abilities.name: No Hands
special_abilities.description: May not wield normal weapons or pilot vehicles. May only carry objects if using wearable storage such as a backpack or utility belt.

csg_whaladon.physiology: Whaladons are a species of giant cetaceans who can grow up to 30 meters in length. Although they breathe air a few times per day, they are entirely aquatic, and they swim deep in the ocean. They have fins to propel them through the water, including a giant horizontal tail. They have a very wide mouth, which they use to feed on plankton and small fish. They have tiny eyes on the side of their head that see well in the dark, allowing them to dive deep into the ocean trenches. Their navy blue skin is covered in ridges, especially on their underside. There is a rare subspecies known as the humpback Whaladon, which has three humps on their back and lighter skin.
csg_whaladon.society: Whaladon society is isolated and peaceful, and they rarely interact with the Mon Calamari and Quarren who share their homeworld of Dac. They are social creatures with a rich musical tradition that has been passed down through the generations. Although few members of other species can understand Whaladon music, it can be appreciated by many. They are somewhat revered by other sentients, regarded as almost mystical wonders of the deep sea. Although Whaladons are generally peaceful, they strongly wish to be left alone and are known to attack submarines that cross into their territory.
csg_whaladon.language: Whaladons rarely know Basic or any of the other languages known on Mon Calamari, and they typically only speak their own language. The Whaladon language is a musical one, composed of their traditional sing-songs.
csg_whaladon.homeworld: Whaladons come from the world of Dac, also known as Mon Cala and, rarely, Mon Calamari. They share the world with several other sentient species, including the Mon Calamari, Quarren, Moappa, and Amphi-Hydrus. It is almost entirely ocean and contains both floating cities and underwater cities. They live outside the cities established by other species, wandering the depths on their own, although they have established an embassy of sorts near the city of Aquarius. Dac is one of the few worlds that has successfully driven off the Empire, although at this point, the Whaladons are typically indifferent to its politics.
csg_whaladon.description: A giant species of mammals the size of many starships, the Whaladons live only underwater. Native to Dac, they are peaceful and known for their sing-songs, but they are battling extinction.
csg_whaladon.sidebar_text: Several years ago, the Whaladons were nearly wiped out by a volcanic cataclysm, but they survived thanks to the coordination of a leader named Leviathor. Since then, Leviathor has acted as the leader of their race. However, the Whaladons are not in the clear yet: Shortly after the Battle of Endor, the Empire will reestablish their presence on Dac. Building the Whaladon Processing Center in the city of Aquarius and operating out of a giant submarine, they will hunt Whaladons for their meat, which will be considered a delicacy, often sold to the Imperial elites for their most exclusive banquets. The Whaladons will again face extinction, but Leviathor will contact the New Republic, who will rat out the Imperial operation in time to save the Whaladons. However, the Imperial hunting will wipe out almost all of the humpback Whaladons, with Leviathor being their only surviving member.

csg_whiphid.name: Whiphid

special_abilities.name: Thick Fur
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for cold conditions, add setback for hot conditions.

special_abilities.name: Claws
special_abilities.description: Deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_whiphid.physiology: Whiphids are large creatures, averaging about two and a half meters in height. They have thick brown fur, which protects them from their homeworld’s cold temperatures. Their face is mostly hairless, although hair can grow on their chin and atop the head. They have two fairly large tusks which protrude from the lower jaw. Their cheekbones are sunken in, and their face is elongated. Their nose appears as two slits in the face, and their black eyes are small. Their hands have three fingers, and they have three toes on each foot. Both end in claws.
csg_whiphid.society: Whiphid society on Toola is relatively primitive. They live in tribes, each with three to ten couples. They are ruled by an elder, who is known as the Spearmaster. Whiphids stay as families for survival reasons but generally don’t form emotional attachments with them. They travel across Toola on sleds, which are made from bone, tusk, and leather hide and are pulled by the domesticated Tuggles. They are nomadic during the winter, living on hunting grounds in animal hide tents. They are more stationary in the summer, when they make a base of operations. It is constructed from rock and covered with mud or animal hide. They hunt large animals like caraboose and motmot. Whiphids are solitary and aggressive in general.
csg_whiphid.language: The Whiphid language is simple, containing about 8,000 words. It is called Whiphid. It has no written form and consists of snorts, growls, and barks. Most Whiphids can speak it, although many cannot speak or understand Basic.
csg_whiphid.homeworld: A frigid world in the northwest portion of the Outer Rim, Toola is the home of the Whiphids. Is it filled with glaciers, frozen oceans, and a snowy tundra. Life is centered around the thin equatorial region, which is the warmest. There are also hot springs, which occasionally burst out of the ground. They are a vital resource for all of the native species.
csg_whiphid.description: Hunter-gatherers on the frigid world of Toola, Whiphids are strong and tough as well as experts with wilderness survival. They may be very violent and somewhat primitive, but they still understand the necessity of peaceful interaction and teamwork.
csg_whiphid.sidebar_text: Whiphid tribes interact surprisingly well. They rarely fight and will meet at hot springs. They trade together or unite on especially difficult hunts. War between tribes is unheard of, as is stealing or raiding. This is because Whiphids view fighting amongst themselves to be inefficient, since it reduces the number of available hunters. Bullies are also rare in Whiphid society. A bully is typically taken on a long hunt with his Spearmaster to “sort him out.” Should the bully fail to correct his ways, he typically never returns from that hunt. The aggressive nature of the Whiphids is more evident in relations with individuals.

csg_wol_cabasshite.name: Wol Cabasshite

special_abilities.name: Hardened Shells
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

special_abilities.name: Pressurized Organs
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for temperature.

special_abilities.name: Magnetic Communication
special_abilities.description: May communicate silently with other Wol Cabasshites within medium range in a way completely undetectable to other species. To speak to other species within medium range without touching, must pass a hard Discipline check, and may not be completely understandable regardless. May purchase a personal conveyance to translate, which costs 1,000 credits.

special_abilities.name: Limbless
special_abilities.description: Reduce encumbrance threshold by 4 and may not move without mechanical assistance, which costs 1,000 credits.

special_abilities.name: Unique Diets
special_abilities.description: Remove penalties for all toxins and do not take wound or strain damage due to vacuum, unbreathable atmosphere, or abnormal air pressure.

csg_wol_cabasshite.physiology: Wol Cabasshites are a smaller species of sentient mollusks that are parasitic, feeding on metals and plasma from wherever they are attached. Less than a meter long when they are curled up, Wol Cabasshites are composed mostly of a large stomach, and they have two eyes and a long tongue extending from one end of their body. They do not need to breathe at all, so they can survive in just about any pressure or atmosphere, even in the vacuum of space, so long as they have a food source. Their internal organs are pressurized, and they are also immune to temperature extremes. Because of their incredible natural hardiness, Wol Cabasshites are extremely long-lived. When they do need to reproduce, they expel their stomach lining, which grows into a new member of their species. They can do this asexually, but they can also be fertilized by one another via their tongue. Wol Cabasshites are unable to move on their own or speak aloud, but they can emit magnetic pulses and lick one another to communicate. However, this form of communication is very difficult to use with other species.
csg_wol_cabasshite.society: Wol Cabasshites are incredibly intelligent, but their strengths are in philosophy rather than technology. They devote their incredibly long life to contemplation, and because of how advanced they are in these areas, they can be almost impossible to truly comprehend, even if they communicate their ideas in a translated form. Although devices have been developed that interpret their magnetic signals, making them capable of speaking aloud, moving, or writing down their ideas, Wol Cabasshites have been mostly indifferent to them, and many continue a lifestyle of isolated contemplation.
csg_wol_cabasshite.language: For the Wol Cabasshites, communication is a blend of licking one another and manipulating magnetic fields to directly impact individual neurons. This works fine for communicating among their own, but it is very difficult to use as a way of speaking with other species, especially if they are not in physical contact with the one they wish to speak to. Although it has an almost musical quality, even those who spend decades with Wol Cabasshites are often baffled by their language.
csg_wol_cabasshite.homeworld: Wol Cabasshites come from the Outer Rim planet of Wol Cabassh, but their ability to survive in a vacuum means that they can be found all throughout the wider galaxy. They often attach themselves to starships.
csg_wol_cabasshite.description: An incredibly intelligent species of tiny mollusks, the Wol Cabasshites cannot move or talk on their own. They are capable of telepathy using magnetic pulses, but their philosophical musings are so bizarre and abstract that they are hard to comprehend regardless.
csg_wol_cabasshite.sidebar_text: Because they typically lack the motivation and the means to properly communicate, Wol Cabasshites are shrouded by mystery, and many believe they are capable of mind control. For the few who recognize their incredible intelligence, Wol Cabasshites are fascinating to study, but their philosophy can be impossible to comprehend by even the greatest minds of the rest of the galaxy.

csg_wookiee.name: Wookiee

special_abilities.name: Climbing Claws
special_abilities.description: Add boost when climbing surfaces that can be pierced by a claw. May also use claws for combat, dealing +1 Brawl damage as wounds.

special_abilities.name: Wookiee Rage
special_abilities.description: When using Brawl or Melee, deal +1 damage when wounded or critically injured.

csg_wookiee.physiology: Wookiees are tall, furry mammals who are over two meters in height. Their body is packed with plenty of muscle, making them excellent brawlers, and their temper is notoriously short. They have long limbs and retractable claws that they use to climb. These claws are never used for combat, which is considered to be extremely dishonorable. They are covered by fur that comes in shades of brown, white, gray, or black. It is darkest around the middle of their lifespan, which lasts several centuries.
csg_wookiee.society: Although their physique may give off the appearance of an intimidating brute, Wookiees are very loyal and honorable. This is best demonstrated in their life debts: Whenever someone saves the life of a Wookiee, that Wookiee will enter a life debt with them, pledging loyalty, and the only way to repay the debt is for the Wookiee to sacrifice his own life. They also form tight bonds with their biological family, and they can go into a rage when they are threatened. Wookiees are not merely warriors, however, and they are mechanically gifted, creating elegant weapons like bowcasters. They also once ran the secretive Claatuvac Guild, which made a network of secret hyperlanes across the galaxy. Prior to the Empire’s closing in on it, Guildmaster Gumbaeki transferred all their invaluable records to a dozen of his most loyal route mappers. However, the Wookiees first travelled into space on the starfighter of Trandoshan scouts whom they killed. Ever since, the species have fought intermittent wars, most of which ended when Republic mediators sided with the Wookiees. The Trandoshans got their revenge, however, now that the Galactic Empire has come to power and sided with them. Kashyyyk rebelled against the Empire from the start, while Trandosha worked with it to put down the uprising. Trandoshans now supply the Empire with the Wookiee slaves who worked on both Death Stars.
csg_wookiee.language: The Wookiees have a few languages, the most prominent of which is Shyriiwook. It and other Wookiee dialects, such as Xaczik, is a combination of grunts, roars, and growls. Humans and most other species are incapable of pronouncing Wookiee languages, just as Wookiees cannot speak Basic. Despite this, almost all Wookiees understand Basic, and surprisingly many non-Wookiees can comprehend Shyriiwook.
csg_wookiee.homeworld: Wookiees come from the forests of Kashyyyk, a prominent Mid Rim world. It is covered in wroshyr trees, which are kilometers tall. Wookiees inhabit the seventh level of the forest, which is near the canopy, since it gets more dangerous as height decreases. Although they have advanced technology, they still live in wooden huts, which are connected using kshyy vines and bridges to form cities.
csg_wookiee.description: Short-tempered but loyal, Wookiees are a furred species and are very strong. Their rivalry with Trandoshans has made them enslaved. They are also known for life debts, which state that a Wookiee who is saved by someone must devote their life to serving him.
csg_wookiee.sidebar_text: When venturing into the depths of their homeworld, Wookiees are hunted by creatures dangerous even to them. There are no records of one returning from the forest floor, but they do on occasion go as low as the fourth level, where the dangerous quillarats live. These needle-hurling creatures must be hunted in a rite of passage called the hrrtayyk, which can be done alone, with friends, or with an older relative. After the hunt, they keep a trophy and often take a new name. Quillarats are also used in marriage proposals, which are even more difficult, as the male Wookiees traditionally complete that hunt without a weapon.

csg_woostoid.name: Woostoid

special_abilities.name: Scholars
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Improved Researcher.”

special_abilities.name: Easily Flustered
special_abilities.description: When in combat or when presented with an extremely chaotic situation, must pass a hard Discipline check or become disoriented for 2 rounds.

csg_woostoid.physiology: Woostoids are thin humanoids with a tall, noseless head and sunken cheeks. Their skin generally has an orangish tint. They have large, black eyes that rarely blink, and their hair is generally long and red. They have no visible ears, just holes in the sides of their head. Most Woostoids prefer to wear long robes.
csg_woostoid.society: A very pacifist people, the Woostoids are extremely averse to warfare, mostly because of their frail build. They are a very logical people, and they excel at finding patterns and connections, but they can become extremely flustered when they witness chaos or randomness. In those cases, they become frustrated by the futility of their search for explanation. Because of their preference for order, Woostoids are strong supporters of the Empire and other centralized governments, even though they are disturbed by the Imperial love of war. Their skills with logic make them excellent researchers, and they also excel in computer technology. Woostoids operate the HoloScan Database, a gigantic library which is recognized to be one of the Wonders of the Galaxy. A kilometer high and several kilometers wide, it is one of the best places in the galaxy to conduct detailed research. Others focus on data analytics or bureaucratic occupations, where they are also very well-suited.
csg_woostoid.language: Woostoids speak Woostese, a language which is very precise, but it also has many different regional dialects. They have no abbreviations or contractions, as they believe that their language is already optimized. Because of how often they interact with other species, most Woostoids also speak Basic.
csg_woostoid.homeworld: Woostoids come from Woostri, an Expansion Region planet with highly advanced technology. It has become a major vacation spot, known for beaches, amusement parks, and theaters. Tourists are welcomed by the Woostoids.
csg_woostoid.description: Mathematically-inclined sentients who value structure, the Woostoids have been able to automate much of the businesses on their world, so they have to work very little. They are very pacifist, and they are easily distraught whenever there is chaos or disorder.
csg_woostoid.sidebar_text: Computer industries have made the Woostoids very wealthy, and many of the businesses on Woostri are almost entirely automated. To take advantage of this advanced technology and combat unemployment, the Woostoids have expanded both taxes and government welfare programs, allowing most of the species to live easily off of businesses that basically run themselves. Now, they work very little, and they have been able to shift their focus towards recreation.

csg_wroonian.name: Wroonian

special_abilities.name: Friendly Demeanors
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Kill with Kindness.”

special_abilities.name: Underworld Savviness
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Street Smarts.”

csg_wroonian.physiology: Wroonians are slightly shorter than humans, but they are almost identical in terms of build and internal anatomy. However, they are visually distinguished by their blue skin and yellow eyes. Furthermore, they tend to have darker hair than humans.
csg_wroonian.society: Seen all throughout the galaxy, the Wroonians are a successful species who have become very wealthy thanks to their powerful trade guilds. They love to travel and explore, both in space and over oceans, and many are smugglers or traders. They are very easy to get along with, a fun-loving and friendly people who excel in social situations of all sorts. This is a skill which helps them in many fields of work, from politics to crime. Wroonians are also known as excellent storytellers, and they will rarely pass up an opportunity to boast about their accomplishments. Although they have been skeptical of Palpatine’s power since the Clone Wars, they continue to live peacefully and successfully under Imperial rule.
csg_wroonian.language: Wroonians speak their native language of Wroonian.  Because of their prominence in the galaxy off of their homeworld, almost all of them know Basic very well and can speak it without issue.
csg_wroonian.homeworld: Wroonians come from the relatively small but very wealthy Inner Rim planet of Wroona, which is mostly covered by oceans. Its continents are long and thin, covered by forests and mountains, but the planet is best known for its beaches, and the Wroonians also have a strong tradition of seafaring for commerce. They have many colonies, including the arid, mountainous world of Saleucami, which means “oasis” in the Wroonian language. This is because all of the other worlds near Saleucami are barren and uninhabitable.
csg_wroonian.description: Blue-skinned near-humans who have been financially successful, the Wroonians' charisma and love for travel has allowed them to excel in many ventures across the galaxy. Many are religious, which they display via their tattoos.
csg_wroonian.sidebar_text: Wroonians are very spiritual, although it is a more materialistic faith than that of many other cultures. One of the most important ways that Wroonians express their devotion is actually through their appearance: Pious Wroonians have tattoos on their face and ornate traditional robes that are decorated with tassels.

csg_xamster.name: Xamster
csg_xamster.physiology: Xamsters are reptilians with loose skin in shades of yellow, green, and blue. With short legs, they are only about one meter tall. They have four digits on each of their limbs. They have a long neck and lack hair, although their head is topped by two large, pointed ears. Their face features a beak-like mouth and red eyes. Three vertical crests traverse across their body: one at the back of their head, one on their stomach, and one on their lower back. The Xamsters’ most distinctive ability is their reflexes: Their brain is very advanced when it comes to processing sensory inputs, and they are able to think and react somewhat quicker than other species. Many Xamsters do not wear clothing, but they often carry bags and pouches.
csg_xamster.society: Xamsters live symbiotically with a semi-sentient species of fungi on their world called malvil-trees. These unique life-forms are each bound to a single family unit of Xamsters. The Xamsters name their tree, and they treat it like a pet by fertilizing it and providing it with food. In exchange, the malvil-trees obey the family of Xamsters that lives with them, moving its branches on command and allowing them to live inside of it. Xamsters also harvest their tree’s spores, which can be used for a number of tasks, including ones that induce paralysis or improve vision. Malvil-trees will sometimes eat creatures that pass by, but if a Xamster is coated by their spores, they will be granted safe passage and recognized as equals. Although Xamsters have a somewhat primitive lifestyle, they are perfectly capable of using technology if they need to. With other species, they tend to be reasonably nice and well-mannered, although they have a strange social custom in that they must repeat a question before they answer it.
csg_xamster.language: Xamsters rarely speak Basic and typically only speak their native tongue of clicks and growls.
csg_xamster.homeworld: Xamsters come from the Outer Rim planet of Xagobah, which has a blue sun. It is of diverse terrain, including jungles, swamps, and mountains, but all of it is covered by vast amounts of fungi, which release many spores into the air. These spores generally require offworlders to take medications and antidotes before travelling to Xagobah, and they cast the entire planet in a hazy mist.
csg_xamster.description: A smaller reptilian species with incredible reflexes, the Xamsters have yellow or blue skin and a beak-like mouth. They live symbiotically and peacefully with the semi-sentient malvil-trees on Xagobah, but their lifestyle was disrupted when the Clone Wars were brought to them, and both sides drafted the Xamsters.
csg_xamster.sidebar_text: Xamsters are peaceful by nature and detest violence, but they were dramatically impacted by the Clone Wars. Wat Tambor came to their world to conduct biological research on their unique fungi sixteen months after the Battle of Geonosis, setting up the Mazariyan fortress. Later in the war, it was besieged by the Republic, which turned into a very large battle. During the conflict, both sides forcibly recruited Xamsters to fight for them, forcing the peaceful natives to take up arms for the first time to fight in a war that had nothing to do with them. The event was a traumatic one for their entire society, and many of the malvil-trees died because they were unattended.

csg_xexto.name: Xexto

special_abilities.name: Courage
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Confidence.”

special_abilities.name: Four Arms
special_abilities.description: May have twice as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

csg_xexto.physiology: Xexto are short and very thin creatures with relatively long limbs. They usually stand at just under one and a half meters tall. Their torso is tiny, and they have two arms coming from each shoulder, each of which has four long fingers including opposable thumbs. Their feet have four long toes as well, and they generally stand entirely on their toes. Their skin is a pasty chalk-white but can also be lavender or pale yellow, and their almond-shaped eyes are a blue or dark purple.
