As adults, they have a very long neck, which connects to their hairless, noseless head, but Xexto young have similar neck length to humans. Their young also lack the ability to use all four of their arms independently, instead doing everything with pairs of arms, perhaps a failsafe for climbing around in treetops. Their brain is actually split, with the head portion controlling primitive actions and the part in the stomach dealing with logic and creative thinking.
csg_xexto.society: Xexto value courage but are still very even tempered. They admire risks, excitement, and thrill-seeking, and they rarely back down from a dare. Many enjoy the sport of Podracing. Questioning the courage of a Xexto is one of the worst insults. However, they are otherwise not prone to dramatic emotion.
csg_xexto.language: Xexto speak Xextese, and although most Xexto are fluent in Basic, they are generally only literate in Xextese.
csg_xexto.homeworld: Xexto come from the world of Troiken. It is a very unique world in that it is tidally locked, and only a thin strip is habitable. One half is an extremely hot desert, and the other half is a cold tundra. The inhabited middle band is made up of dense forests and mountains. The Xexto live in the trees and are still trying to deal with the Challat eaters, which are carnivorous, palm-sized insects that attack in swarms. It is a hub for Podracing and the site of the Stark Hyperspace War, which set up several pieces in Palpatine’s rise to power.
csg_xexto.description: Xextos are short four-armed creatures with pale skin who are known for their courage and recklessness. They are often thrill seekers and few will back down from a challenge. They are distant relatives to the Quermians, who are opposite to them in many ways.
csg_xexto.sidebar_text: Long ago, when Xexto were in hunter-gatherer tribes, their records tell of an account where strange offworlders gave some of them a chance to “see a whole new world,” and these Xexto never returned.

csg_xidec.name: Xi’Dec

special_abilities.name: Extra Limbs
special_abilities.description: May have 3 times as much gear in their hands and do not have to suffer strain for a second maneuver. Still may not make 3 maneuvers in a round without “Unmatched Mobility.”

special_abilities.name: Long Limbs
special_abilities.description: May reach twice as far, and increase encumbrance threshold by 3.

special_abilities.name: Silhouette 2
special_abilities.description: Large Xi’Dec have a silhouette of 2.

special_abilities.name: Flight
special_abilities.description: Can move on the vertical axis and ignore any penalties for terrain. When flying, move twice as quickly.

special_abilities.name: Silhouette 0
special_abilities.description: Messenger Xi’Dec have a silhouette of 0.

special_abilities.name: Spears
special_abilities.description: Deal +2 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 3.

csg_xidec.physiology: Xi’Dec are a species of incredible diversity based on gender, each of which is capable of fulfilling a highly specialized role. This makes Xi’Dec incredibly adaptable as a species, as genders can change in frequency in order to respond to new circumstances. Depending on which genders are involved in parenting, Xi’Dec can reproduce by giving birth live, laying eggs, budding, or a number of other unique options. Children never have the same gender as either parent, and Xi’Dec have more than 180 officially catalogued genders, but there are countless more that have only a handful of members, remaining obscure and unknown. The most common are the Xi’Alpha, who compose six percent of the population. Xi’Alpha have a shiny black carapace with vestigial wings. They have eight legs, and they are able to stand on any two and use the others as arms. Their head features mandibles surrounding a mouth, six slits to smell with, and a dozen eye stalks. All are somewhat insectoid, but other genders include warriors with spears for arms, small but nimble messengers who can fly, and constructors with long limbs. Some are humanoid in shape, some are significantly larger than other Xi’Dec, and others can develop claws, antennae, or natural armor.
csg_xidec.society: Gender has a huge impact on how a Xi’Dec acts, and they tend to have a one-dimensional personality and a narrow skill set. All live within their family units, however, and they tend to focus on advancing their entire family rather than achieving individual goals. Otherwise, they can be very diverse in political structure and organization. They have little interest in mass production because of their diversity, but they excel in biology, geology, and climate sciences.
csg_xidec.language: Xi’Dec tend to be excellent linguists, learning Basic, their native tongue, and often other languages.
csg_xidec.homeworld: Xi’Dec come from Stic, an Outer Rim planet with a rapidly changing climate that is currently very hot. Their unique society attracts some tourists.
csg_xidec.description: Eight-limbed insects who display incredible genetic diversity, the Xi'Dec have hundreds of genders, each of which is highly specialized to fill a particular job. Those with rare genders are seen as very valuable because of their unique skill sets.
csg_xidec.sidebar_text: Because genders are so specialized, having more genders in their family gives Xi’Dec a huge advantage and allows them to become more powerful and technologically advanced. Members of rare and more specialized genders often take advantage of this, demanding huge compensation for marrying. Xi’Dec also often mistake other species for rare genders.

csg_yaga.name: Yaga

special_abilities.name: Starship Experts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Solid Repairs.”

csg_yaga.physiology: Yagai are a species of insects with three legs, the third pointing behind them to make a sort of tripod. They are fairly thin, and their hands have nine deft fingers each, making them adept at precise mechanical work. Their head is perched atop a long neck, and it has a long snout as well as two antennae. Yagai have purple skin and yellow hair. There also exist genetically modified Yagai, who can be up to three meters tall and are extremely muscular. These are drones designed for manual labor, and they require neither food nor air, making them ideal for work in space. However, they are barely intelligent.
csg_yaga.society: Yagai value their technical prowess above all else, and they are particularly skilled in hyperdrive design. Their society is arranged into hives, which have a caste system. Although they can be very territorial, they were overall cooperative members of galactic society during the time of the Old Republic. They typically wear white, blue, or purple, which they perceive as neutral colors.
csg_yaga.language: Due to their enslavement, all Yagai are forced to learn Basic.
csg_yaga.homeworld: Yagai come from Yaga Minor, a temperate planet in the northern Outer Rim. Its gravity is slightly above-average, and its terrain includes jungles, mountains, and caves. Currently, it is of utmost political and military importance due to the Imperial shipyards in orbit.
csg_yaga.description: The Imperials have forced the insectoid Yagai into service at their shipyards of Yaga Minor. These three-legged insects are very technologically gifted, and they have a drone caste that can survive in a vacuum.
csg_yaga.sidebar_text: Yagai were well aware of the many Imperial atrocities when they were first coerced by the Empire, so they were quick to submit in order to avoid an even worse fate. They are effectively slaves, and although they resent being controlled by the Empire, most are too fearful to do anything about it. Yagai encourage one another to take up useful professions and be as productive as possible in order to appease the Emperor. Most work at the Imperial shipyards over their homeworld, while others are sent throughout the galaxy to maintain the vast Imperial fleet. Yagai despise their predicament and as well as the simpleminded drones created by Imperial geneticists. The drones, for their part, do nothing but obey and rarely speak unless spoken to. Although not as intelligent as baseline Yagai, they are still sentient, and many of them secretly hate the Empire and would like to join the Rebel Alliance. Ultimately, the Imperial Remnant will ban slavery in the years following Palpatine’s death, and the freed Yagai will continue to build Imperial ships, this time for their own profit.

csg_yaka.name: Yaka

special_abilities.name: Cyborgs
special_abilities.description: If implants are removed or disabled, reduce Intellect by 2 and may increase Presence by 1 after a month of recovery. Implants cost 10,000 credits after character creation and do not count toward the cybernetic implant cap.

csg_yaka.physiology: Yakas are humanoids on the larger side—they average two meters tall, and they have well-muscled limbs. Like many of the galaxy’s species, this higher strength comes at the cost of intelligence, as they are naturally simpletons who are unskilled in technology. However, the Yakas are beneficiaries of a centuries-old Arkanian experiment which gave them cybernetic implants. These implants have enhanced their mental capabilities, making them highly intelligent. Because of their cybernetics, they have an expressionless face and have metal plates wrapping around their head.
csg_yaka.society: Yakas are not especially friendly; they are often seen as emotionless and stoic because their cybernetics make it hard to express emotions via facial expression. They excel in technological tasks, and many of them wish to grant their children these same abilities. As such, almost all Yakas will give their children cybernetic brain implants. Most Arkanians are proud of the Yaka species, as they demonstrate a successful project which benefited a lesser species and made them more advanced. However, there are some who question the ethics of implanting Yakas with the cybernetics, as the Arkanians conducted their experiments forcibly after conquering the Yakas.
csg_yaka.language: Although they can speak Basic without issue, Yakas also know their native language of Yakan.
csg_yaka.homeworld: The Yaka homeworld is also called Yaka, found in the Colonies. They live very close to the icy planet of Arkania, which is the home of the species who first gave them the implants.
csg_yaka.description: Yakas are large near-humans who are relatively unintelligent by nature, but many have been given cybernetics that make them much smarter. However, the cybernetics make them harder to get along with: They become more stoic, and their humor becomes very dark.
csg_yaka.sidebar_text: A side effect of the cybernetics is how it affects the Yakas' psychology. Because of their advanced intelligence and ability to quickly solve problems, they grow bored very easily. In order to entertain themselves, many Yakas are constantly coming up with sarcastic retorts or pranks. This tendency is persistent even in situations that other species would consider too dark for humor. As such, Yakas will often find irony and comedy in even the saddest deaths. Despite this oddity, their cybernetics are still seen as incredibly advanced.

csg_yamrii.name: Yam’rii

special_abilities.name: Serrated Forelimbs
special_abilities.description: Deal +2 Brawl damage as wounds and have a crit rating of 3. Reduce encumbrance threshold by 2 and may not carry items in hands. May not use technology requiring fingers, such as blasters. At the GM’s discretion, add up to 3 setbacks on checks where fingers are beneficial, such as Piloting.

special_abilities.name: Hardened Carapaces
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Enduring.”

csg_yamrii.physiology: Yam’rii, also known as Huk, are sentient vespids, although their mantis-like appearance is more reminiscent of their Verpine relatives. They are a fearsome species, over two meters tall and protected by durable chitin which can be green, gray, or brown. Their neck is long and narrow, and they have a triangular head with wide, black eyes on either side. They have small nostrils and a wide mouth. For natural defense, they have spikes on the back of their head and on their shoulders. Their rest of their body is split into a thorax and a pointed abdomen. Their limbs are thin but powerful, and they have two-toed feet. Their arms are long and have two joints each. Some have two fingers but lack thumbs, while others have no hands at all. Although this makes it difficult for them to hold objects, those who lack hands have forelimbs which are pointed and serrated, making them deadly weapons in combat. They are carnivores, and they especially enjoy eating eggs.
csg_yamrii.society: Yam’rii are a quick-tempered people who are violent and have little respect for others. They are capable thieves, especially when it comes to eating eggs. As such, many Yam’rii will devote time to stalking various birds or reptiles, such as the Quor’sav. They are militant and ruled by warlords, although they are still intelligent enough to have advanced technology and engage in galactic commerce.
csg_yamrii.language: Yam’rii can speak Basic. It is unknown if they also use a native language or not.
csg_yamrii.homeworld: Yam’rii come from the forested world of Huk, and they also rule a number of other colonies such as Kalee, Abbaji, and Tovarskl, which they exploit for slaves and natural resources.
csg_yamrii.description: A naturally aggressive species of insects, the Yam'rii have a small empire in the Outer Rim and have no qualms about violently colonizing primitive planets. They are inclined towards combat, especially those who lack hands and instead have sharp, serrated forelimbs.
csg_yamrii.sidebar_text: Yam’rii have a history of imperialism, as they have recognized its necessity to achieve prosperity in the galactic economy. They set up colonies on many nearby worlds, and their location on the fringe allowed them to take whatever they could. Exploitation of natives became common, and the Yam’rii became prosperous. However, they ran into trouble one they encountered the Kaleesh, a warlike species capable of fighting back. The Yam’rii began to lose, and they eventually decided to cut their losses and leave the Kaleesh alone. However, the Kaleesh warlord, Grievous, was not satisfied: He continued the crusade and attempted to force the Yam’rii to abandon their other colonies. Just when Yam’rii colonialism seemed over, they finally used their political influence to demand a Republic intervention. With help from the Jedi, the Kaleesh were butchered and enslaved. In the end, the Yam’rii colonies were restored.

csg_yarkora.name: Yarkora

special_abilities.name: Creepy Demeanors
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Intimidating.”

special_abilities.name: Keen Senses
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks from Perception checks. Remove 2 setbacks for concealment from combat checks.

csg_yarkora.physiology: Yarkora are mammals descending from ungulates. Slightly taller than most humans, they possess large, three-fingered hands and are covered in thin fur. Their brown skin is similar in color to the fur. They do have rougher fur that can be more varied in color above their mouth and behind their head. They are further distinguished by a head with a long snout pointing forward. Their eyes are split off to the sides of their head, giving them good peripheral vision. These eyes are quite effective, possessing incredible vision. They also have a large nose and ears which are much more effective than those of humans. They also have a multitude of additional organs that make them much tougher than most humans.
csg_yarkora.society: The Yarkora are a very mysterious people, so very little is known about their culture. Most of what is known is based on how they behave when travelling the spacelanes. They are incredibly secretive, unwilling to discuss their background with outsiders. Few are even willing to be friends with outsiders. Most are also loners, seen with no other Yarkora around them either. Though they have never been represented in any government (no one knows of their homeworld or government) a few have gotten involved in the Galactic Civil War. Most others seem to focus on selfish goals, working for criminal types. They are very unnerving and even creepy, so they can often get any information they need in exchange for going away. Most of the time, they instead rely on other tactics. This includes their skills as con artists, their keen senses, and their knack for making others talk. Married Yarkora live apart and rarely meet.
csg_yarkora.language: Yarkora speak Yarkora, although they only speak Basic when around outsiders.
csg_yarkora.homeworld: The Yarkora homeworld, supposedly in the Outer Rim, is one of the many mysteries surrounding the species. It is rumored to be arid.
csg_yarkora.description: The Yarkora are among the most mysterious peoples in the galaxy, as they are very tight-lipped about their culture and origin. They are very secretive, but they are surprisingly adept at using charm and other forms of manipulation o get what they want.
csg_yarkora.sidebar_text: Just because the Yarkora are so secretive doesn’t mean their culture doesn’t exist. Players controlling a Yarkora should consider the various mysteries of Yarkora culture and try to better flesh out the species. While they should tell their GM, keeping it secret from the other players can provide many opportunities for interesting roleplaying as well. However, the detached nature of the Yarkora may make it difficult for the PC to get along, so being a Yarkora shouldn’t be chosen lightly.

csg_yevetha.name: Yevetha

special_abilities.name: Dew Claws
special_abilities.description: May extend or retract dew claws as an incidental. With extended dew claws, deal +1 Brawl damage as wounds and have a Crit rating of 2 and Vicious 1.

csg_yevetha.physiology: Yevetha are thin and ghoulish. They have an extremely powerful ability in their retractable dew claws, blades that can come out of their wrists. These are as long and almost as effective as a vibroblade. They have small spikes all over their body, generally on their chin, back, and one on their forehead. The largest of these spikes are where humans would have ears. They have black, red, or blue eyes. They are bald and have a very small nose. Their skin is generally yellow or green. They have six-fingered hands and six-toed feet, all of which end in claws. Children need to drink blood to survive, which is typically given to them by their mother. They give birth with eggs, which they call “birth casks.”
csg_yevetha.society: Yevetha are a persistent and extremely violent people. They are obsessed with death and do not believe in incarceration or imprisonment. They are a very religious people, and their religion is centered around blood and sacrifice. The Darama, who leads the religion, is also the Viceroy, who is the political leader. They are also extremely hierarchical. The higher castes are completely justified in killing those of a lower caste, even without any particular reason. While Yevetha can lose status, they cannot gain it. They still consider lower-class Yevetha to be better than non-Yevetha, who are considered to be nothing but vermin. They believe themselves to be the only form of intelligent life in the universe. They learn new skills quickly and have become excellent with technology. In war, they are absolutely brutal but somewhat erratic: They never surrender and ignore humanitarian consequences.
csg_yevetha.language: The Yevetha are isolationist and xenophobic, so they detest Basic and refuse to learn it. As such, almost all of them only speak their language of Yevethan.
csg_yevetha.homeworld: The Yevetha come from N’zoth, a Core World in the Koornacht Cluster. Any Yevetha on N’zoth are enslaved by the Empire and work in shipyards. It is arid and harsh. Giat Nor is the capital.
csg_yevetha.description: Yevetha are thin, ghoulish near-humans with very sharp retractable claws. Though now Imperial slaves, their roles will soon be reversed, as the Yevetha have extreme xenophobia and view any non-Yevetha as vermin.
csg_yevetha.sidebar_text: The Imperials have had a great effect on the Yevetha. Now conquered by the Empire, they have become entirely enslaved. They are treated brutally by the Imperials with a cruelty that matches what they might have towards other sentients. The shipyards where they work are successful and make quality ships. Although the Yevetha seek to eliminate the Imperials, the many attempts at revolution have been put down. They will need to wait for several more years, when Ysanne Isard will pull ships back to the Core Worlds. Since the Imperials are human, the Yevetha will have no qualms about treating them just as cruelly as they are now treated.

csg_yinchorri.name: Yinchorri

special_abilities.name: Cold-Blooded
special_abilities.description: Remove 2 setbacks for hot conditions, add setback for cold conditions.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 3.

csg_yinchorri.physiology: The Yinchorri are a species of cold-blooded reptilians who are much larger and stronger than humans. They also boast great endurance and better tolerance for pain. One of the most unique aspects of their biology is a resistance to telepathic uses of the Force such as mind tricks. Yinchorri have a turtle-like head with yellow eyes and two nostrils at the front of their snout. Their skin is typically green or brown.
csg_yinchorri.society: Yinchorri are strong-willed and believe that anything is morally acceptable as long as they are capable of doing it. They are a violent people who are vicious and unruly, and they will use force to take what they want. Although they are quick to fight, they are still very loyal in marriage and with their family. They typically distrust aliens at first but can change their mind with time. Their planet is arranged into city-states that have their own political and military structures. Their society is also divided into castes: the Intelligentsia, who govern, and the warriors, who fight. However, for all their warlike tendencies, neither caste is any good when it comes to military tactics and planning. They are also a religious people who believe in legends of a spirit world that coexists with reality.
csg_yinchorri.language: Most Yinchorri speak Yinchorri and Basic but are only literate in Yinchorri.
csg_yinchorri.homeworld: Yinchorr is an Expansion Region world composed mostly of rocky deserts. It is primarily agricultural. They also have colonies within their system on the ocean world of Yitheeth and the gas giant of Yibikkoror.
csg_yinchorri.description: Strong, cold-blooded reptiles with green skin, the Yinchorri believe that "might makes right." This philosophy led to an uprising in 33 BBY, an event which ended in the defeat of their military and the isolation of their people.
csg_yinchorri.sidebar_text: After joining the Republic in 58 BBY, the Yinchorri were introduced to a great deal of new technology, which they were quick to embrace. In 33 BBY, they also received cortosis armor thanks to manipulation by Darth Plagueis and began to take territories. First, they took the Golden Nyss Shipyards, then Mayvitch 7, and they murdered the Jedi diplomats sent to them. After that, a large invasion by Jedi and Judicials defeated the Yinchorri, and their system was again left isolated. Although a small Imperial presence was eventually developed, they are still mostly left alone. This will eventually change once the Yinchorri oppose the Empire in 3 ABY, when Yinchorr will be bombarded and cleansed of all Yinchorri.

csg_yodas_species.name: Yoda’s Species

special_abilities.name: Force Prodigies
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on any 3 Force powers.

csg_yodas_species.physiology: A smaller species of green-skinned humanoids, members of Yoda’s Species are most distinguished by long ears similar to those of Lanniks. Their hands and feet each have three front-facing digits, each ending in a longer nail, and they also have a backwards-pointing toe on each foot. They have prominent wrinkles on their face, including a grid of ridges on their forehead. They only have hair behind their head, and they have a small nose and eyes. They are an extremely long-lived species, often living over 900 years.
csg_yodas_species.society: Yoda’s Species is a peaceful one that tends towards a life of detached philosophy and contemplation. They are entirely Force-sensitive, but they are extremely few in number. They study and meditate on the Force for all of their lives, only meeting with one another to teach the young or debate, and they mostly survive off of primitive agriculture, augmented by the Force. Their views tend to match up very well with Jedi teachings, but they are much more passive. Similar to Jedi, they do not bond with their family: Children typically change hands through a multitude of genetically unrelated parental figures throughout their first century of life.
csg_yodas_species.language: Members of Yoda’s Species speak Basic, but they have developed unique grammatical structures in recent millennia that change word order.
csg_yodas_species.homeworld: They come from a Deep Core planet with no offworld contact. It is teeming with plant and animal life but is mostly wilderness, with each of them watching over a vast tract of land.
csg_yodas_species.description: Yoda's species is a great mystery, their name and homeworld unknown to the rest of the galaxy. They are short creatures with green skin and long ears with a long lifespan, and their only known members have been associated with the Jedi Order.
csg_yodas_species.sidebar_text: Although all are Force-sensitive to some extent, it is only those who are strongest in the Force that earn the right to become Jedi. These elect few are chosen at birth, and they are the only members of the species who travel offworld. They only bother to maintain a single ship for their entire species, known as the Yaniket, which takes the babies to the Jedi Temple on Coruscant and then flies back automatically. Babies are sent off with numerous holorecordings which teach them their name, advise them in the ways of the Force, and expose them to the unique grammar associated with the species. These Jedi often take decades to watch all of the recordings, after which they learn only from their Jedi companions. Although other Jedi welcome them into the Order, their mystique means that they are generally loners, detached from their fellow Jedi.
csg_yodas_species._provenance_note: The Yoda’s Species species appears in the EU, but almost all of their societal details are introduced by this guide.

csg_ysannan_human.name: Ysannan Human

special_abilities.name: Projectile Guidance
special_abilities.description: When firing a ranged weapon with physical projectiles, such as grenades or a slugthrower, may spend a maneuver beforehand to roll a number of Force die equal to Force rating as part of the pool. May spend pips to gain success or advantage on the check.

csg_ysannan_human.physiology: The Ysanna are a tribe of humans, indistinguishable from the baseline species and fully capable of breeding with them. They descend from survivors of the Cron Supernova, who included many Jedi, so they are entirely Force-sensitive.
csg_ysannan_human.society: Ysanna are a group of primitive humans, and they tend to be superstitious, with a mystical view of the Force. The history of Jedi knowledge and wisdom has been deeply distorted by millenia of isolation and hardship, and they view its power as pure magic. However, they are very loyal and still have a deep reverence for the Jedi tradition, protecting the ruins of the Great Library of the Jedi as a sacred site. Sith influence is also present among them, such as in the Sith masks which they will wear in battle. Their homeworld, Ossus, has limited offworld contact, and the Empire has forbidden any from visiting it to study the Jedi. For the past decade, some Ysanna have been ruled over by a Dark Jedi named Travgen. Ysanna have a limited knowledge of the Force, but they excel in using telekinesis to guide their Concussion bow slugthrowers, and they are capable of becoming Force ghosts.
csg_ysannan_human.language: Ysanna have a native language called Ysannan and typically do not speak Basic.
csg_ysannan_human.homeworld: Ysanna come from Ossus, once a lush world that was rendered toxic by the detonation of the Cron Cluster. It is plagued by chemical and electrical storms, and it has an unpredictable orbit around a binary star system. Over the millenia, it has gradually become more habitable, with vegetation and animal life slowly returning, but it remains a harsh planet covered by steep mountains and canyons. Long after Yuuzhan Vong Sar, Vong Shapers will terraform the planet to its lush original state.
csg_ysannan_human.description: A primitive culture of humans on Ossus, the Ysanna revere their Jedi ancestors who once thrived more prominently on their world. Now, they have fallen under the sway of the dark side.
csg_ysannan_human.sidebar_text: Ossus will reenter the galactic stage when it will be rediscovered by Luke Skywalker and Kam Solusar in 10 ABY. The Ysanna will at first fight the offworlders, but once they realize that he is a Jedi, they will be reverent, and allow the visitors access to the ruins. Two Ysanna will train as Jedi, Jem Ysanna and Rayf Ysanna, both of whom will die not long after. Due to these tragic fates, Luke will be hesitant to train other Ysanna as Jedi in the future. However, the Jedi Order will relocate to Ossus after the Yuuzhan Vong War, and the Ysanna will welcome them. This will last until the Second Galactic Civil War, at which point Darth Caedus will force the Jedi to evacuate.

csg_yuuzhan_vong.name: Yuuzhan Vong

special_abilities.name: Force Immunity
special_abilities.description: When being targeted by Force Powers, cause the check to automatically fail.

csg_yuuzhan_vong.physiology: Yuuzhan Vong are humanoids from another galaxy with lavender, gray, or yellow skin. They are somewhat larger than most humans and live for much longer. They have a sloped forehead on their ridged head, and about half have pointed ears. Their nose is very short and stubbed, so they have an almost skeletal appearance. A few have black hair, though many are bald. Some have small protrusions under their eyes, which are generally blue. They have a very unique nervous system which is more sensitive. They themselves are entirely cut off from the Force, meaning that their actions are impossible to foresee, their mind is impossible to read, and their body is impossible to manipulate.
csg_yuuzhan_vong.society: The Yuuzhan Vong are a very religious people who are reverent towards pain. They glorify it as a way of living, believing that their body is made to be sacrificed for their many gods. Many cut themselves or even sever limbs. While they never impair their abilities, some with higher standing do amputate themselves before replacing their limbs or organs with those of another creature. Those who fail in the process of getting implants or do not adhere to religion are called Shamed Ones. The Shamed Ones are slaves who are viewed as cursed and completely expendable. They are forbidden from attending the religious services that the other Yuuzhan Vong consider to be vital. In these services, they generally draw blood as worship. They are ruled by a Supreme Overlord, who can supposedly communicate directly with their main god, Yun-Yuuzhan. The Intendant Class focuses on politics.There is also a Warrior Caste, who devote themselves to battle. The Shaper Caste specializes in creating biotechnology. Their Priest Caste specializes in religious matters. Workers, the largest caste, do menial labor. The Yuuzhan Vong children are raised by designated caretakers, and they do not know their families until they are older. They place high value in discipline and obedience.
csg_yuuzhan_vong.language: The Yuuzhan Vong speak Yuuzhan Vong. Some understand Basic using tizowyrm translators.
csg_yuuzhan_vong.homeworld: Their original homeworld of Yuuzhan’tar is destroyed, but the Yuuzhan Vong have reached the outskirts of the galaxy. They live in space aboard giant worldships, planning an invasion that will come in about 30 years. After killing trillions but losing the war, they will resettle on Zonama Sekot. Most will then live peacefully, but a few will attempt to restart their war against the galaxy in 46 ABY, and a few will ally with the One Sith over subsequent decades.
csg_yuuzhan_vong.description: The Yuuzhan Vong will eventually bring about an incredibly brutal war and be responsible for hundreds of trillions of deaths. This is because of their powerful organic technology and religious convictions. They value pain, sacrifice, and death as service to their gods.
csg_yuuzhan_vong.sidebar_text: Yuuzhan Vong are notable for possessing biotechnology. They detest electronic technology, and most do everything in their power to kill and destroy those with technology. While this includes electronics, they also hate other contraptions. They have created lots of organic things, including ships, weapons, armor, and computers. In addition to conquering and killing those who use technology and destroying the technology itself, they also seek to Vongform planets by bringing their own unique forms of life.

csg_yuzzum.name: Yuzzum

special_abilities.name: Friendly
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Smooth Talker.”

special_abilities.name: Mobile Predators
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Outdoorsman.”

csg_yuzzum.physiology: Yuzzums are furry humanoids with long, thin limbs. They are typically taller than most, at above two meters, although some dwarf Yuzzums are born. These are almost always social outcasts. They have no neck, though their face varies. Some have a wide mouth with notable teeth, while others have fangs. They have eyes that can be black or yellow. They have four fingers, hooves or claws as feet, and hairless arms and legs. The rest of their body is covered in thick, brown fur.
csg_yuzzum.society: Yuzzums still live a primitive lifestyle. While some have managed to craft spears and basic tools, others live completely without technology. They hunt small creatures such as ruggers. Some have tamed arachnids, which are called rakazzaks. They can be found offworld for a few reasons. Some have established colonies. Others are taken as musicians, something that they are innately talented with. Also, despite their sentience, some still end up as pets. These ones are typically captured and taken offworld in mass. Yuzzums can be a bit shy but get along well if given the chance. They are brave, however, and their large size can scare off many predators.
csg_yuzzum.language: Yuzzums speak Yuzzum, which is musical by nature. This makes many of them excellent singers. Some are taken offworld to be singers.
csg_yuzzum.homeworld: Yuzzums come from the Forest Moon of Endor, in the Moddel sector. This obscure moon orbits a gas giant and is relatively close to the Unknown Regions. It is composed of forests mainly, with huge trees. Later, it will be host to the construction of the Second Death Star, a major battle in the Galactic Civil War, and the death of Emperor Palpatine. The star system is currently backwater, obscure, and rarely traveled to by other sentients. Nearby astronomical hazards ensure that passing ships are highly likely to crash, which has given Endor its wide variety of immigrated species.
csg_yuzzum.description: Yuzzum are tall primitives from the forest moon of Endor. Their musical language makes many of them excellent singers, so some use that as a profession should they leave their isolated homeworld. Though shy, they are very friendly and typically get along well.
csg_yuzzum.sidebar_text: Yuzzums share their moon with another primitive yet sentient species in the Ewoks. This is a somewhat strained relationship. Most Yuzzums do not know the Ewok language, but mostly because many Ewoks know the Yuzzum language. Despite this ability to communicate, the primitive species still do what they must to survive. For the Yuzzums, this can mean eating baby Ewoks, which are called woklings. The Yuzzums and Ewoks live mostly separately, each going about their own unique way of life. They also share their world with the rodent Teeks, aquatic Gorphs, and the Ewok’s cousins, the Duloks.

csg_zabrak.name: Zabrak

special_abilities.name: Fearsome Countenances
special_abilities.description: Add advantage on all Coercion checks.

csg_zabrak.physiology: Zabrak are tough near-humans that are best distinguished by their horned head. Zabrak have many subspecies that have varying skin tones and horn patterns. Though the arrangement of horns varies, all of these subspecies have about ten, and they are about three centimeters long, starting their growth during puberty. While most subspecies have dark hair, they generally do not grow facial hair. One rarer subspecies does have eyebrows. Their skin is similar to human skin in the various colors that it comes in. They have a high tolerance for pain as well as a second heart.
csg_zabrak.society: Zabak are determined and confident, striving for greatness and working hard to get it. Though they don’t generally develop arrogance in their success, they are strongly competitive, particularly amongst their own colonies and subspecies. As eager explorers, they are proud of their race, their home, and their colonies, and they believe that nothing is impossible if they work hard enough. Constantly attempting to prove their doubters wrong, they accomplish tasks with dedication, hard work, and an intense focus. The independently-natured Zabrak do not like living under Imperial rule, and their defiant spirit gives many the will to fight back. The Empire has responded with harsher penalties, increased taxes, and more garrisons. This has only increased the animosity between Zabrak and Imperials. The Zabrak are also notable for having facial tattoos, which come as thin lines. They are received in a rite of passage and can show the individual’s history, lineage, personality, or achievements.
csg_zabrak.language: Zabrak speak their native tongue of Zabraki as well as Basic. Most are also literate in both languages, and their voice tends to be a low-pitched baritone.
csg_zabrak.homeworld: Iridonia, the Zabrak homeworld, is a harsh planet with dangerous fauna, acid pools, and windy canyons. It is in the northern part of the Mid Rim and situated on the Coruscant-Dantooine hyperlane. The Zabrak also have eight colonies in addition to their long-evolved offshoots on Elom.
csg_zabrak.description: Zabrak are strong-willed and disciplined near-humans distinguished by horns. They have a very high pain tolerance and believe that they can achieve greatness if they work hard enough. Their stubbornness has led to a strong resistance against the Empire on Iridonia.
csg_zabrak.sidebar_text: Zabrak have developed strong martial traditions, and those on Iridonia have developed a physical style of martial arts in order to combat the rugged terrain or because of Sith influence, depending on who you ask. It is mandatory for all children to learn it in school, so Iridonian Zabrak number among the best martial artists in the galaxy. They fight with a quarterstaff called the zhaboka. Although Zabrak on the colonies share the Iridonians’ drive for excellence, they tend to apply it in other fields, such as science, math, art, entertainment, or history. Others take to the field of engineering, as they make excellent weaponsmiths. Although they do not manufacture in mass, their vibroblades and blasters are second to none.

csg_zehethbra.name: ZeHethbra

special_abilities.name: Spray
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as a maneuver, may spray a biochemical compound that affects all engaged non-Zehethbra. Those affected must succeed in a daunting Resilience check or suffer 4 strain and be disoriented for 1 round.

csg_zehethbra.physiology: The ZeHethbra are furry mammals who typically defend themselves through releasing a gaseous compound that can stun or slow down enemies. They are somewhat larger than humans and are typically stronger. Their four-fingered hands have claws for traction, and they also have a small tail. Those from the south have white or blue fur, while those from the north have red or brown fur. Either way, they generally have a white stripe of fur that goes from their dog-like nose up their forehead, over their head, and down their back. Their face is very canine, having black eyes, triangular ears, a snout, and pointed teeth. Their combination of acute smell and pheromones allow them to easily identify one another through scent.
csg_zehethbra.society: ZeHethbra come from many cultures, as the species has divided into more than 80 slightly different groups. All of these groups value honesty, leadership, and status. They are organized into clans of extended families, which they can identify by smell. ZeHethbra value their clans and do what they can to gain status within them. They often leave their homeworld and explore, so the ZeHethbra have many colonies. One such colony on Malastare caused them to go to war with the Dugs.
csg_zehethbra.language: The ZeHethbra speak a language of the same name. To an outsider, it sounds like an angry series of grunts and gurgles. Most eventually learn Basic as a second language.
csg_zehethbra.homeworld: ZeHethbra come from the Mid Rim planet of ZeHeth. It is temperate, with mountains and forests making up much of the terrain. It has giant trees which are filled up with urban centers. The roots of these trees are used as underground lairs and dens. They also have many colonies, including one on Malastare.
csg_zehethbra.description: Violent and easily offended, ZeHethbra are furred canines that are devoted to defending their territory. They have a biochemical spray to ward off attackers.
csg_zehethbra.sidebar_text: The ZeHethbra are best known for their outbursts of anger. They are easily ticked off, getting highly offended by what others consider a minor insult. They are particularly sensitive when it comes to personal space and defending their territory. They will generally growl or spit in response to any insult, but these outbursts can escalate. When they are amongst their own, this typically results in a competitive match of snorting. In some cases, they will attack when aggravated, using their physical strength and biochemical sprays to get revenge. These attacks rarely are intended to be fatal.

csg_zeison_sha.name: Zeison Sha

special_abilities.name: Vehicle Experts
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Fine Tuning.”

special_abilities.name: Telekinesis
special_abilities.description: Receive the mentor discount on the Move Basic Power and the Protect/Unleash Basic Power.

csg_zeison_sha.physiology: The Zeison Sha are composed of a variety of species, including Rodians, Twi’leks, Duros, and humans. Descended from Jedi, many are Force-sensitive.
csg_zeison_sha.society: The Zeison Sha have a fiercely independent culture built on self-reliance and toughness. They have very tightly-knit families and take care of their kin, but they otherwise prefer isolation. This can make them somewhat selfish, which has drawn some over to the Dark Side, but such beings are quickly hunted down by other Zeison Sha. Their warriors are particularly skilled in telekinesis, which they use for attacks, but they can also use the Force to create protective barriers around themselves. Their weapon of choice is typically the discblade, which is circular with a handle in the center and four blades on the ends. They throw it, use the Force to guide it towards their target, and then pull it back into their hand. Others use the Force to imbue it, making it more durable.
csg_zeison_sha.language: The Zeison Sha have no known language of their own and typically speak Basic.
csg_zeison_sha.homeworld: Zeison Sha come from a rural planet on the edge of the Outer Rim which is called Yanibar. It is a harsh world, with dangerous fauna, minimal vegetation, and frequent storms. Its climate is one of extremes, with dry, scorching summers and frigid, snowy winters. It has an Imperial garrison
csg_zeison_sha.description: A multitude of colonist species that settled on the planet Yanibar, Zeison Sha formed an independent and resilient culture.
csg_zeison_sha.sidebar_text: Zeison Sha may have descended from Jedi, but in the 2,000 years since they diverged, they have become very bitter towards the Jedi Order. Their ancestors were originally colonists, trying to escape from the Sith-controlled Outer Rim in the New Sith Wars. They intended to set up a temporary refuge on the uninhabited world of Yanibar, then reunite with other Jedi, but their allies never came. Stranded, they likely would have died if not for their Force powers, and they came to view their fate as abandonment by the Jedi. A few other colonists arrived centuries later, but the society kept itself hidden from the warlords in the rest of the galaxy until the New Sith Wars ended with the Battle of Ruusan. At that point, a few ventured into the galaxy, but they never mended their relationship with the Jedi. They were horrified to learn that the Jedi separated children from their families, and to this day, they will not leave their children alone with Jedi.
csg_zeison_sha._provenance_note: Zeison Sha are comprised of multiple genetically unrelated species. However, since they share a culture and homeworld, they are all on this page.

csg_zelosian.name: Zelosian

special_abilities.name: Gregarious
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Galaxy Mapper.”

special_abilities.name: Nighttime Blindness
special_abilities.description: Remove setback for brightness, add setback for darkness.

special_abilities.name: Photoautotrophic
special_abilities.description: Do not require normal food, surviving only off of sunlight, Carbon Dioxide, and water for long periods of time.

special_abilities.name: Unique Digestive System
special_abilities.description: Remove all effects of alcohol, but suffer similar effects from sugar.

csg_zelosian.physiology: Zelosians appear to be a near-human species, sharing a similar build to humans as well as hair and facial features. However, they are actually very different at the fundamental level. Zelosian heritage is one of plants, and they suspect that their humanoid appearance, sentience, and ability to move are all the result of careful genetic engineering. Although they are capable of eating foods like humans, they can also survive using photosynthesis, thanks to the chlorophyll in their blood, which turns it into a green sap. Unlike humans, they are unaffected by alcohol, but they can be intoxicated if they eat sugar. The most obvious visual difference between Zelosians and humans are in their eyes: Zelosian eyes are always bright green, and they cannot see in darkness.
csg_zelosian.society: Fitting for their physiology, Zelosians are known for their knowledge of plant life, and they also enjoy studying biology in general. They are a gregarious people, but they have a deep-seated fear of darkness. All of their mythology uses light to represent good and darkness as evil, and one of the most terrifying events for them is called the Day of Sepulchral Night. Occurring less than once per century, it is an eclipse that also causes the lowest tides that the planet ever sees. They stop their lives during the eclipse, remaining indoors out of fear. Another will come soon, shortly after the Battle of Endor.
csg_zelosian.language: Zelosians speak their native language of Zelosian, and many also know Basic.
csg_zelosian.homeworld: The Zelosian homeworld, Zelos II, is a mountainous Mid Rim world with many oceans. It has four moons, which are responsible for dramatic tides. A backwater world with about 10 million people, its largest industries are mining and tourism surrounding its spas, casinos, and oceans.
csg_zelosian.description: Near-humans at first glance who are actually plants, the Zelosians are photoautotrophs who tend to enjoy learning about the galaxy and all the life it contains. They are very superstitious, having a deep-seated fear of darkness, which represents all that is evil in their mythology.
csg_zelosian.sidebar_text: Zelosians are currently serving the Empire through their mining industries, but they are kept in the dark about this fact. After the Battle of Endor, the Zelosians will become fully independent and establish themselves as a neutral planet, although they will remain under martial law. The Empire will continue to maintain a secret mining operation in the months following the Battle of Endor, but it will be destroyed by the Zelosians, who will then join the New Republic.

csg_zeltron.name: Zeltron

special_abilities.name: Pheromones
special_abilities.description: Emit pheromones automatically, adding boost on all Charm checks and adding 1 advantage to all Deception and Negotiation checks. Does not apply on targets with breath masks or without lungs.

special_abilities.name: Empathy
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as a maneuver, sense the presence and emotional state of everyone within short range. May use this ability to upgrade the difficulty twice when opposing a Deception check.

csg_zeltron.physiology: Zeltrons are near-humans that tend to be attractive in build. They have black, red, or dark blue hair and pink or red skin. Aside from that, they have no other visual differences from humans. However, they have unique special abilities that add further to their charms. First are pheromones: Similar to Falleen, they can emit pheromones into the air as a way of manipulating others. In addition, they have a limited telepathic ability, allowing them to read emotions. They have an excellent metabolism, staying in good shape despite often eating the richest of foods. Because they have two livers, they are very resistant to alcohol.
csg_zeltron.society: Zeltrons value living life to its fullest and having fun. They are generally careless in nature and tend to easily give in to their own laziness. Their reckless attitude and knack for charm makes them naturals as scoundrels and con artists, but perhaps the most well known characteristic of Zeltron culture is their romantic nature: They shun monogamy and tend to obsess over their pursuit of love. They make no secret of it and are known to dress in shockingly revealing attire. Because of their empathy, they also have a strong cultural focus towards positive emotions like joy, love, and pleasure, while they strongly shun anyone who they can tell is feeling anger, fear, or sadness.
csg_zeltron.language: Zeltrons speak Basic and have no notable languages of their own.
csg_zeltron.homeworld: Zeltrons come from Zeltros, an Inner Rim world. It is ruled by an elected monarch and is economically successful as a hub for luxury. One of the most expensive vacation destinations, it includes art, casinos, theaters, dining, parties, and (most popular of all) the Zeltrons themselves. It has its fair share of wealthy immigrants, typically vacationers who end up staying.
csg_zeltron.description: Zeltrons are red-skinned near-humans who have pheromones that make them more attractive. They are also empaths, so they are extremely effective in social situations. They are lazy, reckless, and focus on being happy. They are also very romantic and shun monogamy.
csg_zeltron.sidebar_text: Zeltrons have certainly developed a reputation as being lazy, careless, and, most notably, inappropriate, but these do not represent every member. Some Zeltrons could very well not follow these stereotypes, but they still have to deal with the consequences of their species’s reputation. Not only this, but they can very well become an exile when among their people, with social pressures forcing them to leave their home.

csg_zeuol.name: Zeuol

special_abilities.name: Dispersed Organs
special_abilities.description: Receive the talent “Durable.”

special_abilities.name: Sensitive Ears
special_abilities.description: Add 2 boosts on auditory Perception checks. Triple all sonic damage and, at the GM’s discretion, increase sonic damage from 0 to 1.

special_abilities.name: Ponderous
special_abilities.description: May only spend 1 maneuver moving per turn.

special_abilities.name: Spores
special_abilities.description: Once per day, produce a dose of spores which are toxic when paired with the opposite gender Zeuol spores. Infected humans suffer one wound per hour and one critical injury per 6 hours until dead or healed by a daunting Medicine check.

csg_zeuol.physiology: To some, the Zeouls appear as a fairly standard near-human species. They see creatures of a humanoid size, upright stature, and a typically pale face with a nose, mouth, and ropelike hair. Their eyes, appearing dark, wide, and often hollow, might seem as their strangest feature, alongside the metal that many implant into their scalps. However, this is only an artificial shell that encloses the Zeuols’ true form: Within their flowing robes and underneath their hollow facemask, they a strange blob of lumpy fungal matter, usually in a mottled mix of dark brown and bone white. The use of robes to disguise their lower half is largely a matter of social norms, but the shape of their mask matching a human face is essential. This is because the Zeuols are evolved to grow within human corpses. Every contour of human skin and bone allows the Zeuol cells to know where it is and how it must function. First the torso, then the limbs, and last the head. But Zeuols are more than parasitic plants: They’re intelligent, and they’ve developed the ability to get their own limited usage out of the fungus growing within limbs. The Zeuols’ “arms” and “legs” can reanimate their host, although many of the finer joints, including the “fingers,” are nonfunctional. Their sensory organs, including beady eyes and very sensitive ears, are on the torso. Their unique structure also allows them to survive extreme wounds.
csg_zeuol.society: Zeuols who attempt parasitism are rare and shunned by their own kind, who generally get along very well in human society, where they are known for their methodical and perceptive nature. Living without families, they are generally quiet loners, listening well and speaking rarely. Many are academics or writers.
csg_zeuol.language: Zeuols have a melodic voice, and being so adapted to living among humans, usually speak only Basic.
csg_zeuol.homeworld: The Zeuols’ homeworld of Ord Zeuol is a populous Mid Rim planet of about half humans and half Zeuols.
csg_zeuol.description: Zeouls are an odd species of ambulatory fungi that grow within human corpses, reanimating the decaying bodies. In modern times, most instead rely on synthetic bodies that can support them more effectively and provide nutrients for longer.
csg_zeuol.sidebar_text: In their natural life cycle, Zeuols deposit spores onto human foods so their offspring are eaten. The spores are usually harmless and go into dormancy within human intestines, where they can survive for years. However, if a person digests both male and female Zeuol spores, the two fuse, forming poisonous fungal cells. The host often dies within a matter of days, and out of their corpse, a new Zeuol emerges. On rare occasions, Zeuols will produce a diploid spore, which is toxic without a mate and can grow into a perfect clone of its forbear. The process of a Zeuol growing up and consuming a corpse takes about two years, at which point they starve and die. However, Zeouls have discovered that by replacing human hosts with elaborate artificial shells, they can extend their lifetime up to forty years and enhance their abilities. Mechanical implants in their host carefully dole out of nutrition to the fungus and can be resupplied by inserting organic material into a machine in the chest cavity. Whereas most Zeuols in human corpses can barely stand upright and need to drag themselves around, those in artificial ones can manage to stand and walk in a way that almost looks human, and they can hold gear via magnets on the arms.
csg_zeuol._provenance_note: Little is known about the Zeuol. The following information is almost entirely made up. Players are not obligated to follow this, but it is encouraged that if not, they imagine their own aspects of Zeuol physiology and culture, rewriting stats accordingly.

csg_zygerrian.name: Zygerrian
csg_zygerrian.physiology: Zygerrians are near-humans with some reddish fur. They are mostly distinguished by their superior strength and the four bony appendages on their chin. They have red-brown fur surrounding their face. They have wide triangular ears at the upper half of their head and a mostly feline appearance with otherwise angular features. They have some fangs in their mouth, which is typically frowning.
csg_zygerrian.society: Zygerrians are most notorious as a culture for their acceptance of slavery. It is a central focus in their philosophy, and they believe that the strong have the natural right to control the weak. They believe in strength above all else, both physically and mentally. Signs of weakness are a taboo to them, and they always try to be seen as strong. Those who do show weakness can end up being slaves themselves, or even executed. They are very hated, although it is somewhat intentional: Fear gives them power. In addition to slavery, they are known for all sorts of violence, such as piracy and warfare. They have a long tradition of settling their differences by a fistfight. Their society is heavily divided by class. Those of noble blood receive the best positions, most slaves, and most respect. The most powerful noble is a monarch, while the other less powerful nobles get to take up an “honorable” position in their military.
csg_zygerrian.language: Zygerrians mostly use Basic in a heavy accent, but they also have their own language, Zygerrian.
csg_zygerrian.homeworld: Though they travel the galaxy, Zygerrians originate from Zygerria. It is an Outer Rim world of great underworld presence, although its impressive architecture brings in a few tourists from the Core Worlds. The planet is otherwise full of mesas.
csg_zygerrian.description: Zygerrians are most notable for almost always working as slavers. They believe that the strong have the right to control the weak and have little compassion. They are physically strong and have feline characteristics.
csg_zygerrian.sidebar_text: Zygerrians have had a long tradition in slavery, which has put them at odds with the law for a long time. Though they mostly got away with their practices under a very corrupt Old Republic, they have had cases of attempting to overreach their Slave Empire and have been quashed by the Jedi or other military. During the Clone Wars, with the Republic and Confederacy busy fighting a war, they again tried to expand by making an under the table deal with Darth Tyranus, who supplied them with slaves captured in secret via his battle droids. However, they again got too aggressive and again underestimated Jedi prowess. Despite that, they are now in a very good position under the Empire. Emperor Palpatine (who ordered Tyranus into dealing with them two decades earlier) has allowed slavery, and their Zygerrian Slave Empire is thriving as well as ever. Many Zygerrians are now quite wealthy.

csg_tlanda_til.name: t’landa Til

special_abilities.name: Empathic
special_abilities.description: Once per encounter as an incidental, may suffer 1 strain to cause a nearby being to experience a particular emotion to a minor extent.

special_abilities.name: Vibrating Neck Pouches
special_abilities.description: May suffer 1 strain to vibrate neck pouch, creating sonic and subsonic vibrations that bring strong pleasure to anyone within medium range. This cannot affect any being that cannot hear. Those affected may develop an addiction similar to when using a narcotic.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: When targeted by a telepathic Force Power, increase the difficulty by 2.

csg_tlanda_til.physiology: The t’landa Til are a species of horned reptilians distantly related to Hutts. They are two meters tall or more and longer than they are tall. They are quadrupedal, and all of their legs are short and wide. Their arms, however, are the opposite: long and thin with four fingers. They also have a thin tail. Their skin, typically a grayish brown, is extremely loose with folds and wrinkles, especially around their neck. This skin is similar to Hutts in that it is thick and oily. They are also similar to Hutts in many other ways. They can live for several centuries and are resistant to Jedi mind tricks. Like Hutts, they lack a neck and have a wide mouth, but they are distinguished by a prominent facial horn atop their forehead. Their white eyes have no pupils. Their internal biology is unique as well. They have three stomachs and two hearts. Perhaps the most unique aspect of the t’landa Til, however, is found only in the males. Using their inflated neck pouch, they can create vibrations, both sonic and subsonic, that female t’landa Til find to be pleasurable. They call this “Exultation.” It is made much more valuable in that it has similar effects on both males and females from a majority of other sentient species. It is very similar to a narcotic in that the pleasure experienced is extremely addictive. Male t’landa Til also have minor empathic abilities that use telepathy to trigger emotions, although they are much less powerful than the vibrations.
csg_tlanda_til.society: As relatives to the Hutts, the t’landa Til are similarly willing to conduct immoral activities of all sorts. T’landa Til lack the success of the Hutts, however. Although some have had success in crime, almost all of them still lack both the wealth and the power that most of the Hutt kajidics possess.
csg_tlanda_til.language: The t’landa Til have their own language, t’landa Til. They are also practical enough to sometimes know more common languages such as Basic and Huttese.
csg_tlanda_til.homeworld: Like the Hutts, the t’landa Til come from the swampy Outer Rim world of Varl. A cataclysmic event of some sort left the planet as a wasteland, so both the Hutts and the t’landa Til were forced to evacuate. Many relocated to Nal Hutta, a swampy world found in what is now called Hutt Space.
csg_tlanda_til.description: The t'landa Til are the less notable relative to Hutts, a quadrupedal species of large reptiles with a horn atop their head. Males have a telepathic ability to manipulate emotions, and they can also emit vibrations which can be addictive.
csg_tlanda_til.sidebar_text: The t’landa Til often work with the Hutts, as was demonstrated with a particularly clever snare on Ylesia. Using male t’landa Til, the Hutts would conduct religious ceremonies as part of the made up “Cult of The One and The All.” As people experienced Exultation, many would become addicted and convert. They would then go on a pilgrimage to Ylesia, where they would improve themselves through hard work- the hard work of mining spice for the Hutts. None would resist for fear of being denied Exultation. Although this particular scheme on Ylesia has been foiled, there is no doubt that other t’landa Til use their abilities to conduct similar operations.

tor_dashade.name: Dashade
tor_dashade.description: A species comprised of large reptilian humanoids, the Dashade are not commonly encountered throughout the galaxy. Their homewold was lost in a massive supernova triggered by an ancient Sith superweapon, with only off-world colony Dashade surviving.

special_abilities.name: Force Resistance
special_abilities.description: Upgrade the difficulty of Force power skill checks targeting a Dashade once.

special_abilities.name: Dissipating Hide
special_abilities.description: Dashade remove [SE] imposed due to hot or radioactive environments. They add [SE] [SE] to any checks made to detect them with thermal sensors.

tor_dashade.physiology: Standing up to two meters tall, most Dashade are of burly stature. Their skin takes shades from beige and olive green over various tints of gray to black. Their arms end in claws, signs of their predatory heritage, and their thick skin renders them resistant to radiation. Furthermore, it is able to dissipate heat quickly, making Dashade adept at surviving in hot environments and making them difficult to pick up on thermal sensors. Dashade are born with a natural resistance to the Force, making them interesting travel companions for Jedi and Sith alike.
tor_dashade.society: Not much is known of the original society of the Dashade, as most records were lost along with their homeworld. The survivors and remnant colony population took to a more adventurous lifestyle, with many using their inherent abilities to become mercenaries or freelancers. Their resistance to the force also led to them easily finding employment as combat instructors to Jedi or assassins and warriors for the Sith.

_book_notes.homeworld: With Urkupp having been lost in the Cron Drift supernova at the end of the Great Sith War, the Dashade became a species without a true homeworld. Though their further outlying colonies survived, many others had to look for new homes, finding them in the galaxy’s outer rim, including worlds of the Sith Empire such as Korriban and Dromund Kaas.
_book_notes.language: Though Dashadi was their native tongue, featuring hard consonants and hissing sibilant noises. Following the supernova, most Dashade adjusted to Basic in order to allow easier communication with other species of the galaxy.

tor_echani.name: Echani
tor_echani.description: The Echani are a near-human species from the galaxy’s inner rim. With martial arts being an integral part of their culture, and honorable duel as a form of communication, they are often regarded as skilled warriors, in a similar vein to Mandalorians.

special_abilities.name: Communication by Combat
special_abilities.description: Echani may spend [AD] [AD] from a Brawl, Melee or Lightsaber check to discover their targets motivation or gain insight into their emotional state.

tor_echani.physiology: While anatomically similar to humans, Echani are distinguished by their very light skin, white hair and silver eyes. Within families, their facial features are remarkably similar, making it difficult for outside observers to tell related Echani apart. The Thyrsian subspecies of Echani starkly contrasts their traditional appearance, with dark skin and dark hair, an evolution that originated on the sun-baked planet of Thyrsus - one of the Echani worlds.
tor_echani.society: Echani society is matriarchal and caste-based, and puts high value in combat skills and martial arts talents. To them, a fight is the purest form of communication, which reveals everything about who a person is, and what they believe in. Within their culture many events such as traditional Firedances involve displays of martial grace. Due to the high biological similarities between family members, detailed knowledge of a person’s body movement has become the preferred way of identifying people. The Echani combat style mostly relies on unarmed or melee combat, making use of swords, staves and other more traditional implements. On the occasions where they do don armor, it is always a light armor set, as heavier ones would restrict their fluid movement too much. In a true Echani duel, combatants wear no armor and carry no weapons, making it the truest expression of their talent and skill.

_book_notes.homeworld: Originating from Eshan, the Echani have populated neighboring planets such as Bengali and Thyrsus, forming confederacy of six worlds, known in their culture as the Six Sisters. Their government is comprised of a central, all-female council known as Echani Command. The atmospheres of their planets are all habitable to most other humanoids, as required by their near-human biology.
_book_notes.language: Few records exist of an original Echani language, as their adoption into the galactic community quickly saw Basic become their language of choice. Adding to this, the species’ culture relies far more on body movement and sparring matches to communicate, making them appear rather silent and reserved to outsiders.

tor_miraluka.name: Miraluka
tor_miraluka.description: The Miraluka are a near-human species with a strong natural connection to the force. They are born without eyes, yet this connection allows them to still navigate and perceive objects and people around them.

special_abilities.name: Force Sight
special_abilities.description: Miraluka are blind from birth but rely on the Force to perceive their environment. They remove any [SE] added to their checks as a result of smoke, darkness or concealment, but add [SE] [SE] to any checks that require precise investigation. They may never benefit from equipment that relies on the user’s vision. Should a Miraluka become disconnected from the Force, they lose any benefits of Force Sight and incur all the penalties of the "Blinded" Critical Injury.

tor_miraluka.physiology: Miraluka are anatomically very similar to humans, sharing typical body types and appearances, though with a slightly lower lifespan. They lack eyes, with skin covering the vestigial eye-sockets of their skull. As a result, they recognize their surroundings through their connection to the force, which allows them to “see”, though not in a manner comparable to humans. Any Miraluka is force sensitive to a degree, though not all of them chose to follow a path that has them capitalize on this connection.
tor_miraluka.society: Miraluka are thoughtful, cautious, and deliberative species. Most of them show little interest in personal gain or glory, believing in strength in unity and living as community instead. They commonly refer to other Miraluka as “sister” or “brother”, treating any of their species as parts of a large family - a gesture rarely extended to outsiders as well. For social reasons, Miraluka often hide their unusual appearance by covering their missing eyes with a blindfold, hood, helmet or other headwear. Their natural receptiveness to the force, while a powerful ally, also leaves Miraluka open to emotional distress. Strong events in the force, such as the destruction of civilizations or planets could be felt by most members of their species. Additionally, encountering a lifeform not connected to the force can prove rather shocking and confusing to Miraluka, as they are unable to sense and perceive them as they normally would. Miralukan religion is founded in the ancient philosophies of the Greater Force. Those dedicated to this belief worship Ashla and Bogan, deities representing the light and dark side of the force, though they interpret them not as good and evil, but rather life and death, constants that must be kept in balance for the sake of the galaxy.

_book_notes.homeworld: The Miraluka have made their home on Alpheridies, adopting this world after their original homeworld was rendered uninhabitable by its depleted atmosphere. With its position not near any of the central trade routes, the Miraluka were mostly undisturbed until the Mandlorians invaded their world during the Great Sith War. They were freed from their conquerors by the Republic, after which a Jedi academy was erected on the world to test and train the many Miraluka gifted in the Force. In the following conflicts, the world has switched allegiance many times, often as a result of military invasion by the Sith Empire and ensuing liberation by the Republic.
_book_notes.language: Though the native tongue of Miralukese exists, all Miraluka children grow up learning basic. With quite a few of them being considered for the Jedi academy and subsequent service in the order, this bilingual upbringing is helpful in integrating into the galactic society more easily.

tor_rattataki.name: Rattataki
tor_rattataki.description: A warrior culture stemming from a hostile outer rim world, the Rattataki grow having to fight for everything in their life. Across the galaxy, they are known as ruthless mercenaries, bountyhunters and Sith warriors.

special_abilities.name: Culture of Violence
special_abilities.description: For their violent nature, Rattataki are poorly regarded across the galaxy. They add [SE] to any Charm, Deception, Leadership and Negotiation checks they make, but they add [BO] to any Coercion checks. This does not apply when interacting with other Rattataki.

tor_rattataki.physiology: Rattataki are near-human, though their skin takes shades between grey and chalk white and they do not grow hair on their heads. Their upbringing on a harsh world hardens them from childhood on, making them resilient, cunning and tough. Most Rattataki feature dark facial tattoos, and some adorn their face further with jewelry and piercings.
tor_rattataki.society: Rattataki live in tribes that constantly fight each other of the sparse resources available. Even outside those civil wars, fighting is deeply rooted in their society. Wrong or right are not decided in court, but in the gladiatorial pits, with the person who emerges victorious being in the right. This development is mostly brought by the isolation the Rattataki have faced from the galaxy, as their homeworld lies far off any trade route and borders wild space. Following the outbreak of the war, the Sith Empire took in countless Rattataki, many as slaves, though some came voluntarily, to be made into soldiers. Those that showed sensitivity to the Force were trained to be Sith Acolytes to serve as assassins and warriors.

_book_notes.homeworld: Rattatak is a rocky world with harsh conditions which makes it unreasonable for colonization. What exactly prompted the development of a sapient species here still eludes scholars, though one of the theories assumes them to be the descendants of a stranded exploration mission. Rattataki settlements are traditionally hewn into the stone pillars and dug deep into rocky chasms, protecting them from the environments. The infamous gladiatorial pits are located on the lowest levels of those settlements.
_book_notes.language: Though their native tongue of Rattataki is still spoken on the homeworld, few outsiders ever hear it. Instead, the Rattataki prefer to address anyone in Galactic Basic, reserving their own language to be used solely among themselves, to not be overheard.

tor_sith_pureblood.name: Sith Pureblood
tor_sith_pureblood.description: In true irony, Sith Purebloods have long since been a hybrid species, which is only faintly rooted in the true Sith species which existed millennia ago. Having interbred with humans, Sith Purebloods is a term for those individuals of the hybrid species that still posses a physiology close to the ancient Sith.
tor_sith_pureblood.physiology: Sith Purebloods are easily identified by their red skin, ranging from dark crimson to lighter pinkish hues. Their facial structure features pronounced bone ridges especially at their eyebrows, across their forehead and along their jawline. Some are also born with tendrils growing from their cheeks or chin. Their eyes take shades from yellow to orange or red and their hair is dark red, brown or black in color. All Sith Purebloods are Force sensitive and feel a natural pull towards a darkside, which is encouraged from a young age.
tor_sith_pureblood.society: Following the collapse of the original Sith species and its society during the multiple conflicts with the Republic the hybridization nearly completely diluted their genetics in the human population of Korriban and the other worlds of the Empire. Those born as Sith Purebloods and showing the relevant physiological traits have thus established themselves on a superior societal level over the rest of their species. They are found throughout the Sith Order and the Empire’s governmental circles, presenting themselves aloof and vain on basis of their heritage.

_book_notes.homeworld: Korriban is the original world of the Sith, and many Sith Pureblood communities still live there. The planet’s environment is harsh, with cold, dry deserts spanning most of it. The few plants and animals that survive on its surface are cunning and deadly, corrupted by the strong dark side vergences that are found all across the planet. The many ancient tombs of the Sith are still rich on ancient knowledge and treasure, but also protected by traps, monster and manifestations of the dark side. In addition to Korriban, Sith Pureblood communities are also found on the other civilized worlds of the Empire, such as Dromund Kaas and Ziost..
_book_notes.language: The Sith language originates from original species that lived on Korriban. With the arrival of the dark Jedi, the latter learned the tongue and writing to gleam insight into the secret rituals of the Sith species. Over the millennia it developed to be an occult language to describe prophecies, alchemy and rituals, serving both preserve the original phrasing of the ancient Sith as well as obfuscate any of the information. Now, not many of the Sith Purebloods can speak or read the language, with its study being reserved to scholars of the Sith Order and Empire.
